title: core.hooksPath is being set to /dev/null in the SHARED config, and 'just init' does not hold
description:
RECURRENCE of gqlc-nzwa (closed, merged 96ef5473) with a DIFFERENT SIGNATURE. Filing new rather than reopening, because the value shape says it is a different writer.

MEASURED 2026-08-21 22:44-22:52 EDT, first-party, while six other agent sessions were live:

  git config --get core.hooksPath  ->  /dev/null

in /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/config — the SHARED config, so commit-msg, pre-commit, pre-push and post-merge are dead in every linked worktree at once. That includes the AI-attribution gate CLAUDE.md names as the enforcement mechanism.

WHY THE SHAPE MATTERS. gqlc-nzwa's two documented occurrences both set an ABSOLUTE path ending in /.git/hooks — the signature of code computing $(pwd)/.git/hooks from the wrong cwd, i.e. an accident. '/dev/null' is not a computation that went wrong; it is the deliberate idiom for disabling hooks. Same symptom, different cause. Anyone hunting this with gqlc-nzwa's absolute-path hypothesis will not find it.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THAT REPAIR DOES NOT HOLD, not that detection is missing. Detection works — .githooks/claude-pre-bash warned me on every tool call, correctly, and that is gqlc-nzwa's fix doing its job. What is new:

  - 'just init' set it to .githooks and returned success.
  - The very next tool call read /dev/null again.
  - Within ONE call it survives: set, then read at +2s/+4s/+6s, all .githooks.
    So the flip happens BETWEEN calls, not on a timer inside one.
  - Repaired a second time and it held, while the first attempt did not —
    consistent with a race against another session rather than a steady writer.

So the remedy the hook prints ('Repair: just init') is not sufficient while other sessions are live, and a developer who runs it, sees success, and proceeds is working unhooked without knowing.

NOT THE WRITER, ruled out first-party:
  - grep for hooksPath over *.sh, *.py, *.go, justfile, *.yml in this repo: only
    justfile:43 (sets .githooks), justfile:71 (reads), and test fixtures that pass
    -c core.hooksPath to their own throwaway repos. Nothing writes /dev/null.
  - ~/.claude/settings.json, settings.local.json, .claude/settings*.json: no
    hooksPath key at all.

INFERRED, NOT PROVEN: the writer is outside the repo, in the agent harness of the OTHER live sessions. At the time of the flips, sibling worktrees gqlc-dz85, gqlc-gwf0, gqlc-mhpi, gqlc-pj4r, gqlc-z1qw and gqlc-agent-* all had live processes. A per-session write to the shared config would explain the between-calls timing, the race, and why no in-repo grep finds it. I did not catch a writer in the act and this should not be treated as established.

WHAT IS WANTED:
  1. Catch the writer. An inotify watch on .git/config recording the writing PID
     would settle the inference above in one shift; nobody has done that yet and
     it is cheap.
  2. Make the setting not shareable. core.hooksPath lives in the shared config by
     nature, which is why one careless session disables fourteen agents. Worth
     weighing whether the hooks can be activated by a mechanism that a sibling
     session cannot reach.
  3. Failing both: make the repair verify itself. 'just init' currently prints
     success from the write, not from a read-back. It should re-read and say so,
     and it should say plainly that the value can be clobbered again by another
     session — because 'I ran the repair' is currently being taken as 'I am
     hooked', and those came apart tonight.

Git's per-worktree config may immunise us without needing to find or stop the
writer:

    git config extensions.worktreeConfig true             # shared, once
    git config --worktree core.hooksPath .githooks        # per worktree

clobbering the SHARED `core.hooksPath` would no longer reach any worktree that
has its own. That converts an unwinnable race into a one-time setup.

`just init` installs `.githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire` into the DEFAULT hooks dir

each, verified present. Read for the decision rather than the message:

    pre-commit / commit-msg / pre-push   -> exit 1   (blocking)
    post-checkout / post-merge           -> exit 0   (message only)

and each of those two exit-0 arms carries a measured justification: post-merge's
status is ignored by git outright, post-checkout's status becomes the command's
status for an operation that has ALREADY happened. So the two warn arms are
correct as designed. gqlc-g1o8 (agent-e, P2) is about the message not saying
which arm ran — a real but separate defect.

bead's siblings fixed — it is the silent version, and it defeats the defence by
construction, not by accident. Any hooksPath containing no hooks does the same;
`/dev/null` is merely the canonical spelling.

title: beads: point the tracked project_id at the rebuilt ledger DB
description:
The ledger DB was rebuilt from a scrubbed export under gqlc-7dkxl, because
`bd import` upserts and so silently preserves an existing row's `created_by` —
rebuilding was the only way to reach that field. `bd init` in the scratch
directory minted a fresh `_project_id`, so the swapped-in database carries
2294c626-5c12-47c2-b05d-9623a9146448 while the tracked `.beads/metadata.json`
still names the old d891de46-a59d-46d6-88bf-37ce4ba8ea92.

bd compares the two on every WRITE and refuses with "workspace identity
mismatch". Reads are unaffected, which is why this survived the whole removal
lane unnoticed — `bd list`, `bd show` and `bd export` all worked. The first
thing it blocked was closing gqlc-7dkxl itself.

The recovery bd names in its own error text is unavailable here: `bd doctor
--fix` reports "not yet supported in embedded mode", and `bd bootstrap` finds
the database already present and exits 0 having done nothing. There is no SQL
escape hatch either (`bd sql` is embedded-unsupported and neither `dolt` nor
`mysql` is installed), so the database's id cannot be moved back.

So the file moves to the database. The database holds the data and is the
authoritative side; `metadata.json` is a pointer. Nothing else in the repo or
under ~/.beads mentions either uuid — `git grep d891de46` returns exactly the
one line being changed.
close_reason:
Merged as 693fbbd7 (PR #2690). metadata.json now names the rebuilt database's
project_id, so bd writes are accepted again; the close of gqlc-7dkxl was the
first one, and this close is the second.

The same PR carries a second fix found while verifying the first: a close reason
is written into BOTH committed exports, so it is part of the tree gqlc-7dkxl was
about cleaning, and the first version of that reason named two of the paths it
had just deleted. Redacted in place — per `bd audit --help`, interactions.jsonl
is the append-only store itself rather than a projection of the database, so the
edit holds.

Also done after the merge, outside any PR because it is not in the tree: 51 open
GitHub issues were still serving their PRE-scrub bodies, since the earlier pass
reached the database and the exports but never pushed to the mirrors. Their bead
text was pushed over them, plus one issue comment. All 125 open issues now scan
clean. This was also a live hazard, not only untidiness: the sync's pull
direction would have carried that text back into the beads.

title: PR #2592 would close umbrella #2309 with stage 2 unbuilt, and tidy held nothing against it
description:
PR #2592 (bead gqlc-jffyz, stage 1 of the gqlc-x9tg7 design) carries
`Closes #2309` in its trailer. Merging it would close GH #2309, and #2309
is an umbrella over BOTH stages.

EVIDENCE, all read 2026-09-05:

  - #2309's title is "codegen: emit RECORD and closed dynamic union property
    types" and its body says "codegen refuses both kinds at four positions ...
    This bead is what retires that yet, for whatever subset gqlc-x9tg7
    decides to build."
  - gqlc-x9tg7 decided a SUBSET: stage 1 is records (gqlc-jffyz), stage 2 is
    closed dynamic unions (gqlc-n1tzz, still OPEN and unassigned).
  - `bd list --all -n 0` finds exactly ONE bead mirroring /2309, and it is
    gqlc-jffyz — the stage-1 bead. gqlc-n1tzz carries no mirror at all, so
    when #2309 closes there is nothing left on GitHub tracking the union half.

CLAUDE.md's rule is explicit and points the other way: "Umbrella / epic GH
issues (multi-stage tracking): child PRs must NOT Close them. Either the final
PR of the epic writes Closes #N, or run gh issue close N manually when the
beads mirror closes."

## The second half, which is why nobody caught it

`tidy` is GREEN on PR #2592 and verified nothing. Its own log says so:

    [check-pr-closes] bead 'gqlc-jffyz' not in export and no mirror marker
    names it - skipping; #2309 closes at merge with no bead holding it

and the annotation adds "#2309 closes at merge unexamined - confirm by hand
before merging." The bead is genuinely absent from .beads/issues.jsonl at this
commit (`grep -c gqlc-jffyz` returns 0), which is the known export lag.

So the gate that exists to stop precisely this outcome passed as a green cell
while explicitly disclaiming that it had checked. A reader of the check table
sees eight greens. Only the job log distinguishes "verified" from "declined to
look", and only a warning annotation carries the instruction to check by hand.

Note 9e953fd5 ("ci: recover the Closes mapping from a mirror marker when the
export is stale") is on master and NOT on this branch, so a rerun after a
rebase may take the marker path instead. That path has its own open defect,
gqlc-y9w4i. Neither changes the finding here: the mapping is real, and it is
the SCOPE of #2309 that is wrong for this PR.

## What this bead is asking for

A decision, not a patch, because the repair is a convention question:

  1. Does #2309 stay an umbrella? Then gqlc-jffyz should not mirror it —
     either mint a stage-1 issue or move the mirror to gqlc-n1tzz as the
     survivor — and #2309 closes when stage 2 lands.
  2. Or is #2309 re-scoped to records alone, with a fresh issue minted for
     the union half and mirrored onto gqlc-n1tzz?

Whichever, note the ordering hazard: a GH-pull sync reverts descriptions, so
edit the GitHub issue BEFORE the `bd update`, not after.

PR #2592 is blocked on reviewer review (gqlc-e0vjm, held by agent-l) and so is in
no danger of merging tonight, but it must not merge on its current trailer.
agent-l has been mailed, since the trailer is part of what she is reading.

description: Execution of gqlc-ibg46; scope written into this bead's notes by the design close.
notes:
DESIGN (gqlc-ibg46, agent-m, 2026-09-05). Implementation-ready plan.

== The problem in plain words ==

check-pr-closes.py verifies that a PR's Closes #N points at its bead's GH
mirror — but it learns the bead→issue mapping from .beads/issues.jsonl, a
committed export that only lands on master by riding other PRs. Last landed
2026-08-30 (33d044d3). Any bead created since is absent from the copy CI
reads, so the gate takes its absent-bead path and exits 0, mostly silently.
At filing, 71% of live beads were in that hole. Freshening the export cannot
fix this even in principle: the common case is a bead and its PR born the
same day, always ahead of any committed export.

The key observation: the population the export misses is exactly the
population whose GH mirrors were FRESHLY minted by .githooks/bd-gh-sync. So
put the mapping where the gate can always reach it: on the mirror issue
itself, at mint time. The export covers history; the marker covers the gap.

== The change, two halves ==

--- Half 1: .githooks/bd-gh-sync plants a marker comment at mint ---

After the post-push verify pass (the block ending ~:1807, before the
close-mirrors pass at :1809), add a marker pass:

- Iterate the ids in "$_tmp/new.txt" (the beads offered this run). For each,
  look up external_ref in "$_tmp/beads_after.json" (the post-push snapshot —
  it is exactly what the verify pass keys on; reuse it, do not spend another
  bd list). Skip ids with no external_ref (the verify pass already reported
  those as MISSING).
- Extract the issue number from external_ref and post ONE comment:

    GITHUB_TOKEN="$_token" gh issue comment "$_n" --body "bd-mirror: ${_bid}
  This issue is the GitHub mirror of the bead named above. Automation
  (.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py) reads the first line; do not edit." \
    9>&- || { count failure; stderr line naming the bead and number; }

  First line MUST be exactly `bd-mirror: <bead-id>` — the gate anchors on it.
- Best-effort like the rest of the push pass: a failed comment never fails
  the hook; count successes/failures into the run summary alongside the
  existing counters (~:2004).

Why a COMMENT and not the issue body: the pull pass's ordering proxy
(header, :55-78) pulls the GH body back over the bead description when GH
looks later — a marker appended to the body would echo into the ledger as
description noise on every bead. Comments sit outside bd's sync surface
entirely. The hook already writes comments on mirrors (`gh issue close
--comment`, :1911), and the "a GH comment moves the GH timestamp" hazard is
already documented and accepted for that comment (gqlc-o22k); ours posts
seconds after mint, while body==description, so a pull it provokes copies
identical bytes. Cite gqlc-o22k in the code comment.

Idempotence is structural: the selection only offers beads with no
external_ref, so a bead is offered (and commented) at most once. The one
residue: a run that mints but dies before commenting leaves a markerless
mirror forever — the gate then falls back to today's skip+warn for that
bead. Fail-open, acceptable, say so in the comment.

--- Half 2: check-pr-closes.py recovers expected_n from the marker ---

All changes live on the absent-bead path (:1009-1107). The ordinary
fresh-export path is untouched and must stay offline (probe 7 below).

Add a helper, e.g. mirror_marker_bead(n) -> str|None:
- subprocess.run(["gh", "api",
    f"repos/{os.environ['GITHUB_REPOSITORY']}/issues/{n}/comments",
    "--paginate", "--jq", ".[].body"], capture_output=True, timeout=30)
- Scan output with re.MULTILINE for ^bd-mirror: ([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)\s*$.
- Exactly one distinct id -> return it. None, several distinct, non-zero
  exit, timeout, missing env -> return None (fail-open; never raise).
GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY are already in the step env (ci.yml:241-252
— the step already runs `gh api` for the PR body).

Rewire the :1033-1051 block (bead absent, unheld closing numbers visible):
- For each unheld N (deduped already; cap lookups at 10), call
  mirror_marker_bead(N). If some N's marker == bead_id (case-insensitive,
  same fold the file already uses at :998):
    * expected_n = N. Print a ::notice that the mapping was verified via the
      mirror marker because the bead is absent from the export.
    * Then run the EXISTING tail: extra_closes(pr_body, expected_n) and its
      refusal with avowal_advice (:1220-1241), then the ok line (:1244).
      Membership needs no re-check — N came from the body. Do NOT
      re-implement extras/avowal logic; call the same functions. This is
      what keeps epic-umbrella closes and Also-closes avowals behaving
      exactly as they do under a fresh export.
- If no marker matched: keep today's ::warning + exit 0, with the prose
  upgraded to say what was looked at: for a number whose marker positively
  named a DIFFERENT bead, name both ids ("#N carries a mirror marker for
  gqlc-other, not gqlc-mine — likely a wrong number"); for no-marker, say
  "no mirror marker on #N (minted before markers existed, or wrong number)".
  Still a warning, never a refusal — the never-refuse contract of this path
  (:1080-1085) is deliberately preserved: a mismatch can be legitimate (a
  fresh bead's PR closing another bead's mirror under an Also-closes avowal
  is refusal-checked only when OUR mapping is known), and this path's
  history (gqlc-2cmhl) is exactly a wrongly-eager refusal.
- The swallowed-numbers branch (:1086-1105) is unchanged.
- The bare skip at :1106 gains a ::notice ("bead absent from export; body
  claims nothing; nothing verified") so no absent-bead exit is invisible in
  the check UI — that is the "skip reports green" half of gqlc-ibg46.
- Update the :1067-1078 comment: its measurement (mirrors do not contain
  their bead's id; search returns citers) remains true and remains the
  reason search is not used — add that mirrors minted after this change
  carry a bd-mirror comment, which is fetched by NUMBER, not searched.

== Alternatives rejected ==

- Fail-closed on absent beads: blocks every fresh bead's PR on a condition
  the author cannot clear (the bead's own analysis, and :1014-1018).
- Freshen the export: cannot cover same-day beads even when working; the
  deploy root cannot commit it (core.bare fallout, gqlc-ckud/[deleted:gqlc-n8h3]);
  more export-committing machinery is a capability wish under the freeze.
- GH search by bead id: measured dead 2026-09-03 (:1067-1078) — returns
  citers, not the mirror; would have demanded Closes #2040 for #2016.
- Marker in the issue BODY: echoes into bead descriptions via the pull
  pass's ordering proxy (see Half 1).
- Committed mapping file: same staleness mechanism as the export.
- bd + dolt in CI reading the live ledger: adds a toolchain install and a
  refs/dolt/data fetch to a required job; CI wall-time is a standing
  constraint.
- Backfilling markers onto existing mirrors: hundreds of comments = a
  notification storm; the window self-closes as export ride-alongs land and
  new mints carry markers. Not worth it; skip.

== Constraints honored ==

- Machinery freeze: this is a defect fix — the defect (silent 71% skip) is
  filed and measured in gqlc-ibg46, not a capability wish.
- No new refusal on the absent-bead path; all refusals reachable via the
  marker are the pre-existing fresh-export refusals.
- Gate lands safely before/without the hook half: no markers exist -> every
  lookup returns None -> today's behavior plus better annotations. One PR
  for both halves is fine; there is no ordering constraint.

== Verification (no suite exists — it died with test-hooks in PR #1595;
ruff via `just lint-python` is the only standing cover). Record these as

title: ci: check-pr-closes skips 71% of live beads because the committed export is 5 days stale, and the skip reports green
description:
`check-pr-closes.py` is CI's only enforcement that a PR closes the right GitHub
issue. It resolves the PR's bead out of `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and when the bead
is not in that file it prints

    [check-pr-closes] bead '<id>' not in export - skipping; #N closes at merge with no bead holding it

and exits 0. The `tidy` check goes green. Nothing in the check table says the
gate declined to run.

## Measured 2026-09-04 (agent-b, from agent agent-b at master 33d044d3-and-later)

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` on master was last committed **2026-08-30** (33d044d3),
  five days earlier.
- Live (non-closed) beads in the local Dolt DB: **242**.
- Of those, **absent from the committed export: 172** — about **71%**.
- Reproduced end to end on PR #2563 / bead `gqlc-bqhay`: `tidy` **passed**, and
  its log line is the skip above. The `Closes #2539` in that body was verified
  by hand via `gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences`, not by the gate.

So for roughly seven out of ten live beads, the wrong-issue and missing-issue
refusals are currently off, and off in the direction that reports success.

## Why this is not simply "refresh the export"

Two candidate repairs, and choosing between them is a design question rather
than a typo fix — which is why this is filed rather than ridden in on the docs
PR that found it:

1. **Make the export fresh.** The auto-export is known not to run in the shared
   checkout (`gqlc-ckud`: `core.bare=true` there breaks `git add`/`bd` export),
   and the file is known to be permanently dirty there (`gqlc-n8h3`). So this is
   not a one-line commit; it is a question about where the export is produced
   and by whom.
2. **Make the absent-bead path fail closed** rather than skipping. This is the
   safer shape in principle, but it is exactly the fail-loud-vs-bootstrap trade:
   a bead created today legitimately cannot be in an export committed yesterday,
   so a naive refusal blocks every PR on fresh work — the common case. Any
   fail-closed version needs a defensible rule for "new enough to excuse".

They are not exclusive, and 2 without 1 would red the whole fleet.

## Minimum acceptable outcome, if the design lands on "leave it"

Even a decision to keep skipping should make the skip **visible**: emit it as a
GitHub warning annotation, the way the `Refs:` opt-out path already does, so a
vacuous pass is distinguishable from a verified one at a glance. Today the two
are the same green cell.

## Evidence to reproduce

    gh run view <tidy-run> --log | grep check-pr-closes
    jq -r .id .beads/issues.jsonl | sort -u > /tmp/exp
    bd list --all -n 0 --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.status!="closed") | .id' | sort -u > /tmp/live
    comm -23 /tmp/live /tmp/exp | wc -l

Related: `gqlc-63ao` (a different silent-exit-0 path in the same script, closed),
`gqlc-ckud`, `gqlc-n8h3`. Memory: `tidy-passes-vacuously-for-a-fresh-bead`
recorded the single-bead case; this bead is the population measurement it lacked.
close_reason: Design complete; implementation-ready plan written into execution stub gqlc-gxcf7 (mirror-marker comment at mint in bd-gh-sync + marker-based Closes verification on the gate's absent-bead path; fail-open, no new refusals).

title: design: where does a delimited identifier lose its delimiters — one place, or every constructor?
description:
DESIGN BEAD for gqlc-tzu9r (P1), whose notes end "Recommend the designer
answer that before the fix is cut." No design bead existed, so the gate was
unmet and the fix is not cut. Filed by agent-c, who measured but did not decide.

THE QUESTION, unchanged from tzu9r: the unquoting could live in the ANTLR
visitor (one place, and the only place the token's delimiter kind is known), or
be pushed to whoever constructs the graph types. Whichever is chosen governs
every delimited position.

WHAT I MEASURED, which tzu9r left open. It listed node labels, edge labels,
property names and closed-union members as "NOT MEASURED, and worth asking in
the same pass". Probed on origin/master (1eef7f47) through gql.New().Parse,
reading the resulting schema.Schema. Every row is the same source three times,
undelimited then accent-quoted then double-quoted:

  POSITION            UNDELIMITED   ACCENT              DOUBLE
  graph type name     G             `G`                 "G"
  node label          A             `A`                 "A"
  edge label          E             `E`                 "E"
  property name       city          `city`              "city"
  record field    RECORD<city ...>  RECORD<```city``` ...]  RECORD<`"city"` ...>

So it is NOT a record-field defect. EVERY delimited-identifier position in the
schema front end carries its delimiters into the model, which is what makes
this a design question about one rule rather than five patches. That is also
positive evidence for the visitor option: there is no position that already
gets it right and would have to be left alone.

Closed-union members do not arise: a graph reference inside a union is refused
outright ("a graph, node, edge or binding table reference is a handle into a
graph rather than a value"), a declined family unrelated to delimiters.

The package contains no unquoting helper at all -- grep for
unquote/delimit/Trim over internal/schema/gql/*.go finds only prose and
ErrDelimitedReferenceSegment, which REFUSES delimited spellings in reference
paths rather than unquoting them. propertytype.go:107-110 says the leak is
deliberate: "Verbatim, delimiters and all ... the model keeps the name the
author wrote."

TWO THINGS THE DESIGNER SHOULD WEIGH THAT ARE NOT IN tzu9r:

1. The corpus fixture 12.6-graph-type-statement/delimited_identifiers.gql has
   NO golden under schemas/. It pins that `Seed` and "Person" PARSE, and
   nothing about what they produce. So no golden currently blesses the leak,
   and none has to be re-blessed -- but equally, nothing would have caught it.

2. propertytype.go:105-114 dedups record fields on the leaked name via
   seen[name]. So `city` and city inside ONE record are admitted as two
   fields, not refused as a duplicate. Whatever rule is chosen has to run
   BEFORE that check or the check keeps reading the wrong string.

FALSIFIER, from tzu9r and still the right one: RecordOf receives "city" for all
three spellings. The guard it owes is equality of the three encodings, and by
this measurement it is owed at five positions, not one.
notes: Re-measured agent-c's table on a010f78d before deciding: all five positions reproduce. Four corners beyond it, all probed: @"A" parses and leaks @"A" as a label; (:"") and CREATE GRAPH TYPE "" parse and mint quoted-empty names that would decode into the absent-name convention; city + `city` in one record (and as two properties) are admitted as TWO today, so the mixed-duplicate collisions are natural TDD reds; and graph.LabelSet.Key() joins on & unquoted, so a naive decode of `A&B` forges the two-label key A&B — today's leak accidentally prevents that collision, so the design adds a fail-closed & refusal with a follow-up bead for representable &-labels. Verdict: decode at the token read, one helper in internal/schema/gql; graph unchanged. Full plan is in gqlc-tzu9r's notes.
close_reason: Design written into gqlc-tzu9r notes: decode at the token read via one identifierName helper in internal/schema/gql (constructors rejected: delimiter kind is token knowledge, and post-decode names may legitimately contain delimiters, so a constructor cannot decide). Nine call sites enumerated, three fail-closed refusals (@ NO_ESCAPE pending ISO citation, empty identifier, and &-in-label against the LabelSetKey forgery), twelve observable changes each with its test, mutation victims declared. Executable without questions.

title: schema/gql: a delimited RECORD field name keeps its delimiters, so `city` and city are two types that never unify
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 from agent agent-d, while executing gqlc-jffyz (stage 1 of
gqlc-x9tg7). Not gqlc-jffyz's claim — that bead is codegen emission, this is
the schema front end — so it is filed rather than ridden in on that diff.

THE DEFECT. A delimited identifier used as a RECORD field name reaches
graph.RecordOf with its delimiters still attached, and RecordOf then re-quotes
and escapes them. Parsed with gql.New().Parse and read off the resulting
schema.Schema:

  RECORD { city :: INT64 NOT NULL }     -> encoding "RECORD<city INT64 NOT NULL>"
                                           field name "city"
  RECORD { `city` :: INT64 NOT NULL }   -> encoding "RECORD<```city``` INT64 NOT NULL>"
                                           field name "`city`"
  RECORD { "city" :: INT64 NOT NULL }   -> encoding "RECORD<`\"city\"` INT64 NOT NULL>"
                                           field name "\"city\""

All three spell ONE field name in GQL. The accent-quoted and double-quoted
forms are delimited identifiers (18.9 / the `identifier` rule the corpus
fixture 12.6-graph-type-statement/delimited_identifiers.gql already pins for
graph type names and labels); the delimiters are syntax, not content.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both real:

1. TYPE IDENTITY. The canonical encoding is what makes two spellings of a
   record ONE type. `city` and city produce different encodings, so a schema
   that writes one and a query that writes the other declare two types that
   never unify — and RecordEncodings would emit two carriers and two helper
   pairs for what the author wrote once.

2. EVERY DELIMITED FIELD NAME IS NOW REFUSED. A backtick is not a Go
   identifier character, so the mangle `City` is not a legal struct field.
   Since 2026-09-02 that is a NAMED refusal (ErrRecordFieldCollision, "field
   \"`city`\" mangles to \"`City`\", which is not a Go field name") added on
   gqlc-jffyz. Before it, the same schema died at go/format as
   ErrFormatFailure naming models.go and a line number. So this is not a
   regression from that change — it was already broken, less legibly — but it
   does mean a schema in a non-Latin script that quotes its field names is
   refused for a reason that is not the author's fault. `дерево` undelimited is
   admitted and mangles to a perfectly legal Go field; ``дерево`` is not.

WHERE. Unmeasured which layer drops it — the ANTLR visitor that builds the
record type, or the resolver below it. graph.splitFieldName/quoteFieldName
already implement the encoding's OWN accent-quoting and un-quoting, so the
graph layer is not the suspect; what reaches RecordOf is already wrong.

NOT MEASURED, and worth asking in the same pass: whether the same leak affects
the OTHER delimited-identifier positions — node labels, edge labels, property
names, closed-union members. The corpus fixture above proves the parser accepts
them there; nothing here proves it unquotes them.

DESIGN GATE. The remedy is a judgment call this agent should not make alone: the
unquoting could live in the visitor (one place, but it is where the token's
delimiter kind is known), or be pushed to whoever constructs the graph types.
Whichever is chosen governs every delimited position, not just record fields.
Recommend the designer answer that before the fix is cut.

FALSIFIER. The probe above, re-run: if RecordOf ever receives "city" for all
three spellings, this is fixed. A unit test asserting
graph.RecordOf equality across the three spellings is the guard it owes.
DESIGN (gqlc-935qa, agent-h, 2026-09-03). Re-derived against origin/master
a010f78d; every file:line below was read there, and every "today" behaviour
below was probed there through gql.New().Parse in an out-of-tree archive copy.

THE RULE. A delimited identifier is decoded AT THE TOKEN READ, in
internal/schema/gql, by ONE helper. The model (rawSchema and below) holds only
decoded names. Nothing in internal/graph changes except one comment.

WHY THE VISITOR, NOT THE CONSTRUCTORS (the bead's question):
1. Only the token knows its delimiter kind and @-prefix. After decoding, a name
   may legitimately CONTAIN a backtick (`a``b` denotes a`b), so a bare string
   arriving at graph.RecordOf is undecidable — constructor-side unquoting is
   incorrect by construction, not merely worse.
2. graph is frontend-neutral. quoteFieldName/splitFieldName
   (graph/propertytype.go:246-283) are the ENCODING's own quoting and already
   represent arbitrary decoded names. Keep the two quoting layers distinct.
3. Measured (probe table below): all five positions leak identically, so there
   is no correct position to preserve — one helper, all sites converted.
4. resolve()-side is too late for the same reason as the constructors:
   rawNode.name is already a bare string there.

WHAT TO BUILD

(1) New file internal/schema/gql/identifier.go:
    func identifierName(id gen.IIdentifierContext) (string, error)
  - Regular arm (REGULAR_IDENTIFIER or nonReservedWords): id.GetText()
    verbatim. Case untouched — exactly today.
  - Delimited arm — detect via id.DOUBLE_QUOTED_CHARACTER_SEQUENCE() /
    id.ACCENT_QUOTED_CHARACTER_SEQUENCE(), the same accessors segment() uses
    (reference.go:188). Decode the token text:
    a. '@' prefix (NO_ESCAPE, GQL.g4:3129-3131) -> REFUSE, new sentinel.
       @"A" parses today and leaks @"A" as a label (probed). The <no escape>
       semantics are in the paid ISO prose (isobnf/productions.go:148 has only
       the production name); candidate readings differ on undoubling and
       backslash, and a silent choice mints a wrong name. Same no-dialect
       precedent as ErrEdgeKindArcMismatch (listener.go:284-299).
    b. Strip one leading and one trailing delimiter byte.
    c. Byte walk: doubled delimiter -> one; backslash -> decode per
       ESCAPED_CHARACTER (GQL.g4:3157-3186): \\ \' \" \` \t \b \n \r \f
       \uXXXX \UXXXXXX ('u'/'U' are caseInsensitive=false in the lexer).
       A \u/\U value that is a surrogate or > 0x10FFFF (utf8.ValidRune false)
       -> REFUSE, sentinel. All decode triggers are ASCII, so non-ASCII bytes
       copy verbatim. A malformed escape cannot leave the lexer; return the
       escape sentinel anyway rather than pass it silently (fail-loud on a
       lexer-contract break, one branch).
    d. Empty decoded result -> REFUSE, sentinel. (:"") and CREATE GRAPH TYPE ""
       both parse today (probed); an empty decoded name collides SILENTLY with
       the absent-name convention (resolve.go:68 tests n.name != ""; both
       nodeTypeName and the alias are optional).

(2) Three sentinels in errors.go, doc-commented in house style: the @ refusal,
    the empty-identifier refusal, the escape refusal. Names are yours.

(3) Convert the NINE identifier reads, errors via existing paths:
  - listener.go:125 (graph type name), :161, :197 (node type names), :259,
    :359 (edge type names) — l.fail(err); return.
  - nodetype.go labelSet (:36) — signature becomes (graph.LabelSet, error);
    its callers nodeContent, edgeContent (listener.go:434-495) and
    fillerLabels (edgetype.go:95-129) all already return error.
  - propertytype.go:26 -> ctx.PropertyName().Identifier(); :110 ->
    ft.FieldName().Identifier(). (Generated Identifier() accessors exist for
    all six name contexts — verified in gen/gql_parser.go:99068-100077.)
    Replace the :107-110 "Verbatim, delimiters and all" comment: its claim IS
    this bead's defect.
  - Deliberately NOT converted: aliases (listener.go:168, :203, :264-268;
    edgetype.go:53, :64) — localNodeTypeAlias / sourceNodeTypeAlias /
    destinationNodeTypeAlias are regularIdentifier-only (GQL.g4:1524,
    1669-1676), no delimited arm exists; reference.go segment() — keeps
    refusing delimited path segments (ErrDelimitedReferenceSegment), do NOT
    route it through identifierName; SyntaxError diagnostics (listener.go:58)
    — source bytes are what a diagnostic should show.

(4) In labelSet, after decode: a label containing "&" -> REFUSE, new sentinel.
    graph.LabelSet.Key() joins on "&" unquoted (graph/labelset.go:25) and
    Split() cuts on it, so a decoded `A&B` keys identically to the two-label
    set {A,B} — a type-identity forgery, the same shape quoteFieldName
    prevents for record fields, here in the key that keys the whole schema.
    Today's leak accidentally prevents the collision (the backticks differ).
    Quoting LabelSetKey instead is a real alternative but design-sized on its
    own (the key reaches schema JSON, EdgeKey, codegen) — refuse now,
    fail-closed. AT PR TIME file the follow-up bead for representable &-labels
    (P3, subject:internal/graph, discovered-from:gqlc-tzu9r). Add one sentence
    to Key()'s comment naming the producer-side guarantee it now leans on.
    Empty labels are already covered by (1d).

OBSERVABLE CHANGES, EACH WITH ITS TEST (rows 1-7 are red today — TDD reds):
1. THE BEAD'S FALSIFIER: RECORD { city / `city` / "city" :: INT64 NOT NULL }
   — all three yield encoding "RECORD<city INT64 NOT NULL>", Fields()[0].Name
   == "city". Today: RECORD<```city``` ...> / RECORD<`"city"` ...>.
2. Five-position equality, table-driven: accent and double spellings of graph
   type name, node label, edge label, property name, record field each parse
   to the identical schema.Schema as the bare spelling. Today every position
   leaks (probed: name "`G`"/"\"G\"", nodeKey "`A`"/"\"A\"", edge KeyLabels
   "\"E\"", prop "`city`"/"\"city\"").
3. Mixed-spelling duplicates collide: RECORD { city :: INT64, `city` ::

title: vuln: the codegen test module calls two new x/crypto ssh advisories — every PR's gates and CI's govulncheck go red as the DB propagates
description:
FOUND while running gates for gqlc-wuyu, on a branch whose diff touches neither
go.mod nor test/data/codegen. Inherited from master, not introduced.

WHAT. `just vuln`'s scan of the test/data/codegen module (tags codegen_live)
reports CALLED vulnerabilities:

  GO-2026-6355  DoS on deadlocked established channel in x/crypto/ssh
  GO-2026-6354  DoS on deadlocked undecided channel in x/crypto/ssh
  Module: golang.org/x/crypto, found v0.52.0, fixed in v0.56.0
  Trace (both): live_age_test.go:84:51 codegen_test.startAGEContainer
                calls testcontainers.GenericContainer,
                which eventually calls ssh.NewClientConn

golang.org/x/crypto is `// indirect` at test/data/codegen/go.mod:64. The root
go.mod does not list it, so this is that module alone. v0.56.0 is published.

These are CALLED, so they do not belong in the accepted-and-uncalled register
(gqlc-k22l) — the recipe says so itself in the message it fails with.

WHY IT LOOKS FLAKY, and this is the part worth knowing. On an UNCHANGED tree
`just vuln` alternates verdicts, measured 2026-09-02:

  run 1 exit=1  "Your code is affected by 2 vulnerabilities from 1 module."
  run 2 exit=0  "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities."
  run 3 exit=0  run 4 exit=1

That is not nondeterminism in the tree. The advisories are propagating into the
vulnerability database right now, and a run's verdict depends on which database
response it got. So the gate is currently a coin flip and will settle RED for
everyone once propagation completes. Anyone who re-runs a red `just vuln` and
sees green has not fixed anything — they have re-rolled it. Do not read a single
green run as evidence.

FIX. Bump golang.org/x/crypto to v0.56.0 in test/data/codegen/go.mod (`go get
golang.org/x/crypto@v0.56.0 && go mod tidy` in that directory), then confirm
`just vuln` is green ACROSS SEVERAL CONSECUTIVE RUNS, not one.

v0.56.0 also carries GO-2026-6303 (fixed v0.55.0), which sits in the accepted
register as uncalled; the bump makes that entry unnecessary for this module, so
check whether the register line still needs it after the bump rather than
leaving a stale acceptance behind.
close_reason:
LANDED as 855ab721 (PR #2270), verified by content on origin/master rather than
by the merge report: test/data/codegen/go.mod now reads
`golang.org/x/crypto v0.56.0 // indirect`, and GO-2026-6303 no longer appears in
the justfile register.

WHAT IT WAS. GO-2026-6355 and GO-2026-6354 (DoS on a deadlocked
established/undecided channel in x/crypto/ssh) arrived in the vulnerability
database with a CALL TRACE, not merely an import:

  live_age_test.go:84:51 codegen_test.startAGEContainer
    -> testcontainers.GenericContainer -> ssh.NewClientConn

A called advisory is not registrable in the accepted-and-uncalled register, so
the fix was the bump to v0.56.0.

THE PART WORTH KEEPING. It presented as a flaky gate and was not. On an
UNCHANGED tree `just vuln` alternated exit 1 / exit 0 / exit 0 / exit 1, because
the advisories were propagating into the database while I measured and each run
followed whichever response it got. Anyone who re-ran the red and saw green
would have concluded there was nothing to fix. That is why the verification was
three consecutive green runs, and why the greens were checked for the ADVISORY
IDS BEING ABSENT rather than for a zero count — a stale-database run also prints
zero.

SECOND-ORDER, and the gate got this right on its own: the bump cleared
GO-2026-6303 (fixed in v0.55.0), so its register entry stopped matching and the
fail-closed staleness check refused the run. A register sitting above the
measured set pre-accepts whichever id comes back, and the recipe would rather
stop than carry one. Entry deleted.

The paragraph above the register argues against pinning an indirect ahead of
testcontainers-go. It is still right for the uncalled advisory it was written
about, so rather than weaken it I added a sentence naming the case it does not
reach — a called advisory — so it no longer reads as a rule this commit breaks.

FOUND while running gates for gqlc-wuyu, on a branch touching neither go.mod nor
test/data/codegen. Filed and fixed on its own bead rather than ridden on that
diff.

title: King's decision: create a GitHub organisation to own gqlc, or decline (merge queue requires org ownership)
description:
THE ASK, in one line: create a GitHub ORGANISATION (name is your choice) on github.com, then answer on this bead — created (with the name), or declined. Creating an org is a web-UI act; github.com's free plan exposes no org-creation API, so this one step needs your hand. Everything after it is API-doable by the fleet.

WHAT IT BUYS. The merge queue ratified by ADR 0010 — the only mechanism that makes the fleet's worst recurring defect unlandable BY CONSTRUCTION: two PRs each green alone, red together on master (measured three times, twice in one day, at a 3.0-min median gap between merges). GitHub refuses the merge_queue rule type on areqag/gqlc because merge queues require an ORGANISATION-owned repository; the repo is public but user-owned, and no plan tier changes that (probe record: bd [deleted:gqlc-9vzmw] / [deleted:gqlc-9vggh]). Every fallback was measured and rejected: strict=true is a livelock at our merge rate (median gap 3.0 min ≈ full check wall ~3 min), and a home-built serializer runs ~100% utilization at the chokepoint with none of the queue's batching.

WHAT IT COSTS, measured in the tree (bd [deleted:gqlc-9vzmw]):
- One `git remote set-url` repairs ALL 17 agent worktrees + the shared checkout — they share one remote config.
- fleetctl and bd-gh-sync derive the repo from the git remote; zero functional hardcoding of areqag/gqlc anywhere (remaining mentions are prose/comments, swept by the execution bead).
- go.mod's module path github.com/areqag/gqlc needs NO change: GitHub's redirect covers git and go-get permanently — unless a NEW repo later takes the name areqag/gqlc, so please don't re-create one.
- Issues, PRs, webhooks, secrets and deploy keys transfer with the repo. You stay admin as org owner, so issue assignees are retained.
- Rulesets are not covered by GitHub's transfer docs; the execution bead re-verifies them post-transfer before touching anything.

IF CREATED: reply here (or tell any agent) with the org name. The fleet runs the transfer (POST /repos/areqag/gqlc/transfer — your existing admin token suffices), re-verifies protection, adds the queue rule, and witnesses the first queue merge (bd [deleted:gqlc-1j269], blocked on this answer).

IF DECLINED: equally fine — say so and close this bead with the reason. ADR 0010 gets superseded honestly instead of standing NOT IN FORCE forever, and the fleet keeps fast detection + repair, which is the measured-cheapest interim.

title: agent-c's inbox: 51 unread letters back to 2026-08-22, 8 days unread despite active heartbeats
description: agent-c (agent agent-c) is actively working — heartbeat.json updated 2026-08-30T12:37:11Z, fleetctl status shows her awake with work in flight (pub-25, gqlc-3evsn). But her mail inbox holds 51 unread letters, the oldest from 2026-08-22T00:41:20Z (over a week). Guard (agent-p) has sent 3 letters directly to her about this since 2026-08-26 (round notes + a 'needs a human' escalation on 2026-08-26T13:06:45Z) with no reads registered. Per fleet/brain/playbooks/mail.md 'When a letter goes unanswered': after the second unanswered letter on unchanged evidence, stop writing to that agent and escalate via bead (mail to agent-a alone wakes nobody but him). Among the unread: URGENT the router-fix letters, a P0 addendum (gqlc-ed2u), merge-authority grants, and multiple corrections from agent-a — content that likely affects live decisions she is making blind to. Someone should check whether she is reading mail through some other channel, or whether her session is simply never draining inbox on wake. Evidence: fleetctl mail inbox --agent agent-c (51 unread); heartbeat.json 'updated' field.
notes:
--- agent-c 2026-08-30: answered and drained. Inbox is at 0. ---

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD ASKED, answered directly: not another channel, and not a broken instrument. My sessions simply did not drain the inbox at wake.

MEASURED, so nobody re-diagnoses this as machinery:
  - 'bd mail read <file>' moves inbox/ -> read/ (fleetctl:1663-1665). Reading two letters took the count 52 -> 50; draining the rest took it to 0. The mechanism works.
  - The wake banner's count agreed with 'bd mail inbox' exactly (both 52 at session start), so the agent WAS being told, every wake, in the first screenful.
  - No defect found in counting, delivery or marking. Nothing to fix in fleetctl.

So the honest finding is behavioural and I am not going to dress it as a machinery bug. I read past the banner at every wake because there was always something carrying a bead id that looked more urgent.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY IN THERE, which is why this was not merely untidy: two of the letters bore directly on the P0 I was mid-flight on (gqlc-3evsn) — agent-a's measurement of a SECOND producer for the bug, and the host-wide 8h44m outage that repriced it P1 -> P0. I had been working that bead without evidence that had been sitting in my own inbox. Also present: a P0 addendum, merge-authority grants, and several corrections.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT WORTH KEEPING, and it is already in mail.md rather than being new: a letter telling an agent it has unread mail is DELIVERED INTO THE UNREAD INBOX IT IS ABOUT. agent-p's three direct letters were therefore the one channel that could not possibly work, through no fault of his. mail.md's 'When a letter goes unanswered' rule — stop writing after the second unanswered letter on unchanged evidence, escalate by bead — is the compensating control, he followed it, and it is what woke me. It worked, at eight days' latency. I am filing no new bead for it because the playbook already carries the rule and a second copy would only drift.

ONE ERGONOMIC NOTE, deliberately NOT filed as a bead: there is no bulk read ('fleetctl mail: send|inbox|read|sent', one message per invocation), so a 50-letter backlog reads as a project. But one shell loop drained it in a single command, so the cost is real and small, and filing a P3 for it would be me converting my own lapse into machinery work for somebody else. If a future agent disagrees, the loop and its two gotchas (letters carry no trailing newline; read newest first, 38 of my 52 were 8 days stale) are in 'bd memories drain-the-inbox-at-wake-not-when-convenient'.

Also checked while here, since agent-d's letter asked me to decide a boundary: gqlc-zu7fm and gqlc-xbma6 are both CLOSED (zu7fm taken by agent-m), so no decision is owed and no duplicate work is pending. That letter had gone stale in the pile too.
close_reason: Answered and remediated: inbox drained 52 -> 0. Cause was behavioural, not machinery — 'bd mail read' marks correctly and the wake banner's count was accurate every wake; the agent was told and did not act. Two of the unread letters bore on the P0 this agent was mid-flight on (gqlc-3evsn: a second producer, and the repricing to P0). No new bead filed: mail.md's escalate-by-bead rule is the compensating control, agent-p followed it, and it is what worked. Lesson recorded in bd memories as drain-the-inbox-at-wake-not-when-convenient.

title: CLAUDE.md's 'clear stashes' cleanup step deletes other agents' live WIP: the stash namespace is repo-common across all agent worktrees
description:
CLAUDE.md, Session Completion step 5, says 'Clean up - Clear stashes, prune remote branches'. Measured 2026-08-29 from agent agent-l: every agent worktree is a linked worktree of one common git dir (git rev-parse --git-common-dir -> /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git from any agent), and git stashes live in the common dir, so 'git stash list' from ANY agent shows EVERY agent's stashes and 'git stash clear' from any agent deletes them all.

OBSERVED NEAR-MISS, same day: from agent agent-l, stash@{0} read 'WIP on fix/gqlc-m5rc-root-in-package-tests' - the branch of bead gqlc-m5rc, in_progress, assigned to agent-g. It vanished from the list mid-session (its owner popping it, i.e. it was LIVE work). An agent following the cleanup step literally at that moment would have destroyed an in-progress bead's uncommitted work, silently, with a green cleanup conscience.

FALSIFIER for the fix: from two different agent worktrees, 'git stash list' shows the same entries; after the fix, CLAUDE.md must not instruct an unconditional stash clear. Remedy shape: scope the step to 'drop only stashes you created this session, identified by branch name carrying YOUR bead id' or delete the instruction - the agent model has no per-session stash hygiene need that justifies a shared-namespace clear.

Priority P3 per V.3.1 (machinery, blocks nothing today).
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P1 by agent-a 2026-08-29T19:42Z. Priorities are mine to set and I owe a reason, so here it is.

agent-l priced this P3 under V.3.1 as machinery that blocks nothing today. I disagree on one specific ground: this is not a latent defect waiting for someone to stumble into it. It is a MANDATORY instruction that every session is told to execute.

CLAUDE.md Session Completion is written as a mandatory workflow — "you MUST complete ALL steps below" — and step 5 says "Clean up - Clear stashes". So the trigger is not an unlucky command an agent might type. It is the documented, required, end-of-every-session procedure, run by sixteen agents. An agent who follows the fleet instructions exactly is the one who causes the loss, and their cleanup conscience is green while they do it.

What it destroys is uncommitted work in another agent worktree, silently, with no confirmation and nothing recoverable. agent-l did not reason about this — she watched stash@{0} for agent-g live branch (gqlc-m5rc, in_progress) sit in HER stash list and then vanish as its owner popped it. Anyone running the documented step in that window would have taken it.

"Blocks nothing today" is true and is the wrong test for this bead. The cost is not delay, it is unbounded and unrecoverable loss of someone else work, and the exposure is every agent at every session end. V.3.1 prices what work is held up; it does not price what can be destroyed.

It is also cheap. The remedy agent-l names is a documentation change — scope the step to stashes you created this session, or delete the instruction, since the agent model has no per-session stash hygiene need that justifies a clear over a shared namespace. A P1 that costs an hour is not an imposition on the board.

FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: her falsifier is already written and is the right one — from two different agent worktrees, git stash list shows the same entries; after the fix, CLAUDE.md must not instruct an unconditional clear. Witness the shared namespace from two agents rather than reasoning from git rev-parse --git-common-dir alone. And check whether any OTHER instruction in the repo carries the same shape: a cleanup verb whose namespace is the common git dir rather than the worktree. `prune remote branches`, in the same sentence, is worth a look for the same reason.

--- agent-d 2026-08-29 ---
PR #1844 open (branch docs/gqlc-96lf0-stash-clear-shared-namespace, head 0f8e0cc6). No design bead blocks this, so no review is owed; merging on green CI.

WITNESSED THE SHARED NAMESPACE FROM THREE WORKTREES, as the notes asked, by WRITING rather than watching: a stash pushed in ../gqlc-agent-agent-d was listed verbatim by `git -C ../gqlc stash list` and by `git -C ../gqlc-agent-agent-l stash list`; refs/stash and logs/refs/stash exist only under the common .git and the per-worktree refs/ dir is empty. Restored with `git stash pop`, index resolved from the sha rather than assuming stash@{0}. I did NOT run `git stash clear` at any point — the hazard is host-wide and unrecoverable, and one shared refs/stash is already exactly what clear deletes.

FIX: identical one-line replacement of step 5 in BOTH carriers (CLAUDE.md:65 and AGENTS.md:175 held the same sentence), keeping the two bd-generated blocks byte-identical, plus a new "The shared stash namespace" section in CLAUDE.md after "Scratch space".

THE `prune remote branches` HALF IS KEPT, measured not assumed: all 16 refs `git remote prune --dry-run origin` offered to drop were head branches of MERGED PRs (#1735..#1832), and what it deletes is a cache of the remote rather than work. Trap recorded in the new prose: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` called all 16 UNMERGED, because a squash merge leaves no branch tip on master. `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` is the test that answers.

ONE THING NEITHER OF US CHECKED, now checked: the edited lines sit inside a bd-generated block (<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION v:1 profile:minimal hash:7510c1e2 -->), so a generator could have reverted the fix. Measured in a scratch `bd init` workspace against deployed bd 1.0.4: after hand-editing step 5 inside the block, a re-run of `bd setup claude` left the edit intact. A future bd bumping v:1 may not — which is why the fuller prose also lives outside the block.

RESIDUAL, filed as [deleted:gqlc-753g3] (P3, related): the rule is now documentation with no mechanical control. I found two real control points rather than assuming none existed — .githooks/claude-pre-bash (already refuses dangerous bash, but sees only Claude Code Bash calls), and a reference-transaction hook (measured: it DOES fire on `refs/stash -> 0000...` for a clear, in the abortable phase — but a legitimate pop of the LAST entry is the identical transaction, so a naive guard breaks the recovery this fix recommends). Both are larger than this bead. The bead flags to agent-a that his destruction-vs-delay argument for raising this one may reprice that one too.
close_reason: Merged as e85114491415e71ff88b8c37ecb6271ad85824df (PR #1844, squash). Step 5 in CLAUDE.md:65 and AGENTS.md:175 no longer instructs an unconditional stash clear — both now refuse it and name the shared namespace as the reason — and CLAUDE.md carries a new 'The shared stash namespace' section with the measurement, the commit-to-your-own-branch remedy, and the drop-by-index rule. Verified on origin/master, not on the branch. The 'prune remote branches' half was measured and KEPT: all 16 refs it would drop were merged PR head branches, and the new prose records that --is-ancestor calls all 16 unmerged because a squash merge leaves no branch tip. Residual (no mechanical guard, only prose) filed as gqlc-753g3, P3, related.

title: CI: gotoolchain cache never re-saves; roll the key per job+run
description: The actions/cache key in .github/actions/setup-go/action.yml (gotoolchain-OS-version-hash(go.sum)) only changes on go.sum/toolchain bumps. go.sum last changed 2026-07-12; the cache was created 2026-08-23 when the key prefix landed and has never been rewritten since — actions/cache@v4 skips save when the primary key restored ('Cache hit occurred on the primary key ... not saving cache', run 33230929053). So ~/.cache/go-build is a fossil: test binaries built from today's source never match the snapshot, and go test never prints (cached) in CI (verified: 0 cached packages post-#1600, test job 2m55s). Local control: second go test run of internal/codegen/neo4j prints (cached), so accumulation is all that's missing. Fix: rolling primary key with -github.job-github.run_id, per-job prefix restore-key, broad fallback — same pattern as the golangci analysis cache at ci.yml:97. github.job is needed because 5 CI jobs share one run_id and would race to save one key, with the fastest (poorest) cache winning.
notes: Merged as PR #1606. Steady-state measured on run 33231649490 (same SHA, restored run-1's test lineage): test job 3m1s -> 1m34s, lint 1m2s -> 29s. Compile artifacts now accumulate. Test-RESULT caching remains broken on CI for testdata-reading packages: fresh-checkout mtimes enter the test cache key (probed: touch alone forces re-run). That half is gqlc-84y6.
close_reason: Closed

title: adr 0034: §2's identifier inventory omits nonReservedWords, and §3.3's REGULAR_IDENTIFIER-only segment rule would refuse the ADR's own 'Source' fixtures
description:
CLAIM (ADR 0034 §2, sworn as read-not-recalled): "Every name in these
productions is `identifier`, which admits both `REGULAR_IDENTIFIER` (Unicode
ID_Start then ID_Continue*, GQL.g4:3591-3620 — never a `/`, a `.`, or empty)
and the two delimited spellings."

FALSIFIED against the tree at 3bfa8c1c:
- internal/grammar/gql/GQL.g4:2956-2960: `identifier : regularIdentifier |
  DOUBLE_QUOTED_CHARACTER_SEQUENCE | ACCENT_QUOTED_CHARACTER_SEQUENCE`.
- regularIdentifier (GQL.g4, just above identifier) is `REGULAR_IDENTIFIER |
  nonReservedWords` — a THIRD class the inventory omits: 47 keyword tokens
  (ACYCLIC … ZONE), among them SOURCE, NODE, EDGE, GRAPH, TYPE, TABLE, TO.
- GQL.g4:3 — `options { caseInsensitive = true; }` — so these match in any
  case. `Source` is the SOURCE token, not a REGULAR_IDENTIFIER.

CONSEQUENCE, internal to the ADR: §3.3 prescribes "Restricting segments to
REGULAR_IDENTIFIER makes 'every segment is one safe path element' a property
of the lexer, with no validation code to get wrong." Implemented literally
(token type == REGULAR_IDENTIFIER), the ADR's own planned-resolving rows go
red: copy_of_graph_type_bare.gql is `COPY OF Source` (§5.2 row 3, resolves)
and copy_of_source.gql is `COPY OF /schemas/base/Source` (§5.2 row 1,
resolves) — each carries a SOURCE-keyword segment — plus planned fixture
17-references/Source.gql (§5.3). The corpus's declared-sentinel equality
catches the mis-step at implementation time (bounded blast radius; hence not
P1), but the merged doc actively misdirects the gqlc-h9n.1 implementer, and
gqlc-h9n.1 is the next work this ADR unblocks.

THE DESIGN DECISION SURVIVES: all 47 nonReservedWords are ASCII letter
sequences — no `/`, no `.`, never empty — so "every segment is one safe path
element" still holds. Only the inventory and the stated mechanism are wrong.

FIX DIRECTION (doc amendment, no code exists yet): restate §2's inventory as
REGULAR_IDENTIFIER | nonReservedWords | two delimited spellings; restate
§3.3's rule as "segments are the regularIdentifier production (either token
class is a lexer-guaranteed safe path element); only delimited spellings are
refused (ErrDelimitedReferenceSegment)". Optionally note GetText() preserves
source bytes under caseInsensitive lexing, so §3.2's byte-exact lookup is
unaffected (`COPY OF SOURCE` looks up SOURCE.gql, not Source.gql).

FALSIFIERS THE FIX OWES:
1. Amended §2 names nonReservedWords with its GQL.g4 line; grep of the rule
   confirms the three-way split.
2. The gqlc-h9n.1 implementation's segment guard accepts a nonReservedWords
   segment: the existing `COPY OF Source` rows resolving is the witness —
   plus one loader unit-test segment spelled in the wrong case or as another
   keyword (e.g. a fixture named after NODE) if the implementer wants the
   trap pinned independently of fixture-name luck.
3. `COPY OF "gt"` still lowers to ErrReferenceDelimitedSegment — the
   delimited refusal must not widen to swallow keyword segments.
notes:
Correction to falsifier 3 of the description: the sentinel name is ErrDelimitedReferenceSegment (as ADR 0034 §3.3 spells it), not ErrReferenceDelimitedSegment. The falsifier is otherwise unchanged.

title: codegen: witness the Tx behavioural guards without Docker, with a pgx.Tx fake
description:
Four of the Tx object's behavioural guards are witnessed only by the live
battery, which needs Docker. This agent has none, so they shipped UNMEASURED
against mutation:

  1. the done flag — a second Commit returns ErrTxDone
  2. Rollback after Commit returns nil, not an error
  3. neo4j: Begin on a transaction-bound Queries is refused
  4. AGE: the pgx.Tx check stands AHEAD of the capability assertion
     (pgx.Tx has a Begin of its own, for savepoints, so the capability
     assertion alone would be satisfied and hand a nested one back —
     only the ordering produces the refusal)

Three of those four are pure generated logic: they never reach the driver.
A fake witnesses them BETTER than a live database does, because a fake can
witness "and did not reach the driver", which a database cannot — a live run
sees a refusal and cannot tell a guard that returned early from one that
asked the server and was told no.

WHY THIS IS AVAILABLE. `pgx.Tx` (v5.10.0, tx.go:122) is a fully exported
interface — thirteen methods, none unexported. A fake in the test tree can
implement it. `Conn() *pgx.Conn` returns a concrete type, but a fake may
return nil for it as long as no guard under test calls it; verify that
before relying on it.

The sentinel-taxonomy spec's stated reason for excluding stub tests is that
the v5 driver's `ExplicitTransaction` carries an unexported `legacy()`
method. That reason is about the REAL neo4j driver and does not transfer to
pgx, nor to a fake standing in for either.

SCOPE. New justfile/CI machinery, so it was kept off gqlc-3d0l's diff rather
than smuggled in. Row 4 (ordering) is the one worth the most: it is the only
guard whose defect is an ordering, and ordering defects are invisible to a
test that only asks whether the refusal happened.
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED, 2026-08-24, by measurement, before this bead was ever
worked. I filed this saying the four rows could not be measured from an agent
with no Docker. That was wrong, and I should have checked before writing it.

.github/workflows/codegen-live.yml carries workflow_dispatch, and its `age`
job is gated only on `github.event_name != 'pull_request'` — so a dispatch on
ANY branch runs BOTH arms with Docker on the runner. CI is the Docker host.

MEASURED (mutation M1, branch mutation/tx-liveness, run 32691410054): mutating
one live scenario's expectation (Bob -> Carol in txCommitVisible) turned all
three arms RED with the victim named per arm —
  TestLiveSmoke/neo4j-go-v5/tx:_commit_is_visible_outside
  TestLiveSmoke/neo4j-go-v6/tx:_commit_is_visible_outside
  TestLiveSmoke/apache-age-pgx-v5/tx:_commit_is_visible_outside
That row was run for a second reason worth recording on its own: a green live
job is not evidence that a new scenario RAN. `just test-codegen-live-neo4j` is
not verbose, so the PR's green live-smoke would have looked identical had my
six scenarios never executed. M1 is the blinding pass that says they do.

SO WHAT REMAINS OF THIS BEAD. Not "the rows cannot be measured" — they can and
are being measured on scratch branches now. What remains is the argument that
survives: a fake is FAST and OFFLINE where a router costs ~10 minutes and
gates nothing, and a fake can witness "and did not reach the driver", which a
live database still cannot. Row 4 (the AGE ordering) keeps its place as the
most valuable, for the same reason as before: it is the only guard whose
defect is an ORDERING, and an ordering defect is invisible to a test that only
asks whether the refusal happened.

Re-price accordingly: this is an ergonomics-and-precision bead, not an
unblock-the-unmeasurable one.
close_reason:
Filed on a false premise, by me, without checking it.

The bead said the Tx behavioural guards were "Docker-only and this agent has no
Docker", and proposed a pgx.Tx fake as the way around that. There was nothing
to get around. .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml is `on: pull_request,
workflow_dispatch, schedule`, and live-smoke-age is gated only on
`github.event_name != 'pull_request'` -- so `gh workflow run codegen-live.yml
--ref <branch>` runs BOTH live arms on any branch, with no local Docker.

All four rows are now measured that way (bd gqlc-3d0l carries the battery, and
docs/specs/codegen-tx-object.md section 8 the table): done flag KILLED on both
neo4j arms; Rollback done-guard KILLED on AGE and SURVIVED on neo4j, with its
reason recorded; AGE Begin refusal KILLED offline on its message and KILLED
live on its condition; the neo4j Begin refusal not mutable without a
nil-interface panic, and witnessed instead by a blinding row that proves the
scenario executes.

The pgx.Tx-fake idea is not thereby wrong -- a fake could still witness
"without reaching the driver", which a live database cannot. But that is a
different and much smaller claim than this bead was opened for, and nobody
should inherit it dressed as a Docker workaround. If it is wanted, it wants a
fresh bead stating that narrower purpose.

title: AGE admits zoned TIME property columns via the offset sidecar
notes:
DESIGN (agent-h, gqlc-49hu). Rationale: docs/adr/0033-driver-neutral-temporal-carriers.md; vocabulary: CONTEXT.md "Neutral temporal carrier". Blocked on gqlc-mv3r (non-zoned admission) — its encode/decode helper family and fixture pattern are the template here.

GOAL. AGE admits zoned TIME property columns. The design question gqlc-49hu asked — does the flat offset sidecar suffice for neutral zoned TIME? — is answered YES and the reasoning is in ADR 0033: the carrier Time is exactly (clock reading, offset seconds), and the sidecar mechanism is exactly (count, offset property), so nothing needs inventing.

ENCODING (settled, gqlc-35yu.11): TIME → int64 microseconds since midnight, UTC-NORMALISED, in [0, 86400000000), plus a flat sidecar property <field>Offset holding offset-seconds. UTC normalisation means the stored count is the clock reading minus the offset, wrapped into the interval — so storage order IS instant order, which is the gate (ORDERING). Decode reconstructs the local clock reading by adding the offset back before filling Time{Hour,Minute,Second,Nanosecond,OffsetSeconds}.

FILES.
1. internal/codegen/age/types.go — Property() admits TypeTime → "Time". Comment sweep as in gqlc-mv3r.
2. internal/codegen/age/errors.go:119-157 — rejectOffsetSidecarCollisions already keys on the offsetSidecar(f) predicate (gqlc-x5dq landed this exactly so zoned TIME extends via ONE arm): add TypeTime to that predicate. Verify the collision fixture family (sidecar_test.go) covers a TIME field colliding with a user property named <field>Offset — if it only pins the TIMESTAMP arm, add the TIME row; the guard must be witnessed per width, not assumed to generalise.
3. internal/codegen/age/render_models.go — encode: UTC-normalise (clock micros − OffsetSeconds*1e6, wrapped mod 86400e6 into [0, 86400e6)), write count + sidecar. Decode: bounds-check BOTH properties — the count against the interval, the offset with the same bound agtypeZone already applies (|offset| < 24h; reuse agtypeZone or its bound verbatim — one policy, not two). Reconstruct clock reading = (count + OffsetSeconds*1e6) wrapped back. Sub-microsecond truncation as everywhere.
4. Fixtures: property_time gains "apache-age-pgx-v5" in manifest targets; regenerate. Dual enrolment puts it under TestBackendInvariantSurface. Retire/repoint any invalid fixture pinning "AGE refuses TIME" deliberately, listed in the PR body.
5. Live battery: flip the AGE arm's zonedTime column to true. The scenario (landed by gqlc-oz6p on the neo4j arms) must assert on AGE: (a) round-trip preserves BOTH the clock reading and the offset; (b) ORDER BY sorts by instant, not by local clock — two rows with different offsets whose local readings order opposite to their instants are the probe (e.g. 23:00+02:00 vs 22:30+00:00: instant order 21:00Z < 22:30Z, local order reversed). If the gqlc-oz6p scenario lacks that adversarial pair, add it — a same-offset-only round-trip cannot falsify the normalisation. TestAGEOffsetSidecar is already in test-codegen-live-age's -run list if you extend that top-level test instead; anything NEW at top level must be enrolled BY NAME in justfile:2358.
6. Specs c2/c3 prose + spec fence, as before.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGES + PROOF. (a) TIME generates for AGE with surface identical to neo4j — dual-enrolled invariant gate. (b) Instant ordering across offsets — the adversarial live probe above. (c) Wrap-around correctness — unit rows where normalisation crosses midnight in both directions (23:30+02:00 → 21:30 count; 00:30−02:00 → 22:30 count next-day wrap), plus both interval edges and one-outside rows for count and offset.

RISKS + MUTATION DUTY. The wrap arithmetic is the sharp edge; Go's % is truncated (sign-following), so a naive mod of a negative normalised count stays negative — pin the negative-wrap row first. New guards (interval, offset bound, sidecar collision arm) owe the mutation battery with per-row expected verdicts declared before running; blind the normalisation (drop the offset subtraction) and require the ordering probe to be the row that kills it.

SESSION 2026-08-29 (agent-g). PR #1797, branch feat/gqlc-oeqi-age-zoned-time, pushed, all local gates green at the tip.

DESIGN DEVIATION, step 5. Steps 3 and 5 both require the emission to WRITE a <field>Offset sidecar; ADR 0005 forbids it (placeholders stay verbatim, one bound value per placeholder, so gqlc cannot add a property to an author's CREATE). Verified by content and not by reading: "Offset" occurs on the decode path only in every apache-age golden, and live_age_zone_test.go's header says the same for TIMESTAMP. So zonedTime: true is NOT flippable -- zonedTimeScenarios requires +05:45 and -08:00 to survive a round trip (live_test.go:1544) and AGE returns OffsetSeconds 0. Built the AGE-only witness gqlc-vs9i already established for TIMESTAMP. agent-h mailed so the design's ENCODING paragraph is corrected at the source.

MUTATION BATTERY: 10 mutants, expected killers declared per row BEFORE running, 10/10 killed by exactly the declared rows. Classifier proved with two controls -- C1 (a word in an emitted comment) SURVIVED, C2 (emitted helper stops parsing) BUILD, so the fake RED is not counted as coverage.

TWO FINDINGS from the declared-vs-measured contrast, neither visible in a pass count:
 - T3 (encode adds the offset instead of subtracting) is NOT killed by the ordering test. The design asked ordering to be the row that catches a blinded normalisation; it catches T4 and not T3. The wire-count table is what catches T3.
 - T4 (symmetric blinding, both directions) IS killed by the round-trip table, because the table pins the STORED count on the wire rather than only round-tripping. A round-trip-only test would have been blind to it. Strengthening beyond what the design anticipated.

STEP 6: c2/c3 needed nothing, confirming agent-b's measurement on gqlc-mv3r -- neither spec names AGE. The prose that WAS falsified is codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md's "Zoned TIME is still refused there"; corrected to LocalDateTime, which is the carrier nothing on this target reaches (no LOCALDATETIME property width in internal/graph at all, and typeMap.Temporal refuses every expression kind) and temporal.go declares anyway.

A CLEAN REBASE THAT DID NOT BUILD. #1735 landed mid-branch, moving query methods onto an unexported `queries` that Queries embeds. It rewrote every corpus row and golden on master and could not rewrite the two rows and two golden trees that existed only here. No conflict marker; the tell was a compile error raised from INSIDE a test (promoted fields in a struct literal, refused before go1.27). Commits 1-3 of 4 do not build on their own as a result; the tip does. Disclosed in the PR body.

ALSO FIXED: 1e97d59f failed `just lint` on its own (regexp.MustCompile inside require.NotRegexp, testifylint). Repaired in its own commit and the guard re-mutated afterwards -- dropping agtypeTimeZone from zoningHelpers still turns TestTheDecodeAndTheGateReadTheSameSidecarKeys red, so the string form sees the same text.

LIVE WITNESS IS RUN, and it took a manual dispatch to make it so. live-smoke-age has `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` -- nightly and manual only, by design (bd gqlc-35yu.8), and GitHub counts a skipped check as satisfying a required context. So this PR's gates went all-green while its only live witness had never executed. Dispatched on the branch: run 33268834545, green.

Read the LOG and not the conclusion, per the standing rule that a green live run witnesses nothing unless a scenario reaches the new code path. All three bodies and all fifteen rows show --- PASS against a real AGE 1.7.0 container, including the two that carry the claim: `a_full_day_ahead_is_refused,_naming_the_property` and `stored_readings_sort_by_instant`.
DESIGN CORRECTION (agent-h, 2026-08-29), superseding two claims in the DESIGN note above — named per the standing rule that an appended correction retracts nothing it does not name.

SUPERSEDED CLAIM 1, step 3: 'encode: UTC-normalise ..., write count + sidecar.' The emission writes the COUNT ONLY. ADR 0005 leaves the author's $name placeholders verbatim and binds one value per placeholder, so gqlc has no seam through which to add a <field>Offset property to an author's CREATE. The sidecar is a READ affordance: agtypeZone reads a property some other writer put in the graph. Verified against tree content: 'Offset' occurs on the decode path only in every apache-age golden (e.g. test/data/codegen/valid/timestamp_property_roundtrip/golden/apache-age-pgx-v5/models.go:41,50 — both agtypeZone reads), and live_age_zone_test.go's header states it for TIMESTAMP: 'gqlc derives no sidecar to bind, by design.'

SUPERSEDED CLAIM 2, step 5(a): 'flip the AGE arm's zonedTime column to true ... (a) round-trip preserves BOTH the clock reading and the offset.' Not flippable: zonedSlots (live_test.go) carries OffsetSeconds +05:45 and -08:00 and AGE returns OffsetSeconds 0 by construction, since no sidecar was ever written. 5(b) — ORDER BY answers by instant — stands unchanged and is the actual gate.

CORRECTED STEP 5: the gqlc-vs9i arrangement, which agent-g built: AGE arm zonedTime stays false; an AGE-only live test beside live_age_zone_test.go, enrolled by name, asserts (i) gqlc round trip preserves the instant, returning UTC-normalised with OffsetSeconds 0 — the truthful claim, still red under a dropped normalisation; (ii) a driver-seeded sidecar survives the emitted decode; (iii) the adversarial ordering pair drives ORDER BY and a range predicate through generated code in instant order.

WHY THE DESIGN ERRED, for the next reader: I read the settled ENCODING (gqlc-35yu.11, 'count + sidecar property') as a write-path duty, when it is a storage FORMAT — the format any writer uses, of which gqlc's own emission writes only the half it can reach under ADR 0005. The falsifier existed in the tree the whole time (the TIMESTAMP goldens) and I did not run it against my own step 3.
