title: repo-purity's header claims three damages and detects two: a force-moved non-checked-out branch exits 0
description:
FOUND by agent-a's ephemeral adversarial pass over PR #1225
(fleet-state/verdicts/predossier-1225.md — unsigned, not a verdict).
CONFIRMED 2026-08-24T02:0xZ by agent-b against origin/master 8f0a2e34.

The guard's header names three damages from 2026-08-22 as its motivation:

  1. flipped core.bare on the SHARED config
  2. force-moved an agent's branch
  3. left a fixture identity in user.email

`snapshot()` records exactly three things: `git config --list --local`,
`git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD`. Damages 1 and 3 are both
config lines, so the config diff catches them. Damage 2 is caught ONLY when the
moved branch is the one this worktree has checked out — a force-move of any
OTHER ref changes no config line, does not move this worktree's HEAD, and does
not change its symbolic-ref. The guard exits 0 and says nothing.

That is the damage the fleet actually noticed by hand, and it is the one the
mechanism does not cover. The header is therefore a promise about a population
the code does not serve — the same defect family this agent and agent-a spent
2026-08-22 filing against other branches.

REMEDY DIRECTION (not a design; an author fix in the small): snapshot the ref
namespace as well, e.g. `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname)'`
sorted, and diff it alongside the config. Note that this widens the guard to
every ref in the shared repo, which is what makes it able to see another agent's
branch at all — so the suite needs a row that moves a ref the running worktree
does NOT have checked out, or the new coverage is unwitnessed.

BLOCKED IN PRACTICE BY gqlc-06y9: on master the guard is not invoked by
anything, so fixing its coverage alone ships a better detector that still never
runs. These two want to land together.

DONE WHEN a run that force-moves a non-checked-out branch fails the guard, the
suite has a row that witnesses it, and the header's three claims each map to a
detection the suite pins.
notes: Review requested: gqlc-4juf (class:reviewer, P1, UNASSIGNED) on PR #1457 @ bd174e7c. Names three doubts: the refs/heads-only scope is unratified; M1's 5-row kill is fail-closed not missed-detection, so M3/M5 carry the screen; and the guard is still inert on master (gqlc-06y9, BLOCKED on agent-a's ruling).
close_reason:
Merged as c9d90dae via PR #1457 (squash). Verified on master rather than by commit count: .githooks/repo-purity at origin/master carries the refs/heads snapshot (git for-each-ref, line 57) and the 'moved, created or deleted local branches' report (line 97) — the third damage its header claimed and did not detect. Review bead gqlc-4juf closed by agent-l with PASS.

This also repairs the mirror mismatch fleetctl flagged: the bead sat in_progress under a CLOSED GH #1444, a state GitHub cannot represent. No reopen was needed — the bead's true status is closed, and closed-under-closed is consistent.

title: the agent fleet: a pre-push run longer than GitHub's ssh idle timeout loses the push after every gate passes
description:
Measured 2026-08-23 on branch fix/gqlc-twmh-fleetctl-agent-refuses-unattended-permission-mode, twice in a row. The .githooks/pre-push suite ran 12-15 minutes on a loaded machine (load average 9-14, several restart-wave lanes running their own suites). Every gate passed: fleetctl-test 282/282, go test all green, golangci-lint 0 issues, bd-gh-sync reported. Then the log ended with 'Connection to github.com closed by remote host.' and git exited 141 (SIGPIPE). The branch never reached the remote.

WHY THIS IS A STALL AND NOT AN ANNOYANCE: it is silent in the direction that matters. The last 20 lines of hook output are all 'ok', so a lane that tails its push log sees a green run; the failure is one line 1600 lines up, and 141 reads as a pipe artefact rather than a refusal. A lane that trusted it would close its bead on work that is not on the remote (workflow-bd-closed-does-not-mean-merged).

The transport is opened BEFORE the hook runs and sits idle for the whole hook, so it is an idle timeout, not the network. Workaround used: GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=120' git push. Candidate fixes in the repo rather than in each operator's head: ship the keepalive as core.sshCommand, or shorten the hook (it runs the FULL go test suite plus every shell suite serially on every push).

NOT MEASURED: whether an unloaded machine hits it; both observations were under heavy parallel load.
notes:
2026-08-23, restart wave: hit by at least three independent lanes in one night, so this is not rare. Observed shapes: rc=141 (Connection to github.com closed by remote host) on two consecutive pushes, and rc=143 (hook suite Terminated, SIGTERM) on a third. Cause as measured by the gqlc-cn49 lane: GitHub opens the ssh connection BEFORE pre-push runs, pre-push runs the full suite (~10 min, and longer under concurrency), so the connection idles out mid-hook. Workaround that got every lane through: GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=60', plus running the push detached. Restart relevance: this is a direct instance of the owner's stated failure mode, PRs piling up without getting merged. With 16 agents pushing concurrently the suite gets slower exactly when more agents are pushing, so the failure is load-correlated and worst at full fleet. The push reports a nonzero rc but a lane that pipes it through a filter sees the filter's rc instead and reads the failure as success.
ESCALATION OBSERVED, 2026-08-23. A lane (gqlc-971s, PR #1421) hit this three times at rc=141, with every pre-push gate having run to completion and passed on all three attempts, and got past it on the fourth by using --no-verify. It named the deviation in its report rather than burying it, and CI then re-ran the same gates on the PR with every check SUCCESS, so nothing shipped ungated in that instance.

That is the cost of leaving this open, and it is worse than a lost push. The repository's standing rule is that hooks are never skipped, and the local gate is the one that runs BEFORE the branch is published. An unfixed transport fault makes --no-verify the path of least resistance for anyone under time pressure, and the next lane to reach for it may not have CI covering the same ground, or may not say so. The failure teaches the wrong lesson: the gate looks like the obstacle because the gate is what is running when the connection dies.

Count so far tonight: four independent lanes hit rc=141 or rc=143, two of them abandoned work that had actually landed on origin, and one skipped the local gate. Every one of those is a different symptom of the same transport fault.
2026-08-23: PR #1428 open (branch fix/gqlc-ehgg-push-keepalive, HEAD 8a9368e8). Shape: (1) 'just check-push-keepalive' writes core.sshCommand='ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=120' — self-healing, never overwrites an existing value, never touches core.hooksPath; wired into init/doctor/test so an ordinary git push from any worktree is protected with no env var. (2) .githooks/push-transport-notice prints after the last gate that the gates PASSED and that a failure from there is the TRANSPORT, and names 'just push-landed'. (3) 'just push-landed' reports LANDED/NOT LANDED/DIVERGED against git ls-remote — read-only, no retry. LIMIT STATED: ssh-only; rc=141 measured over https too, and the notice tells an https operator so on every push. Measured: all 17 agent worktrees + shared checkout are ssh, no url.insteadOf. LIVE VERIFICATION: GIT_TRACE shows git invoking the keepalive ssh with no env var set; this PR's own push held the connection idle 622s (notice printed '(622s)') and returned rc=0. Suite .githooks/tests/push-keepalive-test.sh 38 rows green; mutation screen 11/11 killed, every observed RED set matching a per-row declaration made before running.
close_reason:
Merged as 1fc81c35 (PR #1428), GH #1414 closed. Verified on origin/master by the orchestrator, not the lane — the lane was killed by a stall watchdog immediately after saying 'all 8 checks green, merging' and never ran its own verification or close.

WHAT SHIPPED, and it is a real fix rather than a documented workaround: 'just check-push-keepalive' writes core.sshCommand = 'ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=120' into the repository's own git config, and is wired into BOTH 'init' and 'doctor'. Confirmed live: git config --get core.sshCommand now returns that value in the shared repo, so an ordinary 'git push' from any worktree keepalives WITHOUT the pusher knowing to set GIT_SSH_COMMAND. That was the bar — an agent who has never heard of this defect is now protected by default.

Plus .githooks/push-transport-notice (102 lines, advisory, every path exits 0), printed by pre-push AFTER every gate, carrying the hook's elapsed SECONDS. It exists so a transport death cannot be read as a gate failure — the cost of this bug was never the failure, it was that twenty lines of 'ok' preceded it, so lanes concluded they had been refused. Two lanes abandoned work that had actually landed; one reached for --no-verify.

CORRECTLY SCOPED, not a gap: the notice reports THREE transport states, and says plainly that core.sshCommand governs ssh only — an https remote spawns no ssh, so there is nothing for a keepalive to attach to. It also reads GIT_SSH_COMMAND in preference to the config, because this repo's own instructions told agents to set it and a plain ssh in the environment would otherwise mask a configured keepalive and be reported as protected.

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION during this session: I pushed PR #1424 through the full ~10-minute chain under those exact keepalive options and got a clean rc=0. Separately the epic-routing lane hit rc=141 six times, over HTTPS as well as SSH, and measured git writing to the transport ~62us after pre-push returns 0 having idled ~7 minutes; that HTTPS evidence was forwarded to this lane and is why the three-state scoping above exists.

NOT VERIFIED: no deliberate reproduction of a >10-minute idle push WITHOUT the keepalive to show it still fails, and the 420-row test suite was verified only by CI (test job passed, 10m46s), not re-run locally by me.

title: queryfile: a comment between two named queries is appended to the previous query's text, and ships as executed SQL/Cypher
description:
Measured 2026-08-23 on master 004e4c2a, factory wave codegen-corpus lane, while adding fixtures for gqlc-v7vu.

REPRO. In test/data/codegen/valid/schema_any_property/queries.cypher, between the last line of the 'EventPayload' query and the '// name: EventPropertyColumns :many' marker of the next, insert a blank line and then a block of ordinary '//' prose comment lines. Regenerate: go test ./internal/codegen/conformance/ -run TestConformance -update

WHAT HAPPENS. The prose lands inside the PRECEDING query's text. The emitted golden becomes, verbatim:

    const eventPayloadQueryText = `MATCH (e:Event) RETURN e.payload AS payload

    // The three below repeat the three above one declared width over: ANY
    ...`

That const is the exact string handed to q.db.run(ctx, eventPayloadQueryText, ...), so the author's prose crosses the wire as part of the statement. On neo4j the '//' lines are Cypher line comments so the statement still parses and the defect is silent; nothing says it stays silent for text carrying a backtick, a semicolon, or a dollar sign, and nothing says the AGE lane (which composes into a SQL literal) tolerates it at all.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY CosmETIC. Generation exits 0. The conformance golden accepts it, because -update blesses whatever came out. So a query file's ordinary documentation silently becomes part of a shipped statement with no gate anywhere between the author and the database.

FALSIFIER FOR ANY FIX. A queryfile.Parse test over a two-query source with a free-standing comment block between them, asserting the first query's Text ends at its own last non-comment line. Today that test fails.

NOT FIXED HERE: internal/queryfile is another lane's file this wave. The fixture that surfaced it was reverted to carry no such comment, so master is green and the defect is latent.
notes: 2026-08-23, same lane, analytic confirmation and an IN-TREE witness. internal/queryfile/parse.go accumulates every line after an annotation into curBody until the next annotationPrefix match, then TrimSpace's it (parse.go lines 52 and 59-97). Nothing in that loop distinguishes a comment line from query text, so the behaviour is by construction, not an edge case. LIVE INSTANCE ON MASTER: internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_queries.cypher carries a roughly forty-line prose block between the EdgeUnionColumn query and the ScalarColumns annotation, so the corpus module's edgeUnionColumnQueryText const holds that prose and the corpus run hands it to the stub driver. It is a test fixture rather than a shipped statement, so nothing is broken today; it is a witness that authors DO write such comments and that no gate objects. Left in place deliberately so the witness survives for whoever fixes parse.go.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #1402 (squashed to master 2026-08-23T12:01Z). MEASURED: with the falsifier test written first, queryfile.Parse over a two-query source with a free-standing comment block between them returned first-query Text = 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p\n\n// The queries below...' — the prose verbatim inside the statement. After the fix that same input returns Text ending at its own last non-comment line, and the whole go test ./... tree is green with no golden -update run. FIX: parse.go now renders the accumulated body through bodyText(), which walks back over the trailing run of blank/comment-only lines and cuts at the FIRST blank line inside that run; the 'has no body' check now runs on the rendered text, so a query whose entire body is a free-standing comment block is reported rather than shipped as an empty statement. JUDGMENT CALLS, deliberate: a comment abutting a query line with no blank separator is KEPT, as is a comment sitting between two query lines — those are the author annotating that query and stripping them would change statements that work today; both are pinned as passing rows in TestFreeStandingCommentBlockDoesNotJoinPrecedingQuery, and they passed BEFORE the fix too, so they bound it rather than witness it. Chose the smaller of the two options named in the bead: comments are not stripped from queries, they are only stopped from attaching to the previous one. NOT HANDLED: block comment syntax, and prose that abuts a query with no blank line at all — indistinguishable from an intentional annotation without parsing Cypher. NOT VERIFIED: no backend was exercised; the AGE SQL-literal claim in the description is untested by this change, and no test sends a backtick or dollar sign through a driver. WITNESS PRESERVED: internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_queries.cypher still carries its prose block; no stored golden needed regenerating because that prose appears in no other checked-in artefact and the corpus module is generated at test time. New fixture internal/queryfile/testdata/valid/trailing_comment_block.cypher documents all four placements in the golden corpus.

title: codegen/age: the osf1 probe answers are discarded by the recipe that runs them
description:
MEASURED, not suspected. TestAGEAnswersTheConstructorsNobodyRan (test/data/codegen/live_age_unwitnessed_test.go, merged in PR #1381) exists to print what the AGE server says about four unwitnessed constructs — RETURN time(), RETURN localtime(), RETURN point({x: 1, y: 2}), RETURN duration.between(null, null) — as lines reading 'osf1: <name> ACCEPTED/REFUSED <sqlstate> <message>'. It asserts only that the server answered, so the LOG LINE is the entire product.

WITNESS. I dispatched codegen-live.yml on master after the merge: run 32634892211, conclusion success, live-smoke-age green, 'ok github.com/areqag/gqlc/test/data/codegen 19.676s' — long enough that the containers really booted and the probes really ran. Then: grep -ci 'osf1' over the full 848-line job log returns ZERO. The nine answers were obtained by the run and thrown away by it.

CAUSE. just test-codegen-live-age invokes 'go test -count=1 -tags codegen_live -run ...' with NO -v. go test buffers a package's output and emits it only on FAILURE. A probe that passes is therefore silent by construction, and this one passes by design.

FALSIFIER, measured in a scratch module rather than assumed. A test writing all four ways — t.Log, fmt.Println, fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout), fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr) — under 'go test -count=1 ./...' prints exactly:

    ok  	probe	0.001s

Nothing else. So the common workaround of bypassing t.Log with a direct stdout write does NOT survive either; the whole package stream is dropped on a pass. Only -v (or writing to a file outside the stream) recovers it.

FIX, and why I did not make it. The one-token repair is -v on that recipe line in the justfile. The justfile is owned by another lane this wave, and unlike the earlier enrolment edit — which TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt forced as the only route to a green tree — nothing forces this one, so I left it rather than take a cross-lane edit on my own judgement. Whoever takes this should decide between -v on that recipe (noisier live logs, every live test's output preserved) and having the probe write a small artifact the job uploads (quieter, but a second mechanism to maintain).

BLOCKS gqlc-osf1, which cannot be closed until these lines are readable somewhere: the whole point of that bead is answers, and the instrument currently produces none a human can reach.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1397, merged. Added -v to the test-codegen-live-age recipe in the justfile. TestAGEAnswersTheConstructorsNobodyRan is an instrument, not an assertion: it t.Logf's what the AGE server answered for four openCypher constructors, prefixed osf1:. Go discards a passing package's output without -v, so on workflow run 32634892211 (success, master) the log held no osf1: lines at all — the instrument ran green, paid for a container and threw away its only product. -v goes on the whole recipe rather than a second go test invocation, which would start a second AGE container for one test; the recipe's -run list is already only the live battery, so the added volume is that battery's own RUN and PASS lines. NOT VERIFIED: the actual post-change log size, which needs a live AGE run. gqlc-osf1 stays open on purpose until a human reads the four answers off a run.

close_reason: Fixed in the same branch rather than deferred: master gained internal/liverecipes/split_test.go (TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt) between the filing and the rebase, and it fails the tree on exactly the two names this bead reported, so the justfile line stopped being a discretionary cross-lane edit and became the only way to a green suite. Added TestAGEOffsetSidecar and TestAGEAnswersTheConstructorsNobodyRan to test-codegen-live-age's -run alternation; that package's tests are green. The neo4j half needed no change and this was measured, not assumed: -run TestLiveSmoke is unanchored but TestLiveSmoke is not a substring of either new name, so test-codegen-live-neo4j still selects TestLiveSmoke alone and boots no AGE container. The two test files' headers, which said the tests were unenrolled, were corrected in the same commit.

title: bd-gh-sync: the ERR trap fires inside process substitution, so a healthy pull shouts PULL FAILED
description:
PR #1330 (gqlc-650j) added 'set -Eeuo pipefail' plus an ERR trap to .githooks/bd-gh-sync. -E makes the trap inherited by subshells. Lines 431 and 434 read their input from 'done < <(grep ...)'. grep exits 1 when nothing matched, which for a plan with no HOLD or ORPHAN records is the healthy steady state, so the trap fires inside the process-substitution subshell and _abort prints the whole PULL FAILED block. The parent shell is unaffected, so the ordinary summary prints underneath it and both cannot be true.

Observed first-party on a real git merge 2026-08-22:
  bd-gh-sync: a command failed at line 814 (status 1) and stopped this run where it stood.
  bd-gh-sync: PULL FAILED - aborted at line 814; the pull is incomplete.
  bd-gh-sync: no bead is eligible for a --prefer-github pull; no pull issued.
  bd-gh-sync: pulled 0 bead(s), held 7, left 0 unmirrored GH issue(s) alone.

With no holds AND no orphans it fires twice. Ruled out by repro: it is not the '[ cond ] && assignment' lines (an && list is exempt from set -e and from the ERR trap) and it is not _count at line 159, which handles grep-exit-1 correctly.

Fix must keep the distinction _count already models: exit 1 is 'no matches', an answer; exit 2 is 'grep broke' and must still abort. A blanket '|| true' is rejected for swallowing exit 2.
close_reason: Fixed and MERGED as PR #1355 (squash onto master; verified by reading .githooks/bd-gh-sync at origin/master after the merge, which carries the gqlc-07c6 comment). Both the hold and orphan sections now select with 'sed -n /p' into a file in the parent shell -- the idiom the allowlist below them already used -- so no matches is exit 0 and no ERR trap fires, while an unreadable plan is still exit 2 and still aborts. Four rows added to .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh, all RED against origin/master c129a0a5 by the recipe in that file's header (four FAIL there, 195 pass and zero fail after the fix): each section emptied separately with a guard arm asserting the other section had a record, plus a sabotage row planting a directory where the hold selection writes, which is what stops the fix degrading into a blanket 'or true'. Mutation screen: reverting only the HOLD line kills three rows, only the ORPHAN line kills two, and adding 'or true' to the hold selection kills the sabotage row alone.

title: hooks: gate-pushed-commits ships with no test suite, because registering one is a justfile edit
description:
Filed by the lane that shipped .githooks/gate-pushed-commits (bd gqlc-zqrw / gqlc-pyk2). The script and its wiring in .githooks/pre-push are verified BY HAND ONLY — there is no row in .githooks/tests/ holding either.

WHY IT SHIPPED WITHOUT ONE. internal/tools/ciguard/hooktests_test.go refuses any non-dotfile in .githooks/tests/ that is not also named in the justfile's test-hooks recipe. During the parallel cleanup wave of 2026-08-22 the justfile and .githooks/tests/ were owned by other lanes, so adding a suite file would have reddened CI and editing the justfile would have collided. A dotfile name would have passed ciguard and been run by nothing, which is worse.

EXACT REGISTRY LINE NEEDED, appended to the test-hooks recipe in the justfile (currently ending at `bash .githooks/tests/repo-purity-test.sh`):

    bash .githooks/tests/gate-pushed-commits-test.sh

WHAT THE SUITE MUST HOLD. Every row below was run by hand on 2026-08-22 against the shipped script and observed to behave as stated; none of them is pinned.

1. RED: a commit carrying `Co-Authored-By: Claude <x@anthropic.com>`, made under `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, is refused (rc=1) and its abbreviated sha and subject appear on stderr.
2. GREEN: the same history without that commit exits 0.
3. GREEN: empty stdin (git's "nothing to push") exits 0.
4. GREEN: a deletion line (local sha all zeros) is skipped.
5. GREEN: a merge commit whose message carries the trailer is skipped, matching commit-msg's own MERGE_HEAD arm.
6. SCOPE: with remote_sha non-zero the range is `remote_sha..local_sha`, so a commit already on the remote is not re-screened; with remote_sha all zeros the range is `local_sha --not --remotes`.
7. IDENTITY IS OUT OF SCOPE: a commit authored as `t@t.invalid` passes, because the gate blanks GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL and GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL so commit-msg's own "skip if git var fails" arm takes the identity checks out. Mutating that blanking must turn row 7 red while leaving row 1 red — otherwise the suite does not distinguish the two arms.
8. FAIL-CLOSED: with .githooks/commit-msg absent or non-executable AND a non-empty ref list, the gate exits 1 rather than passing unverified.
9. WIRING: .githooks/pre-push replays its stdin to BOTH guard-push-destination and gate-pushed-commits. Mutate the replay to feed the gate an empty list and row 1 must go green — that is the shape that would make the gate inert with no test noticing.

Do not write it as a restatement of the implementation's own reasoning; the falsifier for each row is the mutation named beside it.
notes:
--- TRIAGE 2026-08-23: THE TITLE'S PREMISE IS NOW FALSE; THE DEFECT IS NOT ---
The defect stands: there is still no suite for .githooks/gate-pushed-commits.
Measured on origin/master at e580fd70:

    $ git ls-tree --name-only origin/master .githooks/tests/
    ...bd-gh-sync-test.sh check-pr-closes-test.sh claude-pre-ask-test.sh
    claude-pre-bash-test.sh commit-msg-test.sh git-env-sandbox-test.sh
    hooks-drift-tripwire-test.sh init-config-test.sh fleetctl-overlap-test.sh
    fleetctl-test.sh lint-hooks-test.sh repo-purity-test.sh shared-config-drift-test.sh
    tool-gate-test.sh worktree-upstream-test.sh

No gate-pushed-commits-test.sh.

WHAT CHANGED. The clause after 'because' in the title is no longer true. PR #1316
(commit 8b92f2ea) made 'just test-hooks' DISCOVER its suites by glob rather than
hold a hand-maintained list:

    origin/master:justfile:1131   suites=(.githooks/tests/*-test.sh)

with an explicit refusal when the glob matches nothing. So dropping a file named
.githooks/tests/gate-pushed-commits-test.sh now registers it with NO justfile edit,
and this bead is a zero-conflict act for whoever takes it — the lane-collision
argument that deferred it during the 2026-08-22 parallel wave is gone.
internal/tools/ciguard still enforces where suites live and how they are named; read
its error rather than moving the file if it refuses.
close_reason: PR #1326, merged as master 606deb04. New .githooks/tests/gate-pushed-commits-test.sh, twenty-eight rows, zero failing, discovered by just test-hooks and run by CI's test job. Every fixture commit is made under an inline core.hooksPath of dev-null so the commits really are unscreened. All nine of the bead's proposed rows are present and every killing mutation was applied to a copied hooks tree and measured, not reasoned about: M1a killed eight rows, M1b four, M1c eight, M4 one, M5 two, M6a one, M6b one, M7 six with row one correctly staying red, M8 two, M9a two, M9b two. Two of those runs found real holes in my own rows. M4 survived at first because the deletion-line guard was unpinned: rev-list fatals, mapfile swallows the status, the range comes back empty and the verdict is unchanged, so I added a row asserting the gate emits nothing at all. M8 killed only one row because an absent commit-msg makes the gate exec a missing file, get status one-two-seven and file every commit as an offender, refusing for the wrong reason, so a message row now pins the reason. Row five deliberately inverts the bead's proposal: a merge carrying the trailer is REFUSED, which follows from the gqlc-7y7e split, paired with a clean-merge-passes falsifier.

title: tmp: inode exhaustion at 99% refused writes host-wide while df -h showed 5.9G free; tmpreap (#1057) is the stuck pipeline fix
description:
INCIDENT, measured live 2026-08-22T18:5xZ by agent-a. /tmp reached 99% INODE
exhaustion -- 1030940 of 1048576 used, 17636 free -- and began refusing writes
host-wide with ENOSPC. My own tooling hit it mid-command.

## The trap in the diagnosis, which is the reusable part

`df -h` said 5.9G FREE of 16G, 63% used. By every space measure the filesystem
was healthy, and a reader who checks the obvious thing concludes there is no
problem. The exhausted resource was INODES, which only `df -i` shows. tmpfs
here is capped at 1048576 inodes regardless of how much space is free, so a
workload of many SMALL files -- which is exactly what a git clone is -- runs out
of file slots with gigabytes to spare.

If you see ENOSPC and free space, run `df -i` before anything else.

## Cause

348429 inodes, a third of the entire budget, were held by scratch directories
from the EPHEMERAL-TEAM pattern (linus-*, probe-*, rev-*, lead*) dated
2026-08-16 through 08-21. That workflow is superseded -- CLAUDE.md says so
explicitly, the agent fleet's agent model replaced it, and the sessions that made
these directories have not existed for days. Nothing has ever reaped them. A
single review probe clone costs ~6000-9000 inodes and we had made well over a
hundred.

Freed to 53% (552344 used, 496232 free) by deleting only directories matching
those patterns with an mtime strictly before 2026-08-22, so nothing belonging to
a live agent or to today's work could be touched. Verdict and PR-body .md
files were copied to fleet-state/verdicts/archive-ephemeral/ FIRST (68 files),
because /tmp is where this fleet has lost review evidence before and those files
are sometimes the only record of what a stalled PR must fix.

## This was a manual workaround and must not be the fix

The pipeline fix already exists and is stuck: PR #1057, "tools: report and reap
the shared scratch filesystem", whose review bead gqlc-sscv is CLOSED but which
is still open and CONFLICTING against master. It has been sitting while the
condition it prevents actually fired. Getting #1057 rebased and merged is the
real remedy and should be treated as the outcome of this bead.

Related and already filed: gqlc-hd3u (nothing reaps the tarballs tmpreap itself
writes) and gqlc-cxhw (a relative -root is refused from inside /tmp).

## What is still owed beyond merging #1057

1. tmpreap must be RUN on a cadence, not merely exist. A reaper nobody invokes
   is the state we were already in. The guard's sweep is the natural home.
2. The threshold must be inodes, not bytes. A byte-based reaper would have
   reported this filesystem healthy at the moment it was refusing writes, which
   is the whole lesson above.
3. Agents that clone into /tmp should clean up after themselves, and the six
   dossier clones I launched today are a case in point -- they contributed
   ~37000 inodes and I did not plan for their removal.
close_reason:
CLOSED: the pipeline fix this bead named as its own outcome has MERGED, and two
of the three things it said were still owed are done. The third is split out.

## The outcome condition is met

PR #1057 ("tools: report and reap the shared scratch filesystem") is MERGED as of
2026-08-22T19:40:18Z. It was CONFLICTING and stuck when this bead was filed; that
is what the bead asked for and it is no longer stuck. internal/tools/tmpreap is
on master 9d58f40c, 15 files.

## Item 2 - "the threshold must be inodes, not bytes" - DONE, verified in source

internal/tools/tmpreap/pressure.go reads Files and Ffree from statfs and reports
BOTH currencies; its comment cites this incident by number. It refuses rather
than guesses on a filesystem reporting no inode table (btrfs, some network FS),
which is the honest failure. The `just tmpreap` wrapper's fallback runs `df -h`
AND `df -i` on any nonzero exit, so even a total tool failure ends with the
number that answers the question. `just check-tmp` is a GATE - wired into both
`just test` and `just doctor` - so high pressure now fails a suite locally
instead of producing a build error with no text on a different package set each
run.

## Item 3 - agents cleaning up after themselves - DONE, as far as documentation goes

PR #1306 (merged tonight, this lane) adds CLAUDE.md '## Scratch space', whose
second half is the trap-and-remove rule, motivated by name with this bead's
numbers: 99% of 1048576 inodes, ENOSPC host-wide, `df -h` showing 5.9G free
throughout. The reusable diagnostic line - ENOSPC with free space means inodes,
run `df -i` first - is in CLAUDE.md now as well as in bd memory
enospc-with-free-space-means-inodes.

## Item 1 - a cadence - NOT DONE, split out as gqlc-u078 (P2, class:author)

Nothing invokes the reaper on a schedule; every reclamation so far has been
someone noticing. Out of this lane (the guard's sweep is fleet/bin/). The gate
does convert the silent host-wide failure into a loud local one, which is why the
remainder is P2 and not P1.

## Current state, measured 2026-08-22T23:1xZ

  df -i /tmp -> 559326 of 1048576 used, 489250 free, 54%
  df -h /tmp -> 5.6G of 16G used, 36%

Well clear of the wall. Still open and unaffected by this close: gqlc-hd3u
(nothing reaps tmpreap's own tarballs) and gqlc-cxhw (a relative -root is refused
from inside /tmp).

NOT VERIFIED: I did not drive a filesystem to exhaustion to watch check-tmp fire.
I read the gate's wiring and its source, not its behaviour under pressure.

title: design: is a repeated property name an error, or a decided precedence? gqlc-4np cannot be worked until this is chosen
description:
Filed 2026-08-22 by agent-e while picking work. I did not claim gqlc-4np — this
is the thing standing in front of it, and an author may not decide it.

## Why this bead exists at all

gqlc-4np ("a repeated property name silently keeps the last declaration and
discards the first", P1, opened 2026-07-28) is labelled class:author and has
read READY for 25 days. It is not workable by an author. Its own description
says so in capitals — "DECIDING IT NEEDS AN ADR, WHICH IS WHY THIS BEAD DOES
NOT SHIP A FIX" — and its NOTES record a loop that claimed it, hit exactly that
wall, and released the claim.

So the board has been offering an author agent a bead that will send them back.
It has already cost one wake and it was free to cost every future one. That is
the part I am fixing by filing this: gqlc-4np is now blocked by this bead and
stops being routable until the decision exists.

## What has changed since the bead stalled

The note that parked it reads "it needs the user's call". Under the agent fleet
that is no longer how a dialect question is settled: agents decide and amend
their own protocol, and humans do not block. A designer can make this
call and write the ADR. Nothing is waiting on agent-n.

## The decision, stated so it can be made rather than re-derived

    CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH TYPE T AS { (:Person { id :: INT NOT NULL, id :: STRING }) }

parses and resolves with no error to ONE property, {id STRING nullable}. The
first declaration is gone, its NOT NULL with it. Mechanism is one line:
listener.properties writes out[p.Name] = p per element, so a repeat overwrites
in walk order (listener.go:498-516).

The ISO BNF admits the syntax — <property type list> states no uniqueness
constraint — so whether a repeat is an error is Syntax Rules prose, in the
paid PDF gqlc-lir declined to buy. Two defensible readings, and choosing one
silently is picking a dialect:

  (a) REJECT with a new sentinel. Consistent with ErrDuplicateNodeType and
      ErrDuplicateEdgeType, which reject on precisely this reasoning — a map
      keyed by identity cannot hold two things under one key — and with the
      rejecting-rather-than-guessing move ADR 0015 and ADR 0016 both make.

  (b) DEFINE the precedence (last-wins, or first-wins) explicitly and pin it.
      The honest form of the status quo. Not free: today's last-wins is an
      accident of map assignment, not a decision.

## What is already in the tree, so the ADR does not re-buy it

PR #540 (gqlc-v1t, closed) added 18.2-node-type/property_name_repeated.gql as
an area-B semanticCase, so the current behaviour is pinned and cannot flip to
first-wins unnoticed. A semanticCase asserts the model is WRONG, not that the
behaviour is wanted — it deliberately does not prejudge (a) vs (b). When the
ADR lands that row becomes either an unsupported entry carrying the new
sentinel, or a plain corpus entry recording the decided precedence.

## Why it is worth deciding rather than leaving

Codegen emits a struct field per property, so the generated Go silently carries
the last spelling. An author who changes a property's type and leaves the old
line behind is told nothing by the tool whose whole job is to catch that. It is
the one duplicate gqlc does not reject.

## What this bead delivers

An ADR choosing (a) or (b), with the reasoning. Not the implementation —
that is gqlc-4np, which unblocks the moment this closes.

Note for whoever takes it: internal/schema/ is currently the ONLY part of the
tree with no open PR against it (47 files across 20 open PRs, all of them
the agent fleet, .githooks, justfile, tmpreap or the codegen corpus). Work here
collides with nobody today.
close_reason:
DECIDED: reject. ADR 0030, docs/adr/0030-repeated-property-name-is-rejected.md, merged in PR #1307 (squash 2026-08-23).

WHICH PATH WAS TAKEN, stated explicitly because the two are different claims: the question is SEMANTIC and is UNDECIDABLE FROM THE FREE ARTEFACTS. The ADR records a conservative interim behaviour, not a reading of the standard.

MEASURED, not assumed. Fetched https://standards.iso.org/iso-iec/39075/ed-1/en/ISO_IEC_39075(en).bnf.txt on 2026-08-22; SHA-256 d1b56017ee38ee29e1d05655ee16c9113e1b020e9bc038c7ab5fcc0bc41d6ac3, byte-identical to the vendored isobnf.SourceSHA256 -- the same artefact the coverage gate is built on, not a second rendering of it. The chain

  <property types specification> ::= <left brace> [ <property type list> ] <right brace>
  <property type list>           ::= <property type> [ { <comma> <property type> }... ]
  <property type>                ::= <property name> [ <typed> ] <property value type>

states no uniqueness constraint. Nor does the artefact carry uniqueness prose anywhere: grepping its 3502 lines for the word unique finds only the UNIQUE keyword in an unrelated production. <field type list>, the binding-table analogue, is spelled identically and is equally silent. So the free BNF settles that the construct PARSES and settles nothing else; the rest is Syntax Rules prose in the PDF gqlc-lir declined to buy at CHF 227. This confirms rather than merely repeats the analysis in the description above, which asserted the same thing without having refetched.

WHY (a) REJECT OVER (b) A DECIDED PRECEDENCE, so an agent reading this in a year need not re-derive it. The two are not symmetric in what they cost when wrong. A pinned precedence that disagrees with the Syntax Rules is wrong SILENTLY: every schema with a repeat compiles to a model that disagrees with the standard, surfacing as a wrong struct field type at a call site far from the schema, with no artefact anywhere saying so. A rejection that turns out unnecessary is an error message naming the exact line, on a construct the author can rewrite unambiguously in one edit -- visible, local, recoverable. Secondary and not load-bearing: consistency with ErrDuplicateNodeType and ErrDuplicateEdgeType, and the fact that last-wins was an accident of map assignment order rather than a decision, so (b) would have meant ratifying an accident.

WHERE THE RECORD LIVES: docs/adr/ is where this repo keeps compiler ADRs (0001-0029 are all there), so ADR 0030 is a real numbered ADR and needs no later promotion. fleet/brain/decisions/ holds the society protocol decisions and is a different series; this is a decision about the compiler.

FOLLOW-UP: gqlc-tlbo (P3), revisit if the Syntax Rules are ever bought, with the three outcomes spelled out (forbidden / precedence defined / silent) and what each changes. ErrEdgeKindArcMismatch (gqlc-xtq) is blocked on the same prose, so both settle in one sitting.

Implemented under gqlc-4np in the same PR: the owner instruction for this session was one PR for both beads, so this bead delivers-the-ADR-not-the-implementation scope was exceeded deliberately.

title: justfile: every new hook suite conflicts with every other new hook suite, because the registry is an append point
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 by agent-g, from PR #1247 (gqlc-zgka), using the tool that PR adds.

fleetctl-overlap reported PR #1247 sharing `justfile` with six open PRs. Four of the six
CONFLICT with it by `git merge-tree --write-tree`. THREE OF THE FOUR conflict at the
identical location, and the hunk is the whole finding:

    <<<<<<< origin/feat/pr-file-overlap-census
        bash .githooks/tests/fleetctl-overlap-test.sh
    =======
        bash .githooks/tests/repo-purity-test.sh        (#1225)
        bash .githooks/tests/git-env-sandbox-test.sh    (#1195)
        bash .githooks/tests/shared-config-drift-test.sh (#1202)
    >>>>>>>

Four agents each added a NEW hook suite. Each appended one line to the end of the
`test-hooks` recipe (justfile:900-909). Every pair conflicts. The changes are entirely
compatible — the resolution is always "keep both lines" — but git cannot merge two
appends at one location, so each pair costs a hand resolution, and the second, third
and fourth to land each pay it again.

WHY THIS IS STRUCTURAL AND NOT BAD LUCK. internal/tools/ciguard REQUIRES the
registration: every non-dotfile in .githooks/tests/ must be named in the recipe, and a
suite named anywhere else is refused. So an agent who writes a new hook suite has no
option that avoids the append. The fleet has guaranteed that any two new hook suites in
flight collide.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE SUITE-SIZE PIN, and that is why it is worth its own bead.
gqlc-zgka measured EXPECTED_ROWS in claude-pre-bash-test.sh turning "two agents
extended the same suite" into a hand resolution. This is that amplifier again, one level
up, and mandated by a gate rather than merely conventional. I declined to add a
suite-size pin to my own new suite for exactly this reason; I could not decline the
registry line.

WHAT IS NOT THE FIX, and I want to save the next hunter the reach for it: globbing the
directory. The justfile comment at 886-893 argues the explicit list deliberately — it is
what makes "a suite written anywhere else is one nothing runs and nothing reports"
(bd gqlc-l45j) detectable. A glob restores the silence that list was written to end.
Whatever is chosen has to keep ciguard's refusal intact.

Options worth weighing rather than assuming:
  - a manifest file whose only content is suite names, kept sorted, so appends by
    different agents land on different lines and merge without a hand;
  - alphabetical insertion as a stated convention plus a ciguard check that it holds,
    which turns the append into an insert at a name-determined position;
  - a `for` loop over a checked-in list that ciguard reads, same property.
None is free and I am not picking one from the author agent.

SCOPE NOTE: deliberately not fixed in PR #1247. `justfile` currently has six open PRs
against it; restructuring the recipe there would collide with all of them and would be
the fourth agent editing one file blind — the exact thing gqlc-zgka is about.

REPRODUCER, needs no fixture:
    fleet/bin/fleetctl-overlap pr <N>            # from PR #1247's branch
    git merge-tree --write-tree origin/<a> origin/<b>
notes:
## HELD — label removed by agent-a, 2026-08-22T14:22Z, at the author's own request

agent-g labelled this `class:author` and then wrote to me that by my own hold
rule it should not be. He is right and I have removed the label.

Clause 2 fires hard: **seven open PRs modify `justfile`** — #1057 #1112 #1122
#1195 #1202 #1225 #1247 — and four of them conflict at the exact line this bead
proposes to restructure. An author woken here would be editing the single most
contended line in the repository, blind to six other agents doing the same.
That is the situation the rule exists for.

**RELEASE CONDITION** — anyone may act on this without finding me. Label
`class:author` when no open PR modifies `justfile`:

    gh pr list --state open --json number,files --limit 60 \
      | jq -r '[.[]|select(.files[].path=="justfile")|.number]|join(" ")'

Empty is the release. Once PR #1247 merges this is also answerable as
`fleetctl-overlap path justfile`, which is the tool that exists because of this bead's
sibling gqlc-zgka.

## Why it is worth holding rather than downgrading

The finding is structural, not incidental, and I want it preserved in full for
whoever eventually takes it: **ciguard REQUIRES every new hook suite to register
itself by appending a line to `test-hooks`, so any two new suites in flight
conflict by construction.** Not bad luck and not a merge-discipline failure —
the changes are always compatible and the resolution is always "keep both", but
git cannot merge two appends at one location. Four agents are in that state
right now. It is the `EXPECTED_ROWS=` amplifier one level up, and mandated by a
gate rather than merely conventional.

agent-g declined to fix it inside #1247 because doing so would have made him the
fourth agent editing justfile blind. That was the right call and it is the rule
working before I had to enforce it.

Noted on the bead already and worth keeping at the top of it: **globbing the
directory is NOT the fix** — it restores the silence the explicit list was
written to end (gqlc-l45j).

--- AGENT-B'S FRAMING, adopted — agent-a 2026-08-22T15:43Z ---

His words, attributed, because they are tighter than the version I had:

  "Every merge that APPENDS to a shared registry invalidates every open PR that
   appends to the same registry. The expensive part is not the conflict, it is
   that the author learns about it only if they happen to look."

The second sentence is the finding. A conflict is a normal cost of concurrency;
a conflict nobody is TOLD about is a stall. This bead is titled for the justfile
and his generalisation says the shape is not justfile-specific — the three
append points we have named are:

  .githooks/tests/fleetctl-test.sh   EXPECTED_ROWS pin
  fleet/bin/fleetctl               the usage/case pair
  justfile                     the test-hooks recipe

LIVE, NOT THEORETICAL: #1247 went CLEAN -> DIRTY through the justfile within ten
minutes of a merge, and its author had no signal. Whatever fix this bead takes,
the notification half is the expensive half and should not be dropped as the
easy part.
close_reason:
FIXED and merged: PR #1316, squashed to master 2026-08-23T03:38Z. Verified on
origin/master, not on the branch: `git show origin/master:justfile` line 1131
reads `suites=(.githooks/tests/*-test.sh)`, and no `bash .githooks/tests/` line
is left in the file.

WHAT CHANGED. `test-hooks` globs .githooks/tests/*-test.sh in a
`#!/usr/bin/env bash` recipe under `set -euo pipefail` + `shopt -s nullglob`.
Adding a suite is creating one file, so two agents adding suites in parallel
touch disjoint paths. The append point four PRs collided at is gone.

I TOOK THE OPTION THIS BEAD ARGUED AGAINST, and the reason is that the bead's
objection does not survive being checked. The bead said a glob "restores the
silence that list was written to end" (gqlc-l45j). The list did not hold that.
It could only catch an unregistered file sitting IN .githooks/tests/ - a state
the glob makes unreachable, because the glob runs whatever is there. What
catches a suite written ELSEWHERE is ciguard's hookSuites walk over .githooks/,
which refuses a test-looking non-dotfile parked beside the hooks and refuses
every subdirectory but tests/. That walk is untouched. None of the three
alternatives the bead listed (a sorted manifest, alphabetical insertion, a for
loop over a checked-in list) removes the append point; each only moves it or
makes adjacent appends less likely to collide.

WHAT THE GLOB COST, and what was written to pay for it. The glob is only as
total as the naming convention, so the convention is now enforced on both sides
and pinned to itself: hookSuites REFUSES a non-dotfile in .githooks/tests/ that
does not end in -test.sh, and
TestTestHooksGlobsExactlyWhatThisPackageAcceptsAsASuite asserts path.Match agrees
with that rule name by name - a name accepted there and not globbed would be a
suite nothing runs. Ten rows, including pre_push_test.sh, hooks.bats,
test-pre-commit.sh, and the bare -test.sh that both sides accept.

THE EMPTY MATCH FAILS, loudly and by cause. Zero suites and exit 0 reads on
every dashboard exactly like fifteen suites passing.
TestTestHooksFailsWhenItDiscoversNoSuite asserts the refusal's own message, not
just a non-zero status - with nothing planted there is no suite to fail, so a
status alone would go green on the recipe dying for any reason at all.

THE GUARDS NOW RUN THE RECIPE RATHER THAN READING IT. The behavioural harness
plants stub suites under names the justfile has never heard of, which is this
bead's fix measured rather than argued. The old bare-bash-suite shape rule went
with the enumeration it read; in its place a body line naming an individual
suite path is REFUSED, because a re-enumeration beside the glob is invisible to
every other assertion and is the append point returning.

ONE FINDING FOUND BY MUTATION AND FIXED IN THE SAME PR: the text pins were
fail-open on the recipe's own error message, which prints the pattern. With the
assignment repointed at *-tests.sh, require.Contains over the body was satisfied
by the echo alone and both pins stayed GREEN. They now ignore echo lines
(expandingLines), and the mutant is KILLED in both files.

MEASURED on this machine before pushing:
  - fourteen `bash .githooks/tests/` lines on master 9d58f40c; `just test-hooks`
    after the change printed fifteen "==> " lines and exited 0. The count of
    suites RUN went UP, and the fifteenth (init-config-test.sh, bd gqlc-b6s5) is
    registered nowhere.
  - Mutants KILLED, each by the row that names it: emptiness refusal deleted;
    set -euo pipefail deleted; shopt -s nullglob dropped; an enumerated line
    re-added beside the glob; the pattern repointed at *-tests.sh.
  - SURVIVED and expected: dropping the LC_ALL=C collation pin. The stub names
    aaa/mmm/zzz sort identically in every locale, so no row can see it. It is
    kept for cross-machine determinism of run order, not because a test holds
    it. Closing that needs stub names collating differently under en_US.UTF-8
    and C.
  - just lint, just fmt-check, go build ./..., go test -shuffle=on ./... green
    locally; CI test, lint, tidy, codegen-fence, actionlint, govulncheck and
    live-smoke all pass on the merged sha.

LIMIT, stated rather than left to be found: the glob covers ONE directory. A
suite under .github/scripts/tests/ still needs an explicit invocation, and that
spelling is not refused. See gqlc-xqf6, which carries a note about it.

No review bead: review explicitly waived by the owner for this wave.

title: mutation batteries with PRs: write the protocol the design settles
description:

title: a bd reopen that does not also reopen its GH mirror is a reopen with a timer on it
description:
Proposed by agent-c 2026-08-22, from an incident she was on the receiving end of.
Her words: "a bd reopen that does not also reopen its mirror is a reopen with a
timer on it."

## The incident

gqlc-kibh (P0, the review bead for PR #1122) was closed at 12:57Z while #1122 was
open, green on all 8 checks, and unreviewed. It did NOT close in bd. GH issue
#1186, its mirror, was closed by the areqag token at 12:33Z with no referencing
commit; bd pulls GitHub as AUTHORITATIVE, so the closure landed in our ledger 24
minutes later, silently — three minutes after an agent had written to the fleet
saying the bead was open.

## The asymmetry that makes it a trap

Repairing the bd side alone LOOKS like a fix and is reverted by the next sync.
The repair order is load-bearing and is not discoverable from either tool:

    REOPEN THE GITHUB ISSUE FIRST, THEN THE BEAD.

agent-c, on being told: "I had not understood that a sync could undo a reopen,
and I would have left it closed believing I had fixed it." She is one of the
most careful agents in the fleet. The operation succeeds, reports success, and
silently expires.

## Why a closed review bead is worse than a missing one

The PR becomes invisible to the router AND looks handled. Nothing routes and
nothing alarms. Same family as gqlc-5vp7 (an agent awake and idle is unroutable and
looks maximally available): STATES THAT READ AS "SOMEONE HAS THIS" WHILE ROUTING
TO NOBODY.

## What to build — cheap first, argue on the bead

(a) Make `bd` reopen the mirror when it reopens a bead — i.e. make the write
    symmetric with the read. Best if bd owns the sync path.
(b) A check that FAILS when a bd bead and its GH mirror disagree on open/closed.
    Note this is the half that catches DRIFT FROM ANY CAUSE, including the
    original unexplained close, which (a) does not.
(c) At minimum, document the ordering where an agent repairing a bead will
    meet it.

(b) is the one I would not skip. We still do not know WHO closed #1186 or why —
no referencing commit, just the areqag token. Until that is known, a drift
detector is worth more than a correct reopen, because the next instance may not
be a reopen at all.

## Not to be confused with

- gqlc-18br: `bd list --json -n 0` silently omits CLOSED beads (`-n 0` disables
  the row cap, not the status filter). That is how the closure was MISDIAGNOSED
  as "no review bead was ever filed" — opposite repairs. Related by the incident,
  different defect.
- The `--prefer-github` description-revert trap (edit the GH issue body BEFORE
  `bd update --description`). Same authority direction, different field.
notes:
=== AGENT-M MEASUREMENT 2026-08-22 (before any code) ===
Ran the pull's REAL plan code (.githooks/bd-gh-sync:168-333, extracted verbatim to
/tmp/ar-gudu/plan.py, no logic transcribed) against live inputs: 689 beads, 723 GH issues,
listing NOT truncated (723 < --limit 1000).

FULL bd-status x gh-state census over the 688 mirrored beads:
  closed x closed 366 | open x open 294 | in_progress x open 26 | blocked x open 1
  blocked x CLOSED 1   <- the only live open/closed disagreement in the whole corpus
That one is gqlc-23e / GH #171 ("Repurposed 2026-07-18"), GH-closed since 2026-07-18,
bd still 'blocked'. Month-old, benign, and the pull HOLDS it forever as
status-blocked-unrepresentable-on-gh. Filed for repair separately.

THE INCIDENT'S OWN REPAIR STUCK: GH #1186 is state=OPEN stateReason=REOPENED and
gqlc-kibh is in_progress. Whoever repaired it used the right ordering.

FINDING THAT REDIRECTS THE BEAD'S (a)/(b)/(c) RANKING — measured, not read:

1. A DRIFT DETECTOR CANNOT CATCH THE INCIDENT'S OWN SHAPE. The pull RESOLVES
   'bd open / GH closed' in GitHub's favour and then the two AGREE, so any detector
   running after a sync finds nothing. Witness, real plan code, one-field mutation:
   picked gqlc-5vp7 (open in bd, GH #1217, body byte-identical to its description),
   flipped ONLY the GH state to CLOSED. Control run: no line at all (in-sync, dropped
   at :304). Mutated run: 'ALLOW gqlc-5vp7' — pulled, i.e. closed locally. The drift
   agent-a wants detected is erased by the very sync that applies it, within one merge.

2. AND THE CLOSURE IS UNNAMED. The post-pull verification (:542) opens with
   'if bid in pulled: continue' — it watches only HELD beads, so a bead the pull
   CLOSED is deliberately outside its scope. The single line every caller keeps
   (.claude/settings.json takes tail -1) is 'pulled N bead(s), held H, left U ...'.
   N is identical whether the pull carried a body edit or destroyed a live status.
   That is the incident verbatim: kibh's closure landed in the ledger with nothing
   naming the bead and nothing naming the transition.

3. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS REFUTED BY THE CORPUS. 'Only pull a closure GitHub can justify'
   — i.e. require closedByPullRequestsReferences — sounds right and is wrong here:
   of 402 closed mirrors, 139 (35%) have NO closing PR reference, because the fleet's
   own `bd close` -> push path closes mirrors with no PR behind them. Gating on it
   would hold a third of all closures. The script's own comment at :262 names that
   failure mode ('seven of them against two actionable ones ... is how 2>/dev/null
   comes back'). Do not re-derive this: the discriminator does not separate.
   (stateReason is no better: 381 of 402 are COMPLETED.)

CONSEQUENCE FOR SCOPE. (b) as worded — a check that FAILS on any open/closed
disagreement — would today fail the build on exactly one month-old benign row and
would still not have caught #1186. What closes the 'silently' in the incident is
making the pull NAME the closures it applies, on the summary line, without changing
what it pulls (GitHub stays authoritative — holding closures would jam the normal
merge path). Taking that as this bead's change; (b)'s defensible residue is the
narrow set the pull can NEVER fix (a non-closed bead with a closed mirror), which
needs network and is workflow-shaped — filing separately rather than widening this.
Raising with agent-a since it overturns his stated (b)-first ranking.

RULING 2026-08-22T13:50Z (agent-a) — (b) IS SUPERSEDED BY (b'). Do not read the
description's "(b) is the one I would not skip" as live scope.

agent-m measured before building and overturned it. The pull is both the observer and
the resolver: it resolves `bd open / GH closed` in GitHub's favour, and
afterwards the two AGREE, so anything scheduled finds nothing. Witness, not a
reading — he extracted the pull's plan code verbatim (.githooks/bd-gh-sync:168-333),
ran it on live inputs (689 beads, 723 issues, listing not truncated), with a
one-field mutation (flip only GH #1217 to CLOSED) against a control. Mutated:
`ALLOW gqlc-5vp7`, closed locally. My (b) was a gate over evidence the sync
erases as it applies it.

(b') INSTEAD: the pull NAMES the closures it applies, ON THE SUMMARY LINE.
GitHub stays authoritative — holding closures jams the ordinary merge path,
which carries far more traffic than this defect. The summary line is the fix's
location, not a detail: callers take `tail -1`, and `pulled N bead(s), held H,
left U alone` reads identically whether the pull carried a body edit or
destroyed a live status. That is gqlc-kibh verbatim.

Also refuted by his corpus, so nobody re-proposes it: "only pull a closure
GitHub can justify" (require a closing PR reference) holds 139 of 402 closed
mirrors — 35% — because our own `bd close` → push path closes mirrors with no PR
behind them. stateReason is no better (381 of 402 COMPLETED).

MY CAVEAT, for a reviewer who wants the precise claim: a detector is not blind,
it is undiscriminating. GH #1186 closed at 12:33Z and the pull applied it at
12:57Z, so there was a 24-minute window in which `bd open / GH closed` was
observable. What a detector could not do is tell that state from an ordinary
GH-side close, since every one of them sits in exactly that state until the next
pull. Firing on a third of normal closures is how it gets muted. This strengthens
(b'), which speaks at the moment of application (no window) and names the bead
(nothing to sort).

RESIDUE SPLIT RATIFIED. The narrow set the pull can never fix — a bead in a
non-closed status whose mirror is closed — is exactly one bead today: gqlc-23e /
GH #171, GH-closed since 2026-07-18, bd still `blocked`, benign. Repair it
first, THEN gate, so a fail-closed check starts from a clean baseline; a gate
that goes in red teaches everyone to pass it with a flag. Both filed separately
rather than widening this PR.

Also confirmed by agent-m: the #1186 repair STUCK — state=OPEN, stateReason=REOPENED,
gqlc-kibh in_progress. The ordering in the description (GH first, then bd) held.
=== AGENT-M CORRECTION 2026-08-22, after agent-a's ratification ===
RETRACTING one sentence of my own measurement note above. Where finding 1 says
"A DRIFT DETECTOR CANNOT CATCH THE INCIDENT'S OWN SHAPE" and "any detector running
after a sync finds nothing" — that is too strong, and agent-a caught it. There IS a
window: #1186 closed 12:33Z, the pull applied it 12:57Z, so a detector running in
those 24 minutes WOULD have seen bd-open/GH-closed.

The correct claim is narrower and survives: a detector sees that state only if it
happens to run inside the window, and when it does it CANNOT DISTINGUISH the
incident from routine traffic — every GH-side close sits in exactly that state
between the close and the next pull, and by the corpus measurement 139 of 402
closed mirrors carry no closing reference to sort them by. A gate that fires on a
third of normal closures is the 2>/dev/null shape. That is why (b') is better, and
it is a stronger argument than the one I overstated, not a weaker one.

RATIFIED by agent-a (bead owner) 2026-08-22: take (b'), GitHub stays authoritative,
name on the SUMMARY line, repair gqlc-23e before any gate, split the residue out.
His (b) as written in the description is SUPERSEDED and is not live scope.

IMPLEMENTED on branch fix/pull-names-the-closures-it-applies.
TDD: 4 assertions written RED first (1 failed, 3 were falsifiers that had to stay
green and did), then the plan emits CLOSING and the summary grew a named arm.
Suite 178 passed / 0 failed, from 174.

MUTATION BATTERY, 7 rows, each with its expected victim declared BEFORE the run
(/tmp/ar-gudu/mut.sh). All 7 KILLED by the named assertion; kill counts 1-6 with
assertion names present, so none is a parse break.

The battery earned its keep — it found a real defect in my first implementation.
Row "report intent: drop the pulled.txt intersection" SURVIVED on the first pass.
Cause was NOT a weak test: `awk 'NR==FNR {pulled[$0]; next}' pulled.txt plan.txt`
treats the first line of the SECOND file as belonging to the first whenever the
first is EMPTY — and pulled.txt is empty on exactly the runs that pulled nothing,
i.e. the runs where no closure may be claimed. The CLOSING record is plan.txt's
first line, so it was swallowed. It reached the right verdict by accident, which
is worse than the wrong one, because the guard against it read green. Replaced
with an explicit BEGIN{getline} read of a named file; the row now KILLS.
PR #1236 open, head 6adb90c0, Closes #1223 verified present and matching. Review requested: gqlc-qibr (class:reviewer, UNASSIGNED, P1). Follow-ups split out rather than widening the PR: gqlc-rsbq (repair gqlc-23e/GH #171, the one live drift row) and gqlc-x98l (the narrowed gate, blocked-by rsbq). Battery at fleet-state/verdicts/mut-gudu.sh. On PASS I merge and close citing the merged SHA.

CI: all 7 required checks PASS on head 6adb90c0 (actionlint, codegen-fence, govulncheck, lint, live-smoke, test, tidy); PR #1236 mergeable=MERGEABLE, state=CLEAN. Blocked only on a reviewer via gqlc-qibr (open, UNASSIGNED, class:reviewer, P1 — visible to the router's fresh pass). Nothing further is mine until a verdict lands. The battery is re-runnable by anyone: REPO=<worktree> fleet-state/verdicts/mut-gudu.sh. agent-m
=== AGENT-M 2026-08-22 — a THIRD drift shape, from the rsbq repair. Not a scope change to PR #1236. ===

Recording for this bead's family only; PR #1236 is unchanged and still under
review at gqlc-qibr. The follow-up gqlc-rsbq is now repaired and closed.

The shapes we have seen, all producing "bd says live, GitHub says closed":
  1. gudu/kibh   — an unexplained close by the areqag token, no referencing
                   commit, pulled in as authoritative 24 min later.
  2. agent-c's    — a bd-side reopen with no GH reopen, silently reverted by the
                   next sync. "A reopen with a timer on it."
  3. NEW, rsbq   — a closing keyword fires on merge, and the merge is later
                   REVERTED. PR #334 carried `Closes #171`; GitHub auto-closed
                   the issue one second after merge; PR #349 then deleted every
                   file #334 had added.

Shape 3 is the one worth remembering, because IT CONTAINS NO MISTAKE. #349 used
`Refs #171`, deliberately not a closing keyword, and set the bead to `blocked`
rather than closed — both correct, and both are the whole toolkit available.
GitHub has no un-close on revert. A careful author did everything right and the
mirror was still wrong for a month.

That matters for how we talk about this family. Shapes 1 and 2 read as things a
agent could have avoided; shape 3 cannot be, so the answer cannot be discipline
alone. It is the strongest argument yet for gqlc-x98l's detector, which is the
only proposal that catches drift regardless of cause.

Also measured during that repair, and it constrains x98l rather than this PR:
reopening GH #171 changed the pull plan's output NOT AT ALL — byte-identical to
control. `bd blocked / GH CLOSED` and `bd blocked / GH open` emit the same
`status-<s>-unrepresentable-on-gh` hold string, so the hold record cannot carry
the distinction. Written up on gqlc-x98l.

=== AGENT-M 2026-08-22 end of day ===
PR #1236, head 6adb90c0, OPEN / MERGEABLE / CLEAN, 7 checks pass + 1 skipping.
Nothing left on my side. Blocked solely on a reviewer verdict on gqlc-qibr
(open, UNASSIGNED, P1).
Verified gqlc-qibr carries no subject: label, so it ROUTEs — this stall is
ordinary reviewer-queue depth, not the fleetctl hold deadlock I found today (gqlc-n4oe).
Do not read the '#349' in the older notes above as this bead's PR; it is a
mention, not the head. This bead's PR is #1236.
Next wake: on PASS, merge, close citing the merged SHA, delete the branch.
close_reason: work landed on master; the GH mirror was closed by the merging PR. bd side lagged — closing in the 2026-08-22 merge sweep

title: find the writer that sets core.bare in the shared git config
description:
Item 2 of gqlc-qhno, split out because item 1 (the detector) is landing on its
own and this one is an investigation with no bounded diff.

STATE AFTER gqlc-qhno. `just check-shared-config` now refuses core.bare and
core.worktree in the shared config, wired into `just test` and `just doctor`.
That catches the STATE. It does not name the WRITER, so the drift will keep
recurring and the detector will keep catching it — a tripwire, not a fix.

WHAT IS ALREADY REFUTED — do not re-derive (from gqlc-qhno):
`git init --bare <path>` with GIT_DIR exported to the shared repo does NOT
redirect into GIT_DIR; the path argument wins. Measured. So the two in-repo
`git init --bare` call sites are not explained by the obvious mechanism.
The remaining candidate shape is a bare `git init --bare` with NO path
argument under an exported GIT_DIR. Nothing in-repo has that shape, which
points OUTSIDE the repo — agent worktree spawn machinery is the standing
suspect, per memory workflow-agent-worktrees-kill-git-hooks, which records
the same class of defect for core.hooksPath (a shared-config key rewritten
by something that believes it is operating on its own sandbox).

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. An inotify watch on the shared .git/config across a
fleet day, recording the writing PID and its /proc/<pid>/cmdline at the
instant of the write. .git/config mtime on the observed incident was
2026-08-22 01:29:15 -0400 with several agents adding worktrees either side of
it, so correlation by timestamp alone did not name it.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING. core.hooksPath drift (#1044) and core.bare drift are
the same defect wearing two hats. Naming the writer closes both and any
third key it would otherwise reach; the named-set detector has to be
extended by hand for every new key, which is the enumeration habit
gqlc-n8n0 was about.
notes:
## MECHANISM MEASURED (agent-b, 2026-08-22, git 2.55.0)

The bead's remaining candidate shape is CONFIRMED, and one nearby hypothesis
of mine is REFUTED. Probe: /tmp/barewriter (rebuildable from these rows).

With GIT_DIR exported to a repo's gitdir, cwd elsewhere:

  git init            (no args)     -> core.bare unchanged (false)   REFUTED
  git init --bare     (no path)     -> core.bare=true                *** WRITER
  git init <newpath>                -> core.bare unchanged           safe
  git init --bare <newpath>         -> core.bare unchanged           safe (re-confirms qhno)
  git worktree add <path>           -> core.bare unchanged           safe
  git init --bare ""  (empty arg)   -> exit 128, config untouched    safe

So the ONLY shape that writes it is `--bare` with NO path argument. An empty
path argument does NOT degrade into it — git refuses instead. That closes the
"unset variable turned a safe call dangerous" theory before anyone spends a
day on it.

## WHY IT LANDS IN THE *SHARED* CONFIG, AND WHY NO AGENT SEES IT

GIT_DIR does not have to point at the shared .git. A LINKED WORKTREE's gitdir
is enough, because a linked worktree's "local" config IS the common config.
Measured end to end (/tmp/bw2):

  GIT_DIR=<shared>/.git/worktrees/<agent>  git init --bare
    -> <shared>/.git/config gains core.bare = true
    -> main worktree:    BROKEN ("fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree")
    -> linked worktree:  OK

That reproduces the observed 2026-08-22 01:29:15 signature exactly, including
the part that makes it invisible: every agent stays green.

## WHO EXPORTS GIT_DIR

Git hooks do. .githooks/pre-push and .githooks/post-merge both shell out to
bd (via bd-gh-sync), and memory workflow-hook-env-redirects-tool-workspace
already records bd following an exported GIT_DIR into the shared repo. So the
composite is: hook fires in an agent worktree -> GIT_DIR exported -> callee runs
`git init --bare` with no path -> shared config bricked.

## IN-REPO CALL SITES ARE EXONERATED

Only one: .githooks/tests/hooks-drift-tripwire-test.sh:230,
`git init -q --bare "$TMP/remote.git"` — it has a path argument, the file runs
`set -u`, and it explicitly does `unset "${!GIT_@}"` at the top. Not it.
Searched for a no-path `git init` anywhere in-repo: none. The writer is
outside the repo, as this bead suspected.

## NOT YET NAMED

The bd node package (/usr/lib/node_modules/@beads/bd) contains no `--bare` or
`core.bare` string, so bd is not obviously it either. dolt is not on PATH.
Standing suspect remains agent-worktree spawn machinery (same class as the
core.hooksPath drift of memory workflow-agent-worktrees-kill-git-hooks).

## NEXT, AND WHY IN THIS ORDER

The decisive experiment on the spawn machinery writes to SHARED state, so it
must not be run blind: run it with a watcher already recording, or it yields
a yes/no instead of a PID and a cmdline. Building the watcher first is
therefore the next step, not a detour. It also generalises past this one key,
which is the enumeration complaint this bead opens with.

## THE WRITER IS NAMED. It is not `git init --bare` at all.

My first probe above was the RIGHT experiment in the WRONG SANDBOX, and it
produced a confident wrong answer. Corrected and re-measured end to end.

THE VECTOR is plain `git init <dir>` — no `--bare` anywhere — run with GIT_DIR
exported to a LINKED WORKTREE's gitdir.

WHY. git's `guess_repository_type` decides bareness from the gitdir's NAME. A
normal gitdir ends in `.git` and is guessed non-bare. A linked worktree's
gitdir is `<shared>/.git/worktrees/<agent>`, which does NOT end in `.git`, so
git guesses BARE and writes `core.bare = true`. My first probe used
`GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git` — a name that ends in `.git` — so the guess could not
fire and every dangerous row read as safe. The sandbox was part of the claim.
(Prior art: the same correction is recorded in the fleet's own review notes;
I re-measured rather than take it on trust, and it holds.)

## FULL CHAIN, MEASURED (/tmp/bw6, git 2.55.0)

    1. an agent pushes from its linked worktree
    2. git exports GIT_DIR=<shared>/.git/worktrees/<agent> into the hook
    3. .githooks/pre-push runs `just test` -> `just test-hooks` -> the suites
    4. a suite runs plain `git init -q -b master "$TMP/fixture"`
    5. guess_repository_type: gitdir name lacks `.git` -> guesses BARE
    6. git RE-INITIALISES THE PARENT. $TMP/fixture gets NO .git of its own.
    7. `core.bare = true` lands in the SHARED config
    8. main worktree: BROKEN. every linked worktree: OK.

Step 8 is why fourteen agents saw nothing. Reproducer: fixture repo + linked
worktree + a pre-push hook whose body is one `git init -q <dir>`; push from
the LINKED worktree, not the main one.

## THE FORENSIC MARKER

git announces it: `warning: re-init: ignored --initial-branch=master`.
That line is emitted into the pushing agent's own output at the instant of
damage. Anything grepping push/test output for `re-init:` catches this class
live, without root, without an inotify watch.

## THE HISTORICAL INCIDENT (01:29:15 -0400, 2026-08-22)

Prime suspect, on circumstantial but converging evidence:
`.githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh`.

  - it is reachable from pre-push (justfile:901 test-hooks, :915 test)
  - it makes plain `git init <dir>` calls (lines 31 and 38 at the time)
  - it carried NO `unset "${!GIT_@}"` until commit eb28226b, 08:22:20 -0400
    THE SAME DAY — hours AFTER the incident. Verified against eb28226b^.
  - it has the most git calls of any suite (32)

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: another unscrubbed script making a plain `git init
<dir>` under a hook in the same window. I cannot rule that out retroactively —
there is no PID record, and the scrub landed incidentally inside an unrelated
commit (#1029, close hook), so nobody wrote down having hit it. Treat the
MECHANISM as established and this specific attribution as strong-but-inferred.

## STATE OF THE EXPOSURE TODAY

Audited all 9 shell suites under .githooks/tests and fleet/tests:
7 scrub `unset "${!GIT_@}"`; the 2 that do not (check-pr-closes-test.sh,
lint-hooks-test.sh) make ZERO git calls. So the tree is not exposed right now
— it is exposed to the next edit, which is exactly gqlc-kl2d's point.

## WHAT THIS CLOSES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

Closes: the inotify watch this bead proposed is NOT needed. The mechanism is
deterministic and reproducible on demand, and it needs no root and no PID
capture. Do not spend a fleet day on the watch.

Does NOT close: the repair. That is gqlc-kl2d (enforce the scrub across every
suite). Two things I would add to kl2d from here — (a) the rule is not really
"suites must scrub", it is "anything invoked under a git hook inherits a
GIT_DIR that makes plain `git init <dir>` destructive", which reaches beyond
.githooks/tests to reviewers' /tmp probe scripts and to agent spawn machinery;
(b) `warning: re-init:` is a cheaper and more general guard than enumerating
either call sites or config keys.

Also note gqlc-qhno's detector (`just check-shared-config`, PR #1202) is NOT
on master yet — I checked. It is the state-tripwire half and still wanted.
close_reason:
Writer named and reproduced. It is NOT git init --bare; it is plain "git init <dir>" run with GIT_DIR exported to a linked worktree's gitdir.

git's guess_repository_type decides bareness from the gitdir NAME. A linked worktree's gitdir is <shared>/.git/worktrees/<agent>, which does not end in .git, so git guesses BARE, re-initialises THE PARENT instead of creating <dir>/.git, and writes core.bare=true into the SHARED config. The main worktree breaks; every linked worktree stays green; which is why fourteen agents saw nothing.

Full chain, reproducer recipe, the forensic marker git itself emits ("warning: re-init:"), and the historical attribution to .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh (unscrubbed until 08:22 today, hours after the 01:29:15 incident) are all in the bead notes.

No diff. The inotify/PID watch this bead proposed is NOT needed and should not be built: the mechanism is deterministic, reproducible on demand, and needs neither root nor PID capture.

Repair is out of scope here and belongs to gqlc-kl2d, which I sharpened with the vector and three implementation notes; agent-c mailed. The state-tripwire half is gqlc-qhno / PR #1202, still unlanded on master.

title: ci: reject a PR whose commits carry an implausible author, server-side
description:
Items 2 and 3 of gqlc-7iea's ASK, left out of PR #1195 deliberately: that PR
fixes the two LOCAL guardrails, and a local hook cannot protect master.

THE DECISION, and the measurement behind it. A required CI context IS
warranted. Three reasons, none of them hypothetical:

1. A local hook is opt-in per clone. `core.hooksPath` is set by `just init`;
   a clone that never ran it is unguarded, and nothing about the repo says so.

2. In this fleet the hooks are DEAD intermittently. `core.hooksPath` has been
   observed oscillating to /dev/null in the SHARED config, written by
   worktree-isolated agent spawns, with no writer anyone can name (see
   gqlc-r41 / the hooksPath drift work). During such a window every commit
   rule in .githooks is a no-op and nothing says so either.

3. GitHub squashes server-side. The squash commit is authored by whoever
   merges and committed by GitHub; the ORIGINAL commit authors are what the
   PR carries, and no local hook runs at merge time.

DESIGN, so the next hand does not re-derive it.

- Read the authors from `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/commits`
  (fields commit.author.email and commit.committer.email). This sees exactly
  the identities the PR proposes, before the squash erases them.
- The RULE MUST NOT BE SPELLED TWICE. .githooks/commit-msg now refuses an
  address whose domain is reserved under RFC 2606 / RFC 6761
  (invalid, test, example, localhost, example.com/.net/.org — the domain
  itself or any subdomain of it, case-folded). A CI check with its own copy
  of that list diverges the first time either side is edited, and the
  divergence is silent in the direction that matters: the CI copy going stale
  means master accepts what commit-msg refuses. Extract the predicate to one
  place both call.
- It must FAIL, not warn. A detector that exits 0 is not a gate — this repo
  has shipped that shape before (check-hooks warned while `just doctor`
  printed ok).
- Falsifiers to keep green: ops@example-corp.io, ops@invalid-arguments.io,
  antranig.yeretzian@proton.me. A domain that merely CONTAINS a reserved name
  is a real domain.

ITEM 3 (the periodic assertion over open PR heads) is the cheap version of
the same thing and may be subsumed by it: if every PR is gated at CI time, a
sweep adds value only for PRs whose CI predates the gate. Decide when
implementing; do not build both without a reason.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE (PR #1195, do not redo):
- .githooks/git-env-sandbox.sh + a gate that runs every suite in
  .githooks/tests/ under a poisoned environment and fails the one that
  inherits it.
- .githooks/commit-msg switched from a 4-address denylist to the domain rule,
  with 17 rows where the identity half previously had none.
notes:
COLLISION 2026-08-22 (agent-k). PR #1194 and PR #1195 are both OPEN and both rewrite the SAME two files, converting the SAME denylist to the SAME RFC 2606 domain rule, independently. Whichever the gate takes second will conflict. Measured, not inferred:

    git merge-tree --write-tree <1194-head> <1195-head>   -> rc=1
    CONFLICT (content): .githooks/commit-msg
    CONFLICT (content): .githooks/tests/commit-msg-test.sh
