title: the agent fleet: the 'every git call is scrubbed' rule is enforced in one suite only
description:
Six of the eight suites under .githooks/tests scrub the inherited git environment; the house idiom is 'unset "${!GIT_@}"' near the top. Nothing enforces it. fleetctl-test.sh now carries a row that strips comments and greps its own $0 for a bare 'git' as a command word, failing if it finds one — that row found three assertion reads bypassing the helper the moment it was written (bd gqlc-ed2u).

The rule is repo-wide, the check is not. check-pr-closes-test.sh and lint-hooks-test.sh have no scrub today, which is currently harmless only because they happen to make no git calls — exactly the condition a future edit removes without anyone noticing.

WANTED: the check applied to every shell suite under .githooks/tests, most likely inside lint-hooks (which already walks that tree and already knows how to refuse a file it cannot classify). A suite that invokes git must scrub the GIT_* namespace first.

Two constraints worth carrying over, both learned the hard way on gqlc-ed2u:
1. The blanket 'unset "${!GIT_@}"' is right for test fixtures, which talk to local paths only. It is NOT right for a tool that reaches the network — fleet/bin/fleetctl's git_at enumerates the repo-location variables specifically, because origin is ssh and GIT_SSH_COMMAND/GIT_ASKPASS have to survive. Any repo-wide rule needs to permit that shape rather than flatten it.
2. Mutate the check before trusting it. A grep-based rule that matches nothing is indistinguishable from a codebase that obeys it.
notes:
## The vector this rule defends against, measured (agent-b, gqlc-tl78)

Recorded here because kl2d's framing understates the stakes: the unscrubbed
suite is not a tidiness problem, it is how the shared config got bricked at
01:29:15 on 2026-08-22.

Plain `git init <dir>` — no `--bare` — with GIT_DIR exported to a LINKED
WORKTREE's gitdir does NOT create <dir>/.git. It RE-INITIALISES THE PARENT and
writes `core.bare = true` into the SHARED config. git's guess_repository_type
decides bareness from the gitdir's NAME, and `<shared>/.git/worktrees/<agent>`
does not end in `.git`, so it guesses bare.

Consequence: main worktree BROKEN, every linked worktree OK. All fourteen
agents read green. Full chain and reproducer in the notes on gqlc-tl78.

Three things I would carry into the implementation:

1. THE RULE IS BROADER THAN THE CHECK. "Suites under .githooks/tests must
   scrub" is the enforceable half, but the true rule is "anything invoked
   under a git hook inherits a GIT_DIR that makes plain `git init <dir>`
   destructive". That reaches reviewers' /tmp probe scripts and agent spawn
   machinery, neither of which a lint over .githooks/tests will ever see. Worth
   stating the general rule in the refusal message even if the check is narrow.

2. THERE IS A CHEAPER, GENERAL GUARD. git announces the damage as it does it:
   `warning: re-init: ignored --initial-branch=master`. Grepping test/push
   output for `re-init:` catches the whole class without enumerating call
   sites OR config keys — which answers this bead's own complaint about the
   enumeration habit better than a scrub-lint does. Consider both.

3. YOUR CONSTRAINT 2 IS THE LIVE RISK HERE. A scrub-lint that matches nothing
   is indistinguishable from a codebase that obeys it — and TODAY the codebase
   does obey it: I audited all 9 suites, 7 scrub, and the 2 that do not
   (check-pr-closes-test.sh, lint-hooks-test.sh) make ZERO git calls. So the
   check has no live positive to prove itself on. It needs a fixture that is
   deliberately non-compliant, or it ships unwitnessed.

I did not touch the repair; it is yours. Ping me if you want the reproducer
walked through — I have it cold.

--- agent-c, 2026-08-22, probing agent-b's item 2 before anyone builds on it ---

MEASURED on git 2.55.0, repo-plus-linked-worktree sandbox. The `re-init:` output
grep proposed above is worth having but CANNOT be the primary guard:

1. `warning: re-init: ignored --initial-branch=master` is printed ONLY when
   --initial-branch is also passed. A plain `git init <dir>` prints no warning.
2. The general line that IS printed — "Reinitialized existing Git repository in
   <path>", on STDOUT, not stderr — is suppressed by `-q`.

Every fixture builder in this repo uses `-q`. So the output grep would have
caught neither the 01:29 outage nor the one described next.

ITEM 3 IS NO LONGER TRUE — the check has a live positive. The audit above found
7 of 9 suites scrubbing and the other 2 making zero git calls, so the check
looked like it would ship unwitnessed. As of 2026-08-22 master's fleetctl-test.sh
carries `git init -q "$FLEET"` (line 900, from the gqlc-w6tl effort rows,
unscrubbed, the only git call in the file). PR #1122's scrub-lint went red on
that call when the branch rebased onto master.

Consequence, measured rather than inferred: pre-push runs that suite, so every
`git push` from any agent writes core.bare=true into the shared config. Observed
live (agent vzqi's push at 12:50:35Z, pre-push at 12:50:37Z, flip at 12:51:21Z),
then reproduced deliberately as an A/B in an agent-shaped sandbox —

    master's fleetctl-test.sh, GIT_DIR exported:  core.bare false -> TRUE
    PR #1122's fleetctl-test.sh, same sandbox:    core.bare false -> false

PR #1122 fixes that one call. This bead remains the general rule, and item 1 —
that the true rule reaches /tmp probe scripts and review harnesses, not just
.githooks/tests — is the part I would not lose. Say the general rule in the
refusal message even though the check is narrow.

WHEN IMPLEMENTING: agent-b found the vector, so ask him to design the
deliberately non-compliant fixture. A check that matches nothing is
indistinguishable from a codebase that obeys it.

2026-08-22T15:2xZ agent-a: RAISED P2 -> P1, on a fresh instance rather than on agent-k's say-so.

She mailed me that this bead is "the only thing that stops recurrence" of the
core.bare brick, and asked agent-c to reprice it. I am doing it instead so it does
not sit waiting for an agent who may be asleep.

I did NOT raise it to P0, and the reason matters more than the number. gqlc-tl78's
close audited all 9 shell suites: 7 carry `unset "${!GIT_@}"`, and the 2 that do
not (check-pr-closes-test.sh, lint-hooks-test.sh) make ZERO git calls. So there is
no live exposure today. The bead's own words are the right frame — the tree "is
exposed to the next edit."

THE FRESH INSTANCE, and it is why P1 rather than P2. The next edit is not
hypothetical; it is in review right now. PR #1247 adds
`.githooks/tests/fleetctl-overlap-test.sh`, 334 new lines, a TENTH suite. Measured by me
at head 5e8a61f9:

    unset "${!GIT_@}"   ABSENT
    git invocations     ZERO  (the two `git` matches are a comment on line 26 and
                              JSON fixture data on line 56, not calls)

So #1247 is NOT a defect and I want that stated plainly, because the cheap version
of this check would have called it one. It joins the population of unscrubbed
suites in the harmless quadrant, exactly where the other two sit. What it does is
grow that population by one while the rule that would protect it is enforced in a
single suite — which is this bead's title, arriving in the flesh within hours of
agent-k asking for the repricing.

The hazard is not the suite as written. It is that the FIRST person to add a git
call to fleetctl-overlap-test.sh — months from now, in a PR about something else,
reviewed by someone who has never heard of this — bricks the shared checkout for
fourteen agents, and every linked worktree stays green so nobody can see it.

Two additions from tl78's close that I do not want lost when this is taken up:
(a) the rule is not "suites must scrub", it is "anything invoked under a git hook
inherits a GIT_DIR that makes plain `git init <dir>` destructive" — which reaches
past .githooks/tests to reviewers' /tmp probe scripts and to agent spawn machinery;
(b) `warning: re-init:` is a cheaper and more general guard than enumerating either
call sites or config keys, because it is what git itself emits at the moment of the
destruction.

METHOD NOTE, since I nearly shipped this finding backwards. My first pass counted
matches with `grep -c '\bgit '` against the file, got 2, and I was one step from
mailing a reviewer that a suite under review made unscrubbed git calls. Both matches
were prose. Count invocations by reading the lines, never by counting the pattern.
I also ran the first check against a FETCH_HEAD in the shared cwd rather than the
worktree I had fetched into, and got `path does not exist` — the shared-cwd stale
ref trap, twice in one measurement.

--- AGENT-B'S FRAMING, adopted over mine — agent-a 2026-08-22T15:41Z ---

His words, attributed, because they are tighter than the version I had been
using and I would rather the bead carry the better sentence:

  "Every merge that APPENDS to a shared registry invalidates every open PR that
   appends to the same registry. The expensive part is not the conflict, it is
   that the author learns about it only if they happen to look."

The second sentence is the finding. A conflict is a normal cost of concurrency;
a conflict nobody is told about is a stall. The three registries we have named:

  .githooks/tests/fleetctl-test.sh   EXPECTED_ROWS pin
  fleet/bin/fleetctl               the usage/case pair
  justfile                     the test-hooks recipe

LIVE, NOT THEORETICAL: #1247 was knocked from CLEAN to DIRTY through the
justfile within ten minutes of a merge, and its author had no signal. That is
what raised this bead from P2 to P1.

--- RETRACTION of the note immediately above — agent-a 2026-08-22T15:43Z ---

THE PRECEDING NOTE ("AGENT-B'S FRAMING, adopted over mine") DOES NOT BELONG ON
THIS BEAD. Disregard it here. It is about shared-registry APPEND CONFLICTS —
fleetctl-test.sh's EXPECTED_ROWS pin, fleetctl's usage/case pair, the justfile's test-hooks
recipe — which is gqlc-234l's subject, not this bead's. This bead is about the

I appended it from memory of which bead I had raised to P1 today, without
reading the title back. Correct home: gqlc-234l, where it now also lives. The
#1247 instance cited in that note is real; only its placement here is wrong.

title: the agent fleet: nothing proves 'just test' leaves the repo it runs in unchanged
description:
The fleetctl suite's fixtures reached outside their own TMP and damaged the repo under test: core.bare flipped to true on the SHARED config, the agent worktree's branch was force-moved onto a fixture commit and then parked on a fixture branch, and a fixture identity (user.email=fleetctl@test) was written into the shared config where it sat until a commit hook refused the address days later. bd gqlc-ed2u fixed that suite and gave it rows that witness each damage shape.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING is the systemic half: no gate proves that running the tests does not modify the repo. Every observation above was made by hand, after the fact, by an agent that noticed its own branch had moved. The suites run under pre-push (just test -> test-hooks) with GIT_DIR exported by git as the agent worktree's gitdir, so any suite that forgets to scrub gets write access to the developer's own repo, and the failure is silent.

WANTED: a guard around the test run that snapshots the repo's own state (core.bare, HEAD, the checked-out branch, user.email/user.name, and whether the worktree is dirty in ways the run caused) and FAILS when the run changed any of it. Note the lesson from gqlc-z1qw and gqlc-ed2u alike: a check that warns and exits 0 is not a gate. Ask 'does it FAIL?', not 'is there a check?'.

Do not test this by pushing from a real worktree. The reproduction shape is a sandbox repo plus a linked worktree with GIT_DIR exported to the worktree's gitdir — /tmp/agent-c-ed2u/mutate-suite.py on the gqlc-ed2u branch builds exactly that and can be lifted.
notes:

It must run cmd, then verify IN A TRAP, so that verification happens even when
cmd fails. The suite has a row for exactly that case (inner failed AND damaged);
a guard that verified only on the success path would report the test failure
and hide the damage, which is the worse half of the pair.

SNAPSHOT THE WHOLE `git config --list --local`, not a named key set. In a
linked worktree that reads the SHARED config, which is the damaged surface.
Snapshotting the whole thing is what lets a row assert on `some.inventedkey`
— the guard must catch a key nobody taught it the name of, which is the
enumeration complaint gqlc-n8n0 and gqlc-kl2d both raise. Plus HEAD sha and
symbolic-ref.

## THE ONE THING I HAD NOT MEASURED, AND IT IS THE SHIP RISK

Whether a clean `just test` on master leaves the tracked tree byte-identical.
If bd's auto-export rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl during the run — and bd's
export is known to lag and fire on a debounce — a worktree-dirtiness assertion
gives a FALSE RED on every honest run, and a gate that cries wolf gets switched
off, which is worse than no gate. MEASURE THIS BEFORE including dirtiness in
the snapshot. The config+HEAD half is safe regardless; ship that half first if
the measurement is awkward.

## SANDBOX SHAPE IS LOAD-BEARING (from gqlc-tl78, which I closed today)

Every fixture must be a repo PLUS A LINKED WORKTREE with GIT_DIR exported to
the worktree's gitdir. In a plain repo the damage CANNOT OCCUR — git decides
bareness from the gitdir's NAME, and only `.git/worktrees/<agent>` fails to end
in `.git`. Build it flat and all seven dangerous rows go green while testing
nothing. The suite says this at the top; keep it there.

the seam (kl2d = prevention at the call site, 2zet = detection at the boundary)
and undertook not to touch lint-hooks or the suites' scrub lines. If she would
rather hold it, hand it back — 246c09ea is the whole of my work.

title: pre-push: the GQLC_ALLOW_MISSING_LINTER hatch is unreachable when the linter is present and panicking
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 by agent-g while pushing PR #1029, blocked by gqlc-35sw.

.githooks/pre-push is shaped:

    if just ensure-golangci >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        just lint-new
    elif [ "${GQLC_ALLOW_MISSING_LINTER:-}" = "1" ]; then
        echo 'WARN: golangci-lint unavailable; lint SKIPPED ...'
    else
        echo 'ERROR: could not provision golangci-lint ...'; exit 1
    fi

The hatch is documented as 'narrower than git push --no-verify, which drops the test run above with it' — i.e. it is the sanctioned way out when the lint leg cannot run. It is guarded by ensure-golangci FAILING.

THE DEFECT: the failure agents actually hit (gqlc-35sw) is the linter provisioning PERFECTLY and then panicking — golangci-lint v2.12.2, built with go1.26, loading the local go1.27.0 toolchain's go list output. ensure-golangci returns 0 (binary present, version matches the pin), so control takes the FIRST branch and dies inside 'just lint-new'. The elif is never evaluated. Setting GQLC_ALLOW_MISSING_LINTER=1 has no effect whatsoever on this failure.

CONSEQUENCE: an agent hitting a panicking linter has NO non-violating way to push. The only remaining lever is git push --no-verify, which Article IV.4 forbids and which additionally drops the full 'just test' leg. The documented narrow escape does not cover the case, and its absence is silent — the agent sees a panic stack, not 'the hatch does not apply to you'.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the hatch's own comment enumerates causes at length — 'no network; HTTP 429 or another rate limit from raw.githubusercontent.com or the release CDN; a proxy or firewall blocking either host; a pinned version whose release is not published; a corrupt or unwritable .bin/' — and closes with 'The list is open, which is why an unrecognised cause blocks instead of passing'. Every listed cause is a PROVISIONING cause. The thoroughness of the enumeration is what makes the gap read as covered. 'Unavailable' and 'available but broken' are different branches and the comment only ever considers the first.

THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF gqlc-35sw. gqlc-35sw is the toolchain skew and will be fixed by pinning GOTOOLCHAIN or bumping golangci-lint. This bead survives that fix: the next time the linter is present and fails for any reason that is not provisioning — a config error, an OOM, a bad .golangci.yml, a plugin crash — the hatch will be unreachable again.

WHAT IS WANTED: decide, deliberately, what an agent should do when the linter runs and fails NON-DIAGNOSTICALLY, and make the hook say it. Options worth weighing rather than assuming: widen the hatch to cover a lint-new that exits on a signal or a non-lint exit code; distinguish 'lint found issues' (must block, always) from 'lint could not form an opinion' (may take the hatch); or keep it blocking but print the diagnosis and the escape that DOES apply, so the agent is not left with only --no-verify. The failure mode to avoid is the obvious over-correction — a hatch that swallows real lint findings.

Verification note for whoever takes it: the reproducer needs no broken toolchain. Any command that makes 'just lint-new' exit non-zero while 'just ensure-golangci' exits 0 exercises it.
notes:
CLAIMED and REPRODUCED 2026-08-22 by agent-g. Worktree ../gqlc-m9ca, branch fix/pre-push-lint-hatch off origin/master b702545a.

THE REPRODUCTION, and it corrects a premise in my own description above.

I filed this bead saying the linter 'panics'. It does not. Measured first-party in
gqlc-agent-agent-g at 33145859 with the machine default toolchain:

  ./.bin/golangci-lint run --new-from-rev origin/master
  ../../../../../usr/lib/go/src/crypto/internal/randutil/randutil.go:11:2:
      could not import math/rand/v2 (... method must have no type parameters) (typecheck)
  ../../../../../usr/lib/go/src/crypto/internal/randutil/randutil.go:21:5: undefined: rand (typecheck)
  2 issues:
  * typecheck: 2
  rc=1

EXIT CODE 1 — THE SAME CODE golangci-lint USES FOR 'I FOUND REAL ISSUES'. That kills
the obvious fix. My description offered 'widen the hatch to cover a lint-new that exits
on a signal or a non-lint exit code' as an option; there is no such code here. Anything
keyed on the exit status cannot tell this from a genuine finding, and a hatch that opened
on exit 1 would swallow every real lint finding in the repo. Whoever reaches for exit
codes first, as I did, should stop here.

WHAT DOES DISCRIMINATE: the diagnostics are (typecheck) and their PATHS ARE OUTSIDE THE
REPO — /usr/lib/go/src, the toolchain's own standard library. The linter is not
reporting on this repo's code at all; it is reporting that it cannot read the stdlib the
machine's Go was built from. go.mod names go 1.26.6; the machine default is
go1.27.0-X:nodwarf5, a custom build. Same family as the govulncheck custom-build
handling already in justfile:1798-1801.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE EVERYWHERE, worth the next hunter's time: the SAME command in a fresh
worktree at origin/master (../gqlc-m9ca) returned '0 issues.' rc=0, both with
--new-from-rev origin/master and HEAD~5. It reproduces in gqlc-agent-agent-g and not in
gqlc-m9ca. I have not isolated why — build-cache state is the obvious suspect and I have
not proven it. Do not conclude from one clean worktree that this is fixed; that is the
same sampling error the hooksPath hunt hit tonight.

THE DESIGN DECISION, which this bead asked to be made deliberately rather than assumed:

  DO NOT WIDEN GQLC_ALLOW_MISSING_LINTER. Its name and its contract are about a linter
  that is MISSING. Widening it to cover 'present but unable to form an opinion' is the
  over-correction the description warns about, and here it is worse than usual because
  the only available signal (exit 1) is shared with real findings.

  INSTEAD: keep the block, and make the hook SAY WHICH FAILURE IT IS. When lint-new
  fails, classify the output; if it is typecheck diagnostics against paths outside the
  repo, print that the linter could not form an opinion, name the cause (a toolchain
  golangci-lint cannot read) and the remedy that makes the gate ACTUALLY RUN —
  GOTOOLCHAIN=<the go directive in go.mod>. Otherwise print the findings and block as
  today.

  THE SAFETY PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS THE RIGHT SHAPE: the classification changes only
  the MESSAGE, never allow/deny. Both branches block. So a misclassified failure costs a
  confusing sentence and can never cost a fail-open — which is not true of any variant
  that routes one class to a hatch.

  And it answers the bead's actual complaint better than a hatch would. The complaint is
  'an agent has no non-violating way to push'. GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 IS that way, and it is
  a fix rather than a bypass: the gate executes. I used it myself on PR #1029 tonight.
  If the linter genuinely cannot be made to run, the block stands and the answer is
  escalation, not a wider hatch.

Also to fix in the same change: the comment at .githooks/pre-push:19-33 enumerates five
PROVISIONING causes and closes 'the list is open, which is why an unrecognised cause
blocks instead of passing'. The thoroughness is what makes the gap read as covered.
'Unavailable' and 'available but broken' are different branches and the comment only
ever considers the first. — agent-g

PREMISE CORRECTION, measured 2026-08-22, and it changes what this bead is grounded on.

The toolchain-skew reproducer this bead was filed from is CLOSED at master. #1071
(merged 2026-08-21) bumped golangci_version v2.12.2 -> v2.13.1 in the justfile. v2.13.1
is built with go1.27.0 and reads this machine's default go1.27.0-X:nodwarf5 fine. In
../gqlc-m9ca at master, `just lint-new` under the default toolchain exits 0, 0 issues,
zero out-of-repo typecheck lines, zero panic markers.

It still reproduces in ../gqlc-agent-agent-g only because that older branch pins v2.12.2
and its .bin/ holds that binary. I got a genuine end-to-end witness there: the fixed
hook printed the typecheck diagnosis and the correct pasteable remedy
(GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6, this repo's own go directive), exit 1. Real linter, real failure,
no stub.

So the fix does NOT rest on the skew. It rests on the class the description already
named -- 'the next time the linter is present and fails for any reason that is not
provisioning'. That class has a live reproducer at the CURRENT pin, measured first-party:

  ./.bin/golangci-lint run --config /dev/null   ->  rc=3
  Error: can't load config: unsupported version of the configuration: ""

A present, healthy, correctly-pinned v2.13.1 failing for a reason no GOTOOLCHAIN moves.
Whoever reviews this should use exit 3, not the skew, as the standing reproducer.

WHAT THAT REPRODUCER CHANGED IN THE FIX. It caught a defect in my own first draft. The
draft printed one remedy block for every classified failure, so a bad .golangci.yml was
answered with 'Re-run the push under the toolchain go.mod names' -- a confident wrong
diagnosis of a real failure, the exact defect class PR #1029 spent eight rounds on. The
remedy now lives inside each branch and each branch says only what it is entitled to:
the typecheck branch has read the diagnostics and prescribes; the exit-code branch knows
only that the run was not a verdict, so it offers the toolchain fix conditioned on what
the output shows and says GOTOOLCHAIN will not move anything else.

Also verified first-party on the CURRENT pin (v2.13.1, not the version the earlier note
cites): `golangci-lint run --help` gives `--issues-exit-code int (default 1)`, and
neither the justfile nor .golangci.yml overrides it. So 1 is the only code meaning
'graded and found issues'.

STATE: .githooks/pre-push + .githooks/tests/tool-gate-test.sh modified. 71 passed /
0 failed. `just lint-hooks` clean. Mutation battery /tmp/mut-m9ca/run.py, 12 mutations
over both tells, the message-selection branch, the block decision, the tee, the remedy
fallback and the hatch: 12/12 killed, no no-ops, no syntax-error fake REDs.

title: hooks: just init's git-config half has no test row, while its install half now has several
description:
Noted 2026-08-21 while landing bd gqlc-4thl (PR #1044).

`just init` does two things: it sets `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`, and it
installs `.githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire` into the repository's default hooks
directory.

The second half is now covered — PR #1044 added rows for the install path, for
what counts as an ABSENT install, for the foreign-squatter refusal, and for the
atomic-per-file and atomic-as-a-set properties.

The first half has none. MEASURED: no row in
`.githooks/tests/hooks-drift-tripwire-test.sh` exercises `just init`'s
`git config` call. Grepping the suite for a row that runs init and then reads
back `core.hooksPath` returns nothing.

So the idempotence CONTRIBUTING.md promises ("The recipe is idempotent — running
it multiple times is safe") and the claim that init is the bootstrap for a fresh
clone both rest on reading the recipe, not on a row.

Worth pinning, at minimum:

  - a fresh clone with `core.hooksPath` unset: after `just init`, the value reads
    `.githooks` and a master commit is refused
  - the drifted shape (an absolute `.../.git/hooks`): after `just init`, the value
    is repaired rather than appended to or duplicated
  - a second `just init` changes nothing — the idempotence claim, which is the one
    CONTRIBUTING.md makes in as many words
  - init does not write to a worktree-local config when `extensions.worktreeConfig`
    is unset, since the shared-config blast radius is the whole point of gqlc-4thl

Not a blocker for #1044: that PR's scope was the detector, and it does not change
init's config half. Filed so the gap is recorded rather than inferred from the
absence of failures.
notes:
--- HELD FROM ROUTING — agent-a, 2026-08-22T02:15Z.

Deliberately unlabelled. `just init`'s git-config half is reached through the
justfile, and PR #1057 (open) modifies `justfile`. Routing this now puts two
branches on that file.

Its premise IS on master, so this is a collision hold, not an absent-premise hold
— the two have different release conditions and it matters which one you are
reading. See gqlc-8zw7 for the union rule.

RELEASE: #1057 merges. Then label by class; no need to ask me.

PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P1 by agent-a, 2026-08-22T04:35Z. Article V.3; the reason,
because a reprioritisation without one is just an opinion:

`just init` is the ONLY repair the fleet has for core.hooksPath drift. Every
drift bead closes with "repaired with just init" (gqlc-hd68 says exactly that),
and the claude-pre-bash detector tells the agent "Repair: just init" in the
text of the warning itself. So this recipe is load-bearing for a defect that
showed THREE distinct signatures in recent history:

  gqlc-5fm   (2026-07-26)  .git/hooks, samples only
  gqlc-hd68  (2026-08-17)  .git/hooks, samples only
  gqlc-o13d  (2026-08-22)  /dev/null  — still open, agent-g
  plus two firings at me tonight with the .git/hooks value that I could not
  reproduce (occurrence recorded on o13d; unresolved whether real flap or a
  detector reading under a different env)

And its git-config half has no test row. That is the exact shape tonight's
postmortem names as the fleet's central lesson:

    "A guard and its reachability are two separate things, and only one of
     them gets tested. Any guard worth having needs a row asserting it FIRES."

Here it is worse than that — the thing untested is not the guard but the
REPAIR, and o13d's title already reports that the repair "does not hold." We
cannot tell whether it does not hold because something rewrites it afterwards
or because the recipe's config half is broken, and we cannot tell precisely
because there is no row.

Not raised to P0: nothing is currently broken-and-unnoticed because of this,
and o13d (P0) is the live incident. This is the reason o13d is hard to close.

Whoever takes it: the row should assert the CONFIG VALUE CHANGES, not that
`just init` exits 0 — it exits 0 today while its config half is unwitnessed,
which is the same fail-silent shape. Mutate it: break the git-config line and
confirm the row goes red.

FIXED and merged: PR #1316, squashed to master 2026-08-23T03:38Z. Verified on
origin/master rather than on the branch: `git cat-file -e
origin/master:.githooks/tests/init-config-test.sh` succeeds.

The new suite drives the REAL `just init` against throwaway repositories, 21
rows, all four shapes this bead asked for:

  - a fresh clone with core.hooksPath unset: after init the value reads
    .githooks, AND the repo's own .githooks/pre-commit actually executes on a
    commit. The second is the load-bearing one. A value written to a config git
    never consults reads back through `git config --get` perfectly well, so a
    row asserting only the string would pass over exactly the failure that
    matters.
  - the drifted absolute shape ($GIT_COMMON_DIR/hooks, the spelling gqlc-5fm
    actually saw): repaired to .githooks, and `--get-all` returns exactly ONE
    value. `git config <name> <value>` replaces and `--add` appends; under
    `--add`, `--get` still reads .githooks while every consumer reading
    --get-all sees two.
  - idempotence, the claim CONTRIBUTING.md makes in as many words: a second init
    exits 0 and changes nothing. Compared over the WHOLE sorted local config,
    not over core.hooksPath alone, so a second run that added some other key is
    caught too.
  - a linked worktree. This is gqlc-4thl's blast radius asserted in the
    direction that matters: an init run from INSIDE a linked worktree lands in
    the config the main worktree reads, so repairing from one worktree repairs
    them all; extensions.worktreeConfig is not turned on; and no config.worktree
    file appears under the common dir.

CONTAINMENT, because the subject of this suite is a recipe that WRITES a config
fourteen agents share. Every invocation goes through run_init, which asserts the
fixture's --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir lands inside $TMP and exits
the suite if it does not - fatal rather than a 99 return, because a row
expecting a repair would go green on a bail-out that never entered the recipe.
GIT_* is unset at the top (a hook-borne GIT_DIR redirects a fixture's git at the
parent repo - the 2026-08-21 postmortem). And the enclosing repository's own
core.hooksPath is recorded before any row runs and compared at the end, which
catches an escape even when it happened to write the value the developer already
had.

    including both behavioural pre-commit rows.
  - `--add` instead of a set -> the value-count row, the idempotence row and the
    after-two-runs count row.
  - a trailing slash on the value -> 3 rows.
  - init rewritten to enable extensions.worktreeConfig and write --worktree ->

No mutant survived.

test-hooks` discover its suites by globbing .githooks/tests/ (bd gqlc-234l), so

title: just lint-new panics locally: golangci-lint built with go1.26 loads a go1.27 GOROOT
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 in two worktrees (gqlc-mb8v at PR #1043's head 5db9e301, and a detached worktree restored to the same SHA, main.go md5 89ae9181 = pristine): `just lint-new` exits 2 with

    panic: file requires newer Go version go1.27 (application built with go1.26)

and a go/types handleBailout stack out of golangci-lint's package loader. Local toolchain is go1.27.0-X:nodwarf5; .bin/golangci-lint is v2.12.2, built with go1.26; go.mod says go 1.26.6.

WHY IT MATTERS: the agent protocol requires `just fmt-check`, `just lint`, `just test` green before any PR (protocol forbids bypassing). `just test` and `just fmt-check` pass; the lint leg cannot be run locally at all on this machine, so every agent is currently opening PRs on a gate it could not execute. It fails loudly rather than silently, which is the good half — nobody is being told 'ok' — but the gate is unavailable, and the standing habit of reading a red local gate as 'environmental' is exactly how a real finding gets waved through.

NOT a code defect on any branch: reproduced on the untouched PR head. CI's lint job is green at the same SHA because the runner's toolchain matches what golangci-lint was built with.

WHAT IS WANTED: make the local leg run — provision a golangci-lint built against the toolchain go.mod names (or pin the local Go), and have the recipe fail with a diagnosis naming the mismatch rather than a panic stack when they disagree. title: close hook: --reason-file relative path is resolved against the hook cwd, not the close tuple's directory
description:
`reason_text` destructures the close tuple as `_, _, reason, reason_file = close`, discarding element 0 — the effective directory the tuple carries. A relative `--reason-file` is therefore opened against the HOOK's cwd rather than the directory bd will actually read it from.

Measured (round-5 review of PR #1029, residue row R2), with a decoy `reason.txt` in the hook cwd:
- `cd /tmp/lead/fx/bd && bd close gqlc-x --reason-file reason.txt` -> `allow-no-sha`, hook=allow, while the file bd will actually read cites an orphan sha.
- Same via `bd -C <dir> ... --reason-file reason.txt`.
- Control (hook cwd == effective dir) -> `deny-unpushed-sha`, DENY.

Exploitation needs a name collision — without one the open fails and the hook fails CLOSED — so this is a real hole but not a trivially reachable one.

Fix threads element 0 of the tuple through `resolve()` so the reason file is opened relative to the effective directory. That is a signature change on `reason_text` and its call sites. Wants rows for: relative path with a decoy present, relative path via `-C`, and absolute path unaffected.

title: hooks: no check on a rewritable artifact can stop core.hooksPath drift, because the writer is the actor
description:
Left open deliberately by the round-4 fix on branch `fix/hookspath-inert-detector` (PR #1044), which named it N1 and declined to close it. Filed so the reasoning does not live only in that branch's review log.

## The gap

`core.hooksPath` drift in the shared config is written by the Claude Code agent-worktree creation path (see gqlc-7ijy, which identifies the writer). Every mitigation on PR #1044 is a *check* — `just doctor`, `check-hooks`, the tripwire hooks themselves. All of them read an artifact the drifting actor can also write.

So the detector is sound against accidental drift and against a stale config, and unsound against the actual writer, which can restore `core.hooksPath` to `.git/hooks` after any check has passed. The check tells you drift happened; it cannot make drift not happen.

## Why the obvious half-measure was rejected

The fixer considered running the tripwire under a faked environment so a hook could tell whether it was invoked by git or by the recipe. It rejected it because moving that one key breaks the tripwire's own `git config --get`, which is how it reads the value it is checking. That is not a detail of the implementation; a check that must lie about the environment to observe the environment has a circularity, not a bug.

## What would actually close it

Unclear, and that is the point of filing rather than fixing. Candidates worth evaluating before anyone writes code:

- Repair rather than detect: make the check's self-heal arm authoritative and run it at a point the writer cannot follow.
- Move the value out of the shared config — `extensions.worktreeConfig` plus a per-worktree setting changes the blast radius from "all ~20 worktrees" to one, without closing the hole.
- Fix the writer (gqlc-7ijy) so nothing drifts, and treat every check here as defence in depth rather than as the gate.
- Accept detection as the ceiling at this layer and move enforcement to CI, where the actor has no write access to the config.

The last is probably the honest answer, and if so this bead closes by writing that down in CONTRIBUTING rather than by adding a guard.

## Related

- gqlc-7ijy — identifies the drift writer
- gqlc-pyk2 — the inert detector, fixed by PR #1044
- gqlc-4thl — the drifted-config incident itself

is the actor'. That is an argument about what is achievable, not a defect with a known fix, and
routing it to an author invites someone to implement a check that the bead itself says cannot
work. What is wanted first is a judgment: accept the claim and design around it (move the gate
somewhere the actor cannot rewrite), or falsify it. Related in-flight work: gqlc-4thl (PR #1044)
and gqlc-pyk2 sit in the same hooksPath family — read both before designing.

=== DESIGN (agent-m, gqlc-p159, 2026-08-22) ===

THE SHAPE, in plain words. Every rule our git hooks enforce is only as alive
as one line (core.hooksPath) in one file (.git/config) that ~90 worktrees,
every test fixture running under a hook, and the agent harness itself can all
write. Two writers were caught first-party this week (the harness's
worktree-isolated spawns — deterministic, o13d; a fixture hijacked by the
GIT_DIR git exports to hooks — PR #1128), and agent-m measured a live oscillation
that a sampling check can only ever report the phase of. The title's claim is
ACCEPTED: no check over that artifact can be the gate. The answer is not a
better check — it is to move each load-bearing rule to a layer its writers
cannot reach, and demote everything reading .git/config to fast feedback.
This bead therefore never touches .git/config at all. That is the point.

INVENTORY of what the hooks guarantee, and where the guarantee lands:
- Push-to-master refusal: ALREADY server-side. Measured 2026-08-22: ruleset
  "protect-master" (id 18407856, active, zero bypass actors) requires
  pull_request on the default branch, plus classic protection with
  enforce_admins and 7 required contexts. A direct push to master is refused
  by GitHub regardless of local hook state. NOTHING TO BUILD — but write it
  down (artifact 3), because the fleet spent tonight fearing a catastrophe
  that is already impossible.
- AI attribution (commit-msg hook): the one rule with a PERMANENT consequence
  (a bot contributor on the repo) and no server-side witness. Merge commits
  and rebase merges are enabled on the repo, so branch commits reach master
  verbatim; only squash+BLANK strips trailers. THIS is the gap. Artifacts 1-2.
- The hooksPath value itself: blast-radius work belongs to gqlc-o13d
  (per-worktree config, agent-g verifying) and the fixture/GIT_DIR class to
  gqlc-10co (shared env-clearing + failing gate, agent-k). OUT OF SCOPE here;
  do not duplicate either.

ARTIFACT 1 — .github/scripts/check_attribution.py (new, python3, stdlib only,
following the check-pr-closes.py pattern). One predicate set, three modes:
  --message-file F [--author-email E] [--committer-email E]
      exit 1 if the message carries an offending co-authored-by line or an
      email fails the identity predicate. Used by the commit-msg hook.
  --pr-commits-json F --expected-count N
      F is the raw JSON array from `gh api repos/$R/pulls/$N/commits
      --paginate`. Checks EVERY commit's message + author/committer emails.
      FAILS if the array length != N (the endpoint caps at 250 commits;
      a mismatch means unscreened commits — fail closed, say so in the
      message). Used by CI. On failure, name each offending SHA and why.
  --body-file F
      exit 1 if the PR body carries an AI-attribution footer. Used by CI.
Predicates (put them in one place in the file, commented as the single source):
  - co-authored-by: match lines ^co-authored-by:[[:space:]] case-insensitively
    ANYWHERE in the message whose value contains "claude" or "@anthropic.com"
    (case-folded). NOTE this is deliberately WIDER than the hook's current
    trailer-block-only scan (git interpret-trailers): a prose mention in a
    commit body now also refuses. Accepted behaviour change; state it in the
    script header. Reimplementing git's trailer folding in python is the
    alternative and was rejected — divergence risk for zero real traffic.
  - identity: exact denylist test@example.invalid, fixture@example.invalid,
    root@localhost, empty; suffixes @example.com, @example.org; then shape
    (must contain @, domain must contain a dot). Same as commit-msg's
    _check_identity today, plus fixture@example.invalid (the identity that
    actually landed on PRs #1133/#1134 — commit-msg's list missed it).
  - body footer: case-insensitive "generated with" within 3 lines of end OR
    anywhere matching "generated with [claude code]" / "🤖 generated with".
    Keep the predicate dumb and enumerable; no regex cleverness.

ARTIFACT 2 — two steps appended to the `tidy` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml,
both `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. tidy is ALREADY a required
context and ci.yml ALREADY runs on pull_request types
[opened, synchronize, reopened, edited] — the `edited` type and the
fetch-the-LIVE-body-via-API discipline exist precisely for the neighbouring
"check PR body carries Closes #N" step (bd gqlc-w4al). Follow that step's
shape exactly:
  step A "commits carry no AI attribution":
    env: GH_TOKEN, PR_NUMBER, EXPECTED: ${{ github.event.pull_request.commits }}
    gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}/commits" --paginate \
        > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/pr-commits.json"       # not piped, no || true —
    python3 .github/scripts/check_attribution.py \
        --pr-commits-json "${RUNNER_TEMP}/pr-commits.json" \
        --expected-count "$EXPECTED"

    array or concatenated arrays — parse with a small tolerant loader.)

close_reason:
Answered by PR #1318 (merged as 8542710d on origin/master), and the answer this bead guessed at is the one that held: detection is the ceiling for a CHECK, so stop checking the config.

WHAT WAS MEASURED FIRST. 2026-08-22, throwaway repo: with core.hooksPath=/dev/null, a commit carrying a Co-Authored-By trailer naming Claude LANDS with no hook run. The #1044 tripwire is blind to it by its own stated limit -- it sits in the git common dir's hooks directory, and git under a /dev/null drift looks in /dev/null and executes nothing. Git is fail-open there by design. So the ceiling is LOWER than this bead assumed: there is no position inside git that survives an arbitrary hooksPath value, and the mitigation this bead was filed against is not merely "unsound against the writer" but structurally blind to the shape actually observed.

WHAT SHIPPED. .githooks/gate-pushed-commits, run from .githooks/pre-push over the push's own ref list. It reads no config and asks nothing about hook state. It re-runs .githooks/commit-msg's trailer arm over every commit the push would PUBLISH. The property that makes it not-another-detector: a drift window only has to END before the push. It need not have been noticed, reported or repaired in time. That converts a one-shot per-commit gate into an idempotent, retroactive one.

Of the four candidates this bead listed: "repair rather than detect" and "move the value out of the shared config" were not taken. "Fix the writer (gqlc-7ijy)" is untouched. "Accept detection as the ceiling and move enforcement to CI" is HALF taken -- the local chokepoint is now enforced, the CI arm is filed as gqlc-a87p. The bead's own suggestion that it might close by writing this into CONTRIBUTING rather than adding a guard was DECLINED: a paragraph would not have caught the /dev/null commit measured above.

LIMITS, in the script header rather than implied: git push --no-verify skips it; a window still OPEN at push time kills it along with every other hook; merge commits are skipped, matching commit-msg's MERGE_HEAD arm; the identity arms are deliberately out of scope, switched off through commit-msg's own "skip if git var fails" escape rather than by handing it a fabricated person.

NOT VERIFIED: no automated test pins any of it. Eight rows were run by hand and are recorded in the PR body; gqlc-z8of carries the exact justfile registry line and nine rows each with the mutation that must kill it.

title:
git worktree add -b
origin/master sets upstream to master, so a bare push targets master
description:
CLAUDE.md's own sibling-worktree recipe is:

    git worktree add ../<repo>-<slug> -b <branch> origin/master

This sets the NEW branch's upstream to origin/master. A later bare `git push` in that worktree therefore resolves to master, not to the branch.

Measured 2026-08-19 in ../gqlc-agt0: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name '@{u}'` returned `origin/master` on branch `fix/vuln-unplaced-stdlib-assertions-covered`. The push was REFUSED, but only incidentally — push.default=simple refuses when the branch name and the upstream name differ. That is the only thing standing between this recipe and an agent pushing a feature branch's commits onto master.

Two things make it worse than it looks:
- Every agent worktree in this repo is created by that recipe, so every one of them carries the misconfiguration.
- The refusal message does not say 'your upstream is master'; it reads as an ordinary push failure, so the natural next move is to add a flag until it goes through.

Candidate fixes, in preference order:
1. Change the CLAUDE.md recipe to pass `--no-track`, or follow the add with `git branch --set-upstream-to` / an explicit first `git push -u origin HEAD`.
2. Set `push.default=current` for the repo so a bare push always targets the same-named remote branch.
3. A pre-push hook clause refusing a push whose resolved destination is master from a non-master branch.

(1) and (2) are not exclusive; (3) is the fail-closed backstop and is the only one that survives an agent typing the raw command from memory.

Verify any fix by creating a throwaway worktree with the documented recipe and asserting `@{u}` is not origin/master.
notes:

Implemented (1) + (3) + a third arm; (2) push.default=current DROPPED — repo scope means the shared .git/config, which this session was forbidden to write, and it would only mask the wrong upstream for push while git pull / @{u} / git status keep reading master.

  1. CLAUDE.md: 'git worktree add --no-track -b <branch> ../<path> origin/master' + 'git push -u origin HEAD'.
  3. .githooks/guard-push-destination, run first in pre-push: refuses a push whose RESOLVED destination is refs/heads/master|main unless the ref pushed IS that ref.
  +. just check-worktree-upstream, wired into just test: names a worktree already tracking master while it is latent (covers git pull, which the push guard cannot).

title: vuln: a grep -q consumer under pipefail conflates SIGPIPE with failure, so the platformtag self-test can refuse a fixture it matched
description:
> **Amended 2026-08-19.** Three claims in the original report were falsified by measurement while the fix was under review. They are corrected inline below; the full record of what was wrong and how each was refuted is in [the correction comment](https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/issues/1033#issuecomment-5350641756). The defect itself, and the fix, are unchanged.

`selftest_platformtag` in the `vuln` recipe pipes `go list -e "${tagflag[@]}" -f '{{.Dir}}' ./...` straight into `grep -qxF "${fixture}"`, under the `set -euo pipefail` the recipe sets at the top of its body.

`grep -q` exits as soon as it matches. The producer then takes SIGPIPE and reports 141, and under pipefail the pipeline's status is 141 even though grep MATCHED. The `if !` fires and the recipe prints 'is not in the set go list ./...' about a fixture that IS in the set, then exits 1.

Found by the Linus review of gqlc-agt0 (verdict `/tmp/lead/verdict-agt0-r1b.md` section 1). Reproduced deterministically by adding `sleep 0.2` to a stub go-list producer and changing nothing else — byte-identical error to the CI failure, with the fixture provably in the set. Unpatched flake rate measured at 1/500 idle and 1/300 under load.

This is a defect in the SHIPPING recipe, present on master, not introduced by any branch.

**Why it stays invisible here** — *corrected; the original said "two accidents: the fixture sorts last of 28, and the output fits a 64K pipe buffer". Both are false.* Sort order is not a guard at this site at all: `selftest_platformtag` issues the **tagged** listing (29 lines, fixture at 28), and the fixture is last only in the *untagged* listing, which this site never runs. Buffer-fit is neither sufficient nor necessary: a 1262-byte listing, 52x inside a 65536-byte pipe buffer, returned 141 in 20 of 20 runs when emitted a line at a time with a 20ms pause; and a 189,019-byte payload, 2.9x OVER the capacity, returned rc 0 in 60 of 60 when the match was on the last line. Size is not the variable in either direction.

What actually decides a piped site is a race — whether the producer still has a write to make when `grep` exits — and what settles it is the producer having none left once `grep` can first match. Nothing in the recipe's text settles that for `go list`, `scope` or `sort`, whose write counts follow buffering inside the producer. The real `go list` won the race in 100 of 100 runs in this checkout, which is a race won 100 times, not a guarantee.

It surfaced via gqlc-agt0's vulnguard harness because that runs the real recipe over a small throwaway tree. *Corrected:* it is not line-at-a-time emission that loses the race — the same 29-write producer without the pause returned 0 in 200 of 200 — but slowness relative to `grep`'s startup, which nothing here bounds.

**FIX:** read the listing into a variable and match with a herestring, which is what the recipe's other membership tests already do.

    listed="$(go list -e "${tagflag[@]}" -f '{{.Dir}}' ./...)" || exit 1
    if ! grep -qxF "${fixture}" <<<"${listed}"; then

*Corrected: the original called this site "the lone outlier".* There is a second site of the same shape in `selftest_tagblind`, and its polarity is worse — there a match means the guard *should* fire, so a SIGPIPE makes the `if` false and lets a regressed fixture through silently. Both are fixed together.

**ALSO:** the recipe's 'TWO HOUSE RULES' block already reasons about process-substitution statuses and about `set -e` inside command substitution. It should gain the third rule of the same family: a pipeline whose consumer can exit early conflates SIGPIPE with failure under pipefail. Because the deciding variable is not settled by anything in the recipe's text, that rule bans the shape rather than offering a test to apply to it.
notes:
2026-08-19 (Carmack, branch fix/vuln-unplaced-stdlib-assertions-covered, PR #1031): FIXED.

Correction to the FIX section above: justfile:1463 was NOT the lone piped site. selftest_tagblind's `if go list -e -f '{{.Dir}}' ./... | grep -qxF "${fixture}"` (was justfile:1363) is a second instance of the same shape, and there the polarity is worse — the match means the guard SHOULD fire, so a SIGPIPE 141 makes `if` false and the guard passes silently. Fail-open. Both sites converted to `x="$(go list ...)" || exit 1` + `grep -qxF ... <<<"${x}"`.

Third rule added to the recipe's house-rules block (now "THREE HOUSE RULES"), citing this bead.

Evidence, /tmp/probe-agt0-r2/: mktree.py replicates vulnguard's justfileFor + writeTree outside the test binary, with `--slow` inserting `sleep 0.2` into the stub's `go list ./...` emit loop (the OUTER loop — slowing go_dirs' inner one does nothing, it pipes into `sort -u`). Same generator, same sleep, only the recipe differs:
  recipe at 23d66ed5 (unpatched): 5/5 runs rc=1, "is not in the set 'go list ./...'"
  recipe with herestrings:        5/5 runs rc=0, message absent
Instrumented scratch copy printed `PROBE rc=141 shellopts=...errexit...pipefail` — SIGPIPE, with the fixture provably in the set (`grep -qxF "$F" <<<"$out"` rc=0 over the same listing).
CORRECTION 2026-08-19 (round-2 review, verified first-party by lead): the 'two accidents' account in this bead is wrong, and the error is not cosmetic.

Only ONE accident guarded master: go list fits its whole output in the pipe buffer, so it never writes again after grep matches and never takes SIGPIPE.

Sort order is NOT the second guard. selftest_platformtag issues the TAGGED listing. Measured in the worktree at cd0b37d4:
  go list -e -f '{{.Dir}}' ./...                -> 28 lines, platformtag at 28 (last)
  go list -e -tags tagblind -f '{{.Dir}}' ./... -> 29 lines, platformtag at 28 (NOT last)
The recorded '28 of 28' figure is of a command that site never issues.

selftest_tagblind is not protected by sort order in either direction: on a healthy tree its fixture is absent entirely.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the account invited the reader to check 'is my match last?' as an all-clear, and that check gives a false negative at the exact site that broke. Anyone auditing other pipelines with it would clear a broken one.

Also corrected: rule (3) summarised itself as 'every grep -q and grep -m1 in this recipe reads a herestring'. justfile:1445 is a grep -q in this recipe reading a FILE ARGUMENT — the summary was false one grep away from where it was written. The normative clause was correct; only the summary overreached. Now states that none reads a PIPE.

Carriers fixed: justfile comment, PR #1031 body, this bead. Commit cd0b37d4, comment-only, no executable line moves.
close_reason: PR #1031 merged as 359e48f8. SIGPIPE/pipefail race fixed at both sites (selftest_platformtag, selftest_tagblind) — verified on origin/master: no live pipe-into-grep -q remains, house rule 3 present. Closed #1033.

title: bd-gh-sync: the unmirrored-bead push is a read-modify-write with no lock, so concurrent runs mint duplicate GH issues that nothing can ever close
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-18. 18 of the 223 open GH issues were permanent zombies: an
open issue with NO bead pointing at it, whose title is byte-identical to a bead
that is bound to a DIFFERENT issue number. Because no bead carries the orphan's
number in external_ref, the close pass (bd-gh-sync lines 438-462, which keys on
external_ref) can never reach it. It stays open forever regardless of whether
the work lands.

THE 18 PAIRS (orphan -> canonical, bead):
  452->453 fer | 505->503 4np | 814->816 u91z | 815->818 f1yf | 817->819 65sl
  820->821 rxq9 | 875->876 t802 | 877->878 dc6k | 879->880 qv80 | 887->890 uc8f
  888->892 w1gc | 889->894 2xkf | 891->896 gyp5 | 893->898 0pb8 | 895->899 oh30
  897->900 komy | 928->930 drvx | 929->931 g3g6

EVIDENCE, counted rather than asserted:
- 16 of 18 pairs have byte-identical bodies (md5 of `gh issue view --json body`).
  The two exceptions are characterised below; neither weakens the account.
- 17 of 18 have the orphan created BEFORE the canonical, by 1-6 seconds.
- They arrive in bursts, not uniformly: 2026-07-28T03:23 (1), 2026-08-17T05:17
  (4), 07:47 (3), 08:40-41 (6), 13:40 (2).

MECHANISM THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS. .githooks/bd-gh-sync:405-426 is a
read-modify-write with no serialization:

    bd list --status all --limit 0 --json >"$_tmp/beads.json"     # READ
    ... python filter: print every bead with no external_ref ...
    bd github push $_ids                                          # WRITE

`bd github push` is what assigns external_ref. Between the READ and the WRITE
there is no lock: `grep -n 'flock|lockfile|\.lock|noclobber' .githooks/bd-gh-sync`
returns nothing. The hook fires from .githooks/pre-push:20 (and `pull` from
.claude/settings.json:29 and post-merge:11), so two concurrent agent sessions
each pushing will each snapshot the ledger before the other's push lands, each
see the same bead as unmirrored, and each mint an issue. The bead ends up
holding whichever external_ref was written last; the other number is orphaned.
The 1-6s separation and the burst clustering are what that race looks like.

NOT YET CONFIRMED: I did not reproduce the race, only showed it is unguarded and
that the artefacts match it. What would confirm it: two `bd-gh-sync push` runs
started concurrently against a scratch repo with one unmirrored bead, asserting
exactly one issue is minted. That test is also the fix's regression pin.

THE TWO EXCEPTIONS, stated because they bound the claim:
- 505/503 inverts the ordering (orphan 14s AFTER canonical) and the bodies differ
  by a trailing 'Tracked as bd `gqlc-4np`.' footer that only 505 carries. This
  pair is probably NOT the race; it looks like a hand-filed issue plus a minted
  mirror. It is included in the cleanup, not in the mechanism claim.
- 895/899 differ because 899 additionally carries a ~40-line 'AMENDMENT (PR #901
  round 7)' section. Same race shape, but the canonical was edited afterwards.

REMEDIATION ALREADY DONE (this is the manual workaround, not the fix): all 18
orphans closed as `not planned` with a comment naming the canonical, plus #892
(bead gqlc-w1gc, landed as PR #996 whose body carried no `Closes #892`). Open GH
issues went 223 -> 204. The remaining 204 are real: 198 open beads, 5
in_progress, 1 blocked.

SCOPE OF THE FIX:
1. Serialize the push pass (flock on a fixed path, or `set -o noclobber` lockdir),
   so a second concurrent run waits or exits rather than double-minting.
2. Re-read the ledger inside the lock rather than reusing the pre-lock snapshot —
   the same defect the existing comment at lines 430-433 already documents for
   the CLOSE pass ("Reusing the pre-push snapshot skips exactly the beads that
   were closed before their first push, leaving the mirror it just minted open
   forever"). That comment identifies the read-staleness hazard on one side and
   the push side has the same hazard, unfixed.
3. Add a reconciler for the orphans this has already produced and will produce
   until (1) lands: an open GH issue whose title matches a bead bound to a
   different number is a duplicate, and should be reported (not auto-closed).
4. Regression pin: the concurrent-run test described above, wired into
   .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh so `just test-hooks` reaches it.

Filed after the user asked why so many GH issues were open. The bookkeeping was
NOT the main story -- 198 of 204 are genuine open work -- but this defect is a
slow leak that adds a permanent zombie every time two sessions push at once.

title: modscope: a 'mod' submodule hides modscope callers from the sweep gate, and both readings agree so the differential stays silent
description:
Found reviewing PR #1001 (gqlc-6n9y) round 2, outside that PR's delta. Live on
master. Reproduced first-party on the real justfile against just 1.57.0 AND
1.55.1.

THE GAP. `just --dump`'s top-level keys are:

    aliases assignments doc first groups module_path modules recipes settings
    source unexports warnings

`justDump` reads only `recipes` (and within it `priors`, `dependencies[].recipe`,
`body`). A `mod` directive puts the submodule's recipes under **`modules`**, not
`recipes`. So a recipe living in a submodule is invisible to the reader.

WHY THE DIFFERENTIAL DOES NOT CATCH IT. This is the important half.
`TestParseJustfileAgreesWithJustOnThisJustfile` compares the raw-text reader
against `just --dump`. Both are blind to `modules` — the reader because it never
looks, the dump consumer because it only reads `recipes`. **Two blind readings
AGREE.** The differential's whole design assumes a disagreement surfaces a gap,
and this gap produces no disagreement.

REPRODUCER (appended to the real justfile, then restored to md5
0a50d4516460ddfcf332977a332cc85b):

    mod probe 'probe.just'
    # probe.just declares probe-caller whose body is
    #   go run ./internal/tools/modscope modules
    # with NO dependencies

    just 1.57.0 and 1.55.1: top-level recipes=29, modules=['probe']
    probe::probe-caller names modscope = True, deps = []
    --- PASS: TestEveryRecipeRunningModscopeSweepsProbesFirst
    --- PASS: TestParseJustfileAgreesWithJustOnThisJustfile

An unswept modscope caller, named by `just --dump`, passing the gate in silence.

CONTRAST, and this is what makes `mod` the dangerous one: `import 'sub.just'`
INLINES into `recipes`, so an imported caller is seen and the gate is loud. The
two directives look similar and behave oppositely here.

WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN A NOTE. The gate exists to guarantee every recipe that
runs modscope sweeps probes first. `mod` turns that guarantee off silently, in
the fail-OPEN direction, with no diagnostic anywhere.

A SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT TO FIX WITH IT. The test's "WHAT THIS DOES NOT REACH"
list does not name `mod`, and its bullet 2 says "Shapes this justfile does not
contain. It reports on these bytes" — which implies that bytes GAINING the shape
would produce a report. The probe put the shape in the bytes and got nothing. So
that bullet is false as written for this shape, independently of whether anyone
fixes the reader.

TWO ACCEPTABLE FIXES, DECIDE DELIBERATELY:
  - Read `modules` recursively and hold submodule recipes to the same gate; or
  - Refuse a justfile containing `mod` outright, so the gate fails CLOSED on a
    shape it does not model.
Either way, pin the choice with a row that RED-s if it flips. And whatever the
prose says afterwards must not claim a boundary over directives nobody enumerated
— `mod` was found by trying it, not by reading a list.

NOT MEASURED: whether `mod` is likely to appear here, and whether ciguard's
justfile reader shares the blind spot. That second question is worth asking —
see gqlc-sgot / gqlc-lisu.

Related: gqlc-6n9y (the PR that surfaced it).

(15634 bytes). Round-2 fix log: /tmp/lead/fix-98ii-r2.md (5750 bytes).

title: codegen: runCorpus discards every subtest event, so a whole subtest tree can go silent unnoticed
description:
Same class as gqlc-wla6 (PR #1002), one level down, and live on master in BOTH
packages today.

`internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go:212` and
`internal/codegen/age/corpus_test.go:143`:

    if event.Action == "pass" && event.Test != "" && !strings.Contains(event.Test, "/") {

The `!strings.Contains(event.Test, "/")` clause drops every SUBTEST pass event,
keeping only top-level ones. That is deliberate — the census compares top-level
test names against the `corpusTests` list, and counting subtests would break the
comparison. The gap is what the filter also buys:

**A top-level test can pass while every subtest under it stops running, and this
census cannot tell.** The name still arrives as a top-level `pass`, `corpusTests`
still matches, `ElementsMatch` is satisfied, and the non-empty guard added by
#1002 is satisfied too. Nothing here observes subtest-level silence.

This is the aggregate-emptiness shape that gqlc-wla6 was opened to close, moved
down one level: the guard proves the SET of top-level names is right and
non-empty, and says nothing about whether anything ran INSIDE them.

WHAT TO MEASURE BEFORE FIXING (do not assume the gap is reachable):
  - Do the corpus fixture's tests actually HAVE subtests? If none do, the gap is
    latent rather than live, and the bead should say which it is rather than
    asserting either.
  - Mutate: make a subtest tree vacuous (e.g. empty the table it ranges over)
    while leaving the top-level test passing, and check the census stays GREEN.
    A GREEN there is the witness; without it this is a code reading, not a
    defect.

SCREENS (these cost real rounds on #1002, do not rediscover them):
  - `go test -c` is NOT the screen here (gqlc-hreu) — the fixture compiles one
    module DOWN. Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log.
  - Assert `\[(build|setup) failed\]` absent — BOTH spellings. A fixture parse
    error prints `[setup failed]`, not `[build failed]`.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on `^[[:space:]]*--- PASS`, never `^ *--- PASS`: testify
    indents with TABs and the space-only class reported 0 where the truth was 21.

Related: gqlc-wla6 (the top-level guard), gqlc-hreu (the wrong screen).

title: hooks: git rebase -i reword bypasses the AI-attribution commit-msg gate under hooksPath drift
description:
Behavioural, not prose. Found while reviewing PR #992 (gqlc-wa8c) round 3; the
branch's own prose sweep was correct and this was outside it.

`git rebase -i` with a **reword** fires `pre-commit` and `commit-msg` — two of
the four hooks — where every in-tree statement says rebase fires none. Measured
first-party in two independently written fixtures, and reproduced by the round-4
reviewer in a third:

    rebase -i REWORD (editor=true)  rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[commit-msg,pre-commit]
    rebase -i REWORD (real editor)  rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[commit-msg,pre-commit] subject="C reworded"
    rebase plain (control)          rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[]
    commit (control)                rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[commit-msg,pre-commit]

rc=0 and the subject really changed, so the row is not vacuous. Exactly the four
hooks this repo ships were armed and nothing else fired.

WHY IT MATTERS: `rebase` is outside `HOOK_GATED` and
`.githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh:355` pins it warn-only. So while
`core.hooksPath` is drifted, a reword silently skips `commit-msg` — which is the
hook enforcing the no-`Co-Authored-By: Claude` rule. Agent spawns rewrite
`core.hooksPath` in the SHARED git config (see gqlc-7y7e and the hooksPath-drift
bead), so the drifted state is reachable in normal operation, not hypothetical.

The in-tree rationale for leaving rebase ungated is pre-existing and honestly
hedged. The gap is that the shape survey behind it missed the reword path.

NOT YET MEASURED, do not claim a closed enumeration: `--autosquash`, `--onto`,
`--root`, merge-preserving and conflict-resume paths were measured firing none;
other rebase shapes were not enumerated at all.
notes:
=== REPRODUCED FIRST-PARTY, THEN CLOSED BY A TRIPWIRE, 2026-08-19 (Carmack) ===

VERIFIED THE HOLE BEFORE FIXING IT, as asked. Fixture: a throwaway repo whose
.githooks/commit-msg refuses a Co-Authored-By naming claude, i.e. this repo's
gate in miniature. GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR flips pick->reword; GIT_EDITOR writes a
message carrying `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

  HEALTHY (core.hooksPath=.githooks): the gate fires, the rebase HALTS, the
    trailer is NOT on HEAD. So the gate does cover a reword when hooks are live.
  DRIFTED, no tripwire: "Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/master",
    and `git log -1 --format=%B | grep -ci claude` = 1. The trailer LANDED.
    That is this bead's claim, reproduced, with the smuggled trailer on HEAD
    rather than inferred from which hooks fired.
  DRIFTED, tripwire installed: HEAD does not move (before==after), rebase halts.

FIXED IN 43ade486. `just init` now installs .githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire into
the git common dir's hooks/ as pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push, post-checkout
and post-merge. Under drift that directory is exactly what git runs, and a
reword fires pre-commit and commit-msg -- which under drift ARE the tripwire.
So the reword path is refused rather than gated: the fix does not depend on
teaching anything about rebase shapes, which is what keeps it from inheriting
this bead's own warning that the shape enumeration is incomplete
(--autosquash, --onto, --root and the conflict-resume paths were never
enumerated). Any rebase shape that writes a commit reaches pre-commit or
commit-msg and hits the tripwire; any shape that writes no commit had no
message to smuggle.

  "drifted: the reword did not smuggle an AI-attribution trailer onto HEAD"

title: hooks: PR #946 core.hooksPath drift detector is inert in the shared repo, because .claude/settings.json runs the WORKING-TREE copy of claude-pre-bash
description:
MEASURED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, 2026-08-18. This is the repository signature defect — a branch that breaks the rule it was written to establish — in the gate built to prevent it.

PR #946 (bead gqlc-nzwa, merged 96ef5473) is titled "hooks: detect core.hooksPath drift on the first Bash call, not the next just test". It added drift detection to .githooks/claude-pre-bash. Master copy: `grep -c hooksPath` = 8.

IT DID NOT FIRE. During this session core.hooksPath drifted twice from `.githooks` to the empty default dir `/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/hooks`, disarming .githooks/commit-msg (the AI-attribution gate) and every other hook repo-wide. I was not warned either time. The drift was found by a PR reviewer doing unrelated work, not by the detector.

ROOT CAUSE. .claude/settings.json wires the hook as a RELATIVE path: `"command": ".githooks/claude-pre-bash"`. That resolves against the WORKING TREE, not against master. The shared repo cwd is parked on branch `chore/bd-ledger-p2`, which has DIVERGED from master (`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/master` = false). Its copy of .githooks/claude-pre-bash predates #946: `grep -c hooksPath` = 0.

So the detector exists in master and is inert in the one place it is supposed to run. Same family as the known trap "the shared cwd is a stale ref — grepping it answers about its parked branch, not master", but with a gate rather than a grep as the victim.

THE TRIGGER IS PER-SPAWN, NOT ONE-OFF. Measured: I restored core.hooksPath to .githooks, spawned one agent, and the value had reverted to the default dir on the next read. Agent-worktree registration rewrites the local [core] section of the shared .git/config. A concurrent reviewer independently observed the same recurrence across its own session and reported it. So any repair that is a one-time `git config` is not a fix.

WHY P1. The disarmed set includes commit-msg, which is the only automated enforcement of the no-AI-attribution rule. Every commit made in the shared repo during a drift window is ungated. It is also self-concealing: the gate that would report the condition is the gate the condition disables.

ACCEPTANCE, and note a detector that exits 0 is not a gate:
1. The drift is reported on the first Bash call REGARDLESS of which branch the working tree is parked on. Demonstrate by parking the shared cwd on a pre-#946 commit, drifting core.hooksPath, and watching the warning still fire.
2. Re-verify after an agent spawn specifically, since that is the live trigger.

DESIGN NOTE, not a ruling — the fix likely cannot live only in the working-tree script, since that is precisely what goes stale. Candidates worth weighing: an absolute or git-common-dir-anchored path in settings.json; running the hook from a location that does not track the parked branch; or having the hook re-exec master version. Whoever takes this should also ask whether any OTHER .claude/settings.json hook has the same staleness exposure, because the answer bounds how much this class costs.
notes:
=== NOT CLOSED. The HARM is closed by 43ade486; the LATENCY is not. (Carmack 2026-08-19) ===

Saying explicitly which half my branch reaches, rather than leaving it to be
inferred from a merged PR.

WHAT IS CLOSED. This bead's stated severity is "every commit made in the shared
repo during a drift window is ungated", and that is gone. 43ade486 installs
.githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire into the git common dir's hooks/ -- the directory
the drift redirects core.hooksPath at -- so during a drift window a commit and a
push are REFUSED, from any branch the working tree is parked on, in every linked
worktree at once. Measured in throwaway repos: commit blocked, push blocked,
commit from a linked worktree blocked, `git rebase -i` reword blocked, healthy
state silent and unaffected. The carrier is outside the working tree, which is
the constraint this bead's own design note identifies and which no tracked file
can satisfy.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, i.e. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1 AS WRITTEN. "The drift is
reported on the first Bash call REGARDLESS of which branch the working tree is
parked on." My branch does not touch that path. .claude/settings.json is TRACKED
and wires the hook by the tree-relative path `.githooks/claude-pre-bash`, so on a
checkout parked at a pre-#946 commit BOTH files are the old ones. No edit to
either can fix a checkout parked before that edit -- that is the root cause this
bead identifies, and it is unfixable from inside the tracked tree by
construction. The remaining carriers are (a) an untracked working-tree file --
but .claude/settings.local.json is per-worktree, so it arms one worktree where
.git/hooks arms all of them, which is strictly worse; and (b) something outside
the repo, e.g. a PreToolUse hook by absolute path in ~/.claude/settings.json,
which is a machine-global edit affecting every project and is not a repo change.
I did not make that call unilaterally.

SO THE RESIDUE IS LATENCY, NOT EXPOSURE. Before: drift was silent and commits
were ungated. After: drift is silent until the next commit or push, which then
fails loudly and names `just init`. The window between the drifting write and
the report is no longer a window in which anything ungated can land. Whether
that is still worth a P1 is the lead's call; my reading is it is not, and this
bead should either be re-scoped to "report drift earlier than commit time" or
closed in favour of gqlc-7ijy's option 2 (keep agents off harness worktrees,
which removes the write instead of reporting it).

ALSO ANSWERED, since this bead asks it: "whether any OTHER .claude/settings.json
hook has the same staleness exposure". Yes, one. Round 1's table:
  PreToolUse/Bash  .githooks/claude-pre-bash            tree-relative -> stale
  SessionStart     .githooks/bd-gh-sync pull            tree-relative -> stale
  SessionStart     bd prime                             PATH lookup   -> not exposed
  PreCompact       bd prime                             PATH lookup   -> not exposed
So bd-gh-sync has the identical exposure: parked on an old branch, the session
runs that branch's sync script. That bounds the class at two, and neither is
touched by 43ade486.
2026-08-19 lead: branch fix/hookspath-inert-detector at 43ade486, NOT pushed, no PR yet. Round-1 adversarial review = REVISE (/tmp/lead/verdict-hookspath-r1.md). Design confirmed sound: carrier premise holds (git rev-parse --git-common-dir from a linked worktree returns the main .git, so one install arms all 73 registered worktrees); both drift shapes fail closed; healthy state provably silent (measured: git does NOT fall back to .git/hooks/<name> when core.hooksPath is set); gqlc-b1kt reproduces on all three arms. TWO BLOCKERS: F1 - 'git ignores the exit status of both of these' is FALSE for post-checkout (measured rc=1 on git checkout -b AND git switch; githooks(5) says the exit status BECOMES theirs). True for post-merge only. F2 - check-hooks certifies presence not function: a 3-line file (shebang + marker + exit 0) installed as all five names makes just doctor print 'ok' while a drifted commit LANDS; same for any cp-truncation between 48 and ~2900 bytes. LEAD DECISION: adopt the reviewer's 8.4 - change check-hooks arm 2 from REFUSE to SELF-HEAL (precedent: ensure-golangci, already cited in .githooks/pre-push). Reason: measured, git push --no-verify skips .githooks/pre-push wholesale, dropping just test AND just lint-new, so a refusal unrelated to your commits makes --no-verify the shortest path. Arm 1 (core.hooksPath itself) stays a hard refusal. F3 (cp -> tmp+mv atomic rename) is a hard prerequisite. Round-2 fixer in flight (agent fix-hookspath-r2, log -> /tmp/lead/impl-hookspath-r3.md).
close_reason:
Closed by PR #1318 (merged as 8542710d on origin/master), together with PR #1044 which landed earlier the same night. Three parts, and one of them is a falsification of this bead's own proposed repair.

1. THE ROOT CAUSE AS FILED IS RIGHT BUT THE REMEDY IS IMPOSSIBLE. This bead reads the defect as a PATH problem: .claude/settings.json wires the hook as ".githooks/claude-pre-bash", relative, so it resolves against the working tree, so a checkout parked on a diverged branch runs a copy that predates the detector. The design note offers "an absolute or git-common-dir-anchored path in settings.json". That cannot work, because .claude/settings.json is ITSELF A TRACKED FILE: a checkout parked before the fix reads its own copy of settings.json and never learns the new path. The path is not the stale thing; the file naming the path is. Every tracked artifact has this shape. The escapes are an untracked carrier (.claude/settings.local.json, ~/.claude/settings.json) or the git common dir, and only the last can be shipped by a commit -- which is exactly what #1044 did for the git-hook channel. This is now written into .githooks/claude-pre-bash's limits block so the next reader does not re-derive it.

Acceptance clause 1 as literally worded ("reported on the first Bash call REGARDLESS of which branch the working tree is parked on") is therefore not met and cannot be met by any commit. What bounds it today is CLAUDE.md's rule that the shared checkout stays on master and every session cuts a sibling worktree from origin/master. Measured 2026-08-22: the shared cwd is on master and core.hooksPath is .githooks. That is a discipline, not a gate, and it is recorded as such rather than claimed closed.

2. THE LIVE TRIGGER IS COVERED, from a carrier the parked branch cannot stale. #1044 installs .githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire into the git common dir's hooks directory -- the directory the drift redirects execution to -- so it refuses the commit or the push in the drifted state, on any branch, in every linked worktree at once. Verified present on this machine 2026-08-22: all five names installed. Separately, master's claude-pre-bash now handles the env-borne shape this bead's trigger produced (GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS carrying core.hooksPath, bd gqlc-o13d), which no one-time git config could have repaired.

3. THE RESIDUE NAMED IN "WHY P1" IS NOW GATED. This bead's strongest point was that "every commit made in the shared repo during a drift window is ungated", commit-msg being the only automated enforcement of the no-AI-attribution rule. Nothing re-screened that history. PR #1318 adds .githooks/gate-pushed-commits, wired into pre-push, which re-runs commit-msg's trailer arm over every commit the push would publish. Measured 2026-08-22: a commit made under "git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null" carrying a Co-Authored-By trailer naming Claude lands, and is then refused at push with its sha and subject named. A drift window now only has to END before the push.

NOT VERIFIED. No automated test pins part 3 -- eight rows run by hand, recorded in PR #1318's body; gqlc-z8of carries the suite that should exist and the justfile line that registers it. Nothing covers a drift window still OPEN at push time, nor "git push --no-verify"; that is gqlc-a87p, the CI arm.

title: factory: /tmp tmpfs exhausts inodes, and the failure looks like a broken tree rather than a full disk
description:

MEASURED: /tmp is a 16G tmpfs shared by every agent. At 91 registered git worktrees it reached 1048576/1048576 inodes with 4.3G bytes still free. Consequences observed:

The second is unreliable -- quota walls and stall watchdogs kill agents with no warning, which is precisely how these accumulated.
