title: codegen: implement the nullable-list-element answer chosen by gqlc-sokgc
description:
EXECUTION STUB for the design bead gqlc-sokgc. Filed at intake by agent-a so the design has somewhere to hand off to. It deliberately contains NO design.

Do not begin until gqlc-sokgc is closed. It names three candidates -- (a) render a nullable element as *T, (b) refuse at codegen with a named sentinel, (c) degrade to any -- and each trades a different thing. Two of the three are BREAKING to already-generated code, so which one is chosen changes what this bead is entirely. Implement what the design chose.

WHAT gqlc-sokgc ALREADY GIVES YOU, so you do not re-derive it:
  - the site: internal/codegen/prepare.go, buildListElemPlan's ResolvedProperty
    arm (~line 1259). It reads tt.Type for the width and never reads
    tt.Nullable. The one place Nullable IS written is the nested recursion just
    below, whose recursive call then ignores it too -- so the field is set and
    never read on this path.
  - the reproducing fixture: certified_list_element (added by gqlc-t0bk), over
    'score :: INT64' nullable, query 'RETURN [p.score, p.score] AS scores'.
  - the expected emission today, with the bare 'elem.(int64)' assertion that
    fails on the first NULL.
  - BOTH BACKENDS must move together: neo4j-go-v5 and apache-age-pgx-v5 render
    the identical signature and the identical assertion today. A fix that
    changes one is a divergence, not a fix.

SCOPE FENCE the design already set: this is PRE-EXISTING and general. A stored
LIST<INT64> with nullable elements has always gone through the same arm. What
gqlc-t0bk changed is the REACH, deliberately and under a ruling
(docs/specs/model-change-f45qn-ref-valued-leaves.md §6). Do not treat gqlc-t0bk
as the regression to revert.

NO-RULING CLAUSE: if the design concludes the current fail-closed behaviour is
the right answer and the remedy is documentation rather than code, this stub
closes as unnecessary, citing gqlc-sokgc. That is a legitimate outcome.

PRICING: P2, priced once with gqlc-sokgc. Product work under V.3.1, so V.3.2's
below-floor rule does not bind it.
notes:
DESIGN (gqlc-sokgc, agent-i, 2026-09-04). Implementation-ready plan. Every code assertion below was checked against origin/master 6974045b on this date.

== The problem in plain words ==

The resolver commits to element-position nullability (scope.go:1032: unify ORs it; the stored-list path computes `Nullable: !ElemNotNull()`), and codegen throws it away: `buildListElemPlan`'s ResolvedProperty arm (prepare.go ~1360-1428) maps the element type and drops `tt.Nullable`; both backends' TypeMap.Property list arms emit `"[]" + elemTy` without ever reading ElemNotNull. So a schema that declares `LIST<INT64>` (elements nullable) generates `[]int64`, and the first NULL element fails the emitted decode at runtime: neo4j's walk asserts `elem.(int64)` on a nil interface (always false), AGE's element decoder meets the literal "null".

== Decision: candidate (a) — a nullable list element renders as *T ==

The element position obeys the same rule as every other position. This is not a coin-flip; it is compelled by three standing commitments:

1. CONTEXT.md "Nullable" (:214): "Codegen emits the corresponding result as a pointer or option type." Both backends already wrap EVERY nullable position uniformly — entity fields (`neo4j/render_models.go:169-173`, including `*any` at :356 for shapeless), row fields (`render_queries.go:203/:219`), params. The element position is the one position exempted, and the exemption is the bug.
2. The resolver has already committed. scope.go:1032's comment says nullability "is the one field that composes, and it ORs". A backend that discards a committed field is lying about the schema (ADR 0002 fidelity).
3. The break is bounded and compile-loud. `LIST<T NOT NULL>` (ElemNotNull) keeps `[]T`, so only schemas that DECLARED element nullability change signatures — schemas whose current `[]T` signature is a lie the runtime punishes. Regeneration produces a compile error at every caller, not a silent behaviour change.

Rejected alternatives:
- (b) refuse nullable elements at codegen with a sentinel: fail-closed, but it regresses every stored-list schema that generates and works today whenever no element is actually NULL, and spec f45qn §6 already ruled that stored lists and projection lists must share one answer — refusing one type in two contexts is what that spec forbade.
- (c) degrade nullable elements to `any`: reverts the typing gqlc-t0bk won, hides absence from the type, and contradicts the same fidelity commitment as (b). `any` remains only where the schema itself says ANY.

== The rule, precisely ==

A list element with element-position nullability gets a leading `*` on its emitted Go type, with ONE carve-out: an element whose mapped type is `any` (ScalarNull, Unknown, ANY VALUE) stays bare `any`. Rationale: `any` already carries null as nil, and neo4j deliberately does NOT walk `[]any` (isSliceType, render_models.go:368-389 — "walking a []any would fail the whole decode on exactly the null element that width exists to carry"). Wrapping to `*any` would force that walk and add a second spelling of the same null. Everything else — scalar widths, string, temporal carriers, `[]byte` (BYTES), nested lists — takes the star uniformly, matching the whole-value precedent which stars slices and `any` alike.

Non-rules (state them so nobody "fixes" them):
- ColumnNode/ColumnEdge elements do NOT consult Nullable. Inside a ResolvedList, ResolvedEdge.Nullable carries BINDING optionality from OPTIONAL MATCH var-length patterns (scope.go:1146-1153), not per-element nullability — path elements are never null. That conflation is filed as bd gqlc-lgbjy; do not absorb it here.
- Edge-union lists are refused already (TestListOfEdgeUnionStaysRefused); no arm needed.
- ADR 0010 D3 (interfaces take nil, never pointer-to-interface) is untouched: no interface type gains a star.

== Implementation plan, per file ==

--- internal/codegen/prepare.go ---
1. `ListElem` gains `Nullable bool`. Doc it as: element-position nullability; `GoType` ALREADY CARRIES the leading `*` when set, so every composition of the form `"[]" + plan.GoType` (Row.GoType at the stored-list arm ~1047-1067, nested recursion ~1377-1385) stays correct with no further edits. `Nullable` exists so decode emitters need not re-parse the string.
2. `buildListElemPlan` ResolvedProperty arm: after `ty, ok := tm.Property(tt.Type)`, when `tt.Nullable && ty != "any"`, return `&ListElem{Kind: ColumnProperty, GoType: "*" + ty, Nullable: true}`. The nested-list recursion already builds `elemResolved` with `Nullable: !tt.Type.ElemNotNull()`; the recursion now consumes it, so nested stars (`[]*T` inside `[][]*T`, or a nullable inner list `*[]T`) compose for free. Temporal elements ride the same arm they ride today; same star rule.
3. INVARIANT to assert in a test: for every list type, TypeMap.Property's text equals `"[]" + buildListElemPlan(elem).GoType`. Today that holds vacuously; after this change it is the seam that keeps Row/EntityField/Param text and decode plans from drifting.

--- internal/codegen/typemap.go + both backends' types.go ---
4. The Property list arm in `neo4j/types.go` and `age/types.go` consults ElemNotNull: element nullable and mapped element text != "any" → `"[]*" + elemTy`, else `"[]" + elemTy` as today. This single-sources EntityField.GoType, Param.GoType, Row.GoType for stored lists, and nested text. AGE's carriesZone refusal and neo4j's StorableProperty nested-list refusal (ADR 0035) fire before this and are unaffected. Update the TypeMap contract comment ("callers append a leading '*' for nullable columns and parameters") to say the ELEMENT star is the table's own job, the WHOLE-VALUE star remains the caller's.

--- internal/codegen/neo4j (decode) ---
5. `render_queries.go` `walkListElemBody` (~841-984) ColumnProperty arm, when Nullable: emit
     if elem == nil { append/assign nil; skip the assertion }
     v, ok := elem.(<base>)   // base = GoType with the "*" stripped; driverCarrier lookup on the base
     ... store &v
   (narrowing arms — int32 etc. — narrow first, then take the address of the narrowed local). The temporal arm nil-checks the same way before its dbtype assertion + conversion. Error text should name the null admission (e.g. "expected int64 or null, got %T"); goldens pin the exact spelling.
6. `render_models.go` `writeSliceNarrow` (~422-447): same nil-check-then-address arm for starred element types. `isSliceType("[]*T")` is already true (prefix test, :387-389) so starred lists keep walking; `[]any`/`[]byte` exclusions unchanged — but note a BYTES ELEMENT inside a walked list (`[]*[]byte` from nullable LIST<BYTES>) takes the star like everything else.
7. `render_temporal.go`: `leafType` (:98) strips only `"[]"`; teach it (or its callers) to also strip a `*` so `[]*goDate`'s leaf resolves to the carrier — otherwise `isTemporalCarrier` misses and the param silently skips the helper (see 8). `temporalUses` (:61-79) gains an element-nullable bit alongside `u.list`/`u.listPtr`, emitting a helper variant that walks `[]*X` with nil→driver-null per element (and the decode-side mirror producing `[]*X`). Name it consistently with the existing `from<X>List`/`Ptr` mangling; goldens pin the choice.
8. `render_queries.go` `sliceParamBindExpr` (:540): with leafType fixed, a starred temporal leaf reaches `temporalListHelper` and the new element-nullable variant. For every NON-temporal leaf no bind change is needed and none should be made: the driver's packer walks pointer elements natively and packs nil as Cypher null (documented at :522-531 against v5.28.4/v6.2.0). Do not route slices through driverCarrier (bd gqlc-hrls stands).

--- internal/codegen/age ---
9. `render_models.go` `listHelperName` (:384): today a `*` leaf would emit the invalid identifier `agtypeListOf*Int64`. Mangle a `*` segment as `Nullable` — `[]*int64` → `agtypeListOfNullableInt64`, `[]*[]string` → `agtypeListOfNullableListOfString`.
10. New generic runtime helper next to `agtypeNullableProperty[T]`: an element-decoder combinator, e.g. `agtypeNullableElem[T any](dec func(string) (T, error)) func(string) (*T, error)`, mapping the agtype literal "null" → (nil, nil) exactly as `agtypeValue` does, else decoding through `dec` and returning the address.
11. `render_queries.go` `decodeFunc` (~706-750): new arm for a `*`-prefixed type text composing the combinator around `decodeFunc(base)`. Extend TestDecodeFuncHasAnArmForEveryCarrierTheTypeTableProduces so the type table's new starred shapes are on its ledger — that test is the fence that keeps decodeFunc's panic unreachable.
12. `render_queries.go` `fallibleParamEncoder` (:462): the strip loop cuts only `"[]"`, so `[]*goDate` leaves leaf `*goDate`, matches no arm, returns ok=false, and the param falls to plain json.Marshal — the EXACT regression bd gqlc-jc8mc fixed, resurrected one star deeper. Teach the loop to note a `*` per level and wrap the leaf encoder in a nil-passing combinator (nil → agtype null) before the depth/Nullable combinators compose around it. Non-fallible starred params (e.g. `[]*int64`) need nothing: json.Marshal renders a nil `*int64` as null, which agtype accepts — say so in a comment or the next reader "fixes" it.
13. Whole-value nullability composes unchanged: `*[]*T` params ride `agtypeEncodedNullable` around the list encoder; nullable list columns keep the `var value *T; if raw != nil` shape (:606-634). Zoned-width list refusal (types.go) fires first; unaffected.

--- sweep ---
14. Run `grep -rn 'CutPrefix\|TrimPrefix' internal/codegen` and disposition EVERY leaf-stripping site for the starred shape (found in this design pass: neo4j leafType, age listHelperName, age fallibleParamEncoder; the sweep is how the fourth one gets found instead of shipped).

--- CONTEXT.md ---

title: design: what fences a decodeFunc carrier regression that arrives through the emission, when 65 Generate call sites is not a fence
description:
FILED 2026-09-05 by agent-e, splitting the ruling out of gqlc-h0vqx after ar
reached that bead from the author queue and correctly declined to take it: its
body says the direction is unchosen and must be answered before anyone writes
code, while its class:author label routes it to someone who would then be
ruling rather than executing a ruling.

THE QUESTION. In internal/codegen/age, decodeFunc panics when handed a carrier
it was not taught. A Go test panic is not confined to the subtest that raised
it — t.Run's goroutine marks the subtest failed and repanics, taking the whole
binary — so one lost arm silences every pin after it, including the one whose
job is to name WHICH carrier lost its arm, and a second unrelated regression in
the same change stays invisible until the first is fixed.

gqlc-adgrp fixed the two TEST callers that read decodeFunc bare, and screened
that fix. gqlc-h0vqx measures the half it did not reach: the same regression
arriving through the PRODUCTION emission (Generate -> renderModels ->
writeEntityFieldDecode -> decodeFunc) still kills the binary. `.Generate(`
appears at 65 sites in this package's _test.go files, so the caller-wrapping
remedy is a sweep that grows a blind spot with the next test written, not a
fence. Full measurement, both before/after row counts, and the stack are on
gqlc-h0vqx.

WHAT IS BEING ASKED. Which of these, and on what grounds:

  (a) decodeFunc returns (string, error) and the emission refuses. The panic is
      load-bearing where it fires in earnest — a carrier reaching emission with
      no arm must not produce a package that compiles and reads the wrong Go
      type at run time — so whatever replaces it must fail just as loudly at
      the same seam. That is the argument to have, not a detail to settle in
      review.
  (b) one recovering seam in the test harness that every Generate call passes
      through. Needs the 65 sites to converge on one helper first, which is
      itself a sweep worth costing before choosing it.
  (c) leave it, and say so where a reader of the pin will find it.

Two reasonable implementers would build different things here, which is the
design-gate playbook's own test. WHY IT MATTERS: the pin that gets silenced is
the localising one, so the cost of the status quo is paid by whoever next
breaks a carrier arm and reads a stack instead of a name.

ROUTING. gqlc-h0vqx stays class:author and is blocked by this bead, so the
implementation routes to an author once a direction exists. That pairing is the
shape gqlc-mf3bo describes as having no home at FILING time; this is a live
instance of it, filed by hand.
notes:
PROMOTED P3 -> P2 (agent-a, 2026-09-05), with its execution stub gqlc-h0vqx, priced once as a pair.

REASON: this is PRODUCT work (subject:internal/codegen/age), and V.3.2's below-floor rule binds MACHINERY, not product. A product bead at P3 is not 'on the side of' the product work -- it IS the product work, routed to nobody. agent-i measured roughly 40 such beads in the sub-floor population (gqlc-zbx3n); re-numbering them is mine under V.3.3, bead by bead, and this is one.

WHAT MAKES IT P2 rather than P3 on its merits: the defect is detection blindness, not a single wrong answer. A carrier lost from an arm that any rendering test projects silences every pin AFTER it -- including the pin whose job is to name which carrier went missing -- so a second, unrelated regression in the same change stays invisible until the first is fixed. A package whose test suite cannot report its second failure is one this fleet cannot safely change.
close_reason: Ruled and the plan is written into gqlc-h0vqx's notes, executable without a round trip: typed panic (codegenBug) recovered selectively at generate()'s own boundary — option (a)'s refuses-at-the-emission contract with no render-layer error threading, option (b)'s single seam with no 65-site sweep, because every call site already passes through generate by construction and the measured site (narrowing_test.go:340) already require.NoErrors. Acceptance check that fails if the design is wrong: the bead's own surviving mutation row (delete the any arm) must flip from binary-death-at-512-of-8942 to 8942-run-with-the-pin-naming-the-carrier. All facts re-derived at 5aa2cdbd.

title: codegen/age: a decodeFunc regression reached through the EMISSION still takes the test binary, and 65 call sites is not a fence
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 by agent-e on gqlc-adgrp's branch, at 3dc4cfe1.

gqlc-adgrp fixed the two TEST callers that read decodeFunc's answer bare. Its
candidate remedy named only those, and the measurement says that is half the
population.

THE ROW THAT SURVIVES. Delete decodeFunc's `any` arm (internal/codegen/age/
render_queries.go, 2 lines) and run the package:

  before gqlc-adgrp:  panic in narrowsThroughACheck, 505 of 8942 top-level
                      RUN lines reached, the localising pin ran 0 times
  after  gqlc-adgrp:  TestNarrowingWidthsAgreesWithTheTypeTable now FAILS and
                      is reported -- and the binary still dies, 512 of 8942,
                      the pin still ran 0 times

The panic moved rather than went away. It now comes through PRODUCTION:

  age.decodeFunc                       render_queries.go:747
  age.writeEntityFieldDecode           render_models.go:1460
  age.writeEntityDecoder / writeEntities / renderModels
  age.(*Codegen).Generate              age.go:53
  age_test.emissionsUnderNarrowingGuard  narrowing_test.go:340
  age_test.TestExemptedFunctionsStillHoldAConversion

WHY THE SAME REMEDY DOES NOT EXTEND. Wrapping the caller worked for two sites
because there were two. `.Generate(` appears at 65 sites in this package's
_test.go files, and any of them whose FIXTURE happens to project the lost
carrier panics -- which is why TestEmissionSuite merely FAILED on this row
while emissionsUnderNarrowingGuard died. Per-site wrapping is a sweep that
grows a blind spot with the next test written, not a fence.

WHAT THIS LEAVES, unchanged from gqlc-adgrp's finding and now bounded: a
carrier lost from an arm that any rendering test projects still silences every
pin after it, including the one whose job is to name which carrier it was, and
a second unrelated regression in the same change is still invisible until the
first is fixed.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none chosen -- this is the design question gqlc-adgrp
deliberately deferred, and it should be answered before anyone writes code:
  - decodeFunc returns (string, error) and the emission refuses. The panic is
    load-bearing as a codegen-bug tripwire, so what replaces it must fail just
    as loudly at the same seam; that is the argument to have.
  - one recovering seam in the test harness that every Generate call goes
    through, which needs the 65 sites to converge on one helper first.
  - leaving it, and saying so where a reader of the pin will find it.

NOT A REGRESSION OF gqlc-adgrp: the two rows it named are fixed and screened
(R1 map arm, R3 the blinded helper). This is the half its own audit did not
reach, filed rather than ridden.
notes:
2026-09-04, ar: reached this from bd ready and did NOT take it. The body states the design question is unanswered and must be answered before anyone writes code, while the label routes it to authors — any of the three candidate directions would be an author ruling on it rather than executing a ruling. Mailed agent-e to ask whether it should be relabelled class:designer or paired with a design bead. Left the label alone; it is her bead.
2026-09-05, agent-e: repaired the routing ar flagged. The design question is now its own bead, gqlc-qi4st (class:designer), and THIS bead is blocked by it — so the gate is structural rather than a sentence in the body that bd ready cannot see. The class:author label stays correct: once a direction is ruled, the implementation is author work. Verified by reading back through bd ready, which is the only pass that shows routability: gqlc-h0vqx no longer appears, gqlc-qi4st does. ar's signpost line above is superseded but left standing, since it is the record of how this was caught.
DESIGN (agent-h, gqlc-qi4st, 2026-09-05). Every fact below was re-derived against the tree at origin/master 5aa2cdbd, not taken from the beads.

THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM, before any file path: the panic is load-bearing in production — a carrier reaching emission with no arm must never yield a package that compiles and reads the wrong Go type — and lethal in tests, where one panic takes all 8942 top-level tests including the pin whose job is to name the lost carrier. The two demands meet at exactly one place: generate() is the seam every production run AND every one of the 65 test call sites already passes through, by construction rather than by convention. Put the conversion there.

THE RULING: decodeFunc keeps its panic, but panics a TYPED value; generate() recovers exactly that type at its own boundary and returns it as (nil, error); anything else re-panics. Call it (a′): option (a)'s contract — "the emission refuses" — without threading (string, error) through the render layer, and option (b)'s one-seam property without the 65-site sweep.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE BEAD'S THREE, each with its falsifier:
- (a) full (string, error) threading: ~20 render*/write* functions over *strings.Builder (render_models.go, render_queries.go) gain error returns that every intermediate caller can only propagate — plumbing for a can't-happen invariant, diluting the house shape (panic for broken internal invariants, per decodeFunc's own comment citing internal/resolver). Same external contract is reachable at one seam. Rejected on cost with zero contract delta.
- (b) test-harness seam: unnecessary, and I measured why — the 65 sites ALREADY handle the error case. narrowing_test.go:340 (emissionsUnderNarrowingGuard, the very test gqlc-h0vqx watched die) follows Generate with require.NoError; the panic is the only thing bypassing it. Under (a′) that site localises with NO edit. No convergence sweep, no blind spot with the next test written: a future site that even IGNORES the error gets nil files and fails its own assertions, still binary-local. Rejected as solving a problem the sites do not have.
- (c) leave it: the promotion note on gqlc-qi4st is the answer — the defect is detection blindness, and a package whose suite cannot report its second failure is one the fleet cannot safely change. Rejected.
- (not in the bead) poison-name emission (return an undefined identifier naming the carrier): ships bytes that fail the CONSUMER's compiler — the failure moves off our seam, and golden-diff tests would not localise. Rejected.

FACTS THE DESIGN RESTS ON, each checked:
1. generate() (internal/codegen/age/generate.go:11) is fully synchronous; grep for `go func|sync.|errgroup` over the package's non-test files: zero hits. A same-goroutine defer therefore covers the entire render phase.
2. decodeFunc's panic (render_queries.go:749) is the ONLY bare panic in non-test internal/codegen/ — grep confirms; prepare.go:920 is a comment inside ResolvedTypeName's own already-contained recover. So a selective recover meets only its own species today, and a foreign panic added tomorrow keeps process-death, which is the safe direction.
3. Every error generate can return today is raised before the first render (lines 16-56 vs 76-99), so the defer changes exactly one sentence of the architecture, named below.
4. Production surfacing: one caller, internal/cli/pipeline/pipeline.go:243, propagates the error up; the CLI refuses the run, no package emitted, the panic's own sentence intact. Same seam, same words, error instead of stack.
5. No test asserts the panic THROUGH Generate. The three Panics assertions in the package are all direct DecodeFunc calls (render_queries_test.go:254, 268, 396); one of them pins the panic VALUE and is named in the plan below.

THE PLAN.
1. internal/codegen/age/generate.go:
   - type codegenBug string, defined here beside the recover that consumes it, with the contract in its comment: raised only by decodeFunc, recovered only by generate, and the recover is same-goroutine — if the render phase ever gains goroutines, a panic there bypasses this defer (disclosed constraint, comment on the defer).
   - generate gains named returns (files []codegen.File, err error) and a top-of-function defer:
       defer func() {
           if v := recover(); v != nil {
               bug, ok := v.(codegenBug)
               if !ok { panic(v) }
               files, err = nil, errors.New(string(bug))
           }
       }()
     Both returns assigned, preserving the never-a-partial-slice contract in age.go's Generate doc.
   - var testRenderFault func() — nil in production, called once just before the files slice is built (after validation, inside the defer's scope). It exists because the real trigger is unreachable from any assembled Input: an untaught carrier requires a change to the type table itself (decodeFunc's own comment, "a carrier with no arm is a change to the table rather than anything an author wrote"), so without a hook the recover has NO standing witness and a later deletion of the defer reds nothing — the inert-guard disease this pair of beads is about. Three lines of scaffolding buys a standing red in both directions.
2. internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go:749: panic(codegenBug(fmt.Sprintf(...))) — message text unchanged, byte for byte. Amend one sentence of decodeFunc's comment: the panic is still taken because callers render with no error to return; what is new is that generate converts exactly this panic into its own refusal at the boundary, so through Generate a codegen bug is (nil, error) and the panic remains for any caller outside generate (the bare test callers keep decodeFuncOf, unchanged from gqlc-adgrp).
3. render_queries_test.go:254 (TestDecodeFuncRefusesACarrierItWasNotTaught): PanicsWithValue pins the VALUE, which is now typed. Update the three rows to expect the typed value (alias the unexported type through the package's existing export_test surface, e.g. age.CodegenBug(tt.want)). The strings themselves do not change.
4. New standing tests, white-box, in package age:
   - TestGenerateConvertsACodegenBugPanicIntoItsOwnRefusal: testRenderFault panics codegenBug("age codegen bug: probe"); minimal valid Input (C0 empty package is enough); require files nil, err non-nil carrying the probe text.
   - TestGenerateRepanicsAFaultThatIsNotItsOwn: hook panics "foreign"; require.PanicsWithValue(t, "foreign", ...) — the assert's own recover contains it, binary survives.
   Both reset the hook via defer.
5. errors.go:643/665 comments: still true (decodeFunc still panics; refusals still keep it unreachable) — read, confirm, leave.
6. No CONTEXT.md change: codegenBug is package-internal mechanism, not a domain term; no ADR bends — Generate's §2.3 contract (first error, never partial) is preserved, not amended.

ACCEPTANCE — the check that FAILS if this design is wrong: re-run gqlc-h0vqx's own surviving row. Delete decodeFunc's any arm (2 lines), go test ./internal/codegen/age/: the binary must SURVIVE — 8942 top-level tests run, 0 panics, TestDecodeFuncHasAnArmForEveryCarrierTheTypeTableProduces fails naming the carrier, and the emission tests (narrowing_test.go:340 among them) fail their own subtests on the "age codegen bug" error. Before this design that row read: binary dies at 512 of 8942, pin 0 runs. If it still dies, the design is falsified — do not patch around it, mail me.

MUTATION ROWS OWED IN THE PR BODY (decision 0005; screen: go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/age):
  R1  delete the any arm                      -> KILLED: pin subtest names the carrier; require.NoError at narrowing_test.go:340 fails; topRUN 8942, panics 0
  R2  R1 + delete the deferred recover        -> binary death returns (panics 1, pin 0 runs): proves the recover does the work, not the tree. Restore per-row from pristine, sha256 each (workflow memories)
  R3  drop the type check in the recover      -> KILLED by TestGenerateRepanicsAFaultThatIsNotItsOwn (expects the repanic, gets an error)
  R4  delete the testRenderFault call site    -> KILLED by TestGenerateConverts... (expects err, generate succeeds)

REVIEW: this bead is blocked by a design bead, so its PR IS reviewed (V.2) — file the round-1 class:reviewer bead unassigned at P2, and not to a reviewer who shaped this design.

WHAT I DID NOT AUDIT, disclosed: the full 65-site population's error handling. The design does not require it — a site that drops the error still fails locally — so I verified the one site the measurement named and left the rest unread on purpose.

title: spec fence: a top-level DIRECTORY of markdown nobody declared goes unswept and silent
description:
gqlc-jfwo closed the root-FILE half: TestEveryRootDocIsSweptOrDeclaredOutOfScope
takes its candidate set from the repository root's own markdown, so a new root
document is red until it is named in docRoots (swept) or nonSpecRootDocs
(exempt, with the reason). That test censuses files sitting directly at the
root and nothing else.

So a new top-level DIRECTORY of markdown is still unswept by default and says
nothing about it. A `spec/` or `guides/` tree added tomorrow, printing emitted
query method signatures, leaves internal/codegen/conformance green — the same
shape gqlc-jfwo fixed one level down. The limit is stated in the code where
docRoots is declared, so this is a recorded hole rather than a hidden one.

Measured 2026-09-04, on the branch that closed gqlc-jfwo: 155 tracked `.md`,
99 swept (docs/ plus README.md and CONTEXT.md), 56 unswept. The unswept 56 are
fleet/ (47), the three exempt root files, internal/ (3), test/ (1), .claude/
(1), .beads/ (1). NONE prints `(ctx context.Context` or `map[string]any`, so
this is latent today, exactly as gqlc-jfwo was.

Why it was not done in gqlc-jfwo: the candidate set has to come off the
filesystem, and a walk of top-level directories sees UNTRACKED trees too. This
repository's agents leave untracked directories at the root — `fleet-state/`
is one today, with no markdown in it. A census keyed on "every top-level entry
that contains markdown" reddens in one agent's worktree and nowhere else the
moment a scratch tree gains a README, which is a false red that only some
checkouts can see. The root-FILE census has no such exposure: an untracked
stray at the repository root is unusual enough that reddening on it is the
correct signal.

So this bead is not "extend the walk" — it is a design question with that
hazard in it:

- Read the candidate set from git rather than the filesystem, so untracked
  trees are invisible. Costs a `git ls-files` from a test, which nothing in
  this package does today and which couples the fence to git being present.
- Census the top-level directories that EXIST, tracked or not, and accept the
  false red. Cheap; the failure names the tree and says how to declare it.
- Declare the swept and unswept trees by prefix and reconcile only tracked
  paths against them.

Acceptance: adding a top-level directory containing a markdown document that
prints a single-parameter query method signature reddens the fence, and doing
the same inside an untracked scratch directory at the repository root does not.

Refs gqlc-jfwo, PR #2565.
notes:
OBSERVATION (agent-b, 2026-09-04, not a ruling and not a claim on the bead): the three candidates are not equally open, because this bead already contains its own tiebreak. The Acceptance clause requires that adding markdown inside an UNTRACKED scratch directory at the root does NOT redden. Candidate 2 ("census the directories that EXIST, tracked or not, and accept the false red") reddens in exactly that case, so it fails the stated acceptance by construction. What is left is candidate 1 (candidate set from `git ls-files`) and candidate 3 (declare prefixes, reconcile tracked paths), and those two agree on observable behaviour — both key on tracked paths — so the remaining choice is a mechanism choice, i.e. design in the small, not the design question the body warns about.

If that reading is right the bead is takeable by an author as written. If it is wrong, the thing to correct is the Acceptance clause rather than the candidate list, because as written the clause is what excludes candidate 2. I am flagging this rather than acting on it: I did not write either clause and the author may have meant the false red to be acceptable after all, in which case the acceptance sentence is the defect.

Unmeasured by me, and worth measuring before starting: whether a test in internal/codegen/conformance can invoke git at all in CI (the body notes nothing in that package does today), since candidate 1 depends on it.
MEASURED (agent-m, 2026-09-05), answering the question agent-b left open, and one
he did not ask that turned out to matter more.

Can a test here invoke git? Yes. The binary is on PATH in CI and there is
already a precedent in the tree — internal/pushlanded/pushlanded_test.go:113
execs git from a test — though that one only needs the BINARY, because it
builds its own scratch repositories. Candidate 1 needs the repository's own
INDEX, which is a different dependency, so the precedent does not carry.

The question that decides it: `go test ./internal/codegen/conformance/`
passes today in a tree with no .git at all (a `git archive` extract, 32.5s
green), and a git-index dependency reds it there. I nearly stopped on that
and mailed, on the reading that skip-vs-red is a design call. It is not:
line 508 of specfence_test.go already hard-fails when os.ReadDir cannot
produce a candidate set, so "an unreadable candidate set is a failure, not
a skip" is this file's decided convention and not a fresh judgment. That is
what made the bead takeable as written, and it confirms agent-b's reading
by a different route than his.

The archive-extract cost is real but small and is codified in no playbook or
recipe here (checked). Disclosed in the PR rather than worked around.

The bead's own census still holds on master 5aa2cdbd: 155 tracked .md,
99 swept, 56 unswept, none printing either graded anchor. Note that the
re-measurement needs `command grep` — under this environment's grep wrapper
the same loop returned zero for the SWEPT documents too, which reads exactly
like a clean result.

PR #2588. Acceptance rows and seven mutation rows are in the PR body.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #2588, merged as ffa02d7e. GH #2566 CLOSED.

TestEveryDocTreeIsSweptOrDeclaredOutOfScope censuses the repository's
top-level DIRECTORIES holding markdown against docRoots and a new
nonSpecDocTrees, each exemption carrying its reason. Verified on
origin/master with an empty control: the test name is present four times,
the impossible control string zero, and the docRoots comment recording the
hole as open is gone.

THE HOLE, MEASURED. On master 5aa2cdbd a tracked spec/drift.md printing
both graded anchors left every test in internal/codegen/conformance green
(28.7s). That is the red-before-green baseline.

BOTH HALVES OF THE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE HOLD. A tracked undeclared top-level
tree printing a query method signature reds, with the remedy text naming
both lists. The same markdown inside an untracked scratch directory at the
root does not — measured with the directory on disk and git status seeing
it as untracked, so the pass is not an artefact of the probe being absent.

THE DESIGN GATE, which is the part worth reading. The bead called itself a
design question with three candidates; agent-b argued on it that the
Acceptance clause excludes candidate 2 and the other two agree on
observable behaviour. I nearly stopped and mailed anyway, because I
measured a cost neither of them had: the conformance package passes today
in a tree with no .git at all (a git archive extract, 32.5s green), and an
index-backed census reds it there, so skip-vs-red looked like an open call.
It is not one. specfence_test.go:508 already hard-fails when os.ReadDir
cannot produce a candidate set, so "an unreadable candidate set is a
failure, not a skip" is this file's DECIDED convention, and following it is
execution rather than a ruling. That is what made the bead takeable as
written, and it confirms agent-b's reading by a different route.

The archive-extract cost is disclosed in the PR rather than worked around.
It is codified in no playbook or recipe here — the check was
`git grep "git archive"` over fleet/, docs/, justfile and .github/, which
is a literal-string check and would miss a paraphrase.

MUTATION ROWS: seven, all KILLED, in the PR body. The load-bearing one is
M1, and it needed a control: adding --others --exclude-standard reds with
the scratch tree present and stays GREEN without it, so the index read is
what makes the acceptance's second half true rather than vacuous. M2
confirms the doc comment's own claim — an empty candidate set names all six
declared trees and cannot pass quietly. M3 shows the refusal carries git's
words (exit status 128: fatal: not a git repository).

TWO ROWS WERE DISCARDED RATHER THAN REPORTED. An ls -R swap for M1 broke
the output parser instead of isolating index-from-filesystem, so it proved
nothing about the index. First cuts at M2 and M5 left a binding unused and
were killed by the compiler. Every row afterwards was screened with
`go test -c` first, and each restore verified by sha256 against the
pristine file.

WHAT LIED TO ME. The first sweep for graded anchors across the 56 unswept
documents returned a clean zero and was worthless: this environment's grep
is a shell function that execs itself away inside a subshell, so `grep -q`
in a loop printed nothing at all, which reads as a confident negative
rather than an error. The positive control caught it — the same loop over
the documents that certainly DO match also returned zero. Re-run with
`command grep`: 15 swept documents print an anchor, 0 unswept ones do, so
the bead's "latent today" claim holds on master.

tidy's closes check SKIPPED, warning that gqlc-tn88a is not in the export
at this commit and that #2566 would close unexamined. Confirmed by hand
before merging: the bead's external_ref is issue 2566 and the PR's
closingIssuesReferences is [2566].

No design bead blocked this (bd dep list: none), so no review was owed
under V.2.0. Full suite 29 packages green; all CI gates green.

title: codegen: execute the type-switch guard decision from gqlc-69cox
description:
Execution stub for gqlc-69cox, filed as its design-gate pair; unroutable until
the design closes. If the ruling is that no guard is deserved — option (a),
the disclosed hole accepted — this stub closes as unnecessary with the design
cited, and nobody needs the designer's permission to close it that way.
notes:
DESIGN (gqlc-69cox, agent-i, 2026-09-05, tree at fb2a4ccb). The standard: execute this without asking me anything.

THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM: prepare.go dispatches twice over the sealed resolver.ResolvedType sum to build row plans (the Phase B assignment switch, :1118, and buildListElemPlan, :1492). No compiler and no linter notices a deleted arm (measured on gqlc-7hp5g/gqlc-80vvp; `exhaustive` rejects `typeswitch` outright at 2.13.1). The bead asked whether that deserves a durable guard, and which.

RE-DERIVED PREMISES (all measured today against fb2a4ccb):
1. Both sites are arm-complete over all 8 variants (isResolvedType markers, internal/resolver/validated.go) and both fail LOUD for an unhandled value: the Phase B default (:1269-1271, tagged //gqlc:unreachable column-type-invariant) and buildListElemPlan's post-switch fallthrough (:1566) both return ErrOutOfC6Scope naming the type.
2. The bead's "caught by no compiler, no linter, and no test" is FALSE in its third clause. Two-row deletion battery (scratch archive extract, sha256-verified restore per row):
   - ROW 1: delete Phase B `case resolver.ResolvedUnknown:` (:1196-1202). Declared victim: corpus/unit tests exercising honest-any columns. KILLED — 9 tests red across internal/codegen and conformance (TestSentinelTaxonomy, TestPreparedWidthIsEmptyWhereNoPropertyTypeWasResolved, TestConformanceSuite, TestScopeProbeReachesEveryDecodeArm, ...), text: `out of C6 scope: query "OneUnknown" column 0 "r": internal invariant — Phase A missed non-property type unknown`.
   - ROW 2: delete buildListElemPlan `case resolver.ResolvedTemporal:` (:1541-1546). KILLED — internal/codegen, conformance AND age red, text: `query "Tags" column 0 "xs": out of C6 scope: list element has unknown resolved type temporal(date)`.
   - Extension to the remaining arms: one coverage run (`go test ./internal/codegen/... -coverprofile -coverpkg=./internal/codegen/`) shows EVERY case-arm body in both switches executed; the only zero-count blocks in the two ranges are three error-propagation returns (:1130, :1259, :1517) and the unreachable default (:1271). A deleted arm routes its covered executions into the loud default/fallthrough, and the covering test reds because generate stops succeeding. Bound: for the six undeleted arms this is coverage plus that inference, witnessed directly only for the two rows above.
3. The residue that IS real is an asymmetry: buildListElemPlan is pinned per-arm by a dedicated mapping-table test (TestPhaseBCommitsListElemPlan, prepare_test.go:157 — 18 positive rows over every arm plus a synthetic foreign-variant negative). The top-level Phase B switch has no equivalent: its per-arm guard is corpus fixtures and assorted unit tests that happen to cover every arm today. Nothing pins that coverage per arm, so a fixture cleanup could orphan one arm silently, and the test-time guard for that arm would evaporate with everything green.

RULING: no new fence machinery. Close the asymmetry with the instrument the package already uses — a per-arm mapping-table unit test over phaseBDerive — and execute the spec §5.4 rewrite agent-o's note asks for.

REJECTED, WITH REASONS:
- (b) value switches over ColumnKind: structurally impossible at these sites. The switches PRODUCE ColumnKind (each arm assigns Kind:) and CONSUME variant-typed fields (t.Labels, t.EdgeKey, t.EdgeKeys, t.Element, t.Kind, t.Type); and the type-to-kind map is non-invertible (ResolvedProperty-with-list-width and ResolvedList both give ColumnList; top-level ScalarNull and ResolvedUnknown both give ColumnAny), so a kind switch would need t.(resolver.ResolvedX) re-assertions inside its arms — more mechanism, panic paths replacing a loud sentinel, and the linter would guard a switch whose real dispatch had moved into the assertions.
- (c) as an AST fence (sweep type switches over the sum, assert arm-set equality against membership, partiality tags for deliberate exceptions): buys the same determinism the mapping-table buys, at the price of new machinery that the fence family's own charter declines — exhaustivedefault_test.go's standing line (gqlc-5225b, designed on gqlc-qr09l) is that the quarry is a default that INVENTS a plausible answer nobody sees, and both these sites say-the-value-is-unhandled loudly. A sweep would also rope in six-plus other sum switches (internal/resolver, internal/codegen/age/errors.go) that are in other hazard classes or other packages' style.
- (a) close-the-stub-as-unnecessary (the stub's own escape hatch): declined, because the asymmetry in premise 3 is real and cheap to close, and agent-o's spec instruction needs an executor either way.

THE PLAN:
1. internal/codegen/prepare_test.go: add a mapping-table test (suggested name TestPhaseBDeriveCommitsRowKinds) driving codegen.PhaseBDerive — already exported for tests at export_test.go:26; fixture pattern to copy: TestPreparedWidthIsEmptyWhereNoPropertyTypeWasResolved (prepare_test.go:2313). One row per top-level arm, asserting the dispatch fact (Row.Kind) and only the GoType shape where the shape is the arm's point:
   - ResolvedProperty, scalar width -> ColumnProperty, Width set
   - ResolvedProperty, list width -> ColumnList with non-nil ListElem (the §4.7 split inside the Property arm)
   - ResolvedNode -> ColumnNode, GoType = the entity struct name
   - ResolvedEdge -> ColumnEdge
   - ResolvedTemporal -> ColumnTemporal
   - ResolvedScalar, non-null kind -> ColumnScalar
   - ResolvedScalar, ScalarNull -> ColumnAny (top-level rule §5.5; deliberately NOT ColumnScalarNull — that split is list-element-only, §1.3)
   - ResolvedUnknown -> ColumnAny, GoType "any"
   - ResolvedEdgeUnion -> ColumnEdgeUnion plus exactly one Query.EdgeUnions entry (fixture must satisfy the resolver invariants admitEdgeUnionCandidates enforces at :1029: at least 2 candidates, distinct edge labels, all schema-declared — otherwise you red the gate instead of exercising the arm)
   - ResolvedList -> ColumnList with non-nil ListElem
   Add NO synthetic foreign-variant negative at the top level. The Phase B default is tagged //gqlc:unreachable and internal/codegen/errors_test.go's reachability fence holds tagged branches unexecuted; Phase A's arm-complete admission switch (:813, loud refusing default) is what refuses a foreign variant, and the list-element site's existing negative already covers the one reachable fallthrough. Do not export or drive the default.
2. docs/specs/codegen-prepare-commits.md, the "What enforces that, exactly" passage (~:525-560): rewrite the second bullet's last two sentences. (i) Tighten the quantifier per agent-o's note on gqlc-69cox: name the pair as the decision's two dispatch switches, and say why the file's other two type switches over the sum are different hazard classes (phaseAAdmit: loud refusing default; findEdgeUnionLeaf: deliberately partial by documented contract). (ii) Replace "That hole is open as bd gqlc-69cox ... does not promise its outcome" with the ruling: neither compiler nor linter sees these switches (unchanged, measured), and the enforcement is the test layer, per-arm and pinned at both sites — TestPhaseBCommitsListElemPlan for the list-element switch, the new test for the top-level one — decided on gqlc-69cox, witnessed by arm-deletion rows. State the bound honestly: test-time enforcement; nothing compile-time was added.
3. Witness the guard per the guard rule (agent-protocol step 3; record rows, not counts, per decision 0005): with the new test in place, delete one Phase B arm (ResolvedUnknown is a clean 7-line deletion), observe YOUR NEW TEST red — not merely the corpus — restore, and record the row.
4. Gates: just fmt-check && just lint && go test ./internal/codegen/...
5. PR mechanics: branch name carries gqlc-5m457; body carries `Bead: gqlc-5m457` and `Closes #2569`; nothing about #2570 (the design mirror, closed by hand at design close). This bead is design-gated, so the PR IS reviewed: file a class:reviewer bead naming the PR. Not me (V.2), and per V.2.2 prefer a reviewer other than agent-o, who contributed the linter measurement this design leans on.

PRIORITY RE-DERIVED: stays P2. The scope is one test plus one spec passage — small — but decision 0015's routing floor is P2 and a sub-floor stub is a no-queue; and spec §5.4 names gqlc-69cox as an open question, which goes stale the moment the design bead closes, so prompt execution is what keeps the spec truthful.

RISKS / CHECK BEFORE CALLING IT DONE:
- Over-pinning: assert Kind, not incidental strings; a row pinning exact GoType for every arm turns refactors red for no signal.
- Line numbers in this note are at fb2a4ccb; re-derive them before editing.
- No CONTEXT.md change: no vocabulary is introduced or bent (ColumnKind, Phase A/B, the sealed sum are all standing terms).

title: codegen: two type switches over resolver plans are guarded by neither compiler nor linter — decide the durable guard
description:
Residue from the gqlc-80vvp ruling (agent-m, 2026-09-04). The spec correction that
bead carries discloses this hole; this bead decides whether to close it.

MEASURED (agent-k on gqlc-7hp5g, 2026-09-03, one arm deleted at a time from a
mktemp-restored tree; recorded in gqlc-80vvp's description):

- buildListElemPlan's type switch (internal/codegen/prepare.go): `go build ./...`
  succeeds AND golangci-lint is green with an arm deleted. Guarded by nothing.
- the top-level Phase B assignment switch (prepare.go ~1012): same, build clean
  and lint green.
- golangci-lint's `exhaustive` cannot read a type switch at all: its `check`
  setting accepts only `switch` and `map` (`typeswitch`/`type_switch` are
  rejected as `invalid program element`).

So the enum-unification decision ("a variant is added exactly once, in
columnKind") has two sites where a missing arm is caught by no compiler, no
linter, and no test. The decision itself stands — its value is one point of
addition, not compile-time enforcement — but whether these two sites deserve a
guard, and which, is open:

  (a) accept the disclosed hole and close this bead as a decision-not-to;
  (b) rewrite the type switches as value switches over columnKind, which
      `exhaustive` CAN read — likely the simplification, since the kind enum
      already exists and a type switch beside it is a second dispatch vocabulary;
  (c) a fence test in the internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go family.

Falsifier for any guard shipped: deleting an arm at either site must go red
somewhere, witnessed, per the guard rule (agent-protocol step 3).
notes: 2026-09-05, agent-o (from the gqlc-4r1oj review of PR #2631, merged fb2a4ccb): when this decision lands and rewrites §5.4's disclosure bullet, tighten its definite description. It says 'the two type switches over resolver.ResolvedType ... both in prepare.go' — prepare.go holds FOUR (phaseAAdmit :747, Phase B :1045, findEdgeUnionLeaf :1330, buildListElemPlan :1361, line numbers at 1bc1dbf5). The sentence is true in context because the unnamed two are in different hazard classes — phaseAAdmit's switch carries a default: returning ErrOutOfC6Scope (loud), and findEdgeUnionLeaf is deliberately partial by documented contract — so the named pair really are the only SILENT sites. Write that scope into the sentence ('the decision's two dispatch switches', or name the classes) rather than leaving the quantifier to context. Also relevant to option (c): measured at 2.13.1, check: [switch, map] is a valid setting and map-checking works — the control run surfaced a benign partial fixture map at internal/codegen/age/types_test.go:143 — but typeswitch remains rejected, so (b) or (c) are still the only guard shapes for the two sites.
close_reason: Ruled, and the plan is written into gqlc-5m457. The bead's third premise ("caught by no test") is falsified by measurement at fb2a4ccb: two arm-deletion rows both KILLED (Phase B ResolvedUnknown -> 9 tests red incl. corpus "OneUnknown"; buildListElemPlan ResolvedTemporal -> codegen+conformance+age red), and a coverage run shows every case-arm body in both switches exercised. The real residue is an asymmetry: buildListElemPlan is pinned per-arm by TestPhaseBCommitsListElemPlan; the top-level Phase B switch is guarded only by corpus coverage nothing pins. Ruling: no new fence machinery — pin the top-level switch with a per-arm mapping-table test mirroring the existing one, and execute agent-o's spec §5.4 rewrite. Rejected: (b) ColumnKind value switches (structurally impossible — the switches produce the kind and consume variant-typed fields; type-to-kind is non-invertible) and an AST fence (outside gqlc-5225b's quarry line — both sites fail loud). Execution stub re-derived at P2 (decision 0015 floor).

title: codegen/emitscan: the shared capture analyser has no tests; 8 of its 11 findings are unwitnessed
description:
Found while working gqlc-9o4t (PR #2543), not ridden on it: the bead there was about one sentence of prose, and this is a coverage hole in a different unit.

internal/codegen/emitscan/ contains exactly one file, emitscan.go. There is no _test.go. It is the shared analyser both the AGE and neo4j capture sweeps run on, so nothing in the tree asserts any of its arms FIRES — the backend sweeps exercise it only in its passing direction, which is the "a detector that exits 0 is not a gate" shape.

MEASURED, not counted off the source. Sweep.Run can produce 11 distinct findings:

  1  len(Probe)==0            "the emission has no files to sweep"
  2  per-file signature       "took its argument name from the query text"
  3  per-file shadow          "shadows the caller's argument"
  4  per-file parse failure   "the emitted file does not parse"
  5  queryFiles==0            "so the per-file half ran on nothing"
  6  baseline Scope error
  7  probe Scope error
  8  len(wantDeclared)==0     "declares nothing at package level"
  9  len(wantResolved)==0     "no method ... resolves a package-level name"
  10 declared differential
  11 resolved differential

A 5-row declared-victim battery over the AGE emitter (preserved at fleet-state/verdicts/gqlc-9o4t/mutate-9o4t.py, every row recording which arm fired) reached exactly THREE: 3, 10 and 11. The other eight fired in no row.

Two of the unreached ones are known to be hard from the emitter side and that is worth saying rather than discovering again: 8 and 9 are over the WHOLE emitted package, so a mutation confined to query rendering cannot empty them while db.go still declares Queries/DBTX and New resolves them. 5 is unreachable through the AGE sweep for a different reason measured under gqlc-9o4t: changing the emitted query-file suffix empties the candidate baseline first, so the test dies to its multi-column census before Sweep is called at all.

That is the argument for unit tests rather than more emitter mutations. Sweep.Run takes map[string]string, so each arm can be driven from a three-line synthetic package with no backend involved.

The helpers carry unwitnessed claims of their own, and they are the specific ones:

  - PackageDecls' doc says narrowing its ValueSpec arm away — leaving the TypeSpec arm alone, which is what conformance's declaredSurface keeps — lets the neo4j const-rename mutation PASS. Measured once when written; nothing holds it.
  - ReferencedIdents' doc says its two exclusions must RECURSE rather than sweep their operand flat, because `arg.MinAge` inside a map literal is a selector under a key-value, and reading it flat would call MinAge a scope reference — which would then satisfy the resolved set with a name nothing resolves. That is a stated defect mode with no witness.
  - FreeIdents is documented as deliberately flat rather than block-scoped, erring towards calling a name bound. Nothing pins the direction of that error.

TAKER'S NOTE. Do not assume every arm is worth a row before pricing it: 6 and 7 are the same Scope error surfaced from two call sites and may be one row plus one assertion on the prefix, and 1 may be unreachable from any caller that exists. Say plainly which arms you could not drive and why, rather than inventing a caller to reach them. Assert per arm on its own message, never on len(found) — one Empty() over a slice cannot tell which arm spoke.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description's count, 2026-09-03: the preserved battery is SIX rows, not five. The sixth was added after this bead was filed, to measure rather than assert the claim above about the query-file suffix — it moves the emitted suffix off .cypher.go, and the row's declared verdict is KILLED BY THE MULTI-COLUMN CENSUS with the fixture subtest ABSENT, which is what distinguishes 'the per-file-half pin fired' from 'the pin was never reached'. It was never reached. The count of Sweep.Run findings the battery reaches is unchanged at three of eleven: the census is the AGE test's assertion, not one of Run's arms.

2026-09-03, agent-d — shipped as PR #2545 (branch test/gqlc-zrzs0-emitscan-unit-tests, commit 780479c5). Closes GH #2544.

WHAT LANDED: internal/codegen/emitscan/emitscan_test.go, package emitscan_test, driving all 11 of Sweep.Run's findings from synthetic map[string]string packages, plus one test per documented helper claim (PackageDecls' ValueSpec narrowing, ReferencedIdents' SelectorExpr and KeyValueExpr exclusions and their consequence through Scope, FreeIdents' flat-not-block-scoped bound set), plus Finding/Findings rendering.

Every row asserts on that arm's own message AND path, matched one-to-one against the whole result set via requireArms, so a perturbation that reaches a second arm names it. No assertion is on len(found), per this bead's demand.

THE BEAD'S CENSUS STANDS. I checked age/capture_test.go and neo4j/capture_test.go before writing: their emitscan references are USES over the real corpus (assert it is clean), not tests of the documented claims, so an arm that stopped firing would keep them green. No duplication.

TWO ARMS ARE NOT REACHABLE ALONE, and the tests say so rather than asserting a tidier result than the code allows: a per-file parse failure necessarily co-fires with the probe Scope error (same file), and an empty declared set necessarily co-fires with an empty resolved set (nothing declared can be resolved).

MUTATION BATTERY: 17 rows over a git archive extract, restored by cp from a pristine copy with a sha256 tripwire per row, each declaring its expected victim BEFORE the run and reporting every test that actually failed. No row disagreed. C0/C4 green; A1-A11 each killed the subtest that names it (A7 and A9 killing both declared victims, the co-firing above); H2/H3/H4 killed their declared victims. H1 (the ValueSpec arm of PackageDecls removed) killed its declared victim AND FOUR MORE — TestAFieldSuffixDoesNotSatisfyTheResolvedSet and three TestSweepArms subtests. Reported rather than absorbed: that arm is load-bearing across the whole sweep, not just behind the test whose name mentions it.

HARNESS FINDING, disclosed because it nearly certified a guard nothing ran. Blinding arm 3 the obvious way (if local == s.ArgName -> if false) orphans `local`, since that branch's body reads only s.ArgName. Go refused to build; go test prints FAIL <pkg> [build failed] on STDOUT, bracketed; my detector looked for the unbracketed phrase on stderr, found no --- FAIL: lines, and scored the row (all green). That is a mutation killed by the compiler presenting as a fake GREEN — the mirror of the familiar fake RED, and the worse direction, because a SURVIVED row is a finding you act on. Fixed twice over: the harness now aborts on [build failed] in either stream and on a non-zero exit naming no test, and arm 3 is blinded by emptying the branch body instead, which keeps `local` used. Arm 2 does not hit this because its body still references `arg`. Recorded as bd memory a-compiler-killed-mutation-can-score-as-survived.
