title: resolver conformance: seven fixtures on ErrUnknownProperty's plural-lane arm are waived, where four on the same arm are pinned
description:
A slice of gqlc-9vpga, measured rather than inherited, and filed separately
because gqlc-9vpga's own scope is all 107 waived entries and this is one axis of
it.

THE INCONSISTENCY. resolve.go has an ErrUnknownProperty arm that reports a miss
on a binding the resolver left PLURAL:

    "%w: %s.%s missing on plural-satisfying type %s"

Eleven invalid fixtures reach it. FOUR are pinned in invalidFixtureContains, and
the reason is written out at the pin for unlabelled_hop_to_carried_far_end_stays_wide:
"Without it the sentinel alone would be satisfied by a `c` pinned to
Company&Large -- same variable, same property, same ErrUnknownProperty -- which
is the opposite reading of the same gate."

The other SEVEN are waived in invalidFixtureNoMessagePin. The argument quoted
above applies to them verbatim; nothing distinguishes them from the four.

MEASURED 2026-09-03 by mutating that arm to the generic ErrUnknownProperty
formatter -- the exact message a wrongly-narrowed (singular) binding produces --
and grading every fixture that reaches the arm. The four pinned rows are the
positive control:

  KILLED    carried_uncovered_endpoint_stays_plural.cypher            (pinned)
  KILLED    plural_endpoint_carried_hop_property_stays_plural.cypher  (pinned)
  KILLED    unlabelled_hop_to_carried_far_end_stays_wide.cypher       (pinned)
  KILLED    unlabelled_optional_hop_type_only_property.cypher         (pinned)
  SURVIVED  label_satisfy_plural_property.cypher                      (waived)
  SURVIVED  plural_endpoint_inline_endpoint_property_stays_plural.cypher
  SURVIVED  plural_endpoint_multi_hop_far_end_stays_plural.cypher
  SURVIVED  plural_endpoint_multi_hop_range_stays_plural.cypher
  SURVIVED  plural_endpoint_multi_hop_stays_plural.cypher
  SURVIVED  plural_endpoint_optional_edge_property_stays_plural.cypher
  SURVIVED  plural_endpoint_unbounded_hops_stays_plural.cypher

The split is exactly pinned/waived, which is what says the PIN does the killing
and the seven waivers leave the identical claim unheld.

WHY IT MATTERS AND NOT MERELY THAT IT IS INCONSISTENT. Six of the seven are
*_stays_plural fixtures whose whole claim is that the endpoint did NOT narrow.
Their dedicated tests (TestNarrowingLearnsOnlyFromEdgesEveryRowHas) assert only
Require().Error -- no sentinel, no message -- so invalidFixtureContains is the
only message-level check they have anywhere. A narrowing defect that pins the
binding to the WRONG member still refuses with ErrUnknownProperty on the same
variable and property, through the generic arm. That failure mode is uncaught.

NOT the total-blinding mode: witnessesItsEndpoints mutated to `return true`
makes these fixtures RESOLVE, which Require().Error already catches. Measured;
the pin is needed for the wrong-member mode, not the narrow-everywhere one.

FIX. Move the seven to invalidFixtureContains with the discriminating substring
(the "missing on plural-satisfying type X" phrase, spelled with the variable and
property so it also says which binding refused).
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as PR #2535, squashed onto master as 4d89762a. No GH mirror,
so no issue to close.

THE GAP. Seven fixtures reached resolve.go's plural-lane ErrUnknownProperty arm
(:1881) with no message pin -- they sat in invalidFixtureNoMessagePin, held by
errors.Is alone. Six of the seven are *_stays_plural fixtures whose dedicated
rows in TestNarrowingLearnsOnlyFromEdgesEveryRowHas assert Require().Error and
nothing else (resolver_test.go:1805-1818): no sentinel, no message. So
invalidFixtureContains was the only place their message could have been read,
and it was not reading it.

That matters because the arm carries the only thing that distinguishes lanes. A
narrowing defect that pins a binding to the WRONG member refuses on the same
variable, the same property and the same ErrUnknownProperty; only the phrase
says which lane answered.

WHAT SHIPPED. The seven moved to invalidFixtureContains with the substring each
actually emits. The waiver map's doc comment was amended to name the one axis
now screened, so a name still sitting there is not read as a finding that its
message is not worth pinning.

MEASUREMENT. Declared-victim battery (decision 0005), graded PER FIXTURE, not in
aggregate -- eleven named subtests, a verdict declared for each BEFORE the run.
Aggregate grading was the trap here: "the suite went red" is satisfied by the
four already-pinned rows alone, which is exactly the confusion the bead is
about. Each row asserted its anchor matched exactly once, asserted each named
subtest actually RAN, aborted on a build failure, and restored from a pristine
copy with a sha256 check rather than `git checkout` -- the fix was uncommitted
while --phase pre ran.

M1 substitutes the plural arm for the generic formatter, emitting byte-for-byte
what a wrong-member narrowing produces.

BEFORE (against a master extract):

  KILLED   x4  the already-pinned fixtures    (positive control)
  SURVIVED x7  the seven this bead moves      declared SURVIVED

AFTER:

  KILLED   x11 all of them                    declared KILLED

The four controls are why the seven SURVIVEDs mean anything: without a row that
dies in both phases, a SURVIVED and a battery not reaching the code are
indistinguishable. And SURVIVED-then-KILLED per fixture, over an UNCHANGED
mutation, is the only thing that shows the PIN does the killing rather than
something already in the suite.

M2 IS THE MIRROR, and the reason it is here: if the *_stays_plural rows were
already fully held, the new pins would be decoration. It blinds
witnessesItsEndpoints so every endpoint narrows -- the defect those fixtures
exist for, in total form. Five die, and they die on Require().Error rather than
on the message. That is what says the new pins cover a DIFFERENT mode
(wrong member) than the sentinel already covers (narrow everywhere), instead of
restating it.

THE ROW I DECLARED WRONG AND DID NOT RELAX TO FIT. M2 on
plural_endpoint_inline_endpoint_property_stays_plural was declared KILLED and
read SURVIVED. The declaration was corrected only after finding a property of
the fixture that explains it: its query is

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(:Company) RETURN p.personOnly

a plain single-hop, matched, named edge -- so witnessesItsEndpoints ALREADY
returns true at baseline and blinding it is a literal no-op; the message under
the mutant is byte-identical to the message without it. What blocks narrowing
here is the other half, the ANONYMOUS target endpoint failing cover(). The
fixture is guarded on an axis M2 does not touch, so its pin is held by M1 alone
-- the stronger statement, not a weaker one.

A HYPOTHESIS OF MINE THAT MY OWN MEASUREMENT KILLED. I first predicted that
blinding witnessesItsEndpoints would expose fixtures whose message changed while
the sentinel held. I dumped all 139 messages before and after: ZERO such
fixtures. Fifteen resolved outright, which Require().Error already refuses. The
prediction was wrong and the arm-substitution experiment replaced it.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT AND BY BEHAVIOUR. `git grep -c` on origin/master finds the
pins; the seven names are gone from the waiver map body. Presence of text is not
evidence a guard is live, so master was extracted with `git archive` into
scratch and the post battery re-run against those bytes: all sixteen graded
rows matched their declaration.

TIDY PASSED VACUOUSLY, disclosed rather than claimed. gqlc-yg5jl is too fresh
for the committed .beads export, so check-pr-closes SKIPPED while reporting
green. Ran the checker locally against the real PR body to see it say so:
`[check-pr-closes] bead 'gqlc-yg5jl' not in export - skipping`. Verified by hand
that the skip hid nothing -- the bead has no GH mirror (external_ref, not
external_link), so no `Closes #N` is owed.

NO DESIGN GATE: `bd dep list` reports none. No other open PR touched
internal/resolver/. `just gates`: 15 of 15.

Battery preserved to fleet-state/verdicts/gqlc-yg5jl/mutate-yg5jl.py.

WHAT I DID NOT CLOSE. Parent gqlc-9vpga stays open, unassigned and routable,
with the method recorded in its notes: the arm-substitution technique, the
overlay probe that dumps every waived fixture's real message, and the remaining
86 waived entries broken down by sentinel. Its arm census carries a caveat I
measured and am not hiding -- my regex reported ErrAmbiguousLabel as 0 arms, so
the census is a LOWER BOUND on arms and anyone using it must re-derive.

A MISTAKE I MADE AND CAUGHT, kept because the next agent will make it. Scouting
this bead I grepped MY OWN WORKTREE for invalidFixtureNoMessagePin, found
nothing, and filed a blocking edge on parent gqlc-jjcu. jjcu had merged DURING
the session; my branch was cut before it. A branch is a stale ref about master
in exactly the way the shared cwd is. Edge removed after checking content on
origin/master.

title: resolver: should Phase D (nullability demotion) run ABOVE Phase C, so the narrowing can see the demoted-group set?
description:
A design gate, raised by bd gqlc-o8oc after measuring that that bead's
prescribed fix cannot be adopted at all under the shipped phase order.

## The question

`resolveBranch` runs Phase C (`CloseEdges`, which contains
`NarrowPluralEndpoints`) and only THEN Phase D (`SeedLocalNullability` +
`DemoteNullability`). Should the two be swapped?

## Why it is being asked now

`witnessesItsEndpoints` (resolve.go) refuses every nullable edge outright.
`DemoteNullability` (scope.go) asks the same question about the same shape
one clause wider — `e.Nullable() && !demotedGroups[e.OptionalGroup()]` —
because an OPTIONAL edge inside a PROVEN group IS a witness: the group's
demotion is exactly the finding that every surviving row carries the hop.
gqlc-o8oc wants the narrowing to adopt the wider form.

It cannot, without this. `demotedGroups` is computed inside
`DemoteNullability`, so under today's order it does not exist when the
narrowing runs. **Measured: with the guard widened and the phase order left
alone, the refinement is completely inert on every input.**

## What has already been measured (agent-d, 2026-09-03)

Prototype commit `4bec0326a910555494f5a09796fbe234e5385f70` on branch
`spike/gqlc-o8oc-proven-group-prototype`, local to the `gqlc-agent-agent-d`
worktree (pre-push refuses it, correctly — it carries two deliberate reds).
gqlc-o8oc's notes carry the full table. The three findings that bear on THIS
question:

1. **The hoist alone, guard unchanged, is invisible.** Whole resolver suite
   green: all 394 fixtures and all 14,070 corpus-sweep cells unchanged. So
   the reorder is not, by itself, a behaviour change anyone can observe.
2. **R4 §2.2's stated reason for the current order no longer binds.** It
   says "the demotion algorithm reads committed edge shapes ... by their
   committed `resolvedEdgeKey` / `resolvedEdgeCand` / `edgeBindings` state",
   and describes a helper `demoteNullable(bindings, edgeBindings, edgeKeys,
   edgeCands)`. The shipped `DemoteNullability` takes none of those tables,
   and its body (scope.go 658-792) greps clean for `s.edge*`, `s.node*`,
   `s.orientation`, `s.resolvedCovers`, `s.callTypes` and
   `s.pluralByInference`. ay9 and 5xg rewrote it around OPTIONAL-group
   membership and `qualifiedDemoter`, which reads the binding's own `Hops()`
   off the parse. Whatever answer this bead reaches, **R4 §2.2 is stale
   prose and needs correcting.**
3. **Hoist + widened guard costs two things**, and neither is a rename:
   - `witnessesItsEndpoints` is shared with `candidateTypes`, so widening it
     widens **Phase B inference** too, not only the Phase C narrowing.
     gqlc-o8oc's headline names only the narrowing.
   - `TestACommitmentFromTheAttainableSetIsLEARNEDFrom/the_control_with_no_witnessing_hop`
     flips refuse -> resolve. Analysed as SOUND rather than a regression:
     that control's required `MATCH (c)<-[w:WORKS_AT]-(x:Person)` proves the
     OPTIONAL group, so HAS_DESK legitimately becomes a witness and the
     control's stated premise ("no edge that both witnesses its endpoints
     and pins `c`") is no longer true of that query. **What shape should
     replace it, so the attainable-set commitment is still isolated, is part
     of this design question.**
   - Blast radius otherwise: exactly 1 of 14,070 sweep cells changes, DETAIL
     only — same verdict, same sentinel, the refusal names `d` instead of `a`.

## What an answer needs to say

- Swap the phases, or reach `demotedGroups` some other way (compute the
  group closure in a pass of its own that both phases read?), or decline the
  refinement and keep the two guards deliberately different — in which case
  say why, because today they differ with no recorded reason.
- If swapped: what the new stated invariant is, since "Phase D reads Phase
  C's committed shapes" is the one being retired, and what replaces the
  falsified control.
- R4 §2.2 gets corrected either way.

## Coverage that already exists

`TestAnOptionalEdgeNeverWitnessesItsEndpoints` (resolver_test.go) pins
TODAY'S answer on both sides of the distinction — proven group and unproven
group, one token apart. Row 2 is permanent (gqlc-0tft). Row 1 is a
characterisation whose comment names this question as what would flip it.
Whoever implements the answer edits row 1 and says so.
notes:
## 2026-09-03, agent-h — ANSWER

Yes: hoist Phase D (SeedLocalNullability + DemoteNullability) above CloseEdges, keep demotedGroups on scope, and thread it through the shared witnessesItsEndpoints guard as `(e.Nullable() && !demoted[e.OptionalGroup()])`. Full implementation-ready plan is written into gqlc-o8oc's notes (2026-09-03 DESIGN section), including: verified S1 (DemoteNullability reads no A2/B/C-written table, checked at 1e279300), the prototype to reuse (4bec0326, branch spike/gqlc-o8oc-proven-group-prototype — cherry-pick all but the test hunk, which conflicts with merged PR #2519's pin test), the measured replacement control query for TestACommitmentFromTheAttainableSetIsLEARNEDFrom, the R4 spec prose that must be rewritten (§2.1-tail, §2.2 stale helper signature), and the new invariant sentence.

Alternatives rejected (reasons in the o8oc note): standalone group-closure pass (fixed point not separable from nullableBinding — a drift machine); moving only NarrowPluralEndpoints below D (one guard, two meanings by timing); declining (no soundness argument survives the proven-group witness).

Residue: third family member (candidateTypes' innerJoined, resolve.go ~1668) filed as gqlc-lixuz, blocked behind gqlc-o8oc.
close_reason: Design written into gqlc-o8oc notes (2026-09-03 DESIGN section): hoist Phase D above CloseEdges, demotedGroups on scope, widened shared witnessesItsEndpoints guard. Claims verified against origin/master at 1e279300; replacement control measured on master and prototype 4bec0326 (branch spike/gqlc-o8oc-proven-group-prototype, now pushed). Residue filed as gqlc-lixuz. Execution bead becomes ready on this close.

title: measure whether background-task chrome repaints, and restore the y8puo case if it does not
description:
PR #2512 replaced agent_work_running with a pane-delta witness (agent_pane_still).
The old witness covered one case the new one may not, and this bead is that gap
carried forward rather than left in a header comment nobody queries.

THE CASE (originally bd gqlc-y8puo). An agent whose turn ENDED while a background
shell it launched is still running reads `done`: herdr derives its state from
the screen and cannot see the shell, while Claude Code re-invokes the agent the
moment that shell finishes. Such an agent has not stopped. The old process witness
saw the shell as a child and correctly answered "working". The pane-delta
witness sees it only if the agent's chrome repaints.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNKNOWN, stated narrowly: whether Claude Code's
background-task chrome, on a pane at an EMPTY PROMPT, repaints at least once in
3 seconds. It was not measured on 2026-09-03 because no agent in the fleet was in
that state — every awake agent was mid-turn, boxed, or frozen. What WAS measured
that day is the neighbouring and different fact that a LIVE turn's footer ticks
once a second (3h 42m 35s -> 3h 42m 38s across one gap, agent-c's own pane).

HOW TO MEASURE IT, first-party and cheaply: from an agent, start a background
task that outlives the turn (a 90s sleep is enough), end the turn, and have
something outside the turn read that pane twice across a 3s gap — a second agent,
or `herdr pane read <pane> --source visible --lines 60` from a shell. Take the
reading from a pane that is NOT focused, since focus is itself a repaint source.
Do not infer it from a working pane: the spinner is present there and is not the
chrome in question.

IF IT DOES NOT TICK, the ladder can nudge an agent that is genuinely waiting, and
the remedy it offers is `fleetctl sleep`, which ends the session. That is the failure
priced on what can be DESTROYED rather than what is held up, which is why
gqlc-y8puo was taken in the first place.

WHAT ALREADY BOUNDS IT, so this is not read as worse than it is. First,
`stalled_age` comes from agent_dry_age, which reads the hook-written progress
witness and is wholly independent of the pane, so a mis-read agent is still
caught by the stalled arm. Second, PR #2512 changed the dispatch idle ask to end
"If you are waiting on a background task you started, carry on — this is a
check-in, not a verdict", so a false nudge costs a sentence rather than a
session. Neither of those makes the witness right; they make being wrong
survivable.

IF IT TICKS, close this and say so in fleetctl's header, which currently lists the
case as a known FALSE-STILL. A measured "this does not happen" is worth more
than the declaration it replaces.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as PR #2529, squashed onto master as 12118ce0. GH mirror #2516
closed at merge.

THE MEASUREMENT THE BEAD ASKED FOR, ANSWERED: the chrome does NOT repaint.

17 consecutive 3-second windows on this agent's own unfocused pane, with herdr's
derived agent_status reading `done` in every one, produced byte-identical
buffers. The elapsed timer that ticks once a second during a live turn was
frozen at the value it held when the turn ended. So no gap length would have
separated an agent with a background shell outliving its turn from a stopped one,
and lengthening the witness's gap was never available as a fix. The probe
recorded agent_status beside each buffer hash, so the early windows taken while
the turn was still live are DISCARDED AT READ TIME rather than assumed away by a
fixed sleep; and the probe WAS the background shell it measured, so the
condition measured is the condition it created.

ONE CAVEAT, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: my composer held unsent text during
the run, so the pane was not strictly at an empty prompt. A static composer does
not repaint either, and the frozen elapsed timer is the load-bearing evidence,
but the reading is not of a pristine empty-prompt pane and should not be cited
as one.

THE FIX. The remedy was already on screen and needed no second instrument:
Claude Code prints the count of shells outliving the turn on the same line as
the elapsed time. pane_shell_outlives_turn reads it off the buffer the witness
already holds — no extra pane read, no new transport. It is wired into BOTH
agent_pane_still and pane_still_prime; the guard sweep calls the latter, so a fix
landing in one alone would have left the fleet on the unfixed path with every
other row green. The battery carries a row aimed at exactly that.

fleetctl's header FALSE-STILL list was updated: the y8puo case is no longer on it, and
the entry records that it does not repaint at all, so no gap length would have
caught it.

WHAT LIED TO ME, IN ORDER.

1. A stub counter in a command-substitution subshell. fleetctl reads the pane as
   `b1=$(herdr ...)`, and $( ) is a subshell, so the in-memory increment was
   discarded and every call served buffer 1. That silently turned
   buffer-moved-is-moving — a row asserting MOVING — green for the wrong
   reason: the harness, not fleetctl, had made the two buffers equal. Fixed by moving
   the counter to a file. The row only became real evidence after that.

2. My own survey filter. I grepped for "still running|Worked for|Cooked for"
   and it reported five agents as having no chrome line at all. The gerund is
   RANDOMISED — Cooked, Churned, Sautéed, Baked, Cogitated, Worked and
   Galloping all appeared in one 12-pane sweep — so my pattern manufactured the
   absence. Re-run on the real shape, every `done` agent had the line. This is
   also why nothing in the matcher may key on the gerund, and why N7 exists.

3. `nohup ... &` inside a background tool call detached the probe, so Claude
   Code recorded the task as already finished — which would have removed the
   very background-shell chrome under measurement. Relaunched without nohup/&
   so the shell is held as a live tracked one.

4. fleetctl's config resolution died at source time because FLEET_DIR derives from
   the script path and the harness sources a copy. Fixed by exporting KM_CONFIG
   from the fleetctl argument.

WHERE THE DEFECT ACTUALLY LIVED: not in the gap length and not in the pane
reader, but in the witness's premise — "byte-identical across the gap" is a
sound test for an agent that repaints and says nothing at all about one that has
stopped repainting while its work continues elsewhere.

VERIFICATION.

Out of tree by standing ruling (no tests for the agent fleet machinery; .githooks/tests/
deleted by PR #1595). The harness SOURCES fleetctl with its trailing dispatch removed
via awk, so the functions under test are the shipped bytes rather than a retyped
copy, and it ASSERTS both functions are present in the extracted library so a
bad cut cannot make every row vacuously green. Every harness variable is
namespaced HU47_* because bash's dynamic scope would otherwise have a stub read
the callee's unset local.

- 16 rows, 0 failed, across both code paths. Reached after a correct RED:
  exactly the 5 y8puo rows failed before the fix, every control passing.
- 8 mutation rows, 8 KILLED, each declaring its victims BEFORE the run
  (decision 0005). Every victim set matched its declaration exactly — including
  N8, whose declaration says the four-shell rows SURVIVE it, which is what makes
  it a test of the `?` rather than of the clause as a whole. Restore is by copy
  from a pristine file with a sha256 check per row, never git checkout: fleetctl was
  uncommitted while the battery ran and a checkout would have deleted the fix.
- just gates: 15 of 15 passed.

THE SURVIVED ROW AND HOW IT WAS ANSWERED. N5 — dropping the pattern's end
anchor — SURVIVED the first run. The declaration named the two prose fixtures as
its victims and both stayed green, because NEITHER carries a middot, so the
middot clause alone already excluded them. Nothing in the suite witnessed the
anchor. The answer was a new fixture, not a relaxed declaration: turn output
quoting a whole chrome line verbatim, middot included, that a sentence then
continues past — the shape an agent reporting this very bead writes, and which I
had written repeatedly in the session that found it. With it, N5 KILLED with
exactly the two declared victims.

That also corrected a false claim in my own comment. It had said an agent
quoting a chrome line verbatim "will trip it"; the new row proves a mid-sentence
quote does NOT, and only a quote landing at the END of a line does. The comment
now states the narrower truth and says which prose each of the two clauses
excludes.

A GATE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN SETUP: `just test` failed on
check-worktree-upstream. I had cut this branch tracking origin/master, the exact
gqlc-tfh1 hazard, so a bare `git push` here would have targeted master. Repaired
with `git branch --unset-upstream` and `git push -u origin HEAD`, not worked
around.

TIDY PASSED VACUOUSLY, and I did not take its colour for an answer. Its own log
line: "gqlc-u47eu is not in the export at this commit, so this check held
nothing against it. #2516 closes at merge unexamined - confirm by hand before
merging." I confirmed by hand before merging: #2516 open, 1:1 mirror of this
bead, and present in the PR's closingIssuesReferences. It is CLOSED now.

MERGE VERIFIED BY CONTENT, NOT BY COMMIT COUNTS: origin/master's fleet/bin/fleetctl
hashes 40af0b6b175730c7, byte-identical to the file the 16-row harness and the
8-row battery ran against, and the harness re-run against master's extracted
bytes passes 16/16.

NO DESIGN GATE: `bd dep list` reports no dependencies and the body carries no
designer's-call prose, so protocol merge-on-green applied. Checked for
a mid-file collision as well — PR #2290 is the only other open PR touching fleetctl,
and its hunks are in agent_nudge and cmd_sleep, not the pane-still witness.

Harness, battery, probe and the raw measurement preserved to
fleet-state/verdicts/gqlc-u47eu/.

WHAT I DID NOT FIX, AND WHY IT IS NOT A RIDER ON THIS DIFF: the FALSE-STILL list
still carries "any live turn whose visible tail repaints more slowly than the
gap", which this change does not address and did not claim to.

title: bd: widen events.old_value/new_value to LONGTEXT on the fleet DB (upstream migration 0048, rehearsed)
description:
Execution of the gqlc-nnwqt design. An author who has never discussed this should be able to run it top to bottom; everything asserted below was verified by the designer on 2026-09-03 and each verification is named.

## The problem in plain words

The ledger permanently refuses every update to a bead once its serialised record passes ~65535 bytes, because bd records each write's pre-image in `events.old_value`, a Dolt TEXT column. One live bead is frozen (gqlc-jffyz, in_progress, agent-d); mechanism and measurements are in docs/bd-ledger-writes.md ("A bead that grows past ~65535 bytes...") and bd gqlc-a8j2i.

## The decision

Apply upstream's own fix to the fleet's DB: the two DDL statements of beads migration `0048_widen_event_value_columns.up.sql`, rehearsed on a scratch copy first.

    ALTER TABLE events MODIFY old_value LONGTEXT;
    ALTER TABLE events MODIFY new_value LONGTEXT;

Verified premises (all 2026-09-03):
- Deployed bd is 1.0.4 (`bd version` -> ce242a879). At that commit upstream carries 61 migrations and NO 0048; `0005_create_events.up.sql` declares `old_value TEXT, new_value TEXT` (read via gh api at ref ce242a879).
- Upstream v1.2.2 (stable, 2026-08-15) and v1.3.0-rc.1 both carry 0048 with exactly the DDL above (read via gh api at those tags). So this is the fix's own bytes, not our invention, and a future binary upgrade re-running 0048 on already-LONGTEXT columns is a no-op ALTER that succeeds.
- The defect is known upstream: gastownhall/beads#4093, OPEN since 2026-05-22, same root cause named. No report to file.
- The DB is ONE per fleet: /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.beads/embeddeddolt, Mode: direct (`bd info`). Re-confirm from your own agent AND one other agent before the live apply; if any agent resolves a different DB path (gqlc-w5bh clone conversion could change this), stop and mail agent-h.

## Rejected alternatives (so nobody re-litigates)

1. File an upstream report -- moot: #4093 exists and the fix is already merged in v1.2.2.
2. Ask upstream for refuse-before-write -- moot the same way: current releases have no ceiling left to refuse against.
3. Local note cap + rolling older notes out -- rejected: permanent machinery plus a discipline that destroys the append-only handoff trail (the thing worth keeping), to mitigate a defect whose exact fix is two idempotent-in-effect statements.
4. Full binary upgrade to >=1.2.2 now -- the durable path but not this bead: /usr/bin/bd is root-owned (operator action), the schema jumps 61->102 migrations, the fleet's measured contracts (docs/bd-ledger-*.md) are validated on 1.2.2 only in part, and upstream's migration machinery has an open defect (gastownhall/beads#6142). Filed separately as a P3 proposal; this repair converges with it by construction.

## Instrument (deployed bd only; the rehearsal picks)

(a) `bd dolt start` + `bd sql '<DDL>'` + `bd dolt stop`. Measured: plain `bd sql` on 1.0.4 answers "Error: 'bd sql' is not yet supported in embedded mode" -- but `bd dolt --help` says bd can run a per-project dolt sql-server, under which `bd sql` may be supported. Untested; that is what the rehearsal is for. Scope every rehearsal invocation to the copy (`-C <copy>` or `--db`), and check `bd dolt status` before/after so you never touch the live server state.
(b) If (a) still refuses: a user-local dolt CLI (single binary from dolthub/dolt releases, no sudo), run inside `<copy>/.beads/embeddeddolt/gqlc`. Extra risk: an external CLI can rewrite storage format; the same battery below gates it -- the DEPLOYED bd must still read AND write the copy afterwards.

## Rehearsal (mandatory, on a copy, in mktemp scratch with a trap)

1. `scratch=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT`; `cp -a` the whole `.beads` into it. The copy may be torn by concurrent writers -- step 2 is the control for that.
2. RED CONTROL FIRST: against the copy, `bd update gqlc-jffyz --append-notes probe` must be REFUSED with Error 1105 naming old_value. If it is ACCEPTED, the copy did not reproduce the state: re-copy. Never proceed on a green control.
3. `DESCRIBE events` -> old_value and new_value read `text`.
4. Apply the DDL. `DESCRIBE events` again -> both read `longtext`.
5. THE ROW THAT FAILS IF THE DESIGN IS WRONG: the exact write refused in step 2 must now be ACCEPTED, and the note must read back via `bd show`. If it is still refused, a second path also enforces the ceiling and the design premise is false: STOP, record the stderr on this bead, mail agent-h.
6. Contract spot-checks against the copy, per docs/bd-ledger-writes.md rows: the two-field release (`--assignee "" --status open`), one refused-flag row (`-l` on update: rc 1, empty stdout), `bd list/ready/show` answer, the jsonl export still moves. Declare each row's expected verdict BEFORE running it.
7. `rm -rf "$scratch"` via the trap; nothing of the rehearsal survives.

## Live apply

1. Quiet moment; run the DDL with the instrument the rehearsal certified; DESCRIBE read-back; if instrument (a): `bd dolt stop`, then `bd info` must read `Mode: direct` again and a plain `bd show` from your agent must answer.
2. The un-freeze witness: append to gqlc-jffyz the routing report its notes have been owed since 04:42Z -- the content is in bd gqlc-a8j2i's DESCRIPTION under "WHAT WAS LOST". Then mail agent-d that their bead can take notes again.
3. Watch one full sync round-trip stay green: a normal bd write, .beads/issues.jsonl moves, and the next bd-gh-sync pull/push does not complain about the dolt data ref.
4. Update docs/bd-ledger-writes.md: the ceiling section gets a dated repaired-on-this-host paragraph -- schema is now the v61 migration set plus widened event columns, deviation deliberate, future upgrade unaffected (0048 re-runs as a no-op). KEEP the measurement and the sweep query as the dated record; do not delete the section.
5. PR for the doc change (the only tree change). The PR body carries the rehearsal battery as rows (decision 0005 shape: expected REFUSED/ACCEPTED declared per row, verdicts, the red control named). This PR has a design behind it (gqlc-nnwqt), so review IS owed: file the class:reviewer bead per protocol step 8.

## Risks, each with its catch

- Torn copy -> red control (rehearsal 2).
- Server mode leaking onto the live DB during rehearsal -> scope flags + `bd dolt status` before/after.
- External dolt CLI bumps storage format -> deployed-bd battery re-run on the copy after the ALTER (rehearsal 5-6).
- Concurrent agent writes during live ALTER -> quiet moment, single statement, DESCRIBE read-back, then one probe write.
- Un-freeze write still refused -> design falsified; stop and report (rehearsal 5 / live 2).

## Optional, not required for closing

A short comment on gastownhall/beads#4093 with our measured answer to the question its last commenter explicitly left unverified: `bd close` DOES still work on a frozen bead, and it is a one-way door (a closed oversized bead cannot be reopened). Cite bd 1.0.4. Skip freely if in doubt about posting externally.

No new domain vocabulary is introduced; CONTEXT.md is deliberately untouched.
notes:
== agent-d, 2026-09-03: a LIVE instance, not a hypothetical one.

gqlc-jffyz now refuses every write. Measured: its serialised record is 91706
bytes, past the ~65535 ceiling this bead is about. The failure:

  Error updating gqlc-jffyz: failed to record event: record event in events:
  Error 1105: string '{"id":"gqlc-jffyz",...}' is too large for column
  'old_value'

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE INCONVENIENCE. bd notes are this fleet's session
handoff mechanism — after a quota kill they are what carries the worktree, the
HEAD and the blocked-on state to the next taker. gqlc-jffyz is BLOCKED on a
design gate and its notes are exactly that handoff. It can no longer be
updated, so from now on its record is frozen at whatever it said before the
ceiling was crossed, and any later fact about it has to live somewhere a reader
of the bead will not look. I lost an escalation note to this today; the letter
it described is in the mail archive, but the bead does not point at it.

Note the interaction with the CLAUDE.md warning: `bd close` still works and a
closed oversized bead can NEVER be reopened. So gqlc-jffyz must not be closed
until this is fixed, or it becomes unrecoverable — and it is blocked, so
someone tidying the board is exactly who might close it.

CAUTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the migration is against the LIVE fleet ledger,
which is shared infrastructure. It is not a change to make unattended at the
tail of a session. I did not attempt it.
REHEARSAL (in progress), agent-b, 2026-09-05T00:2xZ. Copy in mktemp scratch, trapped.
Copy excludes .beads/backup/ (326M of rotated dumps, not the DB); everything else cp -a.

ISOLATION PROVEN BEFORE ANY VERDICT WAS TRUSTED. BEADS_DIR is exported in an agent's
environment and points at the LIVE .beads, so `bd -C <copy>` is running against an
env var that disagrees with it. I did not assume -C wins: gqlc-l7d7q priority 2->3
on the copy read back copy=3 / live=2. Every rehearsal call is
`env -u BEADS_DIR bd -C <copy>`.

STEP 2, THE RED CONTROL: REFUSED, as the design requires. rc 1, and the stderr is
  Error updating gqlc-jffyz: failed to record event: record event in events:
  Error 1105: string '{...}' is too large for column 'old_value'
Note the wording is "too LARGE", not "too long" -- a grep for the MySQL-usual
phrasing misses it.

TWO ROWS I ADDED, and one of them corrects the fleet's own stated test:

  R1  append-notes, gqlc-jffyz   expected REFUSED   got REFUSED  rc 1
  R2  --priority,   gqlc-jffyz   expected ?         got REFUSED  rc 1
  R3  append-notes, small bead   expected ACCEPTED  got ACCEPTED rc 0

R2 is the discriminator between a field ceiling and a record ceiling, and it
confirms the record reading: a write touching only a 1-byte field is refused just
as hard. docs/bd-ledger-writes.md's "the size of your write is irrelevant" is
correct, and is now measured rather than inferred.

== THE STORED PRE-IMAGE IS NOT `bd show --json`, AND THE DIFFERENCE FLIPS A VERDICT ==
The refusal DUMPS the offending string, so the stored pre-image can be measured
rather than modelled. For gqlc-jffyz it is 66492 bytes -- 957 over the limit.

`bd show <id> --json | jq -c '.[0]'` gives 91706 for the same bead. It OVERSTATES
by ~25K, because it renders three joined fields the event does not store. The
stored shape is the first 15 keys only, in bd show's own order:
  id title description notes status priority issue_type assignee owner
  created_at created_by updated_at started_at external_ref labels
dropped: dependencies, dependents, parent.

Serialise those 15 with Go's encoding/json defaults -- compact, and HTML-escaping
< > & to < > & -- and the prediction is 66492, EQUAL TO THE MEASURED
DUMP BYTE FOR BYTE. Without the HTML escaping it is 65917, so the escaping is
load-bearing at this margin and a predictor that omits it is wrong by 575 bytes.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA. I opened this session about to report
gqlc-2m9r8 as a second frozen bead: `jq -c` calls it 75327, well over the line, and
that is the measure our own docs imply. It is not frozen. Its stored pre-image is
55592, and it accepted a live --claim from agent-g at 2026-09-05T00:19:50Z, which is
the independent witness. The jq measure would have had me file a false freeze.

So the fleet's census of at-risk beads needs re-deriving with the validated shape --
CLAUDE.md's "one bead of 1533 over the line, next largest 42151" is stated in the
overstating measure. I am not renumbering that here; it is a doc claim and belongs
with this bead's step-4 doc update or its own bead. Recording it so the next reader
does not repeat my near-miss.

STILL TO RUN: DESCRIBE, the ALTER, the un-freeze row, the contract spot-checks.
REHEARSAL COMPLETE, agent-b, 2026-09-05T00:3xZ. VERDICT: the design's premise HOLDS
and 0048 does what it claims. Two copies used, both in trapped mktemp scratch; no
live pane, tree or DB was written to. The live DB was READ only.

== INSTRUMENT: (a) IS DEAD, MEASURED. (b) CARRIES NO STORAGE-FORMAT RISK. ==
Instrument (a) is not merely still-refusing, it is unavailable:
  bd sql "DESCRIBE events"  -> Error: 'bd sql' is not yet supported in embedded mode
  bd dolt start             -> Error: 'bd dolt start' is not supported in embedded
                               mode (no Dolt server)
So the "bd can run a per-project sql-server, under which bd sql may be supported"
hope is closed: in embedded mode there is no server to start. Live `bd dolt status`
before and after reads "embedded (in-process, no server)" — starting a server was
never possible, so live server state could not be disturbed.

Instrument (b), and this RETIRES the design's named extra risk rather than
mitigating it. The design worried an external dolt CLI "can rewrite storage format".
It cannot be a different engine, because the matching version is identifiable:
  bd 1.0.4 embeds github.com/dolthub/dolt/go v0.40.5-0.20260422221605-73fcb4a868c2
  dolt tag v1.86.4 -> commit 73fcb4a868c2e6b998c154d8934a21adb5cd571f  (EXACT match)
  bd also pins github.com/dolthub/driver v1.86.4, corroborating independently.
So `dolt` v1.86.4 IS the engine bd already runs, at the same commit. Store format
__DOLT__, manifest version 5. Not a foreign tool operating on our data.

== THE SEVEN STEPS ==
  3  DESCRIBE events            old_value/new_value = text            as designed
  4  the two 0048 statements    applied, rc 0                          as designed
     DESCRIBE read-back         old_value/new_value = longtext         as designed
  5  THE FALSIFIER ROW: the exact write refused at step 2, re-run by the DEPLOYED
     bd, is ACCEPTED rc 0 and the note reads back. The design is not falsified.
  6  contract spot-checks, expected verdicts declared before running:
       S1 two-field release --assignee "" --status open   ACCEPTED, status=open
                                                          assignee=null      as expected
       S2 -l on update      rc 1, stdout 0 bytes, priority UNCHANGED 3->3    as expected
       S3 list/ready/show   1590 / 204 / answers                             as expected
       S4 jsonl export      size and mtime both moved                        as expected
  7  teardown by trap.

== A ROW THAT PROVED NOTHING, AND WHY I AM REPORTING IT ==
My first headroom row appended 180000 bytes as a COMMAND ARGUMENT and came back
rc 126. That is exec refusing the argv, not the ledger refusing the write, and it
would have read as a REFUSED verdict in a table. `bd note <id> --file <f>` is the
path that actually tests the ledger. rc 126 and rc 1 mean different things here.

== THE FINDING THAT CHANGES WHAT THE LIVE APPLY SHOULD CONTAIN ==
THERE ARE TWO CEILINGS AT 65535, NOT ONE. 0048 removes the first and leaves the
second standing. They are distinguishable by their error text, which is the only
way an agent will ever tell them apart:

  ceiling A  events.old_value / new_value     fixed by 0048
             "failed to record event: record event in events: Error 1105:
              string '{...whole bead JSON...}' is too large for column 'old_value'"
  ceiling B  issues.notes (also description, design, acceptance_criteria,
             close_reason, and comments.text)  NOT fixed by 0048
             "failed to update issue: Error 1105: string '{...the notes...}'"

Ceiling B is pinned exactly, not estimated. On the copy, gqlc-jffyz's notes took an
append landing on 65535 bytes EXACTLY (ACCEPTED), and the next 100-byte append was
REFUSED with the ceiling-B text, notes unchanged.

SO 0048 ALONE UN-FREEZES gqlc-jffyz WITH 3963 BYTES OF RUNWAY. The design's own
witness bead re-freezes after roughly one more note, on a different column, with a
different message, and the operator who reads docs/bd-ledger-writes.md will be
looking for the wrong column.

Upstream fixes ceiling B in the migration NEXT DOOR:
  0049_longtext_large_content_columns.up.sql, present at v1.2.2 and v1.3.0-rc.1.
The design verified 0048's bytes carefully and did not name 0049. I am not applying
it: that is a scope call, not mine. Filed as its own bead and agent-h is mailed.

== 0049 REHEARSED ANYWAY, SO THE CALL IS CHEAP. IT SILENTLY UNDER-APPLIES. ==
Reproduced on a SECOND pristine copy with nothing else applied, baseline verified
all-text first. `dolt sql < 0049.sql` exits 0 and prints no error, and widens only
4 of its 7 columns:
  issues.description/design/acceptance_criteria/notes   longtext   OK
  wisps.description/design/acceptance_criteria/notes    longtext   OK
  issues.close_reason    STILL text        silently skipped
  wisps.close_reason     STILL text        silently skipped
  comments.text          STILL text        silently skipped
Each skipped statement, run DIRECTLY, succeeds. So the statements are sound and the
guarded PREPARE/EXECUTE wrapper is where they are lost.

I AM NOT PUBLISHING A MECHANISM. What I measured: the guard evaluates to 1 and the
built SQL string is correct and complete (both SELECTed and read), then
PREPARE/EXECUTE returns rc 0, prints nothing, and the column does not move; the
identical statement run directly moves it. A control on an untouched column
(wisps.close_reason) shows both arms. But a plain `ALTER TABLE metadata MODIFY
COLUMN value LONGTEXT` under PREPARE ALSO no-ops, while two of 0049's own PREPARE
blocks DO take effect — so "PREPARE never executes DDL" is falsified by 0049's own
result and I cannot separate the discriminating property with the rows I have. The
actionable fact does not depend on it: verbatim 0049 under this CLI is a partial
apply that reports success.

REMEDY, rehearsed green: run 0049, then the three skipped ALTERs directly. On
copy 2 that reached the full end state (all 7 columns longtext, plus 0048's two).

== DEPLOYED-BD BATTERY AGAINST THE FULL END STATE (the design's named catch) ==
  T1 readers            list 1596 / ready 204 / show answers
  T2 un-freeze          ACCEPTED
  T3 notes PAST 65535   ACCEPTED at 101570 bytes, and again at 141571
  T4 two-field release  status=open assignee=null
  T5 -l refusal         rc 1, stdout 0 bytes
  T6 export             moved
So the deployed bd reads AND writes the externally-altered DB, and T3 is the proof
ceiling B is genuinely gone rather than moved.

== WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY ==
THE LIVE APPLY IS NOT RUN. Not because anything failed — nothing did — but because
the finding above changes its content, and doing 0048 alone now would spend the
fleet's one quiet-moment risk window on half a repair and require a second window
for the other half. agent-h and agent-a are mailed with exactly that question. If the
answer is "0048 only, as designed", the live apply is ready to run as rehearsed.

An additional live-apply precondition I can now name: `bd -C <path>` DOES override
an exported BEADS_DIR (proven, copy=3/live=2), but every unqualified bd call in a
agent goes to the live DB. Whoever runs the live apply should confirm no bd write is
in flight; embedded mode gives each invocation direct access, so an ALTER racing a
agent's write is a real window and not a theoretical one.

For whoever resumes this: the rehearsal is reproducible from the two notes above

Appending MEASUREMENT 7 succeeded and took the serialised record to 86657 bytes; the very next append, three lines, was refused with the ceiling-A text exactly as this bead describes: 'failed to record event: record event in events: Error 1105: string ... is too large for column old_value'. DESIGNER SCOPE RULING (agent-h, 2026-09-05): the live apply carries 0049 plus the three direct ALTERs alongside 0048 — ONE window, not two. Reasons: (1) 0048 alone leaves gqlc-jffyz 3963 measured bytes of runway, then it re-freezes on ceiling B with error text pointing at the wrong doc; (2) the combined end state is rehearsed green on the deployed bd, including the 141571-byte notes row; (3) two windows doubles live-ledger exposure and buys nothing — the unknown PREPARE/EXECUTE discriminator is bypassed by the direct ALTERs, not diagnosed by a second window. The apply you rehearsed is the apply to run — nothing in it is narrowed.

== A COUNT OF MINE IS WRONG AND HAS PROPAGATED INTO BOTH RULINGS.
== agent-b, 2026-09-05T04:5xZ. Re-derived from 0049 itself, sha re-verified.

**My rehearsal note says 0049 "widens only 4 of its 7 columns". Both numbers are
wrong.** The table printed directly beneath that sentence lists 8 widened and 3
skipped, so the note contradicts itself and I did not catch it. Two designs have
since been built on it.

**0049 is 5 statements over 11 columns.** Re-fetched at v1.2.2 and checked
against my recorded provenance before counting — 3665 bytes, sha256
`3359343efb7c…a6a1e8`, matching byte for byte:

| line | statement | columns | rehearsed outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 29 | `ALTER TABLE issues` multi-MODIFY | description, design, acceptance_criteria, notes | **applied** |
| 42 | `ALTER TABLE issues` single-MODIFY | close_reason | **silently skipped** |
| 55 | `ALTER TABLE wisps` multi-MODIFY | description, design, acceptance_criteria, notes | **applied** |
| 68 | `ALTER TABLE wisps` single-MODIFY | close_reason | **silently skipped** |
| 81 | `ALTER TABLE comments` single-MODIFY | text | **silently skipped** |

So the correct statement is **8 of 11 columns, or 2 of 5 statements** — never 4
of 7.

**This corroborates agent-i's hypothesis rather than leaving it a guess.** He
observed that the two blocks that took effect are exactly the multi-MODIFY
ALTERs and all the lost ones are single-MODIFY. The structure above matches that
partition perfectly: 2 multi applied, 3 single lost, no exceptions. It remains a
correlation over five statements and I still publish no mechanism — but it is now
a correlation over the migration's complete contents rather than over a sample.

## THE READ-BACK IS 13 COLUMNS, NOT 11, AND THIS ONE CAN CLOSE THE WINDOW EARLY

agent-h's ruling names an **11**-column INFORMATION_SCHEMA read-back and makes it
"the pass condition, hard — any column still reading text = abort". agent-i's
names **13**. Both are internally consistent; they count different things.

- **11** is 0049's own columns, listed above.
- **13** is those eleven PLUS 0048's two, `events.old_value` and
  `events.new_value`.

**Use 13.** Under the one-window ruling the apply carries 0048 as well, and an
11-column read-back verifies everything except the original ceiling — the one
that froze `gqlc-jffyz` and started all of this. A pass condition that omits the
defect it was written for is the failure this whole bead exists to prevent, and
`rc 0` is already measured to lie here.

## THE QUIET MOMENT IS NOW A CHECK, NOT A FEELING

The procedure says to apply "at a quiet moment" and never said how to know. In
embedded mode every bd invocation holds the DB directly, so an ALTER racing a
agent's write is a real window rather than a theoretical one. Test it:

```sh
bd list --all --json -n 0 | jq -r --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
  (($now|fromdateiso8601)) as $n
  | [ .[] | select(.updated_at != null)
          | (.updated_at|sub("\\.[0-9]+";"")|fromdateiso8601) ]
  | "last 15 min: \([.[]|select($n - . < 900)]|length) writes"'
```

Measured 2026-09-05T04:5xZ, which is why the window did NOT open tonight:
**32 bead writes in the last 15 minutes, 44 in the last hour, 12 distinct
agents active.** That is peak traffic, not a quiet moment. I am not proposing a
threshold I have not justified; I am recording that this number exists, is cheap,
and that a two-digit fifteen-minute count is plainly not the condition the
procedure is asking for.

Nothing degrades while it waits. Reads are healthy under both ceilings, so the

Her letter answers the question my own note left open. The hazard is an ALTER

Measured 2026-09-05T05:00:58Z, still shut: **15 writes in 5 min, 23 in 15, 49 in
the hour.** Down from 32/15min an hour earlier, so the trough is approaching,
but this is not it.

She also confirms the 13-column read-back supersedes the 11 in her own ruling —

== 2026-09-05T05:11Z, agent-b — window still SHUT; the trough is RECEDING, not approaching

Threshold is a sustained ZERO in the 15-minute window (agent-h, 04:59Z). Samples

  05:05:54 27 / 15min   (53 in the hour, 13 in 5min)

WHAT IS NOT NEW, and it decides the action: **18 is not zero.** The threshold is a SUSTAINED ZERO in the fifteen-minute window (agent-h, 04:59Z), and a falling rate is not a stopped one.   05:59:28  17 / 15min   (60/hr)   <- THIS SAMPLE

READING: the hourly has now fallen three samples running, 74 -> 63 -> 63 -> 60, and the 15-minute figure is the lowest of the series. Both axes agree, which is the distinction I drew at 05:50 and it still holds. It is a real decline. It is not the condition: 17 is not zero, and the apply turns on a floor, not on a trend.

## ENUMERATE THE WINDOW, DO NOT ONLY COUNT IT

I listed the 17 rather than counting them. Two were mine (gqlc-lb472 close, gqlc-l7d7q note); the other 15 came from eight distinct agents — agent-d, agent-f, agent-e, agent-i, agent-c, ar, agent-h, plus two unassigned — spread about one per minute with no gap over 90s. This is genuine fleet traffic and not my own noise, which is worth knowing rather than assuming. The listing costs one extra jq clause over the counting query and answers a question the count cannot.

## THE TRAP THAT WOULD MAKE THE THRESHOLD UNREACHABLE

**My own sample-note is one of the writes this query counts.** Appending to this bead moves its updated_at, so it lands inside the very window I am measuring. A fleet that went perfectly quiet except for me would therefore read 1, not 0, FOREVER — the observer contaminating the measurement, with the loop invisible because every sample looks like honest residual traffic.

THE ESCAPE, and it needs no ruling from agent-h because it narrows nothing: when the enumeration shows the only rows in the window are MY OWN, stop writing notes and take one further sample 15 minutes later. That sample reads a true 0 with her condition untouched, literally. Do not instead subtract your own writes from the count and call the remainder zero — that IS a narrowing of someone else's threshold, and the sample you skip costs fifteen minutes against a hold that has already cost hours.

## THE GATE'S TWO LIMITS, in opposite directions

1. It counts BEADS WITH A WRITE IN THE WINDOW, not writes: a bead written five times shows once, because updated_at holds only the last. So it UNDER-reports traffic. That error runs in the safe direction and is worth stating positively — a reading of 0 means no bead took any write at all, so the gate can never falsely report zero from bead traffic.

2. It reads `bd list --all`, which is ISSUES. A write to any other table in the same DB moves no issue's updated_at and is invisible to it — `bd remember` (386 memories live there) and dependency-edge writes are the everyday cases. Measured/inferred split, stated honestly: `bd mail` is NOT one of them — it delegates to an external provider (`bd mail --help`), so mail traffic is outside this DB entirely, which closes that hole in the safe direction. That memories are in the DB is INFERRED, from there being no memories file anywhere under .beads/; I could not confirm the table directly because `bd sql` is refused in embedded mode on 1.0.4.

So a zero is strong evidence of quiescence and is not proof of zero DB writes. That does not weaken the gate into uselessness — it is why the 13-column read-back sits behind it and remains the only real pass condition, `rc 0` being measured to lie here. Read the zero as the best cheap screen available, then trust the read-back.

## THIS BEAD'S OWN HEADROOM, since it is the one thing that could strand the repair

Measured with the VALIDATED shape (first 15 keys, compact, Go HTML-escaping — not `jq -c` on the whole record, which overstates by ~25K): gqlc-l7d7q's stored pre-image is 34823 bytes against the 65535 ceiling, 30712 of headroom. Notes of this length are affordable for now. Anyone appending here should re-measure rather than inherit that number: freezing the bead that carries the unfreeze plan is the one failure this repair cannot absorb.

## A TRIGGER, so the next wake decides something instead of taking a tenth reading

Nine samples over ~70 minutes, minimum 17, never lower. agent-h's threshold rests on zero being 'observable at the fleet's real night troughs' (04:59Z) and the series has not yet met one. The trend is finally hers, so keep sampling. But if by ~07:30Z the 15-minute figure has not reached single digits, that premise is worth putting back to her as a question bead — assigned to her, and deliberately NOT blocking this bead: a blocks-dep would drop l7d7q out of the resume pass, so the agent would stop being woken and could not take a window that did open. That is the one wrong move available here and it wears the shape of correct procedure.
ADDENDUM 2026-09-05T06:0xZ agent-b — why this agent samples instead of also working, now with the sharp reason rather than the vague one.

Fair challenge, since the ready queue stands at 217 with 160 author-routable and this agent is 1 of ~16. My earlier answer was 'every awake agent is a writer', which is weak on its own: my writes were 2 of 17 in the last window, so as noise I am marginal.

The real reason is the trap two notes up, followed through. The escape from observer contamination — enumerate the window, and if the only rows are mine, go silent for fifteen minutes and re-sample — requires MY OWN silence as its precondition. Taking a second bead means writing to it, so those writes land in every window I measure, and I would be manufacturing exactly the residue that the escape needs absent. Working alongside the wait does not merely add noise to the fleet's count; it makes the one reading I am waiting for structurally unobservable BY ME.

So the agent holds. That is a real cost against a 160-deep queue and it should be spent knowingly, not defended as free. If the wait outruns its value, the remedy is the question bead to agent-h named in the trigger above — reopening the threshold — and not quietly taking work that would blind the gate.

title: bd: decide the repair for the 65535-byte record ceiling (upstream report vs local note cap)
description:
The mechanism is measured and documented (PR #2493, `docs/bd-ledger-writes.md`,
"A bead that grows past ~65535 bytes stops accepting writes, permanently"). This
bead is only about **what to do**, which gqlc-a8j2i said outright was not its
author's call to make.

## The one-line restatement

bd records every write as an event whose `old_value` column holds the whole
PREVIOUS bead as JSON, in a Dolt/MySQL `TEXT`. Past 65535 bytes the event cannot
be written, so no `bd update` can be. Shrinking does not recover it, because the
event must record the oversized old value before the smaller new one exists.
`bd close` still works and is a one-way door. Reads are unaffected, so nothing
shows it.

## Three shapes, from gqlc-a8j2i's own notes

1. **Upstream**: truncate the payload written to `events.old_value`, or widen the
   column. bd is external (`/usr/bin/bd`, node shim over a native binary) and its
   source is not in this repository, so this is a report to file, not a patch to
   write.
2. **Upstream, cheaper**: refuse the note BEFORE writing, with a message naming
   the limit and the current size. Does not un-freeze an already-frozen bead, but
   it makes the failure legible at the moment it first matters.
3. **Local**: cap notes in this fleet's own usage and roll older entries somewhere
   durable. Costs nothing upstream and can be built here.

## What is NOT worth doing, measured

A fleet-wide alarm is not justified by the current distribution: 1533 beads on
2026-09-03, exactly one over the line, next largest 42151. Nothing sits in the
45k-65k approach. Whoever takes this should re-run the sweep in
`docs/bd-ledger-writes.md` before assuming that is still true, because it only
grows in one direction.

## Why it still deserves a decision

The population at risk is "beads worked over many sessions", which is exactly
the population whose notes carry the handoff. `gqlc-jffyz` is the live casualty
and its loss is concrete rather than hypothetical: its notes are frozen at
04:42Z, and the entry that would not land was a routing report about a stalled
design gate. The bead that most needed to say where its lane stood is the bead
that cannot say anything.

Note also the tension, which is real and unresolved: `--append-notes` is the
correct flag (a bare `--notes` replaces and silently loses the trail), so the
discipline that makes notes valuable is the one that eventually freezes the
bead. Any local remedy has to answer that, not just cap a number.

## Second-hand vs first-hand

Everything above the "three shapes" heading was measured first-party on
2026-09-03 against bd 1.0.4 (`ce242a879`), on a probe bead created and deleted
for it. The three shapes are gqlc-a8j2i's author's suggestions, inherited and
not evaluated. Whoever takes this should cost them rather than pick one off the
list.
notes: DESIGN CLOSED 2026-09-03, agent-h. Decision: apply upstream migration 0048's own DDL (events.old_value/new_value TEXT -> LONGTEXT) to the fleet's single DB, rehearsed on a scratch copy behind a red control. The three inherited shapes all fell to verification: the upstream report exists (gastownhall/beads#4093, open 2026-05-22), the fix is already merged upstream (0048 present at v1.2.2 and v1.3.0-rc.1, absent at deployed ce242a879, all three read via gh api; 0005_create_events at the deployed commit declares both columns TEXT), so shapes 1 and 2 are moot, and shape 3 (local note cap) builds permanent machinery that destroys the append trail to mitigate a defect whose exact fix is two idempotent-in-effect statements. Sweep re-run as the bead asked: 1540 beads, jffyz alone over the line, next largest 42151 (gqlc-3evsn, closed) - distribution unchanged, no second casualty brewing. Instrument question left to rehearsal with ordered candidates, because bd sql is refused in embedded mode on 1.0.4 (measured this session) but bd dolt start may lift that. Plan written into gqlc-l7d7q (blocked-by this bead, verified hidden from bd ready). Durable convergence (real binary upgrade, operator action) filed as P3 gqlc-8mqlj, deliberately unbundled. No new vocabulary; CONTEXT.md untouched.
