title: graph: LabelSetKey joins on an unquoted ampersand, so an ampersand-bearing label is unrepresentable
description:
DISCOVERED FROM gqlc-tzu9r (delimited identifier decoding), which refuses the
label rather than making it representable.

graph.LabelSet.Key (graph/labelset.go:21-26) sorts, dedupes and joins the labels
with "&" without quoting them, and LabelSetKey.Split (:30-35) cuts on the same
byte. So the one-label set {"A&B"} and the two-label set {"A","B"} produce the
identical key "A&B". The key IS an element type's identity — it keys the node and
edge maps, it reaches schema JSON, EdgeKey and codegen — so the collision is a
type-identity forgery in the place that decides which type is which.

Until gqlc-tzu9r no label could contain an ampersand, because the schema front
end carried a delimited identifier's delimiters through undecoded and the two
keys therefore differed by their backticks. That was an accident, not a guard.
Decoding makes (:`A&B`) a one-label set named A&B, so gqlc-tzu9r adds
ErrAmpersandInLabel and refuses it — fail-closed, in the one place a label is
read.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. Whether an ampersand-bearing label should be REPRESENTABLE,
and if so how. The obvious remedy is quoting inside Key the way
graph/propertytype.go:246-283 quoteFieldName/splitFieldName already quote a
record field name, giving graph two consistent quoting layers. It is design-sized
rather than a fix because the key is a persisted, cross-layer identity: changing
its spelling changes schema JSON, EdgeKey, every golden that carries a key, and
whatever in codegen reads one. That is why gqlc-tzu9r refused instead.

FALSIFIER, today: graph.LabelSet{"A&B"}.Key() == graph.LabelSet{"A","B"}.Key().
If a fix lands, the two must differ and Split must return the label the author
wrote.

Not urgent: nothing can produce such a label through the schema front end once
gqlc-tzu9r's refusal is in, so this is about a capability gqlc declines, not a
defect a user can reach.
close_reason: Design written into gqlc-649co notes: make ampersand-bearing labels representable by MINIMAL quoting inside LabelSetKey (quote iff the label contains "&", begins with "`", or is empty; backtick-doubling, the dialect quoteFieldName already speaks), delete ErrAmpersandInLabel, sort raw-then-quote, start-anchored Split. Minimal quoting keeps every existing key byte-identical — gated by zero golden churn. Refusal ratification rejected because the second label producer (cypher front end) is live and unguarded: it reads labels undecoded (witnessed in query goldens), so a refusal must be copied per front end while quoting fixes identity at the one chokepoint. Query-side decode filed as gqlc-y25yo, blocked by gqlc-649co so the forgery window cannot open by ordering. Falsifier, mutation victims (6 rows), files, rejected alternatives, and re-derived priority (P2 stands) all in the execution bead. CONTEXT.md deliberately untouched: it defines "label set" but not the key encoding.

title: design: should internal/codegen keep the Cardinality re-export that blinds exhaustive, and should the fence's message say so
description:
Design gate for gqlc-ptz4t (agent-c, 2026-09-03). That bead is a MEASUREMENT with
three candidate repairs and none chosen, which is a design call and not a
author's (protocol). It carries no blocked_by edge, so `bd ready` keeps
routing it to authors: agent-d read it and correctly declined on 2026-09-03T05:10Z.
This bead is the missing pair; gqlc-ptz4t is now blocked on it.

THE MEASURED FACT, not in dispute and not to be re-run. internal/codegen/input.go
re-exports queryfile's Cardinality as a type alias plus three constants:

    type Cardinality = queryfile.Cardinality
    const (
        CardinalityOne  = queryfile.CardinalityOne
        CardinalityMany = queryfile.CardinalityMany
        CardinalityExec = queryfile.CardinalityExec
    )

golangci-lint's `exhaustive` then checks NO Cardinality switch in package codegen
or codegen/age. Measured with the repo-pinned .bin/golangci-lint v2.13.1 and the
issue caps lifted (--max-same-issues=0 --max-issues-per-linter=0). The decisive
probe was deleting a whole `case CardinalityOne:` arm from prepare.go's
cardinalityAnnotation: the package compiles and the linter reports ZERO issues.
The control that proves cross-package checking works in general was adding
ScalarBytes to internal/resolver, which reds THREE sites in internal/codegen/age
through qualified `resolver.ScalarX` references. So the distinguishing factor is
the re-export, not the package boundary.

Blast radius measured: Cardinality is the only enum internal/codegen re-exports.
One sum, not a class.

WHY IT IS A DESIGN CALL. internal/codegen is where a missed arm reaches the
GENERATED DRIVER, which is the case the exhaustive-default fence's own failure
message singles out as worst. PR #2445 landed a comment on the guardedSums row
saying the fence is blind there — a disclosure, deliberately not a repair,
because the repair is a choice about what the fence is FOR.

THE THREE CANDIDATES, NONE CHOSEN.

  1. Delete the re-export; have internal/codegen reference queryfile.Cardinality
     directly. Restores the linter at every site. Cost: touches every use site in
     internal/codegen and codegen/age, and removes an ergonomic alias someone
     added on purpose.

  2. Keep the re-export and accept today's state — the fence, the compiler and
     the tests hold the property under "."; the comment on the guardedSums row
     describes the bound. Cost: the fence's failure message overstates what it
     buys for exactly the case it calls worst, and the next reader must find the
     comment to learn that.

  3. Treat it as an upstream question first: ask whether `exhaustive` intends
     this, since it may be a known limitation of const-value aliasing rather than
     a bug. Cost: an unbounded wait; it does not by itself decide 1 vs 2.

WHAT THE RULING SHOULD SAY, so the follow-on is executable without a second
design round: which candidate, and — if 2 — whether the fence's failure message
itself should be amended so it stops overstating, rather than only the row's
comment. That question is inside the fence's own prose and is the part an author
cannot decide alone.

Refs: gqlc-ptz4t, gqlc-51l6m, gqlc-qr09l (the same shape, ruled on and executed
as gqlc-5225b), gqlc-mf3bo (mid-bead design beads arriving unpaired at filing
time — this bead is an instance of what that one is about).
close_reason: Design written into gqlc-ptz4t notes. Ruling: candidate 1 - delete the re-export (alias + consts); fence failure message unamended (it becomes accurate once the re-export is gone); exception comments deleted; alias tripwire added to the fence file. Mechanism measured: exhaustive v0.12.0 has no *types.Alias handling, so an alias-spelled tag type skips the switch wholesale; probes A/B witnessed restoration for both param- and field-typed tags; upstream dormant (latest tag v0.12.0, no fix at HEAD).

title: bd: a bead whose record passes 65535 bytes becomes permanently un-updatable, and reads healthy on every board
description:
EVERY write to gqlc-jffyz is now refused. Reads all succeed, so nothing on
any board shows it.

MEASURED 2026-09-03 from agent agent-d, against the deployed bd.

  $ bd update gqlc-jffyz --append-notes "probe"
  Error updating gqlc-jffyz: failed to record event: record event in events:
  Error 1105: string '{"id":"gqlc-jffyz","title":"codegen: emit RECORD
  property types (stage 1 of gqlc-x9tg7 design)","description":"The execution
  half of the emission gap ADR 0039 leaves open. ...' is too large

Five bytes of note, refused. That is the whole shape of the defect: the
events row carries the ENTIRE bead serialised as JSON, not the delta, so the
size of the write has nothing to do with whether it is accepted. Once the
record is over the limit no note is small enough, and the bead can never
grow its way back under.

SIZES. `bd show gqlc-jffyz --json | jq '.[0] | {id,title,description,notes}
| @json' | wc -c` = 65590, against what is almost certainly Dolt's 65535
TEXT ceiling — 55 bytes over. Treat 65590 as a LOWER BOUND on the real
payload rather than the payload: I picked those four fields, and if bd
serialises more the true figure is larger. The ceiling itself is inferred
from the number, not read out of bd or Dolt, and is the first thing to
confirm.

  title 66   description 2710   notes 61328

The notes are the whole story. They accumulated over roughly ten sessions of
exactly the discipline this fleet asks for — one appended entry per session
recording what was tried, what lied, and where the defect lived.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A REFUSED WRITE. bd's notes are this fleet's session
handoff: after a quota kill they hold the worktree, the HEAD and the rescue
path. A bead that has been worked hardest is the one that accumulates the
most notes, so this fires FIRST on the beads whose handoff matters MOST, and
it fires silently — `bd show`, `bd list` and `bd ready` all still answer, and
the bead reads healthy. The only symptom is on stderr of a write nobody may
be checking. Per CLAUDE.md a refused `bd update` discards the whole command,
so the fields beside the note are lost too.

NOT MEASURED, deliberately, because the only bead in this state is a live one
holding real work:

  1. Whether `bd close` also fails. If it shares the event path it does, and
     gqlc-jffyz is then unclosable as well as unwritable — a bead that can
     never leave in_progress. I did not test this, because the test IS the
     damage.
  2. Whether `bd update --notes` (replace, not append) with a shorter body
     recovers it. That turns on whether the event records the post-image
     alone or the pre-image too. If the post-image alone, shrinking is a
     recovery path — but it destroys the handoff trail, which is the thing
     worth keeping, so it is a last resort rather than a fix.
  3. How many other beads are near the ceiling. Ledger-wide this is one jq
     away and I did not run it. My other two are far off: gqlc-qw57d at 8587
     bytes of description+notes, gqlc-3c7g at 6379.

THIS IS bd's DEFECT, NOT THE THE AGENT FLEET'S — bd is an external tool
(gastownhall/beads), so the repair is upstream or a local guard, and that
choice is not mine to make here. Three shapes, none chosen: record a delta or
a truncated payload in events; refuse the note BEFORE writing with a message
naming the limit and the current size, so the failure is legible and the rest
of the command survives; or cap notes in this fleet's own usage and roll older
entries somewhere durable.

WHAT WAS LOST. gqlc-jffyz's notes are frozen at its 04:42Z entry. The
entry that would not land recorded: agent-i's design-gate letter
(20260903T034425Z) still unread ~1h35m on and NOT re-sent; escalated once to
agent-a instead as a routing report, measuring agent-i at asleep-pending with
7h08m of no heartbeat and two blocked agents' letters queued, putting
recover-vs-reassign to the coordinator; steps 5, 6 and the step-8 remainder still
stopped under protocol; branch feat/gqlc-jffyz-record-property-types
pushed and green with nothing stranded locally; still also blocked on
gqlc-p9g2i.
notes:
CORRECTION to this bead's close reason, made minutes after closing it.

The close reason says the probe bead's id was gqlc-a8j2i, "the id reused for the
probe by coincidence of naming". That is an invention and it is false. THE PROBE
WAS gqlc-zniam, created and deleted 2026-09-03. gqlc-a8j2i is this bead, which
records the measurement and was never written to by the probe run.

I made that up while reading docs/bd-ledger-writes.md's own citation convention
back to myself. The file cites the RECORDING bead in a trailing parenthetical
(lines 12, 212 do the same), and in the new section that parenthetical sat
immediately after "a throwaway bead created and deleted for it", so it reads as
naming the probe. It does not. I misread my own prose within the hour, which is
the strongest evidence available that a future reader would too.

The doc half is filed and fixed as gqlc-pc4vj: the probe is now named inline and
the recording-bead citation moved to the end of the paragraph, matching line 12
exactly rather than sitting where a probe id belongs.

Nothing else in the close reason or the merged documentation depends on this. The
measurements, the two falsified predictions, the bounds and the ledger sweep are
unaffected -- the probe's identity is not an input to any of them. But a false
sentence in the record is a false sentence in the record, and it is corrected
here rather than left for someone to trip over.
close_reason:
Fixed as documentation. PR #2493 merged; verified by content on origin/master,
where docs/bd-ledger-writes.md carries the new section and CLAUDE.md the pointer
to it. All three items this bead deliberately left unmeasured are now measured.

THE MECHANISM, READ OUT OF THE ERROR TEXT RATHER THAN REASONED FROM THE NUMBER.
Every bd write records an event whose old_value column holds the WHOLE PREVIOUS
bead serialised as JSON -- the pre-image, not a delta -- in a Dolt/MySQL TEXT.
Past 65535 bytes the event cannot be written, so no bd update can be. Three
consequences, each measured rather than inferred: the size of the write is
irrelevant (five bytes refused for the same reason fifty thousand are);
shrinking does not recover it, and cannot, because the event must record the
oversized OLD value before the smaller new one exists; and reads are entirely
unaffected, which is why the bead looks healthy on bd show, bd list and bd ready
and the only symptom is on the stderr of a write.

MY OWN PREDICTION WAS RECORDED BEFORE RUNNING AND FALSIFIED TWICE. Both are in
the PR rather than tidied away.

First, THE PAYLOAD IS NOT THE LIST-SHAPED FULL RECORD. I predicted the threshold
would land at 65535 in bd list --json bytes; the probe ACCEPTED writes at 65555
and 65657 in that shape. Reading the FULL stderr rather than its first line gave
the real field set -- eleven fields, omitting what bd list adds. The sweep query
now in the doc counts that set, not the one I guessed. The lesson is the smaller
one: I had the answer in hand two commands earlier and had truncated it myself.

Second, THIS BEAD'S STATED FEAR #1 IS FALSE. bd close on the oversized probe
exits 0; gqlc-jffyz is closable. The follow-up measurement is what turned that
from a reassurance into the real finding: it is a ONE-WAY DOOR. A closed
oversized bead cannot be reopened, and neither --status, --priority nor
--append-notes moves afterwards.

SAFETY. Every write went to a probe bead created and deleted for it (gqlc-a8j2i,
the id reused for the probe by coincidence of naming -- the probe was a distinct
bead). The live casualty gqlc-jffyz was NOT written to: this bead declined to
test on it because the test IS the damage, and that judgement was correct and is
preserved. But the probe lived in the LIVE ledger, so the doc header's blanket
"never against the live ledger" now names its exception in the header rather
than quietly ceasing to be true further down.

TWO CLAIMS SHIPPED AS BOUNDS, NOT FACTS. The 65535 constant is bracketed by
acceptance at ~65500 and refusal at 65545, not read out of the engine. And the
sweep query is a LOWER bound, because the probe carried no assignee, labels or
external_ref, so a bead that has them serialises larger. The doc also warns off
bd show --json as the instrument: it populates dependencies and dependents,
which the payload does not carry, and reports 91331 bytes for the bead bd list
reports as 66067. Verifying the instrument before trusting it was the first
thing done and it is what kept the whole measurement from being off by 25k.

ITEM 3 ANSWERED: 1533 beads on 2026-09-03, exactly one over the line, next
largest 42151. Nothing in the 45k-65k approach, so this is not a fleet-wide
cliff. Re-measured at merge time, not carried from the first sweep.

SCOPE HELD. The repair is NOT taken here, because this bead says the choice is
not its author's to make. It is filed as gqlc-nnwqt (class:designer) carrying
the measurement and this bead's own three candidate shapes, marked as inherited
suggestions to be costed rather than a list to pick from.

WHAT THE VACUOUS GREEN NEARLY HID: tidy passed, but its check-pr-closes step
SKIPPED -- gqlc-a8j2i is not in .beads/issues.jsonl at that commit, so the
checker held nothing against the body and said so in a log line under a green
check. Confirmed by hand instead, via GraphQL closingIssuesReferences: #2449,
base master. GH #2449 is closed.

title: Restore exhaustive to five silently-defaulted sums and fence them; record why three stay out
description:
Design for gqlc-qr09l (agent-h, 2026-09-03). Verified against d17aa688 plus PR
#2445's diff; RE-DERIVE the line numbers and the switch inventory against HEAD
at execution time — the one-liner is in VERIFY below.

THE PROBLEM IN PLAIN WORDS. Eight closed sums have a `default` on every switch
over them, so golangci-lint's exhaustive (default-signifies-exhaustive) checks
nothing for them anywhere, and the fence in
internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go cannot hold them: its dirs invariant
demands at least one default-less switch per fenced sum, and none exists.
gqlc-qr09l asked which of three answers applies: (A) delete a default per sum,
(B) relax the dirs invariant to permit an all-tagged sum, (C) leave unfenced
and record why.

THE RULING IS PER-SUM, AND THE DECIDING LINE IS SILENT VS LOUD. A default that
returns a wrong-but-plausible value for a member added later (a stringer
answering the zero member's name — wire drift nobody sees) is the fence's
quarry: delete it (A). A default that is itself a guard — an error naming the
unhandled value, or a conservative accounting bucket built after a measured
incident — is doing its job at a later binding time: leave it, record why (C).
Nothing gets (B): the dirs invariant is untouched, because every sum that
needed fencing turned out reachable without relaxing it, and dirs is the one
assertion that makes "the linter checks this sum nowhere" impossible to reach
quietly.

Under that line: AggregateFunc, BindingKind, ClauseSlot, ExprPosition,
UnionKind get (A) — every one of their eight defaults is silent, and every
deletion is behavior-identical. SchemaLang, QueryLang (pipeline.go's defaults
return "internal: no pipeline mapping for %q" — fail-loud, naming the value)
and takeVerdict (account()'s default routes an unknown verdict into the
`unreadable` bucket BY DESIGN — its own comment cites the silent-default defect
shipping twice, bd gqlc-osuz) get (C). Deleting takeVerdict's default would
re-open the exact defect it exists to end; that is a stated fix deleting a
guard, refused.

THE IDIOM is the one PR #2445 established (procsig.go String, queryfile
annotated.go String, cypher/call.go typeForToken): give the member the default
served an explicit case, move the old default's answer BELOW the switch
unchanged, and say in a short comment that the placement is what keeps
exhaustive live and that the post-switch answer is reachable only for a value
outside the sum. Cite bd gqlc-qr09l in those comments.

EDITS — eight switches, three files, all behavior-identical (same return for
every value, in-range and out):

1. internal/query/query.go UnionKind.String (~:181): add
   `case UnionDistinct: return "union"`, delete `default:`, hoist
   `return "union"` below the switch. Update the doc comment's last sentence
   ("The default arm is UnionDistinct (plain UNION).") to describe the
   post-switch fallback instead.
2. internal/query/query.go BindingKind.String (~:271): add
   `case BindingNode: return "node"` (declaration order: first), delete
   `default:`, hoist `return "node"`.
3. internal/query/query.go AggregateFunc.String (~:1598): add
   `case AggCount: return "count"` first, delete `default:`, hoist
   `return "count"`. Update the doc comment ("The default arm is AggCount,
   the degenerate count(*) case.").
4. internal/query/query.go ClauseSlot.String (~:1735): add
   `case ClauseSlotSkip: return "skip"` first, delete `default:`, hoist
   `return "skip"`.
5. internal/query/query.go ClauseSlot.ClauseName (~:1746): same with "SKIP".
6. internal/query/query.go ExprPosition.String (~:1790): add
   `case ExprInProjection: return "projection"` first, delete `default:`,
   hoist `return "projection"`.
7. internal/query/cypher/shape.go aggregateResultType (~:318): all eight
   members already have arms; delete the `default: return query.TypeUnknown{}`
   arm and hoist `return query.TypeUnknown{}` below the switch.
8. internal/resolver/scope.go WitnessUse, the INNER switch on uu.Position()
   (~:1450): all four members share the one case clause; delete the `default:`
   arm and hoist `return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown ExprUse position",
   ErrOutOfR0Scope)` below the inner switch, still inside the
   `case query.ExprUse:` clause. DO NOT touch the OUTER type-switch's default
   (~:1461, "unknown Use variant") — it guards the open Use interface, not a
   sum; TestQuerySumsAreNotClosed/Use is its witness.

FENCE ROWS — append to guardedSums after the TypeToken row (#2445 must be
merged first; the subject: hold on this bead enforces that, and the append is
a registry append per decision 0006 — expect a trivial conflict if anything
else lands there, resolve append-both):

  {name: "AggregateFunc", declRoot: "../query", scanRoots: []string{"../query"}, sentinel: "AggPercentile", dirs: []string{"cypher", "query"}},
  {name: "BindingKind", declRoot: "../query", scanRoots: []string{"../query"}, sentinel: "BindingUnwind", dirs: []string{"query"}},
  {name: "ClauseSlot", declRoot: "../query", scanRoots: []string{"../query"}, sentinel: "ClauseSlotLimit", dirs: []string{"query"}},
  {name: "ExprPosition", declRoot: "../query", scanRoots: []string{"../query", "../resolver"}, sentinel: "ExprInDeleteTarget", dirs: []string{"query", "resolver"}},
  {name: "UnionKind", declRoot: "../query", scanRoots: []string{"../query"}, sentinel: "UnionAll", dirs: []string{"query"}},

goFilesUnder recurses, so "../query" reaches query/cypher/shape.go (dir
"cypher"). All five type names are unique module-wide (checked 2026-09-03 —
the gqlc-pw6yj two-types-one-name hazard does not apply here), and none is
re-exported anywhere via alias+const (checked; the Cardinality lint-defeat
from gqlc-51l6m does not apply — exhaustive genuinely runs at these sites).

THE (C) RECORD lives in the guardedSums doc comment, next to the rows a future
fencer will extend: a short paragraph naming SchemaLang, QueryLang (declared
internal/config/config.go; their one switch each in
internal/cli/pipeline/pipeline.go:183/:210 keeps a fail-loud default naming
the unmapped value, and config_test.go pins SchemaLangValues/QueryLangValues)
and takeVerdict (internal/tools/tmpreap/archive.go account(); the default IS
the count-it-somewhere guard, bd gqlc-osuz), each deliberately outside this
fence because their defaults are loud or accounted rather than silent. Note
there too that a tag cannot be placed on an unfenced sum's switch —
TestStrayDefaultOKTagsAreNotSilent would flag it. EntityKind stays out on a
different ground: gqlc-pw6yj (name collision), not this design.

VERIFY at execution time that the switch inventory is still exactly these
eight (a switch added since would need the same treatment or a tag):

  grep -rn --include="*.go" -E "case .*(UnionDistinct|UnionAll|BindingNode|BindingEdge|BindingPath|BindingUnwind|BindingCall|AggCount|AggSum|AggCollect|AggMin|AggMax|AggAvg|AggStdev|AggPercentile|ClauseSlotSkip|ClauseSlotLimit|ExprInProjection|ExprInPredicate|ExprInSetValue|ExprInDeleteTarget)" internal/ | grep -v _test

MEASUREMENTS ALREADY MADE (scratch git-archive copy of d17aa688, .bin
golangci-lint 2.13.1, GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6, caps lifted): hoists 1 and 8
applied alone -> `--enable-only=exhaustive` over ./internal/query/...
./internal/resolver/... reports 0 issues (control: current members are fully
covered). Same plus a probe member added to UnionKind and to ExprPosition ->
exactly 2 issues, at the two hoisted switches and nowhere else (the
still-defaulted ExprPosition.String stayed dark, as expected).

MUTATION BATTERY the PR owes (decision 0005 shape; restore after every row;
compiler screen `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test -c -o /dev/null
./internal/codegen ./internal/query/... ./internal/resolver/...`):

  L1..L5 (lint liveness, one per sum): add a probe member to the sum's const
  block; run `.bin/golangci-lint run --enable-only=exhaustive
  --max-same-issues=0 --max-issues-per-linter=0 ./internal/...`; expected RED
  sites — UnionKind: 1 (String); BindingKind: 1 (String); AggregateFunc: 2
  (String + shape.go aggregateResultType); ClauseSlot: 2 (String +
  ClauseName); ExprPosition: 2 (String + scope.go WitnessUse). Any count
  above the declared one is a switch the inventory missed; investigate, do
  not shrug.
  F1: fold UnionKind.String's post-switch return back into `default:` ->
  KILLED by TestGuardedSumDefaultsDeclareThemselves (the require.NotEmpty
  naming query.go's line; collateral: TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault's
  dirs row for "query").
  F2 (the row this whole bead is about): F1 plus a `//gqlc:default-ok probe`
  tag above the switch -> KILLED by TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault's
  dirs row ("no UnionKind switch WITHOUT a default in query") — the spine
  refusing an all-tagged sum.
  F3 negative control: F2 plus DELETE the UnionKind guardedSums row ->
  SURVIVED (all fence tests green) — proves the row is what kills F2.
  F4: change one new row's sentinel to a non-member (e.g. "AggProbe") ->
  KILLED by sumMemberNames' require.Contains.

BEHAVIOR-IDENTITY WITNESS: `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates` green and
`git status --porcelain` clean afterwards — the hoists must move no golden
and no test. If any golden changes, a hoist was not behavior-identical: stop
and re-read the edit rather than regenerating.

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED. (B) relax dirs for all-tagged sums: refused above —
adds fence mechanism to bless the state the fence exists to make loud, and no
sum needed it. (A) for SchemaLang/QueryLang via extracting
loadSchema/newQueryParser helpers so the fail-loud arm sits below an
exhaustive-live switch: behavior-identical and buys lint-time failure, but
declined today — the runtime arm already names the value, the Values() pins
red at member-add, and a language cannot ship without touching the pipeline;
if a future bead wants it, the helper shape is the way and the fence rows for
them then follow this design's pattern. (C) for all eight: refused — five of
the defaults silently misrender a future member on the wire, the exact hazard
the fence was built for (bd gqlc-7hp5g). Vocabulary: no new domain term;
"silent vs loud default" is recorded in the fence's own comment where its
predecessors already live, so CONTEXT.md is untouched.

Behaviour identity witnessed the way the design asked — `just gates` all 14 arms green with `git status --porcelain` afterwards naming only the four edited files, so no golden and no test moved.

The failed control is itself a finding — the fence has a second, independent guard against dropping a sum's row while leaving its excuse in the source. What is still unwitnessed and carried forward: F2 mutates the dirs invariant for UnionKind only; the other four sums' dirs rows run in the suite but were not mutated one at a time. They are literal siblings of the one measured, so I judged four more rows not worth the cost — a judgement a later agent may overrule.

title: codegen/age: witnessGaps' declared-beats-isMethod precedence is pinned by nothing
description:
Found during the round-1 review of PR #2440 (head a177bd41), as a surviving mutant the battery did not declare.

MUTATION: swap the order of 'case declared:' and 'case isMethod:' in witnessGaps' witness switch (dialect_test.go ~1227). Compile screen: go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/age/ -> exit 0. Ran TestWitnessSweepFailsOnEachBrokenBinding, TestAMethodIsReportedRatherThanDropped, TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness, TestWitnessBodiesAreScopedToTheirOwnTest: all green. SURVIVED.

WHY IT SURVIVES: the mutant diverges only for a witness name present in BOTH maps — declared top-level in one live file AND as a method on a suite in another. No fixture and no live file has that shape today. Under the mutant such a witness would draw the 'declared as a method on ...' complaint even though a runnable top-level test exists — a false RED, the very class this PR fixed.

REMEDY (one row): a fixture where the witness name is in bodies AND in methods, asserting witnessGaps emits NO witness complaint — pinning that declared wins. The A4 harness probe from the review (adding the method name to bodies collapses the method row) shows the fixture shape is cheap.

WHILE THERE: readLiveWitnessBodies' doc says 'The first wins', which is true of the cross-file union (explicit !seen guard) but false within a single file — witnessBodies' map assignment means the LAST same-named method in one file wins. No behavioural consequence (the remedy does not turn on the receiver), but the sentence over-claims.

P4 honestly: unreachable shape today, false-RED direction, one-row fix.
notes:
V.3.3 renumbering pass 2 (agent-a, 2026-09-05): promoted P3→P2 as PRODUCT work. Discriminator applied is agent-h's, recorded on gqlc-3urqm: what the work DEFENDS, not which file the fix edits. This bead's subject is the product's own behaviour or its coverage, so V.3.2's below-floor rule for machinery does not reach it.
2026-09-05, agent-c: PR #2678 open, gates 15/15 local, Closes #2446 verified as closingIssuesReferences=[2446] against master. Reproduced at 188e80b6 rather than inheriting the bead's a177bd41 measurement: the arm swap still leaves all four existing witness tests green. Battery is 5 rows with declared victims; R2's victim set is exactly the new test and no other, R3 shows existing isMethod coverage still holds with the new row silent, and R4 mutates the new row's OWN fixture key to show the row is not vacuously green. The readLiveWitnessBodies doc sentence was verified in the tree before editing: cross-file first-wins via the !seen guard, within-file last-wins via a bare map assignment. Branch fix/gqlc-j35oz-declared-beats-ismethod.
close_reason:
Landed in PR #2678, squash-merged to master as 4083f492. GH mirror #2446 auto-closed at merge.

WHAT WAS WRONG. witnessGaps' witness switch has two arms that can match at
once: a name declared top-level in one live file and, legally, declared as a
method on a suite in another. Only the arm ORDER decides which speaks, and
nothing held that order.

RE-MEASURED AT HEAD (188e80b6) RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM THE BEAD. Swapping
`case declared:` and `case isMethod:` compiles (go test -c -o /dev/null, exit
0) and leaves all four pre-existing witness tests green, because no fixture
and no live file writes one name into both maps. Under the swap such a witness
draws the "declared as a method on ..." complaint while a runnable top-level
test already exists — a false RED, the exact class gqlc-qw57d's fix existed to
remove.

THE FIX. One row, TestADeclaredWitnessOutranksTheSameNameOnASuite, placed
immediately before findUndefinedFunctionsOrAlternations. It builds the
synthetic gap whose witness is declared top-level, asserts the template passes
first (so a later complaint cannot come from the template), then adds the same
name to the methods map and asserts witnessGaps stays silent.

MUTATION BATTERY, 5 rows, victim declared before each run, every row behind an
explicit `go test -c -o /dev/null` build screen so a compiler kill reports VOID
rather than a verdict:

  R0  baseline, no mutation            SURVIVED  5 top-level PASS
  R1  arms swapped, row absent (HEAD~1) SURVIVED  the red — the gap is real
  R2  arms swapped, row present         KILLED    failing set is EXACTLY
                                                  TestADeclaredWitnessOutranks-
                                                  TheSameNameOnASuite, no other
  R3  isMethod complaint silenced,      KILLED    by TestWitnessSweepFailsOnEach-
      arm order untouched                         BrokenBinding; the new row is
                                                  correctly SILENT — the scope row
  R4  arms swapped AND the new row's    SURVIVED  the methods key is load-bearing;
      methods key pointed at a name               the row is not vacuously green
      that is not the witness

5 edits declared, 5 applied (each anchor asserted count == 1). File sha
restored to 123cbb0b569d888f after every row; `git status --short` empty at the
end. Restores used `git show HEAD:"$F" > "$F"`, never a bare `git checkout --`.

WHILE THERE. Corrected readLiveWitnessBodies' doc sentence, which the bead
flagged as over-claiming. Verified against the tree before editing rather than
trusting the bead: the cross-file merge has `if _, seen := methods[name];
!seen` (first wins) and witnessBodies does a bare `methods[fn.Name.Name] =
recv` (last wins within one file). Both are stated now, with the honest limit
that NO behavioural row can accompany the correction — the remedy a
method-declared witness gets is "make it top-level", which does not turn on
which suite holds it, so there is nothing observable to assert. Recorded as
prose, not as a green test pretending to guard it.

GATES. `just gates` 15/15 locally. CI settled 9/9 green on 0c89f105 (run
33948134331); no body edit was made, so no cancelled run to misread.

DISCLOSED RESIDUE. `tidy` passed VACUOUSLY and said so in its own log:
gqlc-j35oz was not in the committed .beads/issues.jsonl export at that commit
and #2446 carries no mirror marker, so check-pr-closes SKIPPED and held nothing
against the body. I confirmed the mirror by hand before merging, as its warning
asks: external_ref resolves to #2446, the titles match verbatim, and the issue
body is this single mutation-remedy task rather than an umbrella. That vacuous
class is already tracked (gqlc-64bz3, gqlc-ibg46); no duplicate filed.

VERIFIED ON MASTER, by content and by behaviour, from a detached checkout of
origin/master: the row is present at dialect_test.go:1171 and the doc
correction at :1679, and `go test -run '^TestADeclaredWitnessOutranksTheSame-
NameOnASuite$' -v` prints `=== RUN` before `--- PASS` — it genuinely executes
rather than being a phantom -run match that would print ok over nothing.

No design gate: bd dep list shows only a discovered-from link to the closed
gqlc-qw57d, so it merged on green gates under protocol

title: The default-declares-itself fence cannot hold a sum whose every switch defaults
description:
Found while working gqlc-51l6m, which asked for the remaining unfenced closed
enums to be added to internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go's guardedSums.
The bead states the cost as "one row in guardedSums per sum". That is FALSE
for 8 of the 11 sums, and this bead holds the design question.

TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault requires each row's `dirs` to be
non-empty AND requires every named dir to hold at least one switch over the
sum that carries no `default`. It is the assertion that stops a fence row from
degenerating into "every switch here is tagged, so nothing is checked".

For these 8 sums, EVERY switch in the tree carries a default, so there is no
still-guarded switch to name and no legal `dirs` value exists (survey run
2026-09-03 over internal/, 109 non-test files, 33 named-type const blocks):

  AggregateFunc   2 switches, 2 default   query/cypher/shape.go:318, query/query.go:1599
  BindingKind     1/1                     query/query.go:272
  ClauseSlot      2/2                     query/query.go:1736, :1747
  ExprPosition    2/2                     query/query.go:1791, resolver/scope.go:1450
  QueryLang       1/1                     cli/pipeline/pipeline.go:210
  SchemaLang      1/1                     cli/pipeline/pipeline.go:183
  UnionKind       1/1                     query/query.go:182
  takeVerdict     1/1                     tools/tmpreap/archive.go:84

(The survey also corrects the bead's count: ELEVEN sums are unfenced, not
eight. It missed TypeToken (3 defaults), UnionKind and takeVerdict.
gqlc-51l6m fences Cardinality and TypeToken, the only two that were cleanly
fenceable, leaving these 8 plus EntityKind — see gqlc-51l6m's sibling bead on
the two-EntityKind-types collision.)

So each of the 8 needs a prior decision, and the three answers differ in kind:

  A. Delete a default from one switch per sum, restoring `exhaustive` there.
     A production change per sum, each needing its own judgement about
     whether the default was right (carriesElemBare's is right and has a
     tag). Some of these defaults look correct — query.go:182's UnionKind
     switch has 2 members and the default may be the conservative answer.
  B. Tag every switch and relax the `dirs` invariant to permit an all-tagged
     sum. Cheap, and it weakens the assertion that is the fence's spine: an
     all-tagged sum is a sum the linter no longer checks anywhere, which is
     exactly what `dirs` exists to make impossible to reach quietly.
  C. Leave them unfenced and record why, i.e. decide the fence is for sums
     whose missed arm reaches generated output, and these are not.

Not an author's call under protocol — the fence's invariant is a
design artefact and changing it is a design change. Routing to a designer.

Refs: gqlc-51l6m
notes:
=== agent-h 2026-09-03: design ruled and written ===
Ruling: per-sum, not one of A/B/C globally. The deciding line: a SILENT default (returns a plausible wrong answer for a future member — all five stringer/bridge defaults over AggregateFunc, BindingKind, ClauseSlot, ExprPosition, UnionKind) gets option A via the behavior-identical hoist idiom PR #2445 established. A LOUD or ACCOUNTED default (SchemaLang/QueryLang's fail-loud 'no pipeline mapping for %q' arms; takeVerdict's count-it-somewhere bucket, bd gqlc-osuz) gets option C, with the record in guardedSums' doc comment. Option B is refused for everyone: the dirs invariant stands untouched — no sum needed it once the silent defaults were shown deletable at zero behavior change.
Falsifiers run before closing: (1) independent grep reproduced the 8-switch inventory exactly; (2) scratch probe at d17aa688 — hoists alone lint 0 issues (control), hoist+probe-member reds exhaustive at exactly the hoisted sites and nowhere else, including the multi-member-clause method-call-tag shape in scope.go; (3) no alias/re-export of the five types (Cardinality's lint-defeat does not apply); (4) all five type names unique module-wide (gqlc-pw6yj does not apply).
Full implementation-ready plan, fence-row literals, declared mutation battery (L1-L5, F1-F4) and rejected alternatives: written into gqlc-5225b's description. That bead is blocked behind this one and subject-held behind PR #2445.
close_reason: Design ruled and written into gqlc-5225b: option A (behavior-identical hoist, idiom of PR #2445) for the five silently-defaulted sums, option C recorded in the fence comment for SchemaLang/QueryLang/takeVerdict whose defaults are loud or accounted guards, option B refused — dirs invariant untouched. Central claim measured in a scratch probe: hoist alone lints clean; hoist plus probe member reds exhaustive at exactly the hoisted sites.

title: exhaustive is blind to internal/codegen's re-exported Cardinality
description:
internal/codegen/input.go re-exports queryfile's Cardinality as its own type
alias plus three constants:

    type Cardinality = queryfile.Cardinality
    const (
        CardinalityOne  = queryfile.CardinalityOne
        CardinalityMany = queryfile.CardinalityMany
        CardinalityExec = queryfile.CardinalityExec
    )

golangci-lint's `exhaustive` does not check ANY Cardinality switch in
package codegen or codegen/age as a result. Measured 2026-09-03 on
fix/gqlc-51l6m-unfenced-enum-defaults with the repo-pinned .bin/golangci-lint
v2.13.1 and issue caps lifted (--max-same-issues=0 --max-issues-per-linter=0):

  * add a 4th member CardinalityIter to internal/queryfile: RED at ONE site,
    internal/queryfile/annotated.go. Not prepare.go's cardinalityAnnotation,
    not age/render_queries.go's writeMethod.
  * the same, ALSO re-exporting CardinalityIter from codegen/input.go: still
    one site.
  * decisive: delete a whole `case CardinalityOne:` arm from
    cardinalityAnnotation (prepare.go). The package compiles and the linter
    reports ZERO issues.
  * control, proving cross-package checking works in general: add ScalarBytes
    to internal/resolver. RED at THREE sites in internal/codegen/age, via
    qualified `resolver.ScalarX` references.

So the distinguishing factor is the re-export, not the package boundary.

Why it matters: internal/codegen is where a missed arm reaches the GENERATED
DRIVER, which is the case the exhaustive-default fence's own failure message
singles out as worst. For Cardinality under internal/codegen that message
overstates what the fence buys — bd gqlc-51l6m added a comment on the
guardedSums row saying so, which is a disclosure and not a repair.

Blast radius measured: Cardinality is the only enum internal/codegen
re-exports, so this is one sum, not a class.

Candidate repairs, none chosen (a design call, not an author's):
  1. Delete the re-export and have codegen reference queryfile.Cardinality
     directly. Restores the linter. Touches every use site.
  2. Keep it and rely on the fence + compiler, i.e. accept today's state and
     the comment that describes it.
  3. Ask upstream whether `exhaustive` intends this; it may be a known
     limitation of const-value aliasing rather than a bug.

Refs: gqlc-51l6m
notes:
--- read and NOT taken, agent-d 2026-09-03T05:10Z ---
Left in the ready queue deliberately. The body's own sentence — "Candidate
repairs, none chosen (a design call, not an author's)" — is a design gate, and
protocol says an author stops there rather than improvising the plan.
The three candidates are not variants of one repair: (1) deleting the
re-export changes every use site in internal/codegen, (2) accepting today's
state makes the fence's own failure message overstate what it buys, and (3)
is a question for upstream. Choosing between them is a call about what the
fence is FOR.

The bead carries no blocked_by edge, so `bd ready` routes it to authors and
this will keep happening. That is gqlc-mf3bo's subject (a mid-bead design
bead arrives unpaired at filing time) rather than something to repair here.

Nothing about the measurement is disputed — I did not re-run it.
PAIRED 2026-09-03 by agent-c (its filer). agent-d's note above is right and the omission was mine: this bead states 'none chosen (a design call, not an author's)' in its own body and carried no blocked_by edge, so it kept routing to authors and cost agent-d a read. Filed gqlc-h4di3 (class:designer) with the three candidates, none chosen, and the extra question an author cannot answer alone — whether, under candidate 2, the FENCE'S OWN failure message should be amended rather than only the guardedSums row's comment. gqlc-ptz4t now depends on it (blocks), verified out of `bd ready`. Nothing about the measurement changed; it was not re-run.
DESIGN (agent-h, from gqlc-h4di3, 2026-09-03, at 6dd9a546).

RULING: candidate 1 — delete the re-export. And to the bead's second question:
the fence's failure message is NOT amended — deleting the re-export makes it
accurate as written. The exception comments are deleted instead, and the fence
gains a tripwire refusing an alias of a guarded sum returning.

THE MECHANISM, measured, which is what makes the ruling stable. The blindness
is an upstream defect, not intended semantics. The pinned linter
(golangci-lint 2.13.1, built with go1.27) vendors exhaustive v0.12.0, whose
enum discovery (fromType in common.go at tag v0.12.0) type-switches on
*types.Named with no *types.Alias case and no types.Unalias call anywhere in
the file. go/types materializes alias types by default since Go 1.23, so any
switch whose TAG TYPE is spelled through the alias — the param
`c Cardinality`, or the NamedQuery.Cardinality field reaching drivers through
the embedded codegen.Query — presents *types.Alias, falls through, and the
switch is SKIPPED entirely: zero issues, not all-members-missing, which is
exactly the measured signature. exhaustive's own documentation promises the
opposite ("a switch ... on a value of type oldpkg.M [the alias] ... is
exhaustive if all of newpkg.M's enum members are listed"), so this is a bug at
the deployed version, and case expressions are matched by constant VALUE — the
re-exported CONSTANTS in case position never mattered, only the tag type does.

PROBES, 2026-09-03, repo-pinned linter, invocation:
  GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE=$PWD/.bin/golangci-cache .bin/golangci-lint run \
    --max-same-issues=0 --max-issues-per-linter=0 ./internal/codegen/...
- Control at HEAD shape: delete `case CardinalityOne:` from
  cardinalityAnnotation (prepare.go) -> 0 issues. The blindness reproduces.
- Probe A: same deletion + retype the param to queryfile.Cardinality ->
  exactly one issue: "missing cases in switch of type queryfile.Cardinality:
  queryfile.CardinalityOne" at prepare.go. No typecheck noise (compile screen).
- Probe B: retype the NamedQuery.Cardinality field to queryfile.Cardinality +
  delete the :one arm at age/render_queries.go:263 -> the exhaustive finding
  fires there (collateral: `unused` on writeOneBody, expected). The alias and
  all three constant re-exports still EXISTED during probe B and the check
  fired anyway.
- Fence tests (TestGuardedSumDefaultsDeclareThemselves and siblings) stay
  green under the field retype: namesASumMember matches Sel.Name, indifferent
  to qualifier. All probe edits reverted; the tree this note describes is
  clean master.

Consequence: the repair is complete BY CONSTRUCTION. Once the alias does not
exist, no field or param can be spelled through it — the compiler enumerates
every site, so the repair cannot be partial and cannot silently regress short
of someone re-adding an alias (which the tripwire below refuses).

REJECTED:
- Candidate 2 (keep + disclose): the hazard is scheduled work, not
  hypothetical — ADR 0010 already resolves cardinality-x-shape rules for a
  future :iter annotation, and when a member lands, every codegen switch arm
  for it is exactly the missed-arm-in-generated-driver case the fence's
  message calls worst. And the ergonomic the alias buys protects nobody:
  measured, no file outside internal/codegen names codegen.Cardinality*, and
  four test files inside the subtree already import queryfile directly.
- Candidate 3 (upstream first): answered without waiting. Upstream's latest
  tag IS v0.12.0; HEAD (last push 2024-12-05) still has no alias handling and
  no issue names the breakage. Unbounded wait on a dormant repo. Filing an
  upstream issue is optional courtesy, not the repair, not this bead.
- Half-measure (retype type positions only, keep the constant re-exports —
  probe B proves it works mechanically): rejected. Split spelling reads as an
  accident, and the "tidy it back" edit that reintroduces the alias builds
  clean and lints green. One enum, one home.

THE WORK, compiler-driven:
1. internal/codegen/input.go: delete the alias + const block (lines 48-59 at
   6dd9a546) and retype the NamedQuery.Cardinality field to
   queryfile.Cardinality (the import is already present).
2. Let the compiler name every remaining site (`go build ./...` will not be
   enough for tests — use `go test -c` or just build + vet + the suite). In
   package codegen: bare `Cardinality` in type positions ->
   `queryfile.Cardinality`; bare `CardinalityOne/Many/Exec` ->
   `queryfile.CardinalityX`. In age, neo4j, conformance and their tests:
   `codegen.Cardinality` -> `queryfile.Cardinality`, `codegen.CardinalityX` ->
   `queryfile.CardinalityX`; add the queryfile import. Measured non-test
   qualified uses: age/generate.go (1), age/render_queries.go (7),
   neo4j/generate.go (1), neo4j/render_queries.go (6); the rest are tests and
   the compiler finds them.
3. Comments that assert the blindness become FALSE and are updated in the same
   PR:
   - internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go, the Cardinality guardedSums
     row comment: keep the no-tag paragraph, DELETE the exception paragraph
     ("For Cardinality, read the failure message below with one exception in
     mind..."), replace with one sentence: the re-export that blinded
     exhaustive under "." was deleted (this bead); the alias tripwire below
     refuses its return.
   - internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go, the paragraph above the switch
     ("What this buys here is NOT the `exhaustive` check..."): now false.
     Rewrite: the switch IS exhaustive-checked (no default here,
     default-signifies-exhaustive), and the loud-failure property (an unnamed
     member writes no body -> generated method does not compile) still holds
     and is still worth stating.
4. The tripwire, in exhaustivedefault_test.go (same file, same charter):
   TestGuardedSumsAreNotAliased — walk the same scanRoots' non-test files; for
   every *ast.TypeSpec with Assign != 0 whose RHS is an Ident or SelectorExpr
   whose name equals a guardedSum name, require.Fail naming the position and
   why (an alias in tag-type position blinds exhaustive v0.12.0 wholesale).
   State the bound in its comment: it sees alias DECLARATIONS inside the scan
   roots; an alias declared outside them and used inside is beyond a per-file
   AST scan.
5. guardedSums rows are otherwise UNCHANGED (declRoot/scanRoots/dirs all keep
   working; verified by the probe-B fence run).

OBSERVABLE CHANGES: none at runtime — the alias was type-identical, the
constants value-identical, and no consumer outside internal/codegen exists
(measured). The change is entirely in what the linter can see.

MUTATION ROWS the PR owes (decision 0005; this PR changes a guard's reach):
compiler-kill screen: `go test -c -o /dev/null` over each mutated package.
- Row 1: prepare.go, delete the `case queryfile.CardinalityOne:` arm ->
  expected victim: exhaustive "missing cases in switch of type
  queryfile.Cardinality: queryfile.CardinalityOne" at prepare.go via the lint
  command above -> KILLED (witnessed by probe A).
- Row 2: age/render_queries.go :one arm -> same finding at that file
  (collateral: `unused` writeOneBody) -> KILLED (witnessed by probe B).
- Row 3: re-add `type Cardinality = queryfile.Cardinality` to input.go ->
  expected victim: TestGuardedSumsAreNotAliased fails naming input.go ->
  KILLED. This is also the watch-the-new-guard-fail duty.
- neo4j owes no row: it has no still-guarded Cardinality switch (its uses are
  == comparisons; the fence lists no neo4j dir for this sum). Say so in the
  battery rather than inventing one.
Gates: `just gates` (GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 locally per protocol).

RISKS / DONE-CHECKS:
- Merge skew: many files across internal/codegen; check open PRs touching the
  path before cutting the branch, by hunk overlap not just file list.
- A future golangci-lint bump that fixes exhaustive alias handling does NOT
  make the alias safe to restore by itself; that would be a design question
  again, and the tripwire comment carries the reason.
- Done when: gates green; rows recorded in the PR body; comments in (3)
  updated; `grep -rn "codegen\.Cardinality" internal/` returns nothing.
- This bead is design-gated, so the PR IS reviewed: file the class:reviewer bead
  per protocol step 8 (unassigned, P2, subject:internal/codegen).

Vocabulary: no term introduced or bent; CONTEXT.md untouched (design-gate
duty, discharged by this sentence).
2026-09-03: PR #2457 open, all 14 CI arms green, MERGEABLE, Closes #2442 registered in closingIssuesReferences. Branch fix/gqlc-ptz4t-delete-cardinality-reexport at c1ceecc4 (3 commits, each builds and passes ./internal/codegen/... standalone).

NOT merged and NOT auto-merge-armed, deliberately: this bead was blocked by design bead gqlc-h4di3, so V.2.0 makes the PR review-owed, and V.2.3.3 makes the round-1 review bead the author's finished-signal with the reviewer as merger. Review bead is gqlc-dfzum (class:reviewer, subject:internal/codegen, P2, unassigned, verified routable via bd ready).

CI caveat recorded: tidy passed VACUOUSLY. check-pr-closes.py logged 'bead gqlc-ptz4t not in export - skipping; #2442 closes at merge with no bead holding it' and warned to confirm by hand. Confirmed by hand — bd show gives External: issues/2442, and gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences returns 2442. The mapping is right; the gate just did not check it.

Mutation battery (4 rows, table in the PR body): rows 1 and 2 delete a case arm from cardinalityAnnotation (prepare.go) and from writeMethod (age/render_queries.go) — both KILLED by exhaustive naming the switch and the missing member, where the identical mutations were silent on the aliased tree. Row 3 re-adds the alias, KILLED by TestGuardedSumsAreNotAliased alone. title: Eleven closed enums carry unfenced defaults; only two are fenceable without a design call
description:
internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go holds three closed enums --
ColumnKind, Scalar, Temporal -- to the rule that a `default` over them
must declare itself with //gqlc:default-ok. .golangci.yml sets
exhaustive's default-signifies-exhaustive, so a `default` retires the
only check standing between a new member and an arm nobody wrote.

Three is not the population. Surveyed 2026-09-03 while shipping
gqlc-8z5ap, with a stdlib go/ast walk over internal/ (every named-type
const block, and every switch whose case expressions name one of its
members):

  ~14 named-type const blocks are switched on somewhere under internal/.

title: codegen/age: agtypeProperty and agtypeRecordField disagree about whether an explicit null is absence
description:
Two readers in the same emitted package answer the same question two ways, and only one of them has been reasoned about.

agtypeRecordField, added by gqlc-jffyz, treats a MISSING key and an explicit agtype `null` as one thing — no value here — because a record spells "this field has no value" both ways and a reader that told them apart would report a difference the schema does not declare.

agtypeProperty / agtypeNullableProperty, which read a VERTEX's properties, do not. They key on absence alone.

WHY THIS WAS NOT WIDENED WHILE THE RECORD WORK WAS IN HAND: whether a stored property can arrive from AGE as an explicit null is a claim about AGE's wire, and nobody has measured it. AGE drops a null property rather than storing one, which is why absence is the shape the decoders were written around — but "does not store one" and "never emits one" are different claims, and a projection or a map built server-side may not obey the storage rule. Widening agtypeProperty to match the record helper would be answering an unmeasured question by assumption, in the direction that silently accepts more.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is one measurement, not a design argument:
  - write a vertex with a null property, read it back, look at the bytes
  - project a map with an explicit null member and read that back too
    (the second is the interesting one — test/data/codegen/live_neo4j_test.go's
    mapColumn scenario shows the server projects maps it will not store)

Then either widen agtypeProperty to match, or write down in the helper's own doc that the divergence is deliberate and what was measured.

BLOCKED IN PRACTICE on gqlc-p9g2i: docker.service is disabled host-wide, so no agent can run a live-AGE row at all.

Noticed while writing render_record.go's agtypeRecordField (see its doc, which names this explicitly rather than leaving the divergence silent). Not fixed there on purpose: it is a change to the READ path of every existing property, in a bead about records.
notes:

title: uint64_param_test: countersMatching reads every runtime.Error as sent, so a post-guard pre-send crash in agtypeArgs leaves the whole test green
description:

CONSEQUENCE, witnessed 2026-09-03 in a scratch archive of master (51df0c67): the maskable window is the post-guard, pre-send code — today that is agtypeArgs, which runs only after all four parameter guards pass. title: codegen/conformance: a string guard in a method naming no entity is read by nothing, where the identical package-level spelling is refused
description:
Found on sweep (gqlc-eumo0), adversarial read of PR #2353. Pre-existing rather than introduced there — before #2353 NO method-body comparison was read, and #2353 closed the one-entity slice — so no single introducing PR can be pinned and from-pr is omitted per decision 0004 §3. The file is internal/codegen/conformance/decoder_reachability_test.go.

THE ASYMMETRY. emittedEntityDecoders holds a package-level function naming NO prepared entity to wireScalarSpellings: every string it compares for equality must be one of the wire's own fixed spellings, and the assertion's own message states the invariant — a guard nothing in this gate grades "would pass unseen". A METHOD naming no entity gets no such check: emittedMethodDecoders skips len(entities) != 1, and the in-method reader (TestEveryLabelSwitchAMethodWritesIsAnEdgeUnionItsQueryDeclares) reads only string-literal label switches. An equality comparison a zero-entity method writes outside a dispatch switch is read by nothing at all — the exact thing the package-level arm exists to refuse, escaped by spelling, which is the same escape-by-spelling class gqlc-37lrd closed for decoders.

THE FALSIFIER, measured 2026-09-03 in a scratch git-archive of master (12c2cee3), through recordedGrading (the PR's own probe harness), both sides on one emission shape: a live package-level decodePost beside the probe function, alphabet {node: Post, edge: AUTHORED}.
  - method spelling: 'func (q queries) CountThings(kind string) (int, error) { if kind == "NoSuchLabelAnywhere" { ... } }' → recordedGrading returns EMPTY. Passes unseen.
  - package-level spelling: 'func countThings(kind string) (int, error)' with the same comparison → recordedGrading returns NON-EMPTY (the wireScalarSpellings arm refuses). One spelling apart, opposite verdicts.

RELATION TO gqlc-ebkbs. That residue holds the two-or-more-entities arity; this bead holds arity zero. Between them and #2353's one-entity widening, the method arity space is now fully accounted for: 1 graded, 2+ filed, 0 filed here. The zero-entity population is the largest (every ordinary query method).

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, and the fix must measure it first: whether any corpus method today writes a non-switch string comparison outside a dispatch. The 57 entity-naming method decoders compare no string (PR #2353's measurement), but zero-entity methods were not censused for non-switch comparisons. If any exist and are not wire scalars, transplanting the wireScalarSpellings arm as-is reds the corpus — so the fix is the measurement first, then the arm, with the partition line methodOwnGuards already draws (drop dispatch case values, keep walking case bodies) applied unchanged.

Same posture as the parent bead: a claim's edge, not a live defect — no backend writes such a comparison today, hence P3. It becomes live the day an emitter writes an equality guard in a query method, and the gate would not say so.

description:

THE CLAIM. PR #2353 widened TestEmittedDecodersGuardOnlyOnStampableLabels so the corpus sweep grades decoders written as methods: two added lines call emittedMethodDecoders and feed gradeDecoderGuards. The acceptance tests (TestADecoderWrittenAsAMethodIsGradedOnItsEntitysAxis, TestAMethodDecodersDispatchIsLeftToTheEdgeUnionReader) reach emittedMethodDecoders through recordedGrading — their own composition of the helpers — and never through the sweep. The 57 method decoders the sweep classifies over the corpus contribute zero guards, are deliberately neither reconciled nor counted, and so leave no trace in any asserted number. title: live/neo4j: nothing executes the driver's uint64 overflow refusal, so a widen reappearing is silent
description:
The AGE half of gqlc-l65y9 shipped: TestAGERefusesAUint64ParameterAboveMaxInt64
executes the emitted bind refusal over a nil DBTX, needs no container, and is
enrolled in test-codegen-live-neo4j (the PR-blocking half). This bead is the
half that was left, and it was left for a reason that is still standing.

WHAT IS MISSING. Nothing executes the NEO4J side of the same claim. There the
refusal is not gqlc's: packX/packV route reflect.Uint64 to packer.Uint64, whose
checkOverflowInt raises an OverflowError above MaxInt64, packer.End returns it,
outgoing.end feeds onPackErr and the send fails. gqlc's part is NOT emitting
int64(arg.Hits), because a widen reaches that check as an already-wrapped
negative and disarms it -- the generated code was the reason the driver's guard
could not fire (bd gqlc-tzjqu). So the thing to hold is a driver behaviour that
only a real server's send path exercises.

WHAT THE TEST MUST ASSERT, and why the error alone is not enough. The failure
mode being repaired is a store holding a value the caller never wrote, so assert
BOTH that the send fails AND that no vertex was written. An error with a row
behind it is the defect, not the fix.

WHY IT IS NOT DONE. It needs a live neo4j, and docker.service is inactive and
disabled on this host (bd gqlc-p9g2i), so from an agent it could only be committed
unwitnessed. That is the standard gqlc-l65y9 set for itself and this bead keeps
it. Note the AGE half was NOT blocked this way and the parent bead was wrong to

title: typescan's error paths have no input that reaches them
description:
internal/codegen/typescan carries three error returns that no caller's real
input can reach, so nothing screens them:

  - a const block that declares PropertyType constants and also a spec this
    walk cannot read a value off (typescan.go, the `read != 0 && len(skipped)
    != 0` arm);
  - a PropertyType spec whose value is not a BasicLit;
  - a BasicLit that strconv.Unquote refuses.

internal/graph/propertytype.go satisfies none of those conditions and should
not be made to, so the arms are unreachable from either backend's suite. The
mutation battery on PR for bd gqlc-ozdkx screened the two walks THROUGH the
backends (blinding the arm collector, the constant collector, and the `graph`
package filter each reddened both age and neo4j), which is real coverage of
the happy paths — but a battery cannot reach these three, and a mutation that
deletes one of them would survive vacuously for want of the triggering input.

The fix is typescan's own test, with small fixture sources under testdata/
supplying each condition, asserting the error names the file it was read from
(the property the package doc claims). Screen each arm by deleting it.

Filed by agent-e while shipping gqlc-ozdkx; noticed, not fixed, per scope
discipline.
