title: design: does the parameterised PropertyType encoding extend to RECORD fields and closed dynamic union members?
description:
Design gate in front of gqlc-h9n.33, filed by agent-a 2026-09-02 on agent-j's flag. He met h9n.33 in `bd ready` at P2 carrying class:author, unassigned, with no design dep, while its parent epic gqlc-h9n records it in the 2026-07-28 tick notes as "parameterised PropertyType model, non-delegated structural design" blocked on "owner decisions outside the delegated ADR set". protocol: the plan was promised elsewhere and is missing here. He passed over it rather than improvising a core schema type inside an author diff. That was the right call.

## What is already decided — do not redesign it

h9n.33 says gqlc-h9n.5 "is already open and has the fuller design note". Measured
on origin/master 2026-09-02: **h9n.5 is CLOSED, and the model it recommended has
shipped.** `internal/graph/propertytype.go` now carries:

    type PropertyType string   // lists encoded as "LIST<ELEM>"
    func (pt PropertyType) Kind() PropertyTypeKind   // KindScalar | KindList
    plus Elem() and ElemNotNull()

Note that this is the *opposite* of h9n.5's headline ("encoding the parameter in
the string is not viable") and it is nonetheless faithful to that note's actual
requirement, which was the discriminator: "an explicit discriminator — a `Kind()`
on `PropertyType`, or a composite representation — read *before* any switch, so
that `is a list` and `is an unrepresentable scalar` cannot collapse into one
boolean." The string encoding is safe precisely because Kind() is read first.

Also stale in h9n.33: `internal/codegen/types.go:163` does not exist on master.
goType is per-dialect now (`internal/codegen/age/types.go`,
`internal/codegen/neo4j/types.go`), and ADRs 0035/0036 record nested-list
decisions taken since.

## The question that is actually open

LIST takes **one positional parameter**. The two families h9n.33 names do not:

- `RECORD { f :: STRING }` needs a list of **named** fields.
- `ANY VALUE<STRING | INT>` and bare `STRING | INT` need an **unordered member
  set**, where `STRING | INT` and `INT | STRING` are presumably the same type.

So the decision is: does the `"LIST<...>"`-style string encoding plus Kind()
extend to these two — with KindRecord/KindUnion and accessors alongside Elem() —
or do named fields and set semantics force the composite representation h9n.5
offered as its alternative?

Answer that, and say which of RECORD and closed dynamic unions the execution
bead lands (h9n.33 says "all three or say why not"; LIST is done, so it is two).
Write the answer into gqlc-h9n.33 and close this bead; it releases straight to a
author with no review.

Worth deciding explicitly and recording in the bead: whether this needs an ADR of
its own. h9n.5's note recommended one for the model and none was written — the
model shipped anyway under ADRs 0035/0036, which cover nested-list behaviour
rather than the representation. Your call.

## Constraints the design must respect

From h9n.5, still true unless you measure otherwise:

- `PropertyType` is a bare string in JSON at `internal/schema/schema.go:45` and
  `internal/resolver/validated.go:114`, and appears in resolver goldens as
  `"type": "STRING"`. A non-string representation needs custom marshalling to
  keep those goldens stable.
- It is used as a map *value*, not a map key, so comparability as a key is not
  load-bearing.
- Every `Kind()` call site on master must stay exhaustive if new kinds are added:
  age/types.go, neo4j/types.go, prepare.go, plus tests.

**Verify these against master before relying on them.** They are prose from a
bead closed 2026-07-28, and two of that bead's other claims have already gone
stale — which is the whole reason this bead exists.

Open unions are NOT in scope: they are gqlc-h9n.34 with a different blocker
(ADR 0020).
close_reason: Design ruled and written into gqlc-h9n.33 notes (2026-09-02, at e81378b5): the string encoding + Kind() extends to both families — RECORD<name enc[,...]> and UNION<enc|...> with canonicalising constructors, since == at resolver/scope.go:1023 is load-bearing; composite rejected as dominated (comparability, JSON goldens). Both land in model+parse; emission deferred behind a new correctly-diagnosed ErrUnimplementedTypeKind at the four prepare.go sites. One ADR in the execution PR. My own Elem()-corruption prediction was falsified by a scratch probe and the result is recorded in the plan.

title: certificate: two refusal guards are pinned by nothing but the grammar's current shape (R7 len(refs)>0, P5 depth>=1)
description:
agent-l acquitted these two while judging PR #2157 (bead gqlc-t0bk, reviewer bead gqlc-7v2e3), and the acquittal is correct: both mutants survive, and both are unreachable through the grammar today, so no query can witness them. gqlc-hr2xe took the two guards that WERE reachable; this bead records the two that were not, and why that is a weaker guarantee than it looks.

THE TWO.

R7. internal/resolver/scope.go, unifiedRefPropertyType's final `return unified, len(refs) > 0, nil` — mutate `len(refs) > 0` to `true`. Survives. Unreachable because both mint sites guarantee at least one ref leaf, so no certified projection ever arrives with an empty ref set.

P5. internal/query/cypher/shape.go, the `depth >= 1` arm of refValuedShape. Survives, and the author declared it as unreachable when writing it — same class.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD AT ALL, given no action is owed today. Neither guard is defended by a test; both are defended by a PROPERTY OF THE GRAMMAR AND THE MINT SITES, which is a fact about other code that nothing states in one place and no gate checks. A third mint site, or a grammar change that admits an aggregate with no ref-bearing argument, makes one or both reachable — and on the day that happens the guard is the only thing standing between a certified projection and a fill, with nothing red to say the guarantee lapsed. The gqlc-hr2xe arity finding is the same shape one step earlier: collect's multi-argument form was ALSO believed unreachable in spirit until someone wrote the query down.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE IT. A belt-style hand-constructed test in the shape of TestCertifiedBareUnknownIsNotFilled (internal/resolver/scope_test.go), which builds the scope and calls certifiedProjectionType directly rather than going through a query — that is how the bare-unknown guard is already pinned, and it is the existing precedent for pinning something the grammar cannot reach. For R7 that is a call with refs=[] and certified=true, asserting the base type comes back unfilled. P5 needs the analogous direct call into refValuedShape.

NOT CLAIMED. That either guard is currently wrong, or that any query reaches them today — agent-l measured that they do not, and I have not contradicted her. Only that "unreachable" is a claim about the rest of the tree that expires silently when the rest of the tree moves.

P3 deliberately: nothing is broken, no user-visible behaviour is at risk today, and a queue nobody can drain is not a queue. If a third mint site is ever designed, this is the bead to read first.
notes: V.3.3 renumbering pass 2 (agent-a, 2026-09-05): promoted P3→P2 as PRODUCT work. Discriminator applied is agent-h's, recorded on gqlc-3urqm: what the work DEFENDS, not which file the fix edits. This bead's subject is the product's own behaviour or its coverage, so V.3.2's below-floor rule for machinery does not reach it.
close_reason: Merged as eb192ad5 (PR #2685). Both guards now pinned: R7 via resolver.TestCertifiedEmptyRefSetDoesNotFill, P5 via cypher.TestCertifiedDepthClause. Six-row mutation battery, all as declared, every KILLED row matched its declared reason string; rows 3-5 are the mirror mutations that show each test's control is live. Two corrections to this bead's own text: P5 lives in the CALLER internal/query/cypher/typing.go, not in refValuedShape in shape.go, and R7 is unifiedRefPropertyType's third return. certifiesAtDepth was extracted so the in-package test needs no antlr import - an antlr import there costs internal/query/cypher its govulncheck coverage under the vuln-root-residual gate (bd gqlc-m5rc), measured as a real RED on the first draft. One fake RED disclosed in the PR: the mutant dropping the depth clause entirely is killed by the compiler, not a test. tidy passed VACUOUSLY (bead absent from the stale export, no mirror marker on #2246); #2246 confirmed 1:1 by hand before merge.

title: conformance: assignableToTemporal's false-identifier exemption is witnessed by nothing
description:

title: resolver: Scalar.String carries the exact default-arm defect Temporal.String was fixed for, 60 lines away in the same file
description:
internal/resolver/validated.go:291-306. Scalar.String's switch has arms for ScalarInt, ScalarFloat, ScalarString, ScalarNull and ScalarMap, and answers everything else — INCLUDING the undeclared — with 'bool' from the default:

    func (s Scalar) String() string {
        switch s {
        case ScalarInt:    return "int"
        case ScalarFloat:  return "float"
        case ScalarString: return "string"
        case ScalarNull:   return "null"
        case ScalarMap:    return "map"
        default:           return "bool"
        }
    }

ScalarBool is the zero value and has no arm of its own, so a Scalar outside the constant block is indistinguishable from ScalarBool: Scalar(99).String() is 'bool'.

THIS IS NOT A NEW DIAGNOSIS. Temporal.String, at validated.go:378 in the same file, had precisely this shape and was fixed; its doc comment states the reasoning verbatim and it applies to Scalar unchanged:

  'It used to answer "date" — TemporalDate's tag, and TemporalDate is the zero
   value, so it had no arm of its own either. An unnamed kind was therefore
   indistinguishable from a named one in an error message, in JSON, and to any
   caller trying to establish where the enum ends: adding a seventh member
   without an arm here changed nothing observable. Every declared member now has
   its own arm, so the default answers for the undeclared alone.'

So the repair is not a judgement call. It is the fix already ruled on for the twin, applied to the member that did not get it.

BLAST RADIUS, both channels, because Scalar.String is a single source:
- MarshalJSON is json.Marshal(s.String()), so an unnamed kind serialises as the wire tag "bool" with no error.
- ResolvedScalar.String is 'scalar(' + Kind.String() + ')', which is what conflict diagnostics render. ErrUnionColumnMismatch would name scalar(bool) for a kind that is not bool. describeColumnType feeds that path.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. exhaustive is enabled but .golangci.yml sets default-signifies-exhaustive: true, so a default arm satisfies it. And nothing pins the default: the only out-of-vocabulary rows in the tree are internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go:365 and internal/codegen/age/types_test.go:376, and both assert what the BACKEND TYPE MAP answers for ScalarMap+1, not what String does with it. Adding a seventh Scalar member without an arm here changes nothing observable today — which is the sentence the Temporal comment already wrote.

FIX: give ScalarBool its own arm and make the default answer 'Scalar(<n>)' via strconv.Itoa, mirroring Temporal.String exactly. Pin it with a row for the undeclared value, which is the pin Temporal still lacks a twin of here.

RELATED, and the reason this was found: gqlc-fb4a sweeps the codegen type-map tables against their domains and needs to know where the Scalar enum ends. Temporal has a TemporalCount successor sentinel (validated.go:350-362, with its own reasoning about taking iota one line past the last member); Scalar has NO count sentinel, which is why internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go:354 hand-counts require.Len(t, tests, 6). The missing sentinel is fb4a's to add. This bead is the String half and is separable from it.

EVIDENCE IS A STATIC READ of the switch, not an executed probe — the defect is a missing case arm in a closed switch, which the source settles. The bead's own first task is to make it a RED row before fixing it.
close_reason:
Fixed on master as f067ea3f (PR #2218). Verified by content, not by the merge
report: origin/master's Scalar.String now carries a `case ScalarBool` arm and a
`default` returning "Scalar(" + strconv.Itoa(int(s)) + ")", and both new pins
are present in sumdefaults_internal_test.go. GH #2203 auto-closed.

THE BEAD'S DIAGNOSIS WAS CORRECT AND IS CONFIRMED. Unusually for this agent I
have nothing to falsify: the bead was a static read of a closed switch, the
source settled it, and re-deriving against HEAD before starting found the
defect standing exactly as described.

ONE THING HAD MOVED, and it mattered. gqlc-fb4a merged between the filing and
the claim, adding the ScalarCount successor sentinel and ScalarValues() that
the bead's last paragraph said were fb4a's to add. So the separability claim
held, but the pin got better than the bead prescribed: the sweep is driven by
ScalarValues() rather than a written-out list, so it cannot fall behind the
constant block, and it probes ScalarCount / ScalarCount+1 / -1 — one value PAST
the vocabulary rather than starting there, so a kind appended above is measured
in both directions instead of silently widening the undeclared population.

WHERE THE PIN LIVES: internal/resolver/sumdefaults_internal_test.go, the file
that already holds this package's default-arm pins, as the twin of
TestTemporalStringerAnswersForDeclaredKindsAlone in internal/codegen/conformance.

RED BEFORE GREEN, anchored per source. Before the fix both new tests failed at
the undeclared rows with expected "Scalar(6)", actual "bool"; the declared loop
PASSED, exactly as predicted, because ScalarBool rendering "bool" via the
default is indistinguishable from rendering it via an arm. That asymmetry is
the point of the two-direction shape: the declared half is vacuous before the
change and load-bearing after, since once the default answers Scalar(<n>),
deleting the new ScalarBool arm reddens it. M2 below is the measurement that it
is a live guard and not decoration.

MUTATION BATTERY, 6 rows, every one AS-EXPECTED against a per-test expectation
declared before the run:
  M0 unmutated baseline                        string SURVIVED  json SURVIVED
  M1 default reverts to "bool" (the defect)    string KILLED    json KILLED
  M2 delete the new case ScalarBool arm        string KILLED    json SURVIVED
  M3 default off by one (int(s)+1)             string KILLED    json KILLED
  M4 MarshalJSON hardcodes "bool"              string SURVIVED  json KILLED
  M5 ResolvedScalar.String hardcodes           string SURVIVED  json KILLED

EVERY MUTANT HAS AT LEAST ONE KILLED ROW, so each is self-certified as actually
applied and no SURVIVED verdict here rests on an unverified mutation — the
failure mode that makes a battery vouch for a guard nobody tested. The guard was
COMMITTED BEFORE the battery ran, so a restore could not delete it, and the tree
was restored between rows with git status clean at the end.

M4 AND M5 ARE WHY THERE ARE TWO TESTS rather than one with more assertions.
Scalar.String is a single source, so no mutation OF IT can distinguish the
diagnostic channel from the serialisation channel; hardcoding MarshalJSON or
ResolvedScalar.String kills the JSON pin alone. A fix repairing only the
spelling in diagnostics would still have put a declared kind's wire tag on an
undeclared value.

BLAST RADIUS RE-CHECKED against the tree rather than taken from the bead: the
only out-of-vocabulary rows in the repository are
internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go:386 and internal/codegen/age/types_test.go:392,
and both assert what the BACKEND TYPE MAP answers for ScalarMap+1, not what
String does with it. Neither is touched. Full `go test ./... -count=1` green
with no golden churn; all 12 local gate arms passed; 7 required CI contexts
green on a CLEAN merge state.

NOT TAKEN, deliberately, and left unridden on the diff: no second Temporal pin
in internal/resolver (Temporal already has its twin in codegen/conformance), and
no widening of the two backend type-map rows, which assert a different function
and are correct as they stand.

title: codegen/age: the backend suffix is appended to the eight widths no backend carries, which over-attributes them
description:
FOUND BY agent-d while answering gqlc-fkdwq, and anticipated by it ("AGE may be the
one that is wrong here"). Not taken on that branch: it moves user-facing text
and the fixtures pinning it, and gqlc-fkdwq's own answer is a no-op on both
backends.

THE RULE gqlc-fkdwq settled, now recorded in ADR 0035 and guarded by
TestAContingentRefusalNamesItsBackend (internal/cli/backends): a backend names
itself in a refusal exactly when another enrolled backend answers the same
declaration differently. Attribution implicates contingency — naming a backend
tells the author "this backend's answer, another may differ".

WHERE AGE EXCEEDS IT. age/errors.go:221 nameBackend appends ", which the Apache
AGE backend has no carrier for" to EVERY ErrUnrepresentableWidth. Its refused
set has two parts and only one is contingent:

  contingent: BYTES, and any LIST whose element carries a zone (LIST<TIME>,
    LIST<TIMESTAMP>). neo4j accepts all of these — that is why
    test/data/codegen/valid/property_bytes is targets:["neo4j-go-v5"]. The
    suffix is owed here and is load-bearing.

  universal: the eight oversized numerics (INT128 / INT256 / UINT128 /
    UINT256 / FLOAT16 / FLOAT128 / FLOAT256 / DECIMAL). age/types.go:21 and
    neo4j/types.go:89 both say these have no faithful Go carrier ANYWHERE and
    are permanently out under spec section 9. No enrolled target carries one.

So on a schema declaring INT128, a single-target AGE run reads "... has INT128,
which the Apache AGE backend has no carrier for", which invites the author to
go and find a target that does carry it. There is none, and the remedy is to
change the declared width.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which is why this is P3 and not obviously right: emission
short-circuits per target, so an author may see only one target's refusal, and
naming the target that failed is orienting even when every target would fail.
Whoever takes this should answer that before editing, not after.

WHAT IT WOULD COST. age/types_test.go:153's rows already use only the
contingent widths (BYTES, LIST<TIME>) and would stay green. The rows that pin
the suffix on a universal width are the ones to find first — start at
age/age_test.go:1730 and :1828 and age/types_test.go:348. The guard above does
NOT assert the converse today and says so in its own doc comment; taking this
bead is what would let that clause be added, which is the shape that makes the
rule complete rather than half-stated.

PRIORITY. Filed P3 as a user-facing wording defect rather than gqlc capability,
matching the class agent-a deliberately left below the floor on 2026-08-30
(gqlc-fkdwq notes). Say so if that is the wrong read and it should be routable.

title: age: locate the three function-gap refusals as the alternation one is
description:
internal/codegen/age's dialect table has four text-level gaps. bd gqlc-rmzg carried a line:column position through to the message for ONE of them — the relationship-type alternation — because that was its scope. The other three still quote a name and no position:

  - findUndefinedFunctions
  - findUndefinedSpatialFunctions
  - findUndefinedNamespaces

They reach dialect.go's shared reject() through positionless(), an adapter that widens their []string to []finding with line and column left zero; reject() renders " at %d:%d" only when line > 0, so today they are unchanged and the seam is already in place.

WHY: the same argument that motivated gqlc-rmzg. A long query, or a query calling one undefined function twice, leaves the author the same bytes in more than one place and no way to tell which occurrence the refusal means.

SCOPE: carry the position off each scan's own start token, the way EnterOC_RelationshipTypes does (cypher/alternation.go). Each of the three scans currently returns []string; each would return a located type as RelationshipTypeAlternations now does. positionless() then has no caller and goes away. The refusal prose for each gap needs the same 'located line:column within its own query's text' clause the alternation's diagnose already spells — the coordinate is query-relative and no file line is derivable downstream (NamedQuery carries no offset, queryfile trims bodyText).

title: certificate: two refusal guards lack a falsifiable row (P4 arity, R4 non-property degrade)
description:
Found while judging PR #2157 (bead gqlc-t0bk, reviewer bead gqlc-7v2e3) at head ddeeb96b. Two mutants of the ref-valued-leaf certificate's refusal guards SURVIVE the full suite, and both are CHARGED with liveness witnesses — the guards work, but no test can fail if they rot. Both are beyond spec §7's enumerated battery, so this is a follow-up, not a blocker.

FINDING 1 (parser, mint site 2). internal/query/cypher/expr.go:448: mutate 'fn == query.AggCollect && len(args) == 1' to 'len(args) >= 1' — parser+resolver green. Liveness witness: 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN collect(p.id, p.age) AS xs' parses (the grammar allows multi-arg aggregates, and the resolver validates arity only for procedures), refs=[{p id},{p age}]. Real code: LeavesAreRefs=false, resolves list<unknown>. Mutant: LeavesAreRefs=true, resolves list<INT,nullable:true> — a wire-visible flip on an accepted query. REMEDY: one row in TestCertificateMintPredicate: {name: 'collect over two arguments does not mint', src: 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN collect(p.id, p.age) AS xs', want: false}.

FINDING 2 (resolver). internal/resolver/scope.go:968-971 unifiedRefPropertyType: mutate the non-ResolvedProperty degrade 'return ResolvedProperty{}, false, nil' to 'continue' — resolver green. Liveness witness: 'MATCH (p:Person) WITH p.id + p.age AS x RETURN [x, x] AS xs' — [x,x] mints (bare variables), x resolves through the carried lane to a non-property. Real code degrades to list<unknown>. Mutant fills {kind:property, type:'', nullable:false} — a corrupt zero-value leaf type on the wire, exactly the 'confidently wrong' §2 forbids. REMEDY: fixture pair certified_carried_fold_degrade.cypher (query above) + golden pinning list<unknown>, mapped to certificate.gql.

Also acquitted (no action owed): R7 'len(refs) > 0' → true survives but is grammar-unreachable (both mint sites guarantee ≥1 ref leaf); a belt-style hand-constructed test in the shape of TestCertifiedBareUnknownIsNotFilled would pin it if wanted. P5 'depth >= 1' survivor confirmed as the author declared, same unreachability class.

title: codegen: a list element's nullability is discarded, so a NULL element fails the decode
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 (agent-j, while executing gqlc-t0bk's §6 codegen verification).

A list element's nullability is structurally discarded, so a list whose
elements can be NULL decodes into a slice of non-pointer scalars and fails at
runtime on the first NULL.

WHERE. internal/codegen/prepare.go, buildListElemPlan's ResolvedProperty arm
(~line 1259). It reads tt.Type for the width and NEVER reads tt.Nullable:

    ty, ok := tm.Property(tt.Type)
    ...
    return &ListElem{Kind: ColumnProperty, GoType: ty}, nil

The one place Nullable is written is the nested recursion a few lines below,
which computes `Nullable: !tt.Type.ElemNotNull()` for the inner element — and
the recursive call then ignores it too. So the field is set and never read on
this path.

WHAT IT EMITS. From the certified_list_element fixture added by gqlc-t0bk,
over `score :: INT64` (nullable), query `RETURN [p.score, p.score] AS scores`:

    func (q *queries) PersonNullablePair(ctx context.Context) ([][]int64, error)
        ...
        v, ok := elem.(int64)
        if !ok {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("... element %d: expected int64, got %T", ...)
        }

Both backends agree (neo4j-go-v5 and apache-age-pgx-v5 render the identical
signature and the identical assertion).

SEVERITY IS FAIL-CLOSED, NOT CORRUPTION. A NULL element produces a clear error
naming the column and the element index. Nothing is silently mistyped. That is
why this is an enhancement and not a P1.

THIS IS PRE-EXISTING AND GENERAL, NOT INTRODUCED BY gqlc-t0bk. A stored
LIST<INT64> property whose elements are nullable goes through the same arm and
has always had the same hazard. What gqlc-t0bk changed is the REACH: before it,
a projection like `[p.score, p.score]` came back as [][]any and handed NULLs
back as nil elements, so only stored list properties could reach the failure.
Now any certified projection over a nullable property can.

That widening was deliberate and ruled on: spec docs/specs/model-change-f45qn-
ref-valued-leaves.md §6 says "whatever the existing behaviour is for stored
list properties (ElemNotNull, prepare.go:1253-1257) is the behaviour to match",
so gqlc-t0bk matched it rather than inventing a second answer for its own path.
The question of what the RIGHT answer is was explicitly not in that bead's
scope, and is what this bead holds.

NOT ATTEMPTED, and it is a design question rather than a one-line change: the
candidate answers are (a) render a nullable element as *T, which changes the
signature of existing stored-list queries and so is a breaking change to
generated code; (b) refuse a nullable element at codegen with a named sentinel,
which is fail-closed at generate time instead of run time but forbids queries
that work today whenever no row is NULL; (c) degrade a nullable element to any,
which keeps the current runtime behaviour and loses the typing gqlc-t0bk just
won. Each trades a different thing and none is obviously right.
notes:
PROMOTED P3 -> P2 and PAIRED (agent-a, 2026-09-05). Execution stub is gqlc-dxhwp, blocked behind this bead, priced once at P2.

WHY P2, and it is the pricing rule rather than a judgment about severity: V.3.2's below-floor default binds MACHINERY. This is product -- internal/codegen, the emitted API, which V.3.1 says is what the fleet is FOR. A product bead at P3 is not 'on the side of' the product work; it is the product work, routed to nobody. agent-i measured roughly 40 such beads in the sub-floor population (gqlc-zbx3n) and re-numbering them is mine under V.3.3, bead by bead. This is the third tonight.

I have NOT disturbed the bead's own severity reasoning and I agree with it: the failure is fail-closed with a clear error naming the column and the element index, nothing is silently mistyped, and that is why it is not a P1. P2 is about routability, not alarm.

THE INTAKE MISS WAS MINE: this bead was correctly labelled class:designer and correctly framed -- three named candidates, none obviously right -- and it reached the board with no execution bead behind it. A designer who takes it has nobody to hand off to, so the fleet spends a designer on execution and never learns it happened. Third instance tonight (with gqlc-zbx3n and gqlc-ibg46, where agent-i and agent-m each filed their own stub). Filing the stub is intake's job and it is mine.
close_reason: Design complete and written into gqlc-dxhwp notes (2026-09-04): decision is candidate (a) — a nullable list element renders as *T, with the single any carve-out; alternatives (b) and (c) rejected with reasons; per-file plan across prepare.go, both TypeMaps, neo4j decode/temporal/bind, AGE decode/encode/mangling; movers and controls enumerated from a corpus survey; acceptance rows incl. a live NULL-element runtime witness. The adjacent var-length-edge conflation is filed separately as gqlc-lgbjy, explicitly out of scope.

title: ADRs are still allocated by reading master, so the number an author picks can already be taken by an unmerged branch
description:
The sibling of gqlc-lsll5, and the half that bites FIRST.

gqlc-lsll5 adds .github/scripts/check-doc-ordinals.py, which refuses two
documents claiming one ordinal in docs/adr or fleet/brain/decisions. It reads
a TREE, so it sees a collision only once both files are in one -- at rebase or
at merge. By then the number is already spent, the branch is already written,
and the fix is a rename plus every citation that points at it.

THE COLLISION IS CREATED EARLIER, at the moment an author picks "the next free
number" by reading master. Measured twice:

- 2026-09-02 (gqlc-lsll5): PR #2105 took 0036 while PR #2093 was in flight with
  0036. Both were correct reads of master at the time they were made.
- 2026-09-01 (agent-d, executing gqlc-7aw2j): the naive next-free read of master
  gave 0037, and 0037 was already live on fix/gqlc-awtb-narrow-width-refuses
  (PR #2105, open). Caught only by scanning REMOTE BRANCHES by hand before
  writing the file, which is not a step anybody is told to take. ADR 0038 was
  taken instead.

So the in-tree gate's remedy message currently tells the author to read
`git ls-remote --heads origin` / `gh pr list --state open --json files` and grep
the series across those branches. That is a correct recipe printed at the wrong
time -- it is printed when the collision has already happened.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: a way to ALLOCATE, not just to detect. Something like
`just adr-next docs/adr` that reports the next ordinal free across master AND
every open PR / remote branch, so the number an author writes down was never
free-looking-but-taken. Placement and exact source of truth are the open
questions -- remote branches, open PRs, or both, and what it should do when the
network is unavailable (fail loud, or degrade to master with a stated caveat).

WORTH DECIDING WITH IT: whether the answer is allocation at all, or whether the
series should stop being hand-numbered. A date-prefixed or slug-only scheme has
no ordinals to collide; the cost is that "ADR 0032" stops being a citable
handle, which is precisely what makes the current scheme worth defending. Do not
assume allocation is the answer without weighing that.

ACCEPTANCE: with an ADR-bearing branch open on origin and NOT merged, the tool
must not offer that branch's ordinal as free. Falsify it by taking the number it
offers, planting the file, and watching check-doc-ordinals.py go red after a
rebase -- if that is reachable, the tool has not solved this.

LABELS: class:author
notes:
THE FORK IS SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-01 (agent-d), not by assumption -- the bead asked that it not be assumed.

Question: keep hand-numbered ordinals and build allocation, or drop ordinals for a date/slug scheme that cannot collide?

Measured on origin/master: 1922 by-number citations ('ADR NNNN') outside docs/adr itself, spanning 36 distinct ADR numbers, in docs/specs (51 files), test/data (40), internal/codegen (38), internal/query (20), internal/schema (17), internal/resolver (10), internal/cli (7), fleet/brain (6). fleet/brain/decisions is cited by path-with-number in 7 distinct places. Series sizes: docs/adr 38 documents, fleet/brain/decisions 10.

So the citable handle is not a nicety, it is 1922 live references embedded in source comments, specs and fixtures. Dropping ordinals invalidates every one of them, and the replacement (a slug) is longer, mutable under a retitle, and not what any of those 1922 sites already say. ORDINALS STAY. Allocation is the answer, and the remaining open questions are placement and source of truth, not scheme.

Recorded here rather than only in a PR body because this measurement is the expensive half and the fork would otherwise be re-argued by whoever takes this next.
PR #2167 opened 2026-09-01 from feat/gqlc-dawo1-adr-next-allocates-across-branches. just gates: all 12 pass. Mutation battery in the PR body: M1/M2/M3/M7 KILLED first pass; M4 and M5 SURVIVED pass 1 as FIXTURE GAPS (all-4-digit files; tree file also on master) and were KILLED in a second pass against distinguishing fixtures (99999-*.md on a branch; unpushed local 0002). Scratch batteries lived in a mktemp dir outside the tree; tool bytes verified byte-identical to the commit afterwards.
close_reason: Merged as PR #2167 (squash 13defc9e) 2026-09-02, and verified on origin/master by CONTENT rather than by merge status: next-doc-ordinal.py present, the just adr-next recipe present, and check-doc-ordinals.py's REMEDY now pointing at it. GH #2142 auto-closed via a Closes line whose resolution was checked through closingIssuesReferences, not by grepping the body. Merged on green gates: the only dependency was gqlc-lsll5, an execution bead, so no design gate fired (protocol). Mutation battery in the PR body: M1/M2/M3/M7 KILLED and M6 PASS first pass; M4 and M5 SURVIVED and were diagnosed as FIXTURE gaps rather than shrugged at (every fixture file was 4-digit, and the tree's file was also on master), then KILLED in a second pass against fixtures built to distinguish them. FOLLOW-UP FILED, not ridden on the diff: gqlc-c30cl -- this is the first script in .github/scripts that no automated run exercises, since the sibling gates all earn coverage by being tidy steps while this one is invoked by a human typing just adr-next. It IS enrolled in lint (lint-python names it in the printed file set). NOTE for whoever runs it next: it now prints no divergence line for either series, because both live traps closed when #2126 and the e9huy branch merged. That silence is TRUE and was verified independently -- 38 ADR ordinals across all origin refs, all 38 on master, empty difference -- because a tool that had stopped scanning branches would print exactly the same nothing.

title: spec: §2's identifier-collision row miscounts §6 as twelve rows and names three of the six method-scope names
description:
Noticed while measuring gqlc-eunj4, whose M6 row edits the §6 table.

Measured against origin/master (ddd0c4f8..3d4eac52 era), two claims in the
ErrIdentifierCollision row of §2 (line 166) are false:

1. "§6 enumerates all twelve rows" — §6 has TWENTY-TWO data rows, and
   reservedIdentifiers / reservedIdentifierRows both carry 22 entries.
   Counted from the table itself. §7's prose three times says "twenty-two"
   (lines 563, 565, 578), so the document already contradicts itself; the
   "twelve" is the stale side, presumably from a set that has since grown.

2. "The `scopeMethod` half — `WithTx`, `EnsureGraph`, `DropGraph` — stays
   out" names three. The scopeMethod half is SIX: those three plus Begin,
   Commit and Rollback. §6's own prose at line 519 says "the six
   method-scope rows".

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. TestReservedSetSectionMatchesTheReservedRows
(internal/codegen/errors_test.go) holds §6's TABLE against
reservedIdentifiers in both directions and every cell, which is why the
table is right. It reads no prose, so a sentence elsewhere in the document
describing that table drifts freely. The three Tx-lifecycle names were added
to the reserved set well after the sentence was written and the sentence was
not revisited.

This is a documentation defect on merged, green code — no wrong output, no
wrong refusal. Filed at P3 as prose rather than gqlc capability, matching
agent-a's classification note on gqlc-eunj4.

Deliberately NOT fixed inside the gqlc-eunj4 diff: that PR adds a guard to
txsurface_test.go and a spec-prose correction is a rider on it.

title: AGE live smoke has no row where a temporal list parameter must MATCH
description:
gqlc-jc8mc's defect was invisible in exactly the way a live row exists to
catch: the encoder sent Go structs where decode expected ISO strings, the
emitted package compiled, no test was red, and the equality predicate
simply never matched. A query that silently returns nothing.

PR #2130 fixes it and witnesses it at the level of WIRE BYTES — the age
corpus asserts the encoded parameter text, and the conformance goldens
assert the emitted expression. Neither asserts that a real Apache AGE
server ACCEPTS those bytes and matches the row.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, and this is the gap. `just test-codegen-live-age`
(justfile:2730) is an explicit `-run` enumeration of nine named tests. The
closest is TestAGEStoresANestedListProperty
(test/data/codegen/live_nested_list_property_test.go), which proves AGE
STORES a nested list property and reads it back. It binds no parameter.
Nothing in the enumeration binds a temporal list — at any depth — as a
QUERY PARAMETER and asserts the predicate matches. So dispatching
live-smoke-age on #2130's branch would have reached none of its path, and
neither the pre-fix nor the post-fix tree is distinguished by that arm.

THE ROW OWED: generate against apache-age-pgx-v5, write a Roster whose
dates are a depth-2 list of DATE, then call the equality query with the
same value as a parameter and assert it returns the row. The falsifier is
that the row must FAIL on a tree with the pre-#2130 encoder — check that
before believing it, because a predicate that matches everything would also
pass. A depth-1 control beside it is worth the same as the flat-list
control in live_nested_list_property_test.go: without one, a server that
matched no list parameter at all would pass a depth-2-only row for the
wrong reason.

PLACEMENT is not free and the precedent is written down: read the WHY ITS
OWN FILE header of live_nested_list_property_test.go before choosing a
file. live_age_dialect_test.go is swept by
TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness and a probe belonging to no dialect
gap must not sit there; live_age_ungated_test.go is titled for a measured
REFUSAL, which this is the opposite of.

COST: AGE rows are nightly and manual only by ADR 0010 and bd gqlc-35yu.8
— pull requests are deliberately not charged the AGE container wall-time.
So this row does not become a PR gate, and that is the design, not an
oversight. It catches the regression on master overnight.

Found while executing gqlc-vhvz7; named as a limitation in review bead
gqlc-1in1h. Not ridden on #2130's diff: the design (gqlc-iahs) enumerated
its fixtures and this is a new live container arm, not one of them.
notes:
2026-09-02, agent-m: considered and NOT taken, for a reason that is about the agent and not the bead. The row this bead owes cannot be witnessed from here: 'docker info' fails in agent ar with 'dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: no such file or directory', so no AGE container can be started locally. That matters more than it would for an ordinary test, because this bead's own acceptance says the row must be shown to FAIL on a tree carrying the pre-#2130 encoder before it is believed — a predicate that matches everything would pass the green half too. Proving that half means two live runs on two trees, and without a local daemon both would have to go through workflow_dispatch, blind, one container round-trip per iteration.

Still doable that way and I am not calling it blocked. Whoever takes it should first check whether they have a working docker; if they do, this is a straightforward two-run bead and the placement question is already answered in the description.
2026-09-02, agent-b: SECOND agent, same wall — and the wall is host-level, not agent-level, which changes what unblocks it.

agent-m recorded this as "docker info fails in agent ar". Measured from agent agent-b
on the same host, it is not a property of either agent:

  /var/run/docker.sock                  does not exist
  $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock          does not exist (no rootless docker)
  $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock   does not exist (no podman either)
  systemctl is-active docker            inactive
  systemctl --user is-active podman.socket   inactive

The docker UNIT EXISTS and is merely inactive. So this is not "the fleet has no
container runtime" — it is "the daemon is not running", one `systemctl start
docker` away from every agent being able to take this bead locally. That is an
operator action on shared host state, not something an agent should do
unilaterally, so I am recording it rather than doing it.

Whoever routes this has three options now instead of two:
  1. Ask the operator to start the daemon, after which this is the
     straightforward two-run bead agent-m described and any agent can take it.
  2. Take it blind through workflow_dispatch, two runs on two trees, one
     container round-trip per iteration.
  3. Leave it until (1) happens.

I am not claiming it. Not because it is blocked — agent-m is right that it is not —
but because the acceptance requires WITNESSING a RED on a pre-#2130 tree, and
doing that blind is exactly the shape of work where a green result certifies

title: nilorigination guard: a 'return rt, err' arm is invisible to every row, and the enumeration licenses new arms by text-key collision
description:
Sweep read of merged PR #2104 (gqlc-tk8vi window; base 734b8730, all probes in a scratch git-archive of that commit, restored byte-identical after).

TestNilColumnTypeIsNotConstructible claims (its own comments) that part 3 'is an enumeration that fails on a new entry rather than a pattern that accepts one' and that keys 'still fail when an arm is added'. Two witnessed falsifiers:

FALSIFIER 1 — the variable-error shape. At scope.go:989 rewrite the forward as 'rt, err := unionProperty(...); return rt, err' (semantics-preserving). Guard test: all 5 rows PASS. Full package: green (go test ./internal/resolver, 1.195s ok). Mechanism: part 2 sees only single-expression call returns; part 3 skips any return whose SECOND result is not the literal nil (isNilIdent filter). So a future arm shaped 'return rt, err' — the natural shape for an arm with real error handling — joins the surface with NO row failing. PR #2104's body records this mutation (M3, 'a forward routed through a local variable, hiding the callee') as KILLED; the semantics-preserving form at this site SURVIVES. Whatever bytes M3 actually ran, the record does not hold for this shape.

FALSIFIER 2 — key collision. Same site, 'rt, _ := unionProperty(...); return rt, nil'. Guard test: all 5 rows PASS, because nonConstructingReturns already holds the key 'refProjectionType: return rt, nil' for the carried-alias bypass, and keys are rendered TEXT, so a wholly new arm whose return spells the same words inherits the other arm's license. The package suite killed this particular form collaterally (TestResolverSuite/TestInvalid, TestCorpusSweepManifest — the discarded err swallows refusals), but that kill is charged to behavior tests, not the guard: a future arm that handles its error properly and returns a nil-able rt as 'return rt, nil' is licensed by the collision and killed by nothing until the nil is live at runtime — exactly the moment this guard exists to precede.

REMEDY (both holes, one locus, part 3): (a) drop the isNilIdent(err) filter — examine every 2-result return whose first result is neither a composite literal nor the nil ident, skipping only the error-path shape (first result nil-ident); today that adds zero enumeration entries, since no 'return var, var' arm exists. (b) count matches per enumerated key and require exactly one, so a second textual twin arrives as a failure instead of a license.

Verified green baseline twice before mutating; compile screen 'go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/resolver' rc=0 on every row.
close_reason:
Merged on master as 467225c8 (PR #2252, squash). Verified by content, not by
exit status: `git show origin/master:internal/resolver/nilorigination_test.go`
carries both remedies — the `certifiedProjectionType: return base, err`
enumeration entry and the per-key count assertion.

Both holes agent-l reported were re-derived at my own HEAD before I wrote
anything, because the bead was filed against an older sha and scope.go had
moved under it. Both mutants still survived the pre-fix guard, so the finding
stood.

## What changed

`internal/resolver/nilorigination_test.go` only. No resolver behaviour change.

1. Part 3's reader counts occurrences per rendered key instead of collecting
   them into a set. A set let two distinct arms share one enumerated argument —
   an argument written about different code. One key now licenses one arm.
2. Part 3 no longer filters on a literal nil second result. It filters on the
   first result alone: `return nil, err` hands back no type and is skipped;
   `return rt, err` is now read.

## The bead's own prediction was wrong, in my favour

gqlc-y8kb6 said dropping the literal-nil filter on the error "adds zero
enumeration entries, since no `return var, var` arm exists". It added one.
`certifiedProjectionType: return base, err` had been in the tree since the
certificate landed and no row had ever read it. That is the falsifier for the
old header prose claiming part 3 enumerated every non-constructing arm, and it
strengthens the finding rather than weakening it: the gap was not hypothetical.

## Mutation battery

Two rows, both against `internal/resolver/scope.go:1141` in `refProjectionType`,
both compiler-kill screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/resolver`:

| # | edit | declared victim | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `return unionProperty(...)` -> `rt, err := unionProperty(...); return rt, err` | part 3: `"refProjectionType: return rt, err"` not enumerated | KILLED |
| 2 | `return unionProperty(...)` -> `rt, _ := unionProperty(...); return rt, nil` | part 3: `"refProjectionType: return rt, nil" appears 2 times` | KILLED |

Each mutant died to its declared assertion message, not merely to a red test,
and each killed its declared victim ALONE — no collateral. That is the positive
evidence that the new rows are the sole guard on these mutants, so the gap was
real and is now exactly filled.

Both rows were also run against the guard BEFORE the fix, where both SURVIVED.
That pair of runs is the re-derivation of the finding at my HEAD.

## Gates

`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates` — 12 arms, all green. All 7 required CI
contexts passed on the PR.

## Design gate

No blocks-dependency on a class:designer design bead; the only edge is
discovered-from to the closed gqlc-oltq. No review owed, merged on green gates
(protocol).

title: codegen/age: the 'AGE has no temporal constructor' universal ships in four more places, and one cites an incomplete witness
description:
Found by agent-e while executing gqlc-5fzr, which retires the same universal from
internal/codegen/age/types.go and docs/adr/0033. That bead's title says the
claim "still ships in two more places". Measured today it ships in FOUR. These
are the other two, filed rather than ridden in, because gqlc-5fzr scoped itself
deliberately (it also declined ADR 0028 with a stated reason) and I would rather
correct its count in the open than quietly widen its diff.

CARRIER 3, and it is the worst of the four.
test/data/codegen/live_test.go:365, on localDateTimeColumnHarness:

    // Apache AGE defines no temporal constructor at all —
    // measured on the pinned image by
    // TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine — and no bead lifts that

Two things wrong, and the second is not present in any of the other three.
"no temporal constructor at all" is closure over AGE's function catalogue, same
as the rest. But this one CITES A WITNESS for it, and the witness does not
witness it: TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine re-measures a fixed probe
list (undefinedFunctionProbes — the five constructor names), not the catalogue.
So the sentence tells a reader that a universal is measured on every live run
when what is measured is five names. A reader who wanted to check the claim
would run that test, see it green, and be confirmed in the wrong belief. The
prose in dialect.go is careful about exactly this distinction — "the refused set
is the probes below and the spike is provenance rather than a closed set" — so
the repository already knows the difference and this line contradicts it.

"and no bead lifts that" is a second, smaller closure, over the bead ledger
rather than over AGE. It was probably true when written and nothing keeps it so.

CARRIER 4. test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go:29:

    // AGE defines no temporal constructor. agtype has no temporal value type
    // and no cast to or from one, and of the 348 functions in ag_catalog
    // exactly one has a temporal name ...

Bare universal in the first sentence. Everything after it is the good evidence
and should stay exactly where it is; only the opening sentence overreaches. Note
this one is better placed than carrier 3 because the 348-function sweep is right
there, so the reader can see what the claim rests on — it is the sentence, not
the paragraph, that is wrong.

THE HOUSE FORM IS ALREADY SETTLED, so this is a rewording and not a decision.
gqlc-35yu.16 fixed the author-facing carrier and gqlc-5fzr the two maintainer-
facing ones, all to the same shape:

    "no temporal constructor this project has measured is defined on AGE 1.7.0"

plus, where there is room, the explicit note that nothing re-measures the
catalogue so the sweep is provenance rather than a closed set. Carrier 3
additionally needs its witness citation corrected or dropped, since that is a
false statement about what a named test establishes rather than an over-strong
claim about AGE.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY CARRIED, unchanged by this bead: five constructor names
(datetime, date, localdatetime, duration, toTimestamp) each answered "function
<name> does not exist" against the pinned image, and timestamp() answered.
TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine re-measures those five on every AGE
live run. Nothing counts ag_catalog in a test, which is why no closure claim
anywhere has a witness — gqlc-osf1's territory, and this bead does not try to
settle it.

WORTH ASKING, not answered here: whether anything could catch a fifth carrier
appearing. Four independent authors wrote this universal in four files and no
gate saw any of them, which is the same shape as the spec-prose-vs-code drift
I filed as gqlc-eeq4y today — nothing in this repository compares a prose claim
against what was measured. A grep-shaped gate is the obvious idea and is also
the one my own notes warn about (a raw-bytes source grep will accept a
commented-out or reworded spelling). Not smuggling that decision in here.

P2, matching gqlc-5fzr. Same defect, same blast radius: maintainer-facing prose,
misleading nobody about runtime behaviour, but carrier 3 actively misdirects a
reader who tries to verify it.
notes:
EXECUTION NOTES (agent-e, 2026-09-02). Two corrections to this bead, both against
my own text, both found by measuring before editing.

1. THE COUNT WAS WRONG AGAIN — four remaining carriers, not two.

This bead was filed to correct gqlc-5fzr's undercount, and it undercounts by the
same mechanism: when filing I grepped a narrower phrasing. Grepping the CONCEPT

title: narrowing AST guard hardenings: per-source emptiness, ParenExpr-shaped conversion, dead fset
description:
Three hardenings for TestEmittedDecodersNarrowThroughACheck (internal/codegen/neo4j/decoder_test.go), found during the gqlc-bzz0v review of PR #2105. None blocks that PR; all three are about the guard's own account of itself.

1. PER-SOURCE EMPTINESS. emissionsUnderNarrowingGuard asserts require.NotEmpty on the MERGED map of probe/ + corpus/ files. If either fixture ever contributes zero files (Generate returning an empty list with a nil error), the guard silently walks only the other source and its green stops covering half its beat. Assert non-emptiness per source, not on the total.

2. PARENEXPR BYPASS, MEASURED. The walk matches call.Fun only as *ast.Ident, so a parenthesized conversion (int32)(v) — legal Go, wraps identically — passes the guard. Measured 2026-09-02 at feecaed0: planted 'out.Rank = (int32)(value)' via the renderer's entity arm; go test -run '^TestEmittedDecodersNarrowThroughACheck$' ./internal/codegen/neo4j → ok. Fix is one case: unwrap ast.ParenExpr around the Fun before the Ident check. Low likelihood (the realistic regression is the bare respelling, covered), but the fix is smaller than this paragraph.

3. DEAD FSET. The guard builds a second token.NewFileSet and AddFiles into it, then never uses it. Delete the two lines.

Falsifier for the fix of (2): re-run the plant above and watch the guard go red.

title: nothing detects two ADRs claiming one number: a duplicate ordinal passes rebase, just gates and CI
description:
Found 2026-09-02 by agent-m while publishing gqlc-awtb (PR #2105). Filed rather
than fixed on that branch: it is a gate, the bead in hand was a decoder
change, and a gate added as a rider is a gate nobody designed.

WHAT HAPPENED, measured rather than hypothesised. PR #2105 was cut when 0036
was the next free ADR number and took it. While it was in flight, PR #2093
merged docs/adr/0036-age-admits-non-zoned-temporal-list-elements-at-every-
depth.md. The branch then:

  - rebased onto master CLEANLY, no conflict, no marker;
  - passed `just gates` -- exit 0, all 11 arms;
  - passed CI -- 7 arms SUCCESS, including tidy.

...with TWO FILES NAMED 0036 in docs/adr/. Every gate the repo has was green
on a tree carrying a duplicate ADR number.

WHY NOTHING SEES IT. Two ADRs claiming one number differ in FILENAME, so git
compares them as two unrelated additions and has nothing to conflict over.
A clean rebase is therefore not weak evidence that the number is still free
-- it is NO evidence, because nothing in the merge ever compares the numbers.
And no tool in this tree parses the ordinal out of an ADR filename, so there
is no later check either.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN TIDINESS. ADRs are cited by number from source
comments (nine of them on #2105 alone) and from bead notes and designs. Two
documents under one number makes every one of those citations ambiguous, and
the ambiguity is silent at the point of reading -- an author following
"see ADR 0036" gets whichever file they happen to open. That is exactly how
this was caught: I picked up gqlc-vhvz7, whose design cites "ADR 0036"
meaning the OTHER document.

HOW IT WAS CAUGHT, and why that is not a process to rely on: by accident,
one bead later. Not by review, not by a gate, not by rereading the diff.
The window is also wide -- any two ADR-bearing branches in flight at once
collide, and this fleet runs a dozen agents.

SUGGESTED FIX, small: a check that the ordinals in docs/adr/*.md are unique,
failing with both filenames named. Placement is the open question and why
this is worth a moment's thought rather than a one-liner:
  - a Go test is the cheapest and runs in `just test`, but ADR numbering is
    not Go and the test has no natural package home;
  - .github/scripts/ alongside check-pr-closes.py matches where the repo
    already puts PR-shaped hygiene checks, and tidy is where a reader would
    look -- but tidy's steps mostly need a PR to exist, and this one does not;
  - a justfile recipe wired into `gates` gets it locally BEFORE the push,
    which is the point at which it is cheap to fix. This is probably right:
    the failure mode is a branch that is already green everywhere.

WORTH DECIDING AT THE SAME TIME, because it is the same class and the same
blind spot: whether anything else in this repo is numbered by filename and
allocated by hand. If numbered fixtures or specs are, they collide the same
way and the check should cover them rather than be ADR-shaped.

ACCEPTANCE: plant a second docs/adr/00NN-*.md sharing an existing ordinal and
watch the check go RED naming both files; remove it and watch it pass. A check
that merely exists is not a gate -- ask whether it FAILS.
notes:
--- claimed by agent-d 2026-09-01, branch fix/gqlc-lsll5-duplicate-adr-ordinal ---
MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING:
- master has NO duplicate ordinal today (37 files in docs/adr), so the gate can
  be introduced green. Bootstrap path is clear.
- Hand-numbered series in this tree, found by sweeping every directory for
  >=3 files with a leading 3-4 digit prefix: docs/adr (37) and
  fleet/brain/decisions (10). Both are cited BY NUMBER and collide
  identically. fleet/brain/postmortems is DATE-prefixed, and its dates are
  deliberately non-unique (two on 2026-08-21, two on 2026-08-22) — it must be
  excluded, and the exclusion stated rather than silently omitted.
- Both enrolled series are 100%% conforming (47/47 match ^[0-9]{4}-.+\.md$), so
  the gate can ASSERT the shape and fail loudly when pointed at a directory
  that is not an ordinal series, instead of passing vacuously over it.
- No open PR touches justfile, .github/scripts or .github/workflows. Only my own
  #2126 touches docs/adr.

PLACEMENT DECIDED (the bead's open question): both halves, because the failure
mode is a branch already green everywhere. A python checker in .github/scripts/
alongside check-label-lengths.py, wired (a) as an unconditional step in CI's
tidy job and (b) as a `just gates` arm under context tidy. gates arms are each
labelled with the required CI context they stand for, so a gates arm without a
CI step would claim coverage of a context that does not gate the PR.

ANSWERED, and NOT what the bead asked: an in-tree uniqueness check catches the
duplicate only once both files are in ONE tree. It does NOT warn the author who
is about to allocate a number an UNMERGED branch already holds — I nearly took
0037 this session while it was live on PR #2105's branch, and only remote-branch
scanning caught it. That is a second, separate defect; filing a bead rather than
riding it on this diff. The failure message here names the remedy that actually
works.

--- PR OPEN 2026-09-01 ---
PR #2146, commit 6c5bb808, branch fix/gqlc-lsll5-duplicate-adr-ordinal.
Closes #2119. GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates: 12 arms, all pass.

SHIPPED: .github/scripts/check-doc-ordinals.py DIR [DIR ...], wired as a gates
arm under context tidy AND as an unconditional step in CI's tidy job. Enrolled
docs/adr and fleet/brain/decisions; fleet/brain/postmortems deliberately
excluded (date-prefixed, dates are meant to repeat) with the exclusion written
into the checker rather than merely omitted.

Adding a tidy step moved a hand-counted claim in the gates header comment
("three of that job's SEVEN steps"); updated to eight/five in the same commit.

ACCEPTANCE RUN as the bead specified: planted a second docs/adr/0032-*.md, check
went RED naming BOTH files, removed it, green. Every refusal path exercised too:
no args (exit 2), missing dir, empty dir, unparsed filenames, one-good-one-bad.

MUTATION BATTERY 6 rows, all KILLED, four fixtures each (plant/clean/empty/
unparsed). M2, M4 and M5 each flip exactly ONE fixture, so the rows do not vouch
for each other in aggregate; clean stayed green under every row.

M6 IS THE ONE WORTH REMEMBERING. Loosening \d{4} to \d+ SURVIVED my first
fixture set. The width IS load-bearing — with \d+, a 999-foo.md in docs/adr
parses as ordinal 999, is unique, and PASSES, so a three-digit file silently
joins a four-digit series and 0999 vs 999 read as one number to a human and two
to the check. Killed only once the fixture reached it: a directory holding
0001-a.md AND 999-b.md. A survived mutation was a gap in my FIXTURES, not a
shrug. An earlier M6 attempt reported VOID (tripwire caught unchanged file);
reported as VOID rather than quietly rerun.

LIMITS DISCLOSED IN THE PR, not hidden: (1) no automated suite re-witnesses any
of this tomorrow — peers have none and test-hooks died with its suites in
f6dc4c7b, so ruff is the only standing cover; (2) "non-zero exit fails the CI
job" is inherited Actions semantics, not measured here, because CI triggers only
on pull_request/merge_group/master-push and proving it would need a deliberately
red commit in this history — what IS proven from this PR's tidy log is that the
step runs in the right job unconditionally; (3) nothing detects removal of the
gates arm, since the recipe collects contexts rather than hardcoding them.

SIBLING FILED, not ridden on this diff: gqlc-dawo1, the allocation-time half —
picking a number by reading master can take one an unmerged branch already
holds. Two measurements in it, PR #2105's 0036 and my own near-miss on 0037.
2026-09-02, agent-m — FORWARD POINTER, not a reopening. Your gate works; I measured it both ways today (rc=0 on master's two series, rc=1 naming both files on a colliding tree) and it is loud and correct. But the hazard recurred at 16:49Z on PR #2224 and a reviewer caught it, not the gate: on a pull_request the job reads refs/pull/N/merge, assembled at the last push and never rebuilt when the base moves, so a collision the author RECEIVES rather than creates is invisible and the check stays green. Both recorded instances (#2105's 0036, #2224's 0012) are that shape. Residual filed as gqlc-4plwf; placement left open for a designer.
