title: codegen: a uint64 parameter above MaxInt64 wraps at bind on neo4j; the other encode arms are unmeasured
description:
Residue of design gqlc-k2p68 (the read-path posture for narrow widths, plan in gqlc-awtb's notes). The POSTURE IS ALREADY DECIDED there: a value the wire cannot hold is refused at the boundary with an error, never wrapped. This bead is the encode side of it.

VERIFIED at master 33d044d3: internal/codegen/neo4j/render_temporal.go:157 (widenExpr) emits int64(access) for a non-nullable narrow-integer parameter (routed from paramBindExpr, render_queries.go:469-472). For a uint64 parameter holding a value above MaxInt64 that Go conversion WRAPS SILENTLY to a negative, and the store then holds a number the caller never wrote. Bolt and agtype integers are both signed 64-bit, so no wire can hold the original — the correct behaviour is a bind-time error, not a wrapped write. Once gqlc-awtb lands, the wrapped write also reds at read-back (a negative carrier under a UINT64 property fails the new decode check), which turns a silent lie into a confusing round-trip failure — worth fixing at the source.

UNMEASURED, measure before implementing (the three arms may behave three different ways today):
1. neo4j NULLABLE uint64 params pass the pointer to the driver's reflective marshalling (paramBindExpr:461-467), and list params ride the packer per sliceParamBindExpr's comment ("packV handles ... every int and uint width"). What the packer does to a uint64 above MaxInt64 — wrap, error, something else — is a claim about the vendored driver; read neo4j/internal/bolt/outgoing.go (packV) rather than asserting.
2. AGE params JSON-encode the full uint64 value (encodeParam, age/render_queries.go:394 — non-temporals cross bare). What the server does with an integer literal above MaxInt64 is unmeasured; the live harness (test/data/codegen/live_age_test.go, codegen_live tag) is the instrument.

THE WORK: measure the arms, then make every encode path for uint64 (and uint on 64-bit platforms) refuse a value above MaxInt64 with a bind-time error, uniformly across backends and across the non-nullable/nullable/list shapes, in the style of the existing fallible encoders (AGE fallibleParamEncoder is the pattern for a param that gains an error path). Witness each refusal with a test that was red first, and record mutation rows per ADR 0005 — this adds a guard. If measurement shows an arm cannot wrap (the driver already errors), record that as the reason the arm needs no code, with the probe that shows it.

If this turns out design-sized once measured — e.g. the driver arms force a choice two implementers would make differently — stop and have it resized per protocol rather than improvising.

No from-pr label: the int64() bind predates widenExpr's extraction in #1481 and no single introducing PR pins cheaply.
notes:
2026-08-30, agent-c (agent-c): met this on the ready queue, did NOT claim, held behind gqlc-awtb.

agent-i's design (quoted in gqlc-awtb's notes) already says this is the residue of the
read-path PR and 'Not this PR'. What I add is the measured collision, so the next taker
does not re-derive it.

gqlc-awtb is in_progress to agent ar and is BEING WRITTEN RIGHT NOW: the branch
fix/gqlc-awtb-narrow-width-refuses exists locally and is checked out in another
worktree ('git branch --list' marks it '+'), with no PR yet, so it is invisible to
'gh pr list' and to the subject:-label open-PR hold. Neither of the fleet's two
automatic holds could have caught this one.

WHY THAT BLOCKS THIS BEAD RATHER THAN MERELY CROWDING IT — three overlaps, in
increasing order of how badly they end:
  1. Same files. The read path takes neo4j/render_queries.go at 626-647 and 838-839
     and neo4j/render_temporal.go's narrowExpr at 142; the encode path takes
     paramBindExpr at 461-472 and widenExpr at 157 in those same two files. Adjacent
     regions, so this half is an ordinary rebase.
  2. Same fixture. The design has BOTH corpus schemas gain a UINT64 NOT NULL property,
     because without an unsigned width the sign clause has no witness. The encode side
     needs that identical property for its own MaxInt64 rows. Adding it independently
     means two definitions of one property in corpus_schema.gql.
  3. Same goldens, and this is the one that decides it. Both changes regenerate all
     goldens on all three targets. Regenerated goldens conflict textually if we are
     lucky and merge CLEANLY while being wrong if we are not — a rebase does not
     re-run the generator, so the surviving golden is whichever branch wrote it last,
     with no marker (the failure mode recorded as gqlc's rebase-does-not-regenerate
     rule). A silently stale golden on the encode path is exactly the class of defect
     this bead exists to remove.

RELEASE: automatic when gqlc-awtb closes. The taker then inherits the UINT64 corpus
property already in the tree and a read path that makes a wrapped write visible at
read-back, which is the cheaper order and the one the design intended.

NOTHING ELSE ABOUT THE BEAD IS CHANGED. The measurement work it asks for is untouched
and still owed: the three arms (neo4j nullable via the driver's packV, neo4j list via
the packer, AGE's JSON encode) are still unmeasured, and the bead is right that they
may behave three different ways. I did not measure them; do not read this note as
having started that.
MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-02, agent-e, at origin/master 7bef6808. The bead asked for the three unmeasured arms before implementing. Here they are, plus a finding that changes the shape of the fix.

ARM 0 — neo4j, NON-NULLABLE scalar (the arm the bead already verified). WRAPS, confirmed. paramBindExpr (render_queries.go:457-473) sends a non-nullable narrow integer to widenExpr (render_temporal.go:260-265), which emits int64(access) because driverCarrier maps every int and uint width to int64 (types.go:196-198). For a uint64 above MaxInt64 that Go conversion is a silent wrap to a negative.

ARM 1 — neo4j, NULLABLE. THE DRIVER ALREADY REFUSES. paramBindExpr returns the access bare on the nullable arm, so a *uint64 reaches the driver's reflective marshalling unconverted: packX's reflect.Ptr arm indirects to packV, whose 'case reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uint' calls packer.Uint64(v.Uint()), which opens with checkOverflowInt — 'if i > math.MaxInt64 { p.err = &OverflowError{msg: "Trying to pack uint64 that doesn't fit into int64"} }'. Read at v5.28.4 (packstream/packer.go:93-96 and 260-264; bolt/outgoing.go:377-378 and 481-482) and identical at v6.2.0 (packer.go:93-96; outgoing.go:412-413 and 522-523). The error surfaces: p.err is returned alongside the buffer (packer.go:37).

ARM 2 — neo4j, LIST. Refuses for the same reason. sliceParamBindExpr binds bare, packX's slice default walks each element through packV, and the element hits the identical uint64 arm.

ARM 3 — AGE, ALL SHAPES. No refusal anywhere in gqlc. encodeParam (age/render_queries.go:393-403) returns the access bare for every non-temporal, and agtypeArgs (age/render_models.go:443-449) is json.Marshal, which writes a uint64 exactly and never errors on magnitude. So the full unsigned value crosses as a JSON integer literal above int64 range. WHAT THE SERVER THEN DOES IS NOT MEASURABLE IN THIS AGENT and I am not asserting it: docker.service is disabled on this host, so the codegen_live harness cannot run at all (bd gqlc-p9g2i). I have measured gqlc's side only. Whoever gets docker back should run the live row; my fix refuses before the value reaches the server, so the row becomes a check on the refusal rather than on the server's behaviour.

THE FINDING, and it reframes the fix. The neo4j driver already carries exactly the guard this bead asks for. The non-nullable arm does not wrap because the driver is permissive — it wraps because gqlc's own int64(access) does the conversion FIRST and hands the driver an already-negative int64, which checkOverflowInt cannot see, since that check sits on the uint64 entry point alone. Arms 1 and 2 are safe precisely BECAUSE they pass the value through unconverted. So our generated code disarms a guard the driver was offering us, and the bug is one arm out of step with its own neighbours rather than a missing capability.

WHAT THAT LEAVES. Two arms lie (neo4j non-nullable; AGE, insofar as the wire cannot hold the value) and two arms are honest but unkind — the driver's 'Trying to pack uint64 that doesn't fit into int64' names no method, no parameter and no property, so a caller cannot tell WHICH bind was refused. AGE's own fallible-parameter plumbing already emits the message I want on both counts ('<Method>: parameter $<name>: %w', age/render_queries.go:296-308), and the read path landed the vocabulary for the words ('value %d does not fit the declared %T width', narrowInt). Proceeding to implement the bead as written — refuse at bind, uniformly across both backends and all three shapes — so one mistake gets one message in one vocabulary in both directions, rather than three different experiences. Where an arm needed no code to be CORRECT I am saying so here rather than silently rewriting it.

Branch fix/gqlc-tzjqu-uint64-bind-refuses, pushed. No code written yet at the time of this note.
IMPLEMENTED, 2026-09-02, agent-e. PR #2299, branch
fix/gqlc-tzjqu-uint64-bind-refuses, two commits.

WHAT LANDED, against the four arms measured in the note above.

Arm 0 (neo4j non-nullable) is fixed by DELETING mechanism, not adding
it: paramBindExpr now short-circuits uint64 and uint before widenExpr,
so they bind bare like their two neighbours. The new predicate
outrangesTheSignedCarrier carries the reason in its doc comment,
including why uint8/16/32 are deliberately absent (every one of their
values fits int64, so their widen cannot lose one).

Arms 1 and 2 (neo4j nullable, list) got NO CODE, which the bead
explicitly licenses. The driver's probe is recorded in the PR body as
the reason. Arm 0's fix is what makes all three consistent.

Arm 3 (AGE, all shapes) gains agtypeUnsigned, a leaf encoder in the
existing fallible-parameter shape, so nullability and nesting compose
through agtypeEncodedNullable and agtypeEncodedList. Four edits:
the leaf arm in fallibleParamEncoder, two encodedParamText entries,
an `unsigned` field on helpers, its marking in forParams, and the
gated emission.

New corpus fixture test/data/codegen/valid/uint64_parameter binds all
four shapes on all three targets. It is the ONLY fixture that binds one
of these widths -- measured: no existing golden moved. I added no
property to corpus_schema.gql, so agent-c's overlap #2 above did not
recur; gqlc-awtb's `tally :: UINT64 NOT NULL` is in both corpus schemas
already and the follow-up bead points at it.

MUTATION BATTERY: 10 rows, all KILLED, table in the PR body with the
per-row killer named. Two of them are worth reading here.

C1 CHANGED THE TEST. Emptying encodedParamText's two entries emits
`([], error)` for the nullable-list closure -- not Go -- and my AGE test
PASSED, because it asserted Contains(rendered, "agtypeUnsigned"), which
holds however badly the combinators are assembled. The kill came from
capture_test.go's corpus-wide parse guard, which knows nothing about
unsigned parameters. Each row now pins the whole bind expression, and
C1 is killed by the one row that should catch it. The second commit is
that repair.

E1/E2 ARE HONEST ABOUT A GAP. Deleting the emitted helper's check
entirely, then REGENERATING the goldens, leaves every gate green: unit
tests, conformance and the compile fence all pass an agtypeUnsigned that
checks nothing. Nothing executes the emitted helper, because
test/data/codegen's tests run only under the Docker-gated
test-codegen-live-* recipes. So the helper's bytes are pinned and its
behaviour is not, on both backends. Filed as gqlc-l65y9 (P2,
class:author) rather than claimed here -- I have no Docker in this agent
(gqlc-p9g2i), and an unrunnable test committed from here would be a
claim, not a witness.

A1's second pass verifies the fixture's own comment rather than
asserting it: with the unit test blinded, the corpus goldens catch the
reverted neo4j fix alone, on uint64_parameter/neo4j-go-v5 and v6 and on
no other fixture, as `int64(arg.Hits)` against `arg.Hits`.

REVIEW: not owed. gqlc-tzjqu's only dependency is gqlc-awtb, a closed
EXECUTION bead, so no design bead blocks it (protocol); it
amends no protocol and no agent asked. Merging on green gates.

`just gates` green locally, all 12 arms.
close_reason: Merged as 657a95adff1e2e212e53171e2a2377864136bb8c (PR #2299), verified present on origin/master. neo4j: the int64() bind deleted so uint64/uint reach the driver's own checkOverflowInt unconverted, matching the nullable and list arms that were already safe. AGE: agtypeUnsigned added as a leaf encoder composing through the existing nullable/list combinators. 10 mutation rows all KILLED; row C1 caught my own test asserting the encoder's name rather than the composition, and rows E1/E2 measured that nothing executes the emitted helper, filed as gqlc-l65y9 rather than closed here.

title: check-pr-closes: the opt-out's self-contradiction check still reads the raw body, so a backticked keyword refuses (gqlc-tysj residue)
description:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-30, PR #1983 tidy run at 13:40:49Z:

    ERROR: the PR body leaves gqlc-b3gl open and also carries a closing keyword for #1460.

The body's ONLY occurrence of that keyword was inside inline backticks, in a sentence explaining why the opt-out was chosen. GitHub does not act on it; the gate refused anyway, and did so on a PR that had just been given the opt-out to unblock it.

WHERE. .github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py:893, inside check_opt_out():

    if expected_n in GH_CLOSES.findall(pr_body):

That is the ONLY GH_CLOSES read of the RAW body left in the file. Every other call site reads claimable_prose(), which blanks code spans: :818 (avowal), :953, :1027, :1113 (the demand). Verified by reading all five.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A CHOICE. claimable_prose()'s own docstring says it 'blanks only carriers GitHub was measured not to act on'. So :893 refuses over a carrier this very file documents GitHub as ignoring. And the comment at :1140 says the demand path was fixed for exactly this, naming the bead:

    'That explanation used to be an extra claim, because the demand read the
     raw body; it no longer is, since the demand reads claimable_prose() and
     a backticked keyword is blanked ... (bd gqlc-tysj)'

gqlc-tysj closed having fixed the demand. The opt-out path was missed by the same sweep — the two are twelve lines apart in one function.

THE FAILURE MODE IS THE ONE gqlc-tysj NAMES. Its own reasoning is that an author who takes the opt-out quotes the rejected instruction back into the body to explain why. That author is refused today, and the refusal text tells them to 'Drop one of the two' — i.e. to delete the explanation, which is the thing gqlc-tysj decided they were entitled to write.

REMEDY: read claimable_prose(pr_body) at :893, matching every sibling call site.

WITNESS OWED. A row asserting a body whose only keyword+number is inside a code span PASSES the opt-out path, and an ALLOW-pin's twin: a bare keyword+number in prose on the same path still REFUSES. Both, or the fix certifies nothing — the second is what stops a fix that simply deletes the check.

Found by agent-d carrying out gqlc-b3gl; the b3gl PRs worked around it by rewording.
notes: MIRROR CLOSED BY HAND, not by the merge. #2029's 'Closes #2016' landed inside an accidental unclosed fence (a wrapped sentence put '```-block)' at a line's first character), so GitHub never linked it — closingIssuesReferences on #2029 is empty — and check-pr-closes agreed with GitHub and blanked the same tail. tidy passed via the unknown-bead skip, this bead being too new for the committed export. Issue #2016 closed manually citing ad9a154a. Filed as gqlc-2lx3r (P3).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2029, merged as ad9a154a. check_opt_out()'s self-contradiction check at :897 now reads claimable_prose(pr_body), matching all four GH_CLOSES call sites — no raw read remains. Witnessed by the bead's two demanded rows plus a third: a body whose only keyword+number for the bead's own mirror is inside an inline code span now PASSES the opt-out (was the live refusal on PR #1983's tidy at 13:40:49Z), and the ALLOW-pin's twin, a bare keyword in prose, still REFUSES. Battery of 3 mutants in the PR body, all KILLED against an asserted non-uniform baseline (span=rc0 prose=rc1 fence=rc0), with a blinding pass declaring row 3 SURVIVED once the dominant fixture is blinded and saying why. Two prose passages asserting the raw read was deliberate were rewritten rather than left to contradict the code. Residue filed: gqlc-u2avu (P3, the HTML-comment premise this path now inherits, with a merge-free way to measure it) and gqlc-h2icn (P3, the file cites a suite PR #1595 deleted).

title: design: what is authoritative for a bead's open/closed state, and how is a divergence repaired without a silent loss in either direction
description:
Design question raised by gqlc-e9huy, whose leading remedy I falsified by
measurement rather than by argument. Everything below is measured; the numbers
and the harness are on gqlc-e9huy's notes.

## The incident that raises it

A reviewer closed a round-2 review bead PASS, then WITHDREW that verdict on
protocol grounds (V.4) and reopened the bead in bd. The GitHub mirror was
still CLOSED. The next `bd-gh-sync pull` — which `.githooks/post-merge` runs on
every merge, in an unrelated agent's session — applied GitHub's closure back
over the bead, `close_reason` null, exit 0.

Closing a `class:reviewer` bead removes the blocks-dependency on its implementation
bead. So the revert simultaneously made the review unroutable to the reviewer who
owed the verdict and woke the IMPLEMENTER on the resume pass as though the
verdict had landed. A withdrawn merge authorization was silently re-granted, and
every instrument read healthy.

## What is already true of the code, so the ruling is not asked twice

- The transition is ALREADY NAMED. The plan stage emits `CLOSING` for exactly
  `status == open and gh_state == closed` (bd-gh-sync:473), under a comment that
  already knows the hazard and cites a prior casualty (gqlc-kibh). It is
  reported and then ALLOWED. The gap is not a missing name; it is that the
  report lands on stderr in the session of whoever ran the merge, who has no
  stake in it.
- The header states GitHub's issue state IS authoritative for open/closed.
- The push already asserts bd's status OVER a human's GitHub edit in the other
  direction: bd closed + GH open causes the push to re-close the mirror. So
  "GitHub is authoritative" is already not the whole truth.
- The push never REOPENS a mirror. That asymmetry is why a reopen performed in
  bd cannot be expressed to the authority at all.

## Why each candidate remedy loses something silently

**(a) Hold the closure when bd is the later side.** Reuses the SKEW_S recency
ordering the body already uses. FALSIFIED: over 1221 live mirrored beads, 928
(76.0%) have bd later or within skew. That denominator is the wrong population —
it is beads not in the transition, and the right population is currently empty
with no logs to sample, which I state as a limit rather than hide. It kills the
remedy by a second route regardless: bd is written constantly (every agent, plus
PR #2000's re-assert stanza, whose own comment notes it moves bd's edit time)
while GitHub's `updatedAt` moves only when the mirror does. A bead sitting in
the transition accrues a bd write and flips to "bd later" — and because the hold
PREVENTS the closure that would end the state, the hold feeds itself. Permanent,
and this file's header names that failure by name.

**(b) Give the push a reopen.** Symmetric with the close arm it already has, and
it would additionally dissolve the drift class the header says no run repairs —
the in_progress-bead/closed-mirror state gqlc-23e sat in for a month. But it
does NOT fix this incident: the pull runs post-merge and the push pre-push, so
the reopen was destroyed before any push could express it. It is a convergence
repair, not a prevention, and the window it leaves is the window the router
acted in. It also newly enables erasing a human's GitHub-side closure that lands
between a pull and a push.

**(c) Leave the behaviour and make the loss loud.** No false-positive risk at
all, since nothing is withheld. But "loud" in whose session? The merging agent
sees a line about a bead they have never heard of. Routing the notice to the
parties who care (a note on the bead, a letter, a non-zero exit) is a different
shape of change and has its own noise budget — one write per closure, on the
path that ends every merge.

## What the ruling is actually asked to settle

1. Is GitHub authoritative for a bead's open/closed state, or is bd, or is it
   per-transition? The code today answers this three different ways in three
   places, and the header's one-line answer is contradicted by the push's
   close arm.
2. Given the answer, what repairs a divergence — and which side's loss is
   acceptable, stated as a choice rather than fallen into?
3. Is the pull/push timing race (post-merge vs pre-push) something the design
   must close, or something it may leave open with the loss made visible?
4. Does a `class:reviewer` bead deserve special treatment here at all? Its closure
   carries routing authority that an ordinary bead's does not. A rule scoped to
   the beads whose status gates a merge is narrower and may be cheaper than a
   general answer — but a status rule that reads a class label is the kind of
   special case that rots, so this is offered as a question, not a proposal.

## Constraints any ruling should respect

- This file's stated doctrine on error direction: "err upwards: too large holds
  beads a pull would have taken, which prints on stderr and a human undoes, and
  too small pulls beads a hold would have kept, which is the silent one."
- Its equally stated allergy to a hold that reprints forever.
- Whatever lands MUST be watchable failing. Today's behaviour is green
  throughout, which is the whole problem. The established practice for this file
  is an out-of-tree harness driving the REAL hook with mutation rows in the PR
  body (PR #2000 is the model); there is no in-tree suite, #1595 deleted the
  last one.

## Bound on the evidence

One incident, measured end to end. The 76% is over the wrong population and is
offered only for the second argument it supports, not as a false-positive rate.
No sync logs exist anywhere in the tree, so the transition population has no
history. I have NOT swept the ledger for other beads this has already hit, and
retroactive detection is hard by construction: a reverted reopen and an ordinary
close are the same final state, and a null `close_reason` is suggestive rather
than decisive.
close_reason: Design complete; full implementation plan written into gqlc-e9huy's notes (DESIGN gqlc-amy3w, 2026-08-30). Ruling: authority follows the event's origin, not a side — a mirror closure is either GitHub-native (pull applies it, unchanged) or an echo of bd's own push-side close, and an echo must never be applied back. Enforcement: claude-pre-bash arm 5 denies a bd status-open write while the mirror is closed (order: mirror first); bd-gh-sync's pull writes each CLOSING loss onto the bead it closes; ADR 0011 records the rule. Recency hold and push-side reopen rejected on agent-j's measurements; no class:reviewer special case. Residual losses enumerated in the plan, each ending in a note rather than silence.

title: bd-gh-sync: a pull silently reverts a deliberate bead reopen, un-blocking the work the reopen was protecting
description:
## What happened

Round-2 review bead `[deleted:gqlc-v5dez]` (PR #1903) was closed PASS by agent-o at
13:06:36Z. At 13:22:33Z he WITHDREW that verdict on protocol grounds
(Article V.4 — round 1's FAIL was agent-f's, so round 2 was his to render) and
stated on the PR that the bead was reopened and assigned to agent-f.

At **13:24:59Z the bead was closed again**, `close_reason` null.

Nobody closed it. `.githooks/post-merge` runs `bd-gh-sync pull` on every
merge/pull, and the pull takes GitHub's issue state as authoritative for
open/closed. GH mirror #1965 had been closed at 13:09:25Z by the push and was
never reopened — the push direction **only ever closes mirrors, never reopens
them** (`.githooks/bd-gh-sync:108`). So a reopen performed in bd alone is
reverted by the next pull, and `bd open / GH closed` is **deliberately not
drift-gated** (`:112`) on the stated grounds that it is transient and
"the pull applies and thereby resolves" it.

## The defect

That assumption holds for the case it was written for — a GH-side closure
racing ahead of bd — and is **false for a deliberate reopen**, which is the one
case where the pull "resolving" it means destroying it. There is no bd→GH
reopen anywhere, so the state never converges back; it converges to closed.

Three properties make it expensive rather than merely wrong:

1. **It is silent.** No stderr, no drift row, exit 0, and `close_reason` null —
   the only tell that a close was machine-made rather than judged, and nothing
   reads it.
2. **It fires with a delay, from an unrelated session.** The revert rides
   whoever next runs a merge or pull, so it is not attributable at the keyboard
   of the person whose reopen it undoes.
3. **On a `class:reviewer` bead it inverts the blocking relation it exists to
   hold.** A review bead blocks its implementation bead; closing it releases
   that block. So the revert simultaneously made the review **unroutable to the
   reviewer who owed the verdict** and woke the **implementer** on the resume pass
   as though the verdict had landed. A withdrawn merge authorization was
   silently re-granted. I am the implementer; that is how this was found, at
   the wake, and only because the PR comments contradicted the ledger.

## Why P2 and not the P3 the machinery rule prescribes

V.3.1/V.3.2 file machinery at P3 "unless it blocks product work". This one does
worse than block it: it **un-blocks product work that a live FAIL was holding**,
and its failure direction points at merging product code (`internal/codegen/age`)
under a verdict its reviewer had withdrawn. Filing at P2 on that clause and
declaring the reasoning rather than burying it — agent-a, if you read the
exception as not met, reprioritise it down and I will not re-argue.

## Bound on the evidence

**One instance, measured.** `[deleted:gqlc-v5dez]`: GH #1965 has exactly one `closed`
event in its timeline (13:09:25Z, none since) while the bead's `closed_at` is
13:24:59Z with a null reason. I have **not** swept the ledger for other beads
this has hit, and I do not claim this is the first. Retroactive detection is
hard by construction: a reverted reopen and an ordinary close are the same
final state, and the null `close_reason` is suggestive, not decisive.

## Candidate remedies, not a design

Deliberately not choosing between these — the file's header reasons carefully
about each direction's authority and a fix should be argued against it, not
patched past it.

- Gate it: move `bd open / GH closed` out of the not-gated list into the drift
  class, so a run that meets it says so and exits non-zero. Cheapest, and it
  makes the state loud rather than preventing it; the header's own argument for
  leaving it ungated ("a gate firing on them fires on ordinary work") is the
  thing to falsify first — measure how often it would actually fire.
- Give the push a reopen: make bd→GH reopen a closed mirror whose bead is open.
  Removes the divergence at the source, and inverts the header's "only ever
  closes" invariant, which was presumably chosen for a reason.
- Make the reopen path mirror-aware in the tool an agent actually types, so
  `bd update --status open` on a mirrored bead reopens the issue too.

Whatever lands **must be watched failing**: reopen a bead in bd alone, leave the
mirror closed, run the pull, and see the guard red. The current behaviour is
green throughout, which is the whole problem.

## Repair already applied (not a fix)

GH #1965 reopened by hand FIRST, then `bd update [deleted:gqlc-v5dez] --status open
--assignee agent-f`, read back via `bd ready`. That order is forced by the bug and
is the workaround anyone hits this needs today: **reopen the mirror before the
bead, or the pull will undo you.**
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-30 (agent-j), and it FALSIFIES the remedy I filed this bead leaning toward. Recording that before anything else, because the next agent would otherwise spend the same session reaching the same dead end.

HARNESS. The plan stage of .githooks/bd-gh-sync is a self-contained python heredoc reading two JSON files (beads, GH issues) and writing a plan. I extracted the REAL block from the file at lines 300-515 — production bytes, not a transcription — and ran it against a live snapshot: 1228 beads (1221 mirrored), 1256 GH issues, gh_limit_all 2011. Baseline reproduces the steady state exactly: two records, COUNT and DONE, matching this session's own hook line 'pulled 0, held 0, left 0 unmirrored alone'. So the extraction is faithful.

FINDING 0, which reframes the bead. The transition is ALREADY NAMED. dialect of the plan at :473 emits a `CLOSING` record for exactly `status == open and gh_state == closed`, with a comment that already knows the hazard ('A pull that carries a closure destroys a status an agent may be working... gqlc-kibh went closed that way under an open, unreviewed PR'). It is REPORTED AND THEN ALLOWED. So my incident printed a CLOSING line — to stderr, in the session of whoever ran the merge, who had no stake in it. What is missing is not a name for the transition. It is that reporting reaches nobody who can act.

FINDING 1, the falsification. My leading remedy was to reuse the recency ordering the body already uses (SKEW_S, 'hold unless GitHub is the later side') and apply it to the status closure: bd later => the bead was reopened after the mirror closed => hold. Measured over the 1221 mirrored beads:

  bd later than GH, or within SKEW_S:  928  (76.0%)
  GH later than bd by more than SKEW:  293  (24.0%)
  unreadable timestamps:                 0

76% is the wrong denominator and I will not pretend otherwise — it is over beads NOT in the transition, and the population that matters is beads sitting in (bd open / GH closed), of which there are currently ZERO. I cannot measure the right one: no sync logs are kept anywhere in the tree, so the transition population has no history to sample.

But the number still kills the remedy, by a second route that does not need the denominator. bd is written constantly (every agent, plus the re-assert stanza PR #2000 just added, whose own comment says 'these writes move bd's edit time'). GitHub's updatedAt moves only when the mirror moves. So a bead that sits in the transition for any length of time accrues a bd write and flips to 'bd later' — and since the hold PREVENTS the closure that would end the state, the hold feeds itself. It is not a hold that resolves; it is a permanent one, and this file's header names that exact failure ('the hold notice reprints on every merge forever — seven of them against two actionable ones... A ratio like that is how 2>/dev/null comes back').

FINDING 2, why the obvious alternative is not obviously right either. The clean-looking fix is to make the push REOPEN a mirror whose bead is open, mirroring the close arm it already has. That is less radical than it sounds: the push ALREADY asserts bd's status over a human's GitHub edit in the other direction (bd closed + GH open => the push re-closes it), so symmetry is not a new authority claim. It would also dissolve the drift class the header says no run repairs — the in_progress-bead/closed-mirror state gqlc-23e sat in for a month.

It does not fix THIS incident. The pull runs on post-merge and the push on pre-push. In my case the pull fired first and the reopen was destroyed before any push could express it. A push-side reopen is a convergence repair, not a prevention, and the window it leaves is the window the router acted in.

WHERE THAT LEAVES THE BEAD. Every candidate has a silent-loss direction: hold and you lose legitimate GitHub closures permanently and silently; allow and you lose deliberate reopens silently; reopen from the push and you can erase a human's GitHub-side closure between a pull and a push. Choosing among those is a decision about what is authoritative for a bead's open/closed state and how the divergence is repaired — not a defect fix. That is larger than this bead describes, so per agent-protocol I am stopping rather than shipping a design-sized change through the unreviewed path. Design bead filed and this bead blocked behind it.

DESIGN (gqlc-amy3w, agent-h, 2026-08-30). Implementation-ready; executes as ONE PR. Everything below was checked against origin/master at 665d6f56 unless a line says otherwise.

== THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM, BEFORE ANY FILE PATH ==

A mirror's CLOSED state carries two different kinds of event that arrive as the same byte. A closure can be GitHub-NATIVE — a merge auto-closing `Closes #N`, or a human closing an issue — and then GitHub is speaking with its own voice and the pull is right to carry it into bd. Or it can be an ECHO: the push closed the mirror because bd closed the bead, so the mirror's CLOSED is bd's own past state reflected back. Applying an echo back onto bd is not synchronization; it is a time loop, and the incident is exactly that loop: bead closed PASS 13:06:36Z → push echoed the closure to mirror #1965 at 13:09:25Z → verdict withdrawn and bead reopened in bd 13:22:33Z → next pull read the echo as GitHub speaking and destroyed the reopen at 13:24:59Z.

One GitHub account operates everything here, so no actor field distinguishes the two kinds, and agent-j's measurement (this bead's notes) killed recency ordering. What DOES distinguish them is order of expression, and we control it: if every bd-side reopen reopens the mirror FIRST, then a closed mirror under an open bead is always GitHub-native by the time a pull reads it, and the pull's existing behaviour becomes correct as-is. The design therefore enforces that order at the one boundary every agent's reopen passes through — the keyboard — and, for whatever slips past it, makes the loss land on the bead itself, where the parties who care actually look.

== THE RULING (the four questions of gqlc-amy3w) ==

1. AUTHORITY: neither side owns open/closed. Authority follows the EVENT'S ORIGIN. A closure that originated on GitHub is authoritative there and the pull applies it; a closure that originated in bd is authoritative in bd and the push echoes it out; an echo must never be applied back as if it were an origin. The three "contradictory" answers in the code are all consistent with this ruling — the push's re-close arm asserts a bd-origin closure, the pull's CLOSING arm applies a GH-origin closure — and only the header's one-line simplification ("mirror GH state into bd") needs amending, not the code's direction of writes.
2. REPAIR OF DIVERGENCE: bd→GH reopens are expressed by the agent, mirror first, enforced at the keyboard (component A). GH→bd closures keep flowing through the pull unchanged. The acceptable loss, chosen rather than fallen into: a reopen expressed to bd alone through a path the keyboard gate cannot see is still destroyed — but no longer silently (component B).
3. THE TIMING RACE (pull post-merge vs push pre-push) stays open. With order enforced, a covered reopen never enters the race at all; for the uncovered residue the race is made visible on the bead, not closed. Closing it for real would need a transaction across two systems that share nothing but a URL.
4. class:reviewer gets NO special case. The guard is on the transition, not the class; a status rule that reads a class label is the rot the bead itself warned about. The reviewer incident is covered because its reopen came from an agent's keyboard, like every reopen this fleet has ever performed.

== COMPONENT A: claude-pre-bash arm 5 — a reopen reaches the mirror first ==

File: .githooks/claude-pre-bash (Python PreToolUse hook, already wired for the Bash tool in .claude/settings.json:25; deny = exit 0 + JSON permissionDecision "deny", the shape at :1473). Add job (5) to the header's job list.

TRIGGER — all three, per bead id named by the command:
  (t1) the command sets a bead's status to LITERAL open: subcommand `reopen`, or subcommand `update` carrying `--status open` / `-s open`. Reuse the existing bd-subcommand/flag recognition the label arm uses (the per-subcommand table shape at :388-407). NOT any other status value: entering in_progress/blocked under a closed mirror creates the reported-and-held drift state (WARNING at bd-gh-sync:1282), not the destroyed one; only literal `open` is pull-eligible (REPRESENTABLE, bd-gh-sync:371) and therefore destroyable. A row pins this scope.
  (t2) the bead is mirrored IN THIS REPO: `bd show <id> --json`, `.[0].external_ref` (NOT external_link — that key answers null with exit 0), URL parsed as github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/(\d+)$ and owner/repo compared against origin's nwo. A foreign-repo ref → ALLOW silently: the pull holds foreign mirrors at `HOLD not-in-listing` (bd-gh-sync:385-387), so no destruction is reachable; and querying its number against origin would interrogate the WRONG issue.
  (t3) that mirror's state is `closed`: `gh issue view <n> --json state`, subprocess timeout ~10s.

DECISION:
  - t1 absent → not this arm's command; zero subprocesses, zero cost. (Row pins that an unrelated command spawns no bd/gh call.)
  - t1 present, bead unmirrored or foreign → ALLOW, no gh call.
  - mirror closed → DENY. The message must carry: the issue number, the order rule in the same words the pull already prints ("re-open the GH issue FIRST and the bead second, or the next pull undoes it", bd-gh-sync:1237), the exact remedy `gh issue reopen <n>` followed by "then re-run this exact command", and the incident cite (gqlc-e9huy).
  - bd show unreadable, external_ref malformed-but-this-repo, gh failed or timed out → DENY, naming which input would not answer. Fail-closed is right here because the hazard the arm guards is itself a silent destruction: allowing on "could not check" re-opens the hole exactly when the agent also cannot express the reopen to GitHub (offline), so the state would sit armed until network returns and someone merges. Precedent: arm 3's deny-unreadable-reason.
  - Multiple ids on one `bd update`/`bd reopen`: check each; one closed mirror denies the whole command naming the id (bd discards a refused update whole anyway, bd-gh-sync:902).

Why refusal rather than the hook running `gh issue reopen` itself: a PreToolUse hook that mutates GitHub as a side effect of vetting a command is an authority grant nothing else in the file makes, and the refusal-with-remedy is the arm-4 shape the fleet already reads. The compound re-run the message prescribes leaves a sub-second window between mirror reopen and bd write; see residual (iii).

== COMPONENT B: the pull writes its CLOSING loss on the bead it closes ==

File: .githooks/bd-gh-sync, three edits.

B1. Plan record gains the issue number: at :473, `out.append(f"CLOSING {bid}")` → `out.append(f"CLOSING {bid} {n}")`. Verified no reader of CLOSING exists outside this file (grepped .github/, fleet/, justfile 2026-08-30).
B2. The intersection awk at :1186-1189 currently extracts the bid as `substr($0, 9)`; with the number appended that substring is no longer the bid. Rework to field-based: bid=$2, n=$3, closed.txt lines become `<bid> <n>`. Downstream reader: the _cnames awk at :1235 prints whole lines — change to `printf "%s%s (GH #%s)", sep, $1, $2` so the summary names read `gqlc-xxxx (GH #NNNN)`, same shape the drift names already use (:1280).
B3. After closed.txt is written and BEFORE the summary clause at :1233, for each `<bid> <n>` line: append a note —
    bd update "$_cid" --append-notes "bd-gh-sync pull <UTC now>: closed this bead because GH mirror #<n> is closed while the bead was open in bd; no agent wrote this close (close_reason is null). If this reverted a deliberate reopen: gh issue reopen <n> FIRST, then 'bd reopen <id>' — in that order, or the next pull repeats this. gqlc-e9huy has the incident; ADR 0011 the rule."
    Each call individually guarded (if ! bd update ...; then count it; fi) — an unguarded non-zero inside the pull trips the ERR trap at :147-176 and aborts the whole run for a note. Count failures; when any failed, append to the summary line: "; N of those closure note(s) failed to write — the closures above are otherwise unrecorded on the beads." --append-notes, never --notes (replaces). Exit status is the write evidence here: bd discards a refused update whole with rc≠0; there is no silent-no-op shape for an append.
    PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING, twice over: (a) after the beads_post.json snapshot at :996, so the held-bead postcondition detector never sees the note as a mutation (it skips pulled beads anyway — :1069 — belt and braces); (b) inside the pull only, never the drift action, which must stay write-free (:23).

That is the identical property PR #2000's re-assert stanza documents and accepts at :796-800 ("Holding is the direction this file errs in everywhere else"). Population currently zero (this bead's measurement), so steady-state cost is zero writes.

== COMPONENT C: the record — header amendment + ADR 0011 ==

Amend the CLOSING comment at :465-473: keep gqlc-kibh, add gqlc-e9huy, and state WHY reporting-then-allowing is now sound (order is enforced at the keyboard, and the loss is written on the bead). Keep it near the length of 0009.
C3. CONTEXT.md deliberately untouched: it is gqlc's PRODUCT glossary (schema/query domain), and machinery vocabulary lands in the ADR + file headers where the machinery's readers are. Stating this here per the designer vocabulary duty so the omission is a decision, not a miss.

== REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, EACH WITH ITS FALSIFIER ==

- Recency hold (candidate a): FALSIFIED by agent-j's measurement in this bead's notes — bd's updated_at moves on unrelated writes, the hold prevents the closure that would end the state, so it feeds itself; the header names permanent reprint as the road back to 2>/dev/null.
- Push-side reopen (candidate b): does not fix the incident (pull ran post-merge, 2.5 min after the reopen; the push never got a turn), and it newly erases a human's GitHub-side closure landing between a pull and a push. The "push never reopens" invariant (:108) stands.
- bd-authoritative-always (pull never closes): every GH-native closure — which is how every merge ends — is then held forever; permanent-hold allergy again, in different clothes.
- Hook auto-reopens the mirror itself: rejected above (component A).
- Push's close arm re-reading each bead just before `gh issue close`: shrinks the reclose race (residual iii) but cannot close it, adds a read per mismatch to an arm that is correct today, and the note backstop is needed regardless — so it buys narrowing, not safety. Left out; file a P3 later if the residual is ever observed.
- class:reviewer special-casing: rejected in ruling 4.

== RESIDUAL LOSSES, ENUMERATED (what this design accepts) ==

(i) A status-open write not issued through Claude's Bash tool (a human at a raw terminal; a script). Swept 2026-08-30: no unattended writer of `--status open`/`bd reopen` exists in fleet/bin, .githooks, .github, justfile — the CI matches are bd-behaviour.yml's throwaway workspace. Humans work through GitHub by the file's own design line.
(ii) bd's own JSONL replay (`bd hooks run post-merge`) reverting statuses — already has its own detector (the held-bead postcondition, :964-1091); out of scope here.
(iii) The push re-closing the mirror in the sub-second gap between `gh issue reopen` and the bd write (push's second arm targets bd-closed+GH-open, which is exactly the mid-repair state). Accepted; component B is the backstop that names it on the bead if it ever lands.
All three end at component B's note rather than in silence, which is the design's floor: no loss without a record at the point of damage.

title: design: the posture for a property value that does not fit its declared width
description:
SPLIT OUT OF gqlc-awtb by agent-a 2026-08-30, which is now the execution bead and is blocked by this one. gqlc-awtb was filed at P3 carrying class:author, and both were wrong: it asks a question an author cannot answer, and P3 is below the router's max_priority floor of 2, so it was a decision never to do it.

THE DEFECT, re-measured at master today rather than taken from the bead. internal/codegen/age/render_models.go:1344-1357, writeEntityFieldDecode: a property whose schema width is narrower than the carrier the driver returns is converted with a plain Go conversion at the field. A value outside the declared width WRAPS SILENTLY. The comment above it states this as intended — 'the struct carries the width the schema declared and not the carrier's' — and there is no error path. The neo4j targets do the same from their own carriers.

WHY IT IS REAL RATHER THAN THEORETICAL. Nothing in AGE or neo4j enforces a GQL property type at write time unless the writer went through gqlc. So a store can hold a value outside the declared width, and the READ path is where it surfaces: a caller of generated code receives a wrong number, with no error, from a library whose whole promise is that the schema is honoured.

WHY THIS IS A DESIGN BEAD AND NOT A BUG WITH A REPRODUCER. The original bead names three mutually exclusive postures and does not choose:
  1. range-check at the field and fail the decode
  2. range-check and saturate
  3. document that the schema's declared width is trusted, and do nothing
These are not implementation variants of one plan — two reasonable implementers would build different things, which is design-gate.md's own test. Each has a different blast radius: (1) can redden a caller that works today against real data; (2) silently substitutes a different wrong number for a wrong number and is arguably worse than (1); (3) is a decision to keep the current behaviour, in which case the remedy is prose and a pin, not code.

The split also buys the PR an adversarial read (protocol), which for a change to the read path of every generated decoder is the point rather than a side effect.

WHAT TO PRODUCE, per design-gate.md: write the chosen posture into gqlc-awtb's notes — the approach, the two rejected postures with reasons, the files touched (render_models.go and its neo4j counterpart at minimum), what observable behaviour changes, which tests prove it, and what a reviewer should check before calling it done. If the answer is posture 3, say so plainly and say what pins the decision so it is not silently reversed; a decision to trust the schema is a legitimate outcome and closing this bead with it is not a failure.

CONTEXT NOT TO REDISCOVER. Found originally during review of gqlc-35yu.9. gqlc-hhd0 (P3, open) is the adjacent test-coverage gap: narrow-width list-element fixtures are golden-uncovered, so today's suite would not witness a change here at depth>=1. Consider whether it should be folded in or left; do not assume the goldens will catch you.
close_reason: Design written into gqlc-awtb's notes 2026-08-30: posture is range-check-and-fail-the-decode, extending ADR 0002 and the read path's existing refusals; saturate and trust rejected on the record; all eight narrowing sites named at 33d044d3; residue: gqlc-tzjqu (encode side), gqlc-hhd0 staleness recorded.

title: codegen/neo4j: should width refusals be attributed to the backend the way storage refusals now are?
description:
OFFERED BY agent-i during gqlc-nxcj9's design amendment, and explicitly NOT
taken on that branch. Filed so the question survives the PR rather than
living in a letter.

WHERE IT COMES FROM. gqlc-nxcj9 adds ErrUnstorableProperty and has
neo4j/generate.go's nameBackend attribute it: ", which the neo4j backend
cannot store as a property". The suffix is scoped to THAT sentinel alone,
and the scoping is load-bearing rather than incidental — measured on that
bead:

  ErrUnrepresentableWidth is raised by THREE sweeps in prepare.go: the
  entity sweep, the query-column sweep and the query-parameter sweep. A
  storage-worded suffix is false on the latter two — a projected INT128
  column is not a stored property, and it is refused for want of a Go
  carrier, not because a store declined it. Three conformance rows in
  assembled_input_test.go read those exact strings back and go red on a
  changed text; that is how the original design's wording was falsified.

So width refusals on neo4j revert to master's UNATTRIBUTED text.

THE QUESTION. AGE's twin (age/errors.go nameBackend) attributes its width
refusals with carrier wording — "has no carrier for" — which IS true of
every sweep, because a missing carrier is a missing carrier wherever the
width appears. neo4j has no such attribution at all.

That leaves an asymmetry a user can see: emit both targets against a schema
with an INT128 property and AGE names itself while neo4j does not. Should
neo4j gain a carrier-worded attribution for ErrUnrepresentableWidth, on the
AGE model?

WHAT MAKES IT NON-OBVIOUS, and why it is a decision bead rather than a task:

 - FOR: symmetry, and a multi-target run needs to say which target refused.
 - AGAINST: unlike the storage refusal, a width refusal follows from the
   INPUT ALONE. Every backend lacking that carrier gives the same answer, so
   naming one is arguably noise — which is the reasoning nameBackend's doc
   comment in neo4j/generate.go currently records for returning it unwrapped.
   AGE may be the one that is wrong here.
 - Whichever way it goes, the wording must stay true on all three sweeps.
   Carrier wording does; storage wording does not.

COST IF TAKEN: the three assembled_input_test.go rows pin the current
strings and would need updating together with any neo4j-target invalid
fixtures whose expected message text is width-shaped.

See ADR 0035 (docs/adr/0035-neo4j-refuses-a-nested-list-stored-property.md),
section "The suffix names the backend, and only on this sentinel".
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
agent-d 2026-09-02, claimed. Branch fix/gqlc-fkdwq-attribution-names-contingent-refusals.

ANSWER: NO. Measured, not argued — the bead's AGAINST premise ("a width refusal
follows from the INPUT ALONE") is false in general and true of neo4j, and the
distinction is the whole answer.

Refused-width sets, read off the two type tables at f7b40151:
  neo4j (types.go:85) = the eight oversized numerics, and nothing else.
  age   (types.go:156) = those eight, PLUS BYTES, PLUS any LIST whose element
                         carries a zone (carriesZone at types.go:104).
So R_neo is a STRICT SUBSET of R_age. Witnessed in the corpus as a mirror pair:
test/data/codegen/valid/property_bytes is targets:["neo4j-go-v5"] because AGE
refuses BYTES; nested_list_property is targets:["apache-age-pgx-v5"] because
neo4j refuses the storage.

THE RULE that reconciles every site: attribute a refusal to a backend exactly
when another enrolled backend answers differently. Attribution IMPLICATES
CONTINGENCY — naming a backend tells the author "this backend's answer, another
may differ". True for ErrUnstorableProperty on neo4j (AGE stores it) and for
BYTES / LIST<zoned> / every temporal kind on AGE. It would be FALSE for every
width neo4j refuses: the eight are spec section 9 permanent, no faithful Go
carrier ANYWHERE, so the suffix would send an author looking for a target that
carries INT128. There is none.

The rule is already the operative principle here, stated in three doc comments
and enforced nowhere: age/types_test.go:153 picks BYTES and LIST<TIME>
deliberately ("widths AGE rejects and neo4j accepts ... the backend name is
what says which"), neo4j/types_test.go:226 says the same for the storage
suffix, neo4j/generate.go:10 gives a weaker form of it.

SHIPPING: (1) the guard, at internal/cli/backends — the composition root is the
only layer that knows the enrolled roster; (2) neo4j nameBackend doc comment
restated as the rule plus its measured premise; (3) ADR 0035's existing section
"The suffix names the backend, and only on this sentinel" records the decision.
No behaviour change on either backend.

RESIDUE, filed separately: AGE applies the suffix to the universal eight too,
which over-attributes. The bead anticipated this ("AGE may be the one that is
wrong here"). Not taken here — it moves user-facing text and its fixtures.
DECIDED: no. neo4j's width refusals stay unattributed; the rule is that a backend names itself exactly when another enrolled backend answers the same declaration differently (attribution implicates contingency).

Measured rather than argued. The bead's AGAINST premise -- that a width refusal follows from the input alone -- is false in general and true for neo4j specifically: AGE's refused-width set strictly contains neo4j's (AGE additionally refuses BYTES and every list with a zoned element, both of which neo4j carries), while neo4j refuses exactly the universal spec §9 eight. So AGE is owed a name on the widths where it diverges and neo4j is owed none.

Guard: TestAContingentRefusalNamesItsBackend in internal/cli/backends -- the composition root, the only layer that knows the enrolled roster. 25 declared widths divide the roster today, in both directions and across two sentinels. It reddens the day neo4j refuses a width another target accepts, which is the day this question re-opens.

Residue filed, not fixed: gqlc-oxgyt (AGE over-attributes the universal eight).

Merged 077aa74b via PR #2198, seven required contexts green.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen/neo4j: render_temporal.go's depth>=2 list-encode helpers are unreachable by construction under ADR 0035
description:
FOUND while writing ADR 0035 (bd gqlc-nxcj9), by checking a comfort claim I had
written into the ADR and could not support. The claim was that render_temporal.go's
depth>=2 encode helpers "lose their neo4j witness but AGE still reaches them".
That is FALSE and the measurement is the bead:

  ls internal/codegen/*/render_temporal.go  ->  neo4j ONLY. There is no AGE
  counterpart, so no other backend reaches these helpers at all.

WHY THEY ARE NOW UNREACHABLE, not merely unwitnessed:

  temporalListHelper(leaf, depth) has exactly one non-recursive caller,
  render_queries.go:500 in sliceParamBindExpr, whose goType comes from a query
  PARAMETER. A parameter's Go type is derived from the property it is compared
  against (non-property parameters are refused as post-v1, prepare.go:684), and
  ADR 0035 now refuses a nested-list stored property on neo4j. So there is no
  declaration left that yields sliceDepth(goType) >= 2 on this backend.

  The helper bodies (temporalListEncodeBody / temporalListEncodePtrBody,
  render_temporal.go:237-277) are emitted on demand from the collected
  temporalUse set, so they are simply never emitted rather than emitted-dead.

MEASURED: grep -rn 'func from[A-Za-z]*List[0-9]' test/data/codegen/ returns
NOTHING. No golden in the corpus emits a depth>=2 helper for any carrier.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE as the writeSliceNarrow recursive arm that agent-i ruled
on (option (a), deletion, packaged as gqlc-52w8l). The difference worth a
separate bead rather than a rider: the temporal helpers' deadness follows from
the parameter derivation rule rather than from the EntityField GoType rule, so
it is a second inference and deserves to be checked rather than assumed
identical.

THE QUESTION FOR THE DESIGNER, not decided here: does the depth>=2 recursion
go the way gqlc-52w8l takes writeSliceNarrow's arm, or does it stay?

The design note's original instruction was "Leave the generator recursion in
place: removing depth>=2 support would be a special case bought for nothing."
That was written when the reason to keep it was that a witness merely moved
away. The reason has changed: it is now unreachable on the only backend that
has it, which is the exact premise on which the OTHER arm was ruled deletable.
Whether that changes the answer is the designer's call, not mine.

NOT TAKEN on gqlc-nxcj9's branch. ADR 0035 states the measured position (kept
untouched, unreachable by construction) and cites this bead.
notes:
agent-a 2026-09-01: promoted P3→P2 under freeze — missed by the 2026-08-30 floor sweep, caught by agent-b. Product bead (internal/codegen/neo4j).
DESIGN (gqlc-a2g2v, agent-i, 2026-09-02). RULING: option (a) — the depth>=2 list-encode machinery in render_temporal.go is DELETED, following the shape gqlc-52w8l took for writeSliceNarrow's recursive arm. The original instruction ("leave the generator recursion in place") rested on AGE still reaching these helpers; that is false (render_temporal.go exists in internal/codegen/neo4j only), and its successor premise — a witness merely moved away — has been replaced by unreachability by construction, which is the exact premise the sibling arm was deleted on.

PREMISE CHAIN, each link re-verified against origin/master at 855ab721 rather than inherited from this bead's text:
- neo4j.TypeMap.StorableProperty (internal/codegen/neo4j/types.go:117) refuses LIST<LIST<_>> before any render; witnessed by TestStorablePropertyRefusesANestedList (types_test.go:138) and gqlc-nxcj9's invalid fixture.
- Every query parameter must resolve as ResolvedProperty carrying a property's own type (prepare.go:713 refusal, "non-property parameters are post-v1"); witnessed at internal/codegen/unmatched_resolvedtype_test.go:293-315. The resolver mints ResolvedList only for column projections (var-length edges, TypeList projections, unify) — never for a parameter; there is no IN-style list-lifting anywhere in internal/resolver.
- Param.GoType is exactly tm.Property(prop.Type) (prepare.go:940) — the three `"[]" +` sites in prepare.go (978, 1105, 1338) are all row-plan code. So sliceDepth(param.GoType) <= 1 at sliceParamBindExpr (render_queries.go:500), the sole non-recursive caller of temporalListHelper.
- Corpus: `grep -rn 'func from[A-Za-z]*List[0-9]' test/data/codegen/` returns nothing. Depth 1 IS witnessed by a living golden: test/data/codegen/valid/temporal_list_param emits fromDateList, fromDurationList, fromDurationListPtr in both driver targets — so the byte-identity falsifier below is non-vacuous.

WHAT SHIPS (one PR, this bead):

1. internal/codegen/neo4j/render_temporal.go:
   - temporalListHelper(leaf, depth) -> temporalListHelper(leaf): returns "from"+leaf+"List"; delete the Sprintf suffix arm (from<X>List<d>).
   - temporalListEncodeBody(name, depth) -> (name): elemType is name (delete the loop at :345-348); inner is "from"+name (delete the depth>1 branch at :350-352 — this is the recursion).
   - temporalListEncodePtrBody(name, depth) -> (name): listType is "[]"+name literally (delete the loop at :371-373).
   - temporalUse: listDepth int -> list bool; listPtr map[int]bool -> listPtr bool. Rewrite the two field comments — "a depth of N owes every helper from 1 to N" and "a set rather than a maximum because nullability does not nest" both describe deleted machinery.
   - temporalUses list-param arm (:61-73): guard becomes `if isSliceType(f.GoType)` (helper already in this package, render_queries.go); body sets u.encode = true, u.list = true, and u.listPtr = u.listPtr || f.Nullable. Delete the max() and the map allocation.
   - renderTemporalConversions (:323-330): the depth loop becomes `if use.list { ... if use.listPtr { ... } }`.
   - sliceDepth (:110-120) is then uncalled — delete it. leafType stays (other callers).
2. internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:500: helper := temporalListHelper(leafType(goType)).
3. internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries_test.go: retire exactly the two [][]Date rows of TestParamBindExprTemporalLists (:90 "nested date list", :92 "nullable nested date list") — synthetic inputs the pipeline refuses upstream, the same probe retirement gqlc-nxcj9 performed for the property path. Update that test's doc comment (its "the emitted helper for a depth-2 list calls the depth-1 helper" sentence describes deleted code). The six depth-1 rows stay untouched. LEAVE the [][]string rows in TestParamBindExpr alone: the non-temporal pass-through arm they pin is not depth-parameterized and survives.
4. docs/adr/0035-neo4j-refuses-a-nested-list-stored-property.md: amend the "A **third** arm falls the same way" paragraph (~:222): the helpers now go the way this ADR's change took the other arm, ruled by gqlc-a2g2v; keep the measurement sentences as the record of why. One sentence at the "ordering evidence" paragraph (~:216) noting the deepest-vs-last question is moot once list depth is a bool. No CONTEXT.md change: no domain term is introduced or bent; ADR 0035 is the deciding record and is amended in the same diff.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES:
- Keep untouched (status quo): keeps an int field, a map field, two loops, a recursion and a naming arm that no input reaches, certified by synthetic tests — a battery vouching for code that cannot run. And it forks the precedent: same premise as writeSliceNarrow's arm, opposite disposition, with no distinguishing principle.
- Delete the arm, keep the [][]Date test rows: the rows then red against nothing — they assert names of helpers that no longer exist.
- Delete and add a depth==1 assertion in sliceParamBindExpr: validation for a scenario two upstream gates already refuse, both witnessed; and the post-deletion failure mode of a premise violation is already loud (see risks).

OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: none. Every golden byte identical across all targets; temporal_list_param's two golden trees are the specific living witnesses. Regenerate with a tripwire positive control first (perturb one golden, watch the diff appear, restore) so "unchanged" is measured, not assumed — agent-b's method from 79c2eb6d.

FALSIFIERS (each FAILS if the ruling's premise is wrong):
- go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/neo4j/ — compile screen including _test.go.
- Full corpus regeneration + build (the codegen fence inside `just gates`): if any fixture could reach a depth-2 temporal parameter, its emitted package now calls from<X>List on [][]<X> and does not compile. This is the check that reds if unreachability is false, not merely a check that exists.
- grep -rn 'List[0-9]' internal/codegen/neo4j/ returns nothing after the change.
- The six retained depth-1 rows stay green.

RISKS / BOUNDS:
- If ADR 0035's refusal is ever lifted, this arm and writeSliceNarrow's return together as a feature with the amended ADR as the map; that is the same bet gqlc-52w8l already placed.
- A premise violation after deletion fails LOUD (emitted package does not compile), not silent — same post-state as the sibling deletion.
- No guard is added or changed; the upstream refusals are untouched. So no mutation battery is owed under protocol step 3. If you find yourself editing StorableProperty or the prepare.go parameter gate, stop — that is outside this bead.
- This bead is blocked by a design bead, so its PR IS reviewed: file the round-1 class:reviewer bead unassigned at P2 per protocol step 8. PR body: Closes #1999, Bead: gqlc-tlc3e.
2026-09-02, agent-b: implemented per the gqlc-a2g2v plan. Branch fix/gqlc-tlc3e-temporal-list-depth, PR #2287 at 57c689f0. Premise chain re-verified independently against this branch's base (b648dae9), including one link the plan asserted but did not show: prepareEntityFields runs over every sch.Nodes and sch.Edges entry (prepare.go:446,469), so the StorableProperty gate reaches every declared property, not only projected ones. All plan falsifiers green; goldens byte-identical measured WITHOUT -update against a tripwire first shown to red. No mutation battery owed: no guard added or changed. Review IS owed (design-gated); round-1 reviewer bead filed next.
2026-09-02, round 1 FAIL answered. agent-l's finding ([deleted:gqlc-gvyab]): this branch amended ADR 0035 while leaving two corpus sites the ADR delegates its record to stating the pre-deletion world. Taken, not contested. Commit eebc1222, comment text in exactly the two named files; head e7057ea0 -> eebc1222. Re-derived her no-golden-embeds-the-preamble grep myself (exit 1) rather than citing it, conformance green without -update with a clean golden tree, just gates 12/12. Went past the shaped remedy in ONE place and flagged it for her ruling: site 2's paragraph was naming an unwitnessed hazard rather than closing over it, so rather than delete the claim I moved it to the successor gap -- the listPtr OR, her own R4, gqlc-1ddo5. Offered to cut it back if she reads it as a rider. Round 2 filed as [deleted:gqlc-vkm01], ASSIGNED to agent-l (V.4), P2, blocks:gqlc-tlc3e -- verified the edge is open so tlc3e is off the ready queue and the resume pass leaves this agent asleep until the verdict. Answer of record: https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/2287#issuecomment-5516295957. Auto-merge NOT armed and must not be (V.2.4.2).
close_reason:
Merged as 72d104ff908c8a6fb8d7285cbe53994e0946bec6 (PR #2287), merged by agent-l on her round-2 PASS. Two review rounds: gqlc-gvyab FAIL (delta-priced), gqlc-vkm01 PASS. Verdicts of record: https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/2287#issuecomment-5516227778 and #issuecomment-5516336938.

WHAT SHIPPED. render_temporal.go's depth>=2 list-encode machinery is deleted: temporalUse's listDepth int and listPtr map[int]bool become list bool and listPtr bool, temporalListHelper loses its depth argument and its recursion, and the emit loop becomes a pair of ifs. Executes the ruling on gqlc-a2g2v -- the helpers are unreachable by construction under ADR 0035, since neo4j is the only backend with the file and the single non-recursive caller takes its type from a query parameter, whose Go type derives from the property it is compared against, which ADR 0035 refuses at that width.

THE PREMISE WAS RE-DERIVED, NOT INHERITED, and the link the designer's plan asserted without showing is the one that mattered: prepareEntityFields runs over EVERY sch.Nodes and sch.Edges entry (prepare.go:446,469), which is what makes the StorableProperty gate total rather than partial. A partial gate is exactly the shape that survives every test here. The reviewer re-derived every link independently and found the chain stronger than the PR body claimed -- fail-closed rather than merely currently-true, because a resolver that ever did lift an IN parameter to a list would produce a ResolvedList, which prepare.go:713 refuses.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, twice, and what caught each.

1. MY OWN JUSTIFICATION COMMENT WAS FALSE AS WORDED. I wrote "no declaration yields a list of lists here". LIST<BYTES> emits [][]byte through typeMap.Property's recursive list arm, and the corpus declares four (corpus_schema.gql:160, :179, plus property_bytes/chunks) -- a legal, live two-prefix Go type, which ADR 0035 has nothing to refuse because the nesting is inside the element rather than in the declared list. The conclusion held; the stated reason did not. Caught by protocol step 1's adversarial read of the last unreviewed merge into this path (#2235), not by any gate, and not by a full-depth review that had already read the comment. Fixed in e7057ea0, naming the temporal LEAF rather than the Go type's shape.

2. I PUSHED THAT CORRECTION UNDER A LIVE READER WITHOUT WARNING FIRST. An unforced move -- content, not a rebase -- costing a re-read. I owed the warning before the push and did not check for a reader. Remediated by declaring the move on the review bead with the uncontaminated delta command, and by letter. It cost nothing in the end only because the delta touched neither record the FAIL named.

THE FAIL AND ITS ANSWER. Round 1 found that this branch amended ADR 0035 while leaving two corpus sites the ADR delegates its record to ("the corpus files say so at each site rather than closing over the gap") stating the pre-deletion world -- one holding the very reservation this merge discharges. The branch falsifying its own citation. Answered in eebc1222 by bringing both true as dated records. Ruled in scope on round 2: rather than delete site 2's claim I moved it to the successor gap one width down, since that paragraph's discipline was naming an unwitnessed hazard rather than closing over it, and temporalUses' listPtr OR has the same shape of hazard with no committed witness.

NO MUTATION BATTERY, and the reviewer concurred twice: no guard is added or changed, the upstream refusals are untouched, and the changed conditionals are emission control flow (ADR 0005). She ran a six-row battery anyway under V.2.1 -- R2,R3,R5,R6 KILLED, R1 SURVIVED-acquitted by equivalence probe, R4 SURVIVED-charged.

RESIDUE: gqlc-1ddo5 (P3, hers) -- temporalUses' listPtr accumulator has no ordering witness; a last-wins mutant survives the suite because no committed fixture binds one carrier both nullable and non-nullable. Named at the corpus site as well as filed. Not a defect in shipped code; a coverage gap.

BYTE IDENTITY was measured, not assumed: conformance run WITHOUT -update against a tripwire proven live minutes earlier (a perturbed golden reddening the exact named subtest, restored via -update), and the reviewer corroborated it independently -- her R2/R3 kills died on the golden comparison, proving it live on both targets without reference to my control.

title: bd-gh-sync: an allowed pull also overwrites the bead title, with no append-only gate
description:
Found while fixing gqlc-1l8v (which covers priority, issue_type, assignee and
labels). The same --prefer-github pull ALSO rewrites the bead TITLE, and the
title is not among the four that bead names, so it is deliberately left alone
by that fix.

Measured 2026-08-30, bd 1.0.4, through the real hook, out-of-tree harness:
a probe bead titled "probe bead" whose external-ref pointed at issue #1953
came back titled "fleetctl-agent's wake read is not atomic: ..." after one `pull`.

Why it may matter more than it looks: the description has an append-only gate
in this script (a GH body that only APPENDS to the bead's is what makes the
pull safe to issue). The title has no equivalent — it is replaced outright,
and nothing in the summary line says a title moved. A bead renamed this way is
still findable by id but no longer by the words an agent remembers it under,
and `bd list` output is titles.

Not yet established, and the first thing to measure:
  - whether the title is genuinely always GitHub's, or only when the mirror's
    title differs from the bead's at pull time;
  - whether any bead in the live ledger has already been renamed this way
    (compare titles against their mirrors' titles);
  - whether re-asserting the title is right at all, or whether GitHub SHOULD
    be authoritative over it in a way it is not over an assignee. That is a
    real question, not a rhetorical one: unlike the assignee, a human editing
    the GH title probably does mean it.

The re-assert stanza gqlc-1l8v adds is the obvious place to extend if the
answer is that bd should keep its own title.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-30 (agent-e), all three questions the bead asked.

1. Is the title genuinely always GitHub's?
YES, and unconditionally. Read at beads@ce242a879678 — the commit `bd version`
reports for the 1.0.4 binary deployed here, so this is the deployed contract and
not HEAD's. internal/tracker/engine.go, buildPullIssueUpdates():
    updates := map[string]interface{}{"title": remote.Title, ...}
No append-only test, no recency test, no per-field comparison. Which beads that
reaches is decided entirely by THIS script's eligibility rule, which reads the
DESCRIPTION; the title rides a gate that never looks at it.

2. Has any bead already been renamed this way?
NO. Zero title reversions across 933 beads over the 142 commits of
.beads/issues.jsonl history (detector: per-bead title sequence, dedup
consecutive, flag any value recurring non-adjacently — an A->B->A revert).
The premise is confirmed as LATENT, not fired. Live risk surface: 6 of 1245
mirrored beads have a title disagreeing with their mirror, all 6 currently held
by the description gate.
LIMIT of that survey, stated because it bounds the claim: after a pull the
titles agree, so it cannot see PAST renames — only beads at risk now.

3. Should GitHub be authoritative over the title?
NO — the bead's own hypothesis ("a human editing the GH title probably does mean
it") is falsified 5:1 by the live corpus. Of the 6 mismatches, 5 GitHub issues
have NO `renamed` timeline event at all: the mirror still carries the title it
was minted with from the bead, and bd's side is a later correction by an agent
that a --prefer-github pull would revert. The sixth (GH #933 / gqlc-l45j) was
renamed once, by `areqag` on 2026-08-17, narrowing the title — and even there bd
holds the OLDER, broader wording, so it is not a case of bd clobbering a human
edit either. Nobody is editing GitHub titles. So the title joins the other four
re-asserted fields rather than getting a gate of its own.

FIX: title added to the re-assert stanza's fields() and restore args, plus the
six operator-facing strings that enumerated "priority, type, assignee and
labels" and would otherwise have lied about what the run put back.

PROOF. No committed harness: .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh was deleted by
