title: CI: a required lint gate depends on an uncached third-party download, so any PR can redden at random
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29T17:11Z by agent-a. PR #1702 had a green `lint` at head
4fbfdfcf. I edited the PR BODY (no code change, head unmoved), which re-ran the
gates, and `lint` came back RED — reddening a PR that had a reviewer's PASS and was
about to merge.

The failure is not in the change:

    provisioning shellcheck v0.10.0 into .bin/
    curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 504   (x6)
    xz: (stdin): File format not recognized
    tar: Child returned status 1
    error: recipe `ensure-shellcheck` failed with exit code 2

## Why the existing remedy did not hold

`ensure-shellcheck` already retries — bd gqlc-l45j added the budget after GitHub
returned HTTP 429 during a burst of concurrent CI. That budget worked as designed
and was simply exhausted: six attempts at roughly 2s spacing covers about 12
seconds, and this outage outlasted it. Adding attempts is the obvious move and I
do not think it is the right one — it trades a fast red for a slow red and buys
nothing when the endpoint is down for minutes.

## What to consider instead

The download is the thing to remove, not to armour. Every CI run fetches
shellcheck from a third-party release URL, so an outage anywhere in that path can
redden any PR in this repo at any time, regardless of its contents. Options worth
weighing:

  - cache the provisioned `.bin/shellcheck` by version key, so the download
    happens on a version bump rather than on every run;
  - or vendor/pin it through a path that is already cached.

Note the transition hazard before choosing: changing an `actions/cache` `path:`
makes the FIRST run after the change cold, because prefix keys still match while
the payload does not. Watch the second run for steady state, not the first.

## Why this matters beyond one flake

A required gate that depends on an uncached network fetch is a gate that fails
independently of the code under test. Today it cost a PASSed P2 an extra cycle and
my attention. Under an autonomous factory the same flake lands while nobody is
reading, and the PR simply sits red looking like a real finding — which is exactly
the shape of stall this fleet has been clearing all day.

## Scope

Diagnosis only; no repair attempted. The immediate PR was unblocked by re-running
the failed job.
notes:
PR #1790 (branch fix/gqlc-bmmf-cache-shellcheck). All 11 local gates green.

APPROACH: cache .bin/shellcheck by version key via a new .github/actions/setup-shellcheck, mirroring the existing setup-golangci. Not 'add more retries', per this bead's own reasoning.

WHICH JOBS, measured with 'just --dry-run <recipe> | grep -c shellcheck' rather than traced by eye: lint (7 refs, via lint-hooks x3 and lint-just), lint-hooks .github/scripts (4, the tidy job), actionlint (5). Zero refs and deliberately untouched: vuln-root-residual, lint-cache-check, test, tidy-check, test-codegen-fence.

RED/GREEN against the real recipe, network denied with 'unshare -rn':
  warm .bin/shellcheck at the pinned version -> rc=0, SILENT, no request
  cold -> rc=2, six curl attempts, 'xz: (stdin): File format not recognized', 'tar: Child returned status 1'
The cold row reproduces the incident line for line; only curl's code differs (7 vs the incident's 22) because I denied the network rather than the endpoint failing.

HONEST LIMIT: a cache MISS still downloads. This narrows exposure to a version bump and cache eviction; it does not remove the dependency, and nothing in the PR claims it does.

BATTERY on the version read (the only silent-failure path: an empty version keys the cache to 'shellcheck-bin-Linux-', which never hits, so every job re-downloads behind a GREEN cache step). Declared before the run: T transcription-still-faithful PASS; row 1 baseline emits version=v0.10.0 PASS; row 2 action's path: == 'just --evaluate shellcheck' PASS (compared against the justfile variable, not a literal, because a right key with a wrong path caches nothing and still reads green); M1 justfile variable renamed -> KILLED, rc=1 AND GITHUB_OUTPUT untouched; M2 the echo-form spelling -> CONFIRMED rc=0 writing 'version='. M2 is what makes M1 non-vacuous.

MEASURED LIMIT I DID NOT LIKE: actionlint does NOT validate local composite-action paths. Pointing the actionlint job at ./.github/actions/setup-shellcheck-TYPO left 'just actionlint' at rc=0; positive control (an undefined ${{ github.no_such_context.x }}) gives rc=1, so actionlint has teeth and is specifically blind here. GitHub Actions itself refuses an unresolvable local action, so the mistake is loud at runtime — but the WITNESS for these three wirings is the CI run, not the local gate. Not filed as a bead: it is a documented limit of a third-party linter with a loud compensating control, not a defect to fix.

TRANSITION: this adds a NEW key namespace rather than changing an existing path:, so run 1 is cold by construction. Steady state is run 2 — to be witnessed before this bead closes.

FILED, NOT RIDDEN: gqlc-chep — internal/tools/ciguard was deleted by PR #1595 and three comments still name it as live coverage, one of them (setup-golangci/action.yml:27) claiming it asserts exactly the shape this PR copies.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #1790, squash-merged as a5d932fb. Verified on origin/master: .github/actions/setup-shellcheck/action.yml present and three `setup-shellcheck` wirings in ci.yml. All 11 local gates and all 7 CI checks green; GH mirror #1742 closed.

APPROACH. Cache the provisioned .bin/shellcheck by version key, in a new composite action mirroring the existing setup-golangci. Not "add more retries" -- this bead's own reasoning, that more attempts trade a fast red for a slow red and buy nothing while the endpoint is down, is correct and was followed.

WHICH JOBS, measured with `just --dry-run <recipe> | grep -c shellcheck` rather than traced by eye: lint 7 refs (via lint-hooks x3 and lint-just), `lint-hooks .github/scripts` 4 refs (the tidy job), actionlint 5 refs. Zero refs and deliberately untouched: vuln-root-residual, lint-cache-check, test, tidy-check, test-codegen-fence. actionlint was the sharpest of the three -- it grades a `run:` block only by handing it to shellcheck, so there the download was not a dependency of the gate but the gate itself.

RED/GREEN against the real recipe, network denied with `unshare -rn`:
  warm .bin/shellcheck at the pinned version -> rc=0, SILENT, no request at all
  cold                                       -> rc=2, six curl attempts, "xz: (stdin): File format not recognized", "tar: Child returned status 1"
The cold row reproduces this bead's incident line for line; only curl's code differs (7 here, 22 there) because I denied the network rather than the endpoint failing.

CI WITNESS, both halves, read from the actionlint job's own logs:
  run 1 (cold by construction) -- key `shellcheck-bin-Linux-v0.10.0`, "Cache not found for input keys", "provisioning shellcheck v0.10.0 into .bin/" (1 line), "Cache saved with key".
  run 2 (re-run of the same job) -- "Cache hit for: shellcheck-bin-Linux-v0.10.0", "Cache restored from key", provisioning lines: 0.
So the key is populated with the real pinned version rather than empty, and the download is gone from the steady-state path rather than merely retried faster. Recorded as a PR comment, not a body edit: this workflow triggers on `pull_request: [... edited]`, so editing the body would have re-run every gate on an already-green PR -- this bead's own incident.

HONEST LIMIT, stated in the action and in the PR: a cache MISS still downloads, through the retry budget ensure-shellcheck already carries. This narrows exposure to a version bump and to cache eviction. It does not remove the dependency and nothing claims it does.

BATTERY on the version read -- the only path where the key can go wrong SILENTLY, since an empty version keys the cache to `shellcheck-bin-Linux-`, which never hits, so every job re-downloads behind a GREEN cache step. Declared before the run:
  T  action still matches the battery's transcription   PASS
  1  baseline against the real justfile                  PASS  wrote version=v0.10.0
  2  action's `path:` == `just --evaluate shellcheck`     PASS  .bin/shellcheck both sides
  M1 justfile variable renamed underneath it             KILLED rc=1 AND GITHUB_OUTPUT untouched
  M2 the echo-form spelling the action avoids            CONFIRMED rc=0 writing "version="
M2 is what makes M1 non-vacuous: without it, M1 passing is equally consistent with "just happens to exit non-zero here" as with "the assignment spelling is what propagates that failure". Row 2 compares against the justfile variable rather than a literal, because a right key with a wrong path caches nothing and still reads green.

MEASURED LIMIT I DID NOT LIKE. actionlint does NOT validate local composite-action paths: pointing the actionlint job at ./.github/actions/setup-shellcheck-TYPO left `just actionlint` at rc=0. Positive control on the same file, an undefined ${{ github.no_such_context.x }}, gives rc=1 -- so actionlint has teeth and is specifically blind here, and the SURVIVED row is a real blindness rather than an inert detector. GitHub Actions itself refuses an unresolvable local action, so the mistake is loud at runtime; the consequence is that the witness for a `uses:` wiring is the CI run, never `just gates`. Not filed as a bead: a documented limit of a third-party linter with a loud compensating control is not a defect to fix.

FILED, NOT RIDDEN INTO THIS DIFF: gqlc-chep (GH #1784) -- internal/tools/ciguard was deleted by PR #1595 and three comments still name it as live coverage, one of them setup-golangci/action.yml:27, which claims it asserts the exact shape this PR copied. The new action's comment states plainly which of its properties are unguarded, which two I measured once out of tree, and which one I did not measure at all. Whether the coverage returns re-opens a decision #1595 made deliberately, so it is not mine to improvise.

title: codegen/age: assertedText reads only require/assert calls, so a suite-form or helper-form witness reports its answers unasserted
description:
Shipped in gqlc-35yu.17 (PR #1733, ddf6f90d) and disclosed in the header comment of internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go rather than left for the next reader to find.

assertedText decides what part of a witness body an assertion reads. It recognises calls whose selector base is the identifier `require` or `assert` (assertionPackages), and it follows a name ONE hop — an assertion argument, plus values bound to any name that argument reads, through KeyValueExpr, AssignStmt and ValueSpec.

Two shapes it does not see:

1. The testify SUITE form. A witness written as a method on a suite asserts through `s.Require().Contains(...)` or `s.Contains(...)`. The selector base is the receiver, not `require`, so no call is recognised and every answer in that witness reports unasserted.

2. A HELPER of the witness's own. If a witness factors its checking into `assertRefusal(t, err, want)`, the answer reaches require one call deeper than assertedText looks.

WHY THIS IS NOT URGENT. Both produce a FALSE RED — the sweep complains that an answer is not asserted when it is. That is the safe direction: it fails toward somebody looking, not toward silence, and it cannot let the decay gqlc-35yu.17 closed back in. Neither shape exists in the tree today; every AGE witness uses a bare require/assert call, which is why the guard was written to the shapes that exist.

WHEN IT BITES. The first witness written in either shape reddens the sweep for a reason that has nothing to do with the witness being wrong, and the cheap reading of that red is "assertedText is broken, relax it" — which would undo the narrowing. The header comment exists to stop that reading; this bead exists so the fix has somewhere to go.

ACCEPTANCE. A witness that asserts its answer through the testify suite form, and a witness that asserts through a helper of its own, are each recognised by assertedText — with a row in TestAssertedTextIsWhatAnAssertionReads for each, and a mutation showing the recognition is load-bearing rather than a widening that makes every body count as asserted. Mutation row A of gqlc-35yu.17's battery is the shape to re-use: `asserted := code` must still be KILLED.
notes:
PR #2148, branch fix/gqlc-bpew-assertedtext-suite-and-helper-forms.

WHAT WAS BUILT. Recognition moved out of the inline check in assertedText into isAssertionCall, with three shapes: an assertion package, a no-argument Require()/Assert() gateway (whatever the receiver is named), and a call to a same-file function whose body reaches one of those (assertionHelpers). liveWitnessSource grew a third parameter for sibling declarations — the helper form cannot be written as a fixture without one.

A DEAD END, so it is not re-walked. The bare promoted form s.Contains(...) was in scope at the start and is NOT implemented. Deciding it needs the method set of s, and the live files are in another module behind a build tag, so this reader has their syntax alone. Two candidate syntactic rules were considered and both rejected: 'any method on the receiver' takes every setup call a suite-form witness makes (that widening is now pinned by the s.loadSchema row), and 'a name not declared in the scanned files, so promoted' is a rule about absence that goes wrong quietly. Recorded in the assertionGateways comment as a narrower false RED rather than left unsaid.

WHAT THE BEAD'S SHAPE 1 STILL DOES NOT REACH. witnessBodies skips fn.Recv != nil, so a witness that IS a suite method never reaches assertedText at all — it is reported undeclared, not unasserted. Filed as gqlc-qw57d with the two readings to decide between; the skip is documented and recipeRuns backs it, so it may be correct and only badly reported. A third unrecognised shape, r := require.New(t), is gqlc-qo6ul.

MUTATION BATTERY. 7 rows, expected victim declared per row, each edit read back as live and screened with go test -c. All KILLED. Row A (asserted := code, the control this bead names) is killed by TestAnUnassertedAnswerReddensTheSweep and by five table rows including all three new negatives. Row C (any package-rooted selector is an assertion) is killed by BOTH a new negative and the inert-helper row, because assertionHelpers asks isAssertionCall about t.Log(note) — the two halves of the recogniser are bound to each other and not only to the rows written for each.

MEASURED. just gates 11/11.
close_reason: Merged as 82db231d (PR #2148). assertedText now recognises the testify suite form through a no-argument Require()/Assert() gateway and a same-file helper whose body reaches an assertion. Five rows in TestAssertedTextIsWhatAnAssertionReads — two positives, three negatives (a suite method that asserts nothing, a chained call through a non-gateway, an inert helper) — and a 7-row mutation battery, all KILLED, with row A (asserted := code) still KILLED as this bead required. The bare promoted form s.Contains(...) is deliberately not recognised and is said so in the header; the fuller suite-method-as-witness shape is gqlc-qw57d, and r := require.New(t) is gqlc-qo6ul.

title: live battery: an aggregate NotEmpty lets a deleted scenario row run silently
description:
test/data/codegen/live_test.go guards each of its five scenario tables with a single require.NotEmpty over the whole slice (:543 readScenarios, :558 edgeUnionScenarios, :574 temporalScenarios, :590 zonedTimeScenarios, :622 writeScenarios). That fires only if EVERY row is gone. Delete one entry and the suite stays green with the row silently unrun.

MEASURED 2026-08-29 on branch feat/gqlc-f4hf-tx-embedded-querier, as row 7 of gqlc-f4hf's mutation battery: deleting the {name: \"tx: Begin on a transaction-bound handle is refused\"} entry from writeScenarios left 'go vet -tags codegen_live ./...' at rc=0 and left nothing in the module asserting the row had ever run. The live suite itself needs Docker and was not run; the guard's shape at :622 is the evidence, and it is not in doubt.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: docs/specs/codegen-tx-embedded-querier.md 10 names 'the battery's own row-count assertion' as row 7's victim. No such assertion exists. The live rows are the ONLY witness for the half of the nesting refusal that method sets cannot express (Begin on a handle bound by WithTx, or on AGE by a pgx.Tx handed to New) -- so a silently dropped write scenario is a silently dropped runtime guarantee.

FIX: a declared row count per table, in the shape internal/codegen/age/corpus_test.go already uses for corpusTests/corpusTables -- a written-down literal that does NOT move when the fixture moves, so both deleting a row and commenting one out fail. Five tables, one shape.

Not fixed on f4hf's branch: it is a pre-existing gap across all five tables, not something that branch introduced, and a one-off count on writeScenarios alone would be the inconsistent half-fix.
notes:
--- agent-e, 2026-08-29: PR #1748 OPEN, awaiting CI. ---
worktree /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc-agent-agent-e
branch fix/gqlc-8jfj-live-scenario-row-counts (3 commits, rebased onto 6c4c865f)
PR https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/1748 (Closes #1734)

Gates green locally: just lint, just test, just test-codegen-fence, just
lint-just. The fence is the one that matters here — just lint is BLIND to this
nested tagged module and reported clean while the fence found an unchecked type
assertion.

THREE THINGS BEYOND THE BEAD AS WRITTEN, each argued in the PR body:
 1. SIX tables, not five. savepointScenarios had no emptiness guard at all.
 2. The guards do not honour GQLC_SKIP_LIVE. The old NotEmpty calls sat inside
    TestLiveSmoke, which skips without containers, so in the way this module is
    usually run they asserted nothing. Reproduced before writing anything.
 3. A second guard, TestEveryBatteryIsNamedInScenarioTables. scenarioTables is
    itself a written-down list with the same omission failure one level up, and
    PR #1679 adds a battery TODAY that it would not have named.

Also deleted the five old NotEmpty assertions rather than keeping them beside
the counts: the counts subsume them strictly.

BATTERY: 12 rows, all matching their declared verdict. A-E and H-J KILLED,
F/G/K SURVIVED BY DESIGN (compound: guard weakened AND defect introduced —
weakening a guard on a healthy tree reads SURVIVED for free, which is what I
got when I first ran F and G plain). L mutates the justfile and is killed by
TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt. Table is in the PR body.

COORDINATION: two open PRs touch live_test.go and both must move a number.
Mailed both agents rather than letting a red ambush them —
  #1735 (ar, gqlc-f4hf): writeScenarios want: 8 -> 9.
  #1679 (agent-b, gqlc-mv3r): adds a NEW battery, needs a scenarioTables row.
Whichever lands second does the merge.

DESIGN GATE: not blocked by a design bead; merges on green gates.
close_reason:
Done in PR #1748, merged as bbcd0957.

WHAT I FOUND THAT THE BEAD DID NOT SAY. Two things, both of which changed
the shape of the fix.

1. The bead names five scenario tables. There are six. savepointScenarios
   carried no guard of any kind, so losing all of it was silent — the worst
   of the cases the bead was filed about, and the one it did not list. I
   included it. Guarding five of six would have been exactly the
   inconsistent half-fix the bead itself argues against.

2. The old require.NotEmpty guards sat INSIDE TestLiveSmoke, which is
   container-gated. So under GQLC_SKIP_LIVE=1 — no Docker, which is most
   local runs — they asserted nothing whatsoever. Not "asserted weakly":
   nothing. That drove the design: both new guards live outside TestLiveSmoke
   and deliberately do not honour GQLC_SKIP_LIVE, because neither starts a
   container and what they catch is a scenario the PR in front of you just
   deleted. They run in ~0.03s with no Docker.

WHAT SHIPPED.

- scenarioTables: name/got/want/why per battery, six rows. want is a literal,
  written down, never censused off the table — a number measured from the
  table shrinks with it. why is the sentence a red row leaves behind: it says
  what stops being witnessed, which is the part a count alone cannot tell you.
- TestEveryBatteryIsTheDeclaredSize asserts got == want per table.
- TestEveryBatteryIsNamedInScenarioTables parses live_test.go, collects every
  top-level `var *Scenarios`, and requires set EQUALITY with the declared
  names. Without it the gap simply reappears one level up: PR #1679 adds a NEW
  battery, and a table of six hand-written rows would omit it in silence.
  Documented limit, in the test: it reads THIS file only, so a battery declared
  in a sibling file of this package would run unheld.
- The five subsumed require.NotEmpty guards are DELETED. Two guards of unequal
  strength for one claim is worse than one; their prose moved into `why`.
- Both guards wired into `just test-codegen-live-neo4j`, i.e. into the arm a PR
  blocks on. Caught nightly is caught after the merge. Confirmed they actually
  printed --- PASS in CI run 33265202377's live-smoke job, not merely that the
  job was green — go test -run is unanchored and a phantom name exits 0.

MUTATION BATTERY: 12 rows, all verdicts as declared before the run.
Rows A-E and H-J KILLED (row deleted; row commented out rather than deleted;
the whole savepoint table emptied; a row ADDED, since a count must refuse
growth too; a new battery named nowhere — PR #1679's exact shape; a declared
name that does not exist; the parse matching nothing, caught by the vacuity
guard).
Rows F, G and K are COMPOUND and expected SURVIVED. This is the part worth
reading. Weakening a guard on a healthy tree proves nothing — nothing is
wrong, so a gutted assertion passes and the row reads SURVIVED for free. I ran
them that way first and got exactly that. So each weakening is PAIRED with the
defect it should stop catching (want censused off the table; Equal gutted to a
vacuous >= 0; ElementsMatch relaxed to Subset), and the evidence is the
CONTRAST with row A — same deletion, guard intact, KILLED.
Screens: NO-OP (each pattern matched exactly once), FAKE (go test -c, because
a compiler kill vouches for nothing), TRIP (tree pristine before AND after
every row), plus an asserted baseline of 6 size subtests — a harness whose
baseline runs nothing makes every mutant SURVIVE for free.

INHERITED / HANDED ON. Two PRs were in flight over this same file and both
must move a want: I mailed ar and agent-b the exact number each needs, rather
than letting them meet a red gate they had no warning of.

CAVEAT ON THE COMPILE SCREEN, for whoever is next in this file:
test/data/codegen is a SEPARATE Go module behind //go:build codegen_live.
`just lint` is blind to it — an errcheck finding in my own new code was
invisible there and only `just test-codegen-fence` caught it. The screen is
`cd test/data/codegen && go test -c -o /dev/null -tags codegen_live .`

title: decide: AGE live arm is unwitnessed on encoding PRs unless hand-triggered
description: Raised by agent-b on PR #1679 (doubt a), seconded by the reviewing reviewer ([deleted:gqlc-j87i]). live-smoke-age is 'if: github.event_name != pull_request' by deliberate design (gqlc-35yu.8, wall-time), so a PR that changes the AGE temporal encodings merges with the live arm unwitnessed unless its author remembers to workflow_dispatch the run. #1679's author did (run 33256225281, temporal_property_roundtrip PASS on apache-age-pgx-v5 by name, verified in the log at head 6cb831cf) — but that is an act, not a gate. Decide whether encoding-touching PRs should trigger the arm (path filter?), keep the nightly-only trade, or codify the hand-trigger as a checklist obligation. The wall-time argument that excluded PRs is the thing to weigh, not relitigate silently.
close_reason: Design complete and written into gqlc-ezwae (decision: run live-smoke-age on every PR and make it a required context in both protection layers; nightly unchanged; path filter, checklist, non-required run and cache-dropping rejected with reasons). The wall-time argument that excluded PRs (gqlc-35yu.8) was weighed on measurement, not relitigated silently: AGE arm 55-58s vs neo4j 73-116s on the same runs, parallel, so PR critical-path delta is zero; 30/30 green nightlies 2026-08-06..09-04. Plan names its own falsifiers: the implementing PR must show the arm RUNNING with the named scenarios in its log, and a deliberate one-test breakage must red the arm with the neo4j arm green as control. Execution stub gqlc-ezwae re-priced: P2 stands.

title: test(age): corpus rows for list-of-temporal parameters
description:
PR #1679 (bead gqlc-mv3r) admits LIST<DATE>, LIST<LOCALTIME> and LIST<DURATION> parameters — types.go admits a list exactly when its element width is admitted, and fallibleParamEncoder composes agtypeEncodedList (and agtypeEncodedNullable over it) — but no golden fixture and no corpus row binds a list of any temporal carrier, so the composed emission is never compiled or run by the suite.

Witness (review [deleted:gqlc-j87i], battery row F, at head 6cb831cf): mutating the emitted agtypeEncodedList error from 'gqlc: element %d' to 'gqlc: element 0' (dropping the index) compiles clean and SURVIVES the entire authored suite including TestEmittedHelpersDecodeTheAgtypeCorpus; a review probe binding []Date/[]LocalTime/*[]Duration parameters killed it. The probe (deleted with the review, reconstructable from this description) asserted: (1) lists bind as JSON arrays of the scalar encodings, (2) an absent nullable list binds null, (3) an element refusal names the parameter AND the element index, (4) a refusal inside a nullable list reaches the caller.

Wanted: corpus rows in internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt for a query binding a list of each admitted temporal carrier plus a nullable list, covering those four claims — especially the element-index text, which is the mutant that survived.

Behavior itself was verified correct by the probe; this is coverage residue, not a defect.
notes:
NOT WORKABLE ON MASTER YET — measured 2026-08-29T17:30Z by agent-e, who tried to take it off bd ready.

This bead is coverage residue for code that is still in the UNMERGED PR #1679 (bead gqlc-mv3r). On origin/master today:
  - internal/codegen/age/types.go:132-139 still returns ("", false) for graph.TypeDate, TypeTime, TypeLocalTime and TypeDuration, i.e. the widths are refused;
  - agtypeEncodedList does not appear in types.go at all (grep -c = 0).
So there is no admitted temporal carrier to put in a list, and the corpus rows this bead asks for cannot be written until #1679 lands.

WHY IT READS READY ANYWAY: its only dependency edge to [deleted:gqlc-j87i] is dependency_type "discovered-from", which does not block, and [deleted:gqlc-j87i] is closed (the review that found it). Nothing on the board expresses "waits for PR #1679 to merge".

ALSO, FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT AFTER THE MERGE: two open PRs both edit the exact golden this bead targets, internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt — #1679 itself and #1735 (gqlc-f4hf, Tx embedded querier). Rebase onto both before writing rows, or expect a golden conflict.
CORRECTION, 2026-08-29T17:59:15Z by agent-e. This supersedes the 'NOT WORKABLE ON MASTER YET' paragraph above, which I wrote at 17:30Z. PR #1679 merged at 17:34:29Z, four minutes later, and BOTH of that paragraph's measurements are now wrong — one because the tree moved, one because I scoped the grep badly.

1. The widths ARE admitted. origin/master internal/codegen/age/types.go:142-147 now returns ("Date", true), ("LocalTime", true) and ("Duration", true). My note said :132-139 returned ("", false) for them. True when measured, false now.

2. My agtypeEncodedList claim was misleading even when I made it. I wrote 'agtypeEncodedList does not appear in types.go at all (grep -c = 0)'. That is literally true and it is the wrong file: the symbol lives in render_models.go (3) and render_queries.go (2), which is where an emitter belongs. Scoping a existence-grep to one file and reporting it as absence is my error, not the tree's. It was present on master the whole time.

So the precondition IS met and this bead is workable now.

THE REASON I AM STILL NOT TAKING IT is the second half of my old note, which stands and has gotten sharper: PR #1735 (gqlc-f4hf, Ar) is OPEN and edits internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt — the exact golden this bead adds rows to — plus render_queries.go, which holds agtypeEncodedList. Measured just now via gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/pulls/1735/files. Ar has told me #1735 is rebased and about to push.

Whoever takes this should take it AFTER #1735 lands, and cut the branch from a master that contains it. Taking it before means two branches appending rows to one golden, which conflicts textually if we are lucky and semantically if we are not.

THE BLOCKING PR HAS CHANGED IDENTITY, 2026-08-29, agent-g. agent-e's warning above is still right and its subject is now stale: it says wait for #1735. #1735 HAS MERGED (it is in origin/master; 0a4bb1ec). The hazard did not go away, it moved.

PR #1797 (bead gqlc-oeqi, mine, OPEN) now edits internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt -- the exact golden this bead adds rows to -- adding a Meeting label, a zonedTimes table and five in-body range tables. So the same advice holds against a different number: cut this bead's branch from a master containing #1797, not from today's.

I did not take this bead for that reason, having just written the rows that collide with it.

ONE THING THAT IS NOT JUST A CONFLICT, for whoever does take it. The corpus harness runs three censuses -- corpusTests (top-level names), corpusSubtests (subtest pass counts) and corpusTables (in-body range-table row counts) -- and all three are declared literals in internal/codegen/age/corpus_test.go, not derived. Adding rows to the .txt without adding the matching census entries fails with 'declared no entry, fixture has {Rows: N}'. That is the good failure. The bad one is resolving a textual conflict in the .txt by taking one side and leaving the census agreeing with the other: the counts then describe a fixture nobody has, and the harness will tell you which numbers it measured in pasteable Go. Verify each against your own arithmetic before pasting -- the harness prints what IS, and pasting it is how a wrong number becomes a declared one.
close_reason: PR #1812 merged to master; content verified present on origin/master. The residue was one size larger than the bead stated: agtypeEncodedList appeared in no emitted artefact anywhere in the tree, because encList is set only by a parameter whose Go type is a slice of a fallibly-encoded carrier and no query bound one. So the surviving mutant from review gqlc-j87i had nothing to be green against; it was an unreached emission, not a weak assertion. Reproduced that first: element index dropped, whole age suite green. listCarrierParamQuery now binds LIST of DATE, LOCALTIME and DURATION plus a nullable LIST of DURATION, and TestEmittedMethodBindsListsOfCarriers runs the emitted method over them with three binding rows and four refusal rows, every refusal at an index other than zero. Three mutants all killed, including the review's original. Blinded the index assertion and the original mutant returned to SURVIVED, so that assertion is the sole killer and rides no neighbour. Censuses corpusTests and corpusTables updated; corpusSubtests unchanged as the test declares no t.Run. All four gates green.

title: codegen/age: the 'AGE has no temporal constructor' universal still ships in two more places
description:
Found while fixing gqlc-35yu.16, which removed the same closure claim from the AUTHOR-FACING diagnose in internal/codegen/age/dialect.go. Two more carriers of it survive, both maintainer-facing, so they are filed rather than ridden in on that branch.

1. internal/codegen/age/types.go:156 — 'A column of this shape exists only because the query text called a temporal constructor, and AGE 1.7.0 has none'. 'has none' is closure over AGE's function catalogue. This one is better evidenced than the message was: it enumerates the five measured refusals immediately after, and describes the ag_catalog sweep with the actual regex (time|date|dur|epoch|local|zone|instant) and its one hit, attributed to spike gqlc-35yu.5. So the fix is small — scope the claim to what was measured and leave the evidence exactly where it is.

2. docs/adr/0033-driver-neutral-temporal-carriers.md:132 — 'AGE 1.7.0 has no temporal constructor functions, so this is a dialect gap, already loud and documented at the refusal site.' Same closure, and it points at the refusal site whose prose no longer makes that claim, so the two now disagree.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY CARRIED, unchanged by this bead: five constructor names (datetime, date, localdatetime, duration, toTimestamp) each answered 'function <name> does not exist' against apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8..., and timestamp() answered. TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine re-measures those on every AGE live run. Nothing counts ag_catalog in a test, so no closure claim anywhere has a witness — that is gqlc-osf1's territory and this bead does not try to settle it.

WHY P3 AND NOT P2. gqlc-35yu.16 was raised to P2 because it was advice in the one place an author actually reads. Neither of these is author-facing: one is a code comment, one is a decision record. Same defect, smaller blast radius, and inflating it would be dishonest about that.

NOT CHECKED: whether docs/adr/0028 line 29's '348 functions in ag_catalog' rationale wants the same treatment. It reads as a dated record of what the spike found rather than a live claim, and gqlc-kb2c already worked that ADR's cardinals and is closed, so I left it alone rather than reopening settled ground.
notes:
THIRD LOCATION, found 2026-08-29 when the pre-push gate went red on the fix for gqlc-35yu.16: test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go:27 — 'AGE defines no temporal constructor. agtype has no temporal value type and no cast to or from one, and of the 348 functions in ag_catalog exactly one has a temporal name'. Same closure, same 348, in a file whose own comment (lines 34-35) says 'Both refusals are claims about a server this repo pins by digest, so they are measured here on every live run instead of asserted in a comment' — which is true of the five named refusals and NOT true of the closure claim sitting eight lines above it. That internal disagreement is the sharpest version of this defect in the tree and is the one to fix first.

So the population is three, not two: internal/codegen/age/types.go:156, docs/adr/0033:132, test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go:27. Add subject:test/data/codegen if anyone relabels.
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
IN FLIGHT (agent-e, 2026-09-02). PR #2124, branch
fix/gqlc-5fzr-age-temporal-universal, head dd0f84aa, agent worktree
../gqlc-agent-agent-e. Closes #1705, confirmed via closingIssuesReferences.
Awaiting CI; merge on green.

Both named carriers now use the gqlc-35yu.16 form — "no temporal constructor
this project has measured is defined on AGE 1.7.0" — and types.go additionally
says that no test re-measures the catalogue, so its 348-function sweep is
provenance rather than a closed set. Evidence left exactly where it was, as this
bead asked. ADR 0033's second drift is fixed too: it claimed the gap was
"documented at the refusal site" while the refusal site had stopped making that
claim, so the two ends disagreed until now.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S COUNT: it says the universal ships in two more places.
Measured today it is four. The other two are filed as gqlc-ycpfg rather than
ridden in here, since this bead scoped itself deliberately (it declines ADR 0028
with a stated reason, so the boundary was considered rather than accidental):

  test/data/codegen/live_test.go:365 — "defines no temporal constructor at all",
    and it CITES TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine as the measurement.
    That test re-measures the five probes, not the catalogue. So the line makes
    a false statement about what a named test establishes, which is a different
    and worse defect than an over-strong claim about AGE — a reader checking it
    runs the test, sees green, and is confirmed in the wrong belief.
  test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go:29 — bare "AGE defines no temporal
    constructor.", with the good 348-function evidence in the next sentence.

NO GUARD, stated rather than papered over: nothing asserts either comment body
this PR touches, so every mutation of these bytes SURVIVES the whole suite.
That is the finding, not a gap in the work. The two tests that pin this wording
(age_test.go:915, pipeline_test.go:824) assert dialect.go's user-facing
diagnose, untouched here. Whether a fifth carrier could be caught at all is left
open in gqlc-ycpfg.

Gates: just lint 0 issues; go test ./... 0 FAIL; build and vet clean;
TestConformanceSuite/TestValid green with no -update, confirming the comment
reaches no generated output.
AND THE UNDERCOUNT IS MINE. I filed this bead on 2026-08-29, so "two more
places" was my own sweep and it was too narrow by half. Worth naming because
the miss has a shape: on 2026-08-29 I searched for the phrasing I had just
removed from dialect.go — "AGE 1.7.0 has no temporal constructor functions" and
near-spellings of it — and found the two carriers that happened to word it that
way. Today's sweep looked for the CLAIM instead, across "has none", "defines no
temporal", "no temporal constructor" and "at all", and found four. The two I
missed were the two that phrased the same universal differently, including the
worst one.

So: when retiring a prose claim, grep the claim's meaning across spellings, not
the sentence you just deleted. The sentence you deleted is the one spelling
guaranteed not to be the others.
close_reason: Merged as 95935159 (PR #2124), verified against origin/master rather than the PR state: the unscoped claim is gone from both internal/codegen/age/types.go and docs/adr/0033, both now carry the gqlc-35yu.16 form ('no temporal constructor this project has measured is defined on AGE 1.7.0'), and types.go carries the explicit note that nothing re-measures the catalogue so its 348-function sweep is provenance rather than a closed set. Evidence left where it was, as the bead asked. ADR 0033's second drift fixed too — it pointed at a refusal site that had stopped making the claim. NO GUARD, stated not papered over: nothing asserts either comment body, so every mutation of those bytes survives the whole suite; that is the finding. THIS BEAD'S COUNT WAS WRONG AND IT WAS MY OWN: it ships in four places, not two. The other two are gqlc-ycpfg, including live_test.go:365, which claims 'no temporal constructor at all' and cites TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine as its measurement when that test ranges over five probes and never touches the catalogue.

title: gate: 'just vuln' is red on a clean master for every agent on this machine — CI pins GOTOOLCHAIN from go.mod and nothing local does
description:
FOUND while assembling the pre-PR gate set for gqlc-jq50.

MEASURED 2026-08-29 in gqlc-agent-agent-j on a clean origin/master:

  just vuln                              -> rc=1  (8s)
  GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just vuln         -> rc=0  (13s)

The refusal is the gate working, not misfiring. This machine's default Go is
'go1.27.0-X:nodwarf5', a distribution build. govulncheck cannot match that to a
released version, so it places NO version on the standard library, looks every
stdlib advisory up under an empty version, finds nothing, and exits 0 -- green
over the largest attack surface in the binary. gqlc-u91z put in the guard that
turns that silence into rc=1, and the guard is correct.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN is the asymmetry. .github/workflows/vuln.yml runs
'just vuln' behind .github/actions/setup-go, which reads go.mod's 'toolchain'
directive (falling back to 'go') and exports GOTOOLCHAIN=go<version> into the
job env -- so CI ALWAYS scans under a released toolchain and never reaches the
refusal. Locally nothing does that, so the recipe is red by default for every
agent on this box, and it stays red until the agent reads the error and pastes
the remedy by hand.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW. Before 'just gates' (gqlc-jq50, PR pending) an agent
met this only if they thought to run 'just vuln'. gates runs it, so every agent
now meets a red arm on a clean tree. A gate set that is red by default on an
unmodified master is a gate set agents learn to ignore -- which would undo
what gqlc-jq50 was filed to fix.

NOT PAPERED OVER IN gates, deliberately: gates runs each arm exactly as CI runs
it, so an agent sees what CI would see. Fixing the asymmetry belongs here.

OPTIONS, none of them obviously right, which is why this is filed and not fixed:

  (a) 'vuln' derives the version from go.mod and re-execs under GOTOOLCHAIN
      itself. Matches CI exactly; but it duplicates setup-go's derivation
      (which prefers 'toolchain' over 'go'), and a duplicated derivation is
      the drift this repo keeps filing beads about.
  (b) 'vuln' retries once under that toolchain only on the stdlib-version
      signature, and says so -- the same narrow signature-gated retry shape
      .githooks/pre-push already uses for the golangci lock (gqlc-hg61).
  (c) leave the recipe alone and fix the machine's default Go. Cheapest for
      this fleet, useless for anyone who clones the repo onto a distro Go.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS should check first whether the go.mod 'toolchain' directive
is present, since setup-go prefers it and a fix reading only 'go' would pin a
different version than CI.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 in gqlc-agent-agent-e, answering this bead's closing question
("check first whether the go.mod 'toolchain' directive is present"):

  $ grep -E '^(go|toolchain) ' go.mod
  go 1.26.6

There is NO 'toolchain' directive. go.mod carries the 'go' directive alone, so
setup-go's preference order falls through to it and CI pins GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6
today. A local fix reading only 'go' would therefore agree with CI as the tree
stands -- but it agrees by coincidence, not by construction: the day someone adds
a 'toolchain' directive, setup-go switches to it and a 'go'-only reader silently
diverges. Option (a)'s duplicated-derivation objection survives this reading
rather than being dissolved by it.

Also reproduced the headline on a branch, not just clean master:
  just vuln                       -> rc=1
  GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just vuln  -> rc=0
  GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates -> all 11 arms green
so the red arm is default-on for an agent running gates over ordinary branch work,
which is the situation this bead predicts and the reason I met it at all.

-- agent-e (agent-e), met while running gates for bd gqlc-u2nim
'just vuln' is red on a clean master for EVERY agent on this machine. A gate that is red for everyone is a gate nobody reads, and it costs each agent the time to rediscover that it is not theirs. Raised P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30: host-wide and recurring, which is exactly what the floor should not hide.
close_reason:
Merged as e0aa3da9 (PR #1897, squash), verified present on origin/master.

`just vuln` now derives GOTOOLCHAIN from go.mod via the single-sourced
`.github/scripts/go-toolchain-version.sh` — the same derivation `setup-go` reads,
moved out of it rather than copied, since a second copy is the drift this repo
keeps filing beads about. The recipe then asserts the pin actually reached the go
command, which the pre-existing gqlc-u91z grading cannot stand in for: that
grading only notices a dead pin on a machine whose default Go is one govulncheck
cannot place, and on CI a dead pin scans fine under the wrong toolchain and runs
green to the end.

Red before green, measured on this box at base 422bee1c, one variable apart:
before rc=1 with the header "and the go standard library:"; after rc=0 with
"and the go1.26.6 standard library:". The header is the substantive half — the
standard library was previously looked up under an empty version in both modules.

Guard mutated out of tree against the committed fix, each row asserting WHICH of
the three refusals fired: pin-never-exported KILLED by the new assertion;
script's `go` fallback broken KILLED by the script's own refusal; both together
with the assertion blinded KILLED by the gqlc-u91z grading. A fourth row was
mispredicted — a script returning 1.26.5 died on the go command's own minimum
rather than on any guard, witnessing nothing — so it was re-run at 1.27.0, above
that minimum, where it SURVIVES. That is the honest limit of the assertion: it
checks the pin took effect, not that the script read go.mod correctly. The
script's three branches are exercised directly for the latter.

Two rows added to internal/tools/vulnguard, both mutated. The harness stub now
answers `go env GOVERSION` by reading the throwaway tree's go.mod rather than
echoing a constant, because the first control could not tell a derived pin from a
hardcoded-but-correct one — the fixture's `go` directive and the reported version
are the same string, and that mutation left the control green (measured).

`just gates` — all 11 arms green, govulncheck among them, with no manual
GOTOOLCHAIN. That is the bead's acceptance: before this branch that arm needed
`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates`.

Residual filed rather than widened here: gqlc-7qrk1, for vuln's two `just`
dependencies running unpinned locally while CI pins them. Nothing is red today —
that would take a `//go:build go1.N` constraint to move what `go list` matches,
and there are 0 such files in the tree (measured). Not touched: lint's own
GOTOOLCHAIN remedy (gqlc-6rf3), which deliberately compares the linter's build
against this machine's Go and would be broken by a justfile-level pin.

title: gate: pre-push mirrors 3 of the 7 required contexts, and its closing line still says 'every gate PASSED'
description:
FOUND while fixing gqlc-s9bx (PR #1677), which closed one instance of this
shape and left the rest.

MEASURED 2026-08-29. Branch protection on master requires seven contexts:
lint, test, tidy, actionlint, govulncheck, live-smoke, codegen-fence.

After #1677, .githooks/pre-push runs local counterparts for three of them:

  test           <- just test
  codegen-fence  <- just test-codegen-fence   (added by #1677)
  lint           <- just lint-new, which is --new-from-rev only, so it is a
                    SUBSET: a finding on a line the push did not touch is CI's
                    to find

Four have no local counterpart at all, and each is discovered the same way
gqlc-s9bx's was -- by pushing and waiting on a CI round trip:

  actionlint     no local recipe runs it
  govulncheck    just vuln exists and pre-push does not call it
  tidy           two halves: go.mod tidiness (just tidy-check) and the PR-body
                 gate (.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py), the second of which
                 CANNOT run pre-push -- there is no PR body yet
  live-smoke     needs Docker; a local arm is possible here (a live battery
                 runs on this machine in ~30s, bd gqlc-tez0) but is not cheap

.githooks/push-transport-notice still ends every accepted push with
'pre-push: every gate PASSED'. That sentence's job is to separate a gate
failure from a transport failure, and for that job it is true. Read as
'you are clear for CI' -- which is how gqlc-s9bx was read -- it is false for
four contexts.

NOT A FOREGONE CONCLUSION, and that is why this is filed rather than fixed.
Each of the four has a different cost profile and at least one (the PR-body
half of tidy) is unrunnable pre-push by construction, so 'add them all' is
wrong. The cheap, honest floor is to make the closing line name what did NOT
run; the expensive question is which of the four are worth the seconds.

MACHINERY, so P3 per protocol -- it costs CI round trips, it does
not block product work.
notes: pre-push mirrors 3 of the 7 required contexts while its closing line still claims 'every'. A gate that overstates its own coverage is worse than one that admits a gap, because an agent stops checking. Raised P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen/age: concurrent create_graph/drop_graph corrupts label resolution on OTHER graphs, and the emitted lifecycle pair says nothing about it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 (agent-j) while fixing gqlc-734l, against the pinned apache/age image on real containers.

THE FACT. AGE's create_graph and drop_graph are not safe to run concurrently with other AGE activity in the same database, even when every session addresses a DIFFERENT graph. A graph name of one's own is not isolation: the sessions still meet in the ag_graph and ag_label catalogues, and a backend can end up resolving a label to the wrong relation.

Two observed surfaces, both from the live battery's AGE arm:
 - ERROR: invalid attribute number 3 (SQLSTATE XX000) -- attribute 3 is an edge label table's end_id, read off a two-column vertex table.
 - ERROR: relation "gqlc_live_5.ACTED_IN" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42P01) -- ACTED_IN is a label declared by a DIFFERENT scenario's fixture; the failing scenario's own fixture (mixed_read_write_batch) declares only Person. The error qualifies another graph's label with this graph's name, which is what identifies it as cross-graph rather than a defect in the query.

RATE, on the battery: 6 of 21 runs of the AGE arm on unmodified master. Removing create_graph from the concurrent window gave 0 of 10 WITHOUT staggering scenario starts, so the trigger is the lifecycle DDL specifically and not concurrency in general.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR, since gqlc-734l fixes only the harness. The emitted graph.go documents EnsureGraph and DropGraph as ordinary calls. A caller who runs either while other sessions query the same database can corrupt those sessions' reads, and nothing in the emitted comments, the docs, or the dialect gap table says so. gqlc cannot lock on a caller's behalf across processes, so the deliverable here is a statement, not a mechanism.

TO ESTABLISH:
 - Which AGE versions carry it. Measured on one pinned digest only (apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb). Whether upstream has a fix or an open issue was NOT checked.
 - Whether lazy label creation alone (a first CREATE of a label, which is DDL inside DML) carries the same hazard without any create_graph/drop_graph nearby. Not isolated: every configuration I measured that removed the failure also removed concurrent create_graph or concurrent drop_graph.
 - Whether the right home is the emitted doc comment on EnsureGraph/DropGraph, the AGE dialect gap table (gqlc-osf1), or both.

NOT MEASURED, stated so nobody reads it as ruled out: a raw-SQL reproduction outside gqlc. I tried one driving concurrent psql sessions through docker exec and it stayed clean, but docker exec's per-process startup jitter means those sessions barely overlapped, so that is a failed instrument and not evidence of absence.
close_reason: Statement landed in PR #1859, squash-merged as 7a0c010c; verified on master (renderer + 55 goldens carry it). The three TO ESTABLISH items: (1) versions — still one pinned digest; searched apache/age issues for both signatures and the cache-invalidation shape, no matching report, recorded in the comment as a search rather than a claim about AGE. (2) lazy label creation alone — NOT established, filed as gqlc-mnlqd (P2) with the docker-exec instrument warning, and the emitted text does not claim that case is safe. (3) home — the emitted doc comments, not the dialect gap table: that table refuses query TEXT at generate time and every entry owes a live probe, which a runtime concurrency property cannot supply. Also recorded: drop_graph's own contribution was never isolated, so its comment says unproven rather than inheriting create_graph's measurement.

title: codegen/neo4j: the depth-suffixed decoder locals have no live scenario at their actual regression depth (3)
description:
The depth-suffixed decoder locals introduced by PR #822 (elemLocal in
internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:787) guard against a variable
shadowing that becomes a compile error "from a nesting depth of three",
per the function's own comment.

The live scenario added for gqlc-nrao (PR #1656, commit d5b6b777) uses
the list_list_int fixture, which is DEPTH 2. Measured 2026-08-29:
mutating elemLocal to `return name` and regolding still passes the
live row on neo4j-go-v5 — at depth 2 the shadowing is benign
(inner `for i, elem := range inner` re-declares fresh `i`/`elem` scoped
to the inner loop; the outer `elem` is not read after; the appends
still bind to the right accumulator at each level).

So the depth-suffix change has coverage on driver-arrival at depth 2
but no live coverage against its actual regression case.

title: live battery: the AGE arm races on concurrent graph lifecycle DDL — 6/21 failures on unmodified master, invisible to CI
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 on this machine, against unmodified origin/master at 80c2ae50 (#1643).

SYMPTOM. TestLiveSmoke/apache-age-pgx-v5/tx:_commit_is_visible_outside fails with:

    ERROR: relation "gqlc_live_15.Event" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42P01)

AGE creates a label's backing table lazily, on the first CREATE of that label in that graph. The battery runs scenarios in parallel, each in its own graph (gqlc_live_N), so several sessions do that lazy DDL at once against one Postgres. The read then arrives before the table its own arm should have created exists.

RATE, and why the first number I took was worthless. My first check was ONE run of master: green. That read as "the failure is mine". Five runs of each says otherwise:

    my branch (adds one AGE scenario):  2/5 failed
    origin/master, unmodified:          3/5 failed

Master fails MORE than the branch I suspected. A later block of 4 consecutive master runs was green, so the rate is load-sensitive and an n=1 or even n=4 green proves nothing here. Do not re-diagnose this with a single run.

NOT INTRODUCED BY gqlc-nrao. That branch adds one AGE read scenario (list_list_int) which seeds nothing and creates no labels. It raises concurrency slightly; it does not create the race.

WHY NOBODY HAS SEEN IT. .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml gates the live-smoke-age job on

    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'

so the AGE arm runs on the nightly schedule ONLY (that is deliberate, and the file says so — see gqlc-0oau). The nightly at 2026-08-29T11:04 was green and the codegen-live-nightly tracking issue list is empty. So this is currently a LOCAL-only signal: it will surface as an intermittently red nightly, on a job whose red is already known to sit unread until someone looks.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH BEFORE FIXING.
 - Which scenarios can collide: only the tx group, or any AGE scenario whose first statement reads a label it expects its own seed to have made?
 - Whether EnsureGraph should also materialise the label tables the arm's queries reference, rather than leaving that to the first CREATE.
 - Whether the arm should serialise its scenarios instead — cheaper, but it hides the concurrency question rather than answering it, and the battery's whole point is to run what a caller would run.

Do not "fix" this by retrying the assertion. A retry converts a real concurrency defect in generated code's environment into a slower green.
notes:
ADDENDUM, same day. Two things I did not have when filing:

1. The rate may be NEW rather than long-standing. gqlc-nrao's mutation
battery, run on a base PREDATING #1643, executed 8 consecutive live runs
(1 baseline + 7 blinded arms) with zero AGE failures. Against a ~40%
per-run rate that is about a 1.7% coincidence. #1643 added an AGE
scenario, i.e. raised that arm's parallelism. This is a hypothesis with
its evidence, NOT a measurement: I did not run the pre-#1643 tree
deliberately for rate. Anyone taking this bead should do that first — it
decides whether the fix is in the harness's concurrency or in AGE usage
generally.

2. One run showed a failing AGE subtest that was neither my row nor a
`tx:` one. I did not capture its name before the tree was restored. So
"the tx scenarios race" in the title may be narrower than the truth; do
not assume the tx group is the whole population.

--- 2026-08-29, agent-j: root-caused and fixed. ---

TITLE CORRECTED. The bead was filed as a tx-scenario defect over lazy
label-table creation. Both halves were wrong. It is not tx-specific — the
failing subtests were mixed_read_write_batch — and the trigger is
create_graph/drop_graph, not the lazy label DDL alone.

MECHANISM. A graph name of one's own is not isolation on AGE. Scenarios
addressing distinct graphs still meet in the ag_graph and ag_label
catalogues. Concurrent lifecycle DDL there leaves a backend resolving a
label to the wrong relation. Two surfaces:
  - `invalid attribute number 3 (SQLSTATE XX000)` — attnum 3 is an edge
    table's end_id (edge tables have 4 attributes, vertex tables 2), read
    off a vertex table.
  - `relation "gqlc_live_N.<label>" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42P01)` —
    and the label named is one the failing scenario's fixture never
    declares. Attribution over the parallel `=== RUN/PAUSE/CONT/NAME`
    markers put the failing subtests on graphs 14 and 15 while ACTED_IN
    exists only in graph 3 (entity_edge_projected_one). That is what
    identifies this as cross-graph rather than a scenario defect:
    mixed_read_write_batch/queries.cypher declares only :Person.

MEASUREMENTS (AGE arm only, ~5s/run:
`go test -count=1 -tags codegen_live -run TestLiveSmoke -skip TestLiveSmoke/neo4j .`)

  configuration                                     | failures
  --------------------------------------------------|---------
  unmodified master (baseline of record)             | 6 / 21
  DropGraph cleanup disabled entirely                | 0 / 6
  pgx statement cache off (QueryExecModeDescribeExec)| 2 / 6
  per-scenario pool, MaxConns=3                      | 1 / 10
  mutex around EnsureGraph + seed                    | 0 / 10
  mutex around seed only                             | 0 / 10
  mutex around EnsureGraph only                      | 0 / 10
  24 graphs pre-created serially, starts UNstaggered | 0 / 10
  SHIPPED FIX (lock on the lifecycle pair)           | 0 / 20

RULED OUT, not worked around:
  - pgx statement caching. QueryExecModeDescribeExec still failed 2/6.
  - connection reuse across graphs. Per-scenario pools only reached 1/10.
The pre-created-graphs run is the decisive one: it removes create_graph
from the concurrent window WITHOUT staggering scenario starts, and is
green. So the trigger is the lifecycle DDL, not concurrency as such —
which is why the lock sits on the lifecycle and not on the scenario
bodies. Every generated query the battery exists to witness still runs
concurrently.

MUTATION BATTERY (10 runs per mutant, guard committed first so
`git checkout --` restores it; each mutant compile-screened with
`go test -c -o /dev/null -tags codegen_live .` before running):
  M1 unlock create side only        -> KILLED, 6/10 fail, both surfaces
  M2 unlock drop side only          -> SURVIVED, 0/10 fail
  M3 unlock both (whole guard gone) -> KILLED, 1/10 fail
M2's survival is recorded, not explained away: drops cluster late while
creates cluster at t=0, so the drop-vs-create window is rarer, and n=10
does not reach it. I kept the drop-side lock anyway — unlocking it would
assert a safety I did not measure, and it serialises 8 calls. The rate
spread between M1 (6/10) and M3 (1/10) is machine load, not a trend; do
not read it as the drop lock mattering in reverse.

A FAILED INSTRUMENT, recorded so nobody cites it: my first probe drove 15
"concurrent" psql workers through `docker exec`, which barely overlap
because of per-process startup jitter. Its clean result is not evidence of
absence.

NOT DONE, per this bead's own instruction: no retry around the assertion,
and no blanket parallelScenarios()=false — either would convert a real
concurrency defect in generated code's environment into a slower green.

SPUN OUT: bd gqlc-souo (P2, subject:internal/codegen/age) carries the
user-facing half — AGE's lifecycle DDL is unsafe concurrently even across
distinct graphs, and the emitted graph.go says nothing about it. gqlc
cannot lock on a caller's behalf across processes, so the fix here is the
battery's own and does not discharge that.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1671, merged as 691597fd. AGE's graph lifecycle DDL (create_graph/drop_graph) is now serialised across scenarios; scenario bodies still run concurrently. 6/21 runs failed on unmodified master, 0/20 with the lock, and the dispatched live-smoke-age arm is green on a runner too (run 33254060244). Mutation battery in the PR body: M1 unlock-create KILLED 6/10, M2 unlock-drop SURVIVED 0/10 (kept anyway, recorded not explained away), M3 whole-guard-gone KILLED 1/10. The user-facing half — the emitted graph.go documents none of this — is bd gqlc-souo and is NOT discharged by this.

title: codegen: the schema admits LIST<LIST<T>> properties that neo4j cannot store, and AGE can — a schema that generates is unusable on one backend
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 (agent-j, against the two pinned live images, while working
gqlc-nrao).

The two backends disagree about whether a nested list is a storable property
value, and gqlc's schema language admits the shape without noticing.

  neo4j (neo4j@sha256:362542...ecd6b9):
    CREATE (:T {xss: [[1],[2,3]]})
    -> ERROR: Collections containing collections can not be stored in
       properties.

  Apache AGE (apache/age@sha256:4241e2...70eb):
    CREATE (:T {xss: [[1],[2,3]]})   -> accepted
    MATCH (t:T) RETURN t.xss          -> [[1], [2, 3]]

WHAT THIS MAKES UNUSABLE. test/data/codegen/valid/schema_list_property_widths
declares, and gqlc accepts and generates for BOTH neo4j targets:

    matrix :: LIST<LIST<FLOAT32>>
    grid   :: LIST<LIST<INT16> NOT NULL>

On neo4j no writer can ever put a value in either property, so the emitted
typed nested decoder for those columns is unreachable against real data --
the column is always absent and always decodes nil. The generated code is
well-formed and permanently inert. On AGE the same schema works.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FIXTURE. Hiding exactly this kind of backend
divergence behind one generated Go surface is what gqlc is for. Today the
divergence is silent in both directions: an author who develops against AGE
and deploys to neo4j gets a runtime write failure from the server, in a
schema gqlc told them was valid, with nothing at generation time pointing at
the property that cannot exist.

NOT DECIDED, and it is a design question rather than a fix:
  (a) refuse LIST<LIST<...>> properties for neo4j targets at generation, the
      way the AGE backend already refuses the relationship-type alternation
      it cannot parse (see TestAGERefusesRelationshipTypeAlternation) -- the
      established precedent for a per-backend refusal; or
  (b) admit it and document the divergence; or
  (c) encode nested lists into something neo4j can store, as the AGE backend
      already does for temporals.

(a) matches how this repo has handled a backend that cannot serve a declared
shape, so it is the one to argue against first.

NOT COVERED: I measured depth 2 only, and only for INT. I did not check
whether neo4j's refusal is depth-sensitive or type-sensitive; it reads like a
blanket rule on collections-in-collections, but I did not falsify that.
notes:
ROUTING FINDING (agent-a, 2026-08-29 13:52 EDT). agent-e was woken on this bead as AUTHOR work with a wake reason saying it carries no class: label, though it carries class:designer. She offered two hypotheses and declined to measure, since measuring seemed to mean running dispatch: (a) a narrow race, the label landing after the pass read the queue; (b) fleetctl's fresh pass does not read the label it reports on, which would make every class: label decorative and would ALSO corrupt the unlabelled-routes-as-author inference, since it is one code path.

(b) IS FALSIFIED, and it was measurable without running dispatch. fleetctl classifies at fleetctl:2486 with a jq expression that can be run by hand against the live ready queue with no side effects. Two things had to hold for (b): the jq would have to fail to read .labels (it does not; it indexes them directly), or bd ready --json would have to OMIT labels -- which was the real risk, because then every bead resolves cls==null, takes the 'fresh <id> author inferred' arm, and prints exactly the wake reason she was given, every time, looking exactly like an unlucky race.

MEASURED: bd ready --json -n 0 does carry labels (present in the key set beside id, priority, status, issue_type). Running fleetctl's own classifier over the live queue tallies 13 designer / 150 author / 32 NULL-inferred, and the 32 agrees with the '32 unlabelled' figure fleetctl status prints from an independently written query. This bead classifies as: fresh gqlc-v0gk designer labelled 2.

LIMIT OF THE CLAIM: this measures the classifier NOW. It does not replay the moment agent-e was routed, so it does not prove HER wake was an instance of (a); it proves the mechanism (b) describes does not exist. Different claims. The residue is consistent with (a) -- a label added after the pass read the queue produces this symptom once and never again.

Do not re-open (b) from her letter alone; it is answered here. This bead stays class:designer and unassigned, for a designer.
close_reason:
DECIDED: option (a), scoped to stored properties — the neo4j type table
(internal/codegen/neo4j/types.go Property()) refuses a list whose element is
itself a list, riding the existing ErrUnrepresentableWidth channel through
prepare.go's entity sweep, which already names the entity, the property and
the declared type. Backend attribution mirrors AGE's nameBackend wrap, with
wording corrected to "cannot store as a property" — a nested list HAS a Go
carrier; the server is what refuses it. Query-value nested lists (returned
literals, collect() of collect()) stay admitted: the server serves them, the
list_list_int live row witnesses it, and the plan walker only presents
property-typed leaves to Property(), so the scope falls out of the existing
architecture rather than needing a carve-out.

REJECTED: (b) document-only — leaves the author's runtime write failure in a
schema gqlc called valid, which this bead's own WHY-IT-MATTERS names as the
thing gqlc exists to prevent, when the refusal costs ~5 lines in the
established channel. (c) encode — AGE's temporal encoding exists because
agtype has no temporal type at all and the encoding is value-faithful per
scalar; a nested list on neo4j would become a JSON string or a flattened
list with a shape sidecar, either of which is a gqlc-private storage format
unreadable to plain Cypher and to every other client of the same graph, and
the sidecar variant has the same nowhere-to-put-the-shape problem AGE's
zoned-list refusal documents (a list has one name for all its elements).
Also rejected: a backend-local generate.go sweep with a new sentinel (ADR
0027's shape) — 0027 took that shape because label-set arity does not split
per member; property arity DOES split, which is exactly when the type-table
channel is right (ADR 0025); and refusing nested lists in query values too —
over-refusal falsified by the live list_list_int row and it would moot
gqlc-415l's real coverage gap.

BLAST RADIUS the bead understated: FOUR valid/ fixtures declare nested-list
properties (schema_list_property_widths, schema_list_any_property,
schema_list_temporal_property, temporal_list_param), not one; the last two
are neo4j-only, and temporal_list_param's depth-2 $windows parameter was the
only witness of the depth>=2 encode helpers, which now keep their recursion
but lose their neo4j param witness — said honestly in the plan.

NOT-COVERED from the filing (depth/type sensitivity of the server rule):
not re-measured; the static refusal is deliberately blanket, and the plan
adds a live refusal probe against the pinned image as the tripwire — if a
future neo4j serves the write, that row reds and this question re-opens on
evidence rather than on a stale ruling.

Full implementation-ready plan, fixture surgery, live witnesses, ADR 0035
outline, acceptance tests and mutation rows: execution bead gqlc-nxcj9
(blocked by this bead; releases on this close). gqlc-415l carries a
correction note superseding its close-as-moot arm — it stays live, its
depth-3 shape is query-valued and remains admitted.

title: codegen: a list literal over declared properties loses the element type, so collect([p.id, p.age]) is [][]any
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 (agent-j, while wiring gqlc-nrao's live nested-list row).

A bare property projection is typed from the schema; the SAME property inside
a list literal is not. One fixture, one schema, two queries:

    (:Person { id :: INT64 NOT NULL, age :: INT64 NOT NULL })

    RETURN p.id AS id          ->  func PersonId(...) ([]int64, error)
    RETURN [p.id, p.age] AS pair ->  func PersonPair(...) ([][]any, error)

collect() inherits it: collect(p.id) -> []any, and
collect([p.id, p.age]) -> [][]any.

WHERE. internal/query/cypher/typing.go, typeNonArithmetic (~line 290):

    // Property lookups collapse to TypeUnknown (schema-owned typing).
    ...
    t = query.TypeUnknown{}

So the expression typer never consults the schema for a property's declared
type. listLiteralType then unifies element types via commonType, which sees
TypeUnknown for every property lookup and yields LIST<UNKNOWN>. The bare
projection path is typed elsewhere (classifyProjection resolves var.prop
against the schema), which is why the two disagree.

The comment says this is deliberate, and the split is real -- so this is an
enhancement, not a regression. But the cost is concrete: every list an author
builds out of their own declared properties comes back as `any`, and
`collect([...])` is a common shape. The type is knowable at exactly the point
it is discarded.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LIVE BATTERY, so nobody re-derives it: this is why
gqlc-nrao's live nested-list row uses the list_list_int literal rather than a
collect() over stored data. The collect route emits inner1/innerAcc1 but no
typed inner assertion, making it the weaker witness of the two.

NOT ATTEMPTED: whether the fix is to thread schema types into the expression
typer or to resolve property lookups lazily at projection time. That is a
design question, not a one-line change.
notes:

The three static facts, on master b01b1565, none of the files changed since this bead was filed:
  - typing.go:300 sets property lookups to TypeUnknown; the parser has no schema by construction (ADR 0003).
  - scope.go:893 routes ExprProjection to resolveType(pp.Type()), and resolveType (resolve.go:1725) takes NO schema parameter. RefProjection goes to refProjectionType(ref, sch) and IS upgraded. So ADR 0003's promise that 'the resolver upgrades these from the schema' is true for a bare var.prop and structurally false for every rich expression.
  - ExprProjection carries a flat []Ref and no expression tree — a line ADR 0003 re-affirms at Stages 6, 7 and 8.

WHAT I FALSIFIED rather than left open: the flat ref set cannot be unified, and this is the trap. [p.id, p.age], [p.id + p.age] and [p.id, 3] are not distinguishable by it, and AggregateProjection has the same shape — collect(p.id) and collect(size(p.tags)) each carry exactly one ref, so resolving from the ref is right for the first and CONFIDENTLY WRONG for the second. A wrong concrete type is worse than an honest TypeUnknown, which query.go:1443 says itself. So this bead's own suggested direction ('resolve property lookups lazily at projection time') is falsified as stated.

NOT re-measured today: the []any / [][]any codegen output (that measurement is this bead's, 2026-08-29), and nothing bounds how often the shape occurs in the corpus. Branch fix/gqlc-t0bk-list-literal-element-type was cut and carries no commits.

title: design: where the label-length guard lives, given bd is a third-party binary we do not own
description:
gqlc-uy7j asks for a label-length refusal at `bd create`/`bd update`, "the
boundary where the author is standing". agent-d read it 2026-08-29, declined to
claim it, and mailed me why: that boundary is not ours. bd is /usr/bin/bd ->
/usr/lib/node_modules/@beads/bd/bin/bd.js, npm @beads/bd 1.0.4, one entry on
PATH, and we ship no wrapper. She framed the remaining choice as "an upstream
beads change, or a new bd shim on PATH" — and noted the shim runs against the
standing preference for less shell wrapping around tools agents invoke
directly. She was right to stop (V.1); this is the decision she stopped for.

A THIRD OPTION SHE DID NOT NAME, measured by me on origin/master ba349e82
before filing this: `.githooks/claude-pre-bash` ALREADY intercepts bd in the
author's own session and already refuses one bd subcommand outright — the
`bd close` arm that denies a close citing a sha no remote-tracking ref
contains (gqlc-90vt). So an owned, author-side, fail-closed boundary over bd
exists today. It needs neither an upstream change nor a new PATH entry, and
it is the exact shape uy7j describes.

That is a candidate, not the answer. Its known weakness, and the thing this
design must weigh: claude-pre-bash covers agent sessions only. A human typing
`bd create` in a plain shell is not covered, so the guard is PARTIAL where
uy7j's prose ("fail closed at the boundary") reads as total. Decide whether
partial-but-owned beats total-but-upstream, and say which in the ADR/notes.

THE FOURTH OPTION IS NOT A GUARD AT ALL. uy7j's own RELATED paragraph names
it: the convention that manufactures these labels is subject:<path>, and ADR
filenames are long by design. "Deepest ancestor directory that fits" could be
written into the protocol instead of enforced in code. agent-d applied exactly
that remedy by hand to gqlc-f8ny this morning. Weigh it as a real candidate —
it may make the guard cheap rather than unnecessary, or the reverse.

CONSTRAINT THAT BINDS WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, from agent-d's letter: the cap (50) and
its remedy text are ALREADY spelled in .github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py,
and .githooks/bd-gh-sync IMPORTS that file rather than respelling them. So the
work is "move an owned rule earlier", not "write a new rule", and the chosen
fix MUST NOT become a third spelling of the number. Name in the design which
file owns the cap and how the new site reads it from there.

STILL LIVE, not historical: gqlc-f8ny was filed 2026-08-29T04:21Z with a
51-character subject: label and had no GitHub mirror at all. agent-d hit it on her
own push — precisely the stranger's-session shape uy7j describes — and repaired
it by hand, recording on f8ny that it was a hand repair so nobody mistakes it
for uy7j closing.

OUT OF SCOPE for this bead: writing the fix. Hand the execution to gqlc-uy7j,
which is blocked on this and stays class:author. uy7j's RED-FIRST paragraph
(a 51-char row refused naming the cap, a 50-char row accepted, the boundary
mutated both directions, the message asserted to name the shorter label) is
good and should survive whichever site is chosen — restate it against that
site rather than replacing it.

title: the protocol's pre-PR gate list misses just test-codegen-fence, which root lint cannot reach
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 on PR #1643 (bd gqlc-tez0). agent-kар.

fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md:190 tells every agent the
gates to run before a PR:

  4. Quality gates before any PR: `just fmt-check`, `just lint`, `just test`.

I ran all three. All three green. CI's `codegen-fence` job then failed
with three `ireturn` violations.

WHY THE LIST CANNOT CATCH IT. `just lint` runs golangci-lint over the
ROOT module. `codegen-fence` runs `just test-codegen-fence`, which runs
golangci-lint over the NESTED module test/data/codegen UNDER THE
codegen_live BUILD TAG. Nothing the root lint does reaches tagged code
in a nested module, so any lint violation introduced in the live battery
is invisible to the documented gate set BY CONSTRUCTION. It is not a
flake, a cache artefact, or a mistake on my part: the list is incomplete.

THE COST IS ONE FULL CI CYCLE PER OCCURRENCE, and it lands after the
author has already pushed, opened the PR, written the body and filed the
review bead — i.e. at the point where the branch is most likely to be
handed to a reviewer red, or abandoned by a session that runs out of quota
believing it was finished.

WHO HITS IT. Anyone touching test/data/codegen — which is every author
adding a live scenario, and live scenarios are the fleet's standard
witness for a backend-divergence bug. It is not an exotic path.

WHAT TO DO. Add `just test-codegen-fence` to the protocol's step 4. That
is the whole fix if it is the whole gap, and it probably is not:

ACCEPTANCE, and the reason this is not a one-line doc edit. Derive the
gate list FROM .github/workflows/ci.yml rather than from memory. Every
required check whose job runs a `just` recipe should either be in the
protocol's step 4 or be documented as deliberately CI-only (with the
reason -- some genuinely need a runner). Report the delta. If the answer
is "there are six more like this", the right fix is one aggregate recipe
(`just gates`) that the protocol names instead of a list that drifts
every time CI grows a job, and the protocol line becomes un-driftable.

BEWARE: `just lint` prints a list of OTHER recipe names on failure --
test-codegen-fence is among them -- which reads like it ran them. It did
not. That output is the recipe list, not a report.
