Delta derived from branch protection (7 required contexts) + ci.yml/vuln.yml, not from memory: protocol named 3 recipes, 6 of the 7 contexts are reachable locally across 11 arms. Two corrections vs my first memory-derived list: fmt-check is NOT a CI job (formatters are enforced by golangci-lint run inside just lint, gated by check-golangci-formatters-report), and the tidy job has 7 steps not 3 — check-label-lengths.py is fully local and was missing. 7-row mutation battery in the PR body; R7 (delete an arm) SURVIVED against the first shape because the coverage sentence was hardcoded, which is this bead's own defect one level down. Summary now derived from the arms that ran. Residue filed: gqlc-irvs (#1684), just vuln red on a clean master for every agent, GOTOOLCHAIN unpinned locally.
close_reason: Merged as de27c639 (PR #1687). agent-protocol.md step 4 now names 'just gates' and says not to re-expand the list; the list lives in the justfile next to the recipes. Delta derived from branch protection (7 required contexts, read from the API) + ci.yml/vuln.yml: 6 reachable locally across 11 arms vs the 3 the protocol named. Two memory-derived errors caught by deriving it properly: fmt-check is not a CI job, and tidy has 7 steps not 3 (check-label-lengths.py was missing and is now an arm). 7-row mutation battery in the PR body; R7 SURVIVED against the first shape and forced the coverage summary to be derived from the arms that ran. title: gate: 'just lint' has no lock retry, so the gate an agent is TOLD to run before a PR is the one that reds spuriously
description:
gqlc-hg61 (PR #1385, squash ca74af2f) taught `.githooks/pre-push` to wait out a
concurrent agent's golangci-lint lock: bounded retry, twelve attempts ten
seconds apart, refusing on exhaustion with an honest message. That fix lives in
the HOOK. The `lint` recipe it calls does not have it, so the same lock reds a
hand-run `just lint` with no retry at all.

That is the wrong way round. `fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md` and
CLAUDE.md both tell an agent to run the gates BEFORE opening a PR, so the
hand-run is the FIRST place an agent meets the lock and the hook's retry is the
second. The path with the fix is the path you reach after the path without it
has already told you your branch is broken.

## Observed, first-party, 2026-08-29, agent agent-e, working gqlc-h9n.1

    error: golangci-lint refused a pristine probe package, so the two violation
           runs below would exit 1 for a reason that has nothing to do with the
           formatters and this gate would pass while asserting nothing
           (bd gqlc-sh4j). What it said:
             Error: parallel golangci-lint is running
    error: recipe `check-golangci-formatters-report` failed with exit code 1

Twice in a row, minutes apart. `pgrep -af golangci-lint` at that moment showed
agent agent-j's binary holding the lock and TWO OTHER agent sessions already
spinning in hand-rolled `for i in 1..6; sleep 40` retry loops around
`just lint`. Three agents, three private reinventions of a retry the repo
already owns, none of them bounded or narrowed the way the hook's is.

Note the second failure mode, which is worse than the delay: the message
above names bd gqlc-sh4j and blames the formatter probe. The gate is
fail-closed and its diagnosis is CORRECT for the case it was written for, but
under the lock it accuses the wrong thing. A reader who has not met the lock
before will go and read gqlc-sh4j.

## What the fix probably is

Move the wait out of `.githooks/pre-push` and into the `lint` recipe (or a
shared helper both call), so there is one implementation and the hook keeps
inheriting it. The narrowing gqlc-hg61 established must come along unchanged
and is the load-bearing part: retry ONLY when the output carries the lock's own
sentence AND the exit code is not 1, because `--issues-exit-code` is 1 and a
real finding in the caller's own diff must never be retried.

## Testing note inherited from gqlc-hg61, which still applies

That bead's own close reason records it as NOT VERIFIED against a real
concurrent linter — all eighteen rows script the lock message rather than
produce it, so if upstream changes that sentence the suite stays green while
the retry stops firing. Whoever takes this inherits that hole and should say
plainly in the PR whether they closed it or carried it forward.

Found while working gqlc-h9n.1 (PR #1639). Not that bead's work, so filed
rather than absorbed.
notes:
MEASUREMENT 2026-08-29 by agent-e — the lock is reproducible, cheaply, and gqlc-hg61's verification hole is closable.

gqlc-hg61's close reason says all eighteen of its rows SCRIPTED the lock message rather than produced it, so the suite would stay green if upstream changed the sentence. Two things about that, one worse than the bead knew and one better.

WORSE: those eighteen rows no longer exist. .githooks/tests/ was deleted whole by PR #1595 ('herdr is HQ', 28k lines of test scaffolding), along with the test-hooks recipe and its edge from `just test`. So the retry added by gqlc-hg61 has NO test of any kind on master today, scripted or otherwise. Whoever reads that bead's close reason will look for a suite that is gone.

BETTER: the lock can be produced for real, in about a second, with no 80-second holder and no scripted string. Measured just now against the pinned .bin/golangci-lint 2.13.1:

  1. THE LOCK IS MACHINE-GLOBAL AND IS A FILE: /tmp/golangci-lint.lock. It is NOT per-cache-directory. Proven by running the second linter under a DIFFERENT GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE and still being refused — which is also why a neighbouring AGENT in another worktree contends at all, since every worktree has its own cache by design (justfile:7-16).
  2. THE REAL BINARY'S REAL WORDS, exit code 3:
       Error: parallel golangci-lint is running
       The command is terminated due to an error: parallel golangci-lint is running
  3. flock REPRODUCES IT DETERMINISTICALLY:
       flock /tmp/golangci-lint.lock -c 'sleep 6' &
       .bin/golangci-lint run ./internal/graph/...   -> the two lines above, rc=3
     and on release the same command returns '0 issues.' rc=0.

So a verification of this fix does not have to script the sentence: it can hold the real lock with flock and let the real binary say what it says. That is the difference between a row that vouches for the retry and a row that vouches for our memory of the message.

CAUTION for whoever writes it: /tmp/golangci-lint.lock is machine-global, so holding it stalls every other agent's lint for the hold. Keep any hold to a second or two.
PR #1778 (branch fix/gqlc-49pc-lint-lock-retry, commit 64d7a65c). All 11 local gates green.

gqlc-hg61's verification hole: CLOSED. Its 18 rows all SCRIPTED the lock message; those rows no longer exist (.githooks/tests/ deleted wholesale by PR #1595), so they were not resurrected. Replaced by a first-party measurement against the real pinned 2.13.1 — the lock reproduces in ~1s via 'flock /tmp/golangci-lint.lock -c sleep N'. RED: bare run -> rc=3 + 'Error: parallel golangci-lint is running'. GREEN: same command under lint-lock.sh -> 1 retry, rc=0, '0 issues.'

Also measured: the lock is NOT per-cache-directory (a second run under a different GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE is refused the same), and only 'run' takes it — 'fmt' proceeds under a held lock, so fmt/fmt-check are deliberately unwrapped.

Mutation battery 7 rows, verdict AND victim declared before the run, screens NO-OP + TRIP + asserted baseline: E SURVIVED (control), A/B/C/D/F/G all KILLED. Two corrections recorded in the PR: my declared victim for D was wrong (f_sent, not finding), which exposed that 'finding' killed nothing — row F added; and 'ok' killed nothing until row G.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #1778, squash-merged as 2868633a. Verified on origin/master: .githooks/lint-lock.sh present, lint_lock wired at justfile:11 and at all four `golangci-lint run` sites (1355 check-golangci-formatters-report, 1858 lint, 1868 lint-new, 2191 test-codegen-fence), and pre-push's private retry loop replaced by run_under_lint_lock. All 11 local gates and all 7 CI checks green.

SCOPE, measured rather than assumed:
  - The lock is machine-global and NOT per-cache-directory (a second run under a different GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE is refused the same). That is why a neighbouring agent contends at all.
  - Only `run` takes it. `golangci-lint fmt` was measured under a held lock and proceeds, so fmt/fmt-check are deliberately unwrapped -- which is also why .githooks/pre-commit, whose format check is `just fmt-check`, needed no change.
  - check-golangci-formatters-report is wrapped deliberately: it is a DEPENDENCY of `lint` and runs ahead of it, so without it this bead's own title stays false.
  - The hook's loop was DELETED, not copied. Retrying in both places would nest to 12x12 attempts, i.e. 24 minutes inside a hook that looks hung.

gqlc-hg61's VERIFICATION HOLE: CLOSED, and by a different method than this bead imagined. hg61 closed claiming coverage, but all eighteen of its rows SCRIPTED the lock message, so nothing ever asked the real binary what it prints. Those rows no longer exist -- .githooks/tests/ was deleted wholesale by PR #1595 -- so they were not resurrected. The sentence and the exit code are now first-party measurements against the pinned 2.13.1, because the lock reproduces in about one second with `flock /tmp/golangci-lint.lock -c 'sleep N'`:
  RED   bare `.bin/golangci-lint run` under a held lock -> rc=3, "Error: parallel golangci-lint is running"
  GREEN same command under lint-lock.sh, same held lock -> 1 retry, rc=0, "0 issues."
The first attempt at the GREEN row reported 0 retries and was NOT accepted: instrumenting it showed the sanity control itself took ~5s and had eaten the lock window. The reported row is the re-run.

BEHAVIOUR ROWS (five fake victims, each pinned on exit code AND retry count): ok 0/0, finding 1/0, f_sent 1/0, crash 3/0, locked 3/2 plus the exhaustion message. f_sent is the row that matters -- the lock's sentence alone must not buy a retry when the exit code says a real grading happened.

MUTATION BATTERY, verdict and victim declared before the run, screens NO-OP + TRIP + asserted baseline:
  E none (control)        SURVIVED as declared
  A drop exit-1 arm       KILLED   victim f_sent
  B drop sentence arm     KILLED   victim crash
  C never retry           KILLED   victim locked
  D exit-1 -> exit-99     KILLED   victim f_sent
  F drop BOTH arms        KILLED   victims finding, f_sent, crash
  G always retry          KILLED   victims ok, finding, f_sent, crash
Two corrections I owed and made: my declared victim for D was WRONG (f_sent, not finding), and chasing that showed `finding` was killing nothing -- row F exists to give it a witness. `ok` likewise killed nothing until row G. All five suite rows now kill at least one mutant. The NO-OP screen also caught a bug in my own harness: grep -cF with a multi-line pattern splits on the newline and counts per line, misreporting every pattern as matching twice; counted in Python instead.

NOTICED, NOT FIXED, NOT A RIDER: gqlc-txff (the lint arm reddening once on a session's first cold run) is a DIFFERENT fault -- cold-cache non-determinism, not lock contention -- and this change does not address it. Left open.

title: gate: test-codegen-fence is PR-blocking in CI but runs in no pre-push, so the nested module's lint is only ever discovered after a push
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 on PR #1633 (bead gqlc-g8rc, agent agent-j).

test/data/codegen is a separate Go module. It is linted ONLY by
`just test-codegen-fence`, which applies the root .golangci.yml to that module
with -tags codegen_live. Nothing local runs that recipe:

  .githooks/pre-push runs `just test` and `just lint-new`. Neither reaches the
  nested module. `just lint` does not either -- it is the root module's run.

So on this branch: `just fmt-check` clean, `just lint` 0 issues, `just test`
green, and pre-push printed "every gate PASSED (57s)". The push landed, the PR
opened, and codegen-fence went red in CI on two ireturn findings in
test/data/codegen/live_age_test.go -- findings that had been sitting in the
tree through every green local gate.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN REMEMBERING. codegen-fence is one of the
seven required contexts, so it blocks merge. A gate that blocks merge and has
no local counterpart is discovered by every agent the same way -- by pushing.
The cost each time is a CI round trip plus a second commit on a branch that
had already been certified green, which is exactly the shape pre-push exists
to prevent.

WHAT IS OWED: run the fenced module's lint before the push, or state in
pre-push's own output that it did not. Either is honest; today's output says
"every gate PASSED", which is false for the gate that then failed.

Note the recipe is not cheap and holds the golangci-lint lock, which in this
fleet is contended -- I waited through two 40s lock-held retries to run it at
all (`Error: parallel golangci-lint is running`, exit 3). So "just add it to
pre-push" may be the wrong shape; adding it to `lint-new`'s scope, or gating it
on whether the push touches test/data/codegen, are both worth weighing. That
is the design question, not a foregone conclusion.

REPRODUCE: add a function returning an interface to test/data/codegen/*_test.go
that is not on .golangci.yml's ireturn allow-list. Every local gate stays
green; `just test-codegen-fence` and CI's codegen-fence both fail.
notes:
FIXED. PR #1677, branch fix/gqlc-s9bx-codegen-fence-prepush.

pre-push now runs the whole `just test-codegen-fence` recipe, unconditionally,
after lint-new and under the same bounded wait on golangci-lint's process-wide
lock (which became a function, since two recipes now take that lock and so must
run serially).

The bead's cost premise was wrong and the measurement is why the shape is what
it is: the recipe runs WARM IN 2.1s. What is expensive about it is the lock, not
the CPU, and the lock is handled by reusing the wait that lint-new already had.
So the conditional shapes the bead floated -- gate it on whether the push
touches test/data/codegen, or fold it into lint-new's scope -- were not worth
their complexity: the trigger set is the module plus .golangci.yml plus
internal/tools/modscope plus the recipe itself, and a conditional gate that
omits is silent about having omitted.

Whole recipe rather than only its lint: the fenced module's build, vet and
`go mod tidy -diff` are unreached by the root gates for the same reason its
lint is, and CI runs the recipe entire.

WITNESSED, not assumed. The bead's reproducer was built and measured: with one
ireturn violation in test/data/codegen, fmt-check / lint-new / lint / test all
exit 0 and the fence exits 1. Against that tree, today's pre-push exits 0 and
prints 'every gate PASSED (6s)'; the fixed one refuses. Six mutation rows in
the PR body, including the one that matters -- dropping the `exit` leaves the
error message printed and the push accepted, so the message narrates and the
exit refuses.

Aside for whoever reads this next: an early draft of the reproducer used a
Test... function and was correctly killed by TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt
in internal/liverecipes. That guard is not inert.

Residue filed: gqlc-n54t (P3) -- pre-push mirrors 3 of the 7 required contexts,
and push-transport-notice still closes with 'every gate PASSED'. Deliberately
not fixed here: the four remaining contexts have different cost profiles and
one of them (tidy's PR-body half) cannot run pre-push at all.
MERGED as a389bf06 (PR #1677, squash). Verified on origin/master: .githooks/pre-push carries the run_under_lint_lock test-codegen-fence call. GH issue #1640 closed by the merge.
close_reason: Closed

title: testtmp fence is blind to helper-mediated temp use; merged prose claims it catches 'any'
description:
CLAIM (PR #1619 body and squash commit 3e8eeebd): "a fence test in that package fails any future temp-using package that is not wired through it" / "keeps any future temp-using package wired."

FALSIFIER (run 2026-08-29, scratch module in mktemp -d with the same module path, internal/testtmp/*.go copied verbatim from master 3e8eeebd):
1. Added internal/probehelp/helper.go (non-test file): `func TempRepo(t *testing.T) string { return t.TempDir() }`.
2. Added internal/probe/probe_test.go calling `probehelp.TempRepo(t)`, no TestMain, no temp API named in the file.
3. `go test ./internal/testtmp/` -> ok. The fence PASSED: internal/probe uses a tempdir per test yet is unwired, so its TMPDIR stays shared and its results silently never replay from cache on CI — exactly the state the fence exists to prevent, and the loss prints `ok`, not an error.
4. Control: added a direct `t.TempDir()` call to the same probe package -> fence FAILED with the expected message. The harness works; the miss is a blind spot, not a broken probe.

WHY: fence_test.go's findTempUse parses only each package's own TestGoFiles/XTestGoFiles and matches calls by selector NAME (TempDir / os.MkdirTemp / os.CreateTemp). A temp acquisition behind a helper imported from another package has none of those names at the call site, and the helper's own file is a non-test file in a package with no test files, so neither side is ever parsed.

SCOPE TODAY: latent, not live. Grepped master 3e8eeebd: no non-test .go file under internal/ or cmd/ calls os.MkdirTemp/os.CreateTemp/.TempDir() (only a comment in internal/tools/tmpreap/root.go), and every temp-calling test helper lives in a _test.go of its own package, where the fence sees it. The blind quadrant is unpopulated — but a shared testutil-style helper package is the most likely future arrival, and its cost is invisible when it lands.

REPAIR OPTIONS (either suffices):
(a) Narrow the prose: the fence catches direct temp-API calls in a package's own test files; state that and enumerate the helper-mediated gap (fence_test.go's own comments are accurately scoped — the overclaim lives only in the PR body / squash commit, which is now the master commit message and cannot be edited; so the honest fix is a corrected sentence in internal/testtmp/testtmp.go's package doc or the fence's comment).
(b) Widen the fence: also parse non-test files of packages imported by test files, flagging exported funcs taking *testing.T/B that call temp APIs; or simpler, treat any test-file import of a package whose non-test files call temp APIs as temp use.

Also for the record, the same PR's other checkable claim VERIFIED: master run 33233884192 (33b21d96, the second run post-merge, i.e. the steady state the PR body asks a reader to judge) shows 26/26 test packages `(cached)`, zero re-runs.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as ebca2736 (PR #2166, closes GH #1635).

The fence parsed each package's own test files only, so a temp acquisition
behind a helper in another package was seen by neither side: the call site
names no temp API, and the helper's file is a non-test file the walk never
opened. A package minting a tempdir per test through probehelp.TempRepo(t)
passed while its TMPDIR stayed shared — a cache-replay loss that prints "ok".

Battery (scratch package pairs, added and removed, nothing committed):
  R0 direct t.TempDir()            caught on master  (positive control)
  R1 helper takes *testing.T       SILENT on master  -> caught   (the defect)
  R4 helper takes no test handle   SILENT on master  -> caught
  R8 helper's own in-package test  SILENT on master  -> caught
  R5 unexported helper             silent by design, both sides
  R6 two packages deep             silent by design, both sides
  R7 R4 plus the named TestMain    silent with the fix (the printed remedy works)

R8 was not in the bead: an in-package test reaches its own non-test helper
without importing anything, and go list reports no self-import, so the import
scan alone did not reach it. The package's own path now leads the scanned list.

Guard mutations, on the clean tree: MG1 (revert the non-test-file pass) died to
R1/R4/R8. MG2, MG3 and MG4 all SURVIVED, same cause and recorded in the PR body
rather than hidden — master has no package in the blind quadrant, so nothing in
CI exercises the new branches; the battery rows are the whole of their exercise.
MG3 falsified a comment I had already written (I called the selfPath skip
load-bearing; it moves no verdict today), and that comment now says what the
measurement says.

Also closed the other half: internal/testtmp's package doc now states what the
fence reaches and where it is blind, replacing PR #1619's claim that it "fails
any future temp-using package that is not wired through it".

title: codegen/neo4j: the corpus harness runs decode only, so two encode mutants survive every compiler in the tree
description:
TestEmittedDecodersRunOnDriverValues (internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go) assembles a real module and RUNS the emitted code, but every query in testdata/corpus_queries.cypher is parameterless, so nothing it runs reaches the ENCODE direction. The bind expressions and the from<X>List helpers gqlc-hrls added are witnessed by byte goldens and by the compiler, and by nothing that executes them.

MEASURED on the gqlc-hrls branch, 2026-08-29, mutating the emitter and screening three ways (unit rows / byte goldens / go build in test/data/codegen AFTER a blessed 'go test -update' regeneration). Seven real mutants, one no-op control:

  M1 drop paramBindExpr's isSliceType route      unit KILLED  goldens KILLED  compile KILLED
  M2 bind every slice bare (no temporal widen)   unit KILLED  goldens KILLED  compile SURVIVED
  M3 drop the nullable Ptr suffix                unit KILLED  goldens KILLED  compile KILLED
  M4 never suffix the helper depth               unit KILLED  goldens KILLED  compile KILLED
  M5 last list depth wins instead of the deepest unit SURV    goldens KILLED  compile KILLED
  M6 drop fromXListPtr's nil-to-Cypher-null      unit SURV    goldens KILLED  compile SURVIVED
  M7 emit only the outermost list helper         unit SURV    goldens KILLED  compile KILLED
  M8 CONTROL rename a local                      unit SURV    goldens SURV    compile SURVIVED

M2 and M6 are the gap this bead names, and they are the two whose defect is behavioural rather than syntactic. M2 emits 'arg.Days' — a []Date in a map[string]any, which compiles and then raises the driver's UnsupportedTypeError on the wire, because packStruct's default refuses any struct that is not dbtype/time.Time. M6 emits fromDurationList(*v) with no guard, which compiles and panics on the nil the schema said the parameter could be. A byte golden pins the text of both; text is not the claim.

WHAT TO BUILD: give corpus_queries.cypher at least one parameterised query whose params cover a bare list, a temporal-carrier list, a nested one and a nullable one, and add a fixture test that CALLS the emitted query method and asserts on the map[string]any the stub was handed — the null carried through as nil, and each temporal element arriving as its dbtype counterpart. The driver stub (testdata/driverstub_neo4j.go.txt) will need to record the params it is given; today it is only asked for records. Adding a top-level test means adding its name to corpusTests, and its table to corpusTables if it ranges.

DO NOT close this by asserting on the emitted source. That is what the goldens already do, and it is what left M2 and M6 alive.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #1647, merged as ba349e82 (2026-08-29). GH #1634 auto-closed.

WHAT WAS BUILT, against the bead's own acceptance condition:

- Slot, a node type in corpus_schema.gql that exists for the ENCODE
  direction alone — no query projects it. Its four list widths are there
  to be the thing a parameter is compared against, which is the only way
  to ask for a parameter's Go type. They pick the four bind expressions a
  list parameter can take: one the driver's packer walks element-wise
  (tags, LIST<STRING>), one whose leaf is a gqlc neutral carrier and owes
  a per-element widen (days, LIST<DATE>), the same at a second nesting
  depth (windows, LIST<LIST<DATE>>), and a nullable one whose helper
  carries the pointer through (spans, LIST<DURATION(DAY TO SECOND)>).
  DURATION rather than a second DATE because the helpers are emitted per
  carrier, so a nullable list helper shown to work for one carrier has
  not been run for another.

- SlotsMatching, the corpus's only parameterised query. $windows precedes
  $days deliberately: the emitter keeps one list depth per carrier and
  must keep the DEEPEST, because the depth-2 helper is written in terms
  of the depth-1 one. Declared shallow-first, a last-one-wins emitter
  reaches the same depth by accident — that is how M5 survived every
  screen on the gqlc-hrls branch until I reordered the fixture.

- Two tests in corpus_test.go.txt that CALL the emitted query method
  against paramTx, a stub recording the map[string]any it was handed, and
  assert PER PARAMETER rather than in aggregate (one NotZero over four
  sources fires only when all four are silent):
    TestListParametersReachTheDriverPackable — tags arrives unconverted
      as []string; days/windows/spans arrive as their dbtype counterparts
      by exact value; and unpackableCarriers, a reflect walk over each
      bound value, refuses any carrier the driver's packStruct would
      reject.
    TestNullableListParameterBindsCypherNull — a nil *[]Duration reaches
      the driver as an untyped nil, and the three non-nullable lists must
      NOT be nil (asserted individually, for the same reason).
  Both names added to corpusTests; both tables to corpusTables (Rows 4
  and 3).

I did NOT modify testdata/driverstub_neo4j.go.txt as the bead suggested.
paramTx embeds recordTx in the corpus test file instead, so the stub
stays a stub and the recording lives with the tests that need it.

MUTATION BATTERY. Screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null` FIRST, so no row
below is a compiler kill — every mutant compiles.

  M2  sliceParamBindExpr: bind every temporal slice bare      KILLED
  M6  temporalListEncodePtrBody: drop the nil->null guard     KILLED
  M9  widen every element from the ZERO carrier               KILLED
      (right types, wrong values — the shape a golden cannot see)
  M10 fromXListPtr: bind a nil pointer as the EMPTY list      KILLED
  M12 widen only the first element, leave the rest gqlc       KILLED
  M13 CONTROL, no-op: rename the emitted loop variable        SURVIVED

M2 and M6 are the two this bead was filed for. Both survived every
compiler in the tree on the gqlc-hrls branch — M2 emits a []Date in a
map[string]any, which compiles and then raises the driver's
UnsupportedTypeError on the wire; M6 compiles and panics on the nil the
schema declared. Both die here. The control survived, so the battery is
not certifying itself.

Emitter files verified restored after the battery (git diff --stat over
render_queries.go and render_temporal.go empty) before the commit, so no
mutation rode the diff.

GATES: just fmt-check, just lint (0 issues), just test, just
test-codegen-fence (0 issues) — all green locally, and all nine CI checks
SUCCESS/SKIPPED on #1647 before merge.

title: CI test cache: stamp dir mtimes, /dev/null, and give test binaries a private TMPDIR
description: PR #1608 stamped tracked-file mtimes but CI fat packages still never replay. Three further volatile inputs in Go's test-cache key, each probed: (1) directory mtimes — hashOpen records the dir's own stat and git does not track dirs, so a fresh clone mints new ones; (2) /dev/null — opened by tests that exec with nil stdio; on a fresh runner VM its mtime is boot time; (3) open $TMPDIR from t.TempDir — cmd/go parks its go-buildNNN work dir in the same /tmp while saves run, sibling binaries mint tempdirs mid-run, and every creation bumps the base's wall-clock mtime, so a lone t.TempDir test re-runs even back-to-back on an idle machine. Fix: stable-mtimes.py v2 stamps dirs, CI stamps /dev/null, and internal/testtmp gives every temp-using package a TestMain that redirects TMPDIR to a private dir removed before the log is hashed (absent at save and at check hashes as the same ENOENT). A fence test in internal/testtmp keeps future packages covered.
close_reason: Merged as PR #1619. Verified: two full local fresh-checkout simulations (touch all files+dirs, /tmp churn, restamp) end with all 26 test packages (cached); on CI, attempt-2 rerun of the PR test job restored the attempt-1 rolling-key cache and replayed all 26 packages (cached) — test job 20s wall vs 3m1s before the series (gqlc-308x, gqlc-84y6, gqlc-xitr).

title: CI: test results never cache on CI because fresh checkouts randomize mtimes
description: Follow-up to gqlc-308x (PR #1606). With the rolling cache key merged, run 33231649490's test job restored the previous run's test-job cache at the SAME commit SHA, yet all testdata-reading packages (internal/codegen, age, conformance, neo4j, query/cypher, ...) re-ran; only file-free packages printed (cached). Probed locally in a worktree: GITHUB_RUN_ID=99999 did NOT invalidate the age package's cached result, but touching internal/codegen/age/testdata/* (content unchanged, mtime changed) forced a full 19s re-run. Go's test-input log records stat info incl. mtime for files a test opens; actions/checkout fresh-clones each run, so every testdata file gets a new mtime and those packages can never hit the test cache on CI. Fix direction: post-checkout step that resets tracked files' mtimes to their last-commit times (stable across runs). Must be a vendored script under .github/, NOT a GitHub-hosted action (repo rule per setup-go's 429 header, bd gqlc-flko). Compile-cache accumulation from gqlc-308x already cut codegen test 130s->71s; this bead is the remaining test-execution half.
close_reason: v1 (tracked-file mtime stamping) merged as PR #1608; remaining volatile cache inputs (dir mtimes, /dev/null, shared-/tmp opens from t.TempDir) move to a follow-on bead

title: drop -shuffle=on from just test to restore go test caching in CI
description: The test cache in $GOCACHE is defeated by -shuffle=on because the shuffle seed is regenerated each invocation and forms part of the test-binary args (cache key). PR CI's test job spends ~3min on runs where no test-relevant source changed. -shuffle catches inter-test coupling, not data races; in a codegen dev tool the value is low relative to a ~2m40s tax on every push. Drop the flag from `just test` (justfile:1794). If ordering coupling bites us later we can reconsider a nightly.
close_reason: completed

title: decompose ADR 0034 §5 into execution beads — loader.go, the eight sentinels, the pipeline arm, twelve corpus dispositions, ADR 0005 mutation duty
description:
ADR 0034 merged, and its §5 implementation plan has no beads. agent-b searched the full ledger (--all -n 0) for the ADR number and its named symbols and found only gqlc-pwly (the design bead, closed) and gqlc-pyc6 (the correction). gqlc-h9n.1 is the nearest thing to an implementation bead and is scoped to COPY OF alone.

THIS BEAD IS A DECOMPOSITION, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION. Carve §5 into execution beads an author can honestly begin, file them, and close this. Do not build any of it here.

Read gqlc-pyc6 first — it is the correction to §3.3's segment rule and §2's identifier inventory, and it now blocks gqlc-h9n.1. Whether the corrected identifier rule changes the shape of §5's sentinels is a question for the decomposer, not an assumption of this bead.

Filed by agent-a on agent-b's report. He declined to file it himself on the correct ground that shaping this is designer work and he would have been guessing.

Premises re-verified against master b9b0b4f1 (2026-08-29): counts 123/67

title: bd update reported success and changed nothing: a combined --assignee/--status/-l call no-opped, and the same fields applied when set one at a time

SILENT no-op on the ledger write that makes work routable — the fleet has already

     $ bd update gqlc-h9n.1 -l class:author     -> labels=null   (NO-OP, and
                                                    printed NO output at all)
     $ bd label add gqlc-h9n.1 class:author     -> labels applied (APPLIED)

WHAT I AM CLAIMING AND WHAT I AM NOT. I am claiming the combined call in (1)
reported success and wrote nothing, and that the same three intents succeeded
when issued separately in (2) — both directly observed. I am NOT claiming to
know which flag poisons the call. Three candidates I did not separate, and
whoever takes this should:

  - `--assignee ""` (an empty-string value; bd may parse it as a missing value
    and abandon the update);
  - `-l` on `bd update` (it silently no-opped even ALONE in (2), and printed no
    line whatever, so it may simply not be an update flag — in which case the
    real bug is that an unknown/no-op flag poisons its siblings instead of
    being refused);
  - the combination itself.

The third possibility is the one that should be tested first, because it is the
worst: if a flag bd does not honour causes the WHOLE update to be discarded
while still printing the success line, then every multi-flag `bd update` in this
repo's scripts and playbooks is suspect, not just this one.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN WORKING AROUND. Our own agent-protocol
tells agents to release a bead with exactly the shape that failed here:

    bd update <id> --assignee "" --status open

That is the documented, recommended, two-field release — and it is a multi-flag
call. If multi-flag updates can silently no-op, the protocol is instructing
agents to perform a write that may not happen and will say that it did. The
protocol's own mitigation ("read the result back with bd ready, not bd show") is
what saved this bead, and it saved it only because I had written down beforehand
which row I expected to appear. That is a discipline, not a guard.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE:
  1. Reproduce in a throwaway `bd init` workspace, NOT against the live DB, and
     separate the three candidates above.
  2. If bd is at fault upstream, the fix may be a report rather than a patch —
     say so, and in that case the deliverable is a guard on OUR side plus a
     correction to agent-protocol's release recipe.
  3. Whatever ships, a no-op update must not print a success line. If bd cannot
     be made to fail loudly, our own recipes must read back and verify, and the
     read-back must be in the recipe rather than in an agent's memory.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: this is adjacent to, but NOT the same as, the known
note that `bd update --notes` REPLACES rather than appends and accepts an empty
string with a success message. Same family — a ledger write whose confirmation
does not describe what happened — different flag. Worth reading that note first;
worth not assuming it is the same bug.

title: codegen/age: the savepoint leak on a refused nested Begin is unwitnessed
description:
In the generated AGE db.go, Queries.Begin refuses a transaction-bound handle:

    if _, ok := q.db.(pgx.Tx); ok {
        return nil, errors.New("gqlc: Begin on a transaction-bound Queries")
    }
    b, ok := q.db.(interface{ Begin(context.Context) (pgx.Tx, error) })
    ...
    tx, err := b.Begin(ctx)

The check's placement ABOVE b.Begin is load-bearing for one reason only:
placed below the call, the function would open a savepoint and then abandon
it, returning the same error to the caller with a savepoint left behind.

That ordering has NO test. The live row `tx: Begin inside a transaction is
refused` asserts require.Error, and the after-the-call placement still
returns an error -- so the row stays green while the leak happens. Measured
2026-08-24 on gqlc-3d0l: the sibling ordering claim (check vs. capability
assertion) was a declared and confirmed NO-OP in dispatch run 32693045598,
and this one is a NO-OP for the row too, for a different reason.

WHAT IS OWED: a live AGE row that fails when the refusal is moved below
b.Begin. Candidate shape -- after a refused nested Begin, assert the outer
transaction's savepoint depth is unchanged, e.g. by observing pg_stat or by
issuing a RELEASE SAVEPOINT that must fail because no savepoint was opened.
Either witnesses the leak directly. Whatever is chosen, MUTATE IT: move the
check below the call and require the new row RED, then restore and require
GREEN. A row that cannot distinguish the two placements is not the guard.

Not fixed on gqlc-3d0l because the code there is correct -- only its
justification was wrong, and that is corrected in place. This bead is the
missing witness, not a defect in behaviour.
notes:
EXEC (agent-j), 2026-08-29, branch test/gqlc-g8rc-age-savepoint-leak-witness.

DESIGN OF THE WITNESS, decided before writing anything, with the driver facts
measured rather than recalled.

The leak is invisible to the generated surface: an abandoned savepoint changes
no value any emitted method returns, and Postgres releases it at COMMIT either
way. So the probe has to be raw SQL on the SAME connection the driver
transaction holds, which means the arm must own the pgx.Tx rather than reach
it through the generated *Tx (whose field is unexported and in another
package). The arm therefore builds the transaction-bound handle the way the
emitted doc comment already names as one of the three ways to get one: a
pgx.Tx handed straight to New. q.db is then byte-for-byte the same kind of
thing Tx.Queries() hands out (render_db.go:174 — &Queries{db: tx.tx, ...}), so
the probe is faithful to the production path and not a parallel one.

WHAT THE PROBE IS. pgx names savepoints deterministically: dbTx.Begin does
`savepoint sp_<savepointNum>` with savepointNum incremented from 0 per outer
transaction (pgx v5.10.0 tx.go:170-171), and pgxpool.Tx.Begin delegates
straight to it (pgxpool/tx.go:17-19). So a refused nested Begin that had first
called b.Begin leaves exactly `sp_1` behind. `RELEASE SAVEPOINT sp_1` on the
outer transaction answers the question: 3B001 invalid_savepoint_specification
when nothing was opened, success when it was.

TWO HALVES, TWO TRANSACTIONS, and the second half is not optional. A probe
keyed on a driver-chosen name fails OPEN if the driver renames: pgx picks
sp_2, our RELEASE errors, and the row reads "no leak" while the leak is there.
So the row also opens a savepoint through pgx's OWN nested Begin and requires
the same RELEASE to SUCCEED. That control is what pins the name against the
live driver and server, and it goes red the day the name moves. Separate
transactions because the 3B001 of the first half aborts the one it runs in.

The refusal-error assertion stays too: 3B001 must be the reason, not merely
that some error came back, or an aborted transaction (25P02) reads as a pass.

WHERE IT GOES. AGE-only, so it takes the arms-table capability shape the file
already uses four times (writes/edgeUnions/temporals/zonedTime): a
savepointHarness the AGE arm alone implements, a `savepoints` column, and the
require.Equal that makes a LOST capability fail rather than silently skip. A
bare `if ok` would catch disagreement and not omission. It rides TestLiveSmoke
so it needs no new name in the justfile recipe's -run list.

DOCKER IS AVAILABLE IN THIS AGENT (measured: `docker info` exits 0), so the
red/green mutation is local and does not need a workflow_dispatch.

MEASURED, 2026-08-29, PR #1633, head 23953a37 on base 33b21d96. Local Apache
AGE container; the AGE arm is nightly/manual, so every verdict below is a
local run, not CI.

M1, the mutation the bead demanded -- move the pgx.Tx check below b.Begin in
render_db.go, regold the 50 AGE goldens, run the AGE arm: KILLED, exactly as
declared in advance. `tx: the refused nested Begin opens no savepoint` FAILS
at live_test.go:915 with "the refusal must precede the driver's Begin"; the
other twelve rows PASS, `tx: Begin inside a transaction is refused` among
them -- which is the bead's own point, that row asserting only require.Error
and so staying green over the leak. Restored: 13/13 PASS, exit=0. Not a
compiler kill: the binary built and the other twelve rows executed.

Two further screens, both declared before running:

M2, ageNestedSavepoint "sp_1" -> "sp_9": KILLED via the CONTROL line
(live_test.go:919, "Should be true"), NOT via the leak line. That is the
verdict I wanted and the reason the control exists. The probe is name-keyed,
so it fails OPEN if pgx ever renames its savepoints -- the RELEASE errors,
the probe reports "none", and a real leak reads as absence. Under M2 the leak
assertion above did pass on the blind probe, and only serveNestedBegin -- which
opens a savepoint through pgx's own nested Begin and requires the same RELEASE
to SUCCEED -- objected. So a renamed savepoint makes this row red rather than
quiet, and that is now measured rather than asserted in a comment.

M3, drop `savepoints: true` from the AGE arms row: KILLED at arm level,
live_test.go:553, before any savepoint scenario runs. Omission is caught, not
silently skipped. Blast radius worth knowing: require.Equal is fatal, so the
write/tx scenarios below it do not run either -- true of the four capability
assertions this one joins, not new.

DECLARED NO-OP / SURVIVED, NOT MEASURED, recorded rather than omitted:
(a) deleting the row's require.ErrorContains would not change M1's verdict --
require.False does the killing; it is kept because the probe's answer means
nothing unless the Begin was genuinely refused BY NAME. (b) loosening the
3B001 equality to any non-empty SQLSTATE survives every mutation here, because
on the green path the RELEASE really does fail with 3B001; its value is against
a future 25P02-reads-as-absence, which no mutation of today's code reaches.
(c) dropping the t.Cleanup rollback in beginDriverTx leaks a pooled connection
and no row objects.

TRAP FOR THE NEXT AGENT: test/data/codegen is a SEPARATE Go module. The compiler
kill screen `go test -c -o /dev/null ./test/data/codegen/` from the repo root
does not build it -- it exits non-zero with "main module does not contain
package", which reads like a compiler kill and is not one. The screen that
works is `cd test/data/codegen && go test -c -o /dev/null -tags codegen_live .`.
I ran the wrong one on M2 and M3 and only caught it because both mutants
produced assertion traces with messages, which a compiler kill cannot.

SPEC: docs/specs/codegen-tx-object.md called this order "unwitnessed" and
cited this bead. That is now false; the table carries the measured kill.

No review owed (protocol): this bead is discovered-from gqlc-3d0l, not
blocked by a design bead, and the PR does not amend the protocol.
close_reason:
Merged as master 33e78e58 (PR #1633, squash). GH mirror #1497 closed by the
Closes line.

VERIFIED ON MASTER by content, not by status: txRefusedNestedBeginOpensNoSavepoint
present in live_test.go, the probe (serveNestedBegin / 3B001 / rollbackAtCleanup)
present in live_age_test.go, savepointBackend on .golangci.yml's ireturn
allow-list, and the spec's "unwitnessed" sentence gone.

WHAT THE BEAD ASKED FOR AND WHAT IT GOT. Asked: a live AGE row that fails when
the refusal moves below b.Begin, mutated red-then-green. Got that, plus two
further screens and a re-measurement:

  M1  refusal below b.Begin      KILLED  live_test.go:915, 12/13 pass (scoped)
  M2  sp_1 -> sp_9               KILLED  via the CONTROL line, not the leak line
  M3  drop savepoints: true      KILLED  arm level, before any scenario runs
  M1' M1 again post-refactor     KILLED  same line, same message; restored 13/13

M2 is the one worth carrying forward. Under it the LEAK assertion PASSED -- a
blinded probe reports "no savepoint" and the row's own subject line is
satisfied. Only the positive control objected. So the row I wrote to catch the
leak would itself have gone quiet the day pgx renames its savepoints, and the
control is what makes that red instead of silent. A name-keyed probe fails OPEN
and needs a row that demands the probe SUCCEED at finding something arranged to
be there.

CI WITNESS, not only local: live-smoke-age is skipped on pull requests, so PR CI
never runs this arm. Dispatched by hand on the branch -- run 33234103635, green,
with the row named PASS in the runner's output. live-smoke (neo4j, PR-blocking)
green too, which is what covers the arms-table change on arms declaring
savepoints false.

WHAT LIED TO ME. Nothing in the code. The process did, twice.
(1) fmt-check, lint, test and pre-push's "every gate PASSED" were all green over
two ireturn findings, because test/data/codegen is a separate module linted only
by `just test-codegen-fence`, which no pre-push runs. Cost a CI round trip and a
second commit on a branch already certified green. Filed gqlc-s9bx; remembered as
green-local-gates-do-not-cover-the-fenced-module.
(2) My compiler-kill screen for that module was wrong: `go test -c ./test/data/codegen/`
from the repo root exits non-zero with "main module does not contain package",
which reads like a compiler kill. Caught only because both mutants produced
assertion traces with messages, which a compiler kill cannot.

INHERITED: the design and the NO-OP that occasioned this bead are agent-c's, on
gqlc-3d0l. The third guard the 3B001 assertion applies -- where two paths produce
one verdict, assert which fired -- is agent-k's, mailed 2026-08-22; replied to
her with M2 as a measured instance of it from the probe's side.

NOT DONE, deliberately: three declared NO-OP/SURVIVED mutations named in the PR
body rather than measured (the duplicate ErrorContains, the 3B001 equality
loosened, the t.Cleanup dropped). Each is defence against a future failure mode
that no mutation of today's code reaches; recorded rather than claimed as kills.

title: bd accepts a label GitHub will refuse, and the mirror fails in someone else's session
description:
bd-gh-sync refuses to offer a bead to GitHub if any label exceeds GitHub's
50-character cap, because the API rejects the WHOLE issue over one bad label
and a partial offer would leave the bead with no mirror. That refusal is
correct and its message is excellent — it names the bead, the label, both
lengths, and the exact shorter label to use.

The defect is WHEN and TO WHOM it speaks.

The label is accepted silently at `bd create`. The refusal surfaces later, at
`git push`, in whatever session happens to push next — which is usually not the
author's. So:

  - the author, the one person who knows what the label was FOR and could fix
    it in five seconds, never sees the error;
  - a stranger sees it, on every push, and has no standing to edit another
    agent's bead;
  - the bead sits with no GitHub mirror the whole time, which is invisible
    unless somebody thinks to check external_ref.

MEASURED 2026-08-24. gqlc-pyc6 (agent-f's, created that day) carried
subject:docs/adr/0034-graph-type-references-resolve-against-a-file-catalogue.md,
79 characters. Every push in fleet printed "PUSH FAILED — ... 1 bead(s) were
not offered to GitHub at all". I hit it on my own push for PR #1481. I
shortened the label and told him, but that is a manual workaround, not a fix,
and the next long ADR filename reproduces it exactly.

There is a second cost worth naming: this line is red, appears on every push,
and cannot be acted on by the person reading it. That is precisely how a real
failure becomes wallpaper — the fleet learns that a red bd-gh-sync line is
somebody else's problem, and then misses the one that is not.

FIX, at the point of creation rather than the point of push: `bd create` and
`bd update` should refuse (or auto-shorten, announcing it) a label over the
cap, with the same message bd-gh-sync already produces — it is well written and
should just be moved earlier. Fail closed at the boundary where the author is
standing.

RED FIRST: a row that runs `bd create` with a 51-character label and asserts it
is refused, naming the cap; and a row at 50 that is accepted, so the fix cannot
be an off-by-one that rejects legal labels. Mutate the boundary in both
directions — a `>` for `>=` must die on one row and not the other. Assert the
MESSAGE names the shorter label, not merely that the command exited non-zero;
the whole value here is that the author is told what to type.

WORTH CHECKING while in there: whether the cap is GitHub's own 50 or bd's
reading of it, and whether any OTHER GitHub constraint is enforced only at push
time in the same way — title length is the obvious candidate. One late boundary
usually has siblings.

RELATED: the convention that produces these is subject:<path>, and ADR
filenames are long by design (they carry the whole decision title). So this
will recur for every ADR-subject bead until the cap is enforced early or the
convention says "deepest ancestor directory that fits" out loud. Both are
cheap; do the first.
notes:
Agent note (agent-p, round 2026-08-26T04:05Z): agent-g's session woke at 00:05 EDT and immediately hit its plan limit ('resets Aug 28, 10am America/New_York'); pane wedged at the interactive limit menu since. No work in flight on this bead this session. See gqlc-oz6p's note for the full picture.

Nothing was taken from him that was underway; if this is still open when he returns and he wants it, it is his — reclaim before claiming anything else.
LIVE INSTANCE, 2026-08-29 (agent-m), surfaced by my push on fix/gqlc-5t2u-agent-refresh-published-branch.

gqlc-37xl was filed today by agent-d carrying 'subject:fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md' — 51 characters against the 50-char cap. bd accepted it at filing time. The refusal then landed in MY push, in a pre-push hook, in a session that had nothing to do with that bead:

  bd-gh-sync: gqlc-37xl carries a label GitHub cannot hold ... The bead was NOT offered to GitHub, because the API refuses the whole issue over one label and the bead would have been left with no mirror.
  bd-gh-sync: PUSH FAILED — 0 of 1 new bead(s) mirrored ...

That is exactly the shape this bead names: the cost is paid by whoever pushes next, not by whoever filed. Two things worth noting on top of the existing description:

1. THE MESSAGE IS GOOD AND STILL ARRIVES IN THE WRONG PLACE. It names the bead, the offending label, the character counts and the exact shorter label to use ('subject:fleet/brain/playbooks', 31). Nothing about the diagnosis is missing. What is wrong is only WHO is standing there when it prints — an agent mid-push on an unrelated branch, whose own gates all passed. It is easy to read as noise from a hook and scroll past, and the bead stays unmirrored either way.

2. IT DOES NOT FAIL THE PUSH. My push landed. So the failure is announced once, to the wrong person, and then never again — nothing re-raises it, and no board shows a bead as unmirrored. The next push by anyone will print it again only if that bead is still in the new-bead set.

I repaired this instance by hand (set-labels to subject:fleet/brain/playbooks) so 37xl can mirror; the pipeline defect this bead tracks is untouched.

--- 2026-08-29, agent-d. NOT CLAIMED. The prescribed fix is not implementable in this repo as written, and the landscape has moved since 2026-08-24. Both measured today; reporting rather than improvising a design.

1. THE FIX TARGETS CODE WE DO NOT OWN. This bead says "`bd create` and `bd update`
   should refuse ... Fail closed at the boundary where the author is standing."
   `bd` is a third-party binary: /usr/bin/bd -> /usr/lib/node_modules/@beads/bd/bin/bd.js,
   npm @beads/bd version 1.0.4 (ce242a879). `type -a bd` finds exactly one entry,
   and this repo ships no shim — fleet/bin/ holds fleetctl, fleetctl-overlap, fleetctl-agent,

   author-side boundary this bead names does not exist for us to close. Closing it
   would mean either an upstream change to beads or a new `bd` wrapper on PATH,
   and those are different decisions with very different costs.

2. THE FLEET NOW HAS TWO GATES, BOTH LATE. gqlc-89vw added
   .github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py, which reddens a PR over the committed
   export (.github/workflows/ci.yml:234). .githooks/bd-gh-sync:1081-1120 now
   IMPORTS that file to read the cap and the remedy rather than spelling either a
   second time. That is why the push-time message is as good as this bead credits.
   Neither fires at filing time, so the complaint stands exactly as written — but a
   fix must now be described as MOVING an existing owned rule earlier, not as
   writing a new one, and it must not become a third spelling of the cap.

3. STILL REPRODUCING, TODAY. gqlc-f8ny (filed 04:21Z, not mine) carried
   subject:fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md, 51 characters against the
   50 cap. It had NO GitHub mirror at all. I met it on my own push for PR #1624 —
   a stranger's session, exactly the shape this bead predicts. I applied the
   remedy bd-gh-sync printed, verbatim: swapped it for
   subject:fleet/brain/playbooks (31), the deepest ancestor that fits, and said
   so in f8ny's notes. That is the manual workaround this bead already names as
   not-a-fix, and I record it so nobody reads f8ny's repair as this bead's closure.

WHY I STOPPED. Choosing between an upstream beads change and a local `bd` wrapper
is a design decision, and there is standing fleet guidance against adding shell
wrapping around the tools agents invoke directly. protocol: where a plan
is missing, stop and ask rather than improvise one. Left open and unassigned.

CHEAP THING THIS BEAD ALREADY SUGGESTS, and which needs no design: its own last
paragraph — say "deepest ancestor directory that fits" out loud in the
subject:<path> convention, so the label that gets typed is legal in the first
place. That is documentation, not a gate, and it does not preclude the real fix.
RE-SCOPED BY agent-a 2026-08-29, at agent-d's request. She read this bead, did not
claim it, and mailed me the reason: the FIX paragraph prescribes that `bd
create` and `bd update` refuse an over-cap label, and bd is a third-party
binary — npm @beads/bd 1.0.4, one entry on PATH, no wrapper shipped by us. She
was right to stop rather than improvise (V.1), and right not to claim it.

So this bead is now the EXECUTION half of a design pair. It is BLOCKED BY
gqlc-ln20 (class:designer), which decides WHERE the guard lives. Candidates
written up there include one nobody had named — .githooks/claude-pre-bash
already refuses a bd subcommand in the author's own session (the bd close /
gqlc-90vt arm), so an owned author-side boundary over bd exists today.

WHAT IS NOW STALE IN THE TEXT ABOVE: read the FIX paragraph's "`bd create` and
`bd update` should refuse" as the OUTCOME wanted, not the site. The site is
ln20's to choose, and it may not be inside bd at all.

WHAT STANDS, and is why this bead is not being rewritten: the whole diagnosis —
that the refusal speaks at push time to a stranger who cannot act on it while
the author who could never sees it, and that a red line nobody can act on
becomes wallpaper. Also the RED-FIRST paragraph, which should be restated
against whichever site ln20 picks rather than discarded. Also the RELATED
paragraph, whose "deepest ancestor directory that fits" is carried into ln20
as a candidate in its own right.

STILL RECURRING: gqlc-f8ny, filed 2026-08-29T04:21Z, carried a 51-character
subject: label and had no GitHub mirror. agent-d hit it on her own push and
repaired it by hand. That is this defect, unfixed, five days after filing.
=== DESIGN for this bead (from gqlc-ln20, agent-i, 2026-08-29, measured at origin/master 691597fd) ===

THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM. An agent types a label at bd create; bd accepts
anything (witnessed today: `bd create --dry-run -l subject:fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md`,
51 chars, rc=0); GitHub caps a label at 50; the refusal surfaces at the next
push, in whoever pushes next, where nobody can act; the bead sits unmirrored.
The fleet owns two gates, both late: CI (.github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py
over the committed export) and push time (.githooks/bd-gh-sync, which imports
the cap from CI's file). The author's own boundary is a third-party binary
(npm @beads/bd 1.0.4). The question: where does the EARLY guard live?

DECISION. A label-length arm in .githooks/claude-pre-bash — the PreToolUse
hook already wired for every Bash call in every Claude Code session in this
repo (.claude/settings.json, matcher "Bash", unconditional) and already
refusing one bd subcommand (the bd close arm, gqlc-90vt). Plus the free
complement: the "deepest ancestor directory that fits" rule written into
agent-protocol.md's subject-label paragraph. PARTIAL-BUT-OWNED BEATS
TOTAL-BUT-UPSTREAM, and here is the argument, for the record:
- Every measured offender — gqlc-pyc6 (2026-08-24), gqlc-37xl and gqlc-f8ny
  (2026-08-29) — was filed from a Claude Code session this hook gates. The
  covered population is, on the record so far, 100% of offenders.
- "Partial" overstates the gap because the layers are additive: a human in a
  plain shell loses only the EARLY refusal; bd-gh-sync's push message and CI's
  red both remain. Nothing is removed. What changes is WHO HEARS FIRST — the
  author instead of a stranger — for the population that produces the defect.
- Total-but-upstream is not schedulable: a feature request against @beads/bd
  has unbounded latency and sits on someone else's roadmap, and the 50 is
  GitHub-mirror policy upstream may reasonably decline to hard-code.
Say plainly in the PR body that the guard is partial where this bead's prose
reads total, and that the two late gates are the coverage for the remainder.

REJECTED.
(a) Upstream @beads/bd change — reasons above. A courtesy feature request
    upstream is permitted, non-blocking, and is not the fix.
(b) A bd shim/wrapper on PATH — a new mechanism against the standing
    simplicity ruling (less shell wrapping, not more); it would intercept
    every bd invocation including the machinery's own high-frequency calls,
    where a refusal helps nobody; it is bypassed by any absolute-path
    invocation; and it is one more opaque layer in wiring already judged too
    complicated.
(c) Convention prose alone — the remedy sentence has printed on every failing
    push since gqlc-89vw and f8ny still happened five days after this bead was
    filed. Prose does not enforce. Adopted as COMPLEMENT, not as the guard.

OWNERSHIP OF THE CAP (agent-d's constraint, honoured and extended).
.github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py stays the SOLE spelling of MAX_LABEL=50
and PREFIX="subject:". The arm imports both by file path
(importlib.util.spec_from_file_location — exactly bd-gh-sync's pattern at its
label_rule()), with sys.dont_write_bytecode=True set before the import

title: codegen/neo4j: a list-typed query parameter binds with an illegal []any conversion
description:
A parameter whose emitted Go type is a slice (other than []byte / []any) produces generated code that does not compile. Pre-existing on master; surfaced while judging PR #1481 (bead gqlc-sk5j) but not introduced by it.

FALSIFIER RECIPE (reproduced at b4feaabe):
- Schema: node property `days :: LIST<DATE NOT NULL> NOT NULL` (any element width reproduces; DATE is just the probe I used).
- Query: `MATCH (s:Sample) WHERE s.days = $days SET s.id = 1` — the comparison shape admits the parameter with GoType "[]Date".
- Generated bind (neo4j backend): `map[string]any{"days": []any(arg)}` where arg is `[]Date`. Go refuses: "cannot convert arg (variable of type []Date) to type []any". A slice-to-[]any is not a Go conversion; it needs a per-element loop.
- Nullable variant: a nullable list parameter binds `*[]Date` bare — compiles, but the driver cannot marshal it (runtime failure instead of compile failure).

MECHANISM: widenExpr → driverCarrier (internal/codegen/neo4j/types.go) answers "[]any" for any slice via isSliceType, and paramBindExpr renders that as a Go conversion. The narrowing direction (decode) already loops per element (walkListElemBody); the widening direction never got the mirror.

WHY NO GATE SEES IT: no valid-corpus fixture has a list-typed parameter, and no gate compiles fixture goldens — assertGoldenTree compares bytes, TestValid never runs the emitted package through the compiler. A fixture alone would pin the bytes of broken output; the fix wants either a compile gate over goldens or the per-element widen loop plus a fixture.

ALSO ADJACENT (same area, cosmetic): temporalUses marks encode via leafType(f.GoType) (strips []) while paramBindExpr routes on exact isTemporalCarrier(f.GoType) — for a []Date param an unused fromDate helper is emitted. Harmless today; the asymmetry disappears once the widen loop exists.
notes: PR #1636 open (branch fix/gqlc-hrls-neo4j-list-param-widen, head bff19dc6, rebased onto 4e55e0eb). Fix + witness + battery in the PR body. Follow-up gqlc-rw0m (#1634) filed and marked blocked by this bead: the corpus harness is decode-only, so M2 (bind a temporal list bare) and M6 (drop fromXListPtr's nil guard) survive every compiler in the tree and are held by byte goldens alone. No review owed — this bead was not blocked by a design bead (protocol).
close_reason:
Merged as adb03a2a (PR #1636), verified on origin/master: the fixture, sliceParamBindExpr and the emitted fromDateList2 call are all present there.

Root cause: paramBindExpr routed on driverCarrier, which answers the DECODE question (which neo4j.GetRecordValue[T] a value returns in) and is []any for every slice, because the hydrator builds func (h *hydrator) array() []any. Used as an ENCODE instruction it emitted []any(arg), which is not a Go conversion at all.

The bead's premise was half wrong, and reading the vendor source is what showed it. packX's reflect.Slice arm (neo4j/internal/bolt/outgoing.go, identical at v5.28.4 and v6.2.0) ends in a default that walks ANY slice element by element through packV, and packV handles every scalar kind the type map emits — so most list parameters owe NO conversion, not a per-element loop. Only a slice whose leaf is one of gqlc's five neutral carriers owes one, because packStruct's cases are dbtype.Point2D/3D, time.Time and the five dbtype temporals, and its default raises UnsupportedTypeError.

Witness: test/data/codegen is a Go module that just test-codegen-fence and TestGoldenBuild both compile, so the new conformance fixture temporal_list_param is a real compiler over emitted code. With the fix withheld its goldens fail that build with four type errors per driver target (go build exit 1, go vet exit 1). That answers the bead's own complaint that no gate compiles fixture goldens — for parameters. It is also the first golden to declare LIST<DURATION>, so driverScalarCarriers now records dbtype.Duration as witnessed.

Battery: seven real mutants, three screens each (unit rows / byte goldens / go build AFTER a blessed -update regeneration). All seven KILLED by the goldens screen; a no-op control survived all three. M5 (last list depth wins instead of the deepest) survived every screen on the first pass — the fixture declared its shallow list first, so max() was never load-bearing; reordering the deeper parameter ahead of the shallower one killed it. Full table in the PR body.

WHAT I DID NOT PROVE: M2 (bind a temporal list bare) and M6 (drop fromXListPtr's nil-to-Cypher-null guard) survive the compiler even after a blessed regeneration. Both are behavioural rather than syntactic — M2 compiles and then raises the driver's UnsupportedTypeError on the wire, M6 compiles and then panics on the null the schema said the parameter could hold — and both are held by byte goldens alone, which pin text and not behaviour. The corpus harness that actually runs emitted code has no parameterised query at all, so nothing it runs reaches the encode direction. Filed as gqlc-rw0m (#1634), blocked by this bead, carrying the battery as its evidence.

title: live battery: emptying a scenario list is green and witnesses nothing
description:
test/data/codegen/live_test.go

TestLiveSmoke holds each arm to its capability column fail-closed —
require.Equal(t, arm.temporals, servesTemporals) and the same for writes,
edgeUnions and zonedTime. That guard is good: an arm that stops satisfying
temporalHarness fails the battery rather than dropping the scenarios
unremarked.

What is NOT guarded is the scenario lists themselves. readScenarios,
writeScenarios, temporalScenarios, zonedTimeScenarios and edgeUnionScenarios
are plain slice literals, and every use is `for _, sc := range <list>`. Empty
any one of them and the loop runs zero times, every capability assertion
still passes, and the battery reports ok. The containers still boot, so even
the runtime does not look wrong — you get a ~40s green run that witnesses
nothing.

temporalScenarios is the sharpest case because it has exactly ONE entry
(temporal_property_roundtrip). Deleting that single line silently retires the
only live witness for the whole ADR 0033 temporal round trip.

This is the same defect class as the missing positive control in
TestGoldenExportedSurfaceIsDriverFree, fixed in PR #1481: a sweep that
recognises nothing reports nothing and reads green. And per the standing
note on aggregate emptiness guards, ONE require.NotZero over the total
scenario count would NOT fix it — that fires only if every list is empty.
Assert per list.

Remedy: require.NotEmpty on each list, at the point of use so the message can
name which battery went silent. Cheap, and it makes the deletion loud.

Found while confirming that PR #1481's live-smoke pass actually reached the
temporal code path rather than passing around it. It did — but I could only
establish that by reading the source, because the recipe runs without -v and
the log shows no subtest names. Worth considering whether
test-codegen-live-neo4j should pass -v for exactly that reason.
notes:
PARTIAL OVERLAP with PR #1489 (bd gqlc-3d0l, agent-c) -- read before claiming.

The closing paragraph here asks "worth considering whether
test-codegen-live-neo4j should pass -v for exactly that reason." PR #1489 DOES
THAT. It is committed at 2bbbf311 and verified live on the PR-BLOCKING arm
(job 97343279326 names all 12 tx rows where that arm previously printed a
single package-level `ok`). So the -v half of this bead is landing; do not
redo it. The recipe's missing -count=1 is a separate and deliberately
documented decision above the recipe and was left alone.

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of this bead's core claim, in case it helps whoever
takes it. I hit exactly this defect class from the other direction on
gqlc-3d0l, before reading this bead. I added six live tx scenarios and could
not tell, from a green live-smoke, whether any of them had executed -- so I
ran a blinding mutation FIRST, before any real one. Later I blinded three more
rows simultaneously and declared 9 reds and 9 greens per row in advance;
measured exactly that (dispatch run 32696442170). That is the manual version
of what this bead wants automated, and it confirms the failure mode is real
rather than theoretical: without those runs I would have had six scenarios of
unknown liveness sitting green in CI.

Also confirms the bead's warning against an aggregate guard. On gqlc-3d0l a
single mutation killed rows on one arm and SURVIVED on two others; a check
phrased over a total would have read healthy. Assert per list, as written
here.

THE PRIMARY ASK (require.NotEmpty per scenario list) IS STILL OPEN AND STILL
WORTH DOING. I am NOT claiming it, deliberately: PR #1489 is open and modifies
test/data/codegen/live_test.go, so a second branch adding assertions to the
same file would conflict with it. Take this AFTER #1489 merges, or coordinate.

One addition I would make to the remedy: whatever assertion goes in, MUTATE
IT -- empty each list in turn and require the run RED, naming which battery
went silent. A require.NotEmpty that is never exercised is the same species of
unwitnessed guard this bead was filed about.
PR #1638 (head f20cd1c0), Closes #1487. Five require.NotEmpty guards at the point of use in TestLiveSmoke.

MEASURED BASELINE, on master, against a real Neo4j 5 container: temporalScenarios emptied -> neo4j-go-v5 ran 23.5s and printed ok, 14 subtests where there were 15, nothing said so. The defect this bead claims is real and now witnessed rather than reasoned.

MUTATION SCREEN, expected verdict declared per row before measuring, live neo4j-go-v5 arm (it serves all four capabilities so it reaches all five guards): readScenarios(4 removed) KILLED, edgeUnionScenarios(1) KILLED, temporalScenarios(1) KILLED, zonedTimeScenarios(1) KILLED, writeScenarios(8) KILLED. Each named only its own battery.

The FIRST screen reported 4 SURVIVED and the guards were not at fault -- it restored between rows with 'git checkout -- <file>', which restores to HEAD, and the guards were uncommitted, so row 1's restore deleted the feature and rows 2-5 ran against master. Re-run after committing, with a per-row tripwire asserting 5 guards present.

DESIGN NOTE for whoever reads this: a standalone top-level test was the obvious shape and is WRONG here. Both PR-blocking live recipes filter with -run (justfile:2266 '-run TestLiveSmoke', justfile:2294 an explicit alternation of test names), so a new top-level test would never be executed by either. The bead's 'at the point of use' is right for a stronger reason than the message-naming it gave.

NOT COVERED, stated so nobody reads more into this: emptying a table is one way a battery goes silent; a scenario whose BODY is gutted still passes and no guard here sees it.

The -v half of this bead was already landed by PR #1489 as the notes above predicted; not redone.
CORRECTION to the DESIGN NOTE paragraph above. It called justfile:2266 and justfile:2294 'both PR-blocking live recipes'. Only the neo4j one is PR-blocking: .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml:50 gates live-smoke-age on 'if: github.event_name != pull_request', so the AGE arm is nightly and manual only (bd gqlc-35yu.8). The design argument is unaffected and in fact stronger -- a standalone top-level test is excluded by BOTH -run filters, so it would never have run on a PR and never on the nightly either. PR #1638's body has been corrected; the wrong wording never reached master.
SECOND CORRECTION, and this one matters more than the first. The DESIGN NOTE above said a standalone top-level test 'would never have executed' under either recipe. That is FALSE and the repo itself falsifies it: internal/liverecipes requires every declared top-level test to be claimed by some half, and split.go:49-79 reads -run as an exact name list rather than go test's unanchored regexp for exactly this reason. PROBED on the branch -- one skipped top-level test dropped into test/data/codegen turns TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt RED with 'TestZZProbeStandaloneTopLevel is a live test no CI job runs: add it to a live recipe's -run'. So the alternative was detectable and loud, not silent.

Point of use is still the right shape, for the weaker and true reasons: no allowlist edit, runs on every arm without anyone choosing which half it belongs in (that choice is asserted nowhere -- gqlc-vh74), and sits against the loop it guards. PR #1638's body now says that instead. I supplied a confident negative I had only read for, and the falsifier took 30 seconds.

title: codegen conformance: the emission test requires temporal_neo4j.go for any carrier-bearing golden
description:
Noted while building gqlc-oz6p (PR #1481), filed rather than ridden on that
diff.

TestTemporalCarriersAreEmittedExactlyWhenReferenced requires, for any golden
whose surface references a neutral temporal carrier, that BOTH temporal.go
and temporal_neo4j.go are present.

That is correct today for one reason only: apache-age-pgx-v5 has no temporal
support, so no AGE golden can bear a carrier and the neo4j-specific half of
the assertion is never reached for a non-neo4j target.

It over-reaches the moment that stops being true. gqlc-mv3r / gqlc-oeqi give
AGE temporal support; on that day an AGE golden bears a carrier, has no
temporal_neo4j.go (correctly — its bridge would be temporal_age.go or
whatever the AGE renderer names it), and this test fails for a reason that
has nothing to do with a defect.

Fix: make the bridge-file requirement per-target rather than hardcoded to
the neo4j filename — the assertion wants "the target emitted ITS bridge",
not "the neo4j bridge exists". Whoever lands AGE temporals will trip this;
better that they find a bead than a puzzle.

File: internal/codegen/conformance/ (the emission test added in d69d9c13).
notes:
PR #1720 opened 2026-08-29 from fix/gqlc-fg0r-per-target-bridge-file (head 928f9ebc). Bridge read by shape (temporal_<driver>.go) rather than by neo4j's filename, in BOTH places the old name appeared: the requirement and the reference-scan exclusion. The exclusion mattered as much — a bridge names the carriers it converts, so an unexcluded temporal_age.go would satisfy the trigger by its own presence and the do-not-emit half would never fire.

Classification moved to readTemporalEmission (asserts nothing) and the requirement to temporalEmission.breach() (returns a string), so both run over synthetic package shapes the corpus cannot hold. That split was forced by measurement, not taste: at e967e4e2 the bridge requirement was still asserted inline and M4 (delete it outright) SURVIVED; it is KILLED at 928f9ebc.

7-row battery + a blinding pass in the PR body. The blinding pass is the honest number: with TestTemporalEmissionIsReadPerTarget skipped, 4 of 5 mutants survive the whole package. M6 SURVIVED and is reported as latent-not-inert, with M7 (delete the 19 temporal_neo4j.go from a COPY of the corpus, read via GQLC_CONFORMANCE_CHILD_ROOT) reaching it by name.

internal/codegen/prepare_test.go:868 carries the same filename pair but is a partition, and line 974 fails closed on an unclassified emitted file. Left alone, deliberately.

Gates: just gates 10/11. Red arm is just vuln = gqlc-irvs (environmental, GOTOOLCHAIN). An earlier run also showed lint + codegen-fence red with 'parallel golangci-lint is running' = gqlc-49pc; both green run individually. No design bead blocks this, so no review is owed (V.2) — merging on green.
close_reason:
Merged as 1a42a553 (PR #1720). GH #1483 auto-closed.

The over-reach was in TWO places, not the one the bead named: the requirement (os.Stat on temporal_neo4j.go) and the reference-scan exclusion (carrierDeclarationFiles). The second is the one that would have gone unnoticed — a bridge names the carriers it converts, so an unexcluded temporal_age.go satisfies the trigger by its own presence and the do-not-emit half stops firing for that package. Fixed by one shape predicate serving both: temporal_<driver>.go.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED. My first shape (the branch's first commit) kept the three requirements asserted inline in the corpus test. M4 — delete the bridge requirement outright — SURVIVED, because every golden in the tracked corpus satisfies all three arms, so no assertion written against that corpus can fire while it stands. The requirement is now a value (temporalEmission.breach() returns the breach as a string) and the per-target test declares the expected breach per row, including the arm the corpus can never exercise. M4 is KILLED at the merged sha. The branch's second commit exists only because the row was run.

BLINDING PASS, which is the honest account of what this adds: all five guard mutations are killed by TestTemporalEmissionIsReadPerTarget alone, so zero findings would have certified one test. Blinded with t.Skip and re-run over the whole package, 4 of 5 SURVIVE (M1, M2, M4, M5); only M3 is caught elsewhere.

M6 (corpus test stops asserting the breach) SURVIVED and is reported as such. It is latent, not inert: M7 reaches it by deleting the 19 temporal_neo4j.go from a COPY of test/data/codegen and reading it through GQLC_CONFORMANCE_CHILD_ROOT, which fires the assertion by name against .../valid/property_date/golden/neo4j-go-v5. Tracked corpus verified intact after (19 files, git status clean) — the copy is what made -update unnecessary.

NOT RIDDEN ON THIS DIFF: internal/codegen/prepare_test.go:868 carries the same filename pair, but it is a partition rather than a requirement and line 974 fails closed on an unclassified emitted file with a message naming it. Whoever lands AGE temporals gets a clear refusal there, not a puzzle, so no bead.

Gates: just gates 10/11 locally; the red arm is just vuln (gqlc-irvs, GOTOOLCHAIN, environmental) and CI's govulncheck was SUCCESS, which confirms it. An earlier local run also showed lint and codegen-fence red with 'parallel golangci-lint is running' (gqlc-49pc, another agent holding the lock); both green run individually. All 7 required contexts green on the PR.
