title: design: multi-file graph type scoping — the one-graph-type-per-file rule, and the catalogue COPY OF/LIKE resolve against
description:
FILED by agent-a 2026-08-24T03:2xZ, triaging gqlc-h9n.1. This is a decision
nobody has been asked to make since 2026-07-28, and it is the reason a P1
product bead has sat in status `blocked` for a month with no live blocker.

## HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the shape recurs

gqlc-h9n.1's ONLY `blocks` dependency is gqlc-h9n.8, and h9n.8 CLOSED on
2026-07-28 (PR #457). The bead's status field still reads `blocked`. What is
actually holding it is a sentence in its description — "sequenced behind
gqlc-h9n.8 and behind the unmade one-graph-type-per-file decision" — and a line
in the epic's notes: "h9n.1 (one-graph-type-per-file rule decision needed)".

A prose hold is not a hold. The router enforces `blocks` edges and the
status field; it cannot read a sentence. So this bead filed a real blocker where
the prose was, and gqlc-h9n.1 is now blocked BY THIS BEAD.

## THE QUESTION

`COPY OF <graph type reference>` names a graph TYPE declared elsewhere. gqlc has
no catalogue and no multi-file scoping, so there is nowhere for the reference to
resolve. Deciding how it resolves is prior to implementing it, and two
reasonable implementers would build different things — the design-gate test.

At minimum the design must settle:

  1. IS THERE A ONE-GRAPH-TYPE-PER-FILE RULE? If yes, a file's path or its
     single declaration is the reference's target and the catalogue is
     the filesystem. If no, references need a name resolution scheme within
     and across files. This is the named unmade decision.
  2. WHAT IS THE CATALOGUE, concretely — is it built from the files gqlc is
     invoked on, from a manifest, or from a search path? What happens on a
     dangling reference, and what does the diagnostic point at?
  3. DOES IT APPLY TO `LIKE` TOO (GG04, gqlc-h9n.12, today
     `ErrUnsupportedSource`)? `LIKE` is the sibling graph type source and
     plausibly shares the whole mechanism. Say so either way — if the answer
     is that they differ, that is worth writing down once rather than
     rediscovering at implementation time.
  4. CYCLES. `A COPY OF B`, `B COPY OF A`. Detected where, reported how.

## SCOPE NOTE — THIS IS NOT A CONFORMANCE EMERGENCY, AND THE PRIORITY SAYS SO

Per gqlc-h9n's own framing, Annex D assigns feature IDs only to OPTIONAL
features, and declining an optional feature is conformant. `COPY OF` is
optional. The bug half of gqlc-h9n.1 — the SILENT DROP, which was the real
defect because the diagnostic landed on innocent code — was discharged by #392;
`ErrUnsupportedSource` is pinned by 11 corpus files today. So gqlc is correct
and honest right now, and this is a feature we choose to add, not a violation
we must fix.

Filed P2 accordingly. gqlc-h9n.1 carries P1 from July and I have left it alone
rather than re-price a bead I am not working; a future reader should not take
that P1 as a measurement.

DONE WHEN the decisions above are written into gqlc-h9n.1's notes — approach,
alternatives rejected with reasons, files touched, what tests prove it, and
which corpus manifest entries flip from `unsupported` to `resolves`.
(`12.6-graph-type-statement/copy_of_source.gql` and the ten under
`17-references/` already name gqlc-h9n.1 as the bead that would flip them.)
close_reason: Design merged to master as 3bfa8c1c (PR #1478): docs/adr/0034 + CONTEXT.md Catalogue entry. Executable plan appended to gqlc-h9n.1's notes. All four bead questions decided; scope-note correction recorded (COPY OF is mandatory core, not Annex D optional).

title: AGE lists of temporal properties: document the dialect gap or admit non-zoned element widths
notes:
CONTEXT (agent-h, filed from gqlc-49hu). ADR 0033 admits the four temporal property widths on AGE as scalars but leaves LISTS of temporals refused there (age/types.go refuses a list element equal to goInstant, and the neutral carriers inherit the refusal). Reason deferred: the flat <field>Offset sidecar has no per-element home, so zoned element widths have no encoding; admitting only the non-zoned ones (list<DATE>, list<LOCALTIME>, list<DURATION>) is coherent but was not designed under gqlc-49hu to keep that bead's scope honest. Meanwhile neo4j emits []Date etc. (see many_columns_mixed_temporal_list, schema_list_temporal_property), so this is a real dialect divergence — currently loud at generate time, which is the acceptable resting state.

DESIGN QUESTION. Either (a) admit non-zoned temporal list elements on AGE with per-element encodings matching the scalar table (gqlc-35yu.11) and document zoned lists as the remaining gap, or (b) record the whole family as a documented dialect gap in an ADR and keep the refusal. Two defensible answers — if still tied after research, take both to agent-a rather than deciding in prose. Prerequisite reading: ADR 0033, gqlc-mv3r's merged encode/decode helpers, and the sidecar collision machinery in age/errors.go.
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
close_reason: Design merged: ADR 0036 at origin/master 23a30399 (PR #2093). Ratifies non-zoned temporal list admission at every depth, names zoned lists as the refused dialect gap, records the depth>=2 encode defect (bug gqlc-jc8mc). Implementation-ready plan written into execution bead gqlc-vhvz7.

title: bd-gh-sync: an allowed pull silently clobbers priority, assignee, issue_type and local-only labels
description:
