against areqag/gqlc issue #1156 (labels priority::high, type::task, class:author; no assignees):

  priority     0                            -> 1
  issue_type   bug                          -> task
  assignee     probe-assignee               -> null
  labels       [class:author,sentinel-label] -> [class:author]
  notes / acceptance_criteria / design / parent / estimate: PRESERVED

So bd derives priority, issue_type and the whole label set from GitHub's labels, and assignee from GitHub's assignees. The eligibility rule in .githooks/bd-gh-sync compares exactly three things -- status, description prefix, and the two edit times -- and NONE of these four. Every bead the plan emits an ALLOW for therefore has all four rewritten from GitHub, unreported and uncounted; the summary line says 'pulled N bead(s)' and an agent reads that as a body edit.

Blast radius, and why it is not zero: ALLOW is reached only where the bodies or the states actually differ (a bead with desc == gh_body and status == gh_state is dropped one line earlier), so this does not fire on the steady state. But the closure transition -- bd open, GH closed -- is an ALLOW, and it is how every merge ends. That is the common case, and it nulls the assignee of a bead somebody was holding. Same family as the memory 'releasing a bead is TWO fields': an unassigned bead in a non-ready status routes to nobody.

FALSIFIER for anyone who wants to check it before acting: fresh scratch dir, git init, bd init --db, one bead with a local assignee and priority and an external_ref to any open mirrored issue, run the scoped pull above, diff bd show before and after. Note the pull is watermarked per DB -- the second scoped pull in one DB is a silent no-op, so use a fresh DB.

REMEDY, not decided here: either widen the eligibility rule to hold a bead whose priority/assignee/type/labels would move, or re-assert those four from a pre-pull snapshot after the sync returns. The second is cheaper and keeps the closure pull working. The first is symmetric with how the rule already treats an unrepresentable status.
notes:
HELD AT P2 by agent-a, 2026-08-24, under protocol/V.3.3 (bead gqlc-f5m5), while 14 sibling machinery beads went to P3. It passes V.3.2 test two — the fleet cannot do its work without it — and the demonstration is this very bead's parent: an ALLOWed pull rewrites priority, assignee, issue_type and the label set from GitHub, unreported. The re-numbering I am doing right now writes exactly the field it clobbers, so this defect can silently revert the decree's own execution. This session's startup hook ran bd-gh-sync live ('pulled 0, held 1'), so it is not dormant.
MERGED 2026-08-30 as PR #2000, squash 665d6f56 (verified present in origin/master:.githooks/bd-gh-sync, not merely in a closed PR).

Remedy taken: the second of the two the description offers — re-assert priority, issue_type, assignee and labels from the pre-pull snapshot the script already takes, scoped to the beads the run actually pulled. Holding was rejected on measurement: of all 800 issues on the mirror exactly one carries a GH assignee and it is open, so no ALLOWed pull here can supply one, while holding would have withheld the closure pull of nearly every bead an agent was working.

The re-assert is read back rather than trusted, because 'bd update' prints its success line for a write that moved nothing; a bead whose fields did not come back is named on stderr and counted on the summary line. Silent in the steady state.

Battery: 2 asserted baselines, 9 KILLED, 2 declared SURVIVED, 0 WRONG, 0 screened out; blinded pass confirms each mutant dies on its own field with the summary-line claim removed. Two things it does NOT cover, declared in the PR body: the hook's exit status, and the 'or ""' on assignee (unkillable here, not merely unkilled — the sole assigned issue #1970 is open).

Not absorbed: the same pull also rewrites the bead TITLE, a fifth field with no append-only gate. Filed as gqlc-wl57h.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen/neo4j: walkListElemBody's ColumnNode case is unreachable from the front end
description:
PR #1387 covered walkListElemBody's ColumnEdge and ColumnEdgeUnion cases with variable-length edge patterns (VarLengthEdgeColumn, VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn in testdata/corpus_queries.cypher). Its ColumnNode case is still unrun, and no query text reaches it today.

Measured: resolveType returns ErrOutOfR0Scope for a list-of-nodes projection, and nodes(p) needs a path binding, which the resolver refuses with 'query construct not supported at resolver stage R0: path binding'. So there is no .cypher text that makes the resolver hand back a ResolvedList whose Element is a ResolvedNode.

Two ways this can be closed and the choice is part of the work: either the front end grows a construct that produces a list of nodes, in which case a corpus query covers the arm the way the two edge arms are covered now; or the arm is dead and should be deleted, in which case deleting it must leave every test green and that is the evidence.

Do not close this by hand-building a Validated shape the front end cannot produce and calling the arm covered. That is a row asserting the emitter agrees with itself.

The unreachability is written down at the fixture, in the comment block above the six added queries in internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_queries.cypher.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on [deleted:gqlc-nhv64].

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.

--- 2026-09-02, agent-m: executed. PR #2158 open, review bead [deleted:gqlc-q7ni1] (unassigned, class:reviewer).

VERDICT ON THE BEAD'S QUESTION: the ColumnNode arm STAYS. It is unreachable and
it is not deletable, and the two facts have different causes.

  Unreachable: resolveType (internal/resolver/resolve.go:1822) refuses a
  list-of-nodes projection at R0. The other two ResolvedList construction sites
  cannot originate an entity element -- scope.go's variable-length edge binding
  builds ResolvedEdge/ResolvedEdgeUnion and never a ResolvedNode, and unify only
  propagates an element both arguments already carry. Coverage confirms:
  -coverpkg over ./internal/codegen/..., eighteen blocks in that switch, and
  ColumnNode is the only CASE with no covered block at all.

  Not deletable: deleting the arm leaves `go build ./...` green and
  `go test -count=1 ./internal/codegen/...` entirely green -- no test in this
  repository defends it -- but golangci-lint's exhaustive reds with "missing
  cases in switch of type codegen.ColumnKind: codegen.ColumnNode", because that
  switch has no default. The only way to satisfy the linter after a deletion is
  to add one, and .golangci.yml sets default-signifies-exhaustive, so that would
  retire the exhaustive check for that switch permanently. A dead arm traded for
  a dead guard is a bad trade.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING was not a deletion but a signal. Nothing in the tree
failed if the refusal were lifted, so the emitter arm would silently become live
and uncovered. TestListElementEntityProjectionsAreRefusedAtR0 is that signal and
its failure message names the arm to go and cover.

FILED, NOT RIDDEN: gqlc-7hp5g (P3) -- render_queries.go:771-773 claims a new
ColumnKind makes buildListElemPlan and the emission switch "fail to compile".
Measured false here. It is the linter, not the compiler, and someone trusting
that comment will read a green `go build` as sufficient evidence.

Five-row mutation battery, all KILLED with per-row declared victims; table in
the PR body. `just gates` 12/12 green locally.
CLOSED 2026-09-02 after verifying the work landed. PR #2158 merged; the bead was left in_progress, which is the lane dying between merge and close rather than unfinished work.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT, not by the PR's state: the branch's only file, internal/resolver/sumdefaults_internal_test.go, is byte-identical between chore/gqlc-rl3c-listelem-columnnode-unreachable and origin/master. The local branch shows commits 'ahead' only because a squash merge leaves no tip on master.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen/age: migrate the capture sweep onto internal/codegen/emitscan
description:
PR #1387 lifted the capture-sweep analyser out of internal/codegen/age/capture_test.go into a backend-agnostic package, internal/codegen/emitscan, and drove it from a new internal/codegen/neo4j/capture_test.go. That closed gqlc-3o3p: the neo4j emitter is now swept.

It did NOT touch age/, because a separate lane held that package at the time. So the analyser now exists twice: emitscan carries Candidates, Scope, PackageDecls, FreeIdents, ReferencedIdents, DeclaredIdents, BodyLocals and the Sweep differential; age_test.go and capture_test.go carry their own copies of all of them, as EmissionSuite methods and free functions.

Two copies of a guard's analyser is one copy that can be fixed and one that cannot. The work is to delete age's copies and have age's TestNoEmittedNameTakesAQueryParameterName, TestNoParameterArityPutsAQueryChosenNameInScope and TestOnlyPackageLevelNamesFollowAColumnName call emitscan instead.

Acceptance: the age suite must still fail on the same emitter mutations it fails on today, and that must be measured rather than assumed — pick at least one mutation per test, declare the verdict first, run it before and after the migration.

Note what the split is NOT. emitscan deliberately does not own fixture loading, arity shapes, or reporting: those are per-backend, and neo4j's capture_test.go keeps its own captureArities and its own corpus. age's ageFixture corpus loader stays where it is.
notes: PR #1891 open, rebased onto ec42bd9e. Two mutation batteries measured; verdicts and the one wrong prediction are in the PR body.
close_reason: Merged as #1891 (squashed to 88376f86). Verified on origin/master: age_test.go no longer declares freeIdents; capture_test.go calls emitscan.Sweep. Two mutation batteries measured, tables in the PR body.

title: PR bodies keep failing the Closes-N gate because branch names carry no bead id, and the failure reads as a test failure
description:
MEASURED TONIGHT, THREE TIMES, across three independent lanes: PR #1382 (fleetctl restart blockers), PR #1387 (codegen/neo4j coverage), and one earlier. Each cost roughly an hour of a lane's wall time, and one lane died before it could diagnose it.

## The shape

The tidy job's step 7, 'check PR body carries Closes #N for beads with GH mirror', runs .github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py. That checker resolves a bead for the PR from either a 'Bead:' / 'Refs:' line in the body OR from a bead id embedded in the branch name. When the body carries a closing keyword but NEITHER source names a bead, it exits 1 with an accurate message: 'the PR body closes #N, but no bead resolves for this PR'.

The message is good. The problem is that nobody reads it, for two compounding reasons:

1. THE FAILURE PRESENTS AS A TEST FAILURE. tidy gates lint, test and codegen-fence. When tidy fails those three report 'skipping'. An author glancing at the check table sees a mostly-empty board and reasonably concludes CI is still running or that something broke in their code. Both lanes I watched went looking at their own diff first.

2. NOTHING WARNS BEFORE THE PUSH. The body does not exist until the PR is opened, so no local hook can see it. The first signal is a red check twenty-odd seconds into a CI run the author is no longer watching.

## The root cause, and why the remedy belongs at the branch

Every one of the three PRs had CORRECT GH issue numbers. Verified for #1387: Closes #998/#985/#675 map exactly to gqlc-8bl0/gqlc-sal9/gqlc-3o3p. So this is not authors guessing numbers. It is purely that the checker had no bead to hold the correct numbers against.

The branch-name fallback exists precisely for this and is not being used, because the repo's own worktree recipe in CLAUDE.md ('## Working directory') shows:

    git worktree add --no-track -b <branch-name> ../<repo>-<bead-slug> origin/master

The DIRECTORY carries the bead slug. The BRANCH does not, and the branch is the half the checker reads. Branches produced by that recipe tonight looked like fix/fleetctl-restart-deploy-selfheal and fix/codegen-neo4j-2-coverage — descriptive, and invisible to the gate.

## Candidate remedies, in rough order of cost

(a) Amend the CLAUDE.md worktree recipe so the branch name carries the bead id, matching the directory. Cheapest, no code, and it makes the existing fallback work as designed. Does not help a branch already cut.
(b) Add the 'Bead: <id>' line to whatever produces PR bodies here, or ship a just recipe that opens the PR with the line prefilled from the branch.
(c) Have the checker's failure ALSO surface at push time by having pre-push warn when the branch name carries no bead id and the branch has commits — advisory only, since it cannot see a body that does not exist yet.

(a) and (c) compose and neither is exclusive with (b).

## FALSIFIER

Cut a branch whose name contains no bead id, open a PR whose body contains 'Closes #<any real issue>' and no 'Bead:' line, and observe: tidy fails at step 7, lint/test/codegen-fence report 'skipping', and the check table reads like a run in progress. Then add a 'Bead: <id>' line to the body and observe the edited trigger re-run the gate green with no push and no new commit.

## Not verified

I have not checked whether the agent worktrees created by fleetctl use a branch naming convention that DOES carry the bead id -- if they do, this defect is specific to hand-rolled and factory worktrees and the remedy is narrower than (a) suggests.
notes:
RESOLVED the bead's own 'Not verified' item: fleetctl agent worktrees do NOT carry bead ids in branch names, so the defect is host-wide and remedy (a) is NOT narrower.

Evidence, read 2026-08-23 at origin/master:
1. fleet/bin/fleetctl cmd_up creates every agent worktree with 'git worktree add --detach "$wt" origin/master'. fleetctl never names a branch at all; the worktree is detached.
2. The branch is cut by the agent, per fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md 'Working a bead' step 1: 'git fetch origin && git checkout --no-track -b <type>/<slug> origin/master'. <type>/<slug> has no bead-id component. So agents produce exactly the same descriptive branch names as hand-rolled and factory worktrees.
3. Measured over the 60 most recently merged PRs: 3 head branches matched check-pr-closes.py BEAD_IN_BRANCH, 57 did not. Several carried a bead's SUFFIX with no gqlc- prefix (fix/sync-drift-x98l-mdhr, fix/hooks-hygiene-7ysc-qh9z-qcen), which the checker cannot read because its pattern is anchored on gqlc-. That shape is worse than a plain descriptive name: it looks to a human like it names beads.
close_reason:
MERGED as PR #1411 (squash, 2026-08-23). Remedies (a) and (c). Verified on master: .githooks/warn-missing-bead-id exists there and .githooks/pre-push invokes it.

(a) CLAUDE.md 'Working directory' and AGENTS.md 'Workflow: stacked branches' now prescribe <type>/<bead-id>-<slug>, and name the 'Bead: <bead-id>' line that rescues a branch already cut. The recipe code block deliberately keeps its <branch-name> token: worktree-upstream-test.sh section C evals that line after substituting the token, and angle brackets left in an eval'd string are shell redirection.

(c) .githooks/warn-missing-bead-id warns at push time, advisory on every path, run last by pre-push after every refusal. 24-row suite at .githooks/tests/pre-push-bead-id-test.sh. Section D pins its pattern byte-for-byte to check-pr-closes.py's own BEAD_IN_BRANCH; section C extracts that same pattern and runs the documented branch form through it, so a reverted document fails.

(b) NOT done: the justfile was owned by another lane. Filed as gqlc-c87g at P3, with the argument for why it is still worth doing after (a) and (c) — it is the only remedy that reaches a branch already cut, and the one branch shape (c) deliberately stays silent about, a name matching the pattern but naming no bead.

RESOLVED the bead's 'not verified' item: fleetctl agent worktrees do NOT carry bead ids, so this is host-wide and remedy (a) is not narrower. fleetctl cmd_up creates each agent worktree with 'git worktree add --detach' and names no branch at all; the branch comes from agent-protocol.md step 1, 'git checkout --no-track -b <type>/<slug>', which has no bead-id component. Over the sixty most recently merged PRs, three head branches matched BEAD_IN_BRANCH and fifty-seven did not. Several carried a bead's SUFFIX with no prefix (fix/sync-drift-x98l-mdhr), which the checker cannot read and which is worse than a plain descriptive name because it reads to a human as if it names beads. The agent-protocol half is filed as gqlc-cn49 at P2, with the one-row extension to section C that would prove it; fleet/ was owned by another lane.

VERIFIED ON A REAL PUSH, not only in the fixture: branch tmp/uz3c-warner-probe-no-id was pushed to origin over ssh, the advisory printed to the terminal, and the push succeeded with status zero. That branch was then deleted from the remote and locally, confirmed by git ls-remote returning nothing. The negative direction was observed on the same remote too: this bead's own branch, fix/gqlc-uz3c-branch-bead-id, printed nothing on any of its three pushes.

MUTATION SCREEN, thirteen mutants, all killed: unwiring pre-push, neutering the warner, making it refuse, dropping the dedupe, the ahead-of-master arm, the master skip and the zero-sha arm, drifting the pattern, reverting either document, and removing either of the two message phrases. One guard was found UNKILLABLE — a '(delete)' string test made redundant by the case statement's fallback arm — and was removed rather than left as a guard nobody tested; its comment now records the measurement.

A STALE CLAIM CORRECTED MID-BRANCH: the warning first described the 'skipping' presentation lint/test/codegen-fence took when tidy failed. That is no longer true. PR #1323 removed those needs: edges the same night for an unrelated reason, so a tidy failure now shows as one red cell among green ones. Demoted to history in the header and replaced in the message by what a reader can act on: the failure appears under 'tidy', a job name that says nothing about bead ids, and a body edit alone re-runs the gate.

NOT VERIFIED: no PR was opened from a bead-idless branch with a closing keyword to watch this PR's own gate refuse it end to end. The falsifier in the description was taken as already measured, three times, on the night it was filed.

NOT COVERED BY DESIGN: a branch whose name matches the pattern but names no bead ('fix/gqlc-parser-rewrite') stays silent and then fails the gate. Deciding it means reading the ledger from a push hook. Stated in the warner's Limits header.

title: gate-pushed-commits prints a fixed /tmp path as advice, teaching the collision the scratch rule forbids
description:
Found by the new .githooks/tests/scratch-literals-test.sh (bd gqlc-wm3x), which sweeps tracked shell/just/instruction-markdown sources for a /tmp path with a fixed name.

.githooks/gate-pushed-commits:146 prints, as a remedy line to an agent:

    git log -1 --format=%B <sha> > /tmp/m && .githooks/commit-msg /tmp/m

That is the exact shape CLAUDE.md's '## Scratch space' section forbids, and it is worse than a private violation because it TEACHES it: the hook is telling an agent to write a chosen name, and two agents screening a commit at the same time both write /tmp/m. The measured cost of that shape is bd gqlc-b8gd — one session's uncommitted work restored into another's worktree, cleanly, with no conflict.

It is allowlisted in scratch-literals-test.sh rather than fixed, because gate-pushed-commits was not this lane's file during the 2026-08-23 parallel wave. The allowlist entry says so and carries this bead.

FIX: reword the advice to allocate, e.g.

    m=$(mktemp) && git log -1 --format=%B <sha> > "$m" && .githooks/commit-msg "$m"; rm -f "$m"

Then DELETE the corresponding line from ALLOWED in .githooks/tests/scratch-literals-test.sh — the suite has a staleness row that will go red and name it if you forget.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged in PR #1399 (squashed to master; verified with git cat-file that .githooks/gate-pushed-commits on origin/master now names mktemp twice). The refusal remedy now allocates its scratch file with mktemp, quotes it, and removes it with rm -f on the way out, instead of the old fixed name under /tmp. The stale ALLOWED entry in scratch-literals-test.sh was deleted with it, as the bead instructed; that suite is green at twenty-six rows.

The guard is three new rows in gate-pushed-commits-test.sh, asserted on the RENDERED refusal rather than by grepping the hook source. The source is already swept by scratch-literals-test.sh, so a second grep there would only re-measure the same bytes. What the new rows add is that the advice an agent actually SEES is runnable and self-cleaning: it names mktemp, it names rm -f, and it spells no fixed scratch path. The third row is the negative half. Without it, an advice line that both called mktemp AND kept the old fixed path would pass the first two.

RED first, measured: all three rows failed against the unfixed hook, twenty-eight passed and three failed. Mutations after the fix, each victim declared beforehand and each killing exactly that: restoring the fixed-path spelling kills two rows (mktemp, no-fixed-name) and leaves the cleanup row green; deleting the trailing rm -f kills one row alone. Neither mutation broke parsing (screened with bash -n) and neither was a no-op (screened with cmp against a pristine copy).

title: resolver: decide whether ErrAmbiguousBinding survives the natively-plural widening
description:
Follow-up from gqlc-icfq, measured on PR #1372 and deliberately NOT taken there.

gqlc-icfq is right that commitUnlabelledRound enters the plural lane only on commit()'s widened flag, so a binding whose inferred set is NATIVELY plural is deferred to ErrAmbiguousBinding even when every candidate declares the projected property — the exact reasoning PR #1032 uses to justify committing the WIDENED plural set. Fail-closed, not unsound: accepting it is a widening in the same direction.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE. Measured in worktree gqlc-query-resolver at 4a478f85, by committing the plural set for every still-pending binding at inferUnlabelled's terminal refusal (after the endpointNarrowing retry, so the narrowing lane is untouched):

  - TestCorpusSweepManifest: zero DIFFERENT VERDICT, zero same-sentinel-different-detail, fourteen DIFFERENT SENTINEL. No query flipped between accept and refuse.
  - TestSweepReachesEverySentinel FAILED: 'no cell of the cross product refuses with ErrAmbiguousBinding'. The deferral is that sentinel's ONLY reachable site, so narrowing it retires the sentinel.
  - Adding '&& covered' to the extension separates nothing: all fourteen moved cells are covered. Same for the attested reading.

Of the fourteen, three become ErrAmbiguousLabel (whole-node projections, e.g. invalid/ambiguous_unlabelled_binding.cypher 'MATCH (x)-[:AUTHORED]->(p:Post) RETURN x') and the rest become the more specific ErrUnknownProperty.

THE DECISION. docs/specs/resolver-stage-r1.md declares ErrAmbiguousBinding and carries an explicit naming defence for it AGAINST ErrAmbiguousLabel (search 'Naming defence'). Two options:

  (a) Retire it: drop from AllSentinels, amend resolver-stage-r1 and -r5, regenerate the sweep manifest.
  (b) Keep it reachable by making a whole-node projection of a Phase-B-inferred plural binding refuse with ErrAmbiguousBinding rather than ErrAmbiguousLabel — which is arguably what the r1 naming defence already asks for. That recovers three of the fourteen and leaves the ErrUnknownProperty ones correctly more specific.

CURRENT STATE IS PINNED, both directions, by internal/resolver/resolver_test.go TestANativelyPluralBindingDefersEvenWhenEveryCandidateDeclaresTheProperty (PR #1372). It uses invalid/schemas/narrowed_ends_disagree.gql, where MEMBER_OF runs from Author and Author&Editor to one Guild type so (p) is natively plural and 'id' is INT NOT NULL on both. That test's first assertion is what goes RED when this bead is taken; it must be rewritten, not deleted.
close_reason: DECIDED: ErrAmbiguousBinding SURVIVES, by the bead's option (b). Shipped as PR #1393, merged to master as fb1ee06b. What settled it was not the posture argument but errors.go, which already drew the line the code did not honour: ErrAmbiguousLabel is documented as a LABEL SET whose proper-superset satisfying set has more than one element and disclaims the other case BY NAME ('Not overloaded onto ErrAmbiguousBinding either, whose documented meaning is Phase B inference failure at an unlabelled binding'), while ErrAmbiguousBinding is documented as an unlabelled binding whose candidate set has more than one node type. A whole-entity projection of an unlabelled binding whose plural set Phase B committed is the second sentence verbatim, and refProjectionType returned the first sentinel for it. So option (b) was not a posture choice, it was the code disagreeing with its own declared contract. FALSIFIER, measured at master 412b9612 on valid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql: one binding, one candidate set, one projection, two sentinels selected by an OPTIONAL MATCH that touches neither. 'MATCH (p:Person)-[q:WORKS_AT]->(c) / OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[h:HAS_DESK]->(d:Desk) / RETURN c' gave 'ambiguous label: c is satisfied by more than one declared node type: Company, Company&Large'; the same query without the OPTIONAL hop gave 'ambiguous binding: cannot uniquely infer type of unlabelled binding c'. The first is PR #1032's widened lane, where commit() substituted attainable for a singleton inferred and the refusal moved to projection time; the second is Phase B's terminal deferral. FIX: scope.pluralByInference records which writer put a name in nodeCands, refProjectionType picks on it. ErrAmbiguousLabel keeps the labelled case, which remains its only fail-site, so no sentinel is retired. Blast radius from the corpus sweep manifest: zero verdicts, two cells, both invalid/plural_endpoint_carried_hop_property_stays_plural.cypher against the two copies of that schema, plus the one TestInvalid mapping entry that moves with them. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR gqlc-icfq: the deferral is no longer ErrAmbiguousBinding's only reachable site, so the natively-plural widening icfq describes no longer retires a sentinel docs/specs/resolver-stage-r1.md declares and defends. That was the sole reason PR #1372 declined it. Whoever takes icfq next should re-run the fourteen-cell measurement in its close reason: it was taken before this split and its 'TestSweepReachesEverySentinel then FAILS' result should no longer hold. THREE MUTANTS SURVIVED and their code is not in the merge. A carry seed of the provenance across branchState, an Export write, and a BindNodeCands write were all written first and all SURVIVED, so all three were deleted rather than shipped unguarded: Phase A1 precedes Phase B so no labelled re-bind can inherit an inference entry, and Export records a nodeCands entry only for a bare 'WITH v', which is itself the refusal, so no carry can ever hold one. The lane has exactly one writer. Five mutations of what remains — reverting the choice, dropping the provenance, dropping the writer, severing the nodeTable lane, flipping the default — are each KILLED, and each still KILLED with the dominant guard TestCorpusSweepManifest blinded. Every row was compile-screened with 'go test -c -o /dev/null' first, so none is a kill by the compiler. NOT VERIFIED: no live codegen backend was exercised against the moved sentinel beyond CI's live-smoke, which passed but reaches no resolver refusal path; and I did not check whether any generator or CLI surface branches on ErrAmbiguousLabel — repo-wide grep found the identifier only inside internal/resolver, which is weaker than reading the callers.

title: hooks: three claude-pre-bash rows fail on the CI runner and pass everywhere else
description:
Observed on PR #1368 (an internal/tools/tmpreap change touching no hook file), CI run 32631514489, job 97174932143, at base origin/master 4a478f85.

just test-hooks reported '222 passed, 3 failed'. The three:

  FAIL - unresolvable cwd is refused, not skipped (expected verdict deny-unverifiable-repo, got allow-no-sha)
  FAIL - unresolvable cwd refuses end-to-end (expected deny-unresolvable-dir, got silent)
  FAIL - an unanswerable object probe refuses end-to-end (expected deny-unanswerable-objects, got silent)

All three live in .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh.

Falsifiers already collected:
- The same suite run locally on the same tree: 225 passed, 0 failed.
- 'gh run rerun --failed' on the SAME sha: test passed, 8m13s. No code changed between the two runs.
- master's own push run at 4a478f85 was green.

So the rows are nondeterministic on the GitHub runner. All three expect a DENY and got an ALLOW or a silence, which is the fail-OPEN direction: whatever makes them flaky makes the guard permissive, not strict. That is the reason this is worth chasing rather than muting -- a guard that fails open on a runner is a guard that is absent exactly when nobody is watching.

Not investigated: whether the runner's environment (no writable /proc? a different git? the sandboxed HOME landed in PR #1363) is what flips them. Filed from the tmpreap lane, which does not own .githooks.
close_reason: Root cause measured, and it is NOT the runner and NOT the HOME sandbox from the adjacent PR. git rev-parse --short=eight draws an ALL-DECIMAL abbreviation about once in forty-three runs, and .githooks/claude-pre-bash deliberately demotes an all-decimal token out of the anchored-citation tier via DECIMAL_TOKEN_RE. The three nondeterministic rows are exactly the arms that need an anchored citation, so on such a draw the set went empty and the hook fell permissive. Reproduced two ways: directly, where an eight-character abbreviation containing a letter is DENIED while an otherwise identical all-digit one is SILENT from an unresolvable cwd; and by pointing the four affected rows at the fixture's all-decimal sha, which reproduced all three reported failures verbatim including 'got allow-no-sha' and 'got silent'. The suite already documented this same hazard for its uppercase rows and fixed it there with the full forty; these four rows had been left on the short form. Fix: cite ORPHAN_SHA_FULL, add a fixture_check that the fixture sha is not all-decimal, and add a deterministic row pinning the demotion itself. Row count and row-name digest pins updated. Mutations: C2 killed the fixture check, C3 killed the new row plus one pre-existing row, both still parsing. NOT VERIFIED: the fix was not observed across a CI sample large enough to witness the one-in-forty-three draw, so confidence rests on the reproduction, not on absence of recurrence. Landed in the merged hooks-suites PR.

title: 7 beads are permanently divergent from their GH mirror; neither sync direction can close the gap
description:
Split out of gqlc-e9lh, whose lane fixed the REPORTING of this and deliberately did not fix the divergence.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 over 784 beads and 806 issues. Seven beads whose status agrees with their GH mirror but whose GH body is not a prefix of the bead description, so the pull holds them with bd-description-not-a-prefix-of-gh-body:

  gqlc-xqf6 / GH #1304, gqlc-l45j / #933, gqlc-3eyw / #645, gqlc-w6bz / #977,
  gqlc-5ckc / #958, gqlc-cgat / #906, gqlc-eb5j / #716

Six of the seven are bd AHEAD of GitHub (gqlc-eb5j carries a '## CORRECTION' block GitHub never received; #958 has an EMPTY body against 888 characters in bd). gqlc-l45j is the one exception, a 'SCOPE NARROWED' banner prepended on GitHub.

WHY IT IS DURABLE. The pull is RIGHT to hold them: pulling would destroy the bd-side amendment. The push path only mints issues for unmirrored beads and closes stale mirrors; it never updates an existing issue body. So neither direction resolves them.

WHAT gqlc-e9lh's LANE DID INSTEAD. Grouped the hold notice by reason, so the seven cost one stderr line per merge rather than seven. The divergence is unchanged.

WHY NOT --prefer-bd. Writing bd descriptions over GH bodies is symmetric to the measured incident where --prefer-github pulls silently REVERTED bead descriptions (bd memory workflow-bd-gh-sync-reverts-descriptions). It would also destroy gqlc-l45j's GitHub-side banner, the one case where GitHub is ahead. A body-overwrite direction is a real design decision and wants a reviewer, not a 3am factory lane.

CANDIDATE FIXES, unranked: (a) reconcile these seven by hand, once, editing each GH body to match its bead description, and let the sync go quiet on its own; (b) an explicit opt-in per-bead 'push this body' path with a dry-run; (c) accept the divergence and record it as knowingly-divergent in a committed file the sync reads.

FALSIFIER for any fix: re-run the classification and the not-a-prefix count must be 0, with each of the seven bd descriptions reproduced verbatim as a prefix of its GH body.
close_reason: Remedy (a) executed 2026-08-23: the seven divergent pairs were reconciled by hand, no code change. Six were bd-ahead (gqlc-xqf6/#1304, gqlc-3eyw/#645, gqlc-w6bz/#977, gqlc-5ckc/#958, gqlc-cgat/#906, gqlc-eb5j/#716); for each, the bd description was written to the GH body verbatim with 'gh issue edit --body-file'. Every diff was read first: in all six the GH text was a strictly earlier draft of the same bead (superseded numbers, an expanded scope paragraph, gqlc-eb5j's retracted diagnosis replaced by its CORRECTION block); nothing existed on GitHub that bd did not supersede, and #958's GH body was empty. gqlc-l45j/#933 was repaired the OTHER way: GitHub was ahead there, carrying a 'SCOPE NARROWED' banner above the original text, so the bd description was a suffix, not a prefix, of the GH body. Overwriting would have destroyed the banner, so the BEAD description was replaced with the GH body verbatim instead; reasoning recorded in that bead's notes. FALSIFIER, run with the classifier's prefix rule reproduced verbatim (norm() CRLF/NBSP/strip, then gh_body.startswith(desc)) over a fresh read of both sides: not-a-prefix count is now zero, over all 811 mirrored beads, not just the seven, and every hold category is empty. Positive control: replaying the captured pre-repair bodies through the same script reports exactly the seven, so the script is not vacuously passing. GH bodies were re-read from the API after editing, not from a local buffer. NOT VERIFIED: no real bd-gh-sync pull was run against the live ledger (deliberate, per the bead's own hazard note); the .beads jsonl export of the gqlc-l45j description change is left for whichever lane commits it. NOT DONE: candidate fixes (b) and (c) remain unbuilt, so a future one-sided body edit can recreate this state; if it recurs, (b) is the design question and wants a reviewer.

title: codegen live battery: no scenario drives a map-returning column against a real database
description:
gqlc-faa1 enrolled scalar_map in neo4j-go-v6, which brings the golden
cross-backend comparison and TestBackendInvariantSurface onto it (both verified
red under a mutated v6 querier.go surface). It does NOT close the third gate the
bead named: the live battery has no scenario that runs a map column against a
running server, so the emitted 'neo4j.GetRecordValue[map[string]any]' read is
pinned as text and as something that compiles, and never as something that works.

What faa1 measured and closed on, worth not re-deriving: apache-age-pgx-v5
CANNOT be the second target. AGE refuses the column kind outright --
  unsupported query: the Apache AGE backend serves scalar and entity columns,
  so 1 query would be dropped: OneMap (column "m" projects scalar(map))
-- and that refusal is already pinned in internal/codegen/age/age_test.go at
four sites. Lifting it is an ADR 0025 question, not a corpus-enrolment one.

Scope: add a live scenario reading a map-valued expression column
(RETURN {a: 1} AS m) on the neo4j arms. The open question the scenario should
answer is whether the driver hands back map[string]any with the element types
the golden assumes, or something the emitted read mis-types silently.

Falsifier: the scenario must fail if the emitted read is changed to
GetRecordValue[map[string]string].
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.

--- agent-m, 2026-09-02, PR #2185 ---

SHIPPED: mapColumnScenarios, one row, driving scalar_map on both neo4j arms of
the live battery. It is a subtest of TestLiveSmoke, so no recipe change and no
new name for TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt to enrol. Verified it
RAN and PASSED rather than silently matching nothing: run 33645849237 logs
=== RUN and --- PASS for it under both neo4j-go-v5 and neo4j-go-v6.

THE FALSIFIER THIS BEAD NAMED DOES NOT EXIST. GetRecordValue[map[string]string]
does not compile: GetRecordValue's parameter is constrained to
neo4j.RecordValue, a union of the driver's own carriers, and map[string]string
is not in it (v5 neo4j/record.go:25, v6 neo4j/record.go:25). The compiler
refuses it on both majors before any test runs, which is a red for the wrong
reason. Anyone re-reading this bead should not go looking for that mutant.

WHAT WAS RUN INSTEAD, and it is a stronger result. The fixture literal was
changed from {a: 1} to {a: 1.5} and the goldens regenerated, which leaves the
emitted Go byte-identical but for the query text — same GetRecordValue call,
same signature, same declared surface — so only what the SERVER SENDS changes.
That mutant passed the ENTIRE `just test` root gate on push (TestConformanceSuite,
TestBackendInvariantSurface, TestGoldenBuild, all of it), and then codegen-live
dispatched on it failed on exactly two rows and no others, both mine, with
expected map[a:1] against actual map[a:1.5]. So: every static gate in the
repository is green on a wrong arrival, and this row is the only thing that
isn't.

The NoError half passed under the mutant too — the driver did hand back a
map[string]any, only the member differed — so the row failed on the assertion it
was written to fail on rather than collapsing earlier.

ALSO CORRECTED, because this change falsified it: ADR 0025 said no scenario in
the live battery drives scalar_map, and said scalar_map is enrolled in ONE
target and so is skipped by TestBackendInvariantSurface. The manifest has listed
neo4j-go-v5 and neo4j-go-v6 since the v6 enrolment, so the second was already
false at master — it clears the two-target floor and IS compared. What the ADR
was reaching for survives for the reason that test's own header gives for the
edge_union_* fixtures: the two targets are one emitter under two version
options.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT WITNESS, stated so nobody reads it wider than it is: one
member of one kind (integer), on one server (the digest-pinned neo4j:5-community
in live_neo4j_test.go). It says nothing about the twelve other kinds ADR 0025
tabulates, and nothing about Aura, a cluster, or another 5.x.
MERGED as PR #2185 (squash 53a3f5a2), 2026-09-02. GH #1361 auto-closed on merge. Verified by content on origin/master, not by the merge command: mapColumnScenarios present in live_test.go, mapColumnV5/V6 adapters in live_neo4j_test.go, both ireturn names in .golangci.yml, the ADR correction in 0025.

Rebased onto master before merging (6 commits had landed, one of them a NEW codegen fence, #2182). Full pre-push gates re-ran green on the new base, and live-smoke's log shows === RUN / --- PASS for the row on BOTH neo4j-go-v5 and neo4j-go-v6 at the rebased head, so the green is a run and not an unselected row.

THE BEAD'S NAMED FALSIFIER IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE and was not used. neo4j.GetRecordValue's parameter is constrained to the closed union neo4j.RecordValue (v5 and v6 both, neo4j/record.go:25); map[string]string is not a member, so the mutant does not compile on either major — a red from the compiler, for the wrong reason.

SUBSTITUTE, strictly stronger: change the fixture query literal {a: 1} -> {a: 1.5} and regenerate. The emitted Go is byte-identical but for the query text — same GetRecordValue[map[string]any], same signature — so only what the SERVER SENDS moves. Run 33645769707 on branch mutant/gqlc-y6mo-map-column-falsifier: exactly two rows failed (v5 and v6, separately) and nothing else; the NoError half PASSED, so the row failed on the assertion it was written for rather than collapsing earlier. Preserved at #2185#issuecomment-5511666548.

Two dead ends worth not repeating: a hand-edited golden is not a pushable mutation (pre-push runs the whole just test and TestConformanceSuite reds it), and the emitter route is blocked — mutating driverCarrier for map[string]any flips 'checked' on in writeSingleColumnDecodeIndent, which emits a narrowCall that does not exist for a map, so the regenerated golden would not compile.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: decide whether endpoint-narrowed (but declared) relationship types deserve a diagnostic
description:
ADR 0032 warns when a query names a relationship type the schema declares NOWHERE. It deliberately says nothing when a DECLARED type is dropped from one edge's candidate set by that edge's endpoints.

Example, from internal/resolver/undeclaredreltype_test.go's driftSchema:
  schema declares (:Person)-[:AUTHORED]->(:Post) and (:Post)-[:REPORTED]->(:Person)
  query  MATCH (:Person)-[r:AUTHORED|REPORTED]->(p:Post) RETURN r
REPORTED is silently dropped. ADR 0022 endpoint narrowing is working, and an
author who spelled the alternation to cover both directions wants exactly that,
so warning here would fire on ordinary correct queries and bury the ADR 0032
signal. TestEndpointNarrowedButDeclaredTypeIsSilent holds that line.

But the same silence covers a real mistake: an author who believes REPORTED runs
Person->Post gets no diagnostic and a query that matches less than they think.

Open question: is there a shape that separates the two? A candidate: warn only
when the endpoints drop EVERY orientation of a named type AND the edge is
directed AND the type is declared with the opposite orientation only — i.e. the
'you wrote the arrow the wrong way' case, which is narrower than 'a candidate
was dropped'. Measure the false-positive rate against the resolver corpus (12880
sweep cells) before adopting anything.

Falsifier for any implementation: TestEndpointNarrowedButDeclaredTypeIsSilent
must be replaced, not deleted, by a row stating the new boundary.
notes:
Labelled class:designer by agent-a, 2026-08-29. The title is the reason: it says DECIDE WHETHER a diagnostic is deserved, not implement one. There is no defect here to fix — there is a question about what the resolver should consider worth telling the author, and either answer produces working software. An author woken on this by class inference (gqlc-38ye routes unlabelled beads as class:author) would have no way to take it except to build the diagnostic, and building it IS the answer to the question the bead is asking. That is settling a design question by implementation, which is the failure the design gate exists to prevent. If the designer who takes this decides a diagnostic IS owed, the implementation should be a separate bead blocked on this one.
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
Claimed by agent-m 2026-09-01. Execution stub gqlc-7aw2j filed and blocked behind this bead (design-gate pair repair). Investigation begun: ADR 0032 detector is a pure text walk (declared-nowhere); candidate wrong-arrow shape needs closure-time endpoint commitments (closeEdge/CloseEdges). Measurement against the 12880-cell sweep corpus next, per the bead's own requirement.
2026-09-04, agent-m: agent-d's two execution corrections (mail 2026-09-02, PR #2126,
merged 202e6c22) are ACCEPTED onto the design's record, both re-verified by me
against master today.

1. THE CONSUMER LIST OVERCOUNTED — design error, mine. generate.go:88 reads
pipeline.Result.Warnings, which stays []string (pipeline.go:75); only
pipeline.go:325 crosses into resolver's []Warning. agent-d missed no consumer. The
mechanism of my error: I listed consumers by matching `.Warnings` without
tracing which TYPE each site reads — the pipeline lane and the resolver lane
share a field name and nothing else. The reviewer's full-depth PASS (gqlc-ukfqi)
stands over the executed truth.

2. THE HARD CHECK FIRED ON THE DESIGN'S OWN STEP 1 — design error, mine, the
worse of the two. "Every EXISTING manifest row byte-identical" cannot be
satisfied by any correct execution, because step 1's []string -> []Warning
refactor necessarily moves sha(json.Marshal(ValidatedQuery)) for every
warning-bearing cell (82/12920) before the detector exists. Accepted repair,
per agent-d: the check is scoped "after step 2, measured against the tree step 1
left behind". His decision to proceed — omitempty establishing that only
warning-bearing cells' digests can move, verdicts and sentinels moving on zero
cells — was the correct discharge, and better than a stop-and-mail would have
been.

DESIGN LESSON, for my own future checks: a byte-identity check written into a
design whose own earlier step rewrites a serialised type must name the tree it
measures against, or it fires on the design itself with a wrong diagnosis.
close_reason: Decision: yes, a diagnostic is deserved, in exactly one narrow shape — the wrong-orientation drop (type declared only in the reversed orientation of the arrow drawn, dropped from the candidate set, both endpoints covering, and surviving on no edge query-wide). Measured against the 12880-cell sweep at 13157072: broad shape 27 FP cells, wrong-arrow-without-suppression 9 FP cells (all one legitimate mirrored idiom), full shape C ZERO corpus cells; both extra clauses independently load-bearing; positive/negative controls all behave. Full six-clause detector, seams, tests (incl. the mandated replacement of TestEndpointNarrowedButDeclaredTypeIsSilent), corpus fixture, ADR/CONTEXT.md work, and the 0032 second-producer struct conversion are written into gqlc-7aw2j's notes.

title: CI has no bd, so no suite can re-check bd's real updated_at behaviour (successor to gqlc-3205)
description:
gqlc-3205 asked for a gate that runs the REAL bd and asserts 'bd update -d' moves updated_at, because .githooks/bd-gh-sync's pull ordering rests on that behaviour and .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh stubs bd on PATH so it can never observe it. 3205 is closed pointing here; this bead is the half that survives, and it lives outside .githooks/.

Verified first-party 2026-08-23 on origin/master c129a0a5:
  - justfile:1328 'hook_suites=(.githooks/tests/*-test.sh)' -- a new suite is wired by
    filename alone, so 3205's stated deferral reason (needing a justfile edit) is gone.
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml:122-130, the 'test' job, has exactly four steps: checkout,
    setup-go, setup-just, 'just test'. THERE IS NO bd ON THAT RUNNER, and no workflow in
    .github/workflows installs one.

So a suite under .githooks/tests/ that shells out to the real bd reddens CI on its first
run, and one guarded on 'command -v bd' is a conditional gate whose absent branch is
silent -- the shape .githooks/tests/lint-hooks-test.sh already refuses by policy ('an
unclassifiable file is refused, not skipped').

The decision belongs with ci.yml's owner, and it is one of:
  (a) install bd in the 'test' job and accept the cost. Measured in a throwaway /tmp
      workspace: 'bd init' on the embedded Dolt engine took tens of seconds, and
      'just test' is also the pre-push hook, so that cost lands on every local push too.
  (b) give the real-bd check its own workflow step or workflow, outside 'just test',
      the way iso-drift-check and codegen-live already sit outside it.

The claim under test still holds as of today, measured once: throwaway workspace under
/tmp with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE cleared, bd 1.0.4 ce242a879, 'bd init
--prefix probe --non-interactive' then 'bd create' then 'bd update <id> -d' moved
updated_at. One-off measurement, which is precisely what 3205 said is not enough.

Falsifier for a fix: with the gate in place, pin bd to a build that does not move
updated_at on a description edit (or stub the field out) and the gate must go RED.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #1379 (squash 2026-08-23) as .github/workflows/bd-behaviour.yml.

The decision the bead left to ci.yml's owner: option (b), its own workflow, NOT installed into the 'test' job. Reasons, in order. 'just test' is also the pre-push hook, so anything added there is paid by every agent on every push, and this repo treats wall-time as critical. bd is a Dolt-backed binary this repo neither owns nor vendors, so a bd release or a GitHub release outage would block every unrelated PR at four in the morning for a reason no author can fix. And the shape 3205 wanted -- a suite under .githooks/tests guarded on 'command -v bd' -- is a conditional gate whose absent branch is silent, which lint-hooks-test.sh already refuses by policy. So: a real-bd check that lives outside 'just test', the way iso-drift-check and codegen-live already do.

It is an ALARM, not a merge gate, and its header says so in those words. Its id must stay OFF master's required-check list. Triggers: weekly cron, workflow_dispatch, and pull_request on .githooks/bd-gh-sync, its own suite, and the workflow file. No cron-freshness watcher of its own -- GitHub's sixty-day disablement is a single repo-wide event, and ci.yml's tidy job already watches codegen-live, the daily cron that goes stale first.

It installs the LATEST bd release rather than the pinned one, deliberately, so a regression is learned BEFORE the fleet upgrades into it. The stub problem 3205 named is answered at the boundary: the real binary runs, in a throwaway mktemp workspace with the git environment cleared.

The falsifier the bead asked for runs IN BAND on every run rather than being performed once by hand. The comparator is a function, and after the real measurement the run drives it against an unchanged timestamp and against an empty before value; if either is accepted the step fails with '::error title=This check cannot fail::'. So a pass is a measurement, not a gate that cannot fire.

Measured first-party 2026-08-23, throwaway workspaces, GIT_DIR and friends cleared: bd one point zero point four (ce242a879) and bd one point two point two (6c124203e) BOTH move updated_at on 'bd update -d', and both answer 'bd show --json' with an array. Green in CI on runs 32632918251, 32633318594, 32634760561, in twelve seconds each including the install.

NOT verified: the workflow does not run .githooks/bd-gh-sync, so it checks the PREMISE the script's dated header records, not the script's use of it. The negative arm falsifies the comparator only; a bd that renamed updated_at outright is caught instead by the non-empty and parseable assertions on the before value. And no run of the scheduled trigger has fired yet -- only the pull_request one has.

title: bd-gh-sync: bd is ahead of GitHub on 7 mirrored bodies and no path ever closes the gap
description:
Measured 2026-08-23 over 784 beads and 806 issues (neither listing truncated), classifying every mirrored bead by the pull gate's own rules in .githooks/bd-gh-sync.

Status pairs: closed x closed 514, open x open 250, in_progress x open 5, blocked x open 2. Zero instances of the non-representable-status x CLOSED-mirror shape, and zero closed-bead x open-mirror. That is gqlc-x98l's target drift, and its baseline today is ZERO.

What IS live is a seventh-of-a-different-kind: 7 beads where status agrees but the GH body is not a prefix of the bead description, so the pull holds them with 'bd-description-not-a-prefix-of-gh-body' on every merge, forever:

  gqlc-xqf6 / GH #1304, gqlc-l45j / #933, gqlc-3eyw / #645, gqlc-w6bz / #977,
  gqlc-5ckc / #958, gqlc-cgat / #906, gqlc-eb5j / #716

Inspected one by one. Every case is bd AHEAD of GitHub, not the reverse: gqlc-eb5j carries a '## CORRECTION (2026-08-03)' block the issue body has never seen; gqlc-3eyw's description corrects a count the issue still spells wrong; gqlc-5ckc's mirror (#958) has an EMPTY body against 888 characters in bd. gqlc-l45j is the one exception in direction, a 'SCOPE NARROWED' banner prepended on GitHub.

Why it is durable: the PULL is correct to hold these -- pulling would destroy the bd-side amendment. But the PUSH path only mints issues for unmirrored beads and closes stale mirrors; it never updates an existing issue body. So neither direction of bd-gh-sync can resolve them, and the hold notice reprints on every merge. Seven recurring stderr lines under a hook that exits 0 is the '2>/dev/null' shape this repo keeps being bitten by.

Falsifier for any fix: after it, re-run the classification above and the not-a-prefix count must be 0, with each of the 7 bd descriptions reproduced verbatim as a prefix of its GH body.

Filed from PR-lane work on gqlc-07c6; out of that lane, which owned only .githooks/bd-gh-sync and its suite.
close_reason:
Closed on the REPORTING half only, merged in PR #1376. THE DIVERGENCE REMAINS AND IS NOW gqlc-myee — read that before assuming this is done.

WHAT WAS FIXED. The hold notice is grouped by reason: one stderr line per distinct reason, naming every bead it holds, ids enumerated up to a cap of twelve with the elision declared and the count never capped. A single-bead group keeps the old wording byte for byte, because one hold is the common case. The seven permanently-held beads therefore cost one line per merge instead of seven.

WHAT WAS NOT FIXED. All seven are still divergent. This bead's own falsifier — re-run the classification and the not-a-prefix count must be zero — is NOT met and was never attempted.

THE JUDGEMENT CALL, and why. A --prefer-bd push direction that overwrites the GH body was considered and rejected. It is symmetric to the measured incident in this repo where --prefer-github pulls silently REVERTED bead descriptions (bd memory workflow-bd-gh-sync-reverts-descriptions), so it trades a loud permanent hold for a silent destructive write. It would also destroy gqlc-l45j's GitHub-side 'SCOPE NARROWED' banner, which is the one of the seven where GitHub is ahead rather than behind — a single rule cannot be right for both directions, and picking one direction for a mixed set loses data on the minority. Choosing a body-authority direction is a design decision that wants a reviewer; it is not a call a factory lane should make unreviewed overnight. Recorded on gqlc-myee with the seven ids, the direction of each, three candidate remedies and the falsifier.

NOT VERIFIED: the seven bodies were not re-inspected in this lane. The classification quoted here is this bead's own, taken on trust.

SEPARATELY, a correction to a premise this lane was handed. The over-long-label beads gqlc-njqk, gqlc-a7we and gqlc-to7k were said to make every push print PUSH FAILED forever. Stale. They now carry subject:fleet/brain/playbooks at thirty-one characters, which is verbatim the remedy bd-gh-sync's own notice prints, and all three mirrored as GH mirrors one-three-five-eight through one-three-six-zero. No bead on the board carries an over-cap label. A demotion of that verdict was written on this branch and then REVERTED; the label path is byte-identical to master. Witnessed out of tree rather than off the alarm's absence: a scratch fixture with one 51-character-labelled bead, run against both revisions, refuses to offer it and exits non-zero on both. For the record, that path skips the ISSUE, not the label — an over-cap bead gains no mirror until an agent renames the label, which is the ratified gqlc-89vw remedy working as designed.

title: a defect bead about merged code carries from-pr:<N>, so V.2.0.4 can be answered with a number
description:
Execution of fleet/brain/decisions/0004-the-adversarial-read-after-the-gate.md
section 3. Docs only.

## Why

protocol binds the fleet to judge the unreviewed-merge regime as a
throughput measure and says what that requires: "a defect found on merged code
records whether its PR was reviewed, or the fleet will have no evidence with which
to re-tune this and will re-tune it on feeling instead."

Nothing records it. A defect bead today carries class:, optionally
subject:<path>, and optionally a discovered-from edge. None of those says which
merge introduced the defect, and reviewedness is not recoverable from the
defect's own text later. So the clause that is supposed to repeal or narrow ADR
0003's change 1 has, at present, no input.

## What to write

In agent-protocol.md, in the "File freely, and label what you file" step,
alongside the subject: and discovered-from advice:

- A defect bead about ALREADY MERGED code carries `from-pr:<N>` — the number of
  the PR that introduced it.
- Where the filer cannot identify a single PR, OMIT the label rather than guess.
  A wrong number is worse than a missing one here, because the whole point is a
  count somebody will act on.
- Reviewedness is derived later, at re-tune time, from PR N's own bead (was it
  blocked by a design bead; was a class:reviewer bead ever filed against it), by
  whoever is doing the re-tuning. This is deliberate: the filer supplies the fact
  they can cheaply know, and is not asked for a judgment they would have to
  reconstruct.
- State the limit honestly, in one sentence: this measures defects FOUND, not
  defects present, and unreviewed code is also less likely to be looked at. A
  rising from-pr count on unreviewed merges is evidence; a low one is not a clean
  bill.

## Not in scope

No tooling. No bd-guard enforcement — an unenforced label that is cheap and
honest beats a gate that makes people invent numbers. If someone later wants the
derivation automated, that is its own bead and it should be written against real
from-pr data rather than in anticipation of it.
close_reason: Merged as PR one-three-seven-zero, squash sha 79314016. The 'File freely, and label what you file' step now says a defect bead about ALREADY MERGED code carries from-pr:<N>, gives two verified one-liners for finding N (git log -S with tail, and gh api commits/<sha>/pulls — both returned issue one-three-five-seven for a known merge), says omit rather than guess, states that reviewedness is derived at re-tune time from PR N's own bead and is not asked of the filer, quotes what protocol actually demands, and states the limit: it counts defects FOUND, so a low count is not a clean bill. No tooling and no bd-guard enforcement, per the ADR.

title: agent protocol: moving a head under a live reader, forced and unforced
description:
Execution of fleet/brain/decisions/0006-a-head-that-moves-under-a-reader.md
sections 2 and 3. Docs only; the fleetctl halves are gqlc-wz47 and gqlc-rc5i.

## Where

fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md, "Working a bead", near step 8 (the
step that files the class:reviewer bead when review is owed).

## What to write

AUTHOR, before asking for review: rebase. Do not ask for review on a PR that is
DIRTY in the files under review — a reviewer's PASS at that SHA is true of a SHA
that never lands, because you must afterwards resolve real conflicts in reviewed
code. State both qualifiers, they are load-bearing:
  - "in the files under review": a conflict in an unrelated file leaves the
    reviewed bytes intact.
  - a FAIL is unaffected; it names a defect the rebase carries forward.

THE FORCED MOVE, which is the common case and currently has no procedure at all.
#1127, #1225, #1172, #1237 and #1195 all needed a rebase on 2026-08-22; none was
optional, several were forced by another PR merging into a shared registry. Four
clauses:
  1. Warn the reader BEFORE the push, not after.
  2. State the delta as a MERGE-BASE COMPARISON, never a commit list. A rebase
     makes `git log old..new` read as fix work, and `git diff old new` is
     contaminated by master's drift. agent-e's came out as: only hunk line
     numbers, blob hashes and one added context line differ, not one line of her
     own — a sentence a reader re-anchors on in seconds.
  3. Correct the head on the review bead in the SAME MINUTE.
  4. A forced move must be CONTENT-IDENTICAL. Content-identity is the entire
     reason a forced move is cheap for the reader. A content change carried
     inside a forced rebase is an UNFORCED move and is treated as one. agent-e
     had an unpinned example.com.evil.io row she had declined to add while a
     reviewer was live; forced to move the head anyway, she could have had it for
     free, considered it, and declined. Without clause 4 the first three can all
     be satisfied while the reader is still stranded.

Worth one cheerful sentence so this does not read as heavier than it is: with
production bytes usually merging clean, "rebase before you ask for review" is
normally an append-both resolution in one file, not a risky merge of reviewed
logic.
close_reason: Merged as PR one-three-seven-zero, squash sha 79314016. Two places. Step 7 gains 'Rebase before you ask for review' with both load-bearing qualifiers (in the files under review; a FAIL is unaffected) and a merge-tree check that discriminates, because gh pr view --json mergeable returns UNKNOWN after a push and reads as clean. A new section 'When your head moves under a reader' carries the forced move's four clauses, which had no procedure at all: warn before the push (with a query that finds the live reviewer bead by PR number), state the delta as a merge-base double-diff, correct the head on the review bead in the same minute, stay content-identical — and names the unforced move as a new change owing a fresh read. Every command was run before it was written: verified merge-tree puts its Auto-merging/CONFLICT prose on STDOUT after a blank line, so the filter stops there. git range-diff was tried for the delta sentence and rejected — a context line of master drift made it report the rebase as a drop plus an add.

title: gate: a scripted bd list/ready call must state its status set and row cap explicitly
description:
FOLLOW-UP to gqlc-18br, filed 2026-08-23 because the fix belongs in a lane the
docs work could not touch.

gqlc-18br is about an affordance in an EXTERNAL tool (/usr/bin/bd, source not in
this repo, unpatchable here): `bd list` has two independent defaults — a status
filter and a row cap — and `-n 0` disables only the second, silently. What this
repo can own is that none of ITS call sites relies on either default.

The doc half shipped: docs/bd-ledger-queries.md, plus a section in CLAUDE.md and
AGENTS.md. Documentation is not a gate. This bead is the gate.

WHAT TO BUILD. A sweep over the repo's scripted bd invocations that FAILS when
one omits an explicit status set or an explicit row cap. Shape suggestions, not
a design: a small `internal/tools/` sweeper wired into `just lint` alongside the
existing hook sweeps, or a `.githooks/tests/` row. Whichever, it must exit
NONZERO on a violation — a detector that exits 0 is not a gate (gqlc-z1qw).

THE ROWS THAT MATTER. Feed it a call site written `bd list --json` and assert
FAIL. Feed it `bd list --all --json -n 0` and assert PASS. And mutate the
sweeper's own pattern, because the population it walks is the part that goes
quietly wrong — a sweep that matches nothing passes everything.

AUDIT BASELINE, measured 2026-08-23 at c129a0a5, in the table at the foot of
docs/bd-ledger-queries.md: nine invocations, eight correct. So a sweeper written
today should be GREEN on the tree except for fleet/bin/fleetctl:1865, which is filed
separately as gqlc-c7b5. Land c7b5 first or the gate lands red.

CARE with the false-positive direction: `bd list --status in_progress -n 0` at
fleetctl:1014/1150/1656 is CORRECT — a single status is a legitimate explicit choice.
The rule is 'stated', not 'all'.
close_reason:
The gate shipped as .githooks/tests/bd-query-flags-test.sh, merged in PR #1399 and verified present on origin/master with git cat-file. It runs under just test-hooks, which the pre-push hook runs, and it is glob-discovered, so no justfile edit (that file belonged to the fleetctl lane).

WHAT IT DOES. Sweeps tracked shell, just and Go sources for scripted bd list / bd ready invocations and exits non-zero when one omits its row cap, or when a bd list omits its status set. bd ready needs the cap only, being open-only by construction; that is asserted in both directions.

WHAT IT ENUMERATES, measured: ELEVEN call sites, not the nine the doc prose claimed. Its own table already listed eleven, so the doc contradicted itself; the enumeration row now MEASURES the count instead of restating it, and the doc was corrected in the same PR.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD, worth reading before anyone acts on gqlc-c7b5 on my account. This bead said a sweeper written today would land red on fleetctl:1865 and that c7b5 must land first. That is wrong, and the bead had already said why two paragraphs earlier: the rule is STATED, not ALL. fleetctl:1865 spells --status open, which is explicit, so it PASSES this gate. c7b5 is a semantic defect (the arm means every unfinished bead and asks for one status) and no sweep over flags can see it. The gate landed green on the whole tree with no dependency on c7b5, and the header and the doc both now say so, so nobody reads a green run as clearing c7b5.

TWO FALSE-POSITIVE DIRECTIONS handled, both measured on the live tree rather than assumed. Comments are cut and quoted spans blanked before matching, and neither pass subsumes the other: without the first, the twenty-odd lines of fleetctl and bd-gh-sync commentary explaining bd list read as call sites; without the second, fleet/bin/fleetctl s BEADS: UNAVAILABLE diagnostic, which spells the command inside an echo behind an opening paren with no cap after it, reads as a capless site. Markdown is not swept at all: the instruction files and docs/bd-ledger-queries.md quote the wrong form deliberately, as the counterexample they teach against.

RED PROOF, since the tree was already clean. Planting a capless call site in a real tracked file reddens the suite with path, line and reason. MUTATIONS, victims declared beforehand, all killing exactly what was declared, none breaking parse (bash -n) and none a no-op (cmp): shell arm blinded kills twelve of twenty-seven with the Go rows surviving; Go arm deleted kills three; cap check disabled kills five; status check disabled kills two; comment strip neutered kills one; quote blanking removed kills two.

TWO HONEST NOTES. First, a mutation initially SURVIVED — the comment strip — because the prose fixture used a backticked mention that the command-position test already refused, so the row certified nothing. The fixture was sharpened to reach the command through an opening paren and the mutation then killed it. Second, the gate caught THIS BRANCH breaking its own rule: once the suite became tracked it entered its own sweep, and the Go arm reported two violations in the suite own source. Repaired by narrowing the arm to *.go with // comments cut, plus two new prose controls, rather than by allowlisting the file.

title: agent protocol: record the mutation you already owe, in a shape a stranger can re-run
description:
Execution of fleet/brain/decisions/0005-mutation-evidence-belongs-to-the-author.md.
READ IT FIRST. Docs only; no code.

## Scope

Amend the agent protocol, "Working a bead" step 3 (the paragraph that already
says a bead adding or changing a GUARD is not done until you have watched that
guard fail). Add the RECORD, not a second obligation — the trigger and the
population are unchanged.

## What to write

1. The trigger is the existing one: a PR that adds or changes a guard records
   its mutation rows; a PR that adds or changes no guard owes nothing and writes
   nothing. Say that exemption explicitly — a requirement with no exemption route
   gets satisfied dishonestly, and here the exemption is built into the trigger.
2. The shape, four requirements (ADR 0005 gives the failure each was earned by):
   - a per-row EXPECTED VICTIM declared BEFORE the run, as a literal assertion
     string. This is what turns a survivor from a shrug into a diagnosis.
   - four verdicts: KILLED (declared victim among the failures, collateral kills
     printed), WRONG (something died, not the declared one), SURVIVED, NO-OP.
   - a compiler-kill screen, named per language: Go `go test -c -o /dev/null
     <pkg>` (go build is blind to _test.go; the tell is kill-count 1 with a BLANK
     test name); just prints `error:` on a parse error too; in shell and jq the
     tell is magnitude.
   - a blinding pass when one guard killed every row.
3. Two standing cautions: KILLED self-certifies and SURVIVED does not (a SURVIVED
   row is a claim about a sandbox); a battery over a directory or glob has a
   green that expires, because master owns the tree it ran on.
4. Where it lives: the PR body. Measured 2026-08-23 on this repo,
   squash_merge_commit_message is BLANK — so a squash lands the title and number
   and nothing else, and a battery in a commit message is destroyed by the merge
   that lands it. The merge commit's (#N) suffix is a one-hop reference to a PR
   that stays readable. An in-branch script is permitted and preferred when a
   later reader will want to re-run rather than read; it is not required, because
   requiring a file on every guard PR puts scaffolding in the tree faster than
   anyone removes it.
5. Where the author cannot get a red, the protocol already says that IS the
   finding; recording "no red obtainable, here is what I tried" satisfies this.
6. One sentence for the reviewed minority: a reviewer may not PASS on the author's
   rows alone. V.2.1 already binds the signer to mutate every guard, so the reviewer
   re-runs the recorded commands and adds at least one mutation the author did
   not declare. The saving is construction replaced by audit-plus-delta; it is a
   saving in labour, not in standard. No protocol amendment is needed.

## Keep it short

This is a paragraph or two inside an existing step, plus a short block for the
shape. The agent protocol is read at every wake; length is a cost.
close_reason: Merged as PR one-three-seven-zero, squash sha 79314016. agent-protocol.md 'Working a bead' step 3 now carries the mutation RECORD alongside the existing guard duty: same trigger, explicit exemption for a PR that adds no guard, and a copyable battery block (per-row expected victim as a literal assertion string declared before the run, four verdicts KILLED/WRONG/SURVIVED/NO-OP, a named compiler-kill screen per language, a blinding pass when one guard swept every row). Plus the two standing cautions and why the rows live in the PR body, not a commit message. Verified on master.

title: fleetctl doctor's IDENTITY arm queries --status open, so an in_progress bead with a fixture owner is invisible to it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 while repairing gqlc-3x1r.

fleet/bin/fleetctl, the IDENTITY arm (near line 1865 on master c129a0a5):

    bd list --status open -n 0 --json | jq -r '[ .[] | .owner // empty | select(. != "") ] | unique | .[]'

`--status open` in bd means the literal status `open`, NOT 'not closed'. A bead
in `in_progress` or `blocked` is omitted.

FALSIFIER, first-party, before the repair: the arm named exactly three beads
(gqlc-r3ac, gqlc-nkg6, gqlc-ufql, all status=open, owner fleetctl@test). A FOURTH bead
carried a fixture owner at the same moment and the arm was silent about it:

    gqlc-o13d  in_progress  fixture@example.invalid

gqlc-o13d was a P0. So the arm's failure mode is exactly the one the file is
organised against: an instrument that reports confidently about a population it
did not query. All four are repaired now, so the arm reads ok today and this
defect is currently invisible.

FIX: query every non-closed status, not just `open`. Either drop the filter and
exclude closed in jq, or enumerate open+in_progress+blocked. Whatever shape it
takes, the guarding row must feed the arm an in_progress bead with a bad owner
and assert FAIL — no current row does, which is why this shipped.

NOT FIXED HERE: fleet/bin/fleetctl is another lane's file tonight.
