title: bd-gh-sync counts a bead as pushed on intent, not on it having gained a mirror
description:
Narrowed remainder of gqlc-7b59, split out when PR #1330 closed that bead's
label-specific half.

WHAT #1330 FIXED. A label over GitHub's cap is now screened out before the
issue is offered, and beads held back that way are counted separately from
mirrored ones. So the ONE failure mode that was measured no longer inflates
"pushed N new bead(s)".

WHAT IS STILL WRONG. The count is still a count of intent. `bd github push`
exits 0 even when the GitHub API refuses an individual bead, and bd-gh-sync's
`_pushed` is derived from how many beads it SELECTED, not from how many gained
an `external_ref`. So any other per-bead API failure -- rate limit, a field
GitHub rejects for some reason nobody has hit yet, a transient 5xx -- still
produces a bead with no mirror underneath a summary line that says it was
pushed. That is the shape gqlc-7b59 called out and the shape the fleet has been
bitten by repeatedly: a success line vouching for work that did not happen.

FALSIFIER. Make the `bd github push` stub in .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh
exit 0 while assigning no external_ref to one of two beads. Today the summary
says 2 pushed. It should say 1 mirrored and 1 not, and name the one.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN #1330. Closing it honestly means counting beads that
actually gained an external_ref, which means re-reading the ledger AFTER the
push. The current stub does not model external_ref assignment at all, so the
post-push ledger every push fixture would be measured against does not exist:
teaching the stub to synthesise one re-bases dozens of existing push rows in
one go. Judged too large and too risky to do at speed alongside three other
changes to the ledger writer.

Files: .githooks/bd-gh-sync, .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged in PR #1376. bd-gh-sync now counts a bead as mirrored only if it carries an external_ref in the post-push ledger, read off the same snapshot the stale-mirror pass already takes, so no extra 'bd list' is spent. Beads offered to 'bd github push' that came back without one are named on their own stderr line. A post-push list that is unreadable or empty withdraws the number entirely rather than reporting the intent count as verified; verification runs only when this run actually offered something, so a repository with nothing to push stays out of the failure path.

The bead's own falsifier, run: with the stub exiting zero and assigning no external_ref to one of two beads, master says 'pushed 2 new bead(s)' and the merged script says 'PUSH FAILED — 1 of 2 new bead(s) mirrored' and names the one. Also witnessed out of tree against the real script on both revisions, with a scratch fixture and stubbed bd/gh: master claims one of two mirrored, this claims none of two and names the bead.

The reason it was deferred is gone: the suite's bd stub now synthesises external_ref on push. That is load-bearing, not decorative — disabling the synthesis reddens twelve existing rows. Suite went from one hundred and ninety-five assertions to two hundred and one, all green.

NOT VERIFIED: the suite stubs bd and gh, so nothing witnesses a real GitHub refusal or a real external_ref write. That external_ref is what 'bd github push' assigns is taken from the suite's pre-existing concurrency fixture, not re-measured against the live tool.

title: hooks tests: eight suites still carry a private copy of the git-env scrub, and no gate refuses a ninth
description:
Follow-up to bd gqlc-07bf, which PR #1326 closed for its three in-lane suites
(commit-msg, hooks-drift-tripwire, repo-purity) by sourcing
.githooks/git-env-sandbox.sh.

## The premise gqlc-07bf understated

That bead said "one suite keeps a private copy". Measured on the #1326 branch,
eight remain, each spelling the scrub inline rather than sourcing the shared
file:

    .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh
    .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh
    .githooks/tests/init-config-test.sh
    .githooks/tests/fleetctl-overlap-test.sh
    .githooks/tests/fleetctl-test.sh
    .githooks/tests/shared-config-drift-test.sh
    .githooks/tests/tool-gate-test.sh
    .githooks/tests/worktree-upstream-test.sh

## Why the copies matter more than duplication usually does

The scrub is what stops a suite's fixture git commands from following git's
exported GIT_DIR into the SHARED repo when the suite runs from pre-push. A
private copy passes every direct run and fails only under a real push, which is
the one context nobody reruns. See the memory
workflow-hook-env-redirects-tool-workspace.

## The part that is the actual value, and is still absent

gqlc-07bf called the repo-wide gate "arguably the whole value": a row that
refuses a NEW suite spelling the scrub inline, so the shared file cannot be
bypassed by a future author. That row cannot land while eight suites would trip
it, so it was deliberately not written in #1326. It should land in the same
change that converts the last of the eight.

## Falsifier for whoever takes this

Convert a suite, then delete the source line and confirm its fixtures reach the
shared repo under a real push rather than passing quietly. A conversion whose
only evidence is a green direct run has measured nothing, because a green direct
run is what the defect looks like.
close_reason: PR #1363, merged as master 4a478f85. Six of the eight suites the bead lists are converted to source .githooks/git-env-sandbox.sh: claude-pre-bash, init-config, shared-config-drift, agent profiles, tool-gate, worktree-upstream. agent profiles-test.sh was not on the bead's list of eight; it was written after the bead was filed, which is the drift the bead predicted, happening while the bead sat open. The gate the bead calls the actual value is part C of git-env-sandbox-test.sh: it refuses any tracked file spelling the scrub inline, and it lands with a named exception list rather than not at all. Five exceptions remain, each outside my lane: bd-gh-sync-test.sh, fleetctl-test.sh, fleetctl-overlap-test.sh, .github/scripts/tests/ci-identity-gate-test.sh and .github/scripts/tests/cron-freshness-test.sh. The last of those is the argument for the design: it landed on master WHILE this branch was in review, spelling the scrub inline, and part C found it on the merge. A separate row fails when an exception outlives the copy it excuses, so the list cannot rot into a standing permission, and the failure message says that emptying the list makes the gate unconditional and the loop deletable. Five mutations measured RED with the message the guard emits: a re-added inline copy names the file, a stale legacy entry, a blinded pattern, the anchor dropped so prose matches, and the gate itself dropping its source line. The falsifier the bead asks for is not what I ran: my evidence is a green direct run plus green CI plus the pre-push that carried each push, not a deliberate deletion of a source line under a real push. What remains for whoever converts the last five is that same falsifier, plus deleting the entry from the legacy list in the same change.

title: ciguard: nothing refuses a needs: or if: on a required ci.yml job, and both make it conclude SKIPPED
description:
Follow-up from gqlc-yc6x, which was settled and fixed in the .github/workflows lane on 2026-08-23 (branch ci/workflow-gate-holes).

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MOTIVATES THIS, first-party on this repo, PR #1323 / ci run 32622299816:
codegen-fence was forced to conclude SKIPPED (job-level 'if: false') while the other six required contexts concluded SUCCESS. The PR's mergeStateStatus read UNSTABLE, not BLOCKED. UNSTABLE is 'mergeable, some non-required check is red'. So a required status context whose newest check run concludes SKIPPED SATISFIES master's branch protection on this repo. It is no longer a belief.

TWO WAYS A REQUIRED JOB IN ci.yml CAN CONCLUDE SKIPPED:
  1. a job-level 'if:' that evaluates false
  2. a 'needs:' whose parent fails or is cancelled

The fix for gqlc-yc6x removed the 'needs: [actionlint, tidy]' edges from lint, test and codegen-fence, so route 2 is closed today by the shape of the file and by nothing else. Re-adding one line reopens it, silently, and the tell is a check table reading 'skipping' — which reads like a pass.

WHAT EXISTS. internal/tools/ciguard's TestEveryLintingCIJobRestoresTheCachedBinary refuses 'if: false' on a job it reaches, and its message already names this hazard ('It is a required context: skipped, it reports as satisfied without having linted or restored anything'). Verified by injection on 2026-08-23: adding 'if: false' to codegen-fence reds that test. But it reaches only jobs that need the linter (lint, codegen-fence). 'test' and 'tidy' are outside it, and NOTHING reads 'needs:' at all.

WHAT TO BUILD. In internal/tools/ciguard, over .github/workflows/ci.yml: read master's required contexts as a literal list in the test (not from the API -- a test that needs a token is a test that is skipped), and for each required job refuse (a) a written job-level 'if:', on being written rather than on its value, and (b) any 'needs:'. The gate job's existing if-is-refused-on-being-written idiom in workflow_test.go is the pattern; note it distinguishes an absent key from one written empty via yaml.Node.Kind, which a string field cannot.

Mutate both arms: add 'needs: [tidy]' to test, and 'if: false' to test, and confirm each reds on its own.

Filed rather than done because internal/tools/ was another lane's during the 2026-08-23 parallel cleanup wave.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1362, merged to master 2026-08-23. internal/tools/ciguard/requiredjobs_test.go. Master's seven required contexts are written out as a literal list with the gh api read that produced them, over three workflow files: lint/test/tidy/actionlint/codegen-fence in ci.yml, govulncheck in vuln.yml, live-smoke in codegen-live.yml. A literal and not the API call, for the reason the bead gave -- a test that needs a token is a test that is skipped, and a skipped guard over a merge gate is the shape being refused. For each required job it refuses a written job-level if: and any needs:, both on BEING WRITTEN rather than on their value, since a test cannot evaluate an expression. Both fields are yaml.Node, not string, because a string cannot part an absent key from one written empty, and needs: additionally takes both a scalar and a sequence shape which no scalar Go type accepts. BOTH ARMS MUTATED against the real ci.yml as the bead required: adding needs: [tidy] to the test job reds TestNoRequiredJobCanConcludeSkipped/test naming the parents; adding if: false to the test job reds it too. Ten decoded rows exercise the refusing side directly through the recordingT/refusalOf idiom, including needs: [] which is written and therefore refused. Two further guards: the list may not go empty or name a job twice, and a required job id that no longer exists in its workflow is refused by name -- that state hangs every PR at 'Expected, waiting for status to be reported'. Also pinned that ci.yml's header still carries the 'Do not restore the' argument, because a refusal with no argument beside it gets removed as an obstacle.

title: justfile: no linter or formatter runs over the Python in .github/scripts
description:
MEASURED at master e580fd70, from worktree gqlc-prclose.

grep for ruff, flake8, pylint, mypy, black, py_compile or 'python -m' across
justfile and .github/workflows/ returns NOTHING. So the two Python files in
this tree are checked by no tool at all:

  .github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py    (the tidy merge gate; ~1000 lines)
  .github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py

Not even a syntax check. The only thing that runs check-pr-closes.py is its
own suite, .githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh, which invokes it through
python3 — so a NameError on a branch never taken, an unused import, or a
shadowed builtin all ship green.

The shell half is gated hard by contrast: just lint-hooks runs shellcheck
v0.10.0 and FAILS on a file whose shebang it does not recognise. Its python
case is an explicit skip:

    # shellcheck only supports shell; SC1071 on a python hook would have
    # to be silenced globally ...
    "#!"*python*) ;;

That comment justifies not shellchecking them; it does not claim anything
else does.

FIX (a justfile edit, which is why this is a bead and not a patch — the
justfile was another lane's on the night this was found): add a python-lint
recipe and call it from lint. ruff is one binary, needs no venv, and can be
provisioned the same way ensure-shellcheck provisions shellcheck. Minimum
useful gate is 'ruff check' over .github/scripts; 'ruff format --diff' in
fmt-check would also pin the style the two files already follow.

FALSIFIER: after the fix, introduce an undefined name in a branch no test
reaches in check-pr-closes.py and confirm 'just lint' goes red. Today it
does not.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1362, merged to master 2026-08-23. New justfile recipes ensure-ruff and lint-python, the latter a dependency of lint, so the required lint context runs it. ruff pinned to version 0.16.4 and provisioned into .bin/ exactly as ensure-shellcheck provisions shellcheck: a download of the static release binary, no venv, no pip, ~10ms version check on the happy path. Rule set pinned in .github/ruff.toml, select = E4/E7/E9/F/B, passed with --config so no pyproject.toml added at the root later and no config in a developer's home can widen or narrow it. It lives in .github/ rather than beside the scripts because just lint-hooks .github/scripts refuses any file there with no shebang it recognises, and that refusal is load-bearing. FALSIFIER RUN, the one the bead asked for: an undefined name added to a function nothing calls in check-pr-closes.py, and separately in check-label-lengths.py, is silent on master and reports F821 Undefined name at rc=1 through just lint-python. The empty-directory case fails rather than passing, measured against an empty temp dir. Also pinned: internal/tools/ciguard/lintdeps_test.go refuses lint losing the lint-python edge, because deleting a dependency edge is otherwise silent -- the recipe stays in the file and the context stays green. NOT DONE and deliberately: ruff format is not run over these files. Reformatting a thousand-line merge gate is a change to the gate, and the bead called that the optional half.

title: ci: nothing holds golangci-lint run to reporting the gofumpt/gci formatters
description:
Follow-up from settling gqlc-lsku (2026-08-23).

MEASURED FIRST-PARTY at golangci-lint v2.13.1 (the justfile pin), in worktree gqlc-ci-gate off origin/master e580fd70, with GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE=.bin/golangci-cache:

  control  .bin/golangci-lint run ./internal/version/...  -> '0 issues.' rc=0
  gofumpt  blank line after a function's opening brace appended to
           internal/version/version.go
           -> 'internal/version/version.go:16:1: File is not properly formatted (gofumpt)' rc=1
  control  .bin/golangci-lint run ./internal/config/...   (pristine) rc=0
  gci      import block reordered in internal/config/count_internal_test.go
           -> 'internal/config/count_internal_test.go:4:1: File is not properly formatted (gci)' rc=1

So the required 'lint' context DOES enforce gofumpt and gci, and 'just fmt-check' is a local convenience rather than the only enforcement. gqlc-lsku closed on that.

THE HOLE THIS BEAD IS. That property is a behaviour of a pinned third-party binary under a config key ('formatters:'), and nothing in this tree asserts it. If a golangci-lint bump stops reporting formatters as issues, or someone moves gofumpt/gci out of 'formatters:', the required lint context goes quiet and every check stays green. The tell would be unformatted Go reaching master, noticed by a human.

WHAT TO BUILD, and it is out of the .github/workflows lane so it was not built with the measurement: a Go test (internal/tools/ciguard is where this repo's CI-wiring assertions live) that writes a known gofumpt violation and a known gci violation into a throwaway package under a temp dir, runs the pinned '{{golangci}} run' over it with the repo's .golangci.yml, and asserts a non-zero exit naming each formatter. Take the pristine rc=0 control in the same test or it witnesses nothing.

Alternative, cheaper and weaker: add 'just fmt-check' as a step in ci.yml's lint job. That closes the hole by redundancy without asserting anything about 'run', and costs a second full golangci-lint pass. Not done, because a redundant gate that nobody knows is redundant is how the current confusion arose.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1362, merged to master 2026-08-23. New private justfile recipe check-golangci-formatters-report, a dependency of lint and placed ahead of the golangci-lint run itself, so a tree whose formatter enforcement has gone quiet says so before spending eighty seconds. Took the bead's stronger option, not the cheaper one: it ASSERTS the behaviour rather than closing the hole by redundancy. It builds a throwaway module in /tmp -- outside the tree deliberately, since a probe under test/data would be seen by go list, by modscope's walk and by the discovery-probe sweep -- copies this repo's own .golangci.yml into it, and makes three runs of the pinned golangci-lint. A pristine control that must exit rc=0, which is what stops the two violations passing for the wrong reason. Then a gofumpt violation (blank line after a function's opening brace) and a gci violation (import block split into two sections), each introduced alone from the clean file, each of which must exit non-zero AND name its own formatter in the output. The probe file carries a package comment and a doc comment on its one exported symbol because .golangci.yml runs revive, and a control that exits 1 for an unrelated reason witnesses nothing. THREE MUTATIONS KILLED: gofumpt removed from the formatters enable list in .golangci.yml, gci removed from it, and the sed writing the gofumpt violation turned into a no-op. The second is the interesting one -- with gci disabled the gci-mutation file trips gofumpt instead, and the recipe correctly refuses on 'did not name gci' rather than accepting the wrong red. Cost measured at about one and a half seconds with a cold cache. The lint dependency edge is itself held by internal/tools/ciguard/lintdeps_test.go.

title: ci: nothing detects GitHub disabling this repo's cron-triggered workflows
description:
Split out of gqlc-0oau while shipping its alerting half (PR on branch ci/workflow-gate-holes, 2026-08-23).

GitHub disables cron-triggered workflows after 60 days with no repository activity. It does so REPO-WIDE, so no other cron in this tree can witness it: codegen-live.yml's nightly and vuln.yml's weekly sweep go dark together. The failure mode is silence, not a red check.

WHAT IS NOW COVERED. codegen-live.yml has a nightly-alert job that opens/reopens a labelled tracking issue when the scheduled run fails. That covers a nightly that RUNS AND FAILS. It cannot cover a nightly that never runs.

WHAT IS NOT. Only a pull_request-triggered check can observe that the schedule stopped firing, because that is the one trigger a disablement leaves alive. Sketch: a step in ci.yml's tidy job querying

  gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/workflows/codegen-live.yml/runs --field event=schedule --jq '.workflow_runs[0].created_at'

and refusing when the newest scheduled run is older than some threshold.

THE UNRESOLVED QUESTION, and the reason this is filed rather than done. Should that check BLOCK merges? Fail-closed means an infrastructure state unrelated to the change blocks every PR, at 4am, with nobody awake -- the same hazard gqlc-flko describes for setup-go 429s. Fail-open (::warning::) means a detector that exits 0, which this repo has repeatedly found is not a gate. Whoever takes this must decide explicitly and record why. A middle option: fail closed but with a threshold so long (14 days against a daily cron) that only a real disablement can reach it, and a message naming 'gh workflow enable codegen-live.yml' as the remedy.

Also note the check's own failure modes: an API error must not read as 'fresh', and an empty workflow_runs list must not read as 'fresh' either.
close_reason:
Landed in PR #1362, merged to master.

WHAT SHIPPED. .github/scripts/check-cron-freshness.sh, wired as a step in ci.yml's tidy job (a required status context), invoked as: check-cron-freshness.sh codegen-live.yml 14. The tidy job gained 'actions: read', because the workflow-runs endpoint is under Actions, not Contents.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD ASKED FOR. It BLOCKS merges rather than warning. Argument, recorded in the script header: a detector that exits zero is not a gate (measured repeatedly here, most recently check-hooks warning while 'just doctor' printed ok). The hazard named in bd gqlc-flko -- unrelated infrastructure blocking every PR at 4am -- is held off by the threshold, not by hope: fourteen days against a DAILY cron means thirteen consecutive missed nights pass in silence, so no transient this repo has seen can reach the refusal. What reaches it is the latched state, and the remedy is one command, named in the message. Reverse cost is bounded: detection lag is at most the threshold, against a sixty-day disablement clock.

OWN FAILURE MODES, all of which this bead required be handled and none of which read as fresh: an API error (exit one, naming the actions-read scope), an empty run list (exit one, said DIFFERENTLY from stale, because never-fired is a different defect from stopped), an unparseable body or created_at. Two wiring refusals besides: a workflow file absent from the tree, and a workflow declaring no schedule trigger, which would otherwise refuse on every PR forever for a reason that is not this one.

EVIDENCE. .github/scripts/tests/cron-freshness-test.sh, sixteen rows, gh stubbed on PATH so rows can reach states the live API will not produce on demand. Every row asserts the REASON, not just the verdict, because the checker has five paths to a refusal. Boundary measured on both sides: thirteen days accepts, fourteen accepts, fifteen refuses. Swept by 'just test-hooks'. Two mutations observed RED: deleting the threshold comparison killed three rows; deleting the empty-list arm killed its row. A python3 row asserts ci.yml's tidy job actually runs the checker and grants the scope -- a checker nothing calls is not a gate.

At merge time codegen-live.yml's newest scheduled run measured zero days old, so the live arm is passing on a healthy cron.

NOT VERIFIED. The blocking behaviour has never run against a genuinely disabled workflow -- only against the stub. Disabling a real cron to witness it was not worth the repo-wide blast radius.

title: hooks: claude-pre-bash's master guard denies a gh pr create whose BODY quotes 'git commit'
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 while shipping gqlc-10co from the sibling worktree
../gqlc-genv (branch fix/git-env-sandbox-escape-hatches).

The command was a single Bash call:

    cd /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc-genv && gh pr create --title ... --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
    ... Mutant 2 (`./usr/bin/git commit`, history rather than config): caught.
    BODY
    )"

It was DENIED:

    Direct commits to master are blocked (target: /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc).
    Create a feature branch with: git switch -c <branch>

No commit was being made. Two separate defects compose here, and the second is
the one that makes the first bite:

1. FALSE POSITIVE ON PROSE. .githooks/claude-pre-bash tokenizes the whole Bash
   command string looking for a `git commit` subcommand. A `gh pr create`
   heredoc body that QUOTES the words `git commit` — inside backticks, inside a
   quoted heredoc that git never sees — is read as a commit. Same family as the
   method note on gqlc-kl2d: counting a pattern is not counting an invocation.

2. THE TARGET IS THE TOOL'S CWD, NOT THE COMMAND'S. `main()` takes
   `cwd = os.getcwd()`, which for an agent Bash call is the SHARED checkout
   (parked on master), even though the command's own first clause is
   `cd <sibling worktree>`. So every leading-`cd` command in this repo's
   mandated sibling-worktree workflow is evaluated against master's branch
   name. That is why the refusal names a directory the command never touches.
   Defect 2 alone means the guard's verdict is about the wrong repository;
   defect 1 alone would be a rare nuisance.

REPRODUCER (deny):   gh pr create --body "see git commit abc"
WORKAROUND USED:     write the body to a file, `gh pr create --body-file`.

WHERE: .githooks/claude-pre-bash — `git_targets` / `FALLBACK_RE` (tokenizing)
and `main`'s `cwd = os.getcwd()` (target resolution), around lines 966-990 at
master 9d58f40c.

NOT FIXED HERE: out of the lane I was given (.githooks/tests/**). Filed rather
than detoured. Whoever takes it should note the guard's stated bias — it fails
OPEN on a tokenizer exception on purpose, so a fix must not turn a parse
failure into a refusal.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #1333 (master b323fed1). Two composing defects in .githooks/claude-pre-bash, both measured first-party. The bead's own reproducer, a gh pr create whose --body is a double-quoted string mentioning the commit subcommand, does NOT reproduce: shlex collapses a quoted run into one token. The real shape is a heredoc inside a command substitution, cd <wt> && gh pr create --body with a quoted-delimiter heredoc in a dollar-paren span. (1) unquoted_positions treated a dollar-paren span inside double quotes as still-quoted, so the heredoc opener was never seen and the PR prose was tokenized as commands; state is now a stack and a dollar-paren reopens unquoted context from both contexts. Backticks deliberately left alone, that is the fail-closed side. (2) A substitution body was analyzed at the TOOL's cwd, not the cwd the command itself had cd'd into; new cd_target() walks the cd/pushd chain preceding the span. Wrong in BOTH directions: it also ALLOWED a dollar-paren git-commit against a master repo reached by cd, run from a feature checkout. That bypass was not in any bead. Suite 193 to 225 rows; new rows run red against the parent commit's hook.

title: hooks: no CI arm re-screens PR commits, so an OPEN core.hooksPath drift window is still unbounded
description:
The local half of this is shipped (.githooks/gate-pushed-commits, bd gqlc-zqrw / gqlc-pyk2): pre-push re-runs commit-msg's trailer arm over every commit the push would publish, which covers commits made inside a core.hooksPath drift window that has since closed. Nothing covers a window that is still OPEN, and nothing covers `git push --no-verify`.

WHY CI IS THE ONLY PLACE LEFT. bd gqlc-zqrw's thesis is that a check reading an artifact the drifting actor can also write cannot bind that actor. The actor here writes the developer's local git config. GitHub Actions' config is the runner's, so the actor has no write access to it. That is the only channel in this repo where the drift's blast radius is zero by construction.

MEASURED, 2026-08-22, in a throwaway repo: with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `git commit` runs NO hook and lands a message carrying `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The #1044 tripwire is BLIND to that shape by its own stated limit — it lives in `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks`, and under a /dev/null drift git looks in /dev/null and runs nothing at all. Git is fail-open there by design; there is no in-git position that survives it.

WHAT TO BUILD. A job in .github/workflows/ci.yml that, over the PR's commit range (`${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}..HEAD`, with fetch-depth sufficient to see it), runs `.githooks/gate-pushed-commits` — it already takes pre-push stdin lines, so one synthesised line does it:

    printf 'refs/heads/pr %s refs/heads/pr %s\n' "$HEAD_SHA" "$BASE_SHA" | .githooks/gate-pushed-commits ci ci

NOT in scope, and note it before sizing this: master is squash-merged, so a trailer on a branch commit never reaches master's history. The value is that the PR — which is a public artifact people read — is held to the rule, and that a drift window becomes visible rather than silent. Whoever takes this should decide explicitly whether that is worth a CI job, and record the decision either way; closing this bead with "not worth it, here is why" is a valid outcome.

Filed rather than done because .github/ was another lane's during the 2026-08-22 parallel cleanup wave.
close_reason:
ALREADY COVERED on master. Closing with the measurement rather than adding a second CI arm.

WHAT THE BEAD ASKED FOR: a job in .github/workflows/ci.yml that screens the PR commits for the AI-attribution trailer, because the runner git config is the one thing a core.hooksPath drift in a developer SHARED config cannot reach.

WHAT IS ON MASTER at e580fd70, in the tidy job of ci.yml -- a REQUIRED status context -- as the step named "PR commits carry a plausible author and no AI-attribution trailer" (bd gqlc-gy3q): it fetches the PR commits from the GitHub API as NDJSON and runs .github/scripts/check-pr-authors.sh over them.

VERIFIED FIRST-PARTY 2026-08-23 by feeding that checker synthetic NDJSON:
  clean commit                                         rc=0, prints "checked 1 commit(s): all author/committer identities plausible, no AI-attribution trailers"
  commit whose message carries a
  Co-Authored-By trailer naming Claude at anthropic.com  rc=1, names the sha and prints the offending line
That is the exact shape this bead measured landing under a /dev/null drift.

WHY IT IS EQUIVALENT TO OR STRONGER THAN THE PROPOSED gate-pushed-commits ARM:
  - same rule source. check-pr-authors.sh sources .githooks/implausible-identity.sh, the same file commit-msg reads, so the rule cannot fork.
  - it ALSO grades author and committer identity, which gate-pushed-commits deliberately does not, because at push time git var reports the pusher rather than the author.
  - it fails closed on a missing commit list, on an empty one, and on a line it cannot parse as JSON, so a broken fetch cannot read as "no bad commits".
  - it covers the two holes named here: a STILL-OPEN drift window, since the runner config is not the developer config, and push --no-verify, where nothing local runs at all and CI still does.

LIMITS, stated rather than left to be found: the commits endpoint caps at 250 per PR; and the value is holding the PUBLIC artefact -- the PR -- to the rule, since this repo squash-merges and a branch commit trailer never reaches master history. The bead asked for an explicit decision on whether that is worth a CI job; the decision was taken when gqlc-gy3q shipped, and this bead is its duplicate arriving from the other direction.

title: suite: nothing fails on a fixed /tmp path literal, so the scratch rule is a hope
description:
Split out of gqlc-b8gd (CLOSED via PR #1306). Filed by the documentation lane
against itself: I wrote the rule and I could not gate it, because the gate lives
in .githooks/tests/ which was another lane tonight.

## The claim the rule makes

CLAUDE.md '## Scratch space' now says every scratch path is allocated
(`mktemp -d` / `mktemp`), never a fixed name, and is removed on exit. The three
agent agent profiles that carried the old line say the same in their own voice.

## Why it is currently unenforced

Nothing fails when the rule is broken. An agent writing `cp x /tmp/fleetctl.orig` gets
a green suite, and the collision it causes is silent by construction — both agents
branch from the same base, so the imported work applies cleanly with no conflict.
That is the property that made gqlc-b8gd cost a falsified mutation battery rather
than a build error.

## Shape of the row

A sweep over tracked shell/just/markdown-instruction sources for a `/tmp/<fixed
name>` literal — i.e. a /tmp path with no XXXXXX template and not produced by
mktemp. Known-legitimate exceptions must be an explicit allowlist with a reason
each, not a pattern carve-out.

Mutation the row must survive, since the interesting failure mode of a grep-based
sweep is that it greps nothing: introduce a fixed literal into a file the sweep
claims to cover and watch it FAIL. Do that once per covered file class, not once
overall — an aggregate emptiness guard fires only when EVERY source is silent.

## Not in scope

The per-agent scratch dir (gqlc-<see sibling bead, class:designer>) is the
mechanism half. This bead is the gate half; they are independent and either is
useful alone.
close_reason:
Gated and merged in PR #1385 (squash ca74af2f). New suite .githooks/tests/scratch-literals-test.sh sweeps seventy-nine tracked files -- shell, .githooks, fleet/bin, .github/scripts, justfile, CLAUDE.md, the agent fleet markdown, .claude markdown -- for a /tmp path with a fixed name, skipping mktemp templates and anything carrying a shell expansion. No justfile edit needed: just test-hooks discovers suites by glob.

The bead asked for a per-class mutation rather than one overall, and that is the shape shipped: nine positive controls run the whole sweep, git ls-files included, over a miniature repository with one planted violation per covered path class, so a class that silently stopped being enumerated cannot hide behind the others. Plus a negative control that mktemp templates and expansions are NOT reported, and coverage rows naming one representative real file per class.

Allowlist is exact path plus exact token with a reason each, never a glob, and every entry is checked for staleness so it cannot rot into a carve-out. Six entries, all prose or fixture text: three in CLAUDE.md naming the anti-pattern, two command strings in claude-pre-bash-test.sh, one advice line in gate-pushed-commits. That last one is a real violation in someone else's lane and is now bead gqlc-7ysc.

Measured, and the best evidence the gate works: on its first run after being committed it reported six violations in its OWN allowlist, because the suite is inside its own sweep. Every /tmp path the file mentions is now composed from a variable.

Mutation screen, all KILLED, all parsing: token regex blinded, fifteen rows red; .claude markdown dropped from the classes, one; fleet/bin dropped, two; allowlist keyed on file rather than file-and-token, one; template skip removed, one. And the bead's own falsifier run for real: a fixed literal planted in the tracked .githooks/pre-push turned the tree row red naming that file.

NOT COVERED, deliberately: docs/specs markdown, eighteen matches across six files, filed as gqlc-hfyo. The honest remedy there is prose editing, not eighteen more allowlist lines.

title: close hook: an all-decimal token is read as a sha, so a close reason cannot quote a measured count
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 during the factory backlog triage, three times in a row, on a close that
was otherwise correct.

The close hook refuses a --reason / --reason-file whose text contains an ALL-DECIMAL token of
sha length, treating it as a commit id:

  bd close gqlc-vze6 --reason-file /tmp/triage-vze6.txt
  -> `bd close` cites 1048576, which names no commit in /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc
     (`git cat-file -t 1048576` finds nothing there). A close cannot record work against a
     commit this repository has never seen.

1048576 is the tmpfs inode budget of /tmp, quoted from the bead's own incident report. It is
hex-legal, so the sha tier accepts it, and it is a number no repository will ever contain, so
the lookup always fails. The close is refused until the agent paraphrases their own
measurement.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IT LOOKS. This fleet's whole close discipline is "close it on a
command whose output you paste into the reason". Byte counts, inode counts, timestamps in
epoch seconds, line totals and row counts are exactly what such output contains. The guard
therefore fires hardest on the closes that carry the most evidence, and its remedy is to make
the reason LESS precise. I paraphrased two numbers to get past it; that is the wrong direction
and it is what the next agent will do too.

FALSIFIER, cheap:
  printf 'measured 1048576 inodes\n' > /tmp/r.txt
  bd close <some-bead> --reason-file /tmp/r.txt      -> refused
  printf 'measured 1,048,576 inodes\n' > /tmp/r.txt
  bd close <some-bead> --reason-file /tmp/r.txt      -> accepted
i.e. the discriminator is the absence of a separator, not anything about commits.

SHAPE OF A FIX, not a ruling: an all-decimal token is never a sha anyone types on purpose —
a real abbreviated sha is overwhelmingly likely to contain at least one of a-f. Requiring one
hex letter before entering the sha tier costs nothing the guard is for (a genuine unpushed sha
citation still contains letters with probability ~1) and removes the whole class. Whoever takes
this should check the same question for the 40-char tier and for gqlc-1pav's four unpinned
regex guards, which are the neighbouring rows, and should pin BOTH directions: a decimal token
passes, a real-but-unpushed sha is still refused.

RELATED: gqlc-1pav (unpinned regex guards in the sha tiers), gqlc-vmlp, gqlc-hv81, gqlc-83hv,
gqlc-8dlo (the other open close-hook defects). This is not a duplicate of any of them: they are
about the option walk, substitution extraction and heredocs; this is the sha PREDICATE itself.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #1333 (master b323fed1). close_verdict() promoted any hex-looking token after an anchor word to the ANCHORED tier, which is refused outright when it does not resolve. An all-decimal token is hex-looking, so a close reason quoting a measured count after an anchor word was refused as an unresolvable sha. Fix is DEMOTION, not exclusion: an all-decimal token is dropped from the anchored set but still lands in the loose set, where git itself adjudicates. Exclusion from both tiers would have been a real hole, because a genuine short sha can be all decimal: about 3.7 percent of seven-char abbreviations. Pinned both halves. The allow half uses a prose number after an anchor. The deny half builds a REAL all-decimal sha at fixture time, looping empty commits until git cat-file resolves a seven-to-twelve-char all-decimal prefix (about ten iterations, cap four hundred), and asserts an unpushed one is STILL refused; a hex token after the same anchor still denies. Note for the reader: the 309-reason corpus replay in the header predates this change; 3 of 309 carry an all-decimal anchored token and move only out of refusal.

title: bd-gh-sync: refuse an unmirrorable label at filing time, not after the fact
description:
The other half of gqlc-89vw. That bead shipped the CI gate
(.github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py, wired into ci.yml's tidy job): a
label over GitHub's 50-character cap now REDDENS a PR, over the committed
export, instead of degrading silently.

What is still missing is the refusal at FILING time, inside
.githooks/bd-gh-sync. Today the API rejection

    Failed to create gqlc-xiri in GitHub: Validation Failed
    value: "subject:fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md"
    resource: Label, field: name, code: invalid

is a WARNING during an unrelated push. The bead is created in bd, the hold
machinery keeps working (it reads bd labels, not GitHub's), and the only
casualty is the bd<->GH 1:1 mirror. So the agent who filed the label is not
the one who finds out.

The CI gate catches it before it reaches master, which is the load-bearing
half. This one is about the feedback landing on the person who can still
choose a shorter label — sync should refuse the label and name the budget (42
characters of path after the `subject:` prefix) at the point of filing.

The decision recorded on gqlc-89vw, for consistency: option (b) of that
bead's three, label the deepest ancestor DIRECTORY that fits. That is what
the scheme already permits and what gqlc-xiri does
(subject:fleet/brain/playbooks, 31 chars). The CI checker already prints
that suggestion; bd-gh-sync should print the same one.

Not done here because .githooks/bd-gh-sync was owned by another lane the
night gqlc-89vw shipped.
close_reason: Done in PR #1330 (squash 912c9a62). bd-gh-sync's push selection now screens every bead's labels BEFORE offering it to GitHub. A bead carrying a label over the cap is held back with a message naming the bead, the label, its length, the cap, and the deepest ancestor directory that fits -- the remedy gqlc-89vw ratified, printed in the same words the CI gate prints. The cap is not spelled a third time: it is imported from .github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py by file path (the filename has hyphens; the module does its work under __main__, so loading runs nothing) and read out of MAX_LABEL and PREFIX. That reuse is proved behaviourally rather than by inspection -- a fixture repo plants a gate declaring MAX_LABEL equal to ten, and an eleven-character label must be refused there; a hard-coded fifty passes every other row in the suite and fails only that one. A gate that cannot be loaded screens nothing and SAYS so, rather than defaulting to a guessed number, because a guess here is the API rejection this path exists to make unreachable. Held-back beads are counted separately from mirrored ones in the summary line. Also fixed here: the import compiles the gate, and python's default cached that compilation as an untracked .github/scripts/__pycache__ in the work tree -- measured on the first real push through this path. sys.dont_write_bytecode is set before the import, with a row pinning it on the same fixture.

title: justfile: register ci-identity-gate-test.sh in test-hooks, and lint .github/scripts locally
description:
Split out of gqlc-gy3q / gqlc-89vw (PR shipping the two server-side gates),
which could not edit the justfile: that file was owned by another change in
flight the same night.

TWO EXACT LINES ARE MISSING, both in the justfile.

1. `test-hooks` is a hand-maintained list of suites. Add, alongside the
   other rows:

       bash .github/scripts/tests/ci-identity-gate-test.sh

   The suite covers .github/scripts/check-pr-authors.sh and
   .github/scripts/check-label-lengths.py; 35 rows, green at filing. It runs
   today ONLY from a step in the tidy job of .github/workflows/ci.yml, so it
   is CI-enforced but `just test` and the pre-push hook do not run it.

   NOTE ON ITS LOCATION, which is deliberate and is the reason this bead
   exists: it is NOT under .githooks/tests. internal/tools/ciguard's
   TestEveryHookTestSuiteIsNamedByTestHooks requires every suite under that
   directory to be named by `test-hooks` — an unwired suite there is an
   absent gate — and satisfying it needs the justfile edit this bead defers.
   Whoever wires it may also move the file back under .githooks/tests if
   they prefer one home for suites; then the ci.yml step can go, since
   `just test` covers it. Either way the two must agree.

2. `lint-hooks` defaults to dir=".githooks" and has therefore never linted
   .github/scripts. That directory is shellchecked today only by an explicit
   `just lint-hooks .github/scripts` step in ci.yml. The local `lint` recipe
   should call the recipe over that directory too, so a developer sees the

title: hooks: bd-gh-sync runs 1067 lines with no shell options, and it is the ledger writer post-merge calls
description:
Found while working gqlc-zxh4, which asked for `set -euo pipefail` on
.githooks/pre-commit and said "worth checking every hook in .githooks/ for the
same gap rather than fixing only pre-commit." This is the result of that sweep,
filed rather than folded in: it is a 1067-line tool and the change is not a
one-liner to verify.

MEASURED 2026-08-22 at master 4b8076e4, `grep -c '^[[:space:]]*set -'`:

    .githooks/commit-msg                    set -euo pipefail
    .githooks/pre-push                      set -euo pipefail
    .githooks/guard-push-destination        set -euo pipefail
    .githooks/install-hooks-drift-tripwire  set -euo pipefail
    .githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire          set -u          (deliberate, below)
    .githooks/git-env-sandbox.sh            none            (deliberate, below)
    .githooks/post-merge                    none            (deliberate, below)
    .githooks/bd-gh-sync                    none            <- THIS BEAD

THREE OF THE FOUR OMISSIONS ARE DELIBERATE, and I am recording why so the next
sweep does not "fix" them:

  git-env-sandbox.sh is SOURCED, not run (its own header says so, and
  .githooks/tests/git-env-sandbox-test.sh:47 sources it). `set -e` in a sourced
  file sets the option in the CALLER's shell, so adding it there would silently
  change the failure behaviour of every suite that sources it.

  post-merge is documented non-blocking — "never fail the underlying git pull"
  — and its whole body is one `bd-gh-sync pull` call followed by `exit 0`. With
  `set -e` that call's failure would pre-empt the `exit 0`.

  hooks-drift-tripwire takes `set -u` only. It is a diagnostic whose job is to
  PRINT and then choose an exit code per hook name; `set -e` would risk it
  dying before it says anything, which is the failure it exists to report.

WHY bd-gh-sync IS DIFFERENT. It is not a diagnostic and it is not sourced. It
is the tool that WRITES the bead ledger, invoked from post-merge on every
`git pull`, and it carries 1067 lines with zero shell options and only 4
explicit `|| true` sites. A mid-run failure therefore continues to the next
statement by default. That is the same shape as the defect gqlc-zxh4 fixed and
the one the post-merge header already reports having been bitten by: "a
fail-open guard revert claimed beads on every merge without anyone seeing a
line about it."

NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, which is why this is a bead and not a follow-up commit.
Adding `set -euo pipefail` to a 1067-line script changes the behaviour of every
arm that currently relies on a non-zero command continuing. The work is: add
the options, then walk every command whose failure was previously absorbed, and
decide each one. There is an existing suite to hang the result on,
.githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP: add the options, run bd-gh-sync-test.sh, and treat every
newly-red row as a site that was depending on fail-open — the reds are the
inventory, not the regression.
close_reason: Done in PR #1330 (squash 912c9a62). .githooks/bd-gh-sync now declares 'set -Eeuo pipefail' with an ERR trap. The trap is load-bearing, not decoration: both callers of this script keep only the LAST stderr line, so a run that dies where it stands writes no verdict at all. The trap emits one per action -- pull prints PULL FAILED and exits zero (post-merge must never fail the underlying pull), push prints PUSH FAILED and exits non-zero. Two rows assert verdict and exit status separately. Every newly-red site was decided rather than silenced with a default: the two pulled.txt writes keep the ratified fail-open design (the held-bead detector reports itself as not-run) but now say so out loud; grep -c goes through a _count helper because exit status one there is a count of zero, an answer and not an error; grep piped into sed became 'sed -n s///p', which exits zero on no match. RED control measured: the three new rows were run against master's bd-gh-sync via the suite's SYNC_BIN knob and all three fail there, and master's actual wrong output is quoted in the test comment. Suite went from 178 to 191 rows, all green.

title: hooks: one test suite keeps a private copy of the shared git-env scrub, and nothing stops a second
description:
Raised by agent-f as non-blocking observation 3 in his round-2 PASS of PR #1195
(bead gqlc-zo6h). Filing it rather than fixing it inside that PR, because
changing a reviewed artifact after a PASS means a new head and a re-review for
a change that is behaviourally a no-op.

## The state

`.githooks/tests/commit-msg-test.sh:16` scrubs git's environment with its own
inline copy:

    unset "${!GIT_@}"

rather than sourcing the shared `.githooks/git-env-sandbox.sh`, which exists
for exactly this and whose own header says "Source it".

This is not a bug today. The line is correct, and the gate
(`git-env-sandbox-test.sh`) verifies BEHAVIOUR — it poisons the environment and
watches what each suite hands to `git` — so a suite that sanitises by any
spelling passes. That is the right design for the gate, and it is why this
never goes red.

## Why it is still worth closing

One inline copy is one copy that can drift. The gate proves the suite is
sanitised NOW; it does not prevent the two spellings diverging later, and the
whole argument of PR #1195 was that an enumerated per-suite approach goes stale
while a single shared line does not. Leaving one suite on its own copy leaves a
small instance of the pattern the PR was written to remove.

It is also the suite for `commit-msg` — the hook that gates every commit in the
fleet — so it is the least good place to keep a private copy of a shared rule.

## Suggested fix

Replace the inline unset with the source, matching every other suite:

    source "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/git-env-sandbox.sh"

(spelling to match whatever the sibling suites settled on — take theirs, do not
invent a third.)

## What would make this verifiable rather than cosmetic

Do NOT rely on the existing gate to prove the change is safe: it passes both
before and after by construction, so it witnesses nothing about this edit. The
honest checks are:

  - `commit-msg-test.sh` still reports its full row count unchanged (29/0 at
    the time of writing), because sourcing must not disturb the suite's own
    setup — the sandbox unsets variables, and a suite that depended on one
    would break here and nowhere else
  - a grep asserting no suite in `.githooks/tests/` carries its own `unset
    "${!GIT_@}"` — which is the row that stops the copy coming back, and is the
    only part of this that is a gate rather than a tidy-up

That second row is arguably the whole value of the bead. Without it this is a
one-line cleanup that the next person is free to undo; with it, the "source
the shared line" rule is enforced instead of merely followed.

## Scope note

Held behind `subject:.githooks/tests/commit-msg-test.sh` while PR #1195 and
PR #1194 are both open on that file — they are already resolving a collision
there and a third edit would make it worse. Releases by itself when they merge.
close_reason: PR #1326, merged as master 606deb04, partially: the three suites in my lane now source .githooks/git-env-sandbox.sh, namely commit-msg-test.sh, hooks-drift-tripwire-test.sh and repo-purity-test.sh, and the new gate-pushed-commits-test.sh sources it from birth. The bead's premise is understated, though. It says one suite keeps a private copy; measured on the branch, eleven did. Eight remain and all eight belong to other lanes: bd-gh-sync, claude-pre-bash, init-config, fleetctl-overlap, fleetctl, shared-config-drift, tool-gate and worktree-upstream. The repo-wide grep row this bead calls arguably the whole value cannot land while eight suites would trip it, so I deliberately did not write it rather than write it disabled. Filed as gqlc-o9wz, which carries the full list and the falsifier a converter should use: delete the source line and confirm the fixtures reach the shared repo under a real push, because a green direct run is exactly what this defect looks like. Verification here is the push that created the branch, which ran the whole suite through the edited pre-push, plus sixteen suites green under just test-hooks and under CI's test job.

title: check-pr-closes: only the resolving bead's Closes is held to anything — a second closing keyword passes unexamined
description:
`.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py` exists so that a closing keyword in a PR
body cannot assert something the bd<->GH mapping does not support. Its own
docstring states the harm exactly:

    "the claim is made, GitHub acts on it at merge, and there is nothing left
     here to hold the number against"

That is true of every closing keyword in the body. The gate holds ONE.

MEASURED 2026-08-22 (agent-c), locally, against the real checker and a real
`bd export`, while fixing PR #1237:

  body: "Bead: [deleted:gqlc-xq8a] / Closes #1218 / Closes #1125"
    -> [check-pr-closes] [deleted:gqlc-xq8a] -> Closes #1218 (ok)      rc=0

  same body, second keyword rewritten to an issue that does not exist:
  "Bead: [deleted:gqlc-xq8a] / Closes #1218 / Closes #999999"
    -> [check-pr-closes] [deleted:gqlc-xq8a] -> Closes #1218 (ok)      rc=0

The output is IDENTICAL. Nothing mentions the second number in either run.
GitHub, at merge, acts on both. So a PR can close an unrelated issue, or claim
to close a number that mirrors nothing, and this gate reports the same green
line it reports for a correct body.

Note the shape: the gate resolves one bead (from `Bead:`/`Refs:`/branch) and
asserts that bead's mirror number appears among the closes. That is an
assertion over the FIRST/declared mapping, not a per-keyword one. It is the
aggregate-guard shape this fleet keeps rediscovering (gqlc-0h8t and the
NotZero-over-three-sources note): one satisfied member makes the whole body
read as verified.

A SECOND, SEPARATE SILENT PASS, found in the same session and worth fixing in
the same breath because it produces a green check that verified nothing:

  against PR #1237's then-committed export, the same body printed
    [check-pr-closes] bead '[deleted:gqlc-xq8a]' not in export - skipping
  and exited 0.

A bead absent from the in-tree export cannot be checked, so skipping is
defensible — but the exit status does not distinguish "mapping verified" from
"mapping not examined", and the in-tree export lags the DB routinely (that is
why `chore(bd): refresh the export ...` commits keep being needed). Whether
the skip should be a hard failure, a `::warning::` annotation, or left alone is
this bead's call; that it is indistinguishable from a pass is the finding.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not binding on whoever takes it:
  - assert per closing keyword, not once over the body: every `Closes #N` must
    resolve to a bead in the export, or be declared and refused deliberately;
  - make the skip say so in a way a reader and a required check can both see.

TESTING NOTE for whoever takes it: both findings above reproduce by running
`python3 .github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py <export.jsonl> <body.txt> <branch>`
directly. It needs no network and no PR. Any guard added here should be
mutated before it is trusted — a row that asserts rc alone will not tell these
two silent passes from a real one, which is how they got here.
notes:
--- 2026-08-23, agent-m ---
Both findings implemented, two commits on fix/7i3g-per-keyword-closes.

1e1e3104  hold every closing keyword (finding 1)      170 rows green at that SHA
a68899a9  name what the export-lag skip skipped (2)   174 rows green at that SHA

REBASE NOTE, the part worth carrying: the branch predated e5e88f0e (#1335),
which split prose_only() into visible_prose()/claimable_prose(). The rebase
MERGED CLEAN AND WAS STILL WRONG -- my calls kept reading the bare prose_only()
that split's docstring says not to call, and exactly one row went red (master's
own, a wrong number quoted in a code span). Clean rebase is not a semantic
check when the upstream change was a refactor of the function you call.

Wrapper now chosen per scan by which way it is expensive to be wrong:
  extras -> claimable_prose()  (a hit refuses; a PR about this gate quotes
                                closing lines as examples)
  avowal -> visible_prose()    (it SUBTRACTS a refusal, so honouring one no
                                reader can find is how an unheld keyword
                                reaches merge)
The avowal choice was unguarded by the existing rows -- a fence and an indent
are blanked by BOTH wrappers -- so it has a new row that separates them: an
avowal hidden in an unterminated HTML attribute.

FINDING 2 resolved as a ::warning:: annotation + numbers on the summary line,
NOT a hard failure. Refusing is for a claim the author can withdraw; the export
lands in its own chore commit after the PR merges, so no author can make their
bead appear in the copy CI reads.

7 mutations, all KILLED, each by the row that argues for it. One correction to
my own method: the first sed for the extras scan also matched main()'s no-bead
line, mutating two call sites and killing 4 rows. Scoped to extra_closes()
alone it kills exactly 1. The 4-row figure certified nothing and is not the
evidence.

DEMONSTRATED ON THIS PR'S OWN BODY: append 'Closes #999999' to it and master's
checker prints "gqlc-7i3g -> Closes #1277 (ok)" at rc=0; this branch refuses.

Residue filed, not ridden: gqlc-peg9 (P3), the module docstring's "until this
commit" is self-dating prose that rots at the next commit. Inherited, not
introduced here.
2026-08-24 (agent-m): PR #1464 opened, 3 commits, suite 152 -> 181. Review bead [deleted:gqlc-jwt4] (unassigned, class:reviewer, P2) names my sharpest doubt: the Also-closes avowal is an author-declared escape hatch nothing verifies, so the guarantee is 'held against a bead OR declared by a human', weaker than this bead asked for. Branch fix/7i3g-per-keyword-closes @ 434c0d22.
2026-08-24T03:13Z: PR #1464 CI fully green (tidy, lint, test, codegen-fence, actionlint, govulncheck, live-smoke). Witness worth keeping: tidy's log shows CI ran the PR head's own check-pr-closes.py over this PR's body and printed '[check-pr-closes] gqlc-7i3g -> Closes #1277 (ok)' — the changed gate judged its own PR on the merge ref and did not false-red. NOT merging on green: no design bead blocked this (bd dep list: none) and it amends no protocol, but I asked for review myself via [deleted:gqlc-jwt4], so protocol's third trigger applies. Left for a reviewer.

Her review added two mutations of her own: the own-number exclusion KILLED (17 rows), and one SURVIVED (skip-path avowal subtraction), filed as gqlc-in4f (P3) rather than fixed here. Also filed by her: gqlc-yh3r (P3, pre-existing — the epic / no-external_ref / unparseable-mirror exits still pass closing keywords unexamined, and the epic exit passes a body closing the umbrella itself). My own residue gqlc-peg9 (P3) stands.

title: a bead in a non-closed status whose GH mirror is CLOSED is drift the pull can never resolve
description:
Split out of gqlc-gudu (PR #1236). This is what survives of agent-a's original (b)
after it was measured; he has ratified the narrowing on gudu.

## What (b) was, and why it was cut down

gudu asked for "a check that FAILS when a bd bead and its GH mirror disagree on
open/closed". Measured against the live corpus, that is too wide to build:

  - The pull is both the observer AND the resolver. It applies a GH-side closure and
    afterwards the two sides AGREE, so a scheduled detector sees `bd open / GH closed`
    only if it happens to run inside the window between the close and the next pull.
  - Inside that window it cannot tell the incident from routine traffic — EVERY
    GH-side close sits in exactly that state — and there is no field to sort by:
    139 of 402 closed mirrors carry no closing PR reference (our own `bd close` ->
    push path closes mirrors with no PR behind them), and 381 of 402 are COMPLETED.

A gate firing on a third of normal closures is the `2>/dev/null` shape. gudu's PR
handles that half instead by NAMING the closure at the moment of application.

## The half that is real, and is not covered by PR #1236

A bead whose status is NOT representable on GitHub (in_progress / blocked / deferred)
with a CLOSED mirror, and the mirror image, a `closed` bead with an OPEN mirror. The
pull HOLDS both forever — it cannot pull them and cannot fix them — so unlike the
closure case there is no window: the drift is durable, and durable drift is what a
gate is for. Today they are reported only on a stderr line under a hook that exits 0,
which is why the one live instance sat for a month unseen.

Same family as gqlc-5vp7: states that read as "someone has this" while routing to
nobody.

## Before building

BLOCKED ON gqlc-rsbq. The one live instance (gqlc-23e / GH #171) must be repaired
first. A fail-closed gate that goes in red teaches everyone to pass it with a flag.

## Notes for whoever takes it

  - Baseline to expect after rsbq: ZERO. Measured 2026-08-22 over 689 beads / 723
    issues (listing not truncated): closed x closed 366, open x open 294,
    in_progress x open 26, blocked x open 1, blocked x CLOSED 1. Only the last is drift.
  - `in_progress x open` (26) and `blocked x open` (1) are NOT drift — GitHub has no
    such states, and bd-gh-sync:266 deliberately stays silent on them when the bodies
    match. A gate that counts them fires 27 times on a healthy fleet.
  - Needs network (`gh`), so it cannot live in `just test`, which runs offline.
    Workflow-shaped, like `iso-drift-check`. Precedent for the tool: internal/tools/
    ghorphan and bdguard.
  - The field is `external_ref` on `bd list --status all --limit 0 --json`; parse with
    `/issues/(\d+)$`, and pass `-n 0` / `--limit 0` or the renderer caps you silently.
notes:
=== AGENT-M 2026-08-22 — blocker rsbq CLEARED, plus one finding that constrains the design ===

BASELINE IS NOW CLEAN. gqlc-rsbq is repaired (GH #171 reopened, bd description
aligned; bd status left `blocked`, which was always correct). Post-repair census
over all 710 mirrored beads, measured on live listings:

  closed x closed 371 | open x open 310 | in_progress x open 26 |
  blocked x open 2 | closed x open 1
  NON-CLOSED bead x CLOSED mirror: 0

The class this gate is for is EMPTY today, so the gate can go in fail-closed and
GREEN — which is exactly the precondition agent-a's ruling on gudu attached to it.

THE FINDING THAT CHANGES HOW THIS MUST BE BUILT. Do not build this gate on the
sync's hold records. Measured, not read: I ran the pull's real plan code
(verbatim from origin/master:.githooks/bd-gh-sync) on live inputs and mutated
exactly one field — flipped GH #171 from CLOSED to OPEN, changing nothing else.

  OUTPUT WAS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE CONTROL. `diff` empty.

Both states emit the same record, `HOLD gqlc-23e 171
status-blocked-unrepresentable-on-gh`. The branch's own comment asserts "A
*closed* mirror is a real disagreement and still reported" — and it is reported,
but under a reason string that does not distinguish it from the benign case. So
the disagreement this gate exists to catch is INVISIBLE in the artifact that
looks like the natural place to read it from.

Consequence for the design: the gate must compare bd status x GH state directly
from the two listings. Any implementation that greps hold reasons, or counts
holds, will pass while the drift is present. This is the 'assert the reason, not
the verdict' shape, one level out — here even the reason is insufficient.

A TEST THIS SUGGESTS: the sweep above IS the gate's own falsifier. Feed the gate
a corpus with one bead flipped to the drift state and require it to FAIL; feed it
the benign `blocked x open` variant of the same bead and require it to PASS. A
gate that cannot separate those two rows is the defect, and a gate built on hold
reasons demonstrably cannot.

SECOND REAL INSTANCE, with a cause distinct from gudu's — strengthens the case
for this gate. rsbq's root cause was not an unexplained close. PR #334 carried
`Closes #171` and merged; GitHub auto-closed the issue one second later; PR #349
then reverted every file #334 added. #349 used `Refs #171` (correctly, not a
closing keyword) and set the bead `blocked` (correctly) — and GitHub still offers
no way to un-close. Nobody made a mistake and the mirror was wrong for a month.
So this class arises from ordinary careful reverting, not only from anomalies,
and it is exactly the class the pull can never resolve.

title: commit-msg: a bare reserved TLD is refused by the shape rule, not by the reserved-name rule
description:
Measured 2026-08-22 by agent-g while cross-running the three colliding commit-msg
branches (PR #1184 / #1194 / #1195) against each other's suites.

## The observation

An address at a bare reserved TLD -- `x@invalid`, `x@test`, `x@localhost`, and an
empty email -- is REFUSED by .githooks/commit-msg today. It is refused by the
SHAPE arm ("must contain @ and the domain part must contain a dot"), not by the
reserved-name arm.

Witnessed on PR #1194's hook (8e4d65c7), which is the measured superset of the
three and the one the resolution should take wholesale:

    x@invalid     -> reject, reason `shape:author`
    (empty)       -> reject, reason `shape:author`

PR #1184's hook (ce82c250, mine, now closed) attributed both to `denylist:author`.
That difference is what made two of my suite's rows fail against #1194's hook --
both hooks reject, they disagree only on which rule did it.

## Why it is a defect and not a curiosity

The reserved-name rule exists so that a name RFC 2606 / RFC 6761 reserves can
never be a commit author. Its coverage of the BARE forms is currently incidental:
it holds because those spellings happen to also violate a rule about dots.

Relax the shape arm -- and there is a plausible reason to, intranet and
single-label addresses -- and `x@invalid` becomes an accepted commit author with
no test row going red anywhere. The gate would still be green and its own stated
thesis would be false.

## The fix, which is small

The reserved-name predicate should match the bare forms itself, and a row should
pin the REASON and not merely the verdict, so that the two arms cannot silently
trade responsibility. Assert `denylist:*` for `x@invalid` / `x@test` /
`x@localhost` / `x@example`, independently of whatever the shape arm does.

## Sequencing

Do NOT land this before the three-way collision is resolved (gqlc-gy3q notes, and
my 3x3 matrix on PR #1194). It is one row plus a predicate line and belongs in the
resolution pass, not in a fourth open PR on the same two files. Filed rather than
pushed onto #1194's head so that head -- and gqlc-8ram's named review head -- does
not go stale for one row.
close_reason: PR #1326, merged as master 606deb04. The premise is largely false on master and I am closing it as measured rather than as fixed. Probing implausible_email_reason directly shows x-at-invalid, x-at-test, x-at-localhost and x-at-example all report the reserved reason, its domain is reserved, not the shape reason. Only the empty address takes the shape arm, and that is correct: an empty address has no domain to call reserved. So the routing the bead asks for is already what the hook does. What was genuinely missing is the pin. Two arms reached one verdict and nothing asserted which one, so a regression that started refusing reserved names for being malformed would have kept every row green. commit-msg-test.sh now has a reason case helper asserting the stderr substring for each of the four reserved domains, plus nobody-at-host and the empty address, so each arm is held to its own reason and not merely to the refusal. Suite is forty passing, zero failing, up from twenty-nine measured on the branch point via git archive of origin master.

title: codegen corpus: an in-body table loop can go vacuous with both censuses green
description:
Follow-up to gqlc-mlf4 (PR #1069), which closes the SUBTEST half of this and leaves this half open. Not a regression from that branch — pre-existing, and strictly narrower after it lands.

## The shape

gqlc-mlf4 gives the corpus census a `corpusSubtests` map, so a top-level test whose `t.Run` tree stops running drops a key and reddens. That guard can only see tests that are subtest-shaped. The corpus fixtures are mostly NOT: they assert through plain in-body `for ... range` loops over a table, inside a top-level test.

Empty such a table and:
  - the top-level test still passes and still carries its name, so `corpusTests` / `ElementsMatch` is satisfied
  - no subtest `pass` event is emitted at all, so `corpusSubtests` is satisfied — the test has no key on either side, which is equality
  - #1002's non-empty guard is satisfied

So the assertions inside vanish with the whole census green. This is the same aggregate-emptiness family as gqlc-wla6 and gqlc-mlf4, one carrier over.

## Measured, with the method, so it can be re-derived rather than trusted

On efc56695 (PR #1069's head):

    grep -c '^func Test'      neo4j fixture 21   age fixture 29
    grep -c 't\.Run('         neo4j fixture  1   age fixture  1
    grep -cE '^\tfor .*range ' neo4j fixture 14   age fixture 31

TREAT THE THIRD ROW AS A FLOOR, NOT A COUNT. It matches only tab-indented (top-level-in-function) loops, so loops nested inside an if or another loop are missed, and it does not distinguish an assertion table from a loop that merely builds a value. What would falsify the framing entirely: if the unconverted loops turn out not to carry assertions, there is nothing here to guard.

## Do not assume the remedy is 'convert them all'

Converting every table loop to `t.Run` and pinning a count is one option and probably the expensive one — it edits two large fixtures and buys a size check, not a membership check (a renamed or swapped case leaves any count where it was; gqlc-mlf4's own PR body states that limit). Price at least one alternative before building: an assertion-count carried out of the child run, or a per-test floor, may cover the plain-loop shape without reshaping the fixtures.

## Screens (inherited from gqlc-mlf4 — these cost real rounds, do not rediscover)

  - `go test -c` is NOT the screen: the fixture compiles one module DOWN. Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log.
  - Assert BOTH `[build failed]` and `[setup failed]` absent. A fixture parse error prints setup, not build — and an unused variable left by a mutation is a fake RED, not a kill.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on '^[[:space:]]*--- PASS', never '^ *--- PASS'. testify indents with TABs; the space-only class reported 0 where the truth was 21.

Related: gqlc-mlf4 (the subtest half), gqlc-wla6 (the top-level half), gqlc-hreu (the wrong screen).

Re-measured the bead's own greps on origin/master 4a478f85 so the framing is not taken on trust: neo4j fixture funcs=21 t.Run=1 tab-indented range loops=14; age fixture funcs=30 t.Run=1 loops=33. Both files carry exactly one t.Run between them, so corpusSubtests holds one key (TestListyRefusesAMisTypedElement: 4) against 51 top-level tests. The age fixture has GROWN since the bead was filed (29 to 30 funcs, 31 to 33 loops), so the gap is widening, not stale. Still open and still correct.
