title: ci: no required context runs just fmt-check, so gofumpt/gci may rest on the local pre-commit hook alone
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-18 at origin/master 07954baf, read-only, by the orchestrator.

THE OBSERVATION. Go formatting (gofumpt + gci) has its own recipe, separate from
lint:

  justfile:677  fmt: ensure-golangci        -> {{golangci}} fmt
  justfile:681  fmt-check: ensure-golangci  -> {{golangci}} fmt --diff

`.githooks/pre-commit:42-51` calls `just fmt-check` and fails the commit on a
non-zero exit ("ERROR: unformatted Go files. Run: just fmt").

No workflow calls it. Enumerated by rendering every file under
.github/workflows/ from origin/master and grepping each for `just <recipe>`:

  ci.yml            vuln-root-residual, lint, lint-cache-check, test,
                    tidy-check, bd-export-monotonic, test-codegen-fence,
                    actionlint
  codegen-live.yml  test-codegen-live-neo4j, test-codegen-live-age
  iso-drift.yml     iso-drift-check
  vuln.yml          vuln

`fmt-check` is not among them, and `lint` runs `{{golangci}} run`
(justfile:663-664), which is a different golangci-lint subcommand from the
`{{golangci}} fmt --diff` that fmt-check runs.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD EXISTS TO SETTLE, AND WHICH I DID NOT SETTLE.
`.golangci.yml:174-177` puts gofumpt and gci under a `formatters:` block. In
golangci-lint v2 (this repo pins v2.12.2, justfile:5) `formatters:` is the
section the `fmt` subcommand applies. Whether `golangci-lint run` ALSO reports
those formatters as diagnostics decides everything here:

  - If `run` reports them, the required `lint` context covers formatting
    independently and there is no hole; fmt-check is a local convenience. Then
    this bead closes as investigated-not-a-defect and the finding is worth one
    sentence somewhere durable, because the separate recipe invites the opposite
    assumption.
  - If `run` does NOT report them, gofumpt/gci are enforced by the local
    pre-commit hook ALONE. That is the failure mode gqlc-4thl documents: when
    core.hooksPath drifts, the hook is silently absent and unformatted Go reaches
    master with all seven required contexts green. It is also this repo's
    recurring shape -- "is there a check?" is not "does it FAIL?".

HOW TO SETTLE IT. Cheap and decisive: in a throwaway worktree, introduce one
gofumpt-detectable violation (a blank line immediately after a function's
opening brace is reliable), then run `{{golangci}} run` scoped to that package
and see whether it reports. Take an rc=0 control on the pristine file first, or
the result witnesses nothing. Note the cache is per-worktree
(GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE := justfile_directory() + "/.bin/golangci-cache",
justfile:16), so a fresh worktree runs COLD and this is slower than it looks.
golangci-lint also holds a global lock -- "Error: parallel golangci-lint is
running" is a lock collision, not a lint failure; poll with `pgrep -x
golangci-lint`.

DO NOT WRITE A COUNT OR A UNIVERSAL INTO THE FIX. The enumeration above is a
result about the workflow files at 07954baf, not a property of the repo.

Related: gqlc-4thl (hooksPath drift kills the local gates; this is the second
half of its open item 2, which I recorded on that bead but did not resolve),
gqlc-7ijy (who writes the drift), gqlc-eo46 and the 'detector that exits 0 is
not a gate' family.
close_reason:
SETTLED, and it is NOT a defect. Measured 2026-08-23 in worktree gqlc-ci-gate off origin/master e580fd70, golangci-lint v2.13.1 (the justfile pin), GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE=.bin/golangci-cache.

THE QUESTION THE BEAD LEFT OPEN was whether 'golangci-lint run' also reports the entries under .golangci.yml's 'formatters:' block, or only 'golangci-lint fmt' does. It reports them.

  control  .bin/golangci-lint run ./internal/version/...              '0 issues.' rc=0
  gofumpt  blank line after a function's opening brace appended to
           internal/version/version.go
           'internal/version/version.go:16:1: File is not properly formatted (gofumpt)' rc=1
           (fmt --diff on the same tree: rc=1, prints the removal)
  control  .bin/golangci-lint run ./internal/config/... pristine      rc=0
  gci      import block reordered in internal/config/count_internal_test.go
           'internal/config/count_internal_test.go:4:1: File is not properly formatted (gci)' rc=1

Both controls were taken on the pristine files first, so the violated runs witness something. Files restored; git status clean after each.

CONSEQUENCE. The required 'lint' context DOES enforce gofumpt and gci, via 'just lint' -> '{{golangci}} run'. 'just fmt-check' is a local convenience, not the only enforcement, so gofumpt/gci do NOT rest on .githooks/pre-commit alone and a core.hooksPath drift window (gqlc-4thl) cannot land unformatted Go on master. The enumeration in the bead's description -- no workflow calls fmt-check -- was correct and is not the hole it looked like. The justfile's own lint recipe comment already said it: 'linters + formatter diffs as issues'.

RECORDED DURABLY, which the bead asked for: a comment beside the 'just lint' step in .github/workflows/ci.yml carrying the measurement, shipped in PR #1331.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, filed as gqlc-sh4j: nothing in the tree holds golangci-lint to this behaviour. It is a property of a pinned third-party binary under a config key. A version bump that stops reporting formatters as issues, or a move of gofumpt/gci out of 'formatters:', would silence the required context with every check green. That wants a Go test in internal/tools/ciguard, which was another lane's tonight.

title: codegen: the neo4j/age corpus comment is byte-identical in two packages by hand, and nothing enforces that
notes:
Surfaced by the independent review of PR #1002 round 3 (bd gqlc-wla6). Classified
residue there: pre-existing, and nothing on that branch made it worse.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY. The comment block above corpusTests in
internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go and internal/codegen/age/corpus_test.go is
byte-identical -- 527 bytes, md5 92236145c7ec46624cbe901ff513cb50 at 15e8f9d2,
measured on both files. That identity is maintained by hand.

THE GAP. No test, no lint rule and no just recipe compares the two. A future
edit to one package's comment leaves the other saying something the author
believed they were changing everywhere. That is this repository's second most
repeated defect -- fix a class in one carrier, leave the twin live on another --
and here the twin relationship is real, deliberate, and unguarded.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL HERE. The comment is not decoration. It is the
carrier that explains what require.NotEmpty refuses and why the list is a
declaration rather than a gate. PR #1002 spent three rounds getting its wording
true. Nothing stops round four of some future branch from correcting one copy.

DO NOT ASSUME THE FIX IS A NEW TEST. Options, not a ruling: a test in one
package that reads the sibling's source and compares the block; a shared const
or a //go:generate; or a deliberate decision that the two should be allowed to
diverge, recorded where the comment is. A test that reads a sibling package's
source bytes has its own hazard -- see the gate-reads-source-bytes note -- and
would need to render from the AST rather than grep raw bytes.

MEASURE BEFORE ACTING. Confirm the two blocks are still byte-identical at
whatever head you start from; if they have already drifted, that drift is the
more interesting finding and should be reported rather than silently repaired.

Measured on origin/master 4a478f85 so the next agent starts from a number rather than the bead title: an automated block-comparison of every comment block of four or more lines in the two corpus_test.go files finds exactly TWO byte-identical blocks, not one large one. A ten-line block opening 'runCorpus runs the assembled corpus module own tests, reporting the' at age:220 and neo4j:284, and a four-line block opening 'The comparison is by multiset, so a name written twice differs from' at age:205 and neo4j:224. Everything else in the two files differs. So the duplication is much smaller than the bead reads, and the cheapest remedy the brief asks to price first is available: both blocks describe a shared harness concept, so one copy could state it and the other point at it by name. Before building any enforcement machinery, re-run the measurement — it is a fourteen-line problem.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #1400, and the bead's premise was understated rather than stale. MEASURED on master 004e4c2a by comparing every comment block of three or more lines in internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go against every such block in internal/codegen/age/corpus_test.go: THREE blocks were byte-identical, not one. The runCorpus doc block, ten lines and 557 bytes, at age line 220 and neo4j line 295; the 'comparison is by multiset' block, four lines and 268 bytes; and the 'Compared whole rather than per key' block, three lines and 211 bytes. Seventeen lines and 1036 bytes in total. The BODY of runCorpus was identical in both files as well, modulo the receiver and how each reached a context, so the duplication was code and not only prose. Given that, a gate comparing two copies was the wrong remedy and none was built. The shared half moved into a new package, internal/codegen/corpusrun: the child run, the three declaration comparisons, and the prose explaining what each refuses. Each backend keeps only its own corpusTests, corpusSubtests and corpusTables literals. The package names no backend, following internal/codegen/emitscan's argument that an equivalent living inside one backend's test package leaves every other backend unswept. corpusrun has its own unit suite, seven tests, including one row per way Declared.Check has to fail.

title: ciguard: justRecipe's header regex turns an unmodelled recipe spelling into a fake RED, and no carrier says so
notes:
Surfaced reviewing PR #996 round 5 (bd gqlc-sgot / gqlc-lisu). Not a defect in
what shipped; the shipped prose is conservative. This is the direction of the
limit, which no carrier currently states.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. internal/tools/ciguard/testhooks_test.go:125 builds
  header := regexp.MustCompile(`^` + regexp.QuoteMeta(name) + `[ \t]*:(.*)$`)
so a recipe header just accepts but this pattern does not match -- a
parameterised header such as `test-hooks *args:` is the obvious one -- leaves
start == -1 and fires require.GreaterOrEqualf at :135 with "has no recipe %q, so
the chain that reaches the shell suites from a required CI context is broken at
that link".

WHY IT MATTERS. That message names a broken CI chain. The actual cause would be
a recipe header spelling the reader does not model, with the chain intact. That
is the fake-RED shape this repository already screens mutations for, and the
comment block at :112-119 discusses fake RED only for `just --dump`'s parse
failures -- not for its own header pattern.

The PR body bullet (996 body 239-241) states the limit non-directionally: a
spelling just accepts and justRecipe does not model "is outside the assertions
built on it". True and deliberately non-directional, which is why this is
residue and not a blocker. But no carrier says which way it falls, and the
direction is the useful part: it is loud, not silent.

WHAT TO DO. Decide and record the direction. Options, not a ruling: widen the
header pattern to admit parameters and default values; or leave the pattern and
give the require message a second clause naming the spelling-not-modelled cause
alongside the broken-chain one; or state the direction in the comment at
:112-119 next to the existing fake-RED discussion. Whichever, the fix belongs in
the code comment or the require message -- the PR body is not a carrier CI
gates.

MEASURE FIRST, DO NOT TRUST THIS NOTE. Put an actual unmodelled spelling through
justRecipe in a scratch worktree and record rc plus the failing line, rather
than reasoning from the regex. Neither the round-5 author nor I ran one; both of
us read the pattern. The author self-reported exactly this gap.

RELATED. justRecipe "finds the recipe ... with a regex" is precise about the
header (:125, :129) and loose about the body, which is taken by indentation at
:138-148, not by a regex. Same function, smaller. Fold it in or leave it.

title: codegen: the corpus ElementsMatch failure message can be read positionally, and age's silent spellings were not re-measured after the guard landed
description:
Two weak residue items from the gqlc-wla6 / PR #1002 review. Both were rated
weak deliberately; neither reopened that PR. Recorded so they are not lost, not
because either is urgent.

1. THE FAILURE MESSAGE CAN BE READ POSITIONALLY.
   The corpus census compares with `ElementsMatch`, whose message says the
   comparison is "entry for entry and counting repeats". `ElementsMatch` IGNORES
   ORDER — it is a multiset comparison — but "entry for entry" is a phrase a
   reader can take positionally, i.e. as index-by-index. A CI reader sees only
   the message.
   The adjacent code comment does carry the correction ("comparison is by
   multiset"), so the information exists in the tree; it just is not in the
   carrier the failing reader gets.
   Note what is NOT wrong here: the message correctly states a RELATION and
   enumerates nothing. That was the round-1 defect (an enumeration of two causes
   that a duplicated entry fell outside of) and it is genuinely closed. Do not
   "fix" this by adding an enumeration back.

2. AGE'S SILENT SPELLINGS WERE NOT RE-MEASURED AFTER THE FIX.
   The three silent spellings and the duplicate-entry row were measured in the
   AGE package before the non-empty guard landed, and nobody re-took them after.
   No movement is EXPECTED — the name sets are identical between the packages
   and the guard was an additive edit — but expected is not witnessed. If anyone
   is in that file for another reason, re-take the four rows.

SCREENS, if either item is picked up (these cost real rounds on #1002):
  - `go test -c` is NOT the screen for these — the fixture compiles one module
    down (gqlc-hreu). Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log.
  - `\[(build|setup) failed\]` — assert BOTH spellings absent. A fixture parse
    error prints `[setup failed]`.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on `^[[:space:]]*--- PASS`; the space-only class misses
    testify's TAB indentation.

Related: gqlc-wla6, gqlc-mlf4, gqlc-lwtp, gqlc-hreu.
notes:

description:
PR #996's body names this as a follow-up rather than a hole it holds open, so
this bead is that follow-up's destination.

THE GAP. In `internal/tools/ciguard`, `continue-on-error` was promoted to a
`yaml.Node` so that its PRESENCE can be distinguished from its absence, but `If`
was left a plain string. A string cannot make that distinction: an explicit
`if: ""` written on a job decodes to the empty string, which is what an ABSENT
`if` also decodes to. So an explicit empty `if:` still passes `require.Empty`.

This is the conditional-gate-omission shape — a check on `X != ""` catches
disagreement but not omission, and silence passes where it should not. The fix
is a positive declaration on both shapes, i.e. a `yaml.Node` whose kind/validity
distinguishes "absent" from "present and empty", the same way
`continue-on-error` already does.

WHAT BOUNDS THE RISK TODAY, and why this is a follow-up rather than a blocker:
`actionlint` is itself one of the seven required CI contexts, and it returned
rc=1 on every empty-decoding spelling put to it, against an rc=0 control on the
unmodified file taken before and after each row. Measured out of tree on a copy
of ci.yml. So a workflow carrying such an `if:` does not reach merge silently —
a different required context refuses it first.

DO NOT WRITE A CLOSED ENUMERATION OF SPELLINGS. That is this PR's own history:
a bullet carried a list of spellings and a sentence closing it off, and the list
was short of what had already been run. YAML decodes to empty in spellings
nobody here has typed. Any claim written under this bead is a result about ROWS
TAKEN, not about the spelling space — state it that way or state nothing.

If you re-measure: `actionlint` exits **3** with "no project was found" outside
a git repo. That is a setup error, not a lint result. `git init` the probe dir,
and take the rc=0 control on the pristine file or your rc=1 rows witness nothing.

Related: gqlc-9qqj (the check-run question the same review routed out),
gqlc-sgot / gqlc-lisu (ciguard).
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-08-18, from the PR #996 round-4 review, verified first-party on
origin/master): the yaml.Node modelling this bead asks for ALREADY EXISTS in
this same package. This is adoption of an in-package idiom, not new design.

  internal/tools/ciguard/golangci_cache_test.go:68   If  yaml.Node  `yaml:"if"`
  internal/tools/ciguard/golangci_cache_test.go:81   func present(n yaml.Node) bool { return n.Kind != 0 }
  internal/tools/ciguard/golangci_cache_test.go:453  require.Falsef(t, present(s.If), "step %q in %s carries `if: %s` ...")

So `golangci_cache_test.go` already distinguishes an ABSENT `if:` from one that
is PRESENT AND EMPTY, for exactly the reason this bead names, and already emits
the refusal. `workflow_test.go` is the file that does not -- its `If` is a plain
string (workflow_test.go:53), which is why an explicit `if: ""` passes
require.Empty there.

The fix is therefore narrow and has a working model 400 lines away: change
workflow_test.go's `If string` to `If yaml.Node`, and assert with the existing
`present()` helper rather than `require.Empty`. Check whether `present()` needs
to move or be shared between the two files.

This also sharpens the defect: the package is INCONSISTENT with itself. One file
models `if:` presence correctly and one does not, and only the correct one is
obvious to a reader who happens to open it. PR #996's closing line "Promoting
`If` to a `yaml.Node` is a follow-up" is true of the workflow_test.go types but
reads as though the modelling were novel.

title: codegen/conformance: sweep the AST-census tests for the aggregate-emptiness shape gqlc-wla6 closed
description:
Same-class sweep opened off the gqlc-wla6 / PR #1002 review. That PR found a
census test whose only completeness check was an aggregate one, so emptying the
source AND the expectation together went GREEN. `internal/codegen/conformance`
has tests of the same construction and none were examined.

DERIVE THE SET YOURSELF. I am deliberately not listing which tests qualify, and
not stating how many. A review-supplied count gets copied into the fix's PR body
and bead notes without being re-measured, and the counts I have supplied on this
class have been wrong repeatedly — the failure mode is always a search scoped
smaller than the claim. Walk `internal/codegen/conformance/*_test.go` with
`go/parser` and select on the SHAPE below; whatever that yields is the set.

THE SHAPE TO SELECT FOR — a test that:
  - builds a census/inventory by walking an AST or parsing a fixture, then
  - compares it against a hand-maintained expectation (a literal slice/map), and
  - has no guard that the census itself is NON-EMPTY, or whose only guard is an
    aggregate over several sources.

Both failure modes are live in this repo and are different:
  - **Aggregate emptiness**: one `require.NotZero(total)` over N sources fires
    only if ALL N are silent; drop 2 of 3 and it stays green (gqlc-…, see the
    aggregate-emptiness note). Assert PER SOURCE.
  - **Total silence expressible**: source empty AND expectation empty ⇒ the
    comparison is vacuously satisfied. Needs a non-empty guard on the census
    BEFORE the comparison.

FOR EACH CANDIDATE, the finding is a MUTATION, not a reading. Empty the source
and the expectation together and show the test still passes. A code reading is
not a defect here.

AND MUTATE THE GUARD YOU ADD. #1002's first round added a guard that was present
but not load-bearing; the row that caught it was "delete the guard ⇒ GREEN
again". Every guard added under this bead needs that third row.

SCREENS — these cost real rounds on #1002, do not rediscover them:
  - `go test -c -o /dev/null <pkg>` is the mutation screen in general, but is
    UNSOUND where a fixture compiles one module down (gqlc-hreu). Check which
    case each test is before choosing.
  - Assert `\[(build|setup) failed\]` absent — BOTH spellings. A fixture PARSE
    error prints `[setup failed]`, not `[build failed]`; a screen grepping only
    the latter misclassifies it as a real RED.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on `^[[:space:]]*--- PASS`. `^ *--- PASS` misses
    testify's TAB indentation and reported 0 where the truth was 21 — a valid
    kill reads as a fake RED.
  - A legitimate RED with ZERO sibling PASS does exist, so the build/setup
    marker is the sound discriminator; sibling count alone is not.
  - Kill-count 1 with a BLANK test name means the COMPILER killed it (fake RED).

Related: gqlc-wla6, gqlc-mlf4 (subtest events discarded), gqlc-hreu (screen).

title: ci: settle what job-level continue-on-error does to a check run, on our own repo via workflow_dispatch
description:
PR #996's body routes a finding here, so this bead is the destination of that
routing. It names no id today, so nothing in that carrier is false — but the
routing has no target until this exists.

THE OPEN QUESTION. `internal/tools/ciguard`'s `require` message says the
check-run question is "not settled here", and that is deliberate and still true
of the branch. Two sub-questions are distinct and only one has any witness:

1. Does a job with job-level `continue-on-error: true` that fails still emit a
   check run concluding `failure` (and therefore still block branch protection)?
2. What does the key do to the enclosing WORKFLOW RUN's conclusion?

WHAT IS WITNESSED, AND HOW WEAKLY. #996 settled (1) on ONE third-party
observation: `cowrie/cowrie` job 95630008478, `test (3.15t, true, true)`, whose
workflow sets `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}` at job level with
`experimental: true`; job and check run of the same id both conclude `failure`.
Job-level placement confirmed by indentation at `tox.yml@708588bc:110`.

Three limits on that witness, all of which this bead exists to remove:
  - **n=1.** The PR body states it as a general present-tense rule. It has one
    observation. The paragraph bounds the RUN axis and leaves the SAMPLE-SIZE
    axis unbounded.
  - **Not two observations.** `/actions/jobs/{id}` and `/check-runs/{id}` are
    two VIEWS of one object, not corroboration.
  - **A third-party job id is a citation that rots.** cowrie can delete logs,
    rewrite the workflow, or age the run out. This is precisely why it was kept
    out of the `require` message.

(2) is NOT witnessed at all: that workflow run also concluded `failure`, but
jobs whose `continue-on-error` resolved FALSE failed in it too, so it is fully
explained without the key and witnesses nothing at run level.

UNRECONCILED TENSION TO RESOLVE HERE. PR #996 body ~line 190 reports a scan of
160 successful runs finding NO job concluding `failure` inside them; ~line 217
asserts such jobs conclude `failure`. Both can hold if continue-on-error jobs
are rare in that sample, but nothing measured that, and the body never says so.
Whatever this bead concludes must reconcile the two or show why they are
compatible.

WHY workflow_dispatch. Live arms are dispatchable — "no Docker locally" is not a
hard limit here. A throwaway workflow on our own repo with a deliberately
failing job under job-level `continue-on-error: true` answers both questions
first-party, with a citation that cannot rot because we own it. Take the
positive control too: the same workflow with the key absent/false, or the run
witnesses nothing.

DO NOT put the result in a `require` message. The message's second clause argues
a required context is not where to settle this, and that argument stands.
close_reason:
SETTLED first-party on this repo, 2026-08-23, throwaway PR #1323 / ci run 32622299816. Both sub-questions, with the enclosing run uncontaminated.

THE PROBE. A job 'coe-probe' added to ci.yml on a throwaway branch, job-level 'continue-on-error: true', last step 'exit 1'. In run 32622299816 it was the ONLY non-success job (tidy success, actionlint success, lint success, test success, codegen-fence skipped by a separate deliberate 'if: false'). That is what the cowrie witness could not give: a run whose failure is fully explained by the continue-on-error job and by nothing else.

(1) DOES THE JOB STILL EMIT A CHECK RUN CONCLUDING failure? YES.
    /actions/jobs/97152198083     -> conclusion 'failure'
    statusCheckRollup on the PR   -> name 'coe-probe', conclusion FAILURE
  So a required context under job-level continue-on-error still blocks branch protection. The n=1 third-party cowrie observation is now corroborated by a first-party one on a repo we own, and the citation cannot rot.

(2) WHAT DOES IT DO TO THE ENCLOSING WORKFLOW RUN? It hides the failure.
    /actions/runs/32622299816 -> conclusion 'success'
  A run containing a job that concluded 'failure' concluded 'success', because that job's continue-on-error resolved true. This was NOT witnessed before -- the cowrie run had ordinary failures in it too.

THE UNRECONCILED TENSION IN PR #996 IS RESOLVED, and in favour of the ~line 217 claim. A scan of successful runs CAN contain jobs concluding 'failure'; that is precisely what continue-on-error produces. #996's scan of 160 successful runs finding none therefore says its sample contained no continue-on-error jobs, not that such jobs do not conclude failure. The two statements are compatible and the body simply never measured the frequency.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH KEEPING: run-level conclusion is not a safe proxy for 'every job in it passed'. Anything reading a run's conclusion -- dashboards, the fleetctl status board, a nightly-liveness check -- is blind to a continue-on-error failure. Read job conclusions or check runs.

Not put in a require message, per the bead. The evidence lives here and in the header of .github/workflows/ci.yml (PR #1331).

title: claude-pre-bash: the deny message's '(… are all dead)' is false in exactly the fail-closed case
description:
Pre-existing prose defect in a runtime-emitted message. Found reviewing PR #992
(gqlc-wa8c) round 3. Identical string exists at cbb11a7e:364, so this is not
that branch's debt.

`.githooks/claude-pre-bash:447` emits:

    (commit-msg, pre-commit, pre-push and post-merge are all dead)

This is a four-way universal asserted at the moment of refusal. It is FALSE in
exactly the fail-closed case that PR #992's round-3 entry discloses: in the
reviewer's fixture `commit-msg` was live and fired while the message claimed it
was dead.

This is the repo's signature defect class — a universal in prose falsified by
the artifact it ships next to — and it is worse here than in a comment, because
this string is what a human sees at the moment they are being refused, and it
tells them not to bother checking a hook that is in fact running.

FIX SHAPE (do not just delete the four names): the message's job is to explain
WHY the refusal is happening. State what is pinned without quantifying over the
four hooks — the shape that survives review here states the negative and
enumerates limits without a count. Do not replace the four-name list with a
smaller list; that is the same defect with a different number.

Related: gqlc-b1kt (rebase -i reword bypasses commit-msg under the same drift).

    origin/master:.githooks/claude-pre-bash:447  "are all dead). Repair: just init"

So by the premise test this bead is routable right now. It is held anyway,
because PR #1029 MODIFIES THAT EXACT FILE — `gh pr view 1029 --json files`
returns .githooks/claude-pre-bash and its test. Routing an author here today
puts two branches on one file and hands somebody a conflict for no gain.

THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD. It means the rule for holding residue is a UNION
of two independent conditions, not one:

    HOLD if the premise is ABSENT from origin/master
       OR if an OPEN PR modifies the file the bead is about

Either alone is insufficient. gqlc-g1o8 is caught only by the first (it is not
even named in #1044's body). This bead is caught only by the second. Both are
mechanically checkable, which is the useful part — recorded on gqlc-8zw7.

no rebase-and-see, the defect is already on master.

title: Write down that go test -c is the wrong mutation screen for a testdata/*.go.txt fixture
description:
Methodology finding from PR #990 (bd gqlc-1uic), confirmed independently by both review rounds with an anchored mutation. It currently lives only in a PR body and two verdict files, none of which is a durable carrier the next author will read. It needs to land somewhere in-tree.

THE FINDING. `go test -c -o /dev/null <pkg>` is this repo's standard mutation screen, and it is UNSOUND for any mutation whose effect lands in emitted code that is compiled one module down -- i.e. anything under internal/codegen/*/testdata/*.go.txt.

Measured: making the emitted entity gate read `if linusUndefinedSymbol != nil {` leaves `go test -c ./internal/codegen/neo4j` at rc=0, while the package goes RED as `FAIL neo4jcorpus [build failed]` with ZERO child test names. `go test -c` compiles the GENERATOR; it never compiles the EMISSION. So the screen a mutation matrix relies on to distinguish a real kill from a compiler fake-RED does not see the artifact under test.

THE SOUND SCREEN, as ruled in round 1 and re-used in round 2:
  - Run the OUTER harness and read the CHILD log.
  - Assert `FAIL <childmod> [build failed]` is ABSENT.
  - Assert at least one `--- FAIL: Test...` NAMING a child test, with sibling child tests still `--- PASS`.
  - Assert `no tests to run` count is 0 (and remember `go test -run` is unanchored -- anchor `^TestX$/^sub$`).

WHY THE MATRICES BUILT ON THE BAD SCREEN SURVIVED ANYWAY, which is worth recording alongside it so nobody re-audits from scratch:
  1. SURVIVED rows are self-screening. The harness does require.NoError on the child `go test` exit status and then require.ElementsMatch(declaredTests(fixture), passed). A green package ENTAILS the child compiled and every declared test ran and passed, so a compiler kill cannot masquerade as SURVIVED.
  2. KILLED rows need the child-name tell, and it discriminates cleanly: a child compile break prints `[build failed]` with zero child names; a genuine kill prints `--- FAIL: <ChildTest>` with siblings still passing.

WHERE TO PUT IT: wherever the `go test -c` screen is currently prescribed. Whatever carrier states the rule must state this exception beside it, or the rule keeps being applied where it does not hold.
notes:

Taken because the bead had sat unclaimed since 2026-08-18 and I held the finding
first-party from gqlc-mlf4, whose description cites this bead as a screen not to
rediscover.

RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN TRANSCRIBED. The claim here is inherited from PR #990,
so I reproduced it in a detached worktree at 24c7b852 before writing it down.
One mutation at a time, restored between runs, honest green baseline before and
after. Captures: /tmp/ar-hreu-mut.txt (compile break), /tmp/ar-hreu-kill.txt
(semantic kill).

  none (baseline)                       go test -c rc=0 | run ok  | 0 build-failed | 21 --- PASS
  render_models.go emitted gate ->
    `if linusUndefinedSymbol != nil {`  go test -c rc=0 | run rc=1| 1 build-failed | 0 child names
  render_queries.go emitted pointer
    gate `!=` -> `==`                   go test -c rc=0 | run rc=1| 0 build-failed | 1 --- FAIL
                                                                    (TestAnythingColumnsCarryTheirNull)
                                                                    + 20 --- PASS

The screen reads rc=0 on all three, so it cannot separate a broken emission from
a correct one -- which is the whole job it is brought in to do.

I ADDED THE THIRD ROW, which the bead did not ask for, and it is the one that
earns the prescription. The bead's tell is "[build failed] absent, plus a named
child FAIL with siblings passing". Measuring only the compile break would have
left that tell resting on a single observation with nothing to discriminate it
FROM. The semantic kill is the contrast case: same blind screen, opposite child
log.

CARRIER CHOICE IS THE WEAK PART AND I FLAGGED IT TO THE REVIEWER RATHER THAN
HIDING IT. The bead says put this "wherever the screen is currently prescribed".
On master it is prescribed nowhere -- the only in-tree mention is a comment at

title: codegen/neo4j: the corpus does not pin the scalar/property/temporal GetRecordValue gate
description:
Residue of PR #990 (bd gqlc-1uic, GH #975), named by both review rounds and deliberately left open there.

PR #990 pinned the entity and list arms of the emitted GetRecordValue error gate. It did NOT pin the scalar/property/temporal arm (the matrix calls it G1), and G1 is the one row in that matrix that produces NO RED at all when mutated -- the gate can be deleted and the corpus stays green.

WHY IT WAS LEFT OPEN, and this is the part to verify before acting: read off the EMITTED child sources (not inferred from the .cypher), the only carrier instantiations the corpus produces are []any, dbtype.Node and dbtype.Relationship. So that arm emits no GetRecordValue call on this corpus at all -- there is nothing to pin. Round 1 verified this claim first-party against the emitted sources and upheld it.

WHAT CLOSING IT NEEDS: a new projection in the corpus that makes the emitter instantiate the scalar/property/temporal carrier, and then a message assertion in the same shape PR #990 used for the entity arm (assert what the refusal SAYS, plus one negative assertion on what it must not say -- the fixture's old err != nil assertion was vacuous because the zero carrier makes the decode helper refuse for a neighbouring reason).

CAUTION carried from #990: the screen for this work is NOT `go test -c`. See the sibling bead on that -- for a testdata/*.go.txt fixture compiled one module down, `go test -c` stays rc=0 while the child module runs zero tests. Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log: assert `[build failed]` absent and at least one `--- FAIL: Test...` naming a child test, with siblings still `--- PASS`.
notes: Landed on master as squash sha 004e4c2a (PR #1387). Verified present on origin/master: internal/codegen/emitscan/emitscan.go and internal/codegen/neo4j/capture_test.go both resolve under git cat-file, so this is a merged bead and not merely a closed one.
close_reason: PR #1387, merged. ScalarColumns in testdata/corpus_queries.cypher makes the emitter instantiate neo4j.GetRecordValue over int64, int32, bool, string and float64 carriers; before it, the corpus only ever produced []any, dbtype.Node and dbtype.Relationship, so writeSingleColumnDecodeIndent's fall-through emitted nothing any row read. Three mutations, verdicts declared first, all KILLED: blinding the err gate (caught by TestScalarColumnRefusalsCarryTheDriversError), blinding the non-nullable isNil gate and inverting the nullable arm's !isNil (both caught by TestScalarColumnsNarrowTheirCarriers). The first re-run against the corpus as it stood SURVIVED. The refusal row asserts the driver's own wording plus the negative on the string non-nullable, so it cannot pass on the null gate one line down; the stub returns a zero and an error for a mis-typed value AND for a missing key, so a dropped err gate yields no error at all and the caller silently gets a rank of zero, which is why the fact of an error is what the row pins. Not verified: nothing was witnessed against a real driver, docker info fails on this machine.

title: ciguard: the hook-suite discovery walk has six measured gaps in what it accepts and rejects
description:
Named as residues F1, F2, F3, F4, F6 and F7 by the PR #951 round-7 reviewer, each graded residue rather than blocker for that PR. They are one coherent defect class — the walk and name-rule that discover hook suites under .githooks/ — so they are filed together rather than as six stubs.

F1  THE SCAN CANNOT TELL A COMMAND FROM ITS ARGUMENT. A recipe line like `command -v just test` reads as a reference to the `test` recipe. The scan is textual, so an argument that happens to spell a recipe name counts as a call.

F2  `.githooks/.hooks.bats` IS ACCEPTED BY NOTHING. A dotfile suite in the very directory the walk owns falls outside every acceptance rule, so it could be added and silently never run.

F3  `hooks-spec.sh` IS ACCEPTED BY THE NAME RULE. The converse of F2 — the name rule is loose enough to admit a file that is not a suite. Note F2 and F3 are opposite failures of the same rule, which is the argument for fixing it rather than patching either end.

F4  HOOK SUITES OUTSIDE `.githooks/` ARE OUT OF THE WALK REACH. The walk is rooted at .githooks/, so a suite placed anywhere else is invisible to it regardless of naming.

F6  THE QUOTED-# TRUNCATION HAZARD IN THE STRIP. The comment strip treats a `#` inside quotes as the start of a comment and truncates there, so a recipe line carrying a quoted hash is read as shorter than it is.

F7  THE `cannot` ABOUT DIRECTORIES IS FALSIFIABLE BY A SYMLINK. os.ReadDir returns a DirEntry whose IsDir() is FALSE for a symlink to a directory, so a symlinked directory falls through to the name rule instead of being skipped as a directory. This one is a prose defect as well as a behavioural one: the comment states a `cannot` that a symlink falsifies. The same paragraph already discloses two adjacent holes, which is why the reviewer graded it residue — the carrier is honest about its limits, just not about this one.

ACCEPTANCE: each of the six gets a test row that reddens when the corresponding rule is reverted. F7 additionally needs its comment corrected — state the limit rather than asserting a cannot, per the standing convention against universals that the tree own artifacts falsify.

NOT THE SAME AS gqlc-sgot. That is a defect in master (a gate that greps raw justfile bytes and so accepts a commented-out dependency). The reviewer measured that they do not interact adversely: PR #951 TestTestHooksIsReachedByARecipeCIRuns is precisely what catches the comment-out spelling gqlc-sgot misses.
close_reason: Closed by PR #1334, squash-merged to master. All six gaps: uncommented split into justUncommented and shellUncommented, each checked against the language it models; justInvocations reads command position via liverecipes.JustRecipes; surveyHooks walks both suite directories, follows symlinks, refuses a leading-dot file the shell glob would skip, and states a reason per refusal; test-hooks refuses per directory. Mutation evidence in the PR body.

title: resolver: the cross-product sentinel differential is a manual procedure with no CI job
description:
Named by the PR #963 round-3 reviewer as residue R4, correctly not blocking that PR.

The resolver corpus sweep now records the refusal sentinel per cell (landed by PR #911, bead gqlc-yb0w). The stronger instrument built on top of it — the branch-vs-master cross-product differential that classifies every cell as same-verdict-same-sentinel / same-verdict-different-sentinel / different-verdict — is what actually caught the +2/-2 movement on #963 and proved the other 12518 cells did not move.

But it is run BY HAND. Nothing in CI runs it, so nothing stops a future resolver change from moving a sentinel inside a FAIL->FAIL cell with a green pipeline. That is precisely the defect class gqlc-yb0w was filed for; the sweep now RECORDS the sentinel, but only the manual differential COMPARES it across a change.

The #963 body states plainly that the procedure is manual, which is why the reviewer graded it sufficient for that PR and residue rather than blocker.

ACCEPTANCE: a CI job that fails when a cell changes sentinel without the manifest being updated in the same commit. Note the standing rule that a detector which exits 0 is not a gate — the acceptance is that it FAILS, demonstrated by deliberately changing one sentinel and watching CI go red, not merely that a job exists and prints.

Adjacent: gqlc-yb0w (closed, PR #911) landed the per-cell sentinel recording this would compare.
close_reason: ALREADY SATISFIED by PR #911 — closing with the mutation that proves the gate FAILS, not merely that it exists. The bead reads the sweep as recording the sentinel while only a manual branch-vs-master differential compares it. That has not been true since commit 1f53dd0f (PR #911, bead gqlc-yb0w), which added internal/resolver/sweep_test.go AND committed test/data/resolver/sweep.manifest.tsv in the same commit: TestCorpusSweepManifest resolves the whole query x schema cross product and diffs every cell against that committed baseline, sorting disagreements into five named categories of which one is 'same verdict, DIFFERENT SENTINEL' — the FAIL to FAIL quadrant the bead is about. The manifest is regenerated in the same commit as the resolver change via -update, which is exactly the acceptance clause. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs 'just test', which runs 'go test -shuffle=on ./...', which includes this package. Measured at master 412b9612 in worktree gqlc-resolver-sentinels. Baseline: 12880 cells, all identical, PASS. Then the case the bead's defect class is really about and the one no errors.Is assertion can see — a same-text sentinel WIDENING: wrap inferUnlabelled's terminal refusal in a type whose Error() delegates unchanged and whose Is() also admits ErrOutOfR0Scope. Screened with 'go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/resolver/' first, so this is not a kill by the compiler. Result: 0 DIFFERENT VERDICT, 0 DIFFERENT DETAIL, fourteen DIFFERENT SENTINEL, and the ONLY failing test in the entire repository under 'go test ./...' is TestCorpusSweepManifest — TestResolverSuite and TestSentinelReachability both stay green, so CI goes red on this and nothing else does. What is NOT verified: I did not push the mutation and watch a real GitHub run go red; the claim that CI is red rests on the local repo-wide run plus ci.yml calling 'just test'. Residue: the sweep compares a change against the COMMITTED baseline, not against origin/master's live behaviour, so a commit that regenerates the manifest absorbs its own movement — the report is printed on the -update run naming every moved cell, but reading it is a reviewer act, not a gate. Filing a bead for that would be filing for the escape hatch the acceptance clause asks for.

title: ciguard: TestTestHooksIsADependencyOfTest reads the justfile raw, so a commented-out dependency passes it
description:
Introduced by PR #901 (internal/tools/ciguard/testhooks_test.go), measured by the PR #951 round-6 author.

The test reads the justfile as raw bytes to assert that the `test` recipe depends on `test-hooks`. Because it never parses, `test: check-hooks # test-hooks` satisfies it — the dependency is commented out, the hook suites drop out of CI, and the package still reports ok. Measured, not reasoned.

This is the repository's "a comment can be a witness" class on a new surface: the gate greps raw source bytes and accepts commented-out evidence.

Fix: parse with `just --dump` (JSON) or `just --evaluate`, or at minimum strip `#` comments before the match. Note that `just --dump` prints `error:` on a parse failure, so a mutation of the justfile can fake a RED — screen for that when pinning the fix.
close_reason:

regex, so a commented-out dependency read as present. Both pins built on it were

title: .githooks: the commit-msg:15-17 line citation is gated by nothing and is cited from three places
description:
Measured by the PR #946 round-7 reviewer, who ran the falsifier the author had not: shifting the guard from line 15 to line 20 in .githooks/commit-msg leaves ALL THREE hook suites green. Nothing detects the rot.

The same range is cited from three sites — .githooks/commit-msg's own header, .githooks/claude-pre-bash, and .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh — so the author's keep rationale was that it rots only if all three rot together. The reviewer upheld the keep for PR #946 (the file is not in that diff, the construct is named alongside the range) but ruled the citation ungated.

Two ways out: retire the line numbers across all three sites in favour of the construct name, or add an assertion that the cited range still contains the construct. The first is cheaper and matches the repository's standing preference for citing a construct a reader can grep.
notes:
--- TRIAGE 2026-08-23: THE ROT THIS BEAD PREDICTED HAS NOW HAPPENED ---
Measured first-party against origin/master at commit e580fd70.

The construct this bead is about — the MERGE_HEAD early exit in .githooks/commit-msg
— is no longer at lines 15-17. PR #1314 (commit 4636f1b5, 'ci: refuse an implausible
commit author') rewrote that hook, moving the rules out into
.githooks/implausible-identity.sh, and the guard now sits at:

    $ git show origin/master:.githooks/commit-msg | grep -n MERGE_HEAD
    29:if git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then

Two carriers still cite the old range, both wrong today:

    origin/master:.githooks/claude-pre-bash:271
      '# does fire on a merge, but .githooks/commit-msg:15-17 exits 0 whenever'
    origin/master:.githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh:389
      '# MERGE_HEAD is set (.githooks/commit-msg:15-17), ahead of both the identity'

The suites were green through that merge, which is precisely the bead's claim: the
citation is gated by nothing. The author's keep rationale — that it rots only if all
three sites rot together — is now falsified by measurement rather than by argument:
the cited FILE moved and the citing SITES did not.

This strengthens the bead's own preferred remedy (retire the line numbers in favour
of the construct name, which a reader can grep) and makes it a live wrong citation
rather than a hypothetical one. Priority left at P2 by the triage lane; an agent who
thinks the now-false citation warrants P1 should say so rather than assume.
close_reason: PR #1326, merged as master 606deb04. The line citations are retired in favour of the construct, MERGE_HEAD, which a reader can grep, and a new row in commit-msg-test.sh scans the whole tracked tree and refuses any commit-msg colon digits citation. Two exclusions, both stated in the file: .beads jsonl, because the beads recording this defect quote the range verbatim and rewriting them would erase the record, and commit-msg-test.sh itself, because the pattern-liveness probe has to construct the shape. That probe is the gate's own falsifier, since a pattern matching nothing would report success over a tree full of citations. Both directions measured: the scan is green on the merged tree, and reinserting a citation line into .githooks/commit-msg turns it red. The bead says three sites; on the branch point there were two, .githooks/claude-pre-bash and its suite, the third having already gone. Both were outside my lane and both were already wrong, naming lines fifteen to seventeen for a guard that had moved to line twenty-nine. I edited both, comments only, and disclosed it in the PR body, because leaving them would have shipped a claim this branch falsifies.

title: codegen/neo4j: declaredTests parses the fixture AST, so a commented-out test is invisible to the completeness check
description:
internal/codegen/neo4j's corpus harness builds its 'declared' set by parsing testdata/corpus_test.go.txt's AST. Commenting out a whole test therefore removes it from BOTH the declared set and the passed set, so require.ElementsMatch stays green and the row silently leaves the suite.

The require.NotEmpty backstop only fires if EVERY test is commented out, so it does not bound partial silence.

This is the 'a comment can be a witness' class inverted: here a comment makes evidence DISAPPEAR from a gate rather than counting as evidence. Pre-existing, not introduced by PR #966; named as a follow-up by the round-3 reviewer.

A fix needs a declaration that does not come from the same artifact the harness parses — e.g. an explicit expected-name list, or a count derived from the fixture's raw bytes rather than its AST.
close_reason:
Merged as 07954baf (PR #1002, squash). GH #974 CLOSED/COMPLETED. Verified on origin/master: corpusTests and require.NotEmpty live in both internal/codegen/neo4j and internal/codegen/age.

WHAT LANDED. declaredTests parsed the fixture AST, so a commented-out test was
invisible to the completeness check. Replaced by an explicit corpusTests name
list in both packages, plus a require.NotEmpty guard so that emptying the
fixture and the literal together cannot produce two empty sets that silently
match. Scope was extended to age during round 1 and stayed ratified.

THREE ROUNDS, and the guard is load-bearing in both packages -- measured by an
independent reviewer, not argued: delete require.NotEmpty and the last-name edit
goes rc=0 GREEN; the one-of-many case is still not swallowed, it reds via
ElementsMatch with 20 sibling child --- PASS.

ROUND 3 CLOSED TWO PROSE BLOCKERS.
  B1: two md5 rows in the body were taken at earlier commits than the heading
      named. Fixed not by editing the two rows but by re-deriving EVERY hash in
      one scripted pass. The reviewer re-derived independently: 22 rows, 22
      MATCH, 0 stale. Round 2's heading-names-the-wrong-commit shape is gone.
  B2: 'Down to the last name ... nothing here prevents' was false about the one
      case those words exist to carve out. Rewritten to state the general case
      and name the exception, dropping 'nothing here prevents' entirely. The new
      block is byte-identical in both packages, 527 bytes.

ON MY OWN WITHHELD SUSPICION. I read 'What the edit costs the remover either way
is writing the removal down' as a possible pseudo-cleft exhaustive reading that
the preceding sentence falsifies, and deliberately kept it out of the reviewer's
brief so its finding would be independent. It found the same clause on its own
and classified it the same way: resolved by the preceding sentence in the same
paragraph. Two instruments, same finding, same classification -- residue, not a
blocker. That is the same-carrier scoping rule applied twice.

RESIDUE FILED: gqlc-vg66 (the two corpus comments are byte-identical by hand and
nothing enforces it -- the unguarded-twin shape, pre-existing); gqlc-gw20 (two
fixture tests are the sole user of an import, so their paired removal reds at
require.NoError with [build failed] rather than at the guard -- a fake-RED shape
any future mutation matrix over this corpus must screen for).
Previously filed and still open: gqlc-lwtp, gqlc-mlf4, gqlc-wuyu, gqlc-8bl0.

title: codegen/neo4j: the corpus does not pin the entity column's GetRecordValue error handling
description:
Dropping the GetRecordValue err gate in writeEntityColumnDecodeIndent SURVIVES the entire internal/codegen/neo4j package. Measured twice independently — by the PR #966 author and reproduced byte-for-byte by the round-3 reviewer: render_queries.go ae2b202a -> 4db81009, changed=YES, 'go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/neo4j' rc=0, package green.

It is killed only one level up, by TestSentinelTaxonomy + TestConformanceSuite, whose golden diff proves the edit was live ('_ = err' appears in the emission).

So the package that owns the emitter cannot tell whether the emitter checks that error. The conformance suite catches it, but only as a whole-golden diff, which names nothing about error handling. A corpus row that reads a wrong-typed column and expects the refusal would pin it locally.
close_reason:
Merged as PR #990 (squash ca7a379a), GH #975 auto-closed. Two rounds; round 2 returned PASS = merge authority. One file changed, tests only, +130 -- NO emitter changed (render_queries.go ends at its pristine md5 ae2b202a09ee86d1bd4b99e74d349ed1).

THE DIAGNOSIS, which was the whole value here. My impl brief's premise was FALSE and the author refuted it with measurement rather than following it. I said the neo4j driver stub needed to start returning errors. In fact testdata/driverstub_neo4j.go.txt copies GetRecordValue VERBATIM from the real driver and already refuses both a wrong dynamic type and an absent key, and the corpus ALREADY fed a relationship under a node column -- it just asserted err == nil. Dropping the gate hands the ZERO carrier to the entity decode helper, whose empty Props map refuses on the first property. So you get a non-nil error either way, FOR A NEIGHBOURING REASON, and the old assertion was vacuous. The gates were already correct; the corpus could not tell. The fix is asserting the MESSAGE, plus one negative assertion on what the message must not say.

Round 2 re-measured this: with the gate dropped, the swap case's failure text is 'decode column "s": decode Scalar.Active: could not find any property named active' where the wanted text is 'expected value to have type dbtype.Node but found type dbtype.Relationship'. A refusal for the neighbouring reason, caught only by the new message assertions.

ROUND 1 (REVISE, one blocker, comment-only) also settled a methodology question that outlives this bead: FAIL	. [setup failed] is UNSOUND as a mutation screen here, because it compiles the generator and not the emission -- an emission-level mutation leaves it at rc=0 while the nested module goes RED with zero child test names. Filed as gqlc-hreu. The reviewer ruled it does NOT invalidate the matrix, and the argument is the durable part: SURVIVED rows are self-screening (the harness requires the child go test to exit 0 AND requires the passed set to match declaredTests read from the fixture AST, so a compiler kill cannot masquerade as SURVIVED), while KILLED rows are discriminated by the child-name tell.

THE BLOCKER was the repo's most repeated mistake: the author corrected its own false claim about the 'e' case and LEFT THE TWIN -- an inherited PR #966 comment above the swap case claiming that case pins which carrier a column commits to. G8 falsified it: forcing the carrier gives 'cannot use rel1 (dbtype.Node) as dbtype.Relationship ... decodeEdgy' and ZERO child tests run, so no assertion refuses it. The file asserted both things at once.

ROUND 2 (PASS) measured first-party:
- The comment-only claim proved at AST LEVEL with the reviewer's own comparator (go/parser mode 0, position-free PUSH/POP stream): 5621 nodes and md5 2f623a9c identical across revisions. Both control directions run -- positive controls (swapping call operands; err == nil -> !=) move the md5 while leaving node count and stream size IDENTICAL, so the equality rides on the hash not on counts; negative controls (a trailing // and a /* */ span) leave the md5 fixed while source bytes move, which are exactly the two classes the author's grep -vE '^\s*//' cannot see. Declared-test set 21 both sides with MEMBERSHIP identical, stronger than the author's count.
- G8 and G3 reproduced with the reviewer's OWN edits, both byte-identical in md5 to round 1's independent run. G4 spot-checked -- a row NEITHER round had ever verified first-party -- and it matched the body's md5 and RED name exactly.
- Merged tree at master 49213009: go test ./... rc=0, zero ^FAIL.

I WAS WRONG ABOUT driverRefusal AND THE REVIEWER SHOWED IT. I briefed round 2 that the comment's 'the nil check is not defensive' looked FALSE, because deleting the check leaves the suite green. The reviewer ran the measurement neither I nor the author had: it pointed a driverRefusal[dbtype.Node] call at a key holding a dbtype.Node and THE GUARD FIRED, with its own message, RED naming the child test, 20 siblings passing. Deletion-survival and reachability are different measurements -- a correct corpus is precisely one where no row trips the guard. The author's grading of 'undecidable' was under-confident rather than wrong, and my framing did not survive contact.

THE AUTHOR CUT BACK ITS OWN DRAFT. Its first replacement comment (ea015e05) carried the full mechanism and was entirely true -- and was wrong for the file, because it put a second copy of the gate-versus-decode-helper explanation fifty lines from the one that owns it: the same geometry that produced the blocker. 9b5f6bf8 cuts it to a scope-limited statement plus one carrier clause.

RESIDUE: gqlc-8bl0 (G1's unpinned scalar/property/temporal gate -- needs a new projection, since that arm emits no GetRecordValue on this corpus at all), gqlc-hreu (write the go test -c exception down in-tree), gqlc-h803 (G4/G5 pinned only by wording the emitter itself chooses), gqlc-09q0 (two cosmetic prose nits; reviewer said explicitly not to spend a round on them).

REVIEWER'S DISCLOSED WEAK SPOTS: G1 and G5 have never been re-derived first-party by ANY reviewer across both rounds; it did not dump the emitted child sources; CI 7/7 inherited from me (I verified it: 7/7 terminal SUCCESS one row per context, Closes #975 x1, 0 body attribution, 0 path:NNN, and 0 AI trailers across all five commits checked BY HAND because core.hooksPath had drifted in that worktree so the commit-msg gate never ran). Its own honest catch: its first test-set extraction returned 0 rows on both sides and printed IDENTICAL -- a vacuous equality it caught only because it had asserted non-empty operands.

title: codegen: scalar_map is the only map-returning fixture and is enrolled in one target, so all three emitted-code gates skip it
description:
Found while reviewing PR #968 (merged as c4081ee4), by independent enumeration rather than by reading the author's work.

`scalar_map` is the ONLY corpus fixture whose emitted API returns a map column: `OneMap(ctx) (map[string]any, error)`, from `RETURN {a: 1} AS m`. A struct-field regexp over the corpus for `map[string]any` returns zero -- the map is a bare return type, not a field -- which is why an earlier search missed it.

It is enrolled in exactly ONE target, `neo4j-go-v5`. The consequence is that the repository's three gates over emitted code all miss it:

  1. Golden cross-backend comparison needs >= 2 targets. `internal/codegen/conformance_test.go:700-702` does `if len(targets) < 2 { continue }`, so a single-target fixture is skipped.
  2. The live battery (7 scenarios in 3 slices, no run-all path) does not include `scalar_map`, so nothing drives it against a real database.
  3. `TestBackendInvariantSurface` skips it too -- `:773-781` `d.Recv == nil -> continue`, and all emitted `agtype*` helpers are receiver-less.

So the one fixture that exercises map-column carriage -- the exact surface ADR 0025 is about -- is held to nothing by any of the three.

The question to answer is whether `scalar_map` should be enrolled in a second target (apache-age-pgx-v5 being the obvious candidate, since that is the backend ADR 0025 says diverges) so the golden comparison starts covering it. That may be cheap or may surface a real emission gap on the AGE side; find out before assuming.

Not a defect introduced by #968 -- pre-existing corpus enrolment -- and #968 correctly declined to widen scope to fix it.
close_reason: Merged as master b30d41e1 via PR #1356. scalar_map is now enrolled in neo4j-go-v6 as well as v5, so TestBackendInvariantSurface no longer skips the only map-returning fixture at its fewer-than-two-targets guard. Not AGE: measured, and the AGE backend refuses map columns by design, pinned at four sites in age_test.go, so that attempt was reverted rather than worked around. Proved the newly-covered gate goes red by mutating the v6 querier map return type.

title: codegen: ADR 0025's map-member runtime types are unmeasured for temporal, spatial, byte-array and v6-only kinds
description:
ADR 0025 (merged in PR #968, master c4081ee4) records measured marker->Go-type mappings for map[string]any members across apache-age-pgx-v5, neo4j-go-v5 and neo4j-go-v6. The measurement covered integer, float, string, nil, bool, array and nested-map members, executed against real packstream hydrators in both driver majors plus the emitted AGE agtypeMap.

Not measured, and therefore not claimed by the ADR: temporal kinds (Date, LocalTime, LocalDateTime, Time, Duration, DateTime), spatial kinds (Point2D, Point3D), byte arrays, and v6-only kinds (the Vector[...] family and PackedUUID).

The ADR is honest about this -- it quantifies only over what was run -- so this is a coverage gap, not a false claim. Closing it means extending the same probe shape to those kinds and recording whether the three backends still agree.

Prior art to reuse rather than rebuild: PR #968's probe built copied driver modules under /tmp and packed a stream the way the server would (neo4j/internal/db hydrator_test.go's `build func()` pattern), then read members back through neo4j.Record (which is a true type alias for db.Record in both majors, so a caller reads the same bytes). The AGE half compiled schema_any_property's emitted models.go into a throwaway module and called agtypeMap directly. Both halves carried positive controls -- pack an int as float, and rename a key -- so a no-op cannot read as PASS.

Note the structural bound already established for integers: packstream has no integer marker wider than 8 bytes (packstream/unpacker.go:202,226-229,248; Int() errors 'Illegal int length' otherwise), so a neo4j map member structurally cannot carry a value outside int64 range. Ask whether an equivalent structural bound exists for each new kind before asserting agreement from a sample.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
PR #2172 opened 2026-09-01 (branch chore/gqlc-c4mb-adr0025-map-member-kinds). Docs-only: extends ADR 0025's map-member measurement.

ANSWER TO THE BEAD'S STRUCTURAL QUESTION. There is no per-kind bound to look for on neo4j, because a stronger one covers all kinds at once: record fills rec.Values[i] = h.value() and amap fills m[key] = h.value() — the same method, entered with the same unp.Curr, in v5.28.4 and v6.2.0 alike. So member carriage equals top-level carriage for every kind value() can return, including kinds nobody packed. The rows check that reading; they do not enumerate a set.

MEASURED (both majors, all agree bare-vs-member): 'D'->dbtype.Date, 't'->dbtype.LocalTime, 'T'->dbtype.Time, 'd'->dbtype.LocalDateTime, 'I'/'i'->time.Time, 'E'->dbtype.Duration, 'X'->dbtype.Point2D, 'Y'->dbtype.Point3D, byte array->[]uint8. v6 only: 'V'->dbtype.Vector[float64], 0xE0 UUID->dbtype.UUID. Both controls fired (int-bare vs float-nested = unequal; renamed key = member absent).

TWO FINDINGS THE TABLE WOULD NOT HAVE SURFACED. (1) A zoned datetime is the only kind here whose carrier is not a driver alias — bare time.Time, indistinguishable from any other time.Time a member holds. (2) The named-zone tag 'i' is the only kind whose carrier is not decided by the wire bytes: it carries a zone NAME, and utcDateTimeNamedZone answers an unresolvable one with *dbtype.InvalidValue. Measured by accident — the probe read *dbtype.InvalidValue on both majors while it had Asia/Yerevan misspelt Europe/Yerevan.

RECORDED AS NOT MEASURED. Whether a correctly spelt zone can miss on a host with no zone database: ZONEINFO pointed at an empty dir does NOT falsify it, because resolution fell through to the system database and answered time.Time anyway. 'F'/'f' were not packed (probe ran useUtc:true, where value() refuses them). And no probe here witnesses that a server ever PLACES these kinds in a map.

AGE HALF. Structural too, and negative: agtypeValue's switch can return exactly string, []any, map[string]any, nil, bool, int64, float64. So each of these kinds is a value the AGE path does not carry — same shape as the out-of-range integer the ADR already records — not one the two backends decode differently. Confirmed against the shipped schema_any_property helper.

NO FOLLOW-UP BEAD FILED. The ::numeric annotation handling looked like a silent-precision-loss defect until measured: both agtypeInt64 and agtypeFloat64 strip the suffix deliberately, TestAgtypeValue already pins 3::numeric->int64 and 1.5::numeric->1.5 and the unannotated overflow, and the behaviour is exactly the int64-range bound the ADR already records. Nothing new to file.
close_reason:
PR #2172 merged 2026-09-02T14:41:28Z (squash), GH #972 closed with it. Docs-only ADR 0025 amendment; 12/12 gates green.

MERGED WITHOUT A REVIEWER, and the reason: gqlc-c4mb has no design blocker (dep tree empty), is labelled class:author, does not amend the protocol, and no agent asked. protocol merges that on green gates. The one hesitation worth recording is that it edits an ADR, which is a designer's artefact — but it changes no decision, it fills a measurement gap the ADR itself flagged as open, and the bead's own text scoped the work as 'extending the same probe shape to those kinds and recording whether the three backends still agree'. agent-l is the only awake reviewer and is already carrying three of my review beads; adding a fourth for a docs PR that V.2 merges on green would have spent her time badly.

WHAT LANDED. The bead's structural question is answered stronger than per-kind: record fills rec.Values[i] = h.value() and amap fills m[key] = h.value() — one method, one entry condition, both driver majors — so member carriage equals top-level carriage for every kind value() can return, sampled or not. Rows check that reading rather than enumerate a set. Measured, all agreeing bare-vs-member on v5.28.4 and v6.2.0: 'D'->dbtype.Date, 't'->dbtype.LocalTime, 'T'->dbtype.Time, 'd'->dbtype.LocalDateTime, 'I'/'i'->time.Time, 'E'->dbtype.Duration, 'X'->dbtype.Point2D, 'Y'->dbtype.Point3D, byte array->[]uint8; v6 also 'V'->dbtype.Vector[float64] and the 0xE0 UUID->dbtype.UUID. Both prior-art controls fired.

TWO FINDINGS A TABLE ALONE WOULD HAVE MISSED. A zoned datetime is the only kind here whose carrier is not a driver alias (bare time.Time). And named-zone 'i' is the only kind whose carrier is not decided by the wire bytes — it carries a zone NAME and an unresolvable one yields *dbtype.InvalidValue. I found that by misspelling Asia/Yerevan as Europe/Yerevan, which is the only reason it is in the record.

RECORDED AS NOT MEASURED, deliberately: whether a correctly spelt zone can miss on a host with no zone database (ZONEINFO at an empty dir does NOT falsify it — resolution fell through to the system database), 'F'/'f' (probe ran useUtc:true, where value() refuses them), and that any server ever PLACES these kinds in a map.

AGE: structurally negative. agtypeValue's switch returns exactly string, []any, map[string]any, nil, bool, int64, float64. Each new kind is a value the AGE path does not carry — same shape as the out-of-range integer already in the ADR — not one the backends decode differently.

NO FOLLOW-UP BEAD. The ::numeric handling looked like silent precision loss until measured: both helpers strip the suffix deliberately and TestAgtypeValue already pins the rows. Nothing new to file.

title: hooks: commit-msg exits 0 on any merge commit, so merge commits are screened for neither AI-attribution trailers nor bogus identity
description:
Found by the Linus review of PR #946 round 3 (head bb473d36), reported as out-of-scope residue rather than a blocker. PRE-EXISTING on master; not introduced by #946.

.githooks/commit-msg:15-17 does

  if git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD ...; then exit 0; fi

BEFORE the identity checks and the Co-Authored-By scan. So the whole
AI-attribution gate is skipped for any commit created while MERGE_HEAD is set.

Measured with hooks HEALTHY (probe /tmp/l946probe/gate.sh):

  plain commit with 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus <noreply@anthropic.com>'
    -> rc=1, REJECTED
  the SAME trailer on a merge commit
    -> rc=0, COMMITTED, trailer present in the object

A wrapper proved the hook really ran and then exited 0 (MERGE_HEAD=c5d48a12),
so this is the early-exit, not a missing hook.

Why it matters: CLAUDE.md states the no-AI-attribution rule is enforced at
commit time by .githooks/commit-msg. That is true for ordinary commits and
false for merge commits. The repo's own docs therefore carry a completeness
claim its artifacts falsify - the house signature defect, in the hook that
polices attribution.

Scope if anyone takes it: the MERGE_HEAD skip presumably exists so that
auto-generated merge messages are not held to the subject-line/format rules.
Those are the checks that need skipping - not the Co-Authored-By scan, which
should run on every commit regardless of MERGE_HEAD. Split the early exit:
skip the format/identity checks, keep the attribution scan. Needs rows for
both a merge commit WITH the trailer (must deny) and a clean merge commit
(must allow), plus a check that an ordinary commit is unaffected.

Do not start until PR #946 merges - it is mid-round on .githooks/ and would
conflict.

isolated fixture (mktemp repo, HOME redirected to an empty .gitconfig,
GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1), with positive controls in both directions.

The description already notes the early exit sits before both. This is the

title: ADR 0025 / age types.go: the map-column runtime-type divergence is recorded against a helper that decodes integers as int64
description:
ADR 0025's bullet 'The declared Go surface is backend-invariant and the runtime types behind it are not' records that a map[string]any column decodes an integer member as float64 on apache-age-pgx-v5 and int64 on neo4j, and that this is 'Reachable only once an agtypeMap helper exists'. The sibling copy is the 'Sharp edge for a map column' paragraph in internal/codegen/age/types.go's Scalar doc.

Both premises fail against the tree at 2df500a6.

agtypeMap is emitted today (render_models.go, under helpers.value) and three goldens carry it: test/data/codegen/valid/{schema_any_property,schema_any_property_alone,schema_list_any_property}/golden/apache-age-pgx-v5/models.go.

It does not unmarshal the object as JSON: agtypeObject splits it by byte scanning and each member is read by agtypeValue, which tries agtypeInt64 before agtypeFloat64. Executed against the schema_any_property golden:

    agtypeMap({"n": 3, "f": 1.5, "s": "x", "b": true, "z": null})
    n -> int64 3 ; f -> float64 1.5 ; s -> string x ; b -> bool true ; z -> <nil>

So the AGE half of the recorded divergence does not hold: an integer member lands as int64.

gqlc-0otp corrected both sites to say only what was measured and left this open: whether ANY runtime-type divergence between apache-age-pgx-v5 and the neo4j targets survives for a map value. Measuring the neo4j half needs the driver (a live target), not a source read, which is why it was not answered there.

## Fix

Measure what neo4j-go-v5/v6 hand back for a Cypher map value member by member against what the emitted agtypeMap returns for the same value, and either name a real divergence in ADR 0025 (with the measurement) or record that none was found. TestBackendInvariantSurface compares declarations and would not see one either way.

Delivered by PR #968, squash-merged to master as c4081ee4. One file: docs/adr/0025-type-map-answers-carriage-per-kind.md (+46/-6). GH #955 closed by the merge.

They agree: an integer member hydrates as int64 on neo4j-go-v5 and neo4j-go-v6, and the emitted AGE agtypeMap decodes integer members as int64 too. The old text recorded a divergence against a helper that does not behave the way the record claimed.

WHY IT IS BELIEVABLE. The reviewer did not accept the author's probe -- it built its own in copied driver modules under /tmp and re-derived every mapping from driver source, then executed BOTH driver majors rather than measuring one and inferring the other. Two positive controls reproduced independently (packing an int as float, and renaming a key), each screened as compiling first, and the probe carried len(buf)==0 / len(m)==0 guards so a no-op could not read as PASS. The AGE half was re-derived by execution -- the reviewer compiled schema_any_property's emitted models.go into a throwaway module and called agtypeMap -- so the two halves are not circular. Two mutations on the emitted code (float-before-int in agtypeValue; coercing an int64 member to float64 in agtypeMap) were each KILLED by two named tests, both screened COMPILES with non-blank test names, so neither is a compiler kill.

The int64-range bound is scoped honestly rather than talked away: packstream has no integer marker wider than 8 bytes (unpacker.go:202,226-229,248), so a neo4j map member structurally cannot carry a value outside int64 range. That is a structural argument, not a sample.

A JUDGEMENT CALL THAT WAS UPHELD. The author declined to restate the runtime measurement in the sibling carrier at internal/codegen/age/types.go:198-207, against this repository's standing twin-carrier rule. The reviewer sustained the decline and gave a stronger reason than the author did: types.go says AGE emits no ScalarMap column at all, so re-stating a map-member runtime measurement there would document the runtime of a column that backend never emits -- inert, and a fresh drift candidate.
