title: ci: actions/setup-go 429s in "Set up job", killing required contexts before any repo step runs
description:
Split out of #933, which has been narrowed to the golangci-lint half that PR
#951 fixes. This is the other half, still open, and it is the live one.

## Witness

WITNESS 1 in #933 (PR #932, round 1): the `test` context died in "Set up job"
downloading `actions/setup-go`, after the runner's own 3 attempts, on HTTP 429
Too Many Requests. `gh run rerun --failed` cleared it.

Reported by the merge orchestrator on 2026-08-17 and not independently
re-verified here: five further CI runs across #911 / #937 / #940 died
downloading `actions/setup-go` with 429, then 502/503, before any repo code
ran. Re-running fixed all five.

## Why it is not covered by #951

#951 fixes the *tool* downloads: `ensure-golangci` now retries, and
`.github/actions/setup-golangci` restores the pinned binary from the runner
cache. Both are repo-controlled steps that run after checkout.

`actions/setup-go@v5` is fetched by the runner from GitHub *before* any
repo-controlled step runs, so no retry or cache written in this tree is
reached in time.

## Levers that do exist

The claim originally made in #951's body — "nothing in this tree can retry or
cache it; the only repo-side lever is using fewer actions" — is wrong, and
#951's own diff is the counterexample.

1. **Vendor the step.** A `uses: ./.github/actions/<name>` reference is read
   out of the checkout, not downloaded. #951 does exactly this for `just` and
   for `golangci-lint`. Replacing `uses: actions/setup-go@v5` with a local
   composite is therefore possible; the cost is reimplementing what setup-go
   does — resolving `go-version-file: go.mod` to a toolchain, and the module
   and build caching that rides with it. Whether the runner image's Go already
   satisfies `go.mod`, and whether `GOTOOLCHAIN` fetching from the module
   proxy is an acceptable substitute for the setup-go download, are the two
   things to measure first.
2. **Fewer actions per job**, which is what #951's body named.

Neither closes the window. `actions/checkout` is itself a downloaded action
and has to run before any local action can be read, so vendoring `setup-go`
narrows the exposure rather than removing it. Say which of those is being
claimed when this is fixed.

## Acceptance

A CI run under this repo's own concurrency where the Go toolchain setup does
not depend on a GitHub-hosted action download — or a measurement showing the
runner image already satisfies `go.mod` and the `setup-go` step can be dropped
outright.

Bonus, carried over from #933 and still unaddressed by #951: something in the
rollup that distinguishes "died in setup" from "the change is red", so a
reader is not trained to re-run red contexts.
notes:
2026-08-23, .github/workflows lane. NOT FIXED. The two things the Acceptance section said to measure first are now measured, first-party, so whoever takes this starts from data rather than from the question.

MEASURED in throwaway PR #1323 / ci run 32622299816, job coe-probe, which deliberately carried NO actions/setup-go step at all (only actions/checkout, then a shell step):

    go: downloading go1.26.6 (linux/amd64)      06:09:57.6
    runner go: go version go1.26.6 linux/amd64  06:10:01.6
    which go: /usr/bin/go
    GOTOOLCHAIN=unset
    go.mod says: go 1.26.6

READ IT PRECISELY. The ubuntu-latest image ships a Go that does NOT satisfy go.mod on its own -- the download line is the tell. What happens instead is that /usr/bin/go, with GOTOOLCHAIN at its default, bootstraps the exact pinned toolchain from the module proxy, and the whole thing costs about 4 seconds. So:

  - "the runner image already satisfies go.mod" -- NO, not directly.
  - "is GOTOOLCHAIN fetching from the module proxy an acceptable substitute for the setup-go download" -- YES on function and on time, and materially: proxy.golang.org is a DIFFERENT provider from the GitHub action download path that has been answering 429, so it does not share the failure this bead is about.

WHAT STOPS IT BEING DONE TONIGHT, recorded so it is a decision and not an omission. Dropping actions/setup-go also drops its module and build caching, which it does by default keyed on go.sum. Replacing that by hand means an actions/cache step over GOMODCACHE and GOCACHE -- and actions/cache and actions/checkout are themselves downloaded actions, so per this bead own analysis the exposure narrows and does not close. It also touches five jobs at once, and this repo has already been bitten by the "first run after changing an actions/cache path runs cold, because prefix keys match but the payload does not" trap, so steady state is only readable on the SECOND run. Landing that unreviewed, overnight, on the workflow file that is now the fleet only merge gate, was judged the wrong trade against an intermittent flake that a rerun clears.

WHOEVER TAKES IT: say which claim you are making -- narrowed or closed -- as the bead already demands. And the bonus item (distinguishing "died in setup" from "the change is red" in the rollup) is still unaddressed.
2026-08-23, factory cleanup wave 3, CI lane. NOT taken; judged not landable unreviewed. Recording the measurement so the next taker does not repeat it.

MEASURED by an earlier agent this same night and relied on here: with NO actions/setup-go step at all, the ubuntu-latest runner's own /usr/bin/go bootstraps the toolchain go.mod asks for (go1.26.6) from the MODULE PROXY in about four seconds — a different provider from the one returning 429. So lever 1 in this bead's body is cheaper than it looked: the answer to 'whether the runner image's Go already satisfies go.mod' is that it does not, but GOTOOLCHAIN fetching does, fast, and off the failing path.

WHAT IS LOST is caching: setup-go writes the module and build caches. Replacing it means either accepting cold builds on every job or adding actions/cache steps by hand — and a path change to an actions/cache is cold on its FIRST run because prefix keys match while the payload does not, so the steady state can only be judged from the second run.

WHY NOT TONIGHT: the change touches five jobs in ci.yml, four of which are required contexts, with no reviewer awake and a merge policy of green-CI-only. A wrong move there does not fail loudly, it changes what the gate costs and what it caches. Wants one PR with a before/after wall-clock comparison over two consecutive runs.

The bonus ask in this bead — something distinguishing 'died in setup' from 'the change is red' — is still unaddressed and is separable from the main fix.

This NARROWS the window, it does not close it, and the composite header says so: actions/checkout is itself a downloaded action and must run before any local action can be read. What is claimed is the download count, not the removal of the exposure.

title: hooks: pre-commit has no `set -euo pipefail`, so the master-branch guard passes on an empty BRANCH
notes:
Found while working gqlc-l45j (PR #951); named in that PR body as out of
scope and deliberately left rather than folded in silently.

.githooks/pre-commit does not start with `set -euo pipefail`. It then does:

    BRANCH="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"

and compares BRANCH against master/main to refuse a direct commit. Without
`-e`/`-o pipefail`, a failing `git rev-parse` does not abort the hook: it
leaves BRANCH empty, and the empty string is neither "master" nor "main", so
the guard falls through and the commit proceeds.

This is the same shape as the bug gqlc-l45j fixed one arm of: a check whose
failure mode is to pass. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` fails on an
unborn HEAD (fresh repo, pre-first-commit) and during some rebase/detached
states, which is exactly when someone is most likely to be committing
somewhere they did not mean to.

.githooks/pre-push DOES set `set -euo pipefail`, so the two hooks disagree
about this — worth checking every hook in .githooks/ for the same gap rather
than fixing only pre-commit.

There is now a suite to hang the regression row on:
.githooks/tests/tool-gate-test.sh (added by gqlc-l45j), wired into the
`test-hooks` recipe, and internal/tools/ciguard/hooktests_test.go asserts
every suite in .githooks/tests/ is named by that recipe.

Fix: add `set -euo pipefail` and re-verify each existing arm still behaves
(an arm that relied on a non-zero command continuing will now abort).

--- agent-c, 2026-08-22, implemented on fix/hooks-fail-open-euo ---

THE BEAD'S STATED MECHANISM IS FALSIFIED IN PART, and the correction changed
the fix. It says a failing rev-parse "leaves BRANCH empty". Measured directly,
git 2.55.0, in a throwaway repo with GIT_* scrubbed:

  not a git repository    rev-parse rc=128 stdout ""       symbolic-ref rc=128
  unborn HEAD on master   rev-parse rc=128 stdout "HEAD"   symbolic-ref rc=0 "master"
  detached HEAD           rev-parse rc=0   stdout "HEAD"   symbolic-ref rc=128

So there are THREE shapes, not one. Empty BRANCH is only the first. In the
unborn case rev-parse exits 128 while still printing "HEAD", so BRANCH is
"HEAD" — non-empty, still neither "master" nor "main", still a fall-through.
Anyone writing the regression row from the bead's wording alone would have
asserted on an empty string and pinned a case that is not the interesting one.

The third shape is not a defect: a detached HEAD genuinely is not master, and
committing there must stay allowed. It is pinned as an ACCEPT, and it is what
stops the fix being "block whenever BRANCH is HEAD", which would refuse every
commit made during a rebase.

THE BEAD'S PROPOSED FIX IS INSUFFICIENT, measured rather than argued. I built
it as a mutant — original arms, plus `set -euo pipefail`, nothing else — and
ran the suite: 48 passed, 2 failed. It does convert fail-open to fail-closed,
so both rc-nonzero assertions pass. The two that stay red are the MESSAGE
assertions, and the reason is visible from the user's side: on a fresh repo on
master the commit is refused with

    fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the
    working tree.

rc=128, and not one word about a branch guard. Refusing for the right reason
while stating the wrong one. That is why the implementation adds an explicit
refusal arm and a symbolic-ref arm rather than only the shell options.

MUTATION, all against .githooks/tests/tool-gate-test.sh (baseline 50/0):

  M1  delete `set -euo pipefail`                50 passed, 0 failed  SURVIVED
  M2  swap the two detection arms               50 passed, 0 failed  SURVIVED
  M3  drop the symbolic-ref arm                 49 passed, 1 failed  KILLED
  M4  drop the rev-parse arm                    48 passed, 2 failed  KILLED
  M5  restore the fail-open shape               45 passed, 5 failed  KILLED
  M6  the bead's literal fix (see above)        48 passed, 2 failed  KILLED

I am declaring the two SURVIVORS rather than leaving them to be found.

  M2 survives because the order genuinely does not matter — either command's
  failure falls through to the other. My first draft of the comment said
  symbolic-ref is asked first BECAUSE it answers on an unborn HEAD, which reads
  as though the order were load-bearing. M2 falsified that sentence and the
  comment now says the order is not load-bearing and that both arms are needed.
  The mutant found a false claim in prose, not in code.

  M1 survives because once the arms handle failure explicitly, `set -e` has
  nothing left to catch: every git call is in an `if` condition, where -e is
  suspended anyway. It is kept for consistency with commit-msg, pre-push,
  guard-push-destination and install-hooks-drift-tripwire, which all carry it —
  but it is NOT what closes this hole, and the bead's title implies it is. If a
  reviewer wants the unwitnessed option out, say so; I would rather keep it and
  have it named as unwitnessed than have it read as load-bearing.

The RED was proven before the fix: the five new rows failed 45/5 against the
unmodified hook, and the two ACCEPT pins (detached HEAD, ordinary feature
branch) were green before AND after, which is what makes them anti-overfit
pins rather than decoration.

SWEEP OF THE OTHER HOOKS, which this bead also asked for. Four lack the full
options; three of those omissions are deliberate and I left them, with reasons
recorded on the bead I filed for the fourth: gqlc-650j (.githooks/bd-gh-sync,
1067 lines, zero shell options, and it is the ledger writer post-merge invokes

No open PR touches either of my two files (checked all open PRs by file list).

EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS RE-MEASURED ON THE NEW BASE. The suite grew 50 -> 82
rows under me, so none of yesterday's counts transferred.

  baseline, fix in place                        82 passed,  0 failed

RED, proven again rather than inherited — master's pre-commit restored under

and the 5 are exactly the predicted rows (3 no-repo, 2 unborn-master). The 6
ACCEPT rows (detached HEAD, ordinary master, ordinary feature branch) were
green before AND after, which is what makes them anti-overfit pins.

MUTATION, per-mutant expected verdict declared BEFORE each run, and each edit
confirmed live in the tree before the verdict was read:

  M1  delete `set -euo pipefail`       82/0  SURVIVED  (predicted survive)

  M5  restore the fail-open shape      77/5  KILLED    (= the RED run)

M3 and M4 each died by the exact rows named in advance, so neither is passing

M1's survival is a claim about THIS hook body, and I read the whole file to

I have written that into the hook as a comment above the line, because the

title: bdguard: showAtRef classifies an unresolvable base SHA as 'path absent', passing vacuously
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17 while closing PR #939 review round 1 (bd gqlc-npyp).

internal/tools/bdguard/main.go showAtRef() matches two `git show` stderr strings and maps them to errPathAbsentAtRef (base treated as nil -> every id looks new -> bdguard passes):

    "does not exist in"
    "exists on disk, but not in"

The comment above that match asserted an unknown ref emits "fatal: invalid object name" and is therefore bubbled up loud rather than silently classified as absent. That is true only for a NON-SHA ref name. Measured in a --depth=1 clone (/tmp/sc939/shallow):

    git show nosuchbranch:f.txt
      -> fatal: invalid object name 'nosuchbranch'.        [bubbled up: correct]
    git show deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef:f.txt
      -> fatal: path 'f.txt' exists on disk, but not in 'deadbeef...'   [MATCHED -> absent]
    git show deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef:nope.txt
      -> fatal: path 'nope.txt' does not exist in 'deadbeef...'         [MATCHED -> absent]

A 40-hex sha git cannot resolve parses as an object name, so git falls through to the path-resolution message, which is exactly what showAtRef reads as 'absent at ref'.

WHY IT MATTERS: .github/workflows/ci.yml:109 invokes `just bd-export-monotonic "$BASE_SHA"` -- the ref IS a hex sha. If the preceding `git fetch --depth=1 origin "$BASE_SHA"` (ci.yml:108) ever failed to place that object, bdguard would compare against a nil base and pass, which is the silently-passing gate this tool exists to prevent. Today the `run: |` block runs under bash -e so a failed fetch aborts the step first; the fail-open is guarded by that ordering alone, not by showAtRef.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) probe `git cat-file -e <ref>^{commit}` before showAtRef and fail loud when the ref does not resolve; (b) tighten the match to require the ref token to resolve. PR #939 corrected the comment only -- the behaviour is untouched and unpinned by any test (showAtRef is at 0.0% coverage, bd gqlc-drvx).

Linus PASS round 3 after independent re-derivation of every table cell in the reviewer's own fixture, 4 mutations (M1/M2 KILLED reproducing author rows M08/M05), and deliberate reproduction of the d41d8cd9 empty-md5 fake pass. CI 7/7 terminal SUCCESS. Closes GH #922 (now CLOSED).

title: core.hooksPath drift: the writer is the Claude Code agent-worktree creation (identified)
description:
**The writer IS identified: it is the Claude Code agent-worktree creation.** This
opening line replaces an earlier one that said the writer was "still unidentified
after a second search" — that sentence was written at the second-search round and
was never retracted after the identification landed in this issue's comments, so
readers met a superseded account first and the correction last. It cost at least
two agents real time (see the 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-24 notes).

## The mechanism, as measured 2026-09-02

A Claude Code agent spawned with worktree isolation creates a **linked** worktree
at `.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>` inside the main repo. Linked worktrees share
one `.git/config`, and `core.hooksPath` is common config — so the value written
there is the value every worktree reads. The written value is byte-identical to
every historical sighting:

    /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/hooks

which is `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks`, i.e. git's default hooks
directory. That directory ships only `*.sample` files, which git ignores, so
while the value stands every local hook in every worktree is dead.

**It is transient.** Three controlled runs against a 0.2s poller:

| run | spawns | write | restore | window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | one | 15:54:21.344 | 15:54:34.257 | 12.91s |
| 2 | one | 15:57:23.238 | 15:57:37.213 | 13.98s |
| 3 | two, overlapping | 15:58:40.950 | 15:59:34.500 | 53.55s |

The restore is tied to worktree **setup** completing, not to teardown: in run 2
it landed 32 seconds before the agent finished. The window is not a fixed cost —
two overlapping spawns gave roughly 4x a single one, and the fleet has 17 agents
that spawn agents.

Origin reads `file:...`, so this is a real write to the shared file and not the
`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` environment shape investigated in #o13d.

## What this supersedes

- "The writer is still unidentified" — superseded; see above.
- "New hypothesis: an agent-authored shell snippet" — **superseded.** The writer
  is the harness, not any file in the tree and not an agent's ad-hoc command.
  That is why four rounds of grepping the tree, ~250MB of transcripts, and the
  global and system config all came up empty: the writer runs outside the tree.
- "It does not restore" / "just init loses to the next spawn" (2026-08-22) —
  **falsified 2026-09-02**, 3 runs of 3. A spawn that completes puts the value
  back.
- "The repo spends a large fraction of wall-clock time unhooked" — not from this
  mechanism as it behaves today. The cost of a completed spawn is one bounded
  window.

## What remains true, and why this is still open

During the window **every** tree is unhooked at once. Census 2026-09-02: the
deploy root plus 17 agents, all still linked worktrees of one common dir, none yet
converted to clones. All 18 are armed with the drift tripwire, which is
fail-closed — a commit or push attempted inside the window is refused, loudly,
rather than landing ungated.

Not measured, and therefore not claimed: that a session **killed** inside the
window leaves the drift permanent. That is the obvious reading of the four
historical permanent occurrences now that the restore is known to exist, but no
kill was arranged. Tracked separately.

## Search log (history, not current state)

Kept because it is the evidence for why grepping could never have found this, and
for nothing else:

- `grep -rn "core.hooksPath"` over the whole tree: the only write is the
  justfile's `just init`, which writes the relative `.githooks`.
- `grep -rn 'exec.Command("git"' --include='*.go'`: one hit, and it is a read.
- `os.Chdir` / `t.Chdir`: zero hits.
- `git config --global` and `--system`: no `core.hooksPath`, no
  `init.templateDir`.
- ~250MB of Claude Code transcripts: every write found is the literal
  `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, i.e. a repair.

The writer is the **Claude Code agent-worktree creation**, not any file in the
tree and not an agent's ad-hoc command. That is why four rounds of grepping the
repo, the transcripts and the global/system config all came up empty: the
writer is the HARNESS, and it runs outside the tree.

## The measurement

Caught in the act with a 29-MILLISECOND window, which is the instrumentation
this bead asked for (the 'suggested next step' was an mtime+value snapshot):

  .claude/worktrees/agent-a75e2fa500d96d8ab   created  10:37:15.460416713
  .git/config                                 written  10:37:15.489417227
                                              delta    +29.000514 ms

The agent id a75e2fa500d96d8ab is the reviewer session spawned for PR #946.
Immediately after, 'git config core.hooksPath' read
'/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/hooks' and .git/hooks held only
*.sample files, i.e. every local hook dead repo-wide. Repaired with
'git config core.hooksPath .githooks'; drifted config saved at
/tmp/factory/gitconfig-drifted-*.bak.

## Why it produces exactly the observed value

The harness places agent worktrees at .claude/worktrees/agent-<id>, INSIDE the
main repo. Those are linked worktrees, so they share the main .git/config —
core.hooksPath is common config, not per-worktree state. And from such a
worktree:

  git -C .claude/worktrees/agent-a75e2fa500d96d8ab rev-parse --git-common-dir
    -> /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git
  "$(... --git-common-dir)/hooks"
    -> /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/hooks

which is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the drifted value recorded in gqlc-5z8 (2026-07-02),
gqlc-5fm (2026-07-26), gqlc-hd68 (2026-08-17 04:41) and this occurrence. This
bead's own untested hypothesis — '$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks
reproduces it exactly' — was right about the EXPRESSION and wrong only about
the actor. The plausible intent is neutralising hooks for a sandboxed agent
worktree; the defect is that the setting is shared, so it kills hooks in the
main checkout and in every other worktree at once.

## Consequences for this factory

This fires on EVERY agent spawn. With 10-12 agents in flight and constant
respawning, the repo spends a large fraction of wall-clock time unhooked, which
is why the drift keeps recurring and why each repair looks unexplained. While
unhooked, .githooks/commit-msg (the AI-attribution gate, per CLAUDE.md) and
.githooks/pre-push ('just lint-new') do not run for ANY session.

## Audit of the unhooked window: CLEAN

Last 60 commits on origin/master: 0 hits for a Co-Authored-By naming
claude/anthropic, 0 for an '@anthropic.com' address, 0 for a 'Generated with
Claude' footer. Author identity is antranig.yeretzian@proton.me on all 60 — no
recurrence of gqlc-r41's test@example.invalid fixture identity. Discipline held
where the gate did not, for the fourth time. That is still luck, not a control.

## What is now needed (the detection half is NOT sufficient)

PR #946 makes the drift VISIBLE on the next Bash call, which is a real
improvement and should still land. But visibility does not stop a writer that
fires every few minutes. The durable options, none yet chosen:
  1. re-assert 'git config core.hooksPath .githooks' after every agent spawn
     (cheap, orchestrator-side, but racy and treats the symptom);
  2. move agent worktrees OUT of the shared config's blast radius, i.e. do not
     use harness worktrees in this repo at all — spawn agents that make their
     own 'git worktree add' under /tmp, which is already the house rule;
  3. set core.hooksPath in a scope the harness does not overwrite.
Option 2 matches the standing worktree rule and is the only one that removes
the write rather than racing it.
=== REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, same session ===

  2. spawned ONE agent (the reviewer for PR #932)
  3. read back immediately: '/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/hooks'

One spawn, one drift, no other action in between. The write is DETERMINISTIC on
agent spawn, not an occasional race. Repaired again.

This also explains the four-occurrence history without needing any bad actor:
the value is rewritten every time an agent starts, so the repo is unhooked
almost continuously during factory operation, and each human-noticed occurrence
was simply the moment someone happened to look.

title: check-pr-closes: a marker inside an unterminated HTML attribute is honoured though GitHub hides it
description:
prose_only() blanks fenced blocks, HTML comments and raw 
/ blocks. It does not model raw HTML attribute values, so a body of

z

renders on GitHub as 
z
 -- the marker is nowhere in the rendered body -- and check-pr-closes.py still honours it: rc=0 with the ::warning that #617 stays open at merge. Measured against POST /markdown (mode gfm) and the checker together on 2026-08-17, at PR #901 head.

This is the fail-open direction the sweep in .githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh claims to bound, found outside the 85-shape sample it was bounded over. Scoped to prose at PR #901 round 5 (a row pins the shape and the sweep sentence now names it); a fix needs prose_only() to track an open tag whose attribute value is unterminated, which is inline-HTML parsing rather than the line-oriented block model the function is.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1335, merged as master e5e88f0e. A marker inside an unterminated HTML attribute value is now blanked before REFS_IN_BODY runs: open_attr_quote() scans the line for a quote that opens an attribute value and does not close on that line, and puts the following lines in an attr state until the matching quote. Applied only under prose_only(strict=True), reached through the new visible_prose() wrapper. WHY IT WAS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX. prose_only() was answering two questions with one body and they err in opposite directions. 'Can a reader see this opt-out marker' has to err towards BLANKING, because honouring an invisible marker makes the gate annotate the check run to say an issue stays open over a body nobody can see it said in. 'Does this body close an issue' has to err towards KEEPING, because a lost claim means the PR merges, the issue closes, and no bead held the number. Blanking the lines under an open attribute is right for the first and wrong for the second. The split into visible_prose() and claimable_prose() is what made this fixable in the safe direction, and the same split closed gqlc-xz16 and gqlc-tysj. MEASURED, not assumed: the body 'z' was put to GitHub's own renderer via POST /markdown mode gfm and comes back with the marker appearing nowhere in the output. Two narrowings are deliberate and each is its own row: a value opens only at a quote preceded by an '=', so a sentence writing an apostrophe after a '<' opens nothing; and an unterminated tag carrying no open quote returns nothing rather than swallowing the rest. Rows: the suite's visibility section, which grew from 137 to 152 rows over this branch. The row that was green here is red now and names this close. Mutation screen over the branch: 14 mutants, all KILLED, each by the row that should kill it.

title: codegen/age: the testdata/ sweep exclusion is justified as 'the generator's OUTPUT', which it is not
description:
Found during PR #913 round-3 review (Linus nit N8), measured not guessed.

The age type sweep excludes testdata/ with the justification that 'that tree is the generator's OUTPUT'. It is not. testdata/ holds 4 .gql generator INPUTS plus a hand-written driver template. The generator's actual output goes to a t.TempDir().

The exclusion itself is SAFE — the reviewer measured 0 .go files and 0 typeMap occurrences under testdata/ — so this is not a live hole. Only the stated reason is false.

This is the repository's signature defect class: a justification in prose that the tree falsifies. It matters because the next person to widen or narrow the exclusion will reason from the false premise. If testdata/ ever grows a .go file, 'it's output, so it can't carry a type' is the sentence that will let it through unswept.

Fix: state the true reason (no .go files, and the tree is fixture input the sweep has no claim over) instead of the false one.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
2026-09-02, agent-m — PR #2281 (fix/gqlc-ww8u-testdata-exclusion-reason), armed --auto --squash. Closes #944.

THE BEAD WAS RIGHT THAT THE SENTENCE IS FALSE, and it is false in three ways
rather than one:
  1. testdata/ is not the generator's output. Four .gql generator INPUTS plus
     corpus_test.go.txt, a hand-written driver; the real output goes to a
     t.TempDir(). (The bead had this one.)
  2. There is NO testdata-specific exclusion. The loop skips entry.IsDir()
     unconditionally, by shape and not by name -- testdata/ is merely the only
     subdirectory internal/codegen/age has (measured: find -maxdepth 1 -type d
     returns it alone). So "which it does not descend into BECAUSE that tree is
     output" attributes a reason to a decision that was never made.
  3. "and which the go tool leaves out of the package FOR THE SAME REASON" --
     no. The go tool ignores any directory named testdata whatever it holds.

WHERE I DEPARTED FROM THE BEAD'S SUGGESTED FIX, deliberately. The bead proposed
the true reason is "no .go files, and the tree is fixture input the sweep has no
claim over". The first half is a COUNT, not a guarantee: true today, needing a
guard to stay true, and it carries the bead's own stated worry that "if
testdata/ ever grows a .go file" the exclusion becomes a hole. IT WOULD NOT.

MEASURED FIRST-PARTY rather than reasoned. I wrote
internal/codegen/age/testdata/zz_probe.go declaring `package age`, a DUPLICATE
`type typeMap struct{}` and a line of invalid Go, then:
  go build ./internal/codegen/age/          -> exit 0
  go list -f '{{.GoFiles}}' ./...age/       -> probe absent
Probe removed; git status --short clean after. So nothing under testdata/ is in
package age, nothing there can declare a method on typeMap, and the exclusion is
guaranteed rather than merely currently-true. That is why the fix adds NO
assertion counting .go files: the guard the bead's wording would have implied is
the one I am saying is not owed.

ALSO CORRECTED, because the two sentences lied jointly: the neighbouring
"selection is by directory listing and not by build list" now says it is a claim
about files IN this directory. Adjacent to the old text they implied the go
tool's view governs the walk, which is backwards -- it is BECAUSE selection is
listing-driven that the directory skip has to be unconditional, since a walk
that descended would read a testdata file the go tool never compiles.

NOT ONE INSTANCE OF SEVEN, checked. Seven sweeps share the os.ReadDir(".")
shape (internal/resolver, internal/query, internal/codegen,
internal/codegen/neo4j, and three in internal/codegen/age). grep for "testdata"
in the other six: zero hits. The false justification was not copy-pasted.

SCOPE: prose only, one paragraph, one file, 26 insertions / 6 deletions.

title: codegen/age: returnedGoType reads first.X and drops first.Y, so a concatenated literal return type is unswept
description:
Found during PR #913 round-3 review (Linus nit N9), measured not guessed.

internal/codegen/age's type sweep resolves a function's returned Go type via returnedGoType, which reads only first.X of the return expression and never reads first.Y. So a return whose RHS is a concatenation of literals is invisible to the sweep:

    return "[]" + "decimal.Decimal", true

is count-preserving (md5 7fac379e) and the sweep PASSES with 23 subtests. A carrier introduced this way would be unswept.

Not a blocker on #913 because (a) the package is still RED elsewhere for that mutation, and (b) the operative disclosure sitting beside the claim is true. But the prose there says 'the AST cannot close it', which is false as stated — the AST can close it; this walk does not.

Two fixes are possible: read the full binary expression when the RHS is a concatenation of literals, or narrow the prose to say what the walk actually does. Prefer the former; the latter alone leaves the hole.

title: codegen: paramFieldName preserves ALL-CAPS, so an ALL-CAPS edge label mangles to an ALL-CAPS or run-together Go type name
description:
Found while reviewing PR #932 (bd gqlc-2sb8). Not in that PR's territory — filed, not fixed.

internal/codegen/names.go:42 — paramFieldName splits the raw name on '_', capitalises the first rune of each non-ALL-CAPS segment, and passes ALL-CAPS segments through unchanged (the isAllCaps branch, names.go:66).

internal/codegen/prepare.go:488 — the derived name for an edge type routes its label through that same paramFieldName, then checks exportedGoIdent (^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$, names.go:35).

Both of those checks pass on ALL-CAPS input, so the Go type name a Neo4j-idiomatic edge label derives is:

- LINKED -> LINKED (a Go type named LINKED)
- ACTED_IN -> ACTEDIN (segments run together, no word boundary left)

Both are valid exported Go identifiers, so nothing refuses them and no test row pins them. Neo4j's own convention is SCREAMING_SNAKE relationship types, so this is the shape a real schema is most likely to hit.

Undecided and part of the work: whether the right answer is Linked / ActedIn (title-case every segment when the whole label is ALL-CAPS), or to keep the pass-through and pin it as intended. paramFieldName's ALL-CAPS branch exists for parameter names ($ID, $URL), where preserving the caps is the point — an edge label is a second caller with a different convention, so a fix has to not regress the parameter case.

title: ci: the modscope-caller sweep reads recipe headers, so a parameter default spelling := hides a recipe
description:
`internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go` (added for bd gqlc-c7o7) finds the
recipes that run modscope by reading recipe headers off the justfile, and holds
each one whose body spells `internal/tools/modscope` to reaching
`sweep-discovery-probes` through its dependency closure. The header is what the
reader keys on, and this issue records the header shapes it does not recognise.

`justHeader` finds the recipe name by taking the first `:` on an unindented
line. A **parameter default containing `:=`** puts that first colon inside the
default, so the line is read as an assignment and the recipe is not read at all.
Measured on a `/tmp` copy at bd gqlc-c7o7: rewriting
`vuln: sweep-discovery-probes vuln-root-residual` to
`vuln x="a:=b": vuln-root-residual` leaves `just --dump` at rc=0 with `vuln`
still carrying its dependency and a body naming the package path 3x, and leaves
`TestEveryRecipeRunningModscopeSweepsProbesFirst` passing, rc=0. The control --
the same edge dropped with a readable header -- fails, rc=1, naming `vuln`.

One of the reader's controls reaches a missed header: every dependency it reads
must resolve to a recipe it read, so a recipe that *depends on* the unreadable
one produces a complaint. That control reaches a missed header only through the
recipes that depend on that header, so it does not reach one nothing depends on
-- `vuln` and `test-codegen-fence` are in that position on this tree
(`just --dump --dump-format json`). A separate complaint covers the case where
the missed header is `sweep-discovery-probes` itself: the reader refuses to
answer if no recipe by that name was read.

**Not live today.** The two recipes on this tree that carry parameter defaults
are `lint-hooks dir=".githooks"` (justfile:130) and `lint-new rev="origin/master"`;
neither default contains `:=`, and neither body spells the package path. A
29-name differential over every header `just` sees passes at bd gqlc-c7o7's
head, with the `vuln x="a:=b":` control failing, so the detector is live and no
header on this tree is missed. The residue is prospective: a *future* recipe
whose parameter default spells `:=`, whose body spells the package path, and
which nothing depends on.

**Why this needs a bead rather than only a comment.** The limit is named at
three sites (justfile's `sweep-discovery-probes` comment, `goDirs` in
`internal/tools/modscope/main.go`, and justfile_test.go's head comment) and
pinned by a row in `TestParseJustfileReadsWhatJustReads`
(`a parameter default spelling := leaves the header unread`, `want: nil`). That
row pins the hole **open**: whoever teaches the reader to read the shape has to
edit a passing test, and without this issue nothing tells them the `want: nil`
was deliberate rather than a bug. The sibling limit -- an invocation that never
spells the package path -- already carries bd gqlc-wkio for exactly that reason,
and the probe-site analogue carries bd gqlc-lj9s.

Closing it means either (a) making `justHeader` find the first colon outside
quotes, in which case the `want: nil` row flips to the recipe it should read and
this issue is the record of why; or (b) reading the recipes off
`just --dump --dump-format json` instead of off the justfile text, which is
option (a) in gqlc-wkio too and would close both limits at once. (b) trades a
hand-written parser for a dependency on `just` being installed in the test
environment; price that before choosing.

title: query sums: three defaults/comments outside internal/query still assume closed sums
description:
Three defaults / prose sites outside `internal/query` were chosen on the premise
that the query model's marker-sealed interfaces are closed sums. #916 (PR on
`fix/query-sealed-sum-universals`) establishes that they are not: an unexported
marker with value receivers seals *declaration*, not *inhabitation*, so
`*query.NodeBinding` and `struct{ query.NodeBinding }` both satisfy the
interface from any package in the module and match no `case query.NodeBinding:`
arm. Control reaches the default.

That branch is scoped to `internal/query` by instruction (`internal/resolver/`
was under concurrent work), so these three are filed rather than edited. Two of
them are named in the new doc comments on `query.Use` and `query.Type`.

1. `internal/query/cypher/expr.go` — `attributeUse`'s default returns its
   argument **unchanged**. A promoted `Use` therefore passes through carrying
   whatever `(branch, part)` coordinate it already had instead of being
   re-stamped: reachable and silent. Every other audited default over a query
   sum refuses soundly (`validateEffect` -> `ErrOutOfR0Scope`, `endpointLabels`
   -> `(endpointKeys{}, false)`, `projectionType`, `bindingVariable`). Decide
   whether this one should refuse too, or document why pass-through is right.

2. `internal/resolver/resolve.go` — `resolveType`'s default **panics**. Not a
   live production bug (only parser-constructed Types reach it today), but it
   is a live branch, not dead code, and its behaviour was picked on the
   closed-sum premise. Decide: keep the panic and say why, or return an error.

3. `internal/resolver/resolve.go:1477-1479` — comment still calls it "the
   closed `Effect` sum" and cites `query.go:1631-1660`, which is not where
   `Effect` lives. Both halves are wrong: the universal, and the line range.

Acceptance: each site either corrected or given a comment that states the real
guarantee (declaration sealed, inhabitation open) and why the current behaviour
is the right one. House rule as in AGENTS.md "Closed sum types": state the
negative and enumerate the limit; no "cannot / never / no other".
notes:
Two more sites, found by re-running #916's claim-phrase sweep at PR #940 head 5bc69b61 (review round 2). They are beyond the three the description enumerates.

internal/codegen/prepare.go:269 - "C3 widens the admissible column shape to the full closed ResolvedType sum minus ResolvedEdgeUnion"
internal/codegen/prepare.go:563 - "full closed sum minus ResolvedEdgeUnion on columns"

Both are about resolver.ResolvedType, the sum gqlc-856f / #881 corrected in internal/resolver/validated.go, not a query sum - which is why PR #940 left them: outside both its package and its sum. Each describes an admission SET ("the whole enumerated set minus one") rather than a dispatch totality, so neither is as wrong as item 3; what "closed" is doing there is naming the enumeration, not promising a switch is exhaustive. Decide whether to reword to "the full ResolvedType sum minus ResolvedEdgeUnion" (dropping only the word that carries the false half) or leave as admission-set vocabulary and say so.

PR #940 also fixed, rather than deferring, two sites the round-1 review found: CONTEXT.md's Use/Effect/Projection/Type glossary entries and internal/query/cypher/typing.go:591. Those are NOT part of this bead.
close_reason: All three sites resolved in PR #1372; none needed another lane. (1) internal/query/cypher/expr.go attributeUse's default returned its argument UNCHANGED — CORRECTED to panic. Pass-through is the one silently wrong answer: the Use keeps whatever (branch, part) it arrived with, and that coordinate is what the resolver keys parameter-type unification on, so the parameter unifies against the wrong Part and the query still compiles. The comment now states the real guarantee (marker seals declaration, not inhabitation) and what actually bounds the arm — provenance, not unreachability: every Use reaching addParameterUse or addParameterUseUnsuppressed is built in that package, and neither call site has an error channel to refuse through. (2) internal/resolver/resolve.go resolveType's default KEEPS its panic, with the reason written down: routing an in-module mistake to ErrOutOfR0Scope would put it in the channel callers render to the user as a diagnostic about their Cypher, and the TypeNode/TypeEdge/TypePath arms above it already take that reading. (3) validateEffect's comment said 'closed Effect sum (query.go:1631-1660)'. Both halves were wrong and both are corrected: the sum is not closed, and 1631-1660 is where query.Use lives, not Effect — Effect is 'type Effect interface' near query.go:2100 with its variants below. Now cited by construct. All three defaults gained foreign-inhabitant pins using struct{ query.X }, each paired with a declared-variant row so the pin is not the only measurement: TestAttributeUseRefusesAForeignUse / TestAttributeUseStampsEveryKnownVariant in internal/query/cypher, TestResolveTypeDefaultPanicsOnAForeignType and TestValidateEffectDefaultRefusesAForeignEffect in internal/resolver. The cypher one asserts with the stdlib, not testify, because an in-package test importing third-party code takes the whole package out of govulncheck's call graph (bd gqlc-m5rc) — that gate caught it on the PR's first run.

title: ci: action and tool downloads hit GitHub 429 under factory concurrency, with no retry or cache around the golangci-lint curl
description:
> **SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-17.** This issue now covers the **golangci-lint
> tool download** only — the `curl | sh` with no retry and no cache, and the
> per-job re-download in CI. That is what PR #951 fixes, and what `Closes
> #933` on that PR closes.
>
> The `actions/setup-go` half named in the title and in SHAPE OF A FIX below
> is **split out to #953** and remains open. It is the live failure mode: the
> runner fetches that action before any repo-controlled step runs, so nothing
> #951 adds is reached in time.
>
> Original body follows unchanged.

---

Two independent witnesses on 2026-08-17, during a wave with ~8 PRs open and
CI firing on each.

WITNESS 1 (PR #932, round 1). Two required contexts went red without running
a line of the change:
  - `test` died in "Set up job" downloading `actions/setup-go`, after 3
    attempts, on HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
  - `codegen-fence` died on `curl: (22)` provisioning golangci-lint.
`gh run rerun --failed` cleared both.

WITNESS 2 (PR #913, round-2 review). `just lint` died provisioning
golangci-lint on HTTP 429. The reviewer recovered by re-running against the
already-cached v2.12.2 binary.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FLAKE. A red required context that never executed
the code is indistinguishable, at a glance, from a real failure. In a factory
where a green rollup is the merge authority, a setup-phase 429 costs a full
review cycle each time someone has to establish that the redness was infra.
It also trains the reader to re-run red contexts, which is exactly the habit
that lets a genuine failure through.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not yet chosen):
  - Cache or vendor the golangci-lint binary rather than curl-ing it per job.
    The `curl` has no retry and no cache; every job pays a fresh download.
  - Add retry/backoff around the tool download step.
  - Check whether `actions/setup-go` is being fetched rather than served from
    the runner image, and pin/cache accordingly.

ACCEPTANCE. A CI run under concurrency where the golangci-lint provisioning
step survives a 429, or a gate whose tool comes from cache and cannot 429 at
all. Bonus: something that distinguishes "died in setup" from "the change is
red" in the rollup, so a reader is not trained to re-run.

RELATED. Territory is the `justfile` and/or the workflow setup steps, which
were held by PRs #920 / #901 / #882 during this wave -- part of why it was
reported rather than fixed on the spot.
notes:
THIRD WITNESS, and a worse defect than the flake — 2026-08-17, on my own
`git commit` for the p4 ledger export:

    WARN: could not provision golangci-lint (offline?); skipping format check

So the 429 window is not confined to CI. BOTH local hooks fail OPEN on a
provisioning failure:

  .githooks/pre-commit:25-32  ensure-golangci fails -> skip `just fmt-check`
  .githooks/pre-push:13-18    ensure-golangci fails -> skip `just lint-new`

Neither exits non-zero. During a 429 window every commit skips the format
gate and every push skips lint, announced only by a WARN on stderr that
scrolls past in normal output. That is the house 'a detector that exits 0 is
not a gate' shape, and it is reachable by ordinary network conditions rather
than by deliberate action.

AND THE COMMENTS ARE FALSE. Both sites justify the degradation with the same
claim:

  pre-commit:22-24  "it only fails when a needed download is impossible
                     (e.g. offline), and then we degrade to a warning rather
                     than block commits"
  pre-push:13-14    "it only fails when a needed download is impossible
                     (e.g. offline) — degrade to a warning then"

`only ... (e.g. offline)` is the falsified universal. I was not offline; the
network was fine and GitHub returned 429. That distinction is what the whole
argument rests on: degrading to a warning is defensible when the trigger is
rare, obvious and developer-local (you know you are on a plane). It is not
defensible when the trigger is a common, silent, server-side rate limit that
fires hardest exactly when the most work is in flight.

title: codegen/neo4j: the corpus edge type carries a subset of the widths, so BYTES / TIMESTAMP element carriers and the third nesting depth run on dbtype.Node alone
description:
Measured on gqlc-2sb8 at 92ebb9a7 (branch feat/neo4j-corpus-edge-type).

The Edgy edge type added there declares rank (INT32), ranks (LIST<INT32>), matrix (LIST<LIST<INT64>>), payload (ANY VALUE), loose (LIST), depths (LIST<FLOAT32>) and weight (FLOAT32). Between them those reach the emitter's narrowing-scalar, nullable-narrowing-scalar, walked-list, nested-walk, walked-nullable-list, unwalked-[]any and shapeless arms over dbtype.Relationship.

Three things the node types exercise are not on the edge:

- LIST<BYTES>, whose elements the driver hands back as []byte and which isSliceType excludes from the walk;
- LIST<TIMESTAMP>, whose element carrier is time.Time and which moves renderModels' 'time' import gate;
- the third nesting depth (LIST<LIST<LIST<...>>>), which is where writeSliceNarrow's accumulator locals first nest one inside another.

The emitter code for those arms is shared between the two entity kinds — writeEntityFieldDecode branches on e.Kind only for the carrier type and the argument name — so a defect specific to the edge kind in one of them is what stays unmeasured, not the arm itself. That is why this is P3 and not P2.

Not blocking gqlc-2sb8.
notes:

Re-derived from the emission for testdata/corpus_schema.gql (Generate at 471e3891, models.go). The per-property arms are eight, not seven: writeEntityFieldDecode (render_models.go:214) branches nullable/non-nullable x {walked slice, narrow-convert, plain assign} = six, and writeShapelessFieldDecode (render_models.go:264) carries two more. The 'nested-walk' this description lists is not one of them — it is writeSliceNarrow recursing, inside the walked-slice arm.

Edgy's seven properties land on SIX of those eight:
  depths  -> nullable walked slice
  weight  -> nullable narrow-convert
  loose   -> nullable plain assign (out.Loose = &s; []any is excluded from isSliceType)
  matrix  -> non-nullable walked slice
  ranks   -> non-nullable walked slice  (same arm as matrix)
  rank    -> non-nullable narrow-convert
  payload -> non-nullable shapeless

So the mapping is neither onto nor one-to-one. Two arms run off dbtype.Node only and never off the Relationship in this fixture, in addition to the three widths already listed here:

  - non-nullable plain assign: out.Loose = value1 in decodeBin (loose :: LIST NOT NULL), also decodeScalar's active and id. Edgy has no non-nullable property whose carrier already equals its emitted Go type.
  - nullable shapeless: out.Maybe = &v in decodeAnything (maybe :: ANY VALUE). Edgy has no nullable ANY VALUE.

Both are now named in the corpus_schema.gql header comment and in PR #932's body. Whoever picks this bead up should treat it as five items, not three.
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is

routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
2026-09-02, agent-m, at claim time. The five-item inventory the note above leaves is now TWO. Re-derived against master (corpus_schema.gql, render_models.go):

  1. LIST<BYTES> off dbtype.Relationship — STILL OPEN. writeSliceNarrow's default arm (carrier == elem; []byte is excluded from isSliceType and asserted straight). Reached by Listy.blobs off a Node, by nothing off a Relationship.
  2. LIST<TIMESTAMP> off dbtype.Relationship — STILL OPEN. writeSliceNarrow's isTemporalCarrier arm (narrowExpr, no error path). Reached by Listy.stamps off a Node, by nothing off a Relationship.

Under ADR 0035 the neo4j server will not hold a nested-list stored property, so Phase Z refuses the declaration (ErrUnstorableProperty) and no fixture can carry one. writeSliceNarrow's recursive arm was DELETED in the same change; the function is flat today, with three element cases and no depth counter. title: codegen/neo4j: the driver-value corpus projects no whole-entity column, so ColumnNode / ColumnEdge / ColumnEdgeUnion row assembly is never run
description:
Measured on gqlc-2sb8 at 92ebb9a7 (branch feat/neo4j-corpus-edge-type).

internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_queries.cypher projects properties only: b.loose, l.tags, n.cube, a.payload. Every column the corpus decodes therefore lands on ColumnProperty or ColumnList. Three of codegen's declared ColumnKind arms are reached by no query the corpus runs:

- ColumnNode, a whole-node projection decoded into its entity struct;
- ColumnEdge, the same for an edge;
- ColumnEdgeUnion, C5's multi-candidate-edge dispatch on the wire label.

gqlc-2sb8 added an edge type to corpus_schema.gql and rows that run decodeEdgy on a dbtype.Relationship, so the ENTITY decode path now covers both carriers. The COLUMN path is the other emission of the same rule (neo4j.GetRecordValue rather than the Props map), and for these three kinds it is run by nothing in this package that executes emitted Go.

Scope if anyone takes it: add 'MATCH (s:Scalar)-[e:Edgy]->(l:Listy) RETURN s AS s, e AS e' style projections to corpus_queries.cypher and the matching rows to testdata/corpus_test.go.txt. ColumnEdgeUnion needs a second edge type sharing the label across endpoint pairs, so it is the larger half.

Not blocking gqlc-2sb8.
notes:

REFUSES: prepare.go's admitEdgeUnionCandidates returns

title: bdguard: allowed-reopens reaches only closes whose close_reason cites a sha
description:
gqlc-npyp added .beads/allowed-reopens.txt, whose entries are `<bead-id> <closing-sha>` and are granted only if the BASE record's close_reason cites that sha as a whole token. That binding is what stops the declaration being a bare id the head can assert unilaterally — base comes out of a git ref.

It also bounds what the remedy reaches. Measured on .beads/issues.jsonl at 92ebb9a7: 449 issue records, 290 closed, of which 8 carry no close_reason at all and only 86 carry a close_reason with a hex token of 7-40 characters. So roughly 30% of closed beads are correctable through this arm today; the rest — anything closed by hand with a prose reason — has no declaration that bdguard will grant, and a wrong close there still has to be carried in the export until it is re-closed for real.

This is the safe direction (the arm refuses rather than grants), and the witnessed defect class — a branch-close hook auto-close — always cites a sha, so the hole is not on the path that motivated the work. Options if it bites:
- accept a second declaration shape carrying the disputed closed_at timestamp instead of a sha, verified against base the same way;
- have the close hook always write a sha (see gqlc-90vt, which is already changing that hook);
- accept a free-text `reason` field whose exact bytes must equal base's close_reason, which keeps the base-quoting property without needing a sha.

Do not widen this to a bare-id entry: that reduces the arm to the allowlist gqlc-npyp exists to avoid.
notes: 2026-08-23, factory cleanup wave: NOT fixed. Left open deliberately. This bead was routed to the claude-pre-bash lane but its implementation is internal/tools/bdguard/main.go, a Go tool, outside that lane's file set (.githooks/claude-pre-bash, .githooks/claude-pre-ask, and their test suites). Grepped to confirm: no allowed-reopens logic exists in .githooks/. The other five beads of that batch landed in PR #1333. Whoever picks this up owns the Go tool, not the hook.
close_reason: PR #1363, merged as master 4a478f85. Taken as the bead's first option: allowed-reopens.txt now accepts a second entry shape, the bead id followed by an RFC3339 timestamp that must name the same INSTANT as the base record's updated_at. The bead's own arithmetic is the reason — of 290 closed records at 92ebb9a7 only 86 carried a hex token, so the other two hundred and four, every close written by hand with a prose reason, had no declaration bdguard would grant. The base-quoting property the bead insists on is intact: updated_at is read from base with git show, so the head cannot assert it, and the bead's explicit prohibition on a bare-id entry is respected. The hole I did NOT expect and which the bead does not mention: the sha shape carries a reachability veto and the timestamp shape has nothing to apply one to, so a declaration whose sha was vetoed could have escaped by quoting the timestamp instead. A timestamp declaration is therefore refused outright when the base close_reason cites a sha some ref contains, with a message naming both the sha and the ref. An ORPHANED sha is not a bar, since the veto would have stayed silent there and the two shapes agree. On the gqlc-7fn3 interaction the assignment asked me to check: they do not collide. That fix taught the bd-close HOOK to stop reading a bare decimal token as a sha; isSHAToken here still accepts one, deliberately, because roughly four in a hundred seven-character abbreviations are all-decimal and refusing the shape would refuse real declarations. It is safe in this direction because looking like a sha grants nothing — citesSHA still requires base to quote the token verbatim, and a decimal token resolves to no object so the veto is silent, the same outcome as any orphan. That reasoning is now a comment on the function. Seven mutations, each killed by a named test: equality blinded, veto-dodge fence removed, the token scanner blinded, the hint sentence dropped, a timestamp stored as a sha, and instant equality narrowed to byte equality. An eighth was rejected as a fake RED — blinding the equality first failed to BUILD on unused variables, which is the compiler killing it, not a test. check, refuseReopen, refuseDeclaredFact, parseAllowedReopens and citedSHATokens are all at 100.0 percent of statements; main, run, showAtRef and gitRefContaining remain at zero, as gqlc-drvx already records.

title: ci: the modscope-caller sweep reads the package path, so an invocation that never spells it is unswept
description:
`internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go` (added for bd gqlc-c7o7) holds a
justfile recipe **whose body spells the package path** `internal/tools/modscope`
to reaching `sweep-discovery-probes` through its dependency closure, so for
those recipes a forgotten edge is caught rather than discovered when a probe
leaks. The spelling is the bound, and this issue records what falls outside it.

It finds callers by matching the package path `internal/tools/modscope` in a
recipe body. That reaches `go run`, `go build` and `go test` alike, because all
three take the package path.

It does NOT reach an invocation that never spells the path:

  - a binary built once under another name (`.bin/modscope`, a `$stage` temp)
    and called by that name;
  - a path assembled from a justfile variable, e.g. `modscope := "./internal/tools/modscope"`
    interpolated at the site — `just --dump` would show the variable, not the path;
  - a recipe that shells out to another script which runs it.

Not currently reachable: at filing, the only four invocation sites in the
justfile are `scope() { go run ./internal/tools/modscope \"\$@\"; }`
(justfile:223, :703, :833, :1139). This is a stated limit of the check, beside
`modscopePkg`, not a live defect — the same shape and the same honesty as
gqlc-lj9s, which records that sweep-discovery-probes recognises only
`mktemp -d` as a probe site.

Closing it means either (a) reading the invocation off `just --dump --dump-format json`
after variable expansion rather than off the recipe text, or (b) routing every
modscope invocation through one `[private]` recipe the others depend on, so there
is one site to hold rather than a pattern to match — the same (b) gqlc-lj9s
proposes for the probe sites.

---

**Amended 2026-08-17.** The opening paragraph previously read "holds **every**
justfile recipe that runs modscope ... so a leaked discovery probe **cannot**
wedge a gate that forgot the edge". Both absolutes are falsified by the
paragraph immediately below them, and by row J6 of PR #920 — a
`check-golangci-build-tags` body rewritten to spell the package path zero times
while still running the program keeps the test green with the edge dropped.
That is the same defect this issue exists to record, restated in the record
itself. The claim is now bounded by the spelling.
notes: Residual left for the justfile owner (vuln-sweeps lane could not touch the justfile this wave; fleetctl-restart lane owned it). PR #1374 widens the RECOGNISER so a path invocation, an interpolated just variable and a bare PATH call are each read as running modscope, and pins each with its own row. It does not close the indirect case: a recipe that runs a script which in turn runs modscope is still invisible to any reader of recipe bodies, because the invocation is not in the body. That row is in the table with refused:false and the reason, so the hole is pinned rather than believed. The remedy this bead proposes is the justfile-side one -- make modscope reachable only through a [private] recipe every caller must depend on, so the dependency edge is what the sweep reads and the spelling stops mattering. Exact edit deliberately NOT applied here.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #1374 (squashed onto master; the branch head that CI certified was 94aa4207). The lane that wrote this was killed by a stall watchdog mid-rebase; I rebased its branch onto master, re-ran the affected packages, force-pushed, and merged it on a green check table with three real check-suites present at the head sha. Files carrying the fix: internal/tools/vulnguard/{selftestcalls_test.go,stdlibgrading_test.go,harness_test.go}, internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go, internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go. Not verified by me: the per-row mutation reasoning in the PR body is the lane's, not re-derived here.

title: AGENTS.md's Closed sum types bullet restates the sealed-sum claim gqlc-856f corrected
description:
`AGENTS.md:105-113`, under **Make illegal states unrepresentable**, still says:

    - **Closed sum types** — an interface with an unexported marker method
      makes the sum exhaustive: only types in the same package can implement it,
      so callers cannot smuggle in a third variant and the compiler sees every
      case.

Both halves are the claim `gqlc-856f` corrected at the source. The marker seals
DECLARATION, not inhabitation: a pointer form of a variant satisfies the
interface (value receivers, and a pointer's method set contains its value
methods), and a struct embedding a variant satisfies it from any package (Go
promotes an embedded type's unexported methods). So callers CAN smuggle in a
type no arm names, and the compiler does not see every case.

This is the guidance document, so it is the source the next agent copies the
wrong claim from — `internal/codegen/age/errors.go`'s fall-through comment
(gqlc-qv80) and `internal/resolver/validated.go` (gqlc-856f / PR #881) were
both written from it.

## Why filed rather than fixed

`AGENTS.md` was outside gqlc-qv80's territory, whose acceptance criterion is
`internal/codegen/age/errors.go`. Prior art for the correct phrasing:
`internal/codegen/errors.go:185-198`, PR #881's rewrite of
`internal/resolver/validated.go`, and this bead's parent
`internal/codegen/age/errors.go`.

## Acceptance

The bullet says what an unexported marker does buy (no out-of-package type
DECLARES it, so the declaring set is closed) and what it does not (the
inhabiting set is unbounded: pointer forms and embedders, which nest), and
either keeps or drops the "Closed sum types" heading on that basis. Whatever
replaces it must not be a universal any test in this tree falsifies —
`internal/resolver/sealedsum_test.go` and
`internal/codegen/age/sealedsum_test.go` are the two that would.
notes:
RESOLVED BY PR #881 (merged 2026-08-17, 2ca30818) — no separate branch needed.

#881's round-4 work rewrote the exact lines this bead was filed against (hunk @@ -103,9 +103,15 @@ of AGENTS.md). Verified against master 92ebb9a7, AGENTS.md:105-114 now reads:

  **Closed sum types** — an interface with an unexported marker method seals
  declaration, not inhabitation. A method of that name declared in another
  package does not satisfy the interface, so the variants are the whole set of
  types declaring the marker. It does not close the set of types that satisfy
  it: where the marker takes a value receiver, a pointer to a variant and a
  struct embedding one both promote it from any package in the module and match
  no case Variant: arm, so control reaches the default or leaves the switch — a
  live case, not a dead one. See internal/resolver/validated.go and
  TestResolvedTypeSumIsNotClosed.

Checked against this bead's acceptance criteria, all three met:
- says what the marker DOES buy (no out-of-package type declares it, so the declaring set is closed) — yes, sentence 2.
- says what it does NOT (the inhabiting set is unbounded via pointer forms and embedders) — yes, sentence 3.
- keeps or drops the heading on that basis — heading kept, and the text now justifies keeping it.

The 'must not be a universal any test in this tree falsifies' clause is also met: the claim is qualified 'where the marker takes a value receiver', which is precisely what internal/resolver/sealedsum_test.go and internal/codegen/age/sealedsum_test.go exercise. Linus round 5 measured the fix commit 3b76df87 as AGENTS.md-only, +6/-5, whose entire content is that qualifier.

That acceptance clause is worth keeping as standing guidance beyond this bead — it is the same 'no universals in prose' rule now applied at review time across the factory.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen/neo4j: the driver-value corpus declares no edge type, so no relationship decoder is ever run
description:
Measured on gqlc-uc8f / PR #912 at 13278990.

internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_schema.gql declares five node types and no edge type. TestEmittedDecodersRunOnDriverValues assembles the emission into a throwaway module and compiles + runs it against the driver stub, so it is the one place in this package that type-checks the emitted decoders and executes them on real Go values — and every arm it reaches is a dbtype.Node arm.

Consequences measured on the branch base bb72fa0f:

- emitting edge structs with no fields at all leaves the emitted decode helper assigning out.<Field> on a struct with no such field. That does not compile, and ./internal/codegen/neo4j/ was still rc=0, because no edge entity ever reaches the corpus module.
- emitting nullable edge fields without the pointer likewise leaves 'out.F = &narrowed' against a non-pointer field: rc=0.

PR #912 catches both by reading the emission's AST against the parsed schema, so nothing ships broken. What stays uncovered is the other half: an edge decode arm whose emitted Go COMPILES but decodes wrong — a mis-narrowed LIST<INT32> off a Relationship's Props, a null that survives the node arm and fails the relationship one. Reading the AST cannot see that; only running it can.

Scope if anyone takes it: add an edge type to corpus_schema.gql carrying the widths the node types already exercise (a narrowing scalar, a nullable, a list, a list of lists, a property of no declared shape), and the matching cases to testdata/corpus_test.go.txt, which is the hand-written driver the emission is compiled against. Note the template names the structs and helpers the emission derives from the schema, so the two files move together.

Filed as residue from gqlc-uc8f; not blocking PR #912.
notes: PR #932 (head 04b50802) opened, Closes #914. Edge type Edgy added to corpus_schema.gql carrying 7 widths decoded off dbtype.Relationship (rank/ranks/matrix/payload/loose/depths/weight); 3 rows added to corpus_test.go.txt. render_models.go unmodified. Control: new schema + pre-change template + an edge-gated '+1' narrow mutation was rc=0 on the whole package; with the new rows it fails TestEdgyNarrowsOverARelationship. 5 mutation rows recorded in the PR body (4 KILLED, 1 recorded as a fake RED / compiler). Holes filed: gqlc-1bxq, gqlc-np7s. Awaiting review; I do not merge.
close_reason: PR #932 merged to master as c30baa86; GH #914 closed. The corpus now declares an edge type (Edgy) so a relationship decoder is actually run. Passed Linus round 3 after two prose rounds: round 2's 'the two the driver hands back as themselves' was a definite-article claim over an unbounded set; r3 replaced it with 'both of which the walk asserts straight to, without narrowing', verified against emitted bytes via go test -overlay (decodeListy asserts []byte and time.Time straight to the leaf, carrier==elem so writeSliceNarrow emits no conversion). Reviewer swept all 11 quantifiers in the branch diff, none falsified, and confirmed the r3 edit removed the colliding second use of 'hands back as themselves' so the surviving use is exhaustive per isSliceType:299. 7/7 CI SUCCESS pinned to 020683c1.

title: docs/adr/0025: the AGE Scalar bullet says decodeFunc has no agtypeNull or agtypeMap arm; it has two
description:
ADR 0025 (`docs/adr/0025-type-map-answers-carriage-per-kind.md`, the 'The AGE `Scalar` table is answered in two places' bullet, around line 113) records:

    `decodeFunc` has no `agtypeNull` or `agtypeMap` arm, so both route to
    `agtypeString`. Lifting the gate arm alone emits a `map[string]any` field
    filled from a `string`-returning helper — the generated package does not
    compile

Neither half holds against the tree. `decodeFunc` (internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go) has had explicit arms for both texts for some time:

    case "any":
        return "agtypeValue"
    case "map[string]any":
        return "agtypeMap"

So neither routes to `agtypeString`, and lifting `unservedColumn`'s gate arm would emit a `map[string]any` field filled from `agtypeMap`, which returns `map[string]any` — it would compile. The stated consequence, which is the bullet's whole argument for the gate being load-bearing, does not follow.

What DOES keep a null or map column out of emission is `unservedColumn` alone: it refuses `ScalarNull` and `ScalarMap` columns before emission. The refusal is still load-bearing; the recorded reason for it is not the real one.

Found during gqlc-u039 (decodeFunc's default arm). The sibling copy of the same claim in `internal/codegen/age/types.go`'s `Scalar` doc comment was corrected on that branch; this one was left because amending an ADR is a decision-record change that wants its own review.

## Fix

Amend the bullet to say what actually holds: the two texts have decode arms, the emitted helpers exist, and `unservedColumn` is the whole of what keeps a column of either kind away. Re-derive whether the two arms are still 'placeholders' on that footing, since the ADR's claim that they are rests on the falsified sentence.

## Also worth a look while there

`decodeFunc`'s `case "map[string]any"` arm is unreachable today by the same `unservedColumn` refusal — an arm whose only witness is the ADR sentence above.
notes:
PR https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/956 (branch fix/adr0025-scalar-decode-arms, HEAD 7d10247740f55e83c3b4dfb704adf86d6d6f8688, base 2df500a6). Not merged; orchestrator holds the merge.

Both premises in this bead verified against the tree at 2df500a6 and both hold. Two amendments to the brief:

1. The bead's 'Also worth a look' says decodeFunc's map[string]any arm has the ADR sentence as its only witness. That is wrong. Two tests pin it: render_queries_test.go's TestDecodeFuncNamesTheHelperForEveryServedCarrier row {"map[string]any" -> "agtypeMap"}, and TestDecodeFuncHasAnArmForEveryCarrierTheTypeTableProduces, which reads typeMap's returned literals out of the package AST and requires an arm for each. Deleting either arm reddens both (mutations recorded on the PR). The arm was LEFT in place and the ADR now names those two pins.

2. 'unservedColumn alone' is not exact. rejectUnservedQueries yields (continue) where !edgeUnion && dialectGapFires(q.SourceText), and rejectDialectGaps answers instead. Both gates run ahead of Prepare, so the column reaches no emission either way. The ADR now states the yield rather than the universal.

Scope grew by two adjacent sites that rested on the same falsified premise, both corrected in the same PR:
- ADR 0025's next bullet said 'Reachable only once an agtypeMap helper exists'. agtypeMap is emitted today in three goldens (schema_any_property, schema_any_property_alone, schema_list_any_property).
- The same bullet, and the duplicate paragraph in age/types.go's Scalar doc, said an integer inside a map decodes to float64. Executed against the schema_any_property golden, agtypeMap({"n": 3, ...}) yields int64 for n. The types.go paragraph was deleted; the ADR now states only the measured AGE half.

gqlc-l6c2 carries the unmeasured neo4j half (what the driver hands back for a map value's members), which wants a live target rather than a source read.
close_reason:
PR #956 merged as 0312371d (squash). GH #909 verified CLOSED. Linus PASS at round 1, no blockers.

WHAT IT ESTABLISHES: ADR 0025 justified the AGE Scalar unservedColumn gate by claiming decodeFunc had no arm for either 'any' or 'map[string]any', so both routed to agtypeString and lifting the gate would emit a package that does not compile. Both halves were false — decodeFunc answers 'any' with agtypeValue and 'map[string]any' with agtypeMap (render_queries.go:554-557), both helpers are emitted, and agtypeString's only decodeFunc return is under case 'string' (:568). The refusal is still load-bearing; the recorded REASON for it was not the real one. That reason is now correct.

The round disproved two of its own brief's premises rather than implementing them, which is the behaviour to reward: the brief said the unreachable map arm's only witness was the ADR sentence, and in fact two tests pin it and both redden on deletion.

INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THE REVIEWER, not accepted from the author: the decodeFunc arms and agtypeString's single routing; agtypeMap's return type at render_models.go:663; both runtime probes re-executed in a throwaway module built from the real emitted golden WITH a positive control (agtypeValue('null') -> nil,nil; agtypeMap over a five-member object -> int64 3, float64 1.5, string x, bool true, nil), confirming the deleted types.go sentence about integers decoding to float64 was false; the dialect-gap yield is not a hole because dialectGapFires and rejectDialectGaps iterate the same table with the same predicate, so a query tripping the yield is guaranteed refused by the other gate, both ahead of Prepare.

The sibling-copy completeness claim was re-run with the reviewer's own wider vocabulary (agtypeMap/agtypeValue/agtypeString/float64/ScalarMap/'does not compile'/'placeholder'/'reachable only'); agtypeNull has zero hits tree-wide; no third copy exists. Two copies found and fixed by the author. The neo4j half is gqlc-l6c2 (GH #955), open.

'No Go behaviour change' proven NON-VACUOUSLY: AST-stripped comparison with operands 2265 bytes on both sides (the guard exits 2 on empty input, so this is not the d41d8cd9 empty-md5 fake PASS), identical hashes, and the types.go hunk has zero added lines.

MUTATIONS on disk, not -overlay: these tests pin via os.ReadDir('.') so an overlay would have measured nothing. M1 delete case 'map[string]any' and M2 delete case 'any' both KILLED with named REDs; the reviewer added M3 (arm -> return 'agtypeString'), which the author had not run, and it KILLED the naming pin while the closure pin SURVIVED — vindicating the ADR's split of the two pins.

Residue filed as gqlc-aq0c.

title: ciguard: a hook suite whose exit status is discarded still passes the wiring pins
description:
internal/tools/ciguard/testhooks_test.go asserts that every .githooks/tests/*-test.sh appears in the test-hooks recipe body, that test depends on test-hooks, and that ci.yml's test job runs just test. All three check that a link is NAMED. None checks that its exit status is carried.

Measured (independent review of PR #901): changing

    bash .githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh

to

    bash .githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh || true

leaves all three wiring tests green while the suite's verdict is discarded. A deletion is caught (that is what the pins were built for); a neutralisation is not.

Acceptance: a test-hooks line whose exit status cannot reach the recipe's status fails a pin, and the pin names the line.
