title: bd-gh-sync: nothing re-checks that bd moves updated_at on a description edit
description:
The pull gate in .githooks/bd-gh-sync orders a bead against its GH mirror using bd.updated_at vs gh.updatedAt. That rests on third-party bd behaviour measured once (2026-08-17, bd 1.0.4 ce242a879) and written into the script header as a dated list.

No gate re-checks it. .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh stubs bd on PATH and drives fixture JSON, so it can never observe the real CLI. If a future bd stops moving updated_at on a description edit (bd update -d), every prefix-relation pair reads as 'GitHub not newer', the hold notice reprints forever, or - the direction that matters - the dated comment still reads true while the fail-open residue widens.

Options: a hook test that runs the real bd in a throwaway workspace and asserts bd update -d moves updated_at, wired into the test-hooks recipe. That needs a justfile edit, which is #846/#882 territory, so it was not done on #868.

Raised as N-2 in the round-2 review of PR #868.
notes:
--- TRIAGE 2026-08-23: the deferral reason is gone ---
This bead's last paragraph says the remedy 'needs a justfile edit, which is #846/#882
territory, so it was not done on #868'. That is no longer true. PR #1316 (commit
8b92f2ea) made 'just test-hooks' discover suites by glob:

    origin/master:justfile:1131   suites=(.githooks/tests/*-test.sh)

so a new .githooks/tests/<name>-test.sh running the real bd in a throwaway workspace
is wired by its filename alone, with no justfile edit and therefore no lane collision.
The defect itself is unverified either way by this triage lane: nothing was measured
about whether bd still moves updated_at on 'bd update -d'.
2026-08-23, worked as part of PR #1330's lane but NOT closed. Two things measured.

FIRST, the third-party claim still holds today. In a throwaway workspace under /tmp with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE cleared, 'bd init --prefix probe --non-interactive' then 'bd create' then 'bd update <id> -d' on bd 1.0.4 ce242a879: updated_at moved from 06:18:04Z to 06:18:07Z. So the dated header comment in .githooks/bd-gh-sync is accurate as of this date. That is a one-off measurement, which is exactly what this bead says is not enough.

SECOND, and this is what blocks the gate this bead asks for: .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh is run in CI. .github/workflows/ci.yml's 'test' job runs 'just test', which depends on 'test-hooks', which now globs every suite under .githooks/tests. That job's only setup steps are checkout, setup-go and setup-just. THERE IS NO bd ON THAT RUNNER. So a row that shells out to the real bd would redden CI immediately, and a row guarded on 'command -v bd' is a conditional gate whose absent branch is silent -- the shape this repo has been bitten by and which the suites here refuse by policy (see lint-hooks-test.sh's 'an unclassifiable file is refused, not skipped').

So this bead is not closeable inside .githooks/ alone. It needs a decision that belongs with the CI workflow's owner: either install bd in the 'test' job (and accept the cost -- 'bd init' on the embedded Dolt engine took tens of seconds in the probe above, and it would land on every pre-push locally too), or give the real-bd check its own workflow step outside 'just test'. Recording rather than choosing, because ci.yml and the justfile were both other lanes' files tonight.
close_reason: Not closeable inside .githooks/ alone; the surviving half is filed as gqlc-1oe1 and this bead adds nothing beyond it. Verified first-party 2026-08-23 on origin/master c129a0a5: the 'test' job at .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 122-130 has four steps -- checkout, setup-go, setup-just, 'just test' -- and no bd, and 'just test' depends on test-hooks which globs every .githooks/tests/*-test.sh (justfile line 1328). So the suite this bead asks for reddens CI the moment it lands, and a 'command -v bd' guard around it is a conditional gate whose absent branch is silent. The underlying claim was re-measured today and still holds: bd 1.0.4 ce242a879, throwaway workspace under tmp, 'bd update -d' moved updated_at. gqlc-1oe1 carries the two options (install bd in the test job, or a workflow step outside 'just test'), the measured costs, and the falsifier.

title: codegen/neo4j: the decoder scope sweep is blind to a whole entity arm going missing
description:
Measured on PR #858 at 428dfb84, reproduced at fa5dade.

`internal/codegen/neo4j/decoder_test.go`'s `DecoderSuite` derives its scope
reference from an emission and compares that emission against its own
re-emission. Two emitter mutations leave the whole package green:

- drop the decode helper for every edge entity (emit none): `./internal/codegen/neo4j/` rc=0
- emit edge structs with no fields at all:                   `./internal/codegen/neo4j/` rc=0

Why each escapes:

- `structFieldTypesOf` dedupes Go types across all emitted structs, so the node
  arms still carry every Go type the probe's widths claim and the edge loss is
  invisible to `TestProbeDeclaresEveryWidthInEveryArm`'s type comparison.
- `decoderScopeOf` compares an emission to its own reference emission, so

title: resolver: the corpus sweep resolves every cell under regR7, so the registry axis of CALL diagnostics is uncovered
description:
TestCorpusSweepManifest (gqlc-yb0w, PR for #841) crosses 310 fixture queries against 38 fixture schemas, and every one of the 11780 cells is resolved as New(sch, WithRegistry(regR7)). WithRegistry is the resolver's only Option (internal/resolver/resolver.go:48), so the schema axis and the query axis are swept and the registry axis is a constant.

ErrCallArgAssignability and the R7 YIELD column typing arms read the registry. A change to one of those diagnostics that only manifests under a registry other than regR7 — a different signature set, a missing procedure, a different param token — moves no cell in the sweep.

FIX candidates: add a second registry to the cross product (regR7 plus an empty or narrowed registry) and key manifest cells on (query, schema, registry); or bound the claim explicitly and leave the registry axis to the targeted R7 fixtures.

Cost note: the sweep runs 11780 cells in ~0.15s, so a second registry roughly doubles a cheap test and doubles the manifest, which is already 1.4MB.

PROVENANCE: self-review of the gqlc-yb0w branch.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
2026-09-02, agent-j. Claimed. Branch fix/gqlc-2xkf-sweep-registry-axis in
../gqlc-agent-agent-j, cut from origin/master 64692c6a. Design settled by
measurement before writing code:

1. ONE OF THE BEAD'S THREE VARIANTS IS NOT RESOLVER-OBSERVABLE. It offers "a
   different signature set, a missing procedure, a different param token".
   A missing procedure is refused at the PARSER's fail-site — procsig.go:100,
   "a CALL against an empty registry raises ErrUnknownProcedure at the parser's
   fail-site". runSweep parses each query once under cypher.WithRegistry(regR7)
   and asserts require.NoError(..., "query fixture %s must parse"), so a second
   registry lacking a name would ABORT the whole sweep rather than move a cell.
   The registry axis this test can sweep is therefore signature VARIATION under
   the SAME names: perturbed param/result tokens and nullability.

2. THE AXIS IS NARROW. 27 of 334 .cypher fixtures mention CALL, so at most
   ~27 x 40 cells can move; the other ~24k cells of a doubled sweep would be
   byte-identical duplicates. The bead's candidate 1 (add a second registry to
   the cross product, key cells on (query, schema, registry)) doubles a manifest
   the bead itself measures at 1.4MB to buy that.

3. THE BEAD'S CANDIDATE 2 IS ALREADY DONE. sweep_test.go:535-536 already bounds
   the claim in prose and cites this bead by id: "The corpus is the fixtures on
   disk, resolved under regR7, which is the only Option the resolver takes
   (gqlc-2xkf)." So disclosure is not the residue; detection is.

PLANNED SHAPE, smaller than candidate 1 and with no classifier to get wrong:
parameterise runSweep by registry, add regR7Alt (same procedure names, perturbed
tokens/nullability), sweep the full corpus under both, and commit only the cells
whose (verdict, sentinel, detail) DIFFER between the two registries, as its own
small artifact. The big manifest stays flat, no query needs to be classified as
CALL-bearing, and a diagnostic change visible only under another registry moves
a committed row. Cells that stop differing show up under the existing
"in manifest, absent from sweep" category.
2026-09-02, agent-j. Implemented. PR #2258, three commits on
fix/gqlc-2xkf-sweep-registry-axis. Shape as planned above, with three
corrections the work forced.

WHAT SHIPPED. runSweep takes the registry and hands it to the parser AND the
resolver, which are the two routes a registry reaches a cell's outcome by.
regR7Alt is signaturesR7 with every TypeToken rotated one step around the
closed sum and every nullability flipped, DERIVED from signaturesR7 rather
than authored beside it, so procedure names, arities and YIELD field names —
collectCall's three fail-sites — stay identical by construction and cannot
drift a fixture out of parsing. TestSweepRegistryDelta commits the differing
cells to test/data/resolver/sweep.registry-delta.tsv through the manifest's
own row grammar and its own parser. Measured: 944 cells over 23 queries,
110KB against the manifest's 1.4MB.

CORRECTION 1, to my own plan above. I wrote "commit only the cells whose
(verdict, sentinel, detail) DIFFER". That is what it does, but the plan did
not say WHICH SIDE to record. It records the regR7Alt side alone: the regR7
side of every one of those cells is already a manifest row under the same
key, so carrying it would duplicate 944 rows and move this file every time
the manifest moved.

CORRECTION 2. The plan said nothing about non-degeneracy. A delta that went
empty — or one-sided, reaching one route only — would be absorbed by -update
in silence as the new baseline. Two counts now run BEFORE the write, asserted
per route rather than over the delta's size, because a single NotEmpty is
satisfied by either route alone. Measured, each dies against its own route:
unthreading the parse site fails the parser-route count and nothing else;
unthreading the resolve site fails the resolver-route count and nothing else.

CORRECTION 3, a prose claim of mine that was false. The generated header first
said an absent cell is a cell of a query with no CALL clause. Measured: 23 of
the corpus's 27 CALL-bearing queries are in the file. The other four
(part_binding_type_conflict_call_vs_{edge,node,unlabelled}.cypher and
param_witnessless_out_of_scope.cypher) refuse UPSTREAM of the CALL's result
type under both registries, and a refusal text carries no column type. The
header now states the subset relation, and counts its queries off the rows it
heads instead of carrying a hand-written number a regeneration would strand.

MUTATION SCREEN, 10 rows, every one gated on md5 + an anchor check so a
non-applying substitution cannot score SURVIVED. M10 (summary() hardcoding
sweepManifestPath instead of its new parameter) SURVIVED the whole package —
my own miss, introduced in this PR — and is now pinned by driving report()
with a path no constant in the file carries. One row COMPILE-FAILed rather
than killing (M6 orphaned a variable) and one scored PATCH-DID-NOT-APPLY
(M4a, an insertion given a vanish-check); both re-run in a correct shape.
Full table in the PR body.

RESIDUE FILED, not ridden: gqlc-uige8 (P3). BindCall's two "parser drift"
tripwires are query-unreachable AND undriven by any test. This sweep cannot
cover them by construction — a registry dropping a name or an arity aborts at
the parser — so they are not residue this bead can absorb.

(2) The plan had no non-degeneracy check -- a delta gone empty or one-sided would be absorbed by -update in silence -- so two counts now run before the write, asserted PER ROUTE because a single NotEmpty is satisfied by either route alone. title: resolver: the corpus sweep's accept column digests the marshalled model, so a field no MarshalJSON emits is outside it
description:
TestCorpusSweepManifest (gqlc-yb0w, PR for #841) records an accepting cell as a digest of json.Marshal(ValidatedQuery). Every ResolvedType in internal/resolver/validated.go writes its own MarshalJSON emitting an explicit anonymous struct, so the digest reaches exactly the fields those methods list. A field added to a ResolvedType struct but not to its MarshalJSON is invisible to the sweep's accept column.

This is the SAME bound the existing test/data/resolver/valid/*.validated.golden.json files already carry — TestValid marshals through the same methods — so the sweep is not weaker than what shipped, but it is not stronger on this axis either, and the bead it came from (gqlc-yb0w) is about a quadrant compared on too little.

Same family as gqlc-yb0w itself: a guard structural on one axis (which cells) and bounded on another (what a cell's value records).

FIX candidates: a reflect-based census asserting every exported field of every ResolvedType appears in that type's MarshalJSON output for at least one corpus cell; or fold the check into the existing sealed-sum work (PR #881 holds validated.go and sealedsum_test.go, so this must sequence after it).

PROVENANCE: self-review of the gqlc-yb0w branch, filed rather than fixed because validated.go is held by PR #881.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,

meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
EXECUTION (agent-j, 2026-09-02). Branch fix/gqlc-gyp5-sweep-digest-field-census,
commit b95655df. One new file, internal/resolver/marshalcensus_test.go; no
production code changed.

THE DEFECT IS LATENT, NOT LIVE, and I measured that before building anything:
the census passes on the unmutated tree, so no ResolvedType currently declares a
field its MarshalJSON drops. This bead is a guard against the drift, not a
repair of a live miss. Saying so plainly because "0 failures" on a new guard is
otherwise indistinguishable from a guard that cannot fail.

WHAT I DID NOT HAVE TO BUILD, inherited from the gqlc-yb0w/#881 lineage:
sealedsum_test.go already holds an `inhabitants` map of every variant, and its
key set is already checked against the package's own isResolvedType
declarations by TestResolvedTypeSumIsNotClosed/declared_variants. So the census
reuses that map rather than restating the variant list. Restating it would have
reproduced this bead's own defect one level up -- a list that can silently go
short -- and the existing guard already closes that.

THE ONE REAL DESIGN CHOICE, and the row that justifies it. Values are filled
NON-ZERO before marshalling. ADR 0008 puts ,omitempty on new additive axes, so
a field marshalled from a zero value can be legitimately absent; a census over
zero values would read that absence as a missing field and fail a CORRECT type.
nonZero also fails the test on a kind it cannot fill rather than returning the
zero value, because a silent zero would reintroduce the blind spot for exactly
the newest field types.

MUTATION BATTERY. Baseline asserted green first; per-row tripwire on git status
before and after; md5 checked so no row is a no-op; restore verified; every row
screened with `go test -c` so a compiler kill cannot be scored as a catch.
Victims are declared per row and each kill is attributed to ONE subtest, never
to an aggregate.

  M1  ResolvedNode drops nullable        KILLED   by ResolvedNode
  M2  ResolvedProperty drops type        KILLED   by ResolvedProperty
  M3  ResolvedEdgeUnion drops edgeKeys   KILLED   by ResolvedEdgeUnion
  M4  ResolvedList drops element         KILLED   by ResolvedList
  M5  ResolvedScalar drops scalar        KILLED   by ResolvedScalar
  A6  nullable gains ,omitempty          HELD     (allow-pin: no false positive)

M5 is not redundant with M1-M4. ResolvedScalar's field is `Kind` while its
MarshalJSON calls the same thing `Scalar`; only the json TAG agrees. It pins
that the census measures tags rather than Go field names, which is the axis
that actually decides what reaches the digest.

A HARNESS ROW THAT VOUCHED FOR NOTHING, caught and corrected rather than
shipped. My first attempt at the nonZero row blinded the filler while
validated.go was UNMUTATED, and scored HELD. That proves nothing: with no
omitempty anywhere in the unmutated source, zero values still emit every key,
so the row would have read green whether or not nonZero did any work. Re-ran as
a pair over BOTH files:

  H7a  omitempty + nonZero INTACT    PASS   (the filler defeats omitempty)
  H7b  omitempty + nonZero BLINDED   FAIL   (false positive appears; killed by ResolvedNode)

Only H7b establishes that nonZero is load-bearing. This is the second time a
row of mine named one mechanism and exercised another; the tell both times was
a verdict that could not have come out otherwise.

BOUND ON THE CLAIM. The census proves each declared field REACHES the JSON, not
that its VALUE is faithful -- a MarshalJSON emitting the right key from the
wrong source field still passes. And it is deliberately one-directional: it does
not forbid keys the struct does not declare, because "kind" is exactly such a
key and is the point of the tagged-union encoding.

title: check-pr-closes: a malformed Bead: id silently passes the gate
description:
Found by the independent review of PR #867 (/tmp/factory/verdict-867.md), filed as
a nit. PRE-EXISTING -- identical behaviour on master before that branch, so #867
neither introduced nor widened it.

.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py resolves the bead id from a 'Bead:' line in the
PR body, then demands a matching 'Closes #N' for the GH issue that bead mirrors.
If the id does not resolve to a real bead the gate has nothing to demand, and
passes.

Two spellings that reach that state:

  Bead: gqlc-x.        a trailing dot / non-existent suffix
  Bead: `gqlc-w4al`    backticked, so the id carries the backticks

Both are plausible typos rather than deliberate evasion -- markdown-inlining the id
is a natural thing for an author to do -- which is what makes it worth closing. The
failure direction is the wrong one: an unresolvable id should be a refusal that
NAMES the id it could not resolve, not silence.

The gate already fails closed on an unreadable body file and an unreadable export
(shipped in #867), so the fail-closed posture exists and this is a gap in it rather
than a new principle.

ACCEPTANCE. A 'Bead:' line whose id does not resolve against the export makes the
gate exit non-zero with a message naming the unresolved id. A row in
.githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh for each of the two spellings above, and
the suite still FAILs (not merely runs) when the refusal is removed -- 'just
test-hooks' rc=1 propagating to 'just test' rc=1.

CARE. Do not make this reject a PR that legitimately has no bead. The distinction
is 'a Bead: line is present and does not resolve' vs 'no Bead: line at all', and
the branch-name fallback path must keep working.
notes:
ROUND 2 pushed: 3098b3af on fix/closes-gate-opt-out (PR #901), bundled with gqlc-1ekq.

The malformed-id half is unchanged by round 2 and still holds: a 'Bead:' or
'Refs:' line whose id does not match BEAD_ID is a refusal that NAMES the token.
Rows: backticked id on a Bead line, trailing full stop, backticked id on a Refs
line, backticked id after 'bead:' in prose, sub-bead id with a dot still accepted,
'Bead:' naming no id at all is not a declaration.

Round 2 added the row 'an absent id on a Bead line overrides a mirrored branch',
which pins the OTHER direction: a WELL-FORMED id that the export does not carry
still takes the not-in-export pass, on any branch. That is a bypass, and it is
now disclosed in the code comment and in the PR body rather than only implied.

DEVIATION NOT YET ON GH #883 (flagged for the coordinator at merge, do not
hand-edit): the acceptance text on #883 says an unresolvable id 'makes the gate
refuse'. The branch refuses a MALFORMED id and deliberately keeps passing a

stated in the PR body.

title: resolver: describeColumnType panics on a nil list element, the in-package twin of edze's prepare.go fault
description:
Found while auditing `internal/resolver`'s `ResolvedType` type switches for
`gqlc-856f`. Recorded here rather than fixed because the nil posture belongs to
`gqlc-edze`, which `gqlc-856f` was explicitly scoped out of deciding.

`describeColumnType` (`internal/resolver/resolve.go:363`) has a default arm
that returns `t.String()`. That refuses gracefully for a pointer or embedded
form — which is why `gqlc-856f`'s audit passed it — but its `ResolvedList` arm
recurses on `v.Element`, and a nil `Element` is a nil interface, which matches
no arm and reaches `t.String()` on nil.

Measured at 52f8662 via `go test -overlay` (no file added to the tree):

    describeColumnType(ResolvedList{Element: nil})
      -> PANIC: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

`resolvedTypeEqual` is safe on the same input — its `a == nil || b == nil`
guard catches the recursion — and returns false:

    resolvedTypeEqual(ResolvedList{Element: nil}, ResolvedList{Element: ResolvedNode{}}) = false

The two compose into the fault path: `compareBranchColumns`
(`resolve.go:~2050`) calls `describeColumnType` only for columns
`resolvedTypeEqual` reported unequal, so a nil-element list on one branch and a
populated list on the other reaches the panic while building the mismatch
message.

## Reachability: latent, not live

No originator was found. All three `ResolvedList{...}` constructions in
non-test code assign a non-nil `Element`:

- `scope.go:1004` — `ResolvedEdge` or `ResolvedEdgeUnion`
- `resolve.go:1294` — the result of `resolveType`
- `resolve.go:1458` — the result of `unify`

`unify` will *propagate* a nil: `unify(ResolvedUnknown{}, nil)` returns
`(nil, true)`, so `ResolvedList{Element: nil}` is constructible at
`resolve.go:1458` from an already-nil element. That is propagation, not
origination. `describeColumnType` is unexported and reached only through the
resolver's own pipeline, so this is not reachable by an out-of-package caller
the way `internal/codegen`'s sites are.

## Relationship to gqlc-edze

`gqlc-edze` already owns `resolver.ResolvedList{Element: nil}` faulting at
`internal/codegen/prepare.go:1050`, plus the eight typed-nil pointer forms.
This is the same question one package earlier. If `edze` chooses normalisation
at the boundary, this site may be covered for free; if it chooses refusal, this
default arm needs a nil check of its own. Fold into `edze` if it is being taken
whole.

## Acceptance

Either `describeColumnType`'s default distinguishes a nil interface from a type
it does not recognise, or `edze` records that the resolver's own pipeline
cannot originate a nil element and this stays latent by argument rather than by
accident. A regression pin either way.

title: codegen: the .cypher.go suffix arm still admits a file only one fixture emits
description:
`internal/codegen/prepare_test.go` (`TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet`, PR #845) now measures which side of the emitted-file partition a basename sits on: a basename more than one fixture emits, and an exported name every one of those fixtures declares, is a name that does not follow from the batch, so its file must be in `fixedDeclarationFiles`. That closes the `helpers.cypher.go` escape — a new emitted file ending `.cypher.go` written into every golden — because `Helper` then reaches 83/83 fixtures and the guard names the file.

THE RESIDUAL HOLE IS THE ONE-FIXTURE BASENAME. The measurement needs two fixtures to have any evidence at all, so a basename exactly one fixture emits is skipped. Today those are `directory.cypher.go` and `people.cypher.go`, both from the `multi_source_files` fixture, both genuinely input-derived (`AllPersonIds`, `PersonNameById`). Measured out-of-tree over the 642 committed goldens:

    db.go               fixtures=83  New/WithTx/Queries at 83/83     -> fixed, measured
    graph.go            fixtures=45  SessionInit/EnsureGraph/DropGraph at 45/45 -> fixed, measured
    querier.go          fixtures=83  Querier/ReadQuerier/WriteQuerier at 83/83  -> fixed, measured
    models.go           fixtures=83  top name Person 62/83           -> no full name, correctly skipped
    queries.cypher.go   fixtures=71  top name GetAction 5/71         -> no full name, correctly skipped
    directory.cypher.go fixtures=1   AllPersonIds 1/1                -> SKIPPED, n<2
    people.cypher.go    fixtures=1   PersonNameById 1/1              -> SKIPPED, n<2

So an emitter that grew a fourth fixed file ending `.cypher.go` AND enrolled exactly one fixture for it would still leave the sweep silently. The suffix arm names no file, which is what makes it the only arm with this width; the two map arms are pinned name by name.

FIX DIRECTION: either enumerate the query-source stems the corpus carries (a fourth hand-maintained list, which cuts against gqlc-qx5p's RELATED note), or read the per-source query file names from the fixtures' own query source files rather than from a suffix, so the arm admits exactly the files the batch's sources justify.

ACCEPTANCE: a fourth emitted file ending `.cypher.go`, written into the golden targets of exactly one fixture with a declaration no `reservedIdentifiers` row holds, turns a NAMED test red, with `go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/` clean before the test runs.

exit status: `git show origin/master:internal/codegen/prepare_test.go` carries

## The fix

Test-only, one file. No generator or emitter behaviour change.

`TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet`'s third partition arm was a bare
suffix: any emitted file ending `.cypher.go` was classified input-derived and
never read, whatever it declared. The suffix now says only what SHAPE a file
has. What admits it is a query source of that name in its OWN fixture directory
— `people.cypher` justifies `people.cypher.go` and nothing else does.

That evidence is per file rather than counted across fixtures, which is exactly
what closes the n=1 hole: the fix direction the bead offered second ("read the
per-source query file names from the fixtures' own query source files rather
than from a suffix") rather than the first, which would have added a fourth
hand-maintained list against gqlc-qx5p's RELATED note.

## Measured before writing anything

166 emitted per-source goldens across the corpus, every one justified by a
`.cypher` source beside its fixture's manifest.json. Zero unjustified. No
fixture keeps its query sources anywhere but the fixture directory top level,
so the tightened arm reds nothing standing today.

## Acceptance criterion

The bead asked for: a fourth emitted file ending `.cypher.go`, written into the
golden targets of exactly one fixture with a declaration no reservedIdentifiers
row holds, turning a NAMED test red, with `go test -c -o /dev/null
./internal/codegen/` clean before the test runs. That is row 1 below, and it
names both the file and the source it looked for.

## Mutation battery

Four rows, each compiler-kill screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null
./internal/codegen/`, which reported clean on all four before the test ran.

| # | mutant | declared victim | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `helpers.cypher.go` declaring `Helper` planted in ONE fixture's golden targets, no `helpers.cypher` source | the per-source justification require | KILLED |
| 2 | `people.cypher.go` declaring `PlantedName` planted in a fixture with no `people.cypher`, while multi_source_files legitimately has one | same require | KILLED |
| 3 | `perSource++` -> `perSource += 0` | the NotZero liveness fence on the new arm | KILLED |
| 4 | `querySourceOf`'s filepath.Dir nesting one level short, reading `golden/` as the fixture dir | the per-source justification require | KILLED |

Rows 1 and 2 were also run against the guard BEFORE the change, where both
SURVIVED: the package reported ok with the planted file in the tree and no test
named. That pair of runs is the hole re-derived at my own HEAD rather than
inherited from the bead's text.

Row 2 is the row that separates this implementation from a weaker one. A
justification looked up across the whole corpus instead of per fixture would
survive it, since `people.cypher` does exist — in a different fixture. Row 4
pins the fixture-directory derivation, which nothing else reads. Row 3 stops the
new arm from being a check that admits nothing.

## The round-6 caveat: deliberately NOT acted on

The notes warned that target-qualifying goldenFixture's key "has to land with
whatever closes this bead". It did not, and that is the right outcome rather
than an omission. The n>=2 everywhere-name loop is a SECOND, independent
measurement, untouched here; target-qualifying the key still puts
directory.cypher.go and people.cypher.go at two fixtures with an everywhere-name
apiece and still demands they enter fixedDeclarationFiles, though both are
genuinely input-derived. So the key is still unsafe to change. What this bead
removed is the reason to want to change it. Both facts are now stated in
TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet's doc comment, which no longer
describes this hole as open.

title: ci: a selective tidy re-run can leave lint/test/codegen-fence 'skipped' and mergeable
description:
Witnessed while landing gqlc-w4al (PR #867), 2026-08-17.

OBSERVED. On PR #867 at head e9119f75 I removed the 'Closes #617' line. Run 32005420996 fired on the edit; its tidy job failed. Because lint, test and codegen-fence all declare 'needs: [actionlint, tidy]', GitHub marked all three SKIPPED, and a skipped check run has conclusion 'skipped', which branch protection reads as a PASS. Rollup at that moment:

  tidy    COMPLETED FAILURE   <- newest, blocks
  lint    COMPLETED SKIPPED
  test    COMPLETED SKIPPED
  codegen-fence COMPLETED SKIPPED

That state itself is safe: tidy is red and blocks the merge.

THE HOLE. gqlc-w4al made tidy re-passable at an UNCHANGED SHA (the gate now reads the live PR body over the API, so adding the Closes line back turns tidy green with no new commit). That creates a sequence that was previously unreachable:

  1. head H, body missing Closes -> run R1: actionlint ok, tidy RED, lint/test/codegen-fence SKIPPED.
     Note lint/test have now never run at H.
  2. Add the Closes line. Run R2 fires on 'edited' and would re-run everything -- CANCEL it.
  3. Re-run ONLY the tidy job of R1 ('gh run rerun <R1> --job <tidy>'). It fetches the live body, passes.
  4. Newest per context: tidy SUCCESS, actionlint SUCCESS, lint/test/codegen-fence SKIPPED (= pass).
     Mergeable green, with lint and test never having executed at H.

Before gqlc-w4al this was not reachable: the only tidy failure fixable without a push was the body gate, and the body gate could not re-evaluate at all. Every other tidy failure (tidy-check, bd-export-monotonic) needs a commit, which moves the SHA and re-runs everything.

SEVERITY. Requires deliberate action by someone with write access: cancelling a run and selectively re-running one job. It is a bypass vector, not an accidental green. Step 3 is exactly the command I ran as the stale-payload witness, so it is not hypothetical -- I ran 'gh run rerun 32004817300 --job 95312044713' and got a fresh tidy check run on the same SHA.

SHAPE OF A FIX (pick one, all have costs):
- Drop 'needs: [actionlint, tidy]' from lint/test/codegen-fence. Loses the cheap-gates-first saving that the ci.yml header comment justifies (~3.5 min of runner time on a trivial formatting miss).
- Move the PR-body gate into its own job with no dependents. Needs a new required context added to BOTH protection configs (classic branch protection and the 'protect-master' ruleset), which strands every open PR on a pending context until they are updated -- the same objection recorded in gqlc-2rli.
- Add 'if: always()' to the dependents so they run and report a real verdict even when a gate fails. Costs the runner time the needs: chain was there to save.

ACCEPTANCE. A test that reaches the state in step 4 and asserts it is not mergeable, or a workflow shape where a skipped dependent cannot be the newest verdict for a required context at a SHA where the job never ran.

RELATED. gqlc-2rli (separate-workflow shape + protection-config steps). The 'skipped reads as a pass' fact is already documented in ci.yml's trigger comment and in vuln.yml.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-17, from the independent review of PR #867 (/tmp/factory/verdict-867.md).

1. A SECOND HYPOTHESIS I RELAYED IS FALSE. I had suggested to the reviewer that a
   path filter on ci.yml could produce the same skipped triple without any re-run,
   which would make this bug far wider (a routine PR-description edit would suffice).
   It does not. Measured: the 'needs:' lines are byte-identical to master, tidy
   failed at 07:21:35 and the dependents skipped at 07:21:36. The cause is only
   ever the needs: chain with a failed gate. The bead's own mechanism paragraph
   was right; my widening was wrong. Severity stays "deliberate action required".

2. THE RE-RUN SEMANTICS IN STEP 3 NEED RE-MEASURING. The reviewer found that
   attempt 2 of run 32004817300 shows lint/test/codegen-fence with NEW job ids and
   NEW 07:22:30 timestamps, while actionlint carried over unchanged at 07:12:54.
   So 'gh run rerun --job <one>' RE-CREATES the dependents and RE-EVALUATES needs:,
   rather than leaving the old skipped runs standing. In that attempt they skipped
   again only because tidy had failed. Step 4 of the sequence above therefore
   assumes something not yet demonstrated: that after a SUCCESSFUL selective tidy
   re-run, the re-created dependents are still skipped rather than executed. If
   they execute, the bypass does not exist and this bead should be closed. That
   case was NOT run end-to-end by anyone; the reviewer states its account of it is
   inference from job records, not execution.

3. THE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE IS UNVERIFIED. "a skipped check run ... branch
   protection reads as a PASS" is asserted here as fact and is repeated in ci.yml's
   trigger comment and in vuln.yml. Nobody has probed it live, and the reviewer
   found ZERO recorded cases across 40 merged PRs of a required context whose
   newest run was skipped. If GitHub in fact treats skipped as unsatisfied, this
   bead is empty. Settle this BEFORE building any of the three fixes -- all three
   cost real runner time or strand every open PR on a pending context.

WHAT SURVIVES REGARDLESS. The merge-precondition rule is unaffected and is the
durable output: evaluate newest check run per context over the seven required
contexts and require SUCCESS, rejecting SKIPPED, NEUTRAL and CANCELLED. Under any
resolution of (3) that query is correct, because a dependency-skip at a SHA where
the job never ran is exactly the state a coordinator must not read as green.

## 2026-08-17 — the load-bearing premise is SETTLED, and it is TRUE

This bead rested on an unverified premise: does GitHub treat a required status
check whose conclusion is `skipped` as SATISFYING the requirement? If it did not,
this bead was empty. It does.

VENDOR-DOCUMENTED (docs.github.com, "About protected branches", read 2026-08-17):

  "Required status checks must have a `successful`, `skipped`, or `neutral`
   status before collaborators can make changes to a protected branch."

So `skipped` and `neutral` both satisfy a required context. The bead is real.

MEASURED alongside it, and worth recording because it explains why nobody has hit
this yet: across the **40 most recent merged PRs**, the only context ever
newest-and-skipped is `live-smoke-age`, which is NOT one of the seven required
contexts. Zero merged PRs have a required context skipped-newest. So the hazard
is documented but has never fired here — untested in practice, not disproven.

Query used (newest run per context, per merged PR head SHA):

  gh api "repos/areqag/gqlc/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" --jq \
    '[.check_runs[] | {n:.name,c:.conclusion,s:.started_at}] | group_by(.n)
     | map(max_by(.s)) | .[] | select(.c=="skipped") | .n'

Required contexts confirmed first-party from
`repos/areqag/gqlc/branches/master/protection`: lint, test, tidy, actionlint,
govulncheck, live-smoke, codegen-fence. `strict:false`.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY MERGE GATE, human or automated: a rollup that accepts
"not FAILURE" is wrong. SKIPPED and NEUTRAL must be rejected explicitly, because
GitHub will merge them and they represent a check that did not run.
## 2026-08-18 — BOTH QUESTIONS SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT. THE BYPASS IS NOT REACHABLE.

Q2 decides the bead, so it goes first.

### Q2 — after a SUCCESSFUL selective re-run of the gate job, are the re-created dependents still skipped? NO. THEY EXECUTE.

Instrument: throwaway branch `probe/xdd0-rerun-semantics` carrying one
push-triggered workflow (ci.yml's push trigger is `branches: [master]`, and
vuln.yml / codegen-live.yml are pull_request-or-schedule, so nothing else fired
and no PR was needed). Shape mirrors ci.yml: `preflight` stands in for
actionlint and is always green; `gate` stands in for tidy and is
`test "$ATTEMPT" != "1"`, i.e. red on attempt 1 and green on any re-run at an
UNCHANGED SHA — the same "flips verdict with no new commit" property gqlc-w4al
gave tidy by moving the body read to the API; `dependent-a` and `dependent-b`
carry `needs: [preflight, gate]` and stand in for lint / test / codegen-fence.

SHA f8301f585a747f78c242a9b15b8c8ff0a74c5fa2, run 32149913422.

Attempt 1 reproduces step 1 of the DESCRIPTION:

    gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/actions/runs/32149913422/attempts/1/jobs \
      --jq '.jobs[]|[.id,.name,.status,.conclusion,.started_at]|@tsv'
    95752916435  gate         completed  failure  2026-08-18T14:41:53Z
    95752916682  preflight    completed  success  2026-08-18T14:41:53Z
    95752961106  dependent-b  completed  skipped  2026-08-18T14:41:57Z
    95752963110  dependent-a  completed  skipped  2026-08-18T14:41:58Z

Step 3 of the DESCRIPTION, run verbatim:

    gh run rerun 32149913422 --job 95752916435

Attempt 2 — the state step 4 assumed and nobody had executed:

    gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/actions/runs/32149913422/attempts/2/jobs \
      --jq '.jobs[]|[.id,.name,.status,.conclusion,.started_at]|@tsv'
    95753853667  gate         completed  success  2026-08-18T14:44:35Z
    95753854577  preflight    completed  success  2026-08-18T14:41:53Z
    95753885061  dependent-b  completed  success  2026-08-18T14:44:42Z
    95753885089  dependent-a  completed  success  2026-08-18T14:44:42Z

`dependent-a`'s log carries `dependent-a EXECUTED on attempt 2`. `preflight` is
the carry-over the earlier reviewer described: a new job id (95753854577, was
95752916682) keeping attempt 1's 14:41:53 timestamp.

And the SHA's check-run list afterwards holds no skipped row — the skipped runs
are replaced, not left standing beside the new ones:

    gh api "repos/areqag/gqlc/commits/f8301f585a747f78c242a9b15b8c8ff0a74c5fa2/check-runs?per_page=100" \
      --jq '.check_runs[]|[.id,.name,.status,.conclusion,.started_at]|@tsv'
    95753885089  dependent-a  completed  success
    95753885061  dependent-b  completed  success
    95753854577  preflight    completed  success
    95753853667  gate         completed  success

So step 4 does not occur. A selective re-run that turns the gate green
re-creates the dependents and runs them, and a skipped dependent cannot be left
as the newest verdict for its context by that route. **The bead is empty and
should be closed as such.** Note 2 above was right to demand this measurement.

### The neighbouring route step 2 gestures at ("CANCEL it") is also closed

If a cancelled run's dependents concluded `skipped`, they would satisfy
protection (see Q1) and the bypass would exist by a route the DESCRIPTION does
not name. In ci.yml the dependents are dispatched as soon as actionlint and
tidy pass, so the reachable cancel window is one where they are in progress.
Reproduced at 4efb277b58a76ae0ee2bc11fa800dbf531904a7e, run 32150832229:
`gate` fast-green, dependents `needs: [gate]` running `sleep 180`; waited for
both to reach in_progress, then `gh run cancel 32150832229`:

    gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/actions/runs/32150832229/jobs \
      --jq '.jobs[]|[.name,.status,.conclusion]|@tsv'
    gate         completed  success
    dependent-a  completed  cancelled
    dependent-b  completed  cancelled

`cancelled`, not `skipped`. That the `cancelled` conclusion then blocks is
GitHub's documentation, not something measured here.

### Q1 — does branch protection treat a skipped required check run as satisfied? YES, and it is now measured rather than cited.

Note 3 above, and the 2026-08-17 note under it, rested on docs.github.com.
Disposable PR #1015 (closed, branch deleted) put it on an instrument. One edit:
`if: ${{ false }}` on ci.yml's `actionlint` job, which skips actionlint and,
through `needs: [actionlint, tidy]`, lint / test / codegen-fence too. tidy,
govulncheck and live-smoke were left to run. Head
b10e89bae937ff530cc5def23248a3b520a69be8:

    gh api "repos/areqag/gqlc/commits/b10e89bae937ff530cc5def23248a3b520a69be8/check-runs?per_page=100" \
      --jq '.check_runs[]|[.name,.status,.conclusion]|@tsv'
    test            completed  skipped
    lint            completed  skipped
    codegen-fence   completed  skipped
    live-smoke-age  completed  skipped
    actionlint      completed  skipped
    govulncheck     completed  success
    live-smoke      completed  success
    tidy            completed  success

    gh pr view 1015 --repo areqag/gqlc --json mergeStateStatus,mergeable
    {"mergeStateStatus":"CLEAN","mergeable":"MERGEABLE"}

lint, test and actionlint are required by the classic protection list AND by
the `protect-master` ruleset; codegen-fence by the classic list. GitHub reports
the PR CLEAN with each of their newest — and only — check runs concluded
`skipped`. The 40-merged-PR survey found no natural witness because no required
context had been skipped-newest here before; this is one.

### What this means for the prose carriers

Q1 holding means nothing in the tree is falsified. `ci.yml:18`,
`codegen-live.yml:51` ("GitHub counts a skipped check as satisfying a required
context", over `live-smoke-age`), and the require-messages in
`internal/tools/ciguard/workflow_test.go`, `testhooks_test.go` and
`golangci_cache_test.go` all say the same thing and all remain correct. No
correction PR is owed on them, and the ciguard guards that forbid a job-level
`if:` on the required jobs are guarding a real hazard.

Two imprecisions in this bead's own RELATED paragraph, corrected here rather
than left to be re-derived: `vuln.yml` does not carry the skipped-satisfies
claim — it says required checks are matched by name with no conditional
primitive, which is a different statement — and `codegen-live.yml` is a carrier
the paragraph does not name.

`gqlc-2rli` already records that the classic list and the ruleset differ (the
ruleset omits live-smoke and codegen-fence), re-verified today, so nothing new
is filed for it.

### What this does not settle

- plain `gh run rerun <id>` and `gh run rerun <id> --failed` were not run
- a dependent cancelled before it is dispatched at all: I could not reach that
  state without also leaving a non-success row on a job it `needs:`, which
  blocks for its own reason
- whether GitHub rejects `cancelled` and `timed_out` — documentation only
- both re-run measurements were on push-triggered runs; the Q1 measurement was
  on a pull_request run

### What survives, unchanged

The merge-precondition rule in the note above: evaluate the newest check run
per context over the required contexts and require SUCCESS, rejecting SKIPPED,
NEUTRAL and CANCELLED. Q1 is exactly why — GitHub will merge a skipped required
context, and PR #1015 is the demonstration.
close_reason: Investigated, not a defect. The selective re-run in step 3 re-creates the dependents and RUNS them once the gate goes green (run 32149913422 attempt 2: both dependents success, no skipped row left at the SHA), so step 4 is not reachable by that route. Q1 was settled in the affirmative and by measurement rather than citation (PR #1015, closed): four required contexts newest-and-skipped, mergeStateStatus CLEAN. No prose carrier is falsified, so no correction PR is owed. Commands and raw output in NOTES.

title: ci: sweep-discovery-probes only recognises mktemp -d as a probe site
description:
`sweep-discovery-probes` (justfile) holds three copies of the probe names to
each other: the `*_probe` variables, the `discovery_probes` concatenation, and
the sites that create the probes. It discovers sites by grepping `just --dump`
for one idiom:

    site_re="mktemp -d ""test/data/"

So a probe directory created under test/data by anything other than
`mktemp -d` — `mkdir -p`, `install -d`, a Go helper this justfile invokes, a
test using t.TempDir with a TMPDIR pointed at test/data — is not a site to any
check in the recipe. The declared names are not held to it, the site-shape
refusal does not see it, and if its spelling is not one of the declared names
the sweep glob does not clear it either.

Not currently reachable: at the time of filing the only three probe sites in
the justfile are `mktemp -d test/data/{{ var }}.XXXXXX` (justfile:721, :832,
:1191, PR #833 head). This is a limit of the check, stated in the tree beside
`site_re`, not a live defect.

Closing it means either (a) discovering sites from the paths that actually
appear under test/data at runtime rather than from the justfile text, or
(b) moving the probe creation behind one recipe/helper that the other recipes
call, so there is one site to hold rather than a pattern to match.
close_reason: Closed by PR #1334. Option (a) in spirit: alloc_re enumerates the allocators rather than matching mktemp -d alone, and the enumeration is backed by a refusal so it is not a list taken on trust — a line naming a probe variable beside test/data through an unrecognised command now FAILS. Differential evidence: an identical mkdir -p site exits one under the new guard and zero under the reverted one. What remains out of reach, a probe made by code the justfile only calls, is stated beside site_re.

title: lint: the justfile's shell is not shellchecked by any gate
description:
`just lint` runs `lint-hooks`, whose default argument is `dir=".githooks"` (justfile: `lint-hooks dir=".githooks"`, and `lint: ensure-golangci lint-hooks check-golangci-build-tags`). So every line of bash in the justfile itself — including the whole `vuln` recipe, several hundred lines of it, which is the body of a required CI context — has no static analysis behind it.

Witness: extract the `vuln` recipe body and run the repo's own `.bin/shellcheck` 0.10.0 over it. It parses and reports SC2015 (info) on `lines() { [ -n "${1}" ] && printf '%s\\n' "${1}" || true; }`. Nothing in CI does that run, so the finding has been sitting there unreported.

The fix is not simply widening `lint-hooks` to the justfile: a just recipe body is not a shell script on disk (interpolation braces, per-recipe shebangs, dedent), so it needs an extraction step first. Scope: extract each shebang recipe body, shellcheck it, fail the gate on new findings, and either clear or baseline the pre-existing SC2015.

Found while reviewing PR #846 (bd gqlc-u91z), which added ~130 lines of unlinted bash to that recipe.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of gqlc-wprl, which is the survivor and is OPEN and in_progress (assignee areqag, started 2026-08-23T05:55:59Z) — read back with 'bd show gqlc-wprl --json' before and after this close. Same defect, same remedy: 'just lint' runs lint-hooks whose default is dir=".githooks" (verified on origin/master, justfile:552 'lint-hooks dir=".githooks"'), so every shebang recipe body in the justfile is outside shellcheck; both beads ask for an extraction step plus a gate that FAILS. gqlc-wprl is the richer record: it carries the per-recipe shellcheck run at warning severity, the pre-existing ERROR at justfile:130 with its cause (a comment beginning '# shellcheck' parsed as a directive between case items) and the one-line reword that clears it. k4h7's only unique datum — SC2015 on the vuln recipe's lines() helper — is already reproduced in wprl's notes and judged intentional. A pointer note recording this close has been appended to gqlc-wprl.

title: vuln: ten assertions guarding the unplaced-stdlib grading are killed by nothing
description:
In `just vuln`, ten assertions that guard the unplaced-stdlib grading are killed
by no mutation, on either toolchain arm. Each passes on a good tree, so
neutering it changes nothing observable.

Measured first-party at `c7bee5cb` (PR #846). Each row applies ONE edit, asserts
the edit is LIVE (`diff` vs pristine, non-empty), asserts the artifact stayed
VALID (`just --summary` parses it AND the extracted 659-line recipe body passes
`bash -n`), runs `just vuln`, then restores by md5 and verifies the restore.

- M9: `expect_refusal`'s marker check `*"${marker}"*)` -> `*)` — SURVIVED rc=0.
  The clause that asserts WHICH refusal fired can be deleted; M8 and M11 are
  killed by it today, so it is live, but nothing regresses it.
- M13: delete the first `expect_refusal` call (bare 'go') — SURVIVED rc=0.
- M14: delete the second `expect_refusal` call (absent header) — SURVIVED rc=0.
- M16: the witness-quotes-the-header `case` -> `*) ;;` — SURVIVED rc=0.
- MW: the witness's two-line acceptance contract
  `[ "${accepted}" != "${witness_where}"$'\n'"${placed_header}" ]` -> `if false`
  — SURVIVED rc=0. MH and MI are killed by it, so it is live.
- M19: the per-module tally guard `if [ -n "${ungraded}" ]` -> `if false` —
  SURVIVED rc=0.
- MA: the tally's `comm -13` -> `comm -23`, so the guard mis-answers while
  looking intact — SURVIVED rc=0. Deletion is not the only shape this family
  takes; mis-direction is uncovered too.
- MG: the call site's header match
  `if ! grep -qxF -- "${graded_line}" <<<"${out}"` -> `if false` — SURVIVED
  rc=0. MF, MJ, MK and MN are killed by it, so it is live.
- ML: the same match's `grep -qxF` -> `grep -qF`, whole-line weakened to
  substring — SURVIVED rc=0. MF still dies under it, so the anchoring itself is
  not what MF turns on.
- MP: the same match's haystack `<<<"${out}"` -> `<<<"${stdlib_graded}"`, so the
  assertion compares the acceptance against itself — SURVIVED rc=0. This is the
  argument-replacement shape that produced MF one line up; here it makes the
  assertion tautological rather than opening the gate, because
  `refuse_unplaced_stdlib` is still reading the real `${out}` and its own
  refusal still fires. Substituting a name that does not exist is fail-closed
  instead: the recipe runs under `set -u`.

## Correction

The first version of this bead, and row B19 of PR #846's matrix, both said M19
"IS killed under `GOVERSION=go1.26.5-X:nodwarf5`, row B19, by the grading's own
exit". That is false, and it measures false:

    diff 846r4z-B0.log 846r4z-bl-M19.log | wc -l   ->   0

Byte-identical to the unmutated blind run. That run is red because the TREE is
blind — the grading's own refusal fires and exits long before the tally is
reached — not because the mutation was detected. Under this recipe's own
screening rule, that a kill must NAME the thing the mutation broke, B19 is not a
kill. The blind arm distinguishes M13, M14, M16, MA, MG, MW, ML and MP no
better: every one of them produces a log 0 diff lines from the blind baseline.
Of that arm's rows only M3, M17 and MF differ from it (270, 269 and 18 lines),
and only those three are kills there.

So the gap is not "killed on the other arm". It is killed by nothing, on either
arm, and that is its real size.

## Why it is still second-order

Every clause above is demonstrably load-bearing on the paths that do run, and
the two guards added for the header match cover disjoint mutants — the witness
kills MH and MI (the accepting arm dropping a line), the call-site match kills
MF, MJ, MK and MN (the arm or the call site reading the wrong string). What is
missing is the regress: nothing fails when one of them is removed.

What two of them removed together costs is measured, not asserted, and the two
pairs do not cost the same thing. Both are the M4 class: two deliberate edits,
disclosed here.

- Row MX applies MF and MG at once and is **rc=0 under
  `GOVERSION=go1.26.5-X:nodwarf5`**, with zero `error:` lines and both headers
  reading `... and the go standard library:`. That is the gate itself open —
  the blind toolchain accepted.
- Row MY applies MH and MW at once. On a release toolchain it is rc=0, with
  `graded_line` empty and `grep -qxF -- ""` matching one of the 13 blank lines
  in govulncheck's output. On the blind arm it is **rc=1, and 0 diff lines from
  the unmutated blind run** — `refuse_unplaced_stdlib` still refuses, naming the
  module and quoting the header. So MY destroys the tie between a grading and
  the scan it read while leaving the gate closed. It is the weaker of the two.

Same family as gqlc-65sl (every `selftest_*` call site in this recipe) and
gqlc-eo46 (`refuse_stale` proven to work and never proven to be called). 4 of
the 5 live `comm -13` guards in this justfile predate PR #846.
notes:
Two more survivors, found by the independent review of PR #846 at 925ca385 and
NOT in the 46-row matrix this bead was filed from. Both SURVIVE rc=0 on the
release arm and are NOT-DISTINGUISHED on the blind arm:

- R1: the accepting arm emits "${scan}" instead of "${line}".
- R9: graded_line is read from <<<"${out}".

Reproduce: /tmp/factory/lin846r5-mut.sh R1 /tmp/factory/lin846r5-edit-R1.py -> R1: rc=0.

Both belong to the already-disclosed two-edit MX class, so neither widens the
defect; they widen the survivor set. This bead makes no exhaustiveness claim and
the count above should not be read as one.

The witness's blind spot has a name and should carry it: the witness cannot see
any grading behaviour that varies with anything in the header line other than the
token, because its fabricated headers differ from a real scan only in the module
count (2 vs 43/54). That is what row R7 establishes.

Two adjacent prose nits from the same review, for whoever takes this:
docs/adr/0026:256 carries an unscoped "every invocation" where justfile:1432-1436
scopes the same claim to the recipe; docs/adr/0026:241's "...and the go standard
library: is exactly and only the unplaced rendering" is true on v1.7.0 but states
its scope 200 lines away at 439-444.

title: codegen/age: the live battery never writes an offset sidecar
description:
DEFECT: the AGE live smoke battery exercises the instant round trip but never puts an <f>Offset property in the graph, so the emitted agtypeZone is only ever live-witnessed on its absent-key branch. Neither the in-range zoned read nor the refusal added by gqlc-x5wx (PR #848) has a live witness — both are pinned only by the corpus harness, which runs the emitted helpers against hand-built props maps rather than against agtype coming back from Apache AGE.

WITNESS: run 32000835738 (codegen-live, headSha 619c7186) is green with live-smoke-age success. The scenario it drives is readScenarios' "timestamp_property_roundtrip: instant round trip + ordering" (test/data/codegen/live_age_test.go), whose oneEvent CREATE binds the instant alone. grep for "Offset" across test/data/codegen returns no write. So the live arm proves the absent-sidecar path returns the instant unchanged in UTC, and says nothing about the two paths PR #848 changed.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a live scenario whose CREATE sets both the instant property and its <f>Offset sidecar, asserting (a) an in-range offset comes back as the zone on the decoded time.Time, and (b) an out-of-range one (86400) fails the decode with an error naming the property. The second half needs the harness to admit an expected-error scenario, which readScenarios does not model today.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #1381, squashed onto master as sha e08ceea5. Verified on master: test/data/codegen/live_age_zone_test.go is present (note the path is under test/data/codegen/, not internal/codegen/age/ as the PR prose implies). The live write battery bound the instant alone, so every live run had only ever reached agtypeZone's absent-key branch; the in-range zone and the out-of-range refusal were pinned by the corpus harness calling the emitted helper against a hand-built props map, never against agtype returned by Apache AGE. The new test seeds the sidecar through the driver and reads it back through the emitted OneEvent, pinning the exclusive bound one second either side on both signs, a non-integer sidecar, the nullable instant's own sidecar, and a sidecar with no instant beside it. Enrolment matters as much as the test: master carries TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt in internal/liverecipes, which fails the tree unless both new names appear in the test-codegen-live-age -run allowlist. I closed this bead, not the lane, which was killed after merging. NOT verified by me: no live run has been dispatched, so the new rows have executed nowhere -- they are enrolled and compiling, not witnessed.

title: codegen/age: agtypeInstant takes any int64 as epoch-micros
description:
DEFECT: the emitted agtypeInstant (internal/codegen/age/render_models.go) reads the stored int64 and calls time.UnixMicro on it with no bound, so a property holding math.MaxInt64 decodes to a year ~294000 instant and is returned without error. Sibling of gqlc-x5wx, which bounded the <f>Offset sidecar.

WITNESS: the emitted helper is

	micros, err := agtypeInt64(raw)
	...
	return time.UnixMicro(micros).UTC(), nil

with no range test between the two. The corpus test TestAgtypeZoneRefusesAnOffsetOutsideADay (internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt) refuses math.MaxInt64 as an offset; the same value as micros is accepted by agtypeInstant.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED ON PR #848 rather than fixed there: the two are not the same shape.
1. The micros count IS the instant. Any bound on it is a calendar-range policy decision, not a well-formedness one, and there is no equivalent of "a zone no clock keeps" to key it on. The live corpus deliberately carries year 9999 and pre-epoch instants (test/data/codegen/valid/timestamp_property_roundtrip), so any candidate bound has to be argued against rows that already exist.
2. gqlc's own encode writes the micros. It is a value this encoding produced and read back, so it is not the untrusted external input the sidecar is — the sidecar is the interop affordance for graphs gqlc did not write.

Reachability is therefore lower and the fix needs a policy decision (what calendar range does this backend admit?) that belongs in its own bead, not smuggled into a bounds fix.
notes:
CORRECTION (PR #848 round 3) to 'WHY IT WAS DEFERRED' point 2. The bead stands; one clause in it does not.

WITHDRAWN, false: 'the sidecar is the interop affordance for graphs gqlc did not write.' A query whose own text names the sidecar key binds it through the emitted agtypeArgs, so a sidecar value can be one a gqlc encoding produced. Measured: one emitted package reads agtypeZone(props, "occurredAtOffset", value1) at models.go:40 and binds that same key through agtypeArgs at queries.cypher.go:51, with both helpers declared in models.go. Also refuted by the sentence's own consequence being deleted from offsetSidecar's doc and from the emitted agtypeZone doc on PR #848.

THE DEFERRAL STANDS on the rest of point 1, which is untouched and was independently judged legitimate: the micros count IS the instant, so any bound on it is a calendar-range POLICY decision rather than a well-formedness one, and there is no equivalent of 'a zone no clock keeps' to key it on. The live corpus deliberately carries year-9999 and pre-epoch instants (test/data/codegen/valid/timestamp_property_roundtrip), so any candidate bound has to be argued against rows that already exist.

What remains true in point 2 is a difference of REACHABILITY, not of provenance: gqlc's own encode writes the micros for every instant it binds, whereas it derives no sidecar parameter at all. That makes the instant path the more reachable one -- it does not make the sidecar path exclusively foreign.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #1329. agtypeInstant now bounds the decoded count to the four-digit calendar, year 1 through year 9999 inclusive, before building the instant; outside that it returns an error naming the count. The bead's two objections are both answered in ADR 0031 (docs/adr/0031-age-instants-are-bounded-to-the-four-digit-calendar.md). (1) Provenance: gqlc's encode does write the micros, but it writes them to an ordinary agtype integer property on a vertex any writer can touch, which is the same argument that already bounds agtypeZone's sidecar one key over on the same vertex. (2) Policy: the key is the wire, not taste — RFC 3339 has four year digits and so does every timestamp text a SQL client prints, so year 10000 and beyond is a number that fits an int64 and not a date another system reads back. Nothing that exists is refused: the corpus's far-end row IS the upper bound exactly, and its pre-epoch row is far inside the lower one. Pinned by TestAgtypeInstantRefusesACountOutsideTheCalendar in internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt over both admitted edges, both one-microsecond-outside rows and both int64 extremes; seen red on the four out-of-range rows before the fix, for the right reason.

title: codegen: the fixed-declaration sweep records a method whatever its receiver, so a non-*Queries method would be forced into reservedIdentifiers and over-refuse queries
description:
`TestEveryEmittedFixedDeclarationIsReserved` (`internal/codegen/prepare_test.go`, PR #845) walks the emitter-fixed golden files and requires a `reservedIdentifiers` row for every exported declaration it finds. Its `*ast.FuncDecl` arm records the name whatever the receiver is.

That is right for the corpus as it stands — probed independently on #845: the three fixed files declare exactly the twelve reserved names, and no method in them has a receiver other than `*Queries`. It is wrong in principle for a method the emitter might add on some other receiver. Such a name occupies no package block and collides with nothing, but the sweep would demand a row for it, and `internal/codegen/prepare.go:570` refuses a *query* on membership in `reservedIdentifiers` alone — at either scope. So satisfying the sweep would refuse a query name that generates fine.

WITNESS (mutation M13, independent review of #845, reproduced first-party at `660fe68a`): appending `func (h qHelper) Validate() bool { return true }` to every golden `db.go` turns `TestEveryEmittedFixedDeclarationIsReserved` red demanding a reserved row for `Validate`. `go vet` clean before the test ran.

Today the limit is stated in the test's doc comment and nothing enforces it. Two ways out, and the second is cheap:

  1. Record a method only when its receiver is `*Queries`, and assert separately that no other receiver appears in those files — so a new receiver type is a decision someone makes rather than a row someone adds.
  2. Leave the sweep as it is and add the receiver assertion alone: the sweep's demand is then correct because the antecedent is fenced.

ACCEPTANCE: the M13 witness above no longer demands a `reservedIdentifiers` row for a method on a non-`*Queries` receiver, and a golden carrying such a method still fails some NAMED test rather than passing silently.

PROVENANCE: nit N1, independent review of PR #845, 2026-08-17. Not reachable at that commit — zero such methods exist in the corpus.
notes:
REVIEW FINDING (PR #845 round 6, 2026-08-17): this bead's description claims golden `db.go` has no non-`*Queries` receiver. Measured false — 108 of 153 golden files carry one. Fix option 1 as written is therefore unimplementable; whoever picks this up must re-derive the fix direction before starting.
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
AGENT-J 2026-09-02 — PR #2182, branch fix/gqlc-tisj-fixed-decl-receiver-fence.

RE-DERIVED FIRST, as the round-6 note asked. The description's fix option 1
(record a method only when its receiver is *Queries) is WRONG at HEAD and I did
not implement it. It would drop Commit and Rollback, both on *Tx, out of the
sweep — and spec docs/specs/codegen-tx-embedded-querier.md section 5 says those
two rows are load-bearing. Following the bead as written would have deleted the
guard on exactly the rows the spec calls essential.

The description is also stale in its REASON. It says reserving Commit/Rollback
is a false refusal because a *Queries method redeclares nothing. Section 5 and
prepare.go:55-72 supersede that: query methods are emitted on the unexported
core, and both Queries and Tx embed the core, so a user query named Commit
promotes into *Tx and is SILENTLY SHADOWED by the depth-0 method. What Phase A
prevents is not a collision but a success. Redeclaration was never the ground,
so the receiver is not what the reservation turns on.

Implemented option 2, the antecedent fence, whose justification is now stronger
than when it was written. TestSweptMethodReceiversEmbedTheQueryCore asserts that
every receiver carrying an exported method in the fixed-declaration goldens
embeds the core. Derived from the goldens per emitted package, not a receiver
name list, so it does not become a fourth hand-maintained list (cf gqlc-6ynu).

MEASURED, against the corpus rather than the description:
  exported methods in fixedDeclarationFiles are on exactly two receivers —
  *Queries (Begin, WithTx, EnsureGraph, DropGraph) and *Tx (Commit, Rollback).
  The sweep's doc comment claimed THREE, naming a Queries accessor on *Tx. That
  accessor was deleted by gqlc-f4hf. Comment corrected in this PR.
  The round-6 note's "108 of 153 golden files carry a non-*Queries receiver"
  counts UNEXPORTED ones too (driverDB.run, txDB.run, queries.boundGraph,
  queries.cypherStmt); the sweep filters on exportedness, so those never reach
  it. Both measurements are right and they are about different populations.

MUTATION BATTERY, guard committed before mutating, tripwire and restore verified
per row, every row screened with go test -c:
  M1 golden gains Validate on a receiver NOT embedding the core  KILLED (fence)
  M2 golden gains Validate on *Queries                           HELD on fence,
                                                                 KILLED on sweep
  M3 core-embedding detection blinded                            KILLED (fence)
  M4 receiver collection blinded                                 KILLED (vacuity)
M1 reproduces the bead's M13 witness, now attributed to the receiver rather than
the name. M2 is the two-factor row and carries the ACCEPTANCE: a golden with such
a method still fails a NAMED test rather than passing silently.

Defect is LATENT, not live — the fence passes on the corpus as it stands. Stated
plainly because a new guard at zero failures is otherwise indistinguishable from
one that cannot fail; M1/M3/M4 are what show it can.

Test-only. No design blocker on this bead, so it merges on green gates (V.2).
Gates: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates, all 12 passed.

The bead was closed by the ANTECEDENT FENCE (its option 2), not by its stated option 1. Option 1 is wrong at HEAD and would have deleted the guard on Commit and Rollback, which spec codegen-tx-embedded-querier.md section 5 calls load-bearing. Full re-derivation, the corpus measurements, and the four-row mutation battery are in the NOTES.

Defect was latent, not live: the fence passes on the corpus as it stands, and rows M1/M3/M4 are what show it can fail at all.

title: codegen: the swept-file partition is complete but its two sides are unmeasured — moving a fixed file to inputDerivedFiles silences the sweep
description:
`internal/codegen/prepare_test.go` (PR #845, `TestEveryEmittedFixedDeclarationIsReserved`) partitions the golden corpus in two: `fixedDeclarationFiles` = `{db.go, graph.go, querier.go}`, whose exported declarations must each carry a `reservedIdentifiers` row, and `inputDerivedFiles` = `{models.go}` plus the `*.cypher.go` suffix, whose declarations follow from the batch and owe nothing. Every golden must fall in one side or the other, so an emitted file nobody classified fails.

THE HOLE IS THE SIDE A NAME IS PUT ON. Membership in `inputDerivedFiles` is asserted, never measured. Moving a fixed file to that side silences the sweep for it and passes the completeness check, because the file is still classified.

WITNESS (first-party, detached worktree at `c4642404`, `go vet ./internal/codegen/` printing BUILD OK before the test ran):

    fixedDeclarationFiles = {"db.go": true, "querier.go": true}
    inputDerivedFiles     = {"models.go": true, "graph.go": true}

    test exit=0 · kill-count(top-level FAIL)=0 · ok github.com/areqag/gqlc/internal/codegen 35.216s

`graph.go` is the Apache AGE-only file: `SessionInit`, `EnsureGraph`, `DropGraph`. All three lose their obligation and the package stays green. This is the same fail-silent family as the aggregate `swept` counter #845 replaced — one edit narrower.

FIX DIRECTION: derive the side rather than declaring it. The property that separates them is measurable in the corpus already: a fixed file's exported names are the emitter's own, so the set it declares is drawn from a fixed vocabulary across every fixture of a target, while an input-derived file's names track the fixture. `graph.go` declares the same three names in all 45 AGE goldens; `models.go` declares `Person` in one fixture and `Movie` in another. A file classified input-derived whose exported names never vary across the fixtures of a target is misclassified, and that is a check, not a claim.

RELATED (nit N2, independent review of #832): there are now three hand-maintained emitted-file lists, two of them of opposite polarity — `conformance_test.go:638` `connectionSurface` (exclusion, `{db.go, graph.go}`), `prepare_test.go` `fixedDeclarationFiles` (inclusion) and `inputDerivedFiles` (exclusion). A derivation would retire two of the three.

ACCEPTANCE: the witness above turns a NAMED test red, with `go vet` clean before the test runs so the kill is not the compiler.

PROVENANCE: found and measured while fixing blocker 1 of the independent review of PR #845, 2026-08-17. The blocker's own prescribed fix (count per basename) does not kill the mutation that motivated it; pinning the file set to the corpus does, and this is what that pinning still cannot see.
notes:
FIXED by PR #845 head a6380994 (round-4). Close on merge; `Closes #861` is in the PR body.

The bead's stated FIX DIRECTION is falsified in its naive form and was NOT implemented as written. "A file classified input-derived whose exported names never vary across the fixtures of a target is misclassified" does not hold on this corpus: db.go's exported name set VARIES within every target (distinct=2), because ErrNoRows and ErrMultipleResults are emitted only for a batch carrying a `:one` query. A variance rule would classify db.go input-derived and bake in the very E1b defect it was meant to close. Symmetrically, directory.cypher.go and people.cypher.go have exactly one fixture each, so "never varies" is trivially true of them and the rule would red-flag AllPersonIds/PersonNameById, which are genuinely input-derived.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD, measured over the 642 committed goldens: per basename, counted by distinct fixtures across the whole corpus, an exported name that EVERY fixture emitting that basename declares (n>=2 fixtures) is a name that does not follow from the batch, so the basename must be in fixedDeclarationFiles.

    graph.go            fixtures=45  SessionInit/EnsureGraph/DropGraph at 45/45  -> fixed
    querier.go          fixtures=83  Querier/ReadQuerier/WriteQuerier at 83/83   -> fixed
    models.go           fixtures=83  top name Person 62/83                       -> skipped, no full name
    queries.cypher.go   fixtures=71  top name GetAction 5/71                     -> skipped, no full name

Margins are wide on both sides (83/83 and 45/45 vs 62/83 and 5/71), so the discriminator is not near a boundary.

title: check-pr-closes forces a Closes on any PR whose branch or body names a bead, including PRs that only change its status
description:
`.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py` derives the bead a PR is about from a
`Bead:` line in the body, falling back to the branch name, and then requires
the body to carry `Closes #N` for that bead's GitHub mirror. The gate has no
way to say "this PR touches the bead but does not resolve it".

## Witness

PR #609 reopened bead `gqlc-4np` (GH issue #503). Its branch happened not to
contain the id, so the gate stayed silent. Had the branch been named after the
bead — the repo's own convention — the gate would have demanded `Closes #503`
on a PR whose whole purpose was that #503 should be open, and merging it would
have closed the issue it had just reopened.

Choosing a branch name that dodges the id is not a control: it is invisible,
unenforced, and it also disables the gate for PRs that genuinely should close
their issue.

## Why it was left out of gqlc-w4al

gqlc-w4al fixed re-evaluation (`edited` in ci.yml's `pull_request` types) and
the frozen-payload read (the body is now fetched from the API). Both make the
gate harder to get past. This one pulls the other way: any opt-out marker is
by construction a one-line bypass, and now that the gate re-evaluates on every
body edit, an opt-out can be added to a body at any point up to merge. What
the marker should be, and what stops it being used to wave a PR through, is a
design decision that deserves its own review rather than a fold-in.

## Shape of a fix

Needs to decide, at minimum:
- the marker's spelling and where it may appear (e.g. `Bead: gqlc-x (refs)` vs
  a separate `Refs:` line vs a label);
- whether an opt-out PR must still say something checkable — e.g. that the
  bead is not `in_progress`/`closed` in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, or that the PR
  demonstrably does not close it — so the marker is not simply "trust me";
- whether a label is better than body text, since labels are events
  (`pull_request: labeled/unlabeled`) and are attributable.

## Acceptance

- A PR that changes a bead's status without resolving it can name that bead
  and merge without `Closes #N`, and does so via a declared marker rather than
  by avoiding the id in the branch name.
- The marker cannot be used to skip the gate on a PR that does resolve its
  bead without that being visible in the diff or the check's output.
- `.githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh` gains a row per new verdict.
notes:
ROUND 2 pushed: 3098b3af on fix/closes-gate-opt-out (PR #901). Round-1 head was cd781383.

Two commits on top of round 1:
  c30eb298  ci: the opt-out is held against every closing keyword GitHub honours
  3098b3af  ci: pin how wide the not-in-export pass is

BLOCKER A (fail-open check 4): fixed with a SECOND pattern, GH_CLOSES, used at
check-pr-closes.py:233 only. CLOSES (the demand, line 67) is byte-identical to
merge-base. GitHub's nine keywords verified first-party against docs, which also
yielded two spellings the brief did not list: the documented colon form
('Closes: #617') and 'GH-N'. 14 spellings are rows.

BLOCKER B (marker matched inside code blocks): REFS_IN_BODY anchored to column 0
plus outside_fences() applied to the marker only. Indented, fenced and
below-closed-fence rows all present.

Suite: 16 rows at merge-base -> 34 at round 1 -> 55 now, 0 failed.

Filed out of this work: gqlc-lisu (GH #904, status-carriage hole in the ciguard
wiring pins, M18b SURVIVED). gqlc-oh30 notes widened with the stronger
'Bead: gqlc-<absent id>' variant.

CLOSE ON MERGE of PR #901. Body carries 'Closes #862' and 'Closes #883'.
close_reason:
Merged as f39a353a via PR #901 (squash), bundled with gqlc-zzz5. GH #862 CLOSED by the merge.

SHIPPED: a PR that names a bead it does not resolve can declare so with a 'Refs:'
opt-out line instead of a 'Closes #N', and the gate honours it. That removes the
forced-Closes on PRs which only change a bead's status.

REVIEW: independent review round 8 returned PASS on the bundle. The reviewer

open) carry what is left.

title: codegen/neo4j: no live scenario decodes a nested list, so the depth-suffixed decoder arms have never met a real Bolt server
description:
PR #822 (`0a139b74`, bd gqlc-ye6g) changed the emitted decoder for nested list
columns: `walkListElemBody`'s `inner`/`innerAcc` and `walkListElemPlan`'s `elem`
are now suffixed by nesting depth via `elemLocal`. The review of that PR recorded
"the emitted decoders were never exercised against a real Bolt server" as an
