Docker is not the binding constraint. I dispatched the live workflow on a branch
carrying that emitter (run 32001875182, `gh workflow run codegen-live`) and both
jobs went green with a REAL execution — 47.3s wall, zero `(cached)` lines, zero
`no tests to run` lines. It still witnesses nothing about this change.

WITNESS — the live battery has no nested-list shape in it:

    grep -rn 'list_list_int|schema_list_property_widths|schema_list_any_property' \
      test/data/codegen/*.go
    -> no matches

title: spec fence: a driver binding written without map[string]any{ is unswept
description:
The binding sweep's anchor is the literal `map[string]any{` — the opening brace is part of the anchor. A spec that states a binding as a bare code span, with no literal around it, is not read at all.

Witness (measured 2026-08-17 on PR #804, head dbeabc3a, and still live): inserting into docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md §5.3 the bullet

    - The driver binding is `"minAge": minAge` inside the map literal.

leaves TestSpecParamsMapBindsGeneratorOwnedValue PASS. That line documents the capture vector gqlc-lhs3 removed from the emitter, in the section gqlc-rz0l exists to correct, and the fence says nothing.

The symmetric signature escape was closed on that branch by anchoring a second scanner on a backtick before the context parameter (ADR 0029 decision 10). The same move was declined for bindings after measurement: the swept documents hold 130+ bare `"key": value` code spans across 21 files, essentially all JSON model shapes with no relation to a driver binding, so a brace-less recogniser would fire on prose across the corpus. See ADR 0029 decision 10.

Closing this needs something narrower than a bare key/value recogniser — e.g. grading only spans whose key matches a parameter name the surrounding section declares, or requiring specs to print bindings only inside the literal and fencing that requirement.

title: codegen/neo4j: the decoder probe stops at two levels of list nesting
description:
`decoderProbeWidths` in `internal/codegen/neo4j/decoder_test.go` derives, for each scalar the type table admits, that scalar plus `LIST<scalar>` plus `LIST<LIST<scalar>>`. Two levels is the first depth that reaches `writeSliceNarrow`'s recursive arm at all: `nested0`, `acc0`, `elem1`, `i1` and `v1` enter the swept set there and are absent at one level.

But no finite depth closes this, because the emitted names are depth-indexed (`internal/codegen/neo4j/render_models.go:327-359`):

    item := fmt.Sprintf("elem%d", depth)
    idx  := fmt.Sprintf("i%d", depth)
    inner := fmt.Sprintf("nested%d", depth)
    acc   := fmt.Sprintf("acc%d", depth)
    ... fmt.Fprintf(b, "%sv%d, ok := ...", body, depth)

So a schema declaring a three-deep list emits `elem2`, `i2`, `nested1`, `acc1` and `v2` — five identifiers the sweep has never seen, and a property named after any of them would collide undetected. Depth 4 adds five more. Extending the probe to depth 3 only moves the boundary.

The fix is different in kind from widening the probe: pin the *family* rather than the set. Either derive the guard from the format strings (no emitted local may be `fmt.Sprintf`-derived from a property name), or assert that the depth-indexed families are closed — that for every name in the swept set of the form `<stem><n>`, no property may be named `<stem><m>` for any m.

Filed from gqlc-320w, which reaches depth 2 and states the limit in the `decoderProbeWidths` doc comment rather than hiding it.
close_reason:
Gap confirmed on master before writing -- decoderProbeWidths still stopped at two levels of list nesting -- then closed. PR #1377, merged as master 1e11bb73.

TestDecoderLocalFamiliesAreClosedUnderDepth generates a schema nesting LIST from depth zero to three, eight properties per entity, including a node type keyed on three labels so the positional has-locals reach index one, plus an edge type. It then runs two independent halves.

The stem half: the set of local-name stems the decoders introduce must be IDENTICAL across depths two and three. If a deeper list minted a stem the shallower one did not, the family is not closed and a property could collide with a local only at some depths.

The candidate half: for every suffixed stem and every index zero through eight, a property named stem-plus-index must leave the decoders' scope exactly where it was. This is the half that catches a collision the stem set alone cannot see, because a stem can be stable while the numbering it hands out overlaps a user-supplied name.

Two mutations, screened twice. The second run was made with the stem half BLINDED, so each half was shown to kill on its own rather than one half certifying both -- the dominant-guard trap. Fifty-seven subtests pass when green, so neither half is vacuous.

Screened for the fake RED throughout with 'go test -c -o /dev/null' against the package, since a row reading KILLED because the artifact stopped parsing certifies nothing.

Scope note: this is a STATIC closure proof over the emitted locals. It shows the emitter's local families do not collide as depth grows. It does not show a real Bolt server round-trips a nested list -- that is sibling gqlc-nrao, deliberately left open, since Docker is unavailable on this box.

title: codegen/neo4j: TestTypeMapProperty leaves ANY VALUE and the bare LIST unswept
description:
`internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go`'s `TestTypeMapProperty` enumerates 29 of the 31 `graph.PropertyType` constants: 21 representable widths plus the 8 unrepresentable ones. `graph.TypeAnyPropertyValue` and `graph.TypeList` are named nowhere in that file, so the two arms of `typeMap.Property` that answer `any` and `[]any` have no unit row behind them.

Found while doing gqlc-320w, which built a walk (`propertyArmNames` in `internal/codegen/neo4j/decoder_test.go`) that reads the case expressions of `typeMap.Property` off types.go. That walk already gives `TestTypeMapProperty` the derivation it needs: hold its case table to naming every constant the switch has an arm for, rather than to a hand list.

Measured 2026-08-17 on fix/neo4j-decoder-probe-derives-coverage:
  grep -o 'graph.Type[A-Za-z0-9]*' internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go | sort -u | wc -l  -> 29
  the same over internal/graph/propertytype.go                                             -> 31

Not a defect in emitted code — both arms are exercised end to end by the decoder probe added in gqlc-320w and by the golden corpus. It is a hole in the unit-level table test.
close_reason:
Gap confirmed on master before writing, then closed. PR #1377, merged as master 1e11bb73.

The measurement: TestTypeMapProperty held its two tables to the literals twenty-one and eight. A count is a SIZE, not a membership -- it says nothing about WHICH constants are named -- so graph.TypeAnyPropertyValue and graph.TypeList sat outside both tables for as long as the arms answering them have existed. Twenty-nine of internal/graph's thirty-one property-type constants were covered; the two the bead names were the residue, exactly as filed.

The fix does not add two rows and a bigger literal, because that leaves the same defect one constant later. The obligation is now DERIVED: propertyArmNames walks typeMap.Property's own case expressions in types.go, graphPropertyTypes walks the const specs in internal/graph, and the test requires set-equality in both directions. A constant that gains an arm arrives owing a row; one that loses its arm stops owing one; and a name in an arm that no constant upstream declares fails too, rather than quietly widening the obligation by a spelling nothing holds. The two walks read DIFFERENT FILES, which is what makes the cross-check mean something.

Non-vacuity is pinned separately: require.NotEmpty on the arm set, because a walk that read nothing would satisfy the coverage obligation with any table at all -- the standing zero-of-zero trap.

One further thing the two new rows exposed. The graph.TypeList arm is UNREACHABLE: the constant is spelled LIST<ANY>, so Kind reports KindList and the recursion at the top of Property answers before the switch is entered. Both paths return the same text, so respelling the constant would move which one runs without moving the result and the arm's own comment would go false with nothing red. TestTypeMapPropertyListArmIsUnreachable pins the two upstream facts that comment rests on.

title: resolver: an unsatisfiable endpoint refuses as ErrUnknownEdge inline and ErrUnknownLabel as a var
description:
On test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql, the same endpoint written two ways refuses two different ways:

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(:Company:Desk) RETURN p
    -> unknown edge: Employee&Person-[WORKS_AT]->Company&Desk, Person-[WORKS_AT]->Company&Desk

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(z:Company:Desk) RETURN p
    -> unknown label: no node type satisfies Company&Desk; declared types carrying these labels: Company, Company&Large, Desk

No declared node type carries both Company and Desk, so the honest diagnosis is the var spelling's: the LABEL SET is unsatisfiable, and there was never an edge to look for. The inline spelling reports a missing edge and invites the author to go declare one.

The cause is ordering. A var endpoint goes through resolveNodeLabels at Phase A1, which refuses an unsatisfiable label set before edges are closed. An inline endpoint has no binding and is only ever read by endpointLabels at edge-closure time, where the empty satisfying set falls through to the spelled key and closeEdge refuses the probe set.

gqlc-3uof's branch pins the CURRENT wording (TestInlineEndpointCommitsOnTheTypesSatisfyingIt/a_conjunction_no_type_satisfies asserts the whole message) because the fallback is what makes the refusal name Company&Desk at all rather than nothing. Any fix here should move that row, not delete it.

Fix is likely a satisfiability check over inline endpoint label sets at Phase A1, before CloseEdges runs. That also makes TestInlineEndpointsAgreeWithTheirVarSpelling assertable on the error message rather than on verdict class alone — today it compares err.Error() and passes only because these unsatisfiable spellings are not among its rows.
notes:

origin/master by merge-base --is-ancestor, not inferred from the API. Full
suite green AT THE MERGE COMMIT (27 packages) against a tree that had already
moved past mine, with the three new guard rows confirmed to actually execute
there (=== RUN lines read, not just an exit 0).

WHERE THE DEFECT LIVED. Phase A1 admits local labelled nodes by looping
sc.bindings. An inline endpoint carries a label expression but no variable, so
it is not in sc.bindings and that arm never reached it. The satisfiability
question was therefore asked of a var spelling and not of the identical inline
pattern. Left to edge closure, an endpoint whose label set no declared type
satisfies fell through endpointLabels to the SPELLED key, which no declared
type carries, and refused as a missing EDGE — inviting the author to declare
`Person-[WORKS_AT]->Company&Desk`, a thing no node could ever be an endpoint
of. The fix asks both endpoints the same question at the same phase (9 lines).

SCOPE, SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT NOT ARGUMENT. The bead scoped this to the
unsatisfiable-conjunction branch; resolveNodeLabels also catches undeclared
labels. I did not narrow it to match the bead, and the reason is a battery row
rather than a preference: M4 encodes the narrow reading exactly (unsatisfiable
only, undeclared falls through) and it is KILLED. The wider scope is
load-bearing. They are one question — no type can stand here — and asking only
the first leaves the inline spelling reporting a missing edge to a type nothing
declares, which is the whole defect in its second shape.

THE DEAD ARM IS PROVED DEAD, WITH A CONTROL. I replaced the endpointLabels
fallthrough with panic(): it never fires across the unit suite or all 12920
sweep cells. That alone proves nothing — so the control is the same panic with
the Phase A1 check removed, which DOES fire (resolve.go:759: PROBE: fallthrough
reached). That also rules out the falsifier that the sweep swallows panics; the
one recover() in sweep_test.go:813 is inside sweepParseError, a manifest-PARSER
probe, not the cell-resolution loop.

77 CORPUS CELLS MOVED, ZERO VERDICT CHANGES. Nothing that accepted now refuses
and nothing that refused now accepts. 71 moved ErrUnknownEdge -> ErrUnknownLabel;
checked mechanically per row that the newly-named label is written (:X) in the
query and appears nowhere in that schema — 77/77, 0 contradictions. The other 6
(all valid/inline_endpoint_source.cypher) moved from naming Post to naming
Person; both labels are undeclared in all six schemas, so the report now names
the first undeclared label in query source order and nothing is lost.

(check only the target endpoint) and M4 (the narrow reading) were caught by the
CORPUS SWEEP ALONE; both unit guards passed them. The manifest is -update
regenerable, so a later sweep run to accept an unrelated change would have taken
either regression silently, with a green conscience. I added two unit rows —
the source-side pair, and the undeclared-label pair — and re-ran: M3 and M4 now

on a regenerable artifact. And these guards are testify SUITE METHODS — the
anchored form is ^TestResolverSuite$/^TestInlineEndpoint...$. The bare

battery reads as SURVIVED for every row at once.

title: resolver: Phase B commits an unlabelled binding to one type through a far end that does not cover
description:
On test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql:

  MATCH (p:Person)-[q:WORKS_AT]->(c)
  OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[h:HAS_DESK]->(d:Desk)
  MATCH (c)<-[w:WORKS_AT]-(x)
  RETURN x.personOnly

accepts {"type":"STRING","nullable":false}. The Employee&Person -[WORKS_AT]-> Company&Large row matches with h/d null, so c is Company&Large, the only WORKS_AT into it comes from Employee&Person, and that x has no personOnly. A NOT NULL column that is null.

candidateTypes computes c = {Company,Company&Large} INTERSECT {Company} = {Company} with covered=false, because the HAS_DESK hop is OPTIONAL and witnessesItsEndpoints refuses it. inferUnlabelled then writes resolved[c]=Company anyway and merely withholds the resolvedCovers mark. The covering lane gates what OTHER bindings learn from c; it does not stop c itself being committed to a strict subset of the attainable types, and x is then inferred singularly from that wrong c and projected directly.

So the resolver has two different notions in one map: 'the type' and 'the types a row can have'. The narrowing respects the difference; the projection path does not.

Same soundness class as gqlc-3uof but a different mechanism — 3uof was endpointLabels under-enumerating, this is Phase B committing on an admittedly-incomplete intersection. Closely related to the unlabelled-binding axis in gqlc-pv0u / gqlc-h6h7, and to gqlc-856f / gqlc-edze (ResolvedType is not a sealed sum), since the honest answer here is probably a plural node type rather than a refusal.

Witness for any fix: the query above must not offer x.personOnly as NOT NULL. The one-token twin with the OPTIONAL made mandatory must stay accepted — every returned row then really does have a HAS_DESK out of c, HAS_DESK is declared from the bare Company only, and the chain is sound.

title: resolver: a refusal-sentinel change inside a FAIL->FAIL cell is invisible to the corpus sweep, so a worse diagnostic can land green
description:
The strongest evidence for PR #806 (merged `aade7a40`, bead gqlc-0tft) was a corpus sweep: 310 queries x 28 schemas = 8680 cells, branch vs base, reporting 8 FAIL->PASS, 2616 PASS->PASS with every golden byte-identical, and zero accept->refuse / accept->different-answer. That is a strong result and it is why #806 was sound to land.

It has a hole, and the hole is a whole quadrant. The sweep compares VERDICTS (accept/refuse) and golden BYTES. It does not compare error strings. So of the 8680 cells, the **6056 that were FAIL before and FAIL after are compared on nothing but the fact of failing.** A change that swaps which sentinel a refusal returns — or degrades a precise diagnostic into a generic one — moves no cell between quadrants, changes no golden byte, and is therefore invisible.

This is not hypothetical. The reviewer found one by hand while spot-checking: a refusal that changed from `ErrAmbiguousLabel` to `ErrUnknownEdge`. That instance is an IMPROVEMENT, so nothing is broken today. But it was found by hand, and the reviewer stated plainly it 'cannot bound the rest' — nobody knows how many of the 6056 changed sentinel, or in which direction.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND #806: this is the sweep methodology the resolver work keeps using to prove a narrowing change is safe. Every future use inherits the same blind spot, and diagnostic quality is exactly what a narrowing change is most likely to perturb — narrowing changes which check fires first.

Same family as gqlc-fd06, gqlc-x5dq, gqlc-320w: a guard that is structural on one axis and blind on another, so it defends the shapes it was written alongside.

FIX: have the corpus sweep record the sentinel (or the full error string) per refusing cell and diff that too, so a FAIL->FAIL cell whose sentinel changed is reported as a third category rather than folded into 'no change'. Then the sweep's own output states which of the three it is: same verdict same sentinel, same verdict different sentinel, different verdict.

ACCEPTANCE: deliberately change one refusal's sentinel in the resolver, run the sweep, and confirm it REPORTS the change rather than printing an all-clear. Today it does not — that is the defect.

Do the before/after drill in both directions, and watch for the fake RED: a sweep that errors out because the harness cannot parse a changed message is not the same as one that detects the change.

title: codegen: reservedIdentifiers is a hand-maintained list — a new emitter-fixed exported name is not reserved and the collision gate fails open
description:
PR #832 (merged as `5718a935`, bead gqlc-e6mh) added `reservedIdentifiers` in `internal/codegen/prepare.go:49` — 12 rows, 9 `scopePackage` + 3 `scopeMethod` — so a schema element named `Queries`/`DBTX`/`ErrNoRows`/... is refused instead of emitting a non-compiling package.

The set is CORRECT today. An independent `go/parser` sweep over all 153 golden target trees found exported package-level fixed decls == exactly the 9 `scopePackage` rows and exported `*Queries` methods == exactly the 3 `scopeMethod` rows. There is no under-broad hole at this commit.

THE DEFECT IS THE MAINTENANCE PROPERTY, NOT THE CURRENT CONTENTS. The list is hand-maintained and nothing holds it against the emitters. A future backend or emitter change that introduces a new exported package-level fixed declaration WITHOUT adding a `reservedIdentifiers` row leaves the gate green, and the collision it was built to refuse silently returns.

WITNESS (independent reviewer on #832, reproduced first-party): appending `type Config = any` to every golden's `db.go` leaves the whole suite green. `Config` is now an emitter-fixed exported package-level name that no reserved row covers, so a schema entity named `Config` would once again emit a package that does not compile — exit 0, broken Go, which is exactly the gqlc-e6mh defect.

This is the fail-open shape this repo keeps getting bitten by: the gate keeps compiling, keeps passing its own tests, and stops covering the thing that was just added. Compare gqlc-x5dq (offset-sidecar gate keyed on the carrier text) and gqlc-eo46 — same family.

FIX (reviewer estimated ~6 lines): derive the obligation instead of listing it. `db.go`/`graph.go`/`querier.go` hold exactly the emitter-fixed declarations, and `conformance_test.go:638` already names a file set (`connectionSurface = map[string]bool{"db.go": true, "graph.go": true}`) — note `querier.go` is NOT in that map today, so the fix must establish its own file set rather than reuse that one. Walk those files' ASTs across the golden targets, collect exported package-level decls and exported `*Queries` methods, and assert set equality against `reservedIdentifiers`. Then adding an emitter-fixed name without a reserved row goes RED naming the missing identifier.

ACCEPTANCE: appending `type Config = any` to the goldens' `db.go` (the witness above) turns a NAMED test red. Mutate it to confirm it is not a fake RED — the tree must still compile when the assertion fires, so the kill must carry a real test name, not a blank one.

title: vuln gate: ADR 0026 overclaims the build-tags check, and a leaked discovery probe wedges four gates
description:
Two findings from the independent adversarial review of PR #813, raised after it
had already squash-merged as 7dfcf04e. Fixed in PR #833.

## 1. ADR 0026 claims a coverage the recipe denies

docs/adr/0026:118-119 said `check-golangci-build-tags` holds `.golangci.yml`'s
`run.build-tags` and the tree to each other "in both directions". justfile:172,
from the same change, says it compares in ONE direction "because the other one
cannot report anything".

The recipe is right. An undeclared term in the tree is refused by the derivation
— `classify` returns `classUnknown`, the caller errors naming the file — so it
never survives to reach a comparison in the recipe. Flip the recipe's `comm` and
the remaining direction is empty by construction, which is why it injects a
stale term of its own on every run.

"still holds" was false as well: the recipe was new on that branch.

This is the two-halves defect (bd gqlc-eo46) expressed in prose, in the artefact
someone reads right before deleting `return classUnknown`.

## 2. `goDirs` asserted a universal the same branch falsifies

main.go said a Go module with no directory holding a Go file "is not a thing".
The branch creates exactly that three times per run — the discovery probes are a
go.mod and nothing else.

Measured: plant test/data/{vuln,fence,xtest}probe.LEAKED and

    check-golangci-build-tags  rc=1      check-codegen-external-tests  rc=1
    test-codegen-fence         rc=1      vuln                          rc=1

all four blaming "the walk broken rather than the module empty" — a misdiagnosis
of the repo's own artefact. .gitignore already anticipated the leak.

Fixed in two parts: the refusal stays but states the negative it can support and
names the leaked probe as the first cause with its remedy; and a shared
`[private] sweep-discovery-probes` dependency clears residue before any of the
four recipes calls modscope. Shared and covering all three names because the
recipe that breaks is not the one that leaked — test-codegen-fence depends on
check-codegen-external-tests, so a leftover fenceprobe takes out the dependency
first. A per-recipe, per-name sweep was tried and measured still wedging the
pair.

## Rejected during the fix

Extending the probe traps to INT/TERM/HUP. A trap on INT runs the handler and
RESUMES, so Ctrl-C would delete the live probe and let the recipe continue
asserting things about it. Bash was measured running the EXIT trap on SIGTERM
regardless. Traps stay EXIT; the sweep covers SIGKILL, which no trap can.
notes:
ROUND 2 (2026-08-17). The independent review of PR #833 at 880a825f returned
REVISE with three blockers, all of them defects the FIX introduced rather than
ones it failed to fix. It confirmed the two originals are genuinely closed and
that the headline gqlc-s3lt empty-walk claim is a real RED (four named FAILs,
tree still compiles, so not a fake RED).

1. The sweep recipe was inserted between check-golangci-build-tags and its
   45-line doc block, so `just --dump` showed that recipe's doc as None and the
   build-tags prose as documentation for a three-line rm -rf. Moved below, blank
   lines restored; verified by diffing the whole recipe->doc map against master.

2. The sweep glob was a FOURTH hand-maintained copy of the probe names, held to
   nothing. Renaming the fenceprobe mktemp literal left `just test-codegen-fence`
   green with the sweep no longer covering it — this bead's own defect class
   (gqlc-oxne), and refused by the standing rule in the comment block the sweep
   had been parked under. Names now come from one variable block; .gitignore,
   which cannot read them, is held by a `git check-ignore` witness inside the
   sweep that reddens on a rename. The lookup counts its own calls (gqlc-eo46:
   a working guard invoked zero times passes as quietly as a broken one).
   Seven mutation rows KILLED, each naming the right cause.

3. The ADR paragraph added to fix the "both directions" contradiction introduced
   a universal of its own: "a term the key does not declare is refused by the
   derivation". False — classify checks four vocabularies in order and the key
   decides only the classCustom arm. Witnessed on a scratch root: hurd, linux,
   go1.24 and unix all exit 0 undeclared; only zzmystery is refused.

Fixed in 2f75d284 (ADR) and d17b81c5 (justfile + main.go comment nits).

Reported honestly, not fixed: two mutation rows SURVIVE — deleting the
invocation counter itself (a second-order guard; guarding it starts a regress)
and silencing the sweep's firing-case echo (observability, not a gate).

title: vuln/modscope: 'A Go module with no such directory is not a thing' is falsified by its own harness
description:
MERGED WITH THIS DEFECT KNOWN. PR #813 (7dfcf04e) landed on master while this was an open Linus blocker — auto-merge fired on green CI ahead of the review verdict. Filing so it is not lost.

THE UNIVERSAL, both on origin/master:
  internal/tools/modscope/main.go:284 — '// is not a thing, and the postcondition this walk feeds — every directory'
  internal/tools/modscope/main.go:324 — '"file. A Go module with no such directory is not a thing, so this is the walk "+'

WHY IT IS FALSE: the branch that wrote it creates exactly that shape THREE TIMES PER RUN. Its own probe harness does mktemp -d plus a lone go.mod, producing a Go module whose directory holds no Go file. The code asserts the shape cannot exist while the test suite manufactures it on every invocation. This is the repo's recurring 'a branch breaks its own rule' pattern, and the standing rule is that a cannot/never/every in prose which the branch's own rows falsify is a blocker: state the negative and enumerate the limits instead.

SECOND, OPERATIONAL DEFECT IN THE SAME AREA: a probe module that leaks — left behind by a killed or interrupted run — wedges 'just lint' across FOUR gates, because the stray go.mod is discovered as a module. That is a self-inflicted outage with no cleanup guarantee. The probe modules need to be created somewhere the walk does not reach, or removed under a defer/trap that survives a kill.

WITNESS: adversarial review of PR #813, blocker 2. Re-verified first-party against origin/master after the merge with:
  git grep -n 'is not a thing' origin/master -- internal/tools/modscope/

FIX: replace the universal at :284 and :324 with the measured negative and its limits, and make the probe modules unable to leak into the walk. Note the :324 text is an ERROR MESSAGE a user can see, not just a comment — so this is user-facing prose asserting something the tool's own tests contradict.

title: vuln: ADR 0026 says the register is compared 'in both directions', justfile:172 says ONE
description:
MERGED WITH THIS DEFECT KNOWN. PR #813 (7dfcf04e) landed on master while this was an open Linus blocker — auto-merge fired on green CI ahead of the review verdict. Filing so it is not lost.

THE CONTRADICTION, both on origin/master, shipped in the same commit:
  docs/adr/0026-govulncheck-cannot-see-in-package-tests.md:119 — 'other in both directions.'
  justfile:172 — '# This recipe therefore compares in ONE direction, because the other one cannot'

One of these is false and they ship together. ADR 0026:83 and :196 and :259 also say 'in both directions', so the ADR is self-consistent and the justfile is the odd one out — which makes it likely the ADR is the stale side, but that must be MEASURED, not assumed.

SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME PASSAGE: ADR 0026:118-119 uses the word 'still', which presupposes a prior state the recipe was already doing this in. The recipe is NEW on that branch.   git grep -n 'both directions' origin/master -- docs/adr/0026-govulncheck-cannot-see-in-package-tests.md
  git grep -n 'ONE direction' origin/master -- justfile

title: codegen: the committed golden corpus has no list column past nesting depth two
description:
`TestGoldenBuild` (internal/codegen/conformance) compiles the committed
`test/data/codegen` module, so it is the gate that says the golden tree
itself builds. Its deepest list column is `LIST<LIST<...>>`:
`list_list_int`, `schema_list_any_property` and `schema_list_property_widths`
are all depth two.

Depth two does not reach the element loop's local collision. gqlc-ye6g's
witness: at `origin/master` before the fix, a depth-three column emitted
`innerAcc = append(innerAcc, innerAcc)` and

    valid/probe_depth3/golden/neo4j-go-v5/queries.cypher.go:55:32:
    cannot use innerAcc (variable of type []int64) as int64 value in
    argument to append

while every committed depth-two golden compiled. So a re-broken emitter
whose goldens were regenerated would leave `TestGoldenBuild` green.

After gqlc-ye6g the depth-three coverage lives only in
`internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go`, whose corpus is assembled in a
temp dir. That harness is stronger (it compiles AND runs the emitted
package) but it is one harness, and deleting the query from
`testdata/corpus_queries.cypher` together with its test from
`corpus_test.go.txt` removes the coverage without failing anything —
`declaredTests` reads the pass set from the same template.

Fix: add a `list_list_list_int` fixture under `test/data/codegen/valid/`
mirroring `list_list_int` one level deeper, so the committed tree carries
a depth-three witness that `TestGoldenBuild` compiles.

"codegen/neo4j: a live scenario at depth 3, where the decoder's local-naming

title: vuln: every selftest CALL in the vuln recipe is deletable with the gate green
description:
The same two-halves defect gqlc-eo46 documents for `refuse_stale`, measured in
the `vuln` recipe. It is not one instance — it is every `selftest_*` invocation
in that recipe, and it predates the branch that added the newest one.

## Reproduction (lead, first-party, at 620cea66 / PR #813)

Each row deletes ONE line from the justfile and runs `just vuln`:

    delete the `selftest_platformtag` call      rc=0   SURVIVED
    delete the `selftest_tagblind` call         rc=0   SURVIVED

The BODY of each selftest is well witnessed — mutate the assertion inside
`selftest_platformtag` (`*",windows,"*` -> `*",zzneverwindows,"*`) and the gate
goes rc=1 immediately; same for `selftest_tagblind`'s derived-tag assertion. So
both halves of gqlc-eo46's pattern are present here too: the guard works, and
nothing proves it runs.

`selftest_tagblind` predates `fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence`, so this is a
standing class the branch extends by one instance rather than one it introduces.
That is why it is filed rather than fixed there.

## Why it does not close in-script

Same regress gqlc-eo46 names: any counter or assertion wrapped around the call
site is itself a line someone can delete, and the recursion does not terminate
inside the script. The close is the same out-of-band move eo46 proposes — run
the recipe against a fixture tree in which the selftest's precondition is
violated, and assert rc=1 with the term named.

Doing it once for the whole family is probably cheaper than doing it per
selftest: a single harness that, for each `selftest_*` function, deletes its
call site, runs the recipe, and requires rc!=0.

## Scope note

Not a defect in what the gates measure — every selftest passes on the real tree
today, and the properties they assert are independently checked elsewhere in the
recipe. The defect is that their continued presence is unenforced.

title: codegen/age: the witness sweep binds the server answer into the body, not into an assertion
description:
`TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness` (internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go) renders the named live test's body from the AST and requires every probe text, every recorded server answer and every served control text to appear in it. That is what makes the witness-required property mechanical rather than aspirational, and it kills the mutations that matter (unwitnessed probe added, probe commented out, witness shared between gaps, table emptied, recipe selector broken four ways).

What it does NOT bind is that the witness **uses** the answer. A live test whose body contains the answer string as a dead local, a log line, or an unasserted variable satisfies the sweep exactly as well as one that does `require.Contains(t, err.Error(), p.answer)`.

Measured, not supposed: mutation M18 in the #809 review moved a recorded `answer` out of its assertion and left it as a bare string in the same body. The sweep stayed green.

The branch shipped this disclosed rather than fixed — `dialect_test.go`'s header comment and ADR 0028 both say the binding is textual containment, not assertion reachability. This bead is to close or ratify it, not to re-litigate the disclosure.

**Severity is low and the reason is specific.** The failure requires a human to write a live witness that carries the exact server answer as a string while not asserting on it — which is more work than writing the assertion. The realistic decay path is refactoring: someone rewrites the witness to assert on a sentinel/SQLSTATE instead of the message text, leaves the old message string in a comment-adjacent position or a table row, and the sweep does not notice the coverage left.

Fix shapes:

1. Narrow the render. Instead of the whole body, render only the arguments of assertion calls (`require.*` / `assert.*` / `s.Require().*`) reachable in the body, and require the answer to appear there. Costs a small call-expression walk; kills M18 directly.
2. Or invert it: have the live witness itself iterate `gap.refused` and assert per probe, and have the sweep require that the witness ranges over the table rather than restating it. That makes the binding structural and removes the string-matching entirely — but it is a bigger change to `test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go` and needs a live run to land safely (Docker/CI, per gqlc-0oau).

Option 1 is the cheap one and is checkable without a container.
notes:
Raised P3→P2 by agent-m 2026-08-24 under the gqlc-35yu decomposition mandate (agent-a, gqlc-f5m5): gqlc product work sits at or above the floor (V.3.1), and this is one of exactly two open children of the P2 epic — below the floor it routes to nobody and the epic never closes. Verified live in the tree 2026-08-24: TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness still binds by textual containment (internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go:84). Fix shape 1 (narrow the render to assertion-call arguments) is the cheap one and needs no container.

title: codegen/age: the undefined-function diagnose ships two universals no witness carries
description:
`internal/codegen/age/dialect.go`'s `ErrUndefinedFunction` diagnose text tells the author two universal things:

- "Apache AGE 1.7.0 defines **no temporal constructor at all**"
- "AGE's **whole** temporal surface is timestamp()"

Neither is carried by anything on the branch that shipped them (PR #809, ADR 0028). The live witness `TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine` measures five refusals and two served texts; five "does not exist" answers and one working `timestamp()` do not establish a closed set over AGE's function catalogue.

The provenance is a hand-run spike, recorded at ADR 0028:29 — "of the 348 functions in `ag_catalog` exactly one has a temporal name". That 348 is itself an unwitnessed cardinal: no live test counts `ag_catalog`, so a version bump of the pinned image (`apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8...`) that adds a temporal function silently falsifies the ADR line AND the author-facing message, with nothing red.

**Why this was not a blocker on #809.** It errs toward under-refusing: the claim only affects the remediation advice, never the refusal decision, so no author is refused because of it. The `find` path is driven entirely by `undefinedFunctionProbes`.

**Why it is still worth closing.** It is advice with a universal quantifier in it, in the one place an author actually reads, and the branch's own posture is that the gap table is short on purpose (bd gqlc-osf1). "No temporal constructor at all" reads as the opposite of "short on purpose" — the message asserts closure over exactly the surface the ADR says is unmeasured.

Fix shapes, in the ratified order (a claim not made > a claim a test carries > a number > a hedge):

1. Drop the universals. The message works as "AGE 1.7.0 defines no temporal constructor this project has measured, and `timestamp()` is the one that answered" — same advice, no closure claim.
2. If closure is wanted, make it a live assertion: query `ag_catalog`'s function names from the pinned image inside the existing `ageDialectHarness` and pin the temporal-named set. That would also give the 348 a witness and redden it on an image bump.

Related: gqlc-osf1 (the table is known short), gqlc-kb2c (the ADR's cardinals rot together — the 348 is a seventh of the same family, on the provenance axis rather than the table-size axis).

title: codegen/conformance: the length guard's bounds direction is pinned only by a panic
description:

title: ci: justfile recipe bodies are outside shellcheck coverage, and lint-hooks:130 is a real ERROR
description:
`just lint` runs shellcheck over the `.githooks` tree only. The justfile's own
recipe bodies — which are `#!/usr/bin/env bash` scripts with `set -euo pipefail`,
several of them 60+ lines and carrying the repo's gate logic — are outside that
coverage entirely.

This is not hypothetical. Two findings this week were plain shell bugs that
shellcheck-class analysis is built to catch:

- `fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence` shipped a collision guard that matched
  newline-delimited `sort -u` scalars with the space-delimited
  `case " ${a} ${b} " in *" ${x} "*)` idiom. It could not fire, and it shipped
  in the commit whose job was to close the finding that the clause it guards had
  no coverage. Found by review, three rounds in.
- The same file uses that idiom correctly seven other times, on genuine arrays
  where `${arr[*]}` joins on a space. Scalar-vs-array is exactly the distinction
  a linter tracks and a reader does not.

Measured while reviewing that branch: shellcheck over the five recipe bodies the
branch owns reports 0 error and 0 warning at enforced severity, so enrolling
them is not a wall of pre-existing noise.

One real pre-existing hit does exist, on master:

    justfile:130  (inside `lint-hooks`)  — shellcheck ERROR

That one needs fixing or an explicit inline disable before the gate can be
turned on, and it is the argument for turning it on rather than against.

## Shape of the work

Extract each recipe body (just already knows them; `just --dump` or a small
reader like the one in `internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go` can enumerate
them), write each to a temp file with its shebang, and run shellcheck at the
same severity `lint-hooks` uses. Gate must FAIL on a finding, not warn — a
detector that exits 0 is not a gate.
notes:
## Measurement from the fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence review (PR #813, 2026-08-17)

That branch adds ~795 lines to the justfile. Shellcheck was pointed at the four
shebang recipe bodies it owns, by hand, with just interpolation ({{x}}) replaced
by a placeholder first:

    check-golangci-build-tags     --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings
    test-codegen-fence            --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings
    check-codegen-external-tests  --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings
    vuln                          --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings

So turning this bead's gate on would NOT have blocked that branch. At info
severity there are three findings, all judged intentional:

  - SC2015 x2, both the same helper `lines() { [ -n "${1}" ] && printf ... || true; }`
    where the `|| true` is the point (the function must always succeed).
  - SC2086 x1, `go list -deps ... ./... ${xtest}` — deliberate word-splitting of
    a newline-separated list into separate arguments.

This bead's headline finding is independently reproduced: extracting `lint-hooks`
and running shellcheck over it gives SC1073/SC1124/SC1072/SC1085 at ERROR, all
from the `# shellcheck only supports shell; ...` comment sitting BETWEEN case
items (justfile:130 on master). Shellcheck parses any comment beginning
`# shellcheck` as a directive, and directives are only valid before a complete
command. The fix is to reword the comment so it does not start with the word
`shellcheck`, which is a one-line change that should land with the gate.

No prose on that branch claims the recipes are linted; verified by grep over its
diff of justfile, docs/ and .github/.

--- TRIAGE 2026-08-23, second factory triage lane ---
gqlc-k4h7 ('lint: the justfile's shell is not shellchecked by any gate', filed
2026-08-17T06:54Z, P2) is CLOSED as a duplicate of this bead. Verified before
closing: this bead is open/in_progress, assignee areqag, started 05:55:59Z today.
Both beads name the same defect ('just lint' runs lint-hooks with dir='.githooks',
so justfile recipe bodies are outside shellcheck) and the same remedy (extract
each shebang recipe body, shellcheck it, fail the gate). k4h7's only datum not
already here is that its author extracted the 'vuln' recipe body and got SC2015
on 'lines() { [ -n "${1}" ] && printf ... || true; }' — the same finding your
notes above already record independently at info severity, judged intentional.
Nothing in k4h7 is lost by closing it.
close_reason: Closed by PR #1334. New lint-just recipe extracts every shebang recipe body from just's own json dump and shellchecks it at warning severity; lint depends on it, so a developer meets it before CI does. Nineteen bodies enrolled. The pre-existing SC1124 ERROR inside lint-hooks (a case-branch comment opening with the tool's name) is fixed. Four mutants killed in internal/tools/ciguard/justbodies_test.go: dependency removed, severity raised, emptiness refusal removed, one body dropped from the selection. No check is excluded.

title: ci: check-golangci-build-tags proves refuse_stale works and never proves it is called
description:
`check-golangci-build-tags` carries a 60-line witness proving `refuse_stale`'s
BODY refuses a stale entry, and nothing at all proving that body is APPLIED to
the real sets. The application is one line:

    justfile:302   refuse_stale "${derived}" "${configured}" || exit 1

Delete it and a genuinely stale entry passes in silence.

## Reproduction (lead, first-party, at 620cea66)

Inject a real stale entry — `- zzstalereal` in `.golangci.yml` run.build-tags,
constraining no file in the tree — then run `just check-golangci-build-tags`:

    A  pristine justfile + stale entry      rc=1  names zzstalereal, 5 stderr lines
    B  justfile:302 deleted + same entry    rc=0  no stderr
    C  pristine justfile + clean config     rc=0  no stderr

B is byte-identical in observable behaviour to C. The gate reports "clean" on a
tree it never checked.

## Why the branch's own idiom does NOT close it

620cea66 introduced a positive control for exactly this class: look up every
term the two sets contain and refuse if the lookup cannot find them. That works
for `uses_term` because the control can positively exercise the predicate. It
does not transfer here — any counter or assertion added around line 302 is
itself deletable, and the regress does not terminate inside the script. The
reviewer's "closable with `control`'s own idiom" is optimistic; measured, it is
not.

The close is out-of-band: a test that runs the recipe against a fixture tree
with a known-stale tag injected and asserts rc=1 and that the term is named.
That is the same move `feat/age-dialect-gap-admission` made for its justfile
recipes (a Go test that parses the artefact and asserts properties of it), so
there is a worked precedent in-tree.

## Related residue on the same branch

- Deleting the whole `control` loop survives (`control=0` -> `1`). Same
  last-line-of-the-script shape, disclosed by the implementer as NB-2.
- Both are "the outermost assertion is unguarded", NOT the vacuous-pass class
  that gqlc-s3lt covered — that one is closed and stays closed.
notes:
PR #833 round 3 widens the surface this bead describes, and does not close it.

sweep-discovery-probes now carries nine refusals (empty aggregate, empty probe
value, no *_probe declared, odd-shaped site, no site at all, site variable off
the *_probe convention, declared-vs-swept in both directions, per-name coverage
asking BOTH `git check-ignore -q` and `-v` with the source pinned to .gitignore,
lookup-membership, uncovered-control, post-sweep verify). Every one has this
bead's shape: the refusal is deletable and nothing inside the script observes
that it is gone.

Measured at a5f07491 (PR head), mutation harness /tmp/r3-mut-833.py, 42 rows,
28 KILLED / 14 SURVIVED, per-row preconditions 'just --summary rc=0' AND the
rendered recipe body passing 'bash -n', md5 restore verified on justfile and
.gitignore per row. The guard-isolation rows -- each refusal deleted ON ITS OWN
with its own defect still applied, so only the deleted guard could have spoken:

  membership refusal deleted, no other defect       rc=0 SURVIVED
  zzuncoveredprobe control mkdir deleted, no defect rc=0 SURVIVED
  final verify loop deleted whole, no defect        rc=0 SURVIVED
  lookup `-v` source check deleted + rules moved
    to .git/info/exclude                            rc=0 SURVIVED
  lookup `-q` hide check deleted + negated
    !/test/data/vulnprobe.*/ rule applied           rc=0 SURVIVED
  site-shape refusal deleted + dotless site         rc=0 SURVIVED
  literal-site refusal deleted + literal site       rc=0 SURVIVED
  declared-vs-swept refusal deleted + its defect    rc=0 SURVIVED
  per-name coverage refusal deleted + its drift     rc=0 SURVIVED

Some refusals overlap, so deleting one is sometimes caught by another (deleting
the empty-aggregate refusal still trips the empty-value one; deleting the
swept-not-declared accumulation still trips the coverage refusal unless
.gitignore is also given a rule for the extra name). Nothing in the recipe makes
that so -- it is incidental, and the rows above are the ones where it does not
hold.

The recipe states this limit in the tree beside the lookup-membership refusal
rather than only in the PR body. The close is unchanged and still out-of-band: a
test that drives the recipe over a fixture tree from outside it and asserts rc
and the named term, per this bead's original description.
2026-08-23, .github/workflows lane, read-only. NOT FIXED, and confirmed STILL OPEN at origin/master e580fd70 -- the bead was assigned to a workflows-only lane and the defect is not in a workflow.

WHERE IT LIVES NOW. The recipe has grown since the bead was written and now carries the zzstaleprobe WITNESS the description asked for: it puts a term no file in this tree constrains into a COPY of the configured set, runs refuse_stale over that copy, and refuses if the clause accepts it or refuses without naming the term. Plus a uses_term lookup control and an empty-union refusal.

That does NOT close this bead, and the bead already said why. The witness exercises refuse_stale against a SYNTHETIC set. The application to the REAL sets is still the last line of the recipe, on its own, guarded by nothing:

    refuse_stale "${derived}" "${configured}" || exit 1

Delete that line and every guard above it still passes: the witness still runs, still refuses the probe, still names it, and the recipe exits 0 over a genuinely stale .golangci.yml entry. Same finding as reproduction B in the description, unchanged by the intervening work. Note also that the witness is at check-golangci-build-tags in the justfile and the deletable line is the recipe last statement, so the regress the description describes -- any assertion added around it is itself deletable -- has not terminated.

WHICH LANE. The fix is a test that runs the recipe against a fixture tree with a known-stale tag injected and asserts rc=1 and that the term is named. That is Go, in internal/tools (modscope or ciguard), or a shell suite under .githooks/tests -- note internal/tools/ciguard enforces where hook suites live and how they are named. It is not editable from .github/workflows. No workflow change can close this: the recipe already runs in the required lint context, so CI calls the gate; what is missing is anything that proves the gate looked at the real tree.

Leaving open and unclaimed for whoever owns internal/tools next.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1362, merged to master 2026-08-23. internal/tools/ciguard/buildtags_test.go, out of band as the bead required. It runs the REAL check-golangci-build-tags recipe out of the REAL justfile in a throwaway tree -- the same move golangci_staleness_test.go makes for ensure-golangci. The fixture holds the justfile, the .gitignore and a git repo (sweep-discovery-probes, a dependency of the recipe, runs git check-ignore), test/data for the probe glob, and a stub go on PATH answering the three modscope queries the recipe's one scope() helper makes. Stubbing go rather than copying the module is what makes the refusal reachable at all: on any real tree derived is a subset of configured by construction, so the live arm can never fire there. Three rows, and they reproduce the bead's A/B/C exactly. C, sets equal, rc=0 silent. A, a term configured and constraining no file, rc=1 naming zzstalereal. B, the recipe's last statement deleted from the fixture's justfile copy, same input, rc=0 silent -- so the deletion is now observable and A is what observes it. The constant holding that line is asserted present in the real justfile before the fixture is built, so the line moving is a red with a message saying so rather than a row that quietly stops measuring anything. Its git init clears GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE from the child environment: the pre-push hook exports them, and a git init inheriting a linked worktree's GIT_DIR re-initialises the parent repository. Also fixed the related residue only partly: nothing yet covers deleting the whole control loop (the bead's NB-2). That is a separate, smaller version of the same shape and is not claimed closed here.

title: codegen spec fence: the census has a per-document floor of one graded site
description:
The spec fence's census reconciles per (document, method-name), so a document keeps its census entry as long as ONE graded site survives. A one-part invisible edit therefore passes green.

The binding half has the same floor: c1.md:1339 map[string]any{"id": arg} -> mapOf{...} is GREEN.

- per-(document, method-name) census: does NOT close it. C4 grades RemovePerson at :363, :404 and :840, so the NAME survives :404 leaving.
- per-site COUNT: closes it, but is exactly the shape specfence_test.go:82-85 argues against (a bare '9 != 10' with no name in the failure).

title: resolver: a directed close still collects the right-to-left endpoint reading

title: resolver: closeEdge reads an inline endpoint's spelled key, not its satisfying set
description:
endpointLabels' InlineEndpoint arm (internal/resolver/resolve.go) returns the exact key the query spells, not the set of declared node types satisfying those labels. edgeCandidates is therefore a SUBSET of the keys a matching row can carry, and closeEdge commits an edge type on that subset.

Reproduction (test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql: Person / Person&Employee, Company / Company&Large, WORKS_AT declared Person->Company and Person&Employee->Company&Large):

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(:Company) RETURN r
    -> ResolvedEdge{Person -[WORKS_AT]-> Company}

Both declarations match the pattern, so r is genuinely plural and the answer names one of two. The var spelling MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN r closes over the full cross-product and is refused, so the two spellings of one pattern disagree.

This predates gqlc-0tft and is unchanged by it: identical on f4fb1a19 and on the branch. gqlc-0tft's NarrowPluralEndpoints stops reading the under-approximation via endpointKeysCoverEveryMatch, which contains the node-type half; this bead is the edge-type half that remains.

Fix is to make the InlineEndpoint arm return satisfyingNodeTypes(ls, sch). That widens closeEdge's candidate sets, so queries that resolve today become ambiguous refusals -- the ADR 0006 forbidden direction -- and it needs its own decision about whether a spelled label set should key exactly or satisfy. Not a drive-by.

The stale citation in endpointLabels' doc comment (it pointed at the CLOSED gqlc-h9n.23, which is about multi-label edge types) is repointed here.

title: resolver: plural endpoint narrowing does not reach across a WITH carry
description:
`gqlc-0tft` made a plural node binding narrow from an edge that every returned
row provably has. It does not reach across a `WITH`:

    MATCH (p:Person) WITH p MATCH (p)-[w:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN p.id

stays refused. The plural carry is rejected before Part 1's edge gets the chance
to narrow `p`, so the query is refused for a reason that the second part would
have answered.

## Why this is a widening and not a bug

Nothing here is unsound: the refusal is conservative and no wrong column is
emitted. It is a query a user can reasonably write and reasonably expect to
resolve, refused because of the *order* two mechanisms run in rather than
because the schema cannot answer it.

Confirmed by `linus-0tft-r2` during the round-2 review, who separately
established that a plural binding cannot cross a `WITH` at all on master
(`MATCH (p:Person) WITH p RETURN p.id` is `ErrAmbiguousLabel` there), so this is
not a regression introduced by the narrowing — it is the narrowing not yet
reaching a place that was already refused.

## Fix

Work out whether the narrowing can run before the carry check, or whether the
carry check can consult the narrowed set. Ordering changes in the resolver have
been load-bearing on this epic — `gqlc-0tft` itself had to move its narrowing
*below* the deferred-edge close, pinned by
`TestDeferredEdgesCloseBeforeTheNarrowing` — so whatever order is chosen needs a
test that fails when it is reversed.

## Acceptance

The query above resolves, with `p` committed to the single type `WORKS_AT`'s
declared source endpoint names, and a test that reddens if the two mechanisms
are reordered.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-0tft-r2`'s non-blocking findings (NB-4),
who described it as "missed widening, filed-shaped".

The fix defers the whole-entity projection refusal in a NON-FINAL Part, where the projection is a carry rather than a user-visible column, and adds a twelfth branchState lane so the carried binding keeps its own category-grained sentinel.

Measured over all 13986 pre-existing corpus cells: 102 change, zero accept->refuse, 10 of the 11 moving queries are valid/ fixtures. Two controls survive.

title: codegen/age: the dialect gap table is short — four constructs are suspected and unwitnessed
description:
The Apache AGE backend refuses a query on its TEXT when it spells a construct
the pinned image cannot accept (`internal/codegen/age/dialect.go`). Every entry
in that table carries a probe and the answer a live session gave, and a sweep
(`TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness`) refuses an entry with no witness. That
is the right shape, and it leaves the table SHORT: three openCypher constructors
and one namespaced call are every bit as suspect as the five that are refused,
and none of them has ever been run.

## Unverified, and therefore not refused

Against `apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb`
(PostgreSQL 18.1, AGE 1.7.0 — the digest is a constant in
`test/data/codegen/live_age_test.go`):

1. `RETURN time()` — expected `function time does not exist`, never run.
2. `RETURN localtime()` — same, never run. Load-bearing: it is what
   `test/data/codegen/invalid/unrepresentable_temporal_localtime_column` and
   `TestTemporalProjectionNamesThisBackend` rest on. If localtime() turns out to
   be undefined, the dialect gate answers those two ahead of
   `codegen.ErrUnrepresentableTemporal` and BOTH have to move to a constructor
   that is still unwitnessed — or the fixture has to reach a temporal column
   some other way.
3. `RETURN point({x: 1, y: 2})` — expected `function point does not exist`,
   never run. Not a temporal, so it would be a third gap rather than a name
   added to this one, and the refusal prose would have to change: the present
   message says "defines no temporal constructor at all".
4. `RETURN duration.between(a, b)` — namespaced, so a different name from
   `duration` (Cypher.g4 §oC_FunctionName is `oC_Namespace oC_SymbolicName`) and
   not covered by the `duration` probe. `cypher.UnqualifiedFunctionCalls` drops
   namespaced calls by design, so refusing it needs a second scanner as well as
   a witness.
5. The SQLSTATE for every refusal in the undefined-function gap. The spike
   (gqlc-35yu.5) recorded the server's MESSAGE and not its code, so
   `TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine` asserts the message alone —
   unlike the alternation gap, which pins 42601. PostgreSQL's
   `undefined_function` is 42883 and AGE plausibly reports through the same
   channel, but plausibly is not measured.
6. The first run of `TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine` itself. It is
   nightly-and-manual only (`codegen-live.yml`, job `live-smoke-age`, skipped on
   PRs), so the five refusals it re-measures ship having been verified by hand in
   the spike and not yet by CI.

## Why this is a separate bead

Answering any of the above needs Docker, and therefore needs CI: the
`live-smoke-age` job is the only place in this project with a container. The
work is to add the probes, read the answers off the run, and then — for whichever
turn out to be refused — add them to the gap table with their recorded answers,
which the sweep will accept only once the live test carries them.

## Done when

- Each of (1)–(4) has been run against the pinned image and its answer recorded
  in this bead.
- Each one that AGE refuses is in `dialectGaps` with its probe and answer, and
  the ones AGE accepts are in the gap's `served` list so the gate is pinned not
  to refuse them.
- The undefined-function rows assert a SQLSTATE, as the alternation rows do.
- `just test` and one green `live-smoke-age` run.
notes:
2026-08-23, codegen-age lane, PR #1381 (merged). INSTRUMENT SHIPPED, ANSWERS NOT OBTAINED — bead stays OPEN deliberately.

I did NOT extend the gap table with more suspicions, and I witnessed ZERO of the four constructs. Docker will not start on this host (systemctl start docker refuses, needing interactive auth), and codegen-live.yml's live-smoke-age job is if: github.event_name != 'pull_request', so it was SKIPPED on the PR. Every unwitnessed row therefore remains explicitly unmeasured rather than being upgraded on a guess.

What did ship is a measurement instrument: test/data/codegen/live_age_unwitnessed_test.go, TestAGEAnswersTheConstructorsNobodyRan, nine rows under ageDialectHarness. It logs 'osf1: <name> ACCEPTED/REFUSED <sqlstate> <message>' and asserts ONLY that the server answered (require.ErrorAs on a pgconn.PgError), so it cannot manufacture a verdict it did not observe. Four probes are the unwitnessed constructors — RETURN time(), RETURN localtime(), RETURN point({x: 1, y: 2}), RETURN duration.between(null, null); the other five re-ask the already-claimed refusals for their SQLSTATE.

One design point worth keeping: duration.between uses LITERAL arguments, not a MATCH. A MATCH that finds no rows returns no rows and no error, which would have printed ACCEPTED without the function ever being resolved — a false witness.

It is ENROLLED: the justfile's test-codegen-live-age -run alternation names it (forced and verified by TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt).

NEXT ACTION for whoever takes this: gh workflow run codegen-live.yml --ref master, then grep the job log for 'osf1:'. Each line is one construct's answer, straight from the server. Write those answers into dialectGaps (or its served list) with the SQLSTATE as the witness, and only then close.
CORRECTION to the paragraph above that said 'a codegen-live dispatch on master will execute it'. It executes it and DISCARDS its answers. I dispatched codegen-live.yml on master after PR #1381 merged: run 32634892211, success, live-smoke-age green, 'ok .../test/data/codegen 19.676s'. grep -ci osf1 over the whole 848-line job log returns ZERO, because the recipe runs go test without -v and go test drops a passing package's output. Measured in a scratch module that nothing survives a pass — not t.Log, not fmt.Println, not os.Stdout, not os.Stderr. Filed as gqlc-8cjn, now blocking this bead. Still ZERO of the four constructs witnessed.

2026-08-29, agent-b. Claimed. Blocker gqlc-8cjn is CLOSED and its -v fix is
verified present on origin/master (justfile:2495), and the recipe -run
alternation does name TestAGEAnswersTheConstructorsNobodyRan, so the answers
should survive this time.

Dispatched codegen-live.yml on master (a12cd69e, master green) as run
33268424367. Branch fix/gqlc-osf1-witness-unwitnessed-constructors cut from
origin/master; git branch --list "*osf1*" found no prior branch, so nobody has a
stranded implementation of this one.

Nothing written into dialectGaps yet and nothing will be until the log is read.

== ANSWERS OBTAINED 2026-08-29 by agent-b ==

Run 33268424367, workflow_dispatch on master a12cd69e. conclusion success,
live-smoke-age success. Nine osf1: lines present in the log, so the gqlc-8cjn
-v repair works and the answers survived this time.

Image: apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb
(PostgreSQL 18.1, AGE 1.7.0), the digest pinned in live_age_test.go.

ALL FOUR UNWITNESSED CONSTRUCTORS ARE REFUSED. None is accepted, so nothing
goes into a served list.

  (1) time()                     REFUSED  42883  function time does not exist
  (2) localtime()                REFUSED  42883  function localtime does not exist
  (3) point({x: 1, y: 2})        REFUSED  42883  function point does not exist
  (4) duration.between(null,null) REFUSED 3F000  schema duration does not exist
  (5) the five already refused, SQLSTATE now measured, ALL 42883:
        datetime, date, localdatetime, duration, toTimestamp
        each with the same message the spike recorded, verbatim.

THREE OF THESE ARE NOT THE SIMPLE ADDITION THE BEAD ANTICIPATED. Recording
before implementing, because each changes what the fix has to be.

(4) IS A DIFFERENT ERROR CLASS, and this is the finding I did not expect.
duration.between does NOT come back as undefined_function. It is 3F000,
invalid_schema_name, and the message is about a SCHEMA and not a function:
PostgreSQL reads the openCypher namespace as a schema qualifier and fails
resolving the qualifier before it ever looks for a function. So a namespaced
call cannot join the undefined-function gap even with a second scanner: it
would be a row whose recorded answer names no function, and
TestEveryRefusedFunctionNameIsNamedByItsProbeAnswer requires the answer to
name the function the probe called. It refuses TODAY on the server, which is
the practical point, but the gate cannot say so under the existing gap.

(2) IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE ANSWER IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE ONE. localtime() IS
undefined, exactly the case the bead flagged. So the dialect gate would answer
invalid/unrepresentable_temporal_localtime_column and
TestTemporalProjectionNamesThisBackend AHEAD of
codegen.ErrUnrepresentableTemporal, and both rest on reaching the CARRIER
refusal. Adding localtime to the gap without moving them changes what those
two fixtures measure, silently: they would keep passing while measuring a
different refusal. That is not a rider I can put on this diff.

(3) point() REFUSED MEANS A THIRD GAP, not a name added to the second. The
present message says AGE defines no temporal constructor this project has
measured, and point is not a temporal, so the existing prose would be false of
it. A third gap needs its own sentinel, its own diagnose prose and its own
witness row.

WHAT IS SIMPLY ADDITIVE: (1) time(), and (5) the SQLSTATE. time() is a
temporal constructor, refused, undefined-function, message names the function
the probe called - it satisfies the existing derivation with no other change.
42883 is uniform across all six undefined-function refusals, so
TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine can pin it the way the alternation
gap pins 42601.

I am NOT writing (2), (3) or (4) into the table under this bead without saying
so first. See the next note for the size.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29, PR #1806, branch fix/gqlc-osf1-witness-unwitnessed-constructors, head 26e1598a.

ALL NINE ANSWERS OBTAINED on codegen-live run 33268424367 (dispatched on master a12cd69e, SUCCESS, all nine osf1: lines present). time/localtime/point all REFUSED 42883; duration.between REFUSED 3F000 schema duration does not exist; the five existing refusals all 42883.

WHAT LANDED: time() and localtime() are now probes, closing the temporal constructor set by measurement. The gap pins SQLSTATE 42883. point() and duration.between() stay out, filed as gqlc-l8e2n and gqlc-dy40s, with their measurements kept as ASSERTIONS in test/data/codegen/live_age_ungated_test.go so each bead inherits a witness rather than a suspicion.

THE CONSEQUENCE, which is bigger than the bead anticipated. Every route to a temporal column runs through a temporal constructor (internal/query/cypher/shape.go temporalConstructorType). I MEASURED the alternative rather than assuming it: an aggregate over a declared LOCAL TIME property, min(e.atLocal), types as UNKNOWN at the shape layer and answers ErrUnsupportedQuery, not the carrier refusal. So closing the bare set puts codegen.ErrUnrepresentableTemporal out of reach of every bare spelling, and the only text still reaching it on this backend is the namespaced duration.between. The corpus fixture and TestTemporalProjectionNamesThisBackend both moved onto it; the fixture is renamed unrepresentable_temporal_duration_column for the kind it now projects.

That fixture is the ONLY one in the corpus naming that sentinel and TestSentinelReachability requires one, so building gqlc-dy40s closes the last route. That question is written into the fixture comment, the ADR and gqlc-dy40s itself.

VERIFIED: just test, lint, test-codegen-fence, tidy-check green. Red-before observed per moved assertion (three distinct sentinels across three candidate routes, so the assertion discriminates). TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness red on the new probes until the live rows carried them. Mutation: adding point to undefinedFunctionProbes kills both new not-refused rows, each named by its own declared row.

NOT YET CLOSED: the SQLSTATE pin is asserted and no local run can witness it. Live run 33269476222 dispatched on the branch. Close only on that plus green CI.
