title: ci: the AGE arm's only gate is a nightly that can fail silently or stop firing
description:
gqlc-35yu.8 moved the Apache AGE live arm off the PR critical path: job
live-smoke-age in codegen-live.yml runs on schedule and workflow_dispatch
only. That trade was deliberate -- PRs are not charged for AGE containers --
and it is sound only while the nightly is actually a gate. Two things weaken
that.

No failure alerting. A red nightly notifies GitHub's default recipient, the
last committer to the cron file, and nothing else. Nobody owns it. An AGE
regression can sit on master indefinitely with every PR green, because no PR
runs the AGE arm.

Scheduled workflows stop firing. GitHub disables cron-triggered workflows
after 60 days with no repository activity. The gate would then be off with no
signal at all -- the failure mode is silence, not a red check.

There is a third, narrower hazard worth closing at the same time: a SKIPPED
check satisfies a required status context on GitHub. live-smoke-age is
correctly absent from master's required list today, but if it were ever added
it would be permanently green on every PR, because it skips on pull_request.
gqlc-35yu.8 leaves a comment on live-smoke recording that its job id is the
required context; the mirror-image warning belongs on live-smoke-age.

Options, roughly in order of cost: route nightly failure somewhere owned;
have a failed nightly open or reopen an issue so the signal is durable; add a
liveness assertion that the AGE job ran at all recently, so disablement is
itself detectable.

Found by Linus as NB3/NB5 in round-2 review of gqlc-35yu.8, alongside the
blocking branch-protection defect. Non-blocking for that bead -- the arm and
its wiring are correct; what is unowned is the signal they produce.
close_reason:
PARTLY FIXED and closed on the half that was the bead point; the remainder is filed as gqlc-zqa3. Merged as PR #1331 (squash f8105d77) on 2026-08-23.

WHAT SHIPPED. .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml gained a nightly-alert job:

    needs: [live-smoke, live-smoke-age]
    if: always() && github.event_name == schedule
        && (contains(needs.*.result, failure) || contains(needs.*.result, cancelled))
    permissions: issues: write

It creates the label nightly-red if absent, then either opens a tracking issue titled "codegen-live nightly is red" or, if one already exists in any state, reopens it and comments. The comment carries both arm results and the run URL. So a red nightly stops being an email to GitHub default recipient -- the last committer to the cron file -- and becomes an artefact on the board that survives until someone closes it. That is the bead second option in its own cost ordering, and it subsumes the first.

cancelled is in the condition beside failure because a nightly the runner killed also produced no verdict on AGE, and silence is what this closes. always() is what lets the job run at all after a needed job failed. Scheduled runs only: on workflow_dispatch someone is already watching, and on a pull request live-smoke red check is the signal.

NOT SHIPPED, and it is why gqlc-zqa3 exists rather than this bead staying open: the disablement half. GitHub disables cron-triggered workflows after 60 days of repository inactivity, and it does so REPO-WIDE, so codegen-live nightly and vuln.yml weekly go dark together and neither can witness the other. Only a pull_request-triggered check can see it, and whether that check should BLOCK merges is a real trade -- fail-closed blocks every PR on an infrastructure state unrelated to the change, fail-open is a detector that exits 0. That decision is recorded as the open question on gqlc-zqa3 rather than taken here at 6am with nobody to ask.

THE THIRD HAZARD IN THE DESCRIPTION IS SETTLED, first-party, and it is worse than "worth closing at the same time". PR #1323 / run 32622299816 measured that a required context concluding SKIPPED reads as SATISFIED by this repo branch protection: the PR read UNSTABLE, not BLOCKED, with codegen-fence skipped. So the warning the bead wanted on live-smoke-age is now not a caution but a measured fact, and the comment above that job already states it. The job id must stay off master required-check list. See gqlc-yc6x.

UNVERIFIED, stated plainly: nightly-alert has never run. It is skipped on pull requests by construction, so PR #1331 green checks witness only that it parses, that actionlint accepts it, and that its condition excludes the pull_request event. Its first real exercise is the next failing nightly. If it is broken, the failure mode is a red nightly-alert job inside an already-red run -- loud, not silent. A deliberate test would be a workflow_dispatch with the event condition temporarily relaxed; not done, because the fleet is halted and dispatching the live codegen-live workflow was out of scope tonight.

title: codegen: dollarTag is computed on bytes the emitted raw string does not carry
description:
Both backends emit a query's text as a Go RAW string literal:

    internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go:89
    internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:179
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, "const %sQueryText = `%s`\n\n", p.Bare, p.SourceText)

Those two lines are byte-identical, so this is epic-wide, not an AGE gap.

## The invariant that breaks

Go discards carriage returns inside raw string literals -- it is in the spec,
not an implementation detail. So the VALUE of the emitted constant is
p.SourceText with every \r removed, while everything computed at generate time
was computed on p.SourceText WITH them. I checked internal/queryfile for
normalisation and found none, so a CRLF-authored .cypher file carries \r into
SourceText and the two byte strings genuinely differ.

For neo4j the consequence is cosmetic: \r\n and \n are the same query to the
server.

For AGE it is not, because dollarTag (age/render_queries.go:52) chooses the
dollar-quote delimiter by scanning the text, and gqlc-35yu.7 established that
the delimiter must be chosen against exactly the bytes the parser will scan --
that was B1, where a tag occurrence straddling the text/tag boundary produced
generated code that could not run. This is the same invariant failing for a
different reason: dollarTag scans the pre-emission bytes, and the parser sees
the post-emission ones. Removing \r can create a $gqlc-shaped occurrence that
dollarTag never saw.

## Reachability is narrow -- confirm before investing

Ordinary CRLF puts \r at line ends, which cannot forge $gqlc$: a trailing
`$gqlc\r\n` still has \n after the token, not $. Breaking it needs a bare \r
INSIDE the token, e.g. `$gql\rc` at the very end of the text, which no normal
authoring produces. That is why the .7 reviewer filed it non-blocking and why I
did not hold the merge for it.

Do NOT start by writing the fix. Start by deciding whether the reachable set is
empty. If it is, the right change may just be to normalise line endings at
queryfile read time so generate-time and emission-time bytes are the same by
construction, which kills the class rather than the instance -- and which is
probably worth doing anyway for golden stability across checkouts with
different autocrlf settings.

## Whichever way it goes, leave a fence

.7's TestDollarTagClosesOnlyAtTheEnds (age/render_queries_test.go) covers the
predicate but feeds it strings directly, so it cannot see this: the gap is
between what dollarTag is HANDED and what is EMITTED. A fence has to compare
the emitted constant's value against the bytes the tag was chosen on.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.

REACHABILITY DECIDED 2026-09-02, agent-j — NOT empty. Measured with the real CLI
(built from HEAD 734b8730, `gqlc generate` on a scratch project, apache-age-pgx-v5).
Two reachable shapes, BOTH exit 0 and emit corrupt Go:

  1. Bare CR inside a Cypher string literal, forging the tag. Source
     `... <> '$gq<CR>lc$' ...` emits
         const crProbeQueryText = `MATCH (p:Person) WHERE toString(p.id) <> '$gqlc$' RETURN p.id AS id`
         stmt, err := q.cypherStmt("$gqlc$", crProbeQueryText, ...)
     dollarTag was handed bytes with no `$gqlc$` in them; the parser gets bytes
     that have one. This is the bead's predicted B1 failure, and it reproduces.

  2. Bare CR BETWEEN TOKENS — needs no string literal and no tag at all.
     Cypher treats CR as whitespace so `MATCH (p:Person)<CR>RETURN p.id AS id`
     parses and resolves; the raw literal drops the CR and the emitted constant
     is `MATCH (p:Person)RETURN p.id AS id`, which is not a Cypher query. The
     defect is therefore WIDER than the dollar tag: any CR corrupts the emitted
     text, and neo4j is not cosmetic-only as the description supposes.

TWO FINDINGS AGAINST THE DESCRIPTION'S PREMISES:

  A. "a CRLF-authored .cypher file carries \r into SourceText" is FALSE.
     internal/queryfile/parse.go:32 reads with bufio.NewScanner + default
     ScanLines, which drops the CR of a CRLF; bodyText's TrimSpace then takes
     any CR at the very start/end of the body. Measured: a CRLF file and an LF
     file emit byte-identical constants. So the proposed remedy — normalise
     line endings at read time "for golden stability across autocrlf checkouts"
     — fixes nothing that is broken; that stability already holds, and it would
     not touch shape 1 or shape 2 either, since neither CR is a line ending.

  B. Lone-CR (classic Mac) line endings are ALREADY refused upstream: the whole
     file is one ScanLines line, so the annotation grammar rejects it with
     ErrMalformedAnnotation.

So every CR that reaches SourceText is CONTENT, never a line ending. Stripping
it at read time would silently rewrite a user's string literal. The remedy is
to REFUSE, at internal/codegen/prepare.go:638 beside the existing backtick
check, for the identical reason already written into the
out_of_c6_scope_backtick_text fixture: the emission carries the text through a
Go raw string literal, which cannot hold the byte faithfully. One guard on the
shared prepare path covers both backends.

FIXED on fix/gqlc-7f9a-dollartag-emitted-bytes, PR #2125 (Closes #656, verified
via closingIssuesReferences -> [656]). One commit, f72696d0.

REMEDY: refuse, at internal/codegen/prepare.go beside the backtick, per the
reachability decision above. NOT normalised at read time -- every CR reaching

    ErrMalformedAnnotation -- one line the annotation grammar rejects.

title: codegen tests: sweep the type-map tables against their domain, not a hand-counted length
description:
internal/codegen/age/types_test.go and internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go (:45, :60, :96, :118, :155) drive their type-map assertions from hand-written literal tables. Both carried require.Len(table, <literal count>) assertions, which assert that a literal sitting directly above has the length someone counted by hand: they fire only if an editor changes the table and forgets the number, and when they fire they name nothing about what was lost. The AGE ones were removed in gqlc-35yu.6; the neo4j ones remain.

Removing them leaves a real gap: deleting a row from a table now fails nothing, so a type silently stops being tested.

Fix: assert domain COVERAGE, not length — the union of the representable and unrepresentable tables must ElementsMatch the full domain, the way TestRunDriverAxis sweeps config.DriverValues(). That bites on both growth and shrink and is not tautological, because the expected side is derived rather than counted.

Blocker: the enumerators do not exist. There is no graph.PropertyTypeValues(), no resolver.TemporalValues(), no resolver.ScalarValues() — config.DriverValues() exists only because the YAML loader needed one. This bead adds them to internal/graph and internal/resolver and then sweeps both backends. Note graph.PropertyType is an OPEN string type, so its enumerator is a maintained list rather than a closed set, and the enumerator itself needs a fence.

Do both backends in one change: fixing one leaves the same hole plus an inconsistency.

Out of scope: typeMap.Temporal returning "any" for every kind with no rejection channel is gqlc-9n6t. Temporal has no switch at all, so it has neither growth nor shrink coverage today — but that fence and 9n6t's rejection channel are the same edit, so 9n6t owns it.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on gqlc-nhv64.

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
PR #2207 opened 2026-09-02 (branch feat/gqlc-fb4a-type-map-domain-sweep), 3 commits.

WHAT LANDED. Five sweeps moved from size to membership: neo4j TestTypeMapTemporal/TestTypeMapScalar/TestDriverCarrier and age TestTypeMapTemporal/TestTypeMapScalar. The AGE scalar one had NO obligation at all — gqlc-35yu.6 removed its count and nothing replaced it, so deleting a row failed nothing.

THE FINDING. TestDriverCarrier's require.Len(tests, 23) was missing 22 of the 45 Go types the type table can emit — the entire isSliceType branch, which is the FIRST thing driverCarrier does, plus both exclusions that branch is built around ([]byte and []any). isSliceType's own doc comment argues those two are load-bearing rather than an optimisation, and neither had a row.

MEASURED, per guard and never in aggregate. Each of the four vocabulary guards killed on a size-preserving mutant (duplicate one kind, drop another). The control that matters: with require.Len(t, tests, 6) restored over the IDENTICAL 6-row mutant table (ScalarFloat twice, ScalarNull absent), the package reports ok. driverCarrier was screened against a real emitter mutation — deleting the isSliceType branch from types.go — where master's TestDriverCarrier says ok and this branch fails.

The branch was covered by goldens and the decoder runner, just not by the test whose job is to pin driverCarrier's contract. What changes is where the failure lands and that a new emitted type owes a row automatically. No behaviour changed and none was wrong — driverCarrier already answers correctly at all 45. This is a coverage hole closed, not a defect fixed.

THE BEAD'S BLOCKER WAS PARTLY STALE. graph.PropertyTypeValues() was not added: gqlc-2l8v has since converted the property sweeps to graphPropertyTypes, an AST read of internal/graph's own const specs, which is stronger than a maintained list and needs no fence. The derivation reuses it. resolver.ScalarValues/TemporalValues WERE added, built from the iota sentinels. Scalar had no successor sentinel at all, which is why its sweep counted to 6 by hand; ScalarCount now mirrors TemporalCount.

title: vuln: govulncheck never scans the codegen_live dependency tree
description:
`just vuln` runs `govulncheck ./...` untagged and against the ROOT module only. Two consequences, both meaning the live battery's dependencies have never been scanned:

1. Untagged: files behind //go:build codegen_live are outside the default build configuration, so govulncheck does not load them. gqlc-3eyw fixed exactly this blindness for golangci-lint and go vet by putting the tag in .golangci.yml — govulncheck reads neither that config nor the tag, so it is the one gate that inherited nothing from that change.

2. Root module only: the live battery lives in the NESTED module test/data/codegen, which has its own go.mod. The root go.mod has no require or replace on it, so `go list ./...` at root emits zero packages from that tree. Its dependency graph — testcontainers-go, the neo4j Go driver, docker/docker and their transitive trees — is invisible to the root scan by module boundary, independent of build tags.

That dependency set is large and network-facing. It is test-only and never ships in a user binary, which is why this is P2 and not P1, but it does run in CI with credentials in the environment.

FIX: extend the vuln recipe to cover both axes — the codegen_live tag and the nested module — mirroring how test-codegen-fence already reaches into test/data/codegen. Prove it the way gqlc-3eyw proved its claims: demonstrate the scan reports a known-vulnerable pin before trusting a green result.

PROVENANCE: raised as NIT 3 in the gqlc-3eyw adversarial review (2026-08-01), out of scope there. Verified by grep: no direct govulncheck invocation exists outside the just recipe.
notes:
Design forks resolved while fixing the scan (all conclusions measured, govulncheck v1.6.0, DB 2026-07-27):

1. The bead premise was incomplete. Adding -tags codegen_live and scanning the nested module is necessary but NOT sufficient. Measured: with the battery as package fixtures (in-package tests), `govulncheck -tags codegen_live -test ./...` in test/data/codegen scanned 9 modules — pgx, neo4j v5/v6, x/text, x/sync, pgpassfile, pgservicefile, puddle. testcontainers, moby/docker, otel and x/crypto were still absent. Cause: govulncheck keys loaded packages by import path, so the in-package test variant `p [p.test]` collides with plain `p` and loses; anything only that variant imports drops out of the scanned module set with no diagnostic. Isolated in a minimal module with a single-variable A/B (identical deps, identical flags, only `package v` vs `package v_test` changed): in-package reported nothing, external reported the vulnerability with a call trace.

2. Chose to convert the live battery to `package fixtures_test` rather than work around the scanner. Alternatives rejected: (a) -mode=binary on `go test -c -tags codegen_live` output — measured dead, `go version -m` shows a test binary embeds zero dep records, so binary mode saw 1 module and found nothing; (b) -scan module — measured worse, 7 modules, it is derived from loaded packages too, not from go.mod requires; (c) adding a tagged non-test file that imports testcontainers purely to widen the graph — a decoy with no other reason to exist. The conversion is free here: the nested module non-test files (include.go, contract_age.go) export nothing and the battery references none of them. Effect measured: 9 -> 54 modules scanned.

3. Positive control, as the bead asked. Pinned golang.org/x/crypto to v0.30.0 via replace (MVS floor from testcontainers-go v0.43.0 is v0.51.0, so a require edit cannot downgrade it; source mode honours replace, verified separately — -scan module does not). Before the conversion that pin produced ZERO findings. After, it produced 7 called vulnerabilities from 2 modules. The scan is now demonstrably capable of failing.

4. The scan was red on the real tree, not just hypothetically. Once the live tree became visible it reported 6 called vulnerabilities, exit 3: GO-2026-5970 (x/text v0.37.0, reached via pgx.Connect) plus GO-2026-5013/5017/5018/5019/5020 in x/crypto/ssh v0.51.0, all reached via testcontainers.GenericContainer. Only the x/text one was visible through the drivers; the other five needed the package conversion. Fixed by bumping the nested module to x/text v0.39.0 and x/crypto v0.52.0 (go mod tidy also moved x/sync v0.20.0 -> v0.21.0). Gate is now exit 0.

5. Added a guard to test-codegen-fence asserting no live file declares `package fixtures`. Reasoning: the fix silently depends on a source convention with no compiler or tool enforcement, and this bead exists precisely because a required gate was silently scanning nothing. Put it in the fence because that is the only always-run required job over the nested module — `just vuln` itself only runs on dependency changes, so a guard there would not fire on a PR that only changed the package clause.

6. Root module also got -test (previously godog, testify, rapid, gherkin, messages and go-memdb were unscanned: 32 -> 43 modules). Measured clean.

7. Residual, all uncalled so the gate is green by govulncheck design: GO-2026-5158 (otel v1.41.0, imported not called), GO-2026-5932 (x/crypto/openpgp, no fix available), GO-2026-5841 (klauspost/compress v1.18.5, required not imported). Not bumped — churn on indirect deps with no reachable exposure.

NO JOB IDS CHANGED. The govulncheck job id in .github/workflows/vuln.yml is untouched, no job added, renamed or split, so the required status contexts (lint, test, tidy, actionlint, govulncheck, live-smoke, codegen-fence) are all still produced. The workflow change is confined to the dependency-change detection paths, which now also diff test/data/codegen/go.mod and go.sum.
HANDOFF 2026-08-01. Branch fix/govulncheck-live-tree clean at 0475cdb. Adversarial review was dispatched and DIED ON SESSION QUOTA before returning a verdict — NO VERDICT EXISTS, do not merge. Re-dispatch.

Manager verification already done (do not redo): job ids are IDENTICAL between f1fd981 and the branch in BOTH .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/vuln.yml, so no required branch-protection context was silently deleted — this was the highest-stakes check because GitHub derives a check context from the job id and a rename blocks every future PR repo-wide. Dependency bumps confirmed real in test/data/codegen/go.mod (x/crypto 0.51.0->0.52.0, x/sync 0.20.0->0.21.0, x/text 0.37.0->0.39.0), and 'just vuln' exits 0 on both modules.

Still UNREVIEWED and the highest-value attacks for the next reviewer: (a) does the live battery still actually RUN after the package clause changed to fixtures_test in live_age_session_test.go / live_age_test.go / live_neo4j_test.go / live_test.go — an external test package loses access to unexported identifiers, so it could compile-and-skip while still printing ok; always -count=1 since Go serves a cached ok in 0.2s without starting a container and a real run is ~18-25s; (b) reproduce the positive control independently (pin x/crypto low via replace, confirm the gate goes red, restore exactly); (c) can vuln.yml's widened change-detection still fail open — what changes the dependency graph WITHOUT touching the four listed go.mod/go.sum files; (d) does the new 'package fixtures' guard in test-codegen-fence actually fire, and is its file-matching narrow enough to be escaped by a live file in a subdirectory.
close_reason: Merged as PR #725. govulncheck now scans both modules under -tags codegen_live with -test; the nested battery converted to package fixtures_test to escape the x/vuln p [p.test] path collision (9 -> 54 modules). Six called vulnerabilities found and fixed (x/text v0.39.0, x/crypto v0.52.0). Two guards added: a fence assertion that no live file declares package fixtures, and a ratchet on the root module's residual blind set. vuln.yml's dependency probe no longer fails open. Both go directives bumped to 1.26.5 after the first real scan found 5 called stdlib vulnerabilities. ADR 0026.

title: codegen: TypeMap.Temporal has no rejection channel, so an unrepresentable temporal silently generates 'any'
description:
`internal/codegen/typemap.go:13` gives `Property` a rejection channel and denies one to `Temporal`:

    Property(pt graph.PropertyType) (goType string, ok bool)   // ok=false -> ErrUnrepresentableWidth
    Temporal(k resolver.Temporal) string                        // documented 'Total over the closed enum'
    Scalar(k resolver.Scalar) string                            // documented 'Total over the closed enum'

'Total over the closed enum' was true while neo4j was the only backend. AGE falsifies it: agtype carries no temporal scalar, so there is no faithful Go carrier for ANY temporal kind. Surfaced during gqlc-35yu.6.

## The failure mode is silent wrong code, not an error

With no way to say 'I cannot carry this', the AGE TypeMap returns `"any"` for every kind (`internal/codegen/age/types.go:84-86`). A query projecting a temporal expression against AGE therefore generates a column typed `any` that no decoder can fill — code that compiles, passes the fence, and is meaningless at runtime. Compare the `Property` path, which refuses at generate time with `ErrUnrepresentableWidth` naming the offending width. Same class of gap, opposite outcome, purely because of the missing bool.

Generate-time refusal is the established posture in this codebase for 'this backend cannot represent that'. Temporal expressions escape it by accident of interface shape, not by decision.

## Reachability

Unreachable at C0 (no query methods emitted), which is why gqlc-35yu.6 ships with the hole open and a comment acknowledging it. It becomes reachable as soon as query methods exist for AGE — gqlc-35yu.7 onward — and it is squarely load-bearing at gqlc-35yu.11, which decides the temporal encodings.

## Shape of the fix

Widen to `Temporal(k resolver.Temporal) (goType string, ok bool)` mirroring `Property`, route ok=false to a sentinel naming the kind (either reuse the unrepresentable family or add a sibling), update the neo4j TypeMap to return ok=true unconditionally, and let AGE return ok=false until the temporal arm commits an encoding. Mechanical apart from the sentinel choice.

Audit `Scalar` at the same time — it carries the identical 'Total' claim. AGE appears to cover the scalar enum today, so it may be genuinely total; confirm rather than assume, and if it is total, say WHY in the doc comment instead of restating the claim that just failed for Temporal.
acceptance_criteria: TypeMap.Temporal exposes a rejection channel; a temporal projection against a backend that cannot carry it fails at generate time with a sentinel naming the kind, proven by a negative fixture; no backend returns a placeholder Go type for a kind it cannot decode; the Scalar totality claim is either verified and justified in the doc comment or given the same treatment.
notes:
=== ADDITIONAL SCOPE (from gqlc-35yu.6 round 4, 2026-08-01): Temporal has no drift fence either. ===
internal/codegen/age/types.go declares:
    func (typeMap) Temporal(resolver.Temporal) string { return "any" }
It IGNORES ITS ARGUMENT. There is no switch, so the exhaustive linter has
nothing to hold: resolver can GAIN a Temporal kind and nothing in the age
package notices. Property and Scalar both switch and are exhaustive-linted, so
this is the one type-map entry with no growth coverage at all.

Folded here rather than filed separately because the fence and this bead's
rejection channel are the same edit: once Temporal can refuse a kind it has to
branch per kind, and the branch is what the linter holds.

Related: gqlc-fb4a adds domain-sweep fences (ElementsMatch against a canonical
enumeration) to the type-map tables in both backends, which is the SHRINK half
of the same problem. It deliberately leaves Temporal to this bead.

Reachability note: harmless while AGE emits no query methods. gqlc-35yu.7 is
where query methods first appear for AGE, and its notes already carry the
guardrail forbidding enrolment of any fixture with a temporal projection for
apache-age-pgx-v5 until this lands.
=== REACHABILITY CLAIM CORRECTED (manager, verified 2026-08-01 during .7 review) ===

The Reachability section says the silent-'any' hole "becomes reachable as soon
as query methods exist for AGE -- gqlc-35yu.7 onward". That is FALSE. .7 ships
query methods and the hole stays shut. Surfaced by the .7 reviewer; I verified
it in the .7 worktree rather than taking the report's word.

typeMap.Temporal has exactly two callers, prepare.go:752 and prepare.go:998,
both inside codegen.Prepare. For AGE, nothing reaches Prepare with a temporal
in it, because .6 reordered generate() so rejectUnservedQueries runs BEFORE
Prepare, and unservedColumn (age/errors.go:78) rejects on both channels:
  - resolver.ResolvedTemporal is named in the reject arm outright, alongside
    ResolvedList, so a temporal projection and a list of temporals both go.
  - a temporal-WIDTH property goes through scalarWidth (errors.go:131), which
    is `ty, ok := typeMap{}.Property(pt); return ok && ty != "any"` -- so a
    width the AGE Property table refuses OR types as "any" is rejected too.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD. The defect is real but it is LATENT, not live: no
query that reaches Prepare on the AGE path can carry a temporal, so no user can
currently generate the meaningless `any` column this bead describes. It becomes
live at gqlc-35yu.11, which lifts the rejection when it commits the temporal
encodings. Fix it BEFORE .11 lands the encodings, not urgently as a shipping
bug. The [BUG] type and the "silent wrong code" framing are both still accurate
about the interface shape; they overstate the current exposure.

The ADDITIONAL SCOPE note below is UNAFFECTED and is now the stronger half of
this bead: Temporal ignoring its argument means resolver can gain a kind and
the age package notices nothing. That drift gap is live today regardless of
whether the value is reachable, because it is about growth, not calls.

Also settled by the same review, so it is not re-opened here: .7 correctly
enrols NO temporal fixture for apache-age-pgx-v5, and the absence is fenced
rather than merely observed -- there are positive tests pinning both rejection
channels ("a temporal column is dropped" pinning `column "t" projects
temporal(date)`, and TestTypeMapPropertyRejectionReachesTheCaller pinning
ErrUnrepresentableWidth for TIMESTAMP). Those two tests are what will go red if
.11 lifts the rejection without widening the interface, so they are this bead's
tripwire. Do not delete them when widening -- change them deliberately.

Agent killed mid-task by a quota limit, not by a failure. Dirty set spans the rejection channel end to end: internal/codegen/{typemap,prepare,errors}.go plus both backends' types.go and the conformance test, plus a new untracked invalid fixture test/data/codegen/invalid/unrepresentable_temporal_date_column/. Do not discard; read the diff before resuming.

title: lint: build-tagged code (codegen_live) is outside every lint gate
description:
`.golangci.yml` sets no `build-tags`, so golangci-lint analyses only the default build configuration. Every file behind `//go:build codegen_live` — today `test/data/codegen/live_test.go` and `live_neo4j_test.go` — is invisible to `just lint` and to `just test-codegen-fence` (whose `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` are also untagged).

Scope the damage accurately: COMPILE and behaviour coverage do exist, because `.github/workflows/codegen-live.yml` runs the real `just test-codegen-live` against docker on every PR. What is missing is LINT coverage specifically. So the failure mode is not broken code shipping — it is that the tagged files silently diverge from the standards the rest of the tree is held to, and nobody finds out.

Surfaced during gqlc-35yu.4. Running `golangci-lint run --build-tags codegen_live` in the nested module reports 10 issues against that bead's new seam: 8 x ireturn, 2 x thelper. (An earlier draft of this description said 8 issues / 6 ireturn; the measured inventory in the NOTES is authoritative and was confirmed a third time during review.) The pre-refactor baseline was coincidentally clean, so nothing regressed against a gate that was running — the gate was never running.

## Why this is not just 'set build-tags and fix them'

The two linters disagree with the code for opposite reasons and need opposite treatment:

- `ireturn` fires on the adapter constructors and per-fixture querier accessors. Returning an interface IS the seam that lets one scenario body serve N backends; that is the point of the bead, not an accident. Needs an allow-list entry, not a code change.
- `thelper` wants `t.Helper()` on the scenario bodies. Adding it would mark them as helpers and push require-failures up to the caller — destroying the failure-pointing that gqlc-35yu.4 carries as an explicit acceptance criterion, and that the pre-refactor file's inlined bodies existed to preserve. Satisfying this linter would make the suite worse. Needs suppression for scenario bodies.

So the resolution is a config decision with a rationale, not a mechanical cleanup, which is why it is its own bead rather than scope creep on .4.

## Growth

gqlc-35yu.8 adds the AGE live adapter arm behind the same tag. Every bead after it that touches live code widens the unlinted surface. Cheaper to settle the config before .8 than after.
acceptance_criteria: just lint (or an equivalent gate) analyses codegen_live-tagged files; the ireturn allow-list covers the adapter seam with a recorded reason; thelper does not fire on scenario bodies and the failure-pointing acceptance criterion of gqlc-35yu.4 still holds — proven by breaking an assertion and showing the failure points at the scenario's own line.
notes:
Schedule opportunistically alongside gqlc-35yu.7, i.e. after .4 merges and before .8 starts. Not a blocking edge on .8 (see the note there), but the cost grows once .8 lands more tagged code.
=== MEASURED INVENTORY (manager, 2026-08-01, on branch test/codegen-live-battery @ 23384c3) ===
Ran the tagged config by hand so whoever picks this up does not have to:

title: codegen/age: temporal encodings per spike table, gated on live round-trips
description:
Implement the spike-validated temporal encoding table in the AGE backend: param encode + decode helpers for TIMESTAMP/DATE/DURATION/zoned types (fallback table pending spike: timestamp=epoch-micros integer, date=ISO string, duration=ISO-8601 string, zoned=offset-preserving string). The Go surface stays identical to the neo4j target (time.Time etc.) — only the wire representation differs, owned entirely by emitted helpers. Any type the spike marked unfaithful becomes a generate-time first-offender error naming property, type, and backend, extending the existing unrepresentable-width taxonomy (invalid fixture per errored type).

Gates are live, not just golden: per encoding, a round-trip scenario (write via :exec, read back, require.Equal on the original value) AND an ordering probe (WHERE n.ts > param returns the correct subset) where the encoding claims ordering. Duration claims no ordering (not totally ordered even in neo4j) — its gate is component-faithful round-trip only.

Document the convention in the generated package doc header: encoded values are a gqlc convention; other tools reading the graph see the raw encoding.
acceptance_criteria: Temporal fixtures enrolled for AGE pass goldens; live round-trip + ordering scenarios green per encoding; unfaithful types have invalid fixtures proving the generate-time error; zoned round-trip preserves the offset (not normalized to UTC) with a test pinning it.
notes:
=== SPIKE gqlc-35yu.5 OUTCOME — THE ENCODING TABLE THIS BEAD IMPLEMENTS ===
Owner-approved 2026-07-31. Full ordering battery + captured output in
gqlc-35yu.5.

AGE has NO native temporal types (prior CONFIRMED empirically, not just from
the header enum). No temporal casts exist — the full pg_cast table is captured
in the spike. The only temporal function is timestamp(), which returns epoch-
MILLIS (note: millis, not micros — do not confuse it with the encoding below).

FINAL TABLE:
  timestamp/instant | epoch-MICROS int64                     | CONFIRMED
  date              | ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, zero-padded   | CONFIRMED
  duration          | total-MICROS int64                     | AMENDED
  zoned datetime    | TWO int64 props: <f> epoch-micros      | AMENDED
                    |   plus <f>Offset offset-seconds        |
  calendar duration | no faithful encoding — months/years    | generate-time
                    |   are not a fixed micro count          |   error

THE GATE IS ORDERING, NOT ROUND-TRIPPING. Both amended encodings round-tripped
fine and still failed; that is exactly why they were amended:
  - duration as ISO-8601 string sorted P1D, PT10H, PT1H, PT2H, PT90M, and
    WHERE v > 'PT2H' returned only PT90M (1.5h) — one false positive and two
    false negatives.
  - zoned as an offset-preserving string returned an 07:00Z row for
    WHERE v > '...08:00+00:00'.
  - zoned as a map {t,o} ALSO sorts wrong (jsonb key order) AND would force
    gqlc to rewrite user ORDER BY. The FLAT SIDECAR was chosen because it
    keeps the sort key as the property itself, so user ORDER BY passes through
    untouched. Preserve that property.
So every encoding here needs a live ORDER BY + range-predicate test, not just
an encode/decode round-trip test.

date stays a STRING by owner decision despite agtype string comparison using
DB COLLATION rather than byte order (readability in the stored graph wins;
ISO dates are fixed-width digits and hyphens). If a collation is ever found
where ISO dates misorder, that reopens this — worth one explicit test.

STILL OPEN, NOT COVERED BY THE SPIKE: time-of-day encoding. Resolve it in this
bead, using the same ordering battery.

The encoding table it was implementing is the owner-approved spike result and is SETTLED — do not relitigate it:
  timestamp / instant  -> epoch-MICROS int64            (CONFIRMED by live spike)
  date                 -> ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' zero-padded  (CONFIRMED)
  duration             -> total-MICROS int64            (AMENDED)
  zoned datetime       -> TWO int64 props: <f> epoch-micros + <f>Offset offset-seconds, flat sidecar (AMENDED)

The gate is ORDERING, not round-tripping. Evidence from the spike: ISO-8601 duration strings sort P1D, PT10H, PT1H, PT2H, PT90M and 'WHERE v > PT2H' returns only PT90M. The flat sidecar was chosen because it keeps the sort key as the property itself, so a user ORDER BY passes through untouched.

Resuming now. The successor is told to judge the inherited diff on its merits rather than assume it is correct.
=== TIME-OF-DAY DECIDED (the one open row) — 2026-08-03 ===
TIME / LOCAL TIME = microseconds since midnight, int64, in
[0, 86_400_000_000). Offset-bearing TIME normalises to UTC before
counting and carries its offset in the same flat <f>Offset sidecar
the zoned datetime uses; LOCAL TIME carries no sidecar.

Rationale, on the bead's own gate (ordering, not round-tripping): a
non-negative fixed-range integer is ordered by agtype's integer
comparison exactly as chronology within a day, so ORDER BY n.t and
WHERE n.t > $t are answered correctly with the author's text run
verbatim (ADR 0005) — same argument that carried ENC1 and the amended
duration encoding live, one width down. UTC-normalising is not
optional: an offset-preserving count makes two spellings of one moment
compare unequal, which is the exact defect that killed the
offset-preserving zoned-datetime string in this spike. The day-boundary
wrap a UTC normalisation can produce is a property of the width (a bare
time of day has no date to carry into), not of the encoding.

The table is now complete:
  timestamp/instant | epoch-MICROS int64                   | CONFIRMED
  date              | ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, zero-padded | CONFIRMED
  duration          | total-MICROS int64                   | AMENDED
  zoned datetime    | <f> epoch-micros + <f>Offset secs    | AMENDED
  time / local time | micros-since-midnight int64,         | DECIDED
                    |   UTC-normalised, + <f>Offset        |
  calendar duration | none — generate-time error           | PERMANENT

=== WHAT LANDED (81d2205 on feat/age-temporal-encodings) ===
Only TIMESTAMP is served. typeMap.Property admits graph.TypeTimestamp ->
time.Time; encode via agtypeMicros / agtypeNullableMicros, decode via
agtypeInstant, zone via agtypeZone reading the flat <f>Offset sidecar.

typeMap.Temporal still refuses ALL SIX kinds and that is deliberate. An
earlier working tree admitted TemporalDateTime; reverted. A temporal
*expression* column exists only because the query called a temporal
constructor, and AGE 1.7.0 has none (date/datetime/localdatetime/
duration/toTimestamp all "function does not exist"; one hit in 348
ag_catalog functions, age_timestamp, an epoch-MILLIS integer that is not
a temporal value). Admitting a kind emits a compiling method the server
rejects at run time — worse than the failure ADR 0025 built the channel
to prevent. No `default` arm in either Temporal switch, so `exhaustive`
with default-signifies-exhaustive: true remains the growth fence.

=== CARRIER, NOT ENCODING, IS WHAT BLOCKS THE OTHER FOUR ===
DATE, TIME, LOCAL TIME and DURATION have settled encodings (above) and
still refuse in Property, because every other backend spells them with a
neo4j driver type (dbtype.Date / dbtype.Time / dbtype.LocalTime /
dbtype.Duration) and a pgx package cannot declare one without making the
caller-facing surface vary by backend. TIMESTAMP is admitted precisely
because time.Time is what neo4j spells it with too. Unblocking the other
four is a backend-invariant temporal carrier, not more encoding work.

=== KNOWN GAP: THE OFFSET SIDECAR HAS NO WRITE PATH ===
agtypeZone is the read half only. gqlc binds the instant alone; writing
<f>Offset would need gqlc to inject a $<name>Offset parameter into the
author's CREATE/SET, which ADR 0005 forbids, and an auto-bound parameter
does not resolve anyway (confirmed: a non-property parameter fails C6
scope). A graph that wants its original zone back must name the sidecar
in its own query text. Documented in the emitted helper docs. Value
written through gqlc reads back at the same instant, in UTC.

neo4j render_queries.zeroValueText routed a single-column :one over a

them: timestamp_projection (entity with a single NON-nullable instant,
and queries that project instants while binding none) and
timestamp_nullable_param (a batch binding a nullable instant and nothing

=== LIVE TESTS ARE UNVERIFIED LOCALLY ===

title: codegen/age: write path — :exec methods and write-param coverage
description:
The :exec cardinality for AGE: CREATE/SET/DELETE query emission through the same server-side param mechanism, zero-column cypher() invocation shape (AGE still requires an AS projection clause — the spike corpus documents the zero/one-column form), and command execution over DBTX.Exec. Completes param-encoding coverage for every property type the scalar stage admits, on the write side.

TDD: red goldens first; the live battery's mixed read-write scenarios (write via :exec, re-read via :one/:many, delete, confirm ErrNoRows) enabled for the AGE arm — these already exist backend-invariantly from the live-refactor bead.
acceptance_criteria: Write-path fixtures enrolled for AGE pass golden + compile gates; mixed read-write live scenarios green on the AGE arm; :exec on a projection-shaped query still rejected by shared admission (existing invalid fixtures run under the AGE target).
notes:
MANAGER NOTE AT START (2026-08-01).

Branch feat/codegen-age-write-path, worktree gqlc-35yu10-write, cut from
cdd09ca (post-.9).

Correction to this bead's own description before anyone acts on it: it says
"the spike corpus documents the zero/one-column form". It does not. I read
gqlc-35yu.5 end to end — it captures the temporal encoding table with ordering
evidence, the param mechanism with server-log proof of server-side binding, and
the agtype result-text corpus for reads. Every cypher() invocation recorded
there projects at least one column from a RETURN. There is no CREATE, SET or
DELETE anywhere in it, and so no evidence for what the AS clause must look like
when the Cypher body returns nothing.

So the write invocation shape is NOT settled by prior work and must not be
assumed from the AGE docs alone. Establish it live against the pinned image
first (apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8... — PostgreSQL 18.1, AGE 1.7.0), record the
exact statement and observed output in this bead the way .5 did, and only then
emit against it. The specific things unproven: the column-definition list AGE
demands for a RETURN-less body, whether a write body may project columns at
all, and what pgconn.CommandTag carries back for a cypher() call (AGE's write
happens inside a set-returning function, so the tag is the SELECT's, not the
CREATE's — if RowsAffected is meaningless the emitted :exec must not pretend
otherwise).

Two drop reasons in internal/codegen/age/errors.go unservedReason() are what
this bead removes: "writes to the graph" (Validated.Statement ==
resolver.StatementWrite) and ":exec returns no rows to decode"
(CardinalityExec). They are separate axes and they come off separately — a
:many that writes and returns rows is a different shape from a :exec that
writes and returns none. Whichever this bead does not serve must keep its drop
reason and keep its invalid fixture.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS, unchanged: string interpolation of user args is banned
unconditionally — only the graph name may be interpolated, escaped and
length-checked; everything else binds. No AI attribution in any commit or PR.

LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-08-01), apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8... — AGE 1.7.0 on
PostgreSQL 18.1. Probes were scratch (psql scripts + two pgx v5 programs);
nothing shipped. The three unproven questions, answered.

(1) The column-definition list for a RETURN-less body must be EXACTLY ONE
ag_catalog.agtype column.

  no AS clause:
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('writeprobe', $$ CREATE (:P {n:1}) $$);
    ERROR:  a column definition list is required for functions returning "record"
  AS () :
    ... $$) AS ();
    ERROR:  syntax error at or near ")"          -- zero columns is not expressible
  two agtype columns:
    ... $$) AS (v0 ag_catalog.agtype, v1 ag_catalog.agtype);
    ERROR:  column definition list for CREATE clause must contain a single
            agtype attribute  (SQLSTATE 42804)
    HINT:   ... cypher($ ... CREATE ... $) AS t(c agtype) ...
  one non-agtype column:  same 42804.
  one agtype column: OK, zero rows returned.

  The same 42804 (text unchanged, still saying "CREATE clause") is what a
  RETURN-less DELETE and a RETURN-less SET give for a two-column list. So the
  emitted shape is "v0 ag_catalog.agtype" whatever the write clause is.

(2) A write body MAY project, and then the list must match the RETURN arity
exactly; a mismatch either way is
    ERROR:  return row and column definition list do not match
  Verified for CREATE ... RETURN p / RETURN p.n, SET ... RETURN p / RETURN
  p.name, MERGE ... RETURN r, DETACH DELETE ... RETURN 1. The existing
  recordShape (one v<i> per RowField) was therefore already correct for
  write-with-projection; only the zero-RowFields case was new.

(3) pgconn.CommandTag is the enclosing SELECT's, not the write's. Measured
through pgx v5.10.0 Conn.Exec:

    CREATE 1 vertex,  bound params      -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    CREATE 3 vertices in one statement  -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    DELETE 2 vertices                   -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    SET on 2 vertices                   -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    DELETE matching nothing             -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    CREATE (p:P {n:5}) RETURN p.n       -> "SELECT 1"  RowsAffected=1
    MATCH (p:P) RETURN p.n  (3 rows)    -> "SELECT 3"  RowsAffected=3

  RowsAffected is the projected row count and nothing else. It cannot tell
  "created three vertices" from "matched nothing". DECISION: the emitted :exec
  returns error alone and discards the tag. Justified twice over — the
  measurement above, and TestBackendInvariantSurface, since the neo4j targets
  emit Method(ctx, ...) error for :exec. A RowsAffected in the AGE signature
  would have broken the surface invariant AND lied.

OTHER LIVE FINDINGS

- All four non-interpolating pgx QueryExecModes (CacheStatement,
  CacheDescribe, DescribeExec, Exec) work on writes. SimpleProtocol — the one
  interpolating mode — fails closed on the write path:
    ERROR:  third argument of cypher function must be a parameter (SQLSTATE 22023)
  Note for the next reader: a QueryExecMode must be passed as the FIRST query
  argument to pgx, not the last; passing it last gives a misleading
  "mismatched param and argument count" (pgx v5 conn.go:41).

title: codegen/age: live adapter arm + nightly CI wiring
description:
Bring the AGE arm into the shared live scenario battery: adapter implementing the per-backend harness interface — apache/age container image pinned by digest, not tag (gqlc-9u5 precedent: tag drift can serve a stale cached PASS from the Go test cache); pgx pool constructed with SessionInit as AfterConnect; seed(cypher) via ag_catalog.cypher over the pool; isolation = unique graph per scenario via EnsureGraph + Cleanup DropGraph, so AGE sub-tests run in parallel (unlike the serialized neo4j DETACH-wipe arms) and the lifecycle helpers get exercised as the isolation mechanism itself.

CI: the arm joins the existing codegen_live nightly/manual job. PR CI wall-time must be untouched — the codegen_live tag boundary already guarantees that; do not add the arm to any PR-triggered workflow. GQLC_SKIP_LIVE behavior extends to the AGE arm. Watch the second nightly run for cache steady-state if any actions/cache path changes (bd memory: first run after a path change is cold).
acceptance_criteria: Shared battery (scalar scenarios) green against a live AGE container locally under -tags codegen_live; nightly job runs the AGE arm and fails red on a seeded assertion break (prove the gate fails, not just that a check exists); AGE sub-tests demonstrably parallel (unique graph names in logs); PR CI workflow diff shows no new PR-time steps; SessionInit FAILURE path covered — a pool whose sessions lack ag_catalog on search_path must fail at pool ACQUISITION, with the test proving the canary discriminates (a canary literal that survives agtype_to_bool would pass on the broken session and must be shown not to be the one shipped).
notes:
SCHEDULING: gqlc-3eyw (codegen_live code is outside every lint gate) is deliberately NOT a blocking dependency of this bead — .8 can ship unlinted exactly as .4 did, and a hard edge would stall the epic critical path on a config decision. But .8 widens the unlinted surface with the AGE adapter arm, so settle gqlc-3eyw BEFORE starting .8 if the slot is free. It is small config work.
=== SessionInit FAILURE-PATH REQUIREMENT, INHERITED FROM .6 (recorded 2026-08-01) ===
.6's notes carry: "Test the failure path, not just the happy path: a connection
whose search_path lacks ag_catalog must be REJECTED by SessionInit, and that
rejection must be observable as a pool-acquisition failure."

.6 is a golden-EMISSION bead — it has no live container and no pool, so that
requirement is not dischargeable there and .6 will not be held for it. It lands
here, where the pool and the container both exist for the first time. Recorded
now so the deferral survives outside a commit message.

WHY IT IS SHARP, NOT CEREMONIAL: the canary's discriminating power depends on
the literal chosen. The .6 review established that
  SELECT '1'::ag_catalog.agtype = '1'::ag_catalog.agtype
fails on a misconfigured session inside agtype_to_bool — i.e. for a reason
unrelated to operator resolution via search_path. A canary using a literal that
happens to survive agtype_to_bool (e.g. 'true') would PASS on a connection with
ag_catalog off the path, which is exactly the deployment the canary exists to
reject. So the failure path is what proves the canary is the right canary; the
happy path proves nothing.

HOW TO APPLY: add a scenario that builds a pool whose AfterConnect runs
SessionInit against a session with ag_catalog deliberately off search_path, and
assert pool acquisition FAILS. Assert on the rejection being observable at
acquire time, not merely that some error exists somewhere.
=== NON-SUPERUSER ARM REQUIREMENT, INHERITED FROM .6 (recorded 2026-08-01) ===
The harness MUST exercise at least one arm connecting as a NON-SUPERUSER role,
not only as postgres.

WHY: .6 round 2 shipped a SessionInit whose first statement was LOAD 'age'. I
verified against the pinned image that LOAD 'age' is superuser-only:

  LOAD 'age' as postgres  -> LOAD, rc=0
  LOAD 'age' as appuser   -> ERROR: access to library "age" is not allowed

Because an error returned from pgxpool's AfterConnect DISCARDS the connection,
that statement bricked the entire pool for any least-privilege role: the pool
would never yield a usable connection at all. A total, deployment-fatal defect.

And it would have sailed straight through this bead's battery, because the
harness connects as postgres. A green live suite would have certified it. The
bug was caught by adversarial review, not by the tests that exist to catch
exactly this class of thing. That is the gap this requirement closes.

HOW TO APPLY: create a role with only the privileges a generated client
actually needs (no SUPERUSER), and run the scalar battery — or at minimum the
pool-construction and one read scenario — as that role. Treat "works as
postgres" as proving nothing about deployability. Any future statement added to
SessionInit is then privilege-checked by construction rather than by review.

Related: LOAD 'age' is now DELETED from SessionInit (see gqlc-35yu.6 notes).
The canary is the loader -- its '+' is an AGE C function, so evaluating it
forces the implicit library load and _PG_init before any user query is parsed.
=== TWO RECORDED FACTS ON THIS BEAD ARE WRONG (verified 2026-08-01) ===

(1) "PR CI wall-time must be untouched -- the codegen_live tag boundary
already guarantees that". FALSE. .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml carried
`on: pull_request` and its own header called it a "PR-blocking merge gate"
(bd gqlc-rvw promoted it). The tag boundary keeps codegen_live out of the
DEFAULT build; it does not keep it out of PR CI, because that workflow passes
the tag explicitly. Adding the AGE arm to `just test-codegen-live` would have
added an apache/age container boot to every pull request.

RESOLUTION: the battery is now split by backend at the recipe level and the
workflow runs one job per backend.
  test-codegen-live        everything (local + as the union)
  test-codegen-live-neo4j  -run TestLiveSmoke -skip TestLiveSmoke/apache-age
  test-codegen-live-age    -run 'TestLiveSmoke|TestAGESessionInit'
                           -skip TestLiveSmoke/neo4j
Job `neo4j` keeps every existing trigger; job `apache-age` carries
`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`. -skip rather than a narrower -run
so an arm named in neither half shows up as skipped instead of silently
vanishing. Verified empirically that -skip does not run the excluded
subtest body: the neo4j half boots only neo4j (18.3s, unchanged), the AGE
half boots only apache/age.

(2) HOW TO APPLY for the SessionInit failure path -- "build a pool whose
AfterConnect runs SessionInit against a session with ag_catalog deliberately
off search_path" -- is NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE. SessionInit's own first statement
unconditionally prepends ag_catalog to the search_path, so no session it runs
on can be off the path by the time the canary executes. Worse, every failure
reachable that way (extension absent, role lacks USAGE) fails the shipped
canary and a weak canary IDENTICALLY, so it does not demonstrate
discrimination at all.

RESOLUTION: decomposed into three separately provable properties, all in
TestAGESessionInit (test/data/codegen/live_age_session_test.go):

  (A) acquisition-time refusal on genuinely broken deployments. Table over
      a role with no USAGE on ag_catalog (SQLSTATE 42501) and a database with
      no age extension (3F000). Each asserts: a plain pgx.Connect on the same
      DSN SUCCEEDS (so it is the session being refused, not the credentials);
      pgxpool.NewWithConfig succeeds; Acquire fails wrapped in "gqlc: AGE
      operator canary"; pool.Stat().TotalConns() == 0.

  (B) acquire-observable A/B, which is the discrimination proof. A database
      with age installed, granted and on the path, from which only
      ag_catalog.+(agtype,agtype) has been removed (ALTER EXTENSION age DROP
      OPERATOR, then DROP OPERATOR). A pool running a hook whose probe is
      'true'::agtype = 'true'::agtype ACQUIRES; a pool running the shipped
      SessionInit FAILS to acquire with 42883. The two hooks share the
      shipped hook's own search_path statement, captured from it via a
      pgx.QueryTracer, so the probe is the only thing they differ in.

  (C) statement replay on a real off-search_path session, with the canary
      taken from the tracer capture rather than retyped. Rejected-literal
      table:
        shipped '1'+'1' = '2'  -> 42883 (operator resolution)
        'true' = 'true'        -> succeeds, returns true (would false-pass)
        '1' = '1'              -> 22023, cannot cast agtype integer to
                                  type boolean, i.e. fails for an unrelated
                                  reason
      NOTE: .6's note names the '1' = '1' failure as being "inside
      agtype_to_bool". Confirmed exactly: cannot_cast_agtype_value,
      agtype.c:2744. Its SQLSTATE is 22023, not 42846.

  (D) a fence that every AGE target's emitted SessionInit issues byte-identical
      statements, which is what licenses one pool serving handles generated
      into several packages.
=== NON-SUPERUSER ARM: MINIMUM GRANT SET, EMPIRICALLY DERIVED ===

.6's note implies a bare `appuser` could run the canary. It cannot. A plain
LOGIN role with no grants gets, on the shipped canary:
  ERROR: 42501: permission denied for schema ag_catalog
AGE grants nothing to PUBLIC. The minimum set a generated client needs is
three grants, one per emitted requirement (ageAppGrants in live_age_test.go):
  GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA ag_catalog          every emitted statement names it
  GRANT SELECT ON ag_catalog.ag_graph       EnsureGraph/DropGraph existence guard
  GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE <db>             create_graph builds a schema
EVERY pool in the package -- the battery arm and all of TestAGESessionInit's
pools -- logs in as this role. The superuser connection exists only for
bootstrap DDL and is closed before anything under test opens.

=== MUTATION PROOFS (all run against real containers, -count=1) ===

Requirement 1, the canary discriminates. Mutated the EMITTER
(internal/codegen/age/render_graph.go canaryStmt) to
  SELECT 'true'::ag_catalog.agtype = 'true'::ag_catalog.agtype
and regenerated every AGE golden, i.e. the mutation is "the emitter shipped a
weaker canary", not a hand-edit of one file. Result: exit 1 in 5.65s, red on
exactly the two discrimination assertions and nothing else --
  .../the_shipped_canary  "An error is expected but got nil"      (property C)
  .../the shipped canary refuses a session a weaker probe admits
                          "An error is expected but got nil"      (property B)
Property (A) stayed GREEN under the mutation, which is the bead's point stated
as a test result: a coarse broken-deployment test cannot tell the two canaries
apart, so only B and C carry the requirement.

Requirement 2, the non-superuser arm. Two mutations, run as a pair:
  2a  removed GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE from ageAppGrants
      -> TestLiveSmoke/apache-age-pgx-v5 exit 1, both scenarios red with
         gqlc: ensure graph "gqlc_live_1" (the name bound at New):
         ERROR: permission denied for database postgres (SQLSTATE 42501)
      The arm genuinely runs on the limited role's privileges.
  2b  same grant still removed, arm's pool DSN switched to ageSuperuser
      -> exit 0, PASS in 4.686s.
2b is .6's recorded defect reproduced in miniature: a battery that connects as
postgres certifies green a deployment the application role cannot run at all.

=== NIGHTLY GATE FAILS RED (not merely "a check exists") ===
Seeded require.Equal(t, "Alice", name) -> "AliceBROKEN" in the shared battery
and ran the literal nightly command, `just test-codegen-live-age`:
  exit 1, --- FAIL: TestLiveSmoke/apache-age-pgx-v5/one_col_one_param_one
  expected: "AliceBROKEN"  actual: "Alice"

=== PARALLELISM AND ISOLATION ===
ageArm.parallelScenarios() reports true; scenario graph names come from an
atomic counter and appear in the logs as gqlc_live_1 / gqlc_live_2. Isolation
mutation-proven earlier: forcing the name to a constant reds the arm with
duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pg_namespace_nspname_index"
(SQLSTATE 23505).
=== DESIGN DECISIONS THE BEAD DID NOT DICTATE ===

1. Battery interface split into read and write halves. The AGE target does not
   emit :exec yet (that is .10), so it cannot serve mixed_read_write_batch.
   Rather than let the AGE arm silently skip write scenarios, `harness` now
   carries only the scalar surface and `writeHarness` extends it; the `arms`
   table records `writes: bool` and TestLiveSmoke asserts
   `arm.writes == (h implements writeHarness)`. An arm that gains or loses
   :exec emission fails the battery until both are updated, instead of
   dropping scenarios unremarked. .10 flips one bool.

2. one_col_one_param_one added to the shared scalar battery, and its manifest
   gained the neo4j-go-v6 target (it had v5 + age only). Without it the only
   shared :one/sentinel coverage came from mixed_read_write_batch, which AGE
   cannot serve. Golden subtree for v6 regenerated via the conformance
   -update path.

3. TestAGESessionInit boots its own apache/age container rather than sharing
   the battery arm's. It creates roles, creates databases and drops an

title: codegen/age: scalar read path — :one/:many methods, param encoding, agtype scalar decode, error taxonomy
description:
First query-bearing AGE stage. Emits per-query :one/:many methods for scalar params + scalar columns: the cypher() invocation uses the parameter mechanism the spike selected (server-side binding — string interpolation of user args is banned), column lists emitted as the AS (v0 ag_catalog.agtype, ...) projection, and emitted agtype scalar decode helpers (bool/integer/float/numeric/string/null, driven by the spike text corpus) in models.go. Error taxonomy mirrors the neo4j impl: ErrNoRows when :one matches nothing, ErrMultipleResults on more than one — identity-matchable sentinels (errors.Is).

TDD: for each fixture enrolled for the AGE target, write the golden red first, then emit; decode helpers get direct unit tests against the spike corpus text before any golden lands.
acceptance_criteria: Applicable valid fixtures gain AGE golden subtrees and pass; goldens compile under the generic build gate; decode helpers unit-tested against captured agtype text including malformed input; ErrNoRows/ErrMultipleResults emitted and sentinel-matchable; no fmt.Sprintf or string concatenation of user params anywhere in emitted query text.
notes:
=== SPIKE gqlc-35yu.5 OUTCOME — DECISIONS THIS BEAD DEPENDS ON ===
Full evidence in gqlc-35yu.5 (818 lines, incl. the complete agtype text
corpus this bead's decode helpers should be TDD'd against).

PARAMETER MECHANISM (selected, with server-log proof of server-side binding):
direct cypher('<graph>', $$...$$, $1) over the pgx extended protocol.
age_prepare_cypher was REJECTED — it latches query text into the plan via
connection-global state at Parse time, which pgx statement caching schedules
unpredictably. String interpolation of user args remains banned unconditionally;
note pgx SimpleProtocol (the only interpolating mode) is the one mode AGE
rejects outright, so the unsafe path fails closed.

BINDING GOTCHA — params must be bound as a Go `string`. Both []byte and
map[string]any FAIL. agtype travels as TEXT format in both directions, and its
OID is DATABASE-SPECIFIC (16461 on the spike container) — do NOT hard-code it.

DECODE GOTCHAS the corpus exposes, each of which a naive parser gets wrong:
  - ::vertex / ::edge / ::path / ::numeric are VALUE-LEVEL annotations at
    ARBITRARY DEPTH, not merely trailing suffixes.
  - Map keys come back in jsonb order: LENGTH FIRST, then lexicographic.
    Goldens must expect this ordering, not insertion or plain lexicographic.
  - NaN and Infinity are valid agtype but are NOT valid JSON — a plain
    encoding/json decode path will break on them.
  - NULL properties are DROPPED entirely. A nullable field comes back as an
    ABSENT KEY, never as an explicit null. This directly shapes the nullable
    decode + error taxonomy in this bead.

SESSION PRECONDITION (see gqlc-35yu.6): ag_catalog must be on the session
search_path or every WHERE/operator query fails — SessionInit enforces this.

    DropGraph:    ag_catalog.drop_graph($1::name, true)
`name` is NAMEDATALEN-1 = 63 BYTES, and the cast TRUNCATES SILENTLY -- no
error, no warning, no notice. Consequences proved against the pinned image:
two distinct names sharing a 63-byte prefix collapse to ONE graph; the second
EnsureGraph returns nil having created nothing; DropGraph on the second
CASCADE-DROPS the first's graph, its labels and its data.

.6 fixes it by REJECTING len(graph) > 63 (Go len, i.e. BYTES) inside
EnsureGraph and DropGraph -- not in New, which stays I/O-free, error-free and
panic-free, matching the neo4j constructor. See the ruling on .6.

    ag_catalog.cypher($1, $$ ... $$) AS (...)
which is a third site where a truncated name silently addresses the WRONG
GRAPH -- and the worst-behaved of the three, because it is on the READ path.

were its own. EnsureGraph/DropGraph at least fail loudly once .6 lands; a
read that silently answers from a neighbouring graph does not.

site. The guard belongs at ONE choke point that every graph-name-binding
statement passes through, and .7 is the bead where the second consumer appears
and the choke point becomes worth having. Factor .6's check into that shared
guard and route cypher() through it. Test the boundary in BYTES, not
characters -- a 63-character multibyte name is over the limit and a
rune-counting test will not see it (see .6's note on the two length axes).

delimiter matches inside the body the lexer does yyless(1), advancing exactly
one byte, so it can never skip a candidate start. The literal therefore closes
at the FIRST occurrence at or after that point, which is exactly what
strings.Index(text+tag, tag) == len(text) names. Occurrences straddling the
OPENING tag are correctly out of scope because that region is already tokenised.
Termination: rejection needs an occurrence starting at some j < len(text), and
two candidates cannot both match at one j (they diverge at byte 5), so the loop
ends within len(text)+1 turns.

He also checked whether the straddle class exists ELSEWHERE rather than assuming
dollarTag was the only site, and found the one other raw composition --
render_queries.go:89 emitting SourceText into a Go raw string, where the grammar
does admit backtick-escaped identifiers. Already closed upstream:
prepare.go:571 rejects any query whose source text holds a backtick with
ErrOutOfC6Scope, confirmed live. Every other user-controlled value reaching
emitted source goes through %q or is a validated Go identifier. Only the graph
name is spliced raw, which is N1's subject.

MANAGER'S INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION, not taken from the report:
- All four gates re-run by me. test/lint/fence green; live at 18.068s with
  -count=1 after `just test-codegen-live` first handed me a CACHED ok -- the
  trap fired on me, noting it so the next bead does not trust a bare recipe run.
- I re-ran the N1 laundering attack myself, since I was the one who promoted it
  to blocking. Replaced the escaping with a no-op ReplaceAll (keeping `strings`
  used so the failure is behavioural, not a compile error). The corpus fence
  went red naming my injection payload; I then ran conformance -count=1 -update,
  which rewrote all 11 AGE db.go goldens and reported ok -- i.e. the laundering
  reproduced -- and the fence STAYED RED. That is the property the promotion
  demanded. Worktree restored to 4db6bdb clean afterwards.
- I verified the 11-golden reflow from c6fdfc7 is comment-only: every changed
  line in those files is a comment or blank, no code churn.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: gqlc-7f9a (P3). Go raw string literals discard \r, so the
emitted query constant can differ from the bytes dollarTag was computed on --
the same invariant as B1 failing for a different reason. Epic-wide (age and
neo4j emit byte-identically) and reachable only via a bare \r inside the token,
so not held against this bead. There is no CRLF normalisation in
internal/queryfile; I checked.

DECLINED AGAIN at round 2: the reviewer re-raised narrow-width overflow as
epic-wide context only, and noted graphStub's hardcoded import list in
corpus_test.go:29 is a future confusing-compile-error risk rather than a gap.
Neither blocks; neither gets a bead.
