    the tree today: no corpus entry, no semantic case, no invalid fixture.

That is a live risk independent of the ADR. Last-wins today is an accident of `out[p.Name] = p` in listener.properties (listener.go:498-516) writing in walk order — not a decision, and nothing pins it. A refactor that iterated the property type list in reverse, or that skipped a name already present, would flip the tool to first-wins with the whole suite green and no reviewer signal. Whichever way the ADR lands, silently changing behaviour beforehand is strictly worse than either outcome.

## Fix

A corpus semanticCase in area B (18.2-node-type), which is exactly the construct for this: per corpus_test.go, 'a semantic case is a promise that something is broken.' Recording one asserts the model is WRONG; it does not endorse the behaviour, so it cannot pre-empt the ADR. semanticAreaB is currently empty and its comment invites the edit in place.

  file:     18.2-node-type/property_name_repeated.gql
  bead:     gqlc-4np   (the case is discharged when the ADR ships, not by this bead)
  spelling: the doubled declaration, verbatim
  siblings: the single-declaration spelling its model cannot be told apart from

When gqlc-4np's ADR lands, this row either becomes an `unsupported` entry with the new sentinel (option a) or gains a corpus entry recording the decided precedence (option b). Either way the flip is caught in the meantime.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: the target half of edge-driven demotion and the source half of endpoint inference failure are both unpinned
description:
A 26-mutation sweep over DemoteNullability, CloseEdges, InferUnlabelled and
BindCall caught 18. Two survivors are real, reachable gaps, and they have the
same shape: a symmetric pair where one half is pinned and the other is not.

## 1. Only the SOURCE endpoint of a required edge is pinned as a demoter

DemoteNullability's fixed point walks both ends of a qualifying required edge:

    for _, side := range [2]query.Endpoint{e.Source(), e.Target()} {

Narrowing that to [1]{e.Source()} leaves the whole suite green. Probed at
cd2826c against social_r6.gql, two queries discriminate:

    OPTIONAL MATCH (b:Post) MATCH (a:Person)-[:AUTHORED]->(b) RETURN b
        today:   b nullable=false
        mutated: b nullable=TRUE

    OPTIONAL MATCH (a:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (b:Post)
    MATCH (a)-[:AUTHORED]->(b) RETURN a, b
        today:   a=false b=false
        mutated: a=false b=TRUE

This is fail-open in the direction that matters for codegen: a column that is
provably non-null becomes nullable, so generated Go gets a pointer where a value
belongs. Every existing demotion fixture happens to demote through the source
position, or demotes the target through some other channel (the group cascade,
or a local re-MATCH), so the target arm of the loop has never been the thing
under test.

## 2. Only the TARGET half of CloseEdges' post-Phase-B failure is pinned

CloseEdges reports an endpoint still unresolved after inference with two arms,
one per side. Replacing the SOURCE arm with a no-op leaves the suite green;
replacing the TARGET arm is caught, by empty_inline_endpoint.cypher
(`MATCH (p:Person)-[r:AUTHORED]->() RETURN r`). The source twin does not exist.

Probed -- reachable, and rejects today with the source-named message:

    MATCH ()-[r:AUTHORED]->(b:Post) RETURN r
    -> unknown label: cannot infer type of source endpoint of edge "r"

## Fix

- valid/demote_target_endpoint.cypher (and the both-optional variant), with
  goldens, for (1). Positive fixtures, because the mutation is fail-open: only a
  golden that records nullable=false can catch it.
- invalid/anonymous_source_endpoint.cypher -> ErrUnknownLabel, for (2).

## Survivors that are NOT gaps

- `5xg pre-pass skips edge bindings` -- the EDGE arm of the bare-reference
  pre-pass is unreachable by parser construction. cypher/pattern.go:314 says so
  outright: "an edge is grammatically never bare -- it always sits inside -[...]-
  between two node positions -- so the parameter is a compile-time constant false
  at this site." So EdgeBinding.ReferencedInRequiredBarePattern() is always false
  and the resolver arm can never fire. Worth one comment linking the two, since
  the resolver side does not mention the guarantee it depends on. The NODE arm is
  caught.
- `addMember accepts a zero or negative group id` and `demoteGroup stops guarding
  against group zero` -- a mutually-masking pair. Group 0 means "not in an
  OPTIONAL group"; either guard alone keeps group 0 inert, so removing one is
  invisible. Removing BOTH would not be. Not a test gap: no single-mutation
  fixture can distinguish a redundant pair of guards.
- `addMember stops deduplicating group ids` -- equivalent mutant. Duplicates in
  members[g] only cause repeated idempotent writes of false.
- `BindCall stops checking procedure arity` and `BindCall's duplicate-variable
  tripwire is removed` -- both documented in situ as parser-authoritative
  pre-conditions ("parser drift", "grammar-impossible; defensive tripwire").
close_reason: Closed

title: schema/gql: an empty inline endpoint property block is accepted by an unpinned boundary
description:
A 20-mutation sweep over the endpoint-reference and resolve() lanes caught 18.
One survivor is a real gap.

fillerLabels rejects an inline endpoint that carries property types
(ErrEndpointFillerHasProperties, gqlc-h9n.18). The guard is

    if list := spec.PropertyTypeList(); list != nil && len(list.AllPropertyType()) > 0 {
        return nil, ErrEndpointFillerHasProperties
    }

Dropping `&& len(list.AllPropertyType()) > 0` leaves the whole suite green. So
nothing asserts what that clause decides: an endpoint written with an EMPTY
property block is accepted.

Probed at ce07430 -- reachable, and accepted in both endpoint positions:

    (:Person { }) -[:KNOWS]-> (:Person)      RESOLVED  nodes=1 edges=1
    (:Person) -[:KNOWS]-> (:Person { })      RESOLVED  nodes=1 edges=1
    (:Person { id :: INT }) -[:KNOWS]-> ...  REJECTED  edge endpoint filler carries properties

This is the endpoint half of a case the node types already have.
18.2-node-type/pattern_empty_property_block.gql pins that `(:Person { })` is a
valid node type declaration. The same spelling in an endpoint has nothing, so
the boundary between "declares no properties" and "declares properties" is
implemented and undefended: narrowing the guard to `list != nil` turns a valid
schema into a rejected one with no test going red.

## Fix

A corpus file under 18.3-edge-type with an empty property block on an inline
endpoint, outcome resolves. A positive case, because the mutation is fail-closed
-- which is exactly why no negative fixture would catch it.

## One survivor that is NOT a gap

`rejectInheritance stops naming the colliding label` -- replacing
fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrImpliedLabelIsKeyLabel, label) with the bare sentinel
survives. The corpus asserts sentinels via errors.Is and never message text, so
no schema test can distinguish it. This is the same policy question as gqlc-ka1
on the resolver side (ErrParameterTypeConflict's message dropping the kind):
whether these suites should start asserting message content at all. Recorded
there rather than fixed here.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
PREMISE WAS WRONG — correcting it here rather than shipping the test it implied.

The bead read the surviving mutation as a missing case: an endpoint written
`(:Person { })` accepted by an unasserted boundary. I wrote the corpus file for
that and re-ran the mutation against the branch. It still survived.

The length clause is UNREACHABLE. propertyTypeList is optional inside the braces
and requires at least one propertyType when present (GQL.g4:1691-1697), so `{ }`
yields a nil list, not an empty one — a non-nil list can never have length zero.
Confirmed by planting a panic on the non-nil-but-empty state and running the full
suite: never fired.

So there was no gap to close, and no test could have closed it. Shipping instead:

- the clause deleted, replaced by a comment saying why the nil check carries the
  whole test (a reader's default assumption is the opposite, which is what made
  the mutation look like a gap)
- the corpus file kept on its own merits — `(:X { })` in an endpoint is a
  grammar-reachable spelling nothing covered, running through fillerLabels where
  the node-type twin runs through nodeContent — but NOT claimed as a mutation
  kill, in either its comment or the commit message.

title: schema/gql: the bare-bar closed dynamic union is unpinned, and a corpus reason claims otherwise
description:
A 22-mutation sweep over the property-type lowering in internal/schema/gql
caught 17. One survivor is a real gap, and it comes with a corpus comment that
states the opposite.

## The gap

declineValueType lists four contexts under ErrDynamicUnionType. Deleting
*gen.ClosedDynamicUnionTypeAtl2Context from that list leaves the whole suite
green. closedDynamicUnionTypeAtl2 is the bare-bar spelling (GQL.g4:1732,
`valueType VERTICAL_BAR valueType`), as opposed to Atl1's angle-bracket form at
:1731.

It is reachable and it does reject today:

    (:Person { id :: INT NOT NULL, p :: STRING | INT })
    -> unsupported property value type: ANY VALUE and the closed unions need a
       property type that carries alternatives ...

Without the case it falls through declineValueType to normaliseType, misses the
spelling table and lands on the bare ErrUnsupportedType instead. So the family
attribution ADR 0019 makes for this spelling is unasserted: the file rejects
either way, and only the sentinel changes.

## The comment that says otherwise

corpus_area_d2_test.go's entry for 18.9-value-type/constructed_dyn_closed_union.gql
reads:

    "ANY VALUE<STRING | INT> discharges valueType alts 9 and 10 in one parse,
     because the inner STRING | INT is itself a nested closedDynamicUnionTypeAtl2"

That is not what happens. declineValueType reads the outermost context and does
not descend — its own doc comment says so, and gives the reason (a subtree search
would report a RECORD field's family in place of the property's). The outer
context is Atl1; the inner Atl2 is never dispatched on.

Verified by failure rather than by reading: replacing the Atl2 arm with a panic
and running `go test ./...` produced no panic. The one file that claims to reach
it does not.

## Fix

- New corpus file 18.9-value-type/constructed_dyn_closed_union_bare.gql carrying
  `p :: STRING | INT`, outcome unsupported, sentinel ErrDynamicUnionType.
- Correct the reason on constructed_dyn_closed_union.gql: it discharges alt 9,
  not alts 9 and 10, and the nested Atl2 is invisible to declineValueType by
  design.

## Two survivors that are NOT gaps (recorded so they are not re-swept)

- `truncateParenthetical stops trimming the space before (` — unreachable.
  normaliseType only ever calls it on canonicalSpelling's output, and
  canonicalSpelling ends with collapseParenthetical, which already trims that
  space. A panic-if-the-trim-would-change-anything tripwire never fired across
  the full suite.
- `collapseParenthetical stops collapsing spaces around a comma` — reachable but
  outcome-inert. The tripwire DOES fire (unrepresentable_width_decimal_schema
  feeds it `10, 2`), but no typeSpellings key contains a comma: all 18
  parenthesised rows are the scale-free binary-width forms INT(n)/UINT(n)/
  INTEGER(n). Collapsed or not, `DECIMAL(10, 2)` misses the exact lookup and
  falls to truncateParenthetical -> DECIMAL. The normalisation targets keys that
  do not exist, so no test can distinguish it without adding one.
close_reason: Closed

title: schema/gql: rejectInheritance is half-pinned — the edge-vs-edge decline and the per-label (not first-label) claim have no corpus case
description:
A 13-mutation sweep over the semantic guards in internal/schema/gql caught 11.
Both survivors are in rejectInheritance, the ADR 0015 decline of the one part of
GG21 gqlc does not implement. Both were probed and are reachable.

## 1. rejectInheritance is never exercised for edge types

resolve() calls rejectInheritance twice — once for nodes against node key labels,
once for edges against edge key labels. Deleting the EDGE call leaves the suite
green. No corpus file has an edge type implying another EDGE type's key label:

    CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH TYPE T AS {
        (:Person { id :: INT NOT NULL }),
        (:Person) -[:KNOWS { since :: DATE }]-> (:Person),
        (:Person) -[:FRIEND => :KNOWS { since :: DATE }]-> (:Person)
    }
    -> implied label is also a declared element type's key label: KNOWS

18.3-edge-type/implied_label_is_node_key_label.gql covers the adjacent case and
pins the opposite outcome — an edge implying a NODE key label RESOLVES, because
the two vocabularies are separate namespaces. Its own comment states the rule as
"called once for nodes against node key labels and once for edges against edge key
labels", but only the resolves half is verified. The rejects half for edges is not,
so the edge call can be deleted and only that comment would still claim otherwise.

## 2. The per-label check is only ever exercised at the first label

rejectInheritance loops over every label in each implied set. Narrowing the loop to
the first label of each set leaves the suite green — every existing collision case
has the colliding label first. The doc comment makes the per-label claim explicitly
("`(:A&B)` holds both A and B as key labels, so implying either collides") and
nothing tests it:

    CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH TYPE T AS {
        (:Zeta { id :: INT NOT NULL }),
        (:Engineer => :Alpha&Zeta { level :: INT })
    }
    -> implied label is also a declared element type's key label: Zeta

The label is second both as written and in sort order, so the case discriminates
regardless of how the implied set is ordered. The mirrored control (collider first,
:Alpha declared instead) is rejected today too, which is what the existing corpus
already covers.

## Fix

Two corpus files with entries in the matching area tables:
- 18.3-edge-type/implied_label_is_edge_key_label.gql   (unsupported, ErrImpliedLabelIsKeyLabel, GG21)
- 18.2-node-type/implied_key_label_not_first.gql       (unsupported, ErrImpliedLabelIsKeyLabel, GG21)

Re-run the sweep on the branch and show both survivors flip to caught.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: scope.go's parameter-witness and RETURN * lanes are 4/12 pinned — Contains' edge-union arm, PropertyUseWitness' guards, and virtualProjection's var-length/carry arms are all unpinned
description:
A 12-mutation sweep over the cold methods in internal/resolver/scope.go caught only
4. Seven of the eight survivors are reachable. Each was probed against social_r7.gql:
the five error-path cases are rejected today, the two type-path cases resolve to a
type the mutation changes.

## Reachable, error path (fixture asserts a sentinel)

partScope.Contains drops the edge-union arm -> a parameter used on a multi-type edge
property is never witnessed, so a conflict goes undetected:

    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES]->(b:Post) WHERE r.likedAt = $x RETURN a LIMIT $x
        -> parameter type conflict: parameter "x": property:TIMESTAMP vs scalar

PropertyUseWitness drops the variable-length edge rejection. The existing coverage
(var_length_edge_property_projection.cypher) is on the PROJECTION path
(refProjectionType); the witness path has the same guard and no test:

    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS*1..3]->(b:Person) WHERE r.since = $x RETURN a
        -> query construct not supported at resolver stage R0: property projection
           on variable-length edge binding

PropertyUseWitness drops nullability demotion (prop.Nullable || nullableBinding), so
a NOT NULL property behind OPTIONAL MATCH is witnessed as non-nullable and stops
conflicting. parameter_type_conflict_nullability.cypher does not reach this — it
conflicts two non-optional bindings whose DECLARED nullability differs, so the
demotion term is never the deciding factor. Both node and edge arms are unpinned:

    MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name = $x OPTIONAL MATCH (q:Person) WHERE q.name = $x RETURN p.name
    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:AUTHORED]->(b:Post) WHERE r.views = $x OPTIONAL MATCH (c:Person)-[s:AUTHORED]->(d:Post) WHERE s.views = $x RETURN a
        -> parameter type conflict

PropertyUseWitness stops reporting an unknown edge property (the node arm IS pinned):

    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS]->(b:Person) WHERE r.notAProp = $x RETURN a
        -> unknown property: r.notAProp

## Reachable, type path (fixture is valid, the golden pins the type)

virtualProjection's RETURN * expansion has two unpinned arms. No returns_all_*
fixture uses a variable-length edge or a carried projection alias:

    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS*1..3]->(b:Person) RETURN *   -> [a node] [r list] [b node]
        mutation types r as a plain edge instead of a list
    MATCH (p:Person) WITH p.name AS n RETURN *             -> [n property:STRING]
        mutation drops the carry arm and the query is rejected (fail-closed)

## Not a defect: scope.HasNode / HasEdge / HasCall are dead production code

The eighth survivor (HasEdge stops seeing edge-union bindings) is not a fail-open.
All three Has* methods have ZERO production callers — grep across internal/ excluding
_test.go returns nothing. They are test-only affordances used by scope_test.go, and
the only HasEdge assertions there are negative (require.False), which is why removing
an arm survives. Worth a separate cleanup decision, not a fixture.

## Fix

Five invalid fixtures, two valid fixtures with goldens, and a valid control for the
nullability pair (same shape, both sides nullable, must still be accepted — otherwise
a blanket-reject mutation satisfies the negatives). Re-run the sweep on the branch and
show the survivors flip to caught.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: R6 write-effect validators are 4/15 pinned — ON CREATE is entirely unvalidated, and every multi-type/var-length edge guard is fail-open
description:
A 15-mutation sweep over the validate*Effect family in internal/resolver/resolve.go
caught only 4. Nine of the eleven survivors are REACHABLE fail-opens: a query the
resolver rejects on master becomes ACCEPTED under the mutation. Verified by probe,
not by reading — each query below returns an error today, and three control queries
of the same shape without the offending part are accepted.

## Reachable fail-opens (each needs an invalid fixture)

MERGE ... ON CREATE is not validated at all. validateMergeEffect walks ON MATCH
effects and ON CREATE effects through the same code, but only ON MATCH is pinned
(invalid/merge_on_match_unknown_property.cypher). Delete the ON CREATE arm and the
suite stays green:

    MERGE (a:Person) ON CREATE SET a.notAProp = 30 RETURN a
        -> unknown property: a.notAProp
    MERGE (a:Person) ON CREATE SET a:NotALabel RETURN a
        -> unknown label: label "NotALabel" not declared on any node type

The variable-length edge guard is pinned for exactly one of the five places it
appears. invalid/set_property_on_var_length_edge.cypher covers SET property on a
single-type edge. The other four are unpinned:

    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES*1..3]->(b:Post) SET r.likedAt = date('2020-01-01') RETURN a
    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS*1..3]->(b:Person) SET r = {since: date('2020-01-01')} RETURN a
    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES*1..3]->(b:Post) SET r = {likedAt: date('2020-01-01')} RETURN a
    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS*1..3]->(b:Person) REMOVE r.since RETURN a
    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES*1..3]->(b:Post) REMOVE r.likedAt RETURN a
        -> invalid effect target: SET/REMOVE on variable-length edge "r"

The multi-type edge property lookup (unionProperty) is unpinned on the write path.
Reads are covered (unknown_property_union_*), writes are not:

    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES]->(b:Post) SET r.notAProp = 1 RETURN a
    MATCH (a:Person)-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES]->(b:Post) REMOVE r.notAProp RETURN a
        -> unknown property: property r.notAProp missing on union member Person-[AUTHORED]->Post

## Not defects

Three survivors are diagnostic-only: dropping the edge-binding rejection in
validateSetLabelsEffect / validateRemoveLabelsEffect, and the projection-alias
rejection in validateDeleteEffect, each falls through to the "not in any Part scope"
branch and returns the SAME ErrInvalidEffectTarget sentinel. The suite asserts
sentinels via errors.Is and never asserts message text, so these are indistinguishable
by construction — consistent with the package's posture, not a hole. See
bd memory resolver-formatdeclaredcarrying-diagnostic for the same call.

Two more (validateCreateEffect / validateMergeEffect rejecting an unbound variable)
are documented defensive tripwires and were not probed; they may be unreachable.

## Fix

Add invalid fixtures for the nine reachable cases against social_r6.gql, plus valid
controls where the shape is otherwise untested. Re-run the sweep on the branch and
show the survivors flip to caught.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: resolvedTypeEqual's edge-union arity check is unpinned — a prefix union is declared equal, and the reverse ordering panics
description:
Found by mutation sweep of internal/resolver. Dropping
`len(aa.EdgeKeys) != len(bb.EdgeKeys)` from resolvedTypeEqual's
ResolvedEdgeUnion arm (resolve.go:339) survives the full suite.

resolvedTypeEqual backs compareBranchColumns (resolve.go:312), the R5 UNION
column compatibility check. Without the arity guard the arm loops
`for i := range aa.EdgeKeys` and indexes bb.EdgeKeys[i] unchecked, so there are
TWO failure modes depending on which branch is longer — and note the call is
resolvedTypeEqual(other[i].Type, base[i].Type), so aa is the non-zero branch:

  branch 0 longer  -> aa shorter, prefix matches, returns true
                      FAIL-OPEN: two different edge-union types declared equal,
                      and the model emits branch 0's type for a query whose
                      other branch cannot produce it
  branch 0 shorter -> aa longer, bb.EdgeKeys[i] runs off the end
                      PANIC on user input

Neither is reachable today, and the reason is specific: the guard only matters
when one key list is a strict PREFIX of the other. The obvious candidate pair
is not — against social_r3.gql,

  [r:AUTHORED|LIKES]->(post:Post)  ->  [P-AUTHORED-Post, P-LIKES-Post]
  [r:AUTHORED|LIKES]-(post:Post)   ->  [P-AUTHORED-Post, Post-AUTHORED-Person,
                                        P-LIKES-Post]

differ at index 1, so the element-wise loop rejects them with the arity check
already removed. Verified empirically: both orderings still error under the
mutation, and neither panics.

A prefix pair needs three edge types between ONE ordered endpoint pair, so the
2-set is the 3-set minus its last element:

  [r:A|B]->(post:Post)    -> [K1, K2]
  [r:A|B|C]->(post:Post)  -> [K1, K2, K3]

No schema fixture has 3+ edge types on a single ordered pair — checked all 9 in
test/data/resolver/*/schemas. So this needs a small purpose-built schema
(a third Person->Post edge type alongside AUTHORED and LIKES) plus two UNION
fixtures, one per ordering, to pin the fail-open and the panic separately.

The undirected 3-key set cannot be reached with a bare [r:AUTHORED]- because
undirected single-type AUTHORED is rejected as ErrAmbiguousEdgeOrientation.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: ErrParameterTypeConflict messages read 'scalar vs scalar' — String() drops the kind
description:
Observed while shipping gqlc-9ka. unifyParameterUsesAcrossBranches formats the
conflict as:

  fmt.Errorf("%w: parameter %q: %s vs %s", ErrParameterTypeConflict, p.Name,
             unified.String(), w.String())

but ResolvedScalar.String() returns the constant "scalar" and
ResolvedTemporal.String() returns the constant "temporal" (validated.go:247,
:310). So a genuine kind conflict renders as:

  parameter type conflict: parameter "x": scalar vs scalar
  parameter type conflict: parameter "x": temporal vs temporal

which tells the user nothing about which two kinds disagreed. Both are real
conflicts — the fixtures added in gqlc-9ka produce exactly these strings.

Diagnostic-only, hence P3: the sentinel is correct and TestInvalid asserts via
errors.Is, so nothing is fail-open. But it is the message a user actually sees
when their query is rejected, and the information needed to fix it (bool vs
int; date vs duration) is present and discarded.

Note the resolver suite asserts NO error-message content anywhere today, so
fixing this needs a decision about whether to start — see bd memory
resolver-formatdeclaredcarrying-diagnostic for the same tension.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
Schema-side instance of the same policy question, found by mutation sweep at ce07430 (see gqlc-445).

internal/schema/gql's rejectInheritance formats its diagnostic as

    fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrImpliedLabelIsKeyLabel, label)

so the message names WHICH implied label collided. Replacing that with the bare
sentinel survives the full suite: the corpus asserts sentinels through errors.Is
and never reads message text, so the label name is unprotected.

That makes two suites with the same shape -- a message carrying information the
tests cannot see. Whatever this bead decides about ErrParameterTypeConflict's
kind should decide the schema corpus too, or say explicitly why not.

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
This bead's premise is now empirically false, and that changes its
priority. Evidence from the mutation sweep in gqlc-xem.

The description says: 'the sentinel is correct and TestInvalid asserts
via errors.Is, so nothing is fail-open'. Nine guards are fail-open,
and the sentinel-only assertion is the reason.

Every per-variant effect validator in resolve.go ends in the same
three-arm ladder:

    if _, ok := sc.edgeBindings[v]; ok         { ... ErrInvalidEffectTarget }
    if _, ok := sc.carriedResolvedTypes[v]; ok { ... ErrInvalidEffectTarget }
    return                                       ... ErrInvalidEffectTarget

Deleting either of the first two arms makes control fall through to the
third, which raises the SAME sentinel. errors.Is cannot tell them
apart, so the suite stays green. Confirmed by mutation for all seven
projection-alias arms plus both SET/REMOVE-labels-on-edge-binding arms:

  validateSetPropertyEffect     alias arm      SURVIVED
  validateSetEntityEffect       alias arm      SURVIVED
  validateSetLabelsEffect       alias arm      SURVIVED
  validateSetLabelsEffect       edge arm       SURVIVED
  validateRemovePropertyEffect  alias arm      SURVIVED
  validateRemoveLabelsEffect    alias arm      SURVIVED
  validateRemoveLabelsEffect    edge arm       SURVIVED
  validateDeleteEffect          bare alias arm SURVIVED
  validateDeleteEffect          prop alias arm SURVIVED

There are named fixtures for these — set_property_on_projection_alias,
set_labels_on_projection_alias, delete_projection_alias and five more.
They reach the arm. They cannot pin it. Nine tests that look like
coverage and are not.

So the question this bead frames as diagnostic-quality ('the message a
user actually sees') is also a coverage question. Two ways out:

  (a) assert message substrings for the fixtures where two arms share a
      sentinel. Test-only, no exported-API change, closes all nine.
  (b) split ErrInvalidEffectTarget into distinct sentinels. Changes
      exported errors, so it wants an ADR — and TestSentinelReachability
      would then require a fixture per new sentinel, which is the
      coverage guarantee (a) only approximates.

Related: the same shape has now produced six confirmed
sentinel-collision instances across the suite (bd memory
sentinel-collision-disjunct-heuristic). This is the largest cluster.

title: resolver: unify's scalar and temporal Kind discriminators are unpinned — a parameter used at two kinds silently takes the first
description:
Found by mutation sweep of internal/resolver. Two mutations of unify
(internal/resolver/resolve.go:840) survive the full suite:

  case ResolvedScalar:   drop `bb.Kind != aa.Kind`   SURVIVED
  case ResolvedTemporal: drop `bb.Kind != aa.Kind`   SURVIVED

unify is reached only from unifyParameterUsesAcrossBranches (resolve.go:421),
so it IS the ErrParameterTypeConflict detector. With either check gone, a
parameter witnessed at two different kinds unifies to whichever use is seen
first, and the resolved model reports a confidently wrong parameter type —
which downstream codegen turns into a wrong Go type on the parameter binding.
Fail-open, not diagnostic.

The four existing parameter_type_conflict_* fixtures all conflict at the type
ASSERTION (`!ok`), never at the Kind field:

  clause_slot_vs_string    ResolvedProperty vs ResolvedScalar
  property_vs_expr_bool    ResolvedProperty vs ResolvedScalar
  two_properties           ResolvedProperty vs ResolvedProperty (Type differs)
  nullability              ResolvedProperty vs ResolvedProperty (Nullable differs)

No fixture has ever put two ResolvedScalars, or two ResolvedTemporals, of
different kinds against each other. The Kind arms are dead for the whole suite.

Reachability proved against schemas/social_r7.gql — both already error today:

  MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name = 'a' AND $x RETURN p.name LIMIT $x
      ScalarBool (predicate) vs ScalarInt (LIMIT slot)
      -> parameter type conflict: parameter "x": scalar vs scalar

  MATCH (p:Person) RETURN date($x) AS d, duration($x) AS e
      TemporalDate vs TemporalDuration
      -> parameter type conflict: parameter "x": temporal vs temporal

And the same-kind control resolves cleanly, so the fixtures fail for the kind
mismatch rather than for using the construct at all:

  MATCH (p:Person) RETURN date($x) AS d, date($x) AS e   -> temporal/date

Note the witness for an ExprUse is resolveType(uu.EnclosingType()) — the type
of the ENCLOSING expression (scope.go:975) — which is why date($x) witnesses
the parameter as temporal/date.

Fix: two invalid fixtures mapped to ErrParameterTypeConflict, plus the
same-kind positive control as a valid fixture.

Separately observed, filed apart: both messages read "scalar vs scalar" /
"temporal vs temporal" because ResolvedScalar.String() and
ResolvedTemporal.String() drop the kind.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: intersect is unpinned — no fixture has two edges touching one unlabelled variable, so cross-edge narrowing is fail-open
description:
Found by mutation sweep of internal/resolver (3/11 caught). intersect
(internal/resolver/resolve.go:686) has 0.0% coverage and every mutation of it
survives the full suite, including the maximally destructive one:

  - `return a`                                 SURVIVED
  - union instead of intersection              SURVIVED
  - `return map[graph.LabelSetKey]struct{}{}`  SURVIVED
  - candidateTypes: `acc = cand` (drop the accumulate, last edge wins) SURVIVED

Why: intersect exists to narrow an unlabelled binding's candidate set across
several edges, and its only caller is candidateTypes (resolve.go:627) via
inferUnlabelled (resolve.go:568). But every unlabelled fixture in
test/data/resolver has exactly ONE edge touching the unlabelled variable —
unlabelled_binding_from_edge, unlabelled_binding_target_inferred,
unlabelled_via_undirected, unlabelled_via_multi_type,
carry_wins_over_unlabelled_rebind. With one edge the accumulator is seeded and
never intersected, so the function body is dead for the whole suite.

This is a fail-open, not an equivalent mutant: reachability is proved. Against
schemas/social_r7.gql this query resolves today and pins all four mutations at
once:

  MATCH (a)-[:AUTHORED|KNOWS]->(x:Person), (a)-[:EMPLOYS|KNOWS]->(y:Person) RETURN a

  edge 1 alone -> {Person, Post}    (ErrAmbiguousBinding)
  edge 2 alone -> {Company, Person} (ErrAmbiguousBinding)
  intersection -> {Person}          resolves cleanly today

The intersection is strictly smaller than BOTH operands, so `return a` and
`acc = cand` each yield an ambiguous binding, the union yields
{Person, Post, Company} ambiguous, and the empty set yields ErrUnknownLabel.
Every surviving mutation becomes a failure.

Existing invalid/ambiguous_unlabelled_binding.cypher pins that ambiguity is
rejected; nothing pins that a second edge RESOLVES the ambiguity, which is the
entire reason intersect is written.

Fix: add the fixture above to test/data/resolver/valid plus its golden and
schema.mapping.json entry.
close_reason: Closed

title: schema/gql: a stale alternativeExemption is silently inert — requiredAlternatives' rejection branches are unpinned
description:
Mutation sweep of corpus_grammar_test.go at 70cba7d. All four rejection branches in requiredAlternatives (corpus_grammar_test.go:762-771) can be deleted with the whole suite green:

  - `!candidates[ex.tag]` — exemption naming a tag that is not a candidate
  - `exempt[ex.tag]` — duplicate exemption
  - `ex.stolenBy == "" || ex.bead == "" || ex.why == ""` — missing fields
  - `ex.stolenBy == ex.tag` — self-stealing exemption

The first is a genuine fail-open on a hand-maintained registry, the recurring shape in this package (cf. gqlc-ii8, gqlc-1uf, gqlc-d9b). Without the guard, an exemption whose tag stops being a candidate — a grammar change, or a typo — marks a tag nothing ever consults: the loop over invisible never matches it, so required is unchanged and the exemption silently stops excusing whatever it was written for. TestAlternativeExemptions does not catch this, because it asserts got.alternatives[ex.tag] is false and a tag no file can take is false for the stale entry too. The guard is the only thing standing between a stale exemption and silence.

The other three are integrity checks on the same registry, unpinned for the same reason: the checked-in list has exactly one well-formed entry, so no branch is ever taken.

requiredAlternatives already takes exemptions as a parameter precisely so a synthetic list can be supplied — the comment at :746-750 says so, and TestRequiredAlternativesDemandsTheThief uses it for the positive path. The rejection half was never written. TestIsValidFeature makes the identical argument one file over: 'the rejection half is the one that matters'.

Fix: a table test supplying one malformed exemption list per branch (three separate cases for the missing-field disjunction, so each disjunct is pinned individually) and asserting the error names the problem.

NOT in scope, deliberately — three other survivors from the same sweep are message-sharpeners already backstopped by the membership goldens, not fail-opens:
  - the root/cut-is-a-real-rule check (:705-709): a mistyped cut silently fails to apply, the closure explodes, and wantObligationRules fails by name.
  - the cut-reachability check (:712-716): same backstop.
  - scanGrammarRules' zero-rule guard (:486-488): an empty scan empties the closure and the goldens fail.
Two further survivors are inert against the SHA-pinned grammar and are forward-defence for a re-vendor: withoutLiterals (GQL.g4 has 0 parser rules containing a quoted literal) and cleanRuleBody's alt-label stripping (all 44 alt labels are lowercase-initial and none collides with a rule name, so grammarRefs' parserRules membership check already drops them). Both measured directly.
close_reason: Closed

title: schema/gql: the lexer error listener is unpinned — dropping it silently accepts trailing garbage
description:
Mutation sweep of parser.go at 70cba7d: deleting `lex.AddErrorListener(l)` (Parse, parser.go:82-83) leaves the entire suite green. It is a genuine fail-open, not an equivalent mutant.

Probed directly: `CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH TYPE T AS { (:A { p :: INT }) } #` currently yields `syntax error at 1:54: token recognition error at: '#'`. With the lexer listener removed it parses SUCCESSFULLY — nil error, one node type. Trailing garbage is silently accepted and a caller gets a schema it did not write.

Why nothing catches it: every negative fixture that exercises a bad character puts it where the *parser* also objects (`(:A$`, `% CREATE ...`, a stray backtick inside a body), so the parser listener alone still produces an error and the message merely changes. The discriminating shape is an unrecognisable token positioned where the parser is already content — after a complete graph type, where the token stream the parser sees ends at EOF either way. No fixture has that shape, so the lexer half of the error plumbing has never been exercised.

Fix: add `test/data/schema/gql/invalid/lexer_error.gql` carrying a trailing unrecognisable token, map it to nil in invalidFixtures (TestInvalid is fail-closed on registration, so the mapping is forced), and add a test that parses the same source with and without the offending token — the without-it parse must succeed, which is what proves the rejection is the lexer's doing and not the parser's, without coupling to ANTLR message wording.

Sibling of gqlc-p9v (PR #507): same package, same plumbing, same shape of gap.
close_reason: Closed

title: schema/gql: the lossiness rewrite changes every occurrence of a spelling, not the argument under test
description:
TestNoUndeclaredLossiness decides whether a type argument is discarded by rewriting it and comparing models. discardedArguments builds the variant with strings.ReplaceAll(src, spelling, ...), so it rewrites every occurrence of that spelling in the file rather than the occurrence the typeArgument scan reported.

GQL spells CHAR/VARCHAR and BINARY/VARBINARY, and typeArgument's leading \\b makes VARCHAR(10) a single match. So in a file holding both VARCHAR(10) and CHAR(10), testing CHAR(10) rewrites the tail of VARCHAR(10) too, and the verdict returned under the name CHAR(10) is really a verdict about both.

The direction that bites is fail-open: if the neighbour records its argument and the one under test discards it, the variant's model differs and the discard goes unreported -- which is the exact silence this gate was written to close (gqlc-eh4).

Inert today because no type argument reaches the model at all, so both halves are discarded and the answer is right by accident. It activates the moment some arguments start reaching the model, i.e. when gqlc-5md lands -- which is when this gate starts having anything to distinguish.

Fix: rewrite at the offset typeArgument reported instead of by string match, and witness the mechanism directly (as perturb already is), because the corpus cannot witness a verdict that is currently correct either way.
close_reason: Closed

title: schema/gql: carrierExemptions violates its own stated cap, with 29 entries encoding one derivable rule
description:
`carrierExemptions` (corpus_carriers_test.go:109) documents its own failure mode and threshold:

> If this list grows past a handful the ownership model is wrong, not the exemptions — file the finding rather than adding a tenth entry.

It has **35 entries**. Nothing enforces the threshold: unlike the sibling `isoGaps` list in corpus_iso_test.go, which has `isoGapRatchet`, `carrierExemptions` is referenced nowhere outside its own file and has no cap.

## The 29 are one rule, written 29 times

Measured against the grammar (`scanRuleSections` + `grammarObligation`):

- **29 obligation names are declared under ISO clause 21** (21.1 identifier lexis, 21.2 literals/vocabulary). All 29 are currently exempted, and every one carries the same prose: `STRUCTURAL: ... No retirement path — clause 21 has no corpus directory by design.`
- **0 clause-21 names are un-exempted**, so the partition is exact.
- **6 exemptions are not clause 21**: `graphExpression` (11.1, the query-surface cut) and the five gqlc-h9n.27 section-heading misfits (`graphTypeLikeGraph`, `LIKE` at 12.4; `isOrColon`, `IS`, `COLON` at 16.7).

The list's stated value is that "an exemption is a reviewer's checklist item with a stated reason". Twenty-nine copies of an identical sentence are not a checklist — the premise the design rests on is contradicted by the data.

## What to change

Split the register:

1. `clause21Unowned` — a **membership golden** of the 29 names, one line each, with the reason stated once for the class. Exact-set matched against the obligation names whose section is 21.x, so it cannot drift and so adding a clause-21 name to the grammar reddens the build. That answers the doc's objection to widening ("a widened rule is invisible"): this widening is counted and diffed.
2. `carrierExemptions` — keeps the 6 genuine entries, each with its own reason and bead. That is the "handful" the doc asked for.

A membership golden rather than a count, per the corpus convention: a count would let one clause-21 name replace another silently.

**No ratchet on the clause-21 list.** `isoGaps` ratchets because an unimplemented ISO production is debt that must not grow. A clause-21 name is not debt — it means the grammar named another identifier production — so capping it would be a number that gets raised rather than a guard.

## Verification

Mutation sweep as with gqlc-cer/eh4/w2o: prove the exact-set match fires when a clause-21 name is added, removed, or moved between the two registers.
close_reason: Landed as PR #487 (squash 2026-07-28). carrierExemptions cut 35 -> 6; the 29 clause-21 names moved to clause21Unowned, a membership golden exact-set matched against the grammar by TestClause21Unowned. Mutation sweep: 10 mutations, 9 caught; the survivor (token attribution) is filed as gqlc-1uf.

title: schema/gql: perturb type arguments as well as remove them, to close the no-verdict hole
description:
TestNoUndeclaredLossiness (gqlc-eh4, PR #482) decides whether a resolving corpus file discards a parenthesised type argument by removing the argument and re-resolving: an identical model proves the argument reached nothing. Removal is sound but incomplete, because the bare spelling is not always grammatical, and an ungrammatical variant yields no verdict rather than a verdict of "lossless".

The demonstrated instance is DECIMAL. decimalExactNumericType (GQL.g4:1832) puts notNull? inside the parenthesised group, so `DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL` cannot become `DECIMAL NOT NULL` — that is a syntax error, the comparison never happens, and a file of that shape could hide a discard indefinitely. The same is true of DURATION: bare `DURATION` does not parse ("no viable alternative").

## What to change

Try a *perturbed* argument before falling back to removal. Probed and confirmed working:

- `DECIMAL(10,2)` vs `DECIMAL(11,3)` — parses, and the models collide, so the discard IS detectable this way
- `STRING(5)` vs `STRING(6)` — parses, collides
- `DURATION(DAY TO SECOND)` vs `DURATION(YEAR TO MONTH)` — parses, collides

A numeric perturbation is mechanically derivable: if the argument is made only of digits, commas, whitespace and 0x/0b/0o literals, substitute a different literal of the same shape. That covers every gqlc-5md and gqlc-h9n.31 case and is grammatical wherever the original is, because the argument's syntactic slot is unchanged.

## Residual after that

A non-numeric qualifier still needs a substitute nobody can derive — DURATION's field list is the known example, and its two files are already registered as semantic cases, so nothing is hiding there today. Either leave it as a stated limit or register the qualifier alternatives by hand; the former is probably right until a second non-numeric qualifier exists.

## Why it is P2 and not urgent

The sweep found nothing hiding behind this hole right now: every corpus file that spells a parenthesised argument is either declared lossy or is an unsupported entry. This closes a future gap, and makes the check's "no verdict" branch rare enough to be worth trusting.
notes:
PR #484 (branch test/w2o-perturb-type-arguments, commit eb55910). Replaced removal with a rewrite in discardedArguments; dropped removal entirely rather than keeping both.

Two findings beyond the bead's plan:

1. The hole was live. scalar_decimal_precision_scale.gql is a real corpus file removal could not reach, and the corpus had ALREADY worked around it by hand — that entry's semanticCases sibling is DECIMAL(8), with a comment explaining bare DECIMAL will not substitute. This makes mechanical what an author had derived manually.

2. Removal turned out to be redundant, not merely weaker. Probed every type keyword in the corpus vocabulary: none rejects T(1) while accepting bare T. So removal could not reach a case a rewrite misses. A mutation deleting the removal variant left the suite green, which is what settled it.

Verified by 10 mutations, 9 caught. W10 (strip the bead+reason+semanticCases row from scalar_decimal_precision_scale.gql and repin wantSemanticCases) was SILENT before this change and now reddens TestNoUndeclaredLossiness — that is the regression this bead existed to make visible.

W8 (drop the !ok guard) survived: DURATION() is not GQL either, so the outcome matches by accident of the grammar. Guard kept with a comment saying so rather than a claim it is witnessed.

Residual unchanged and stated in the test doc: a non-numeric qualifier has no derivable rewrite. DURATION's field list is the only instance and both files are registered (gqlc-8pe).
close_reason: Landed PR #484 (merged bed5030). Replaced argument removal with argument rewriting in TestNoUndeclaredLossiness, and dropped removal entirely rather than keeping both — probing showed no type in GQL's vocabulary rejects a rewritten argument while accepting a bare one, so removal could not reach a case a rewrite misses, and the mutation deleting it left the suite green. Verified by 10 mutations, 9 caught; the headline (W10) is that undeclaring scalar_decimal_precision_scale.gql was silent before and now reddens the gate. Residual stated in the test doc: a non-numeric qualifier has no derivable rewrite (DURATION's field list, both files already registered under gqlc-8pe).

title: schema/gql: RECORD and closed dynamic unions need a property type that carries members
description:
Split out of `gqlc-h9n.6`, which decided *why* these are declined and gave them
sentinels; this is the work that would lift the decline.

`graph.PropertyType` is `type PropertyType string` over a flat set of constants
(internal/graph/propertytype.go). Three declined families need it to carry
something more:

- `recordType` (GQL.g4:1977-1980) — `RECORD { f :: STRING }` needs a field list.
  Declined today with `ErrRecordValueType`.
- `closedDynamicUnionType` (valueType alts 9 and 10) — `ANY VALUE<STRING | INT>`
  and the bare `STRING | INT` need a member list. Declined today with
  `ErrDynamicUnionType`, which they share with the *open* unions — those have a
  different blocker and are `gqlc-h9n.34`.
- `LIST` / `ARRAY` — `gqlc-h9n.5`, which is already open and has the fuller
  design note. **Read that note before starting here**: it establishes that
  encoding the parameter in the string is not viable, because `goType`'s bare
  `return "", false` (internal/codegen/types.go:163) already means "permanently
  unrepresentable", and a structured string would be reported to users as a
  permanent boundary rather than as an unimplemented feature.

So this is the same missing thing three times, and `gqlc-h9n.5` is the one with
a design note. Whoever lands the parameterised model should land all three or
say why not.

ADR 0019 records that these are unimplemented rather than declined, and that the
`yet` in their error messages is what says so.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 by agent-a 2026-08-30, under the king's ruling on [deleted:gqlc-nhv64].

WHY. The RCA behind that ruling found the fleet had spent 88% of its completed
work since the founding on the machinery and 12% on gqlc. Part of the remedy is
that the router's max_priority is 2, so this bead sat where nobody could ever be
routed to it. It is gqlc work and the fleet is being pointed back at gqlc.

This is a deliberate, reasoned promotion and not a sweep: of 92 product beads on
the floor I promoted 42. Left down there on purpose were 37 that are prose,
comment, fence and witness defects rather than gqlc capability — the same
meta-work pathology the RCA found in the machinery, and promoting those would
have moved the disease into the product — plus 6 blocked on the missing ISO
arbiter (gqlc-lir), 4 misfiled machinery beads, and 3 deliberately deferred to a
later version.

If you believe this bead was sorted wrongly, say so and I will re-rule it; the
classification was mine and it was a judgement, not a measurement.
BLOCKED ON A DESIGN BEAD by agent-a 2026-09-02: gqlc-be1me (class:designer, P2).

agent-j met this bead in `bd ready` — P2, class:author, unassigned, no design dep —
and passed over it rather than claiming it, because the parent epic gqlc-h9n
records it in its 2026-07-28 tick notes as "parameterised PropertyType model,
non-delegated structural design", among children blocked on "owner decisions
outside the delegated ADR set". Nothing in the ledger held it. That is
protocol exactly: the plan was promised elsewhere and was missing here.
His call was right, and the missing design dep was an intake defect of mine.

TWO CLAIMS IN THE DESCRIPTION ABOVE ARE STALE. Measured on origin/master today:

1. "gqlc-h9n.5 ... is already open and has the fuller design note" — h9n.5 is
   CLOSED, and the parameterised model it recommended HAS SHIPPED for LIST.
   internal/graph/propertytype.go carries Kind()/Elem()/ElemNotNull() over a
   "LIST<ELEM>" string encoding. So "land all three or say why not" is now two:
   RECORD and closed dynamic unions.
2. "internal/codegen/types.go:163" does not exist on master. goType is
   per-dialect now (internal/codegen/age/types.go, internal/codegen/neo4j/types.go).

I have NOT edited the description, so the record of what was believed stays
readable. Read these notes as the correction.

WHAT IS LEFT TO DECIDE, and why it is genuinely a design and not ceremony: LIST
takes one positional parameter. RECORD needs NAMED fields and a closed dynamic
union needs an unordered MEMBER SET. Whether the shipped string encoding plus
Kind() extends to those, or whether they force a composite representation, is a
structural decision about a core schema type. gqlc-be1me asks exactly that.

When be1me closes, the plan will be written into THIS bead and it releases
straight to an author — no review, per protocol

The P3->P2 promotion recorded above stands; this changes routing, not priority.
DESIGN (gqlc-be1me, agent-h, 2026-09-02, at e81378b5). This is the plan h9n.33 was blocked on. Every file:line below was verified against origin/master today; where I ran a falsifier its result is stated, including the one that killed my own first claim.

## The problem in plain words

A property's type is one string with one parameterised form, LIST<ELEM>. Two declined ISO families need parameters that string does not yet carry: RECORD needs a list of NAMED fields, each with its own type and NOT NULL; a closed dynamic union (ANY VALUE<A|B>, bare A|B) needs a MEMBER SET where spelling order presumably does not matter. Decide: extend the string encoding plus Kind(), or move PropertyType to a composite struct.

## Ruling: extend the string encoding. Land BOTH families in model+parse. Land NEITHER in emission — refuse there with a correctly-diagnosed sentinel.

Composite rejected, with falsifiers, all measured at e81378b5:
- Comparability is load-bearing THREE ways: `case graph.TypeString:` switch tables (age/types.go:109, neo4j/types.go:38), `prop.Type != unified.Type` in ref unification (resolver/scope.go:1023), and typeSpellings map values. A struct carrying []field/[]member slices is not comparable; every one of those sites breaks at compile time and must be rewritten in the same PR.
- JSON: PropertyType marshals as a bare string at schema/schema.go:75 and resolver/validated.go:181 and appears in resolver goldens as "type": "STRING". Composite needs custom marshalling just to stand still.
- The discriminator h9n.5 actually demanded is Kind(), which shipped. Composite adds no diagnostic power over an encoding read through Kind() first.
This is dominated, not a coin-flip: the string extension is cheaper on every axis and loses on none I could find. The extension is safe for the same reason LIST's was: Kind() is read before any scalar switch, so "is a record" and "is an unrepresentable scalar" cannot collapse.

## The canonical encoding

  enc     := <scalar constant>                          (unchanged)
           | "LIST<" enc [" NOT NULL"] ">"              (unchanged)
           | "RECORD<>"                                 (RECORD { } — zero fields)
           | "RECORD<ANY>"                              (braceless RECORD / ANY RECORD)
           | "RECORD<" field ("," field)* ">"
           | "UNION<" member ("|" member)+ ">"
  field   := name " " enc [" NOT NULL"]
  member  := enc [" NOT NULL"]
  name    := bare if it matches ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$, else backtick-quoted
             with internal backticks doubled (the lexer's own escape — the
             "double grave accent" convention).

Why quoting is not optional: fieldName : identifier (GQL.g4:2891) and identifier admits DELIMITED_IDENTIFIER (:2956-2958), so a grammatical field name can contain "," "|" "<" ">" and forge structure in an unquoted encoding.

Canonicalisation, done ONLY by the constructors (nothing else may build these strings by hand):
- RecordOf: fields sorted by name (byte order). Duplicate field names never reach it — the parser rejects them (below).
- UnionOf: recursively flatten nested unions; a bare TypeAnyPropertyValue member absorbs the union to TypeAnyPropertyValue; sort members by their encoded string; drop exact duplicates (Type+NotNull); a single remaining member with NotNull=false collapses to that member's type. A NOT NULL singleton stays a union — collapsing it would drop the qualifier on the floor.

Why canonicalisation is the point: scope.go:1023 compares property types with == to unify a query ref across labels. Canonical construction is what makes string equality structural equality, so {a INT, b STRING} unifies with {b STRING, a INT} and STRING|INT with INT|STRING. Under-canonicalising refuses valid queries; over-canonicalising at worst equates types no emission distinguishes yet. Sorting is therefore the safe direction of error.

ISO-SEMANTICS CAVEAT, for the ADR: the semantics volume is unavailable (the free artefacts are BNF + Annex D; the arbiter bead is gqlc-lir). These are recorded gqlc decisions, revisable when an arbiter exists: field-order insignificance; union set semantics; member-level NOT NULL preserved literally; bare-singleton collapse; ANY absorption; RECORD<> and RECORD<ANY> being distinct types.

## internal/graph/propertytype.go — the API

  KindRecord, KindUnion appended to PropertyTypeKind (KindScalar stays the zero value).
  Kind(): two more prefix tests, "RECORD<" and "UNION<". No scalar constant collides with either prefix (checked the full typeSpellings table).
  type RecordField struct { Name string; Type PropertyType; NotNull bool }
  type UnionMember struct { Type PropertyType; NotNull bool }
  func RecordOf(fields []RecordField) PropertyType
  func UnionOf(members []UnionMember) PropertyType
  func (pt PropertyType) Fields() []RecordField    // nil for RECORD<>, RECORD<ANY>, non-records
  func (pt PropertyType) Members() []UnionMember   // nil for non-unions
  const TypeAnyRecord PropertyType = "RECORD<ANY>"

Fields()/Members() need a depth-aware AND quote-aware top-level splitter (track '<'/'>' depth; treat backtick spans as opaque, honouring doubled backticks). ~30 lines plus tests. Naive strings.Split dies on RECORD<a RECORD<x INT,y INT>,b STRING> and UNION<LIST<UNION<A|B>>|STRING> — pin both shapes.

MEASURED, against my own prediction: Elem() and ElemNotNull() do NOT need rewriting. I predicted the trim chain corrupts LIST<RECORD<a INT NOT NULL>> (claim: TrimSuffix " NOT NULL" eats the field qualifier); scratch probe at e81378b5 says otherwise — TrimSuffix(">") removes exactly one byte, so the remainder still ends in ">" and the NOT NULL trim never fires. All five rows I tried came back correct, including LIST<RECORD<a INT> NOT NULL>. But that safety is an ACCIDENT of removing one byte: pin these rows in propertytype tests so a refactor (e.g. TrimRight) cannot silently break it. If your implementation finds a case where the trim chain IS wrong, that is a finding — record it and rewrite over the splitter.

## internal/schema/gql/propertytype.go — the parser

resolveValueType gains three cases BEFORE the declineValueType call, exactly where the list alternatives sit and for the same stated reason (the comment at :33-39 — outer notNull must be read from the DIRECT child; a hasNotNull subtree scan would steal a field's or member's qualifier for the property):
- *gen.RecordTypeLabelContext: ctx.RecordType(). If FieldTypesSpecification() is nil → braceless → (TypeAnyRecord, direct NotNull() != nil). Else walk FieldTypeList(), which is NIL for {} (ANTLR non-nil accessor ≠ non-empty — walk to the leaf): nil → ("RECORD<>", notNull). Each fieldType: name from FieldName().GetText() (verbatim; use the token-stream spelling() if delimited text needs its raw form — check what GetText returns for a delimited identifier and keep the UNQUOTED name in RecordField.Name), type+notNull via recursive resolveValueType on its valueType. REJECT a duplicate field name with a new named error mirroring ADR 0030's repeated-property rule.
- *gen.ClosedDynamicUnionTypeAtl1Context (ANY VALUE?<A|B|...>): members via recursive resolveValueType over AllValueType(). The grammar gives this alt NO outer notNull (GQL.g4:1731) → outer false.
- *gen.ClosedDynamicUnionTypeAtl2Context (A|B): same; grammar-literal reading means a trailing "NOT NULL" binds to the RIGHT MEMBER, not the property (GQL.g4:1732 has no outer notNull). Record this in the ADR — an author may expect otherwise, and we are choosing the grammar's reading, not the charitable one.

Then: declineValueType drops its RecordTypeLabelContext and ClosedDynamicUnion cases; delete ErrRecordValueType and ErrDynamicUnionType from errors.go (the comment at errors.go:120-121 already names h9n.33 as the bead that deletes them); sentinel_coverage_test adjusts. NOTE the behaviour change recursion brings: members/fields are now DESCENDED, so a nested declined family (PATH | STRING) surfaces ErrPathValueType instead of the old outer-context sentinel — corpus_area_d2 rows that pinned no-descent (e.g. the reason at :59, :67) flip accordingly, and the RECORD {} decline pinned at corpus_area_d2_test.go:184 flips to resolution.

## internal/codegen — the third question, and the misdiagnosis this design exists to prevent

Today a record/union string reaching a dialect typeMap falls through the scalar switch to ("", false) — age/types.go:168's fallthrough, neo4j/types.go:93 — and prepare wraps that as ErrUnrepresentableWidth (prepare.go:573), whose meaning is PERMANENT. That is the exact diagnosis collapse h9n.5 was written against, one layer down.

Add to internal/codegen/errors.go (beside ErrUnrepresentableWidth at :75) a shared sentinel, e.g. ErrUnimplementedTypeKind = errors.New("property type kind not implemented yet") — the "yet" is load-bearing, per ADR 0019's discipline; the wrapped message names entity/property/type as the width errors do. Add a small recursive helper in prepare.go that walks a PropertyType via Kind()/Elem()/Fields()/Members() and returns the first KindRecord/KindUnion sub-type found; call it BEFORE typeMap.Property at all four sites — :573 (entity properties), :672 (columns), :716 (params), :1281 (list elements). It must recurse: a shallow check passes LIST<RECORD<...>> (Kind()==KindList) and the nested record then dies inside the typeMap's recursion as a width error.

CONTEXT.md vocabulary (my duty, discharged through this PR): the "Carrier question / storage question" entry gains the emission question — "has gqlc built an emission for this kind at all?" — asked before both, routing to the new sentinel; and "a property type describes a stored scalar" (Result type entry, ~:487) becomes "a stored value", which a record no longer contradicts.

Both dialect typeMaps stay UNTOUCHED. The kind walk intercepts before them, and their scalar switches keep meaning what they mean today.

## Tests that FAIL if this design is wrong (name these in your battery)

1. Entity with a record property fails generation with ErrUnimplementedTypeKind and NOT ErrUnrepresentableWidth. Red on any implementation that lifts the parse decline without the prepare walk — the central risk, witnessed.
2. Same assertion for LIST<RECORD<a INT>> — kills the shallow-walk mutant of the helper.
3. Two fixtures spelling {a INT, b STRING} and {b STRING, a INT} resolve to the SAME PropertyType string; same for STRING|INT vs INT|STRING. Kills any implementation that skips canonicalisation, which nothing else will catch until a user's unification silently refuses.
4. The splitter over RECORD<a RECORD<x INT,y INT>,b STRING>, UNION<LIST<UNION<A|B>>|STRING>, and a backtick-quoted field name containing "," and ">".
5. The Elem()/ElemNotNull() accident-pins listed above.
6. Singleton collapse (ANY VALUE<STRING> == TypeString), NOT NULL singleton non-collapse, ANY absorption, duplicate-field rejection.

## Corpus / ratchet

corpus_area_d2 record and closed-union rows flip from decline to resolved-type assertions. isoGaps (corpus_iso_test.go) retires 4 of today's 14 rows: "constructed value type", "component type list", "dynamic union type", "closed dynamic union type" — all four cite h9n.33 or h9n.5's completion as their condition. isoGapRatchet updates to whatever the row count then is; measure, do not arithmetic it from this note.

## Scope boundary

- OPEN unions are gqlc-h9n.34 (ADR 0020 blocker) — untouched here.
- Emission of records and unions (what Go type a caller gets) is DEFERRED, refused with the new sentinel. At close, file the emission follow-up as a design+stub PAIR under epic h9n (record emission needs struct naming and per-backend storage answers — neo4j's map-storage refusal wants an ADR-0035-style live witness; union emission has a cheap any-carrier candidate but discards declared members, an ADR-0017-shaped loss someone must decide to accept). Do not absorb emission into this bead.
- maxLength on lists stays dropped, as today.

## ADR

Write ONE ADR in this PR, drafted from this note: the parameterised-encoding decision, the canonicalisation rules, and the ISO-semantics caveats flagged above. h9n.5 recommended an ADR for this model and none was written; 0035/0036 cover nested-list behaviour, not representation. Re-derive the number at push time with `just adr-next` and check open PRs/branches — numbered-artifact collisions survive a rebase.

## Review

This bead is design-gated, so the PR IS reviewed (protocol): file the round-1 class:reviewer bead UNASSIGNED at P2, wired --deps blocks:gqlc-h9n.33, naming the PR and what you most doubt.

Questions to me by mail (agent agent-h); I stay reachable. — agent-h

Reviewer bead [deleted:gqlc-ng1vr] filed UNASSIGNED and wired blocks:gqlc-h9n.33 — this PR is design-gated on gqlc-be1me so it does NOT merge on green gates alone. Two deviations from the ruled design recorded in the ADR, the code and the reviewer bead: (a) the kind walk does not descend into Fields()/Members(), (b) isoGaps rows and isoGapRatchet=14 stand, measured. Filed not ridden: gqlc-ke7ox (isoGaps conflation), gqlc-ozdkx (AGE type-table arms unswept). Emission is NOT in this PR and is owed as a design+stub pair under epic h9n.
