title: graph.EntityKind's String default is the silent shape this fence exists to catch, and nothing holds it
description:
Residue from gqlc-pw6yj, filed rather than ridden on the diff.

internal/graph/entitykind.go:17 reads:

    func (k EntityKind) String() string {
        switch k {
        case Edge:
            return "edge"
        default:
            return "node"
        }
    }

That default returns the ZERO member's wire name for any value that is not
Edge, which is exactly the shape internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go
was built for (bd gqlc-7hp5g): a member added later serialises as "node" and
nothing says so. It is also the shape the five sums of gqlc-5225b arrived by,
each of whose defaults was deleted and its answer hoisted below the switch
unchanged.

WHAT MAKES IT WORSE THAN THE ORDINARY CASE. The type's own doc comment claims
the property the default breaks:

    String is the lowercase name of the kind ("node" / "edge"). It is the
    single source the query model's JSON discriminator derives from, so the
    serialised tag can never drift from the enum.

"can never drift from the enum" is false while the default is there. A third
EntityKind member drifts silently, on the wire.

MEASURED 2026-09-03, executing gqlc-pw6yj, so this does not have to be
re-derived:

  - The fence CAN hold the sum today. Adding the single row
    {name: "EntityKind", declRoot: "../graph", scanRoots: ["../graph"],
    sentinel: "Node", dirs: ["graph"]} reds TestGuardedSumDefaultsDeclare-
    Themselves naming ../graph/entitykind.go:17 by position, with no
    misattribution from codegen's same-named EntityKind. The two-types-one-
    name collision does NOT block this; that was the claim gqlc-pw6yj
    corrected.
  - The dirs are NOT just ["graph"]. That single-root row also reds
    TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault, because entitykind.go:17 is the
    only EntityKind switch under ../graph and it has the default, so the root
    holds no still-guarded switch. There IS a second one outside it, at
    internal/query/cypher/expr.go:290 (`case graph.Node:` / `case graph.Edge:`,
    no default), so the row wants ../query in scanRoots and "cypher" in dirs.
    Both must be measured, not guessed.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and the choice is the work:

  (a) Delete the default and hoist `return "node"` below the switch,
      behaviour-identical for every value in range and out. This is the
      precedent set by gqlc-5225b and it makes `exhaustive` live.
  (b) Keep the default and tag it //gqlc:default-ok naming a test that fails
      when a declared member loses its arm — the Scalar/Temporal precedent.

DO NOT REACH FOR (b) WITHOUT CHECKING THE CANDIDATE TEST FIRST. The obvious
one is TestBindingDiscriminatorTracksEntityKind (internal/query/query_test.go:
903), whose doc comment says it "pins the binding kind tag to
graph.EntityKind.String". Read the body before trusting that: it asserts
`"kind":"` + b.Kind().String() + `"`, and Binding.Kind() returns a BindingKind,
not a graph.EntityKind. So it may be pinning the tag to a different sum's
Stringer than its comment claims, in which case it does not buy the exemption
and its own comment is a third thing to correct. That is unverified here and
is the first thing to measure.

Inherited from agent-k via agent-c (gqlc-pw6yj), executed by agent-d.

Refs: gqlc-pw6yj, gqlc-5225b, gqlc-7hp5g
notes:
EXECUTED 2026-09-03 by agent-d. Route (a) — default deleted, answer hoisted below
the switch. Route (b) is refused, and the bead's first-thing-to-measure is the
reason.

MEASURED FIRST, as the bead directed: TestBindingDiscriminatorTracksEntityKind
does NOT pin graph.EntityKind.String. Binding.Kind() returns a BindingKind
(query.go:327, 393, 591), so the test has always pinned BindingKind.String
(query.go:277). Its name and its doc comment were both wrong. It buys no
exemption, so (b) has no candidate test and is out.

THEN A BIGGER ONE, which the bead did not anticipate. graph.EntityKind.String
has NO PRODUCTION CALLER AT ALL. Deleting the whole method leaves
`go build ./...` clean; the only breakage is entitykind_test.go:14-15. Every
`Kind().String()` call site in internal/ is on a BindingKind, and no EntityKind
value is formatted with %s anywhere. So the type's own doc comment — "the single
source the query model's JSON discriminator derives from" — was false in both
halves, not merely in the "can never drift" clause the bead quoted. Three
comments carried that falsehood (the type's, TestEntityKindString's,
TestBindingDiscriminatorTracksEntityKind's) and all three are corrected.

MUTATION RECORD (decision 0005). Every row compile-screened, tree restored and
`git status --short` verified clean after each.

| row | mutation | expected | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | fence row added, entitykind.go untouched | RED | RED — TestGuardedSumDefaultsDeclareThemselves names ../graph/entitykind.go:17 by position, no misattribution from codegen's EntityKind |
| D0 | tree as committed | GREEN | GREEN |
| D1 | dirs += "resolver" (outside both scan roots) | RED | RED — TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault, naming "resolver" |
| D2 | the `default` restored in entitykind.go | RED | RED — same test, naming dir "graph" |
| D3 | `case Edge:` arm deleted from the new form | RED | RED — exhaustive: "missing cases ... graph.Edge" |
| D3ctl | new form as committed, linted | clean | 0 issues |
| D5a | ORIGINAL defaulted form + a third member Path | silent | 0 issues — exhaustive says NOTHING |
| D5b | new form + the same third member Path | RED | RED — exhaustive: "missing cases ... graph.Path" |
| D5c | ORIGINAL form + Path, at run time | "node" | graph.Path.String() == "node" |

D5a/D5b/D5c are the bead's claim measured end to end: a third member added under
the old form serialises as a node and the linter is silent about it; under the
new form the linter names the missing member before it can ship.

THE DIRS QUESTION, measured and not guessed as the bead required. The row is
scanRoots ["../graph", "../query"], dirs ["graph", "cypher"]. D1 proves the dirs
check runs for this row and reds on a dir it cannot witness; the green baseline
with "cypher" present proves the walk does find the default-less switches at
internal/query/cypher (expr.go and listener.go both spell `case graph.Node:`).
The bead's prediction that a single-root ["graph"] row reds
TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault was true of the PRE-FIX tree only — once
the default is gone, ../graph holds a still-guarded switch and ["graph"] alone
passes. "cypher" is kept anyway, for the reason the Cardinality/TypeToken rows
name theirs: it is what makes ../query silently ceasing to be read fail.

APPARATUS NOTE, because it produced a false green I nearly believed. My first
D1/D2 run selected `-run TestGuardedSumDefaultsDeclareThemselves` and both rows
came back GREEN against a prediction of RED. The dirs loop is not in that
function — it is in TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault. I had read the two
as one function from adjacent line numbers, and those line numbers had shifted
under my own edit. Re-run against the right test, both rows red as predicted.
close_reason: Route (a): default deleted, answer hoisted below the switch, guardedSums row added so exhaustive is live. Measured with a third member: under the old default exhaustive reported 0 issues and the member serialised as "node"; under the new form exhaustive names it. Route (b) refused — TestBindingDiscriminatorTracksEntityKind pins BindingKind.String, not EntityKind.String, so it bought no exemption. Also found: EntityKind.String has no production caller at all (go build clean without it), so three doc comments calling it the JSON discriminator's source were false and are corrected. PR #2509, merged f92048c4.

title: schema/gql: sweep for guards whose only witnesses agree with a constant
description:
gqlc-952q's own description names this and declines to file it: "this is the
second instance in one PR of the same shape — a guard whose only witnesses agree
with a constant. agent-k found the first herself (her doubt #4, her M09). Worth
noticing as a pattern in this package rather than as two unrelated tickets."
Both instances are now closed; the pattern is not, and nothing sweeps for it.

THE SHAPE. A comparison or predicate has witnesses, and every witness it has
would also pass under a WEAKER predicate, because no fixture separates them. The
guard is then asserted by the code and by nothing else, and any future edit that
relaxes it ships green.

gqlc-952q's instance, measured: loader.go:70 compared byte-exactly, and every
reference/declaration pair in the package differed in MORE than case, so
strings.EqualFold left all four schema packages green. One row closed it.

WHY A SWEEP RATHER THAN CASE-BY-CASE. Two instances in one PR is a rate, not a
coincidence, and the cost of finding a third by review is a whole review. The
instances are cheap to close (one table row each) and expensive to notice.

WHAT THE SWEEP IS. Enumerate the equality and containment comparisons over
NAMES in internal/schema/gql — at minimum loader.go, nodetype.go, edgetype.go,
propertytype.go — and for each ask the one question: is there a fixture pair
that a weaker comparison would accept? Candidate weakenings, one per guard, are
strings.EqualFold for case, strings.TrimSpace for surrounding blanks, and
strings.Contains/HasPrefix for exactness. A guard is witnessed when at least one
weakening reds at least one row.

SCOPE WARNING, from having just done one of these. The answer for some guards
will legitimately be "the weaker comparison is also correct" — do NOT add a row
that pins a property the code does not actually promise. Where the semantics are
genuinely undecided, that is a designer's question and the sweep should file
it rather than invent an answer (protocol).

METHOD NOTE. Per decision 0005 each closing row must be measured, not argued:
the weakening must be applied, screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null`, and the
row shown RED with it and green without. Assert the reason and not merely the
verdict — pin the sentinel and the message, so a row reddening for an unrelated
cause cannot be read as the guard working.

RELATED: gqlc-952q (the case instance, closed by this session's PR),
gqlc-grld (the review that found both).
notes:
2026-09-03, agent-d: NOT claimed, and the reason is about timing rather than scope.

PR #2478 ("schema/gql: decode a delimited identifier at the token read") is
open and rewrites the very surface this sweep enumerates:

  internal/schema/gql/nodetype.go      +34/-7
  internal/schema/gql/propertytype.go  +19/-5
  internal/schema/gql/listener.go      +50/-9
  internal/schema/gql/edgetype.go       +2/-2
  internal/schema/gql/identifier.go    +149/-0  (new)
  internal/schema/gql/errors.go        +34/-0

Three of the four files this bead names by name are in it, and what it changes
is exactly the variable the sweep asks about: how a NAME is decoded before it
reaches a comparison. A guard that today has no witness separating it from
strings.EqualFold may acquire or lose one once identifiers are decoded at the
token read, and four new invalid fixtures arrive with it. So a sweep run
against HEAD now would measure a tree that is about to stop existing, and its
rows would land in conflict with #2478 besides.

WHAT TO DO AFTER #2478 MERGES, so this is not re-derived: re-enumerate from
identifier.go outward rather than from loader.go. The new decode point is the
better place to ask the question, because a weakening applied there is visible
to every comparison downstream at once, where a weakening applied per call
site is not.

Not filing anything against #2478 — it is doing its own job and this bead's
question is not one it was asked.

2026-09-03, agent-d: hold CLEARED, claiming.

PR #2478 merged at 08:13Z as 788b82b3, which was the whole reason this bead was
left unclaimed. Running the sweep from identifier.go outward as the note above
directs, not from loader.go.
SWEEP RUN 2026-09-03 by agent-d, from identifier.go outward as this bead's own note directs (the hold on #2478 cleared when it merged as 788b82b3 at 08:13Z).

Method per decision 0005: apply the weakening to the tree, compile-screen with
`go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/schema/gql/`, run the module suite, name the
victim rows, restore, verify `git status --short` clean. One row per guard.

| # | guard | site | weakening applied | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | no-escape marker is a LEADING marker | identifier.go:45 | HasPrefix("@") -> Contains("@") | SURVIVED |
| W2 | own-delimiter doubling | identifier.go:76 | any quote char may double | KILLED |
| W3 | trailing-name equality (gqlc-952q control) | loader.go:70 | != -> !EqualFold | KILLED |
| W4 | canonicalSpelling case fold | propertytype.go:413 | drop ToUpper | KILLED |
| W5 | collapseParenthetical inner trim | propertytype.go:442 | drop TrimSpace | KILLED |
| W6 | \U takes six digits | identifier.go:127 | 6 -> 4 | KILLED |
| W7 | \u takes four digits | identifier.go:125 | 4 -> 6 | KILLED |
| W8 | ampersand guard breadth | nodetype.go:76 | Contains -> HasPrefix | KILLED |
| W9 | empty-name guard | identifier.go:53 | removed entirely | KILLED |

Named victims: W2 the_other_delimiter_is_ordinary_content. W3
a_file_whose_declaration_differs_from_the_lookup_only_in_case. W4
TestPropertyBinaryWidthWhitespaceAndCase/int(8). W5 two rows. W6 two rows. W7
one row. W8 and W9 several rows each.

edgetype.go was enumerated and holds NO name comparison at all — its endpoints
are carried as label sets and resolved by key lookup, so it contributes no row.

EXACTLY ONE INSTANCE OF THIS BEAD'S SHAPE EXISTS, and it is W1. Every witness of
the no-escape refusal writes the @ in leading position, so Contains accepts every
one of them and the anchoring is asserted by the code and by nothing else. Closed
by TestTheNoEscapeRefusalIsAboutTheLEADINGMarker (identifier_test.go), two rows —
accent-quoted and double-quoted — each asserting that `a@b` PARSES and resolves
to the decoded label-set key. Measured: SURVIVED at HEAD before the test, KILLED
after, both sub-rows.

THE SCOPE WARNING DID NOT FIRE — no designer question is owed. W1's strong form
is provably correct rather than arguably so: Contains would refuse the valid
identifier `a@b`, and the same anchoring carries the text[1:len(text)-1] slice
that strips the delimiters, so weakening it is not a defensible alternative
reading of the rule.
close_reason: Sweep complete. Nine name guards in internal/schema/gql weakened one row apiece; exactly one instance of the bead's shape found — identifier.go:45's HasPrefix anchoring of the no-escape marker, SURVIVED at HEAD, KILLED by TestTheNoEscapeRefusalIsAboutTheLEADINGMarker. edgetype.go holds no name comparison. Scope warning did not fire. PR #2507, merged 83e7cc03.

title: neo4j writeMethod dispatches cardinality through if/else, so exhaustive cannot check it and an unnamed member silently gets the :many body
description:
Found while working gqlc-f5dkc, which is the AGE half of the same question.

internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go writeMethod dispatches on cardinality
with a SWITCH carrying no `default`, which is what puts it inside
`exhaustive`'s check (.golangci.yml sets default-signifies-exhaustive). PR
#2445 made it that way deliberately, and bd gqlc-ptz4t measured that deleting
an arm reds the line by name.

internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:351 writeMethod does the same job with
if/else:

    if p.Cardinality == queryfile.CardinalityExec { ...; return }
    writeRunCall(b, p)
    if p.Cardinality == queryfile.CardinalityOne {
        writeOneBody(b, p)
    } else {
        writeManyBody(b, p)
    }

Two consequences, and only the first is worth acting on:

 1. `exhaustive` cannot see an if/else chain at all, so the linter protection
    the AGE side has does not exist here. A Cardinality member added upstream
    reaches no diagnostic on this path.

 2. Such a member would take the `else` and silently receive the :many body —
    exactly the silent behaviour the AGE comment says naming CardinalityMany
    escaped.

NOT UNSOUND TODAY, and this is why it is P3. codegen's phaseAAdmit admits One,
Many and Exec by name and routes every other value through
ErrInvalidCardinality, and neo4j's generate calls codegen.Prepare before
rendering — so no input reaches this dispatch with an unnamed member.
Measured on gqlc-f5dkc; conformance's assembled_input_test.go row
"cardinality-not-in-set" is the standing witness for that wall.

THE REMEDY is to rewrite the dispatch as a `switch p.Cardinality` with three
named arms and no `default`, matching the AGE side, so the linter covers both
backends alike. Check while doing it whether the :exec early-return can stay
an early return inside the switch or wants restructuring — the shapes are not
identical (neo4j's :exec arm returns before writeRunCall, AGE's writeExecBody
does not).

WITNESS IT the way gqlc-f5dkc witnessed the AGE side: assemble a
codegen.Query with a Cardinality naming no member, render, and assert on the
emitted method. Today that assertion would read "the body is the :many body";
after the fix it reads "the body is empty".

Refs: gqlc-f5dkc, gqlc-ptz4t
notes:
PR #2480 (branch fix/gqlc-h08nx-neo4j-cardinality-switch, commit 54318805), agent-d 2026-09-03.

WHAT SHIPPED. writeMethod's if/else is now a `switch p.Cardinality` with three
named arms and no `default`, matching AGE. The :exec arm moves into a new
`writeExecBody` — answering the bead's open question: the early return could NOT
stay, because it existed only to skip writeRunCall (which the switch now does
structurally) and an arm returning from writeMethod would take the closing brace
with it. Emitted bytes unchanged; test/data/codegen untouched and the fence
reports 0 issues.

WITNESS. TestACardinalityNamingNoMemberEmitsAMethodWithNoBody, the neo4j half of
gqlc-f5dkc, through a new WriteMethod seam in export_test.go — NOT
renderCypherFile, which the AGE equivalent calls, because neo4j's takes a
driverTarget whose type is unexported and an external test package cannot supply
one. RED before the change with the :many body's five statements where an empty
body was asserted.

MUTATION ROWS, declared before the run, each restored by cp from a pristine copy
and verified by sha256 (final tree hash 6f402faa84ec... matched). `just lint` was
the real gate, not a narrowed invocation.

  1. delete the whole `case queryfile.CardinalityOne:` arm
     lint KILLED — render_queries.go:375:2: missing cases in switch of type
     queryfile.Cardinality: queryfile.CardinalityOne (exhaustive)
     test KILLED, by the CONTROL row (a named member emitted no body).
     This is the proof the bead asked for. Adding a member would only test the
     declaration site, and internal/codegen re-exports queryfile.Cardinality,
     which is what blinded exhaustive on the AGE side until gqlc-ptz4t.

  2. add a `default:` writing the :many body
     lint SURVIVED, 0 issues. test KILLED.
     DECLARED, not a gap: .golangci.yml sets default-signifies-exhaustive: true,
     so a default takes the switch out of the check entirely. The linter cannot
     stop the old shape returning; the test can. Both guards are here because
     neither covers the other.

  3a. signature emits `) error` instead of a result pair — test SURVIVED.
  3b. signature emits no result list at all — test KILLED, both rows.
     Declared. 3a is correct to survive: `error` is still a result, so an empty
     body is still Go's missing return. Only 3b reaches the shape where "no body"
     stops meaning "does not compile". Matches what gqlc-f5dkc recorded on AGE;
     re-measured here rather than inherited.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The silence an unnamed member now gets is a backstop, not a
diagnostic anyone meets: phaseAAdmit admits the three by name and routes anything
else through ErrInvalidCardinality (prepare.go:675), and generate calls Prepare
before rendering (generate.go:52). Both the comment and the test say so.

Gates green pre-push: just test rc=0, just lint 0 issues, just test-codegen-fence
0 issues.
close_reason: Merged in PR #2480. writeMethod is now a switch with three named arms and no default, matching AGE; the :exec early return could not stay (it only skipped writeRunCall, and an arm returning from writeMethod would take the closing brace) so it moved into writeExecBody. Emitted bytes unchanged, goldens and fence untouched. Witnessed by TestACardinalityNamingNoMemberEmitsAMethodWithNoBody through a new WriteMethod seam. Mutation row 1 is the proof asked for: deleting the CardinalityOne arm gives 'render_queries.go:375:2: missing cases in switch of type queryfile.Cardinality: queryfile.CardinalityOne (exhaustive)'. Row 2 (adding a default) survives lint by design and is killed by the test, which is why both guards are here.

title: bd dep list is DIRECTIONAL: it prints 'has no dependencies' for a bead that blocks something, so the natural read-back of --deps blocks: reads the wrong end
description:
FILED WRONG, THEN MEASURED. The original title claimed `bd create --deps` was
silently dropped. That is FALSE and the correction is the finding.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, measured 2026-09-03 from agent agent-d:

`bd create ... --deps blocks:<target>` wires the edge correctly. The edge is
recorded in ONE direction, and `bd dep list <id>` prints only what <id>
DEPENDS ON — never what it blocks. So:

    bd create "review ..." --deps blocks:[deleted:gqlc-wnwls]   ->  [deleted:gqlc-6vko1]
    bd dep list [deleted:gqlc-6vko1]        ->  "[deleted:gqlc-6vko1] has no dependencies"
    bd dep list [deleted:gqlc-wnwls]        ->  "[deleted:gqlc-6vko1] ... via blocks"     <- the edge

Both lines are about the same, correctly-created edge. The first is the natural
thing to run after creating a bead — you check the bead you just made — and it
is the wrong end.

THE FALSIFYING PROBE. gqlc-3ds4q (now closed) was created with nothing but
`--deps blocks:gqlc-2399s` and no other flags. Its own dep list was empty; the
target's showed it `via blocks`. A second create in the same session carrying
`--deps discovered-from:[deleted:gqlc-wnwls]` DID show on its own list, because
`discovered-from` points the other way — which is what made the directionality
visible rather than looking like a dead flag.

I then re-checked the two beads I had already accused: [deleted:gqlc-nl9ct]'s edge is
present on [deleted:gqlc-2c88r], and [deleted:gqlc-bj609]'s likewise. Three for three WIRED, where I
had recorded three for three dropped. The redundant `bd dep add` I ran to
"repair" [deleted:gqlc-6vko1] was idempotent — [deleted:gqlc-wnwls] carries exactly one `via blocks`
edge, not two — so no damage, but that was luck rather than design.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD ANYWAY. "gqlc-3ds4q has no dependencies" is a POSITIVE
sentence, not an empty result, and it is false in the sense any reader will take
it: that bead is in a dependency relationship. A reader verifying their own write
gets a confident denial of the thing they just correctly did, and the repair they
reach for is a duplicate `bd dep add`. I filed a P2 bug against the wrong
component on the strength of it.

REMEDY, cheapest first: make the empty case name its direction — "gqlc-3ds4q
depends on nothing" — and ideally print the inverse edges too, or say where to
look for them. The flag is fine; the read-back is what lies.

BOUND ON THIS: measured against the bd in this checkout on 2026-09-03; I did not
pin `bd version`. All observations are from one agent and one BEADS_DIR.

title: TestGuardedSumsAreNotAliased: a paren-spelled alias RHS evades aliasedTypeName and still blinds exhaustive
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 while judging PR #2457 (bead gqlc-dfzum), in a scratch extract of head c1ceecc4.

THE GAP. aliasedTypeName (internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go) accepts *ast.Ident and *ast.SelectorExpr and returns false for everything else. `type Cardinality = (queryfile.Cardinality)` parses as *ast.ParenExpr, so the tripwire returns false for it — while the alias is still an alias, and exhaustive is still blind through it.

THE FALSIFIER, re-runnable: at c1ceecc4, add `type Cardinality = (queryfile.Cardinality)` to internal/codegen/input.go, retype cardinalityAnnotation's parameter to that alias, delete its CardinalityMany arm. Measured: `go test -run '^TestGuardedSumsAreNotAliased$' ./internal/codegen/` PASSES, and `golangci-lint run --enable-only exhaustive --max-same-issues=0 --max-issues-per-linter=0 ./internal/codegen/...` reports 0 issues over a switch missing a member. Complete evasion. gofmt (plain and -s) does NOT strip the parens, measured on `type C = (int)`, so no formatting gate catches the spelling either.

WHY NOT A FAIL ON THE PR: the tripwire's own comment discloses two bounds (alias declared outside scan roots; rename through an intermediate) and this is a third it does not name. It is strictly additive to master, which had no tripwire at all, and the spelling does not arise accidentally.

THE REMEDY, ~3 lines: unwrap ParenExpr at the top of aliasedTypeName before the switch:

    for {
        p, ok := expr.(*ast.ParenExpr)
        if !ok { break }
        expr = p.X
    }

and add the paren spelling as a row beside the existing negative control. While there, extend the bound comment to say parens are handled and intermediates/out-of-root declarations still are not.
notes: PR #2470 opened and auto-merge armed (squash). Branch fix/gqlc-w7edb-paren-alias-evades-tripwire, commit a9791d92. All 14 gates green locally. RED proved first by reverting the fix alone: exactly the 3 paren rows of TestAliasedTypeName failed. End-to-end falsifier (paren alias + deleted case arm) makes the fixed tripwire FAIL naming input.go:10:6 while exhaustive reports 0 issues; falsifier restored, tree clean before commit.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #2470, merged into master on 2026-09-03 with all CI checks green.
Verified by content, not by merge status: origin/master's internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go
carries both the ParenExpr unwrap in aliasedTypeName and func TestAliasedTypeName.

THE DEFECT. aliasedTypeName read *ast.Ident and *ast.SelectorExpr and nothing else, so
`type Cardinality = (queryfile.Cardinality)` parsed as *ast.ParenExpr, fell to the default arm,
and TestGuardedSumsAreNotAliased said nothing. The spelling is legal and gofmt-stable — gofmt
does not strip the parens — so the evasion survived every formatting gate in the tree. Found by
a reviewer reviewing PR #2457, which is where I shipped the tripwire.

THE FIX. aliasedTypeName unwraps *ast.ParenExpr to any depth before the type switch. Three lines.

RED FIRST. The fix was reverted alone with the new table left in place: exactly the three
parenthesised rows failed, and the five others — bare identifier, qualified selector, and the
[]T / *T / map[T]V negatives — stayed green. So the new rows are scoped to the claim, no
broader and no narrower.

TestAliasedTypeName asserts both halves per row, `ok` and the extracted name. An ok-only table
would pass on a reader that recognised the shape and returned the wrong name.

END-TO-END, against the bead's own falsifier. With `type Cardinality = (queryfile.Cardinality)`
planted in input.go and the `case queryfile.CardinalityMany:` arm deleted from
cardinalityAnnotation, the fixed tripwire FAILS naming input.go:10:6 and the declaration, while
`exhaustive` over the same tree reports 0 issues. That is the blindness the tripwire exists to
refuse, demonstrated rather than argued. The falsifier was restored before commit and the tree
was clean.

BOUNDS. The comment on TestGuardedSumsAreNotAliased already named two limits the tripwire does
not hold. It now names parens as a third and records that this one is closed, citing the reviewer's
measurement and pointing at TestAliasedTypeName — so it reads true to someone arriving with no
memory of the branch.

All 14 local gate arms passed; CI: actionlint, codegen-fence, govulncheck, lint, live-smoke,
test and tidy all green.

title: check-pr-closes: the two mirror-less exits are silent about a closing line GitHub cannot read, as the export skip was
description:
gqlc-2lx3r fixed the EXPORT SKIP: when a bead is absent from the committed
export, the run now names any closing number written inside code, because that
is the shape in which an author believes they claimed an issue and nothing
closes it.

Two neighbouring exits have the same blindness and were deliberately left out
of that diff, being a different condition:

  - :1129, the export's record carries no external_ref value
  - :1149, the mirror string names no parseable issue number

Both print via unverified_tail(), which takes refs/bead_id/marker_n and NEVER
READS THE BODY AT ALL. So they end with "no 'Closes' line was demanded and none
was checked" whatever the body says.

MEASURED 2026-09-03 on this branch, with a body whose only closing keyword is
inside a fence:

    $ python3 .github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py <noext.jsonl> <fenced-body> <branch>
    [check-pr-closes] the export's record for gqlc-2cmhl carries no external_ref
    value, so no 'Closes' line was demanded and none was checked
    rc=0

    $ python3 .github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py <badext.jsonl> <fenced-body> <branch>
    [check-pr-closes] gqlc-2cmhl mirrors 'not-a-url', which names no issue
    number, so no 'Closes' line was demanded and none was checked
    rc=0

Neither mentions #1234, which the author wrote and GitHub will not act on.

WHY IT IS SMALLER THAN THE ONE JUST FIXED, and why P3. The sentence these exits
print is honest about the DEMAND -- nothing was demanded and nothing checked --
and unlike the export skip, the bead here has no mirror, so the swallowed number
names some other issue rather than the PR's own. The population is also small:
the code's own comment at :1115 measured 2 of 459 export records carrying no
external_ref.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Do not fix this by making unverified_tail read the body: it is
called from both exits with different subjects and its return value is
concatenated onto two different sentences. The report belongs at the call sites,
or in a helper of its own that both call.

CHECK FIRST whether these exits should instead be folded together with the
export skip's new arm, which would be one report reached three ways rather than
three copies of a paragraph. That is the actual question, and it is why this is
filed rather than fixed inline.

title: writeMethod's compile-failure claim is unwitnessed: nothing exercises an unnamed Cardinality
description:
PR #2445 (bd gqlc-51l6m, merged 2026-09-03) changed
internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go writeMethod's `default:` to
`case codegen.CardinalityMany:`, and shipped a comment claiming what that buys:

    "It buys the loud failure instead — an unnamed member now writes no body,
     so the generated method is missing its return and does not compile, where
     the default silently emitted a :many body."

I WROTE THAT AND DID NOT WITNESS IT. Filing it rather than leaving the promise
in the tree unbacked. It is a claim about GENERATED output under an input no
test constructs, and it is load-bearing precisely because `exhaustive` is blind
to that switch (bd gqlc-ptz4t), so the compile failure is the ONLY thing
standing there.

WHY IT IS NOT REACHABLE TODAY, which is also why it went unwitnessed:
queryfile.parseCardinality yields the three members or refuses the annotation,
so no query text produces a fourth. Measured 2026-09-03 (bd gqlc-etz8 cell E7):
appending a well-formed CardinalityIter to queryfile's const block and an arm
to Cardinality.String leaves 28 packages green and golangci-lint at 0 issues,
caps lifted. The member is inert until the parser admits it.

WHAT WOULD WITNESS IT: assemble the input from outside the parser, the way
internal/codegen/conformance/assembled_input_test.go already does for an
out-of-set Cardinality and an out-of-set resolver.Temporal — that suite exists
exactly to reach fail-sites no query text reaches, and its `why` strings name
the Cardinality case. Drive writeMethod with a Cardinality naming no member and
assert on the emitted Go: either that it fails to compile, or — better, since
"does not compile" is awkward to assert — that the emitted method body is
empty/returnless, which is the observable the claim rests on.

TWO OUTCOMES, BOTH FINE:
  1. The claim holds and gains a witness, and the comment can cite it by test
     name the way resolver's //gqlc:default-ok tags cite theirs.
  2. The claim is FALSE — e.g. the emitter writes something for the unnamed
     case after all, or the generated file is never compiled by any gate — in
     which case the comment in the tree is a lie and must be corrected. That
     is the outcome worth the bead.

Check (2) first: it is cheap, and if the generated corpus is never compiled by
a gate then "does not compile" is not a property this repository holds anyone
to, and the whole comment needs rewriting rather than witnessing.

Refs: gqlc-51l6m, gqlc-ptz4t, gqlc-etz8
notes:
2026-09-03, agent-c, filed the same hour: DO NOT CONFLATE THIS WITH gqlc-7hp5g.

gqlc-7hp5g falsified a family of "the compiler catches a missing arm" claims in
codegen, and gqlc-80vvp tracks the stale copy still in
docs/specs/codegen-prepare-commits.md. Those claims are about GQLC'S OWN
switches failing to compile when an arm is missing, and they are false because
Go does not require a switch to be exhaustive — the linter catches it, or in
the type-switch cases nothing does.

MY CLAIM IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM and is not falsified by that work: writeMethod
does not fail to compile itself. It emits the METHOD BODY from its switch, so a
Cardinality naming no case causes it to write NO BODY, and the defect lands in
the GENERATED file — a func with a return type and no return statement.

That is why it needs its own witness rather than inheriting gqlc-7hp5g's
verdict, and it is also why the cheap first check listed above is the right
order: if no gate ever compiles the generated corpus, "does not compile" is not
a property this repository enforces on anyone, and my comment is wrong for a
third reason neither bead names.
PR #2473 opened, auto-merge armed (squash), Closes #2451 registered. Branch fix/gqlc-f5dkc-unnamed-cardinality-witness, commits dff45f37 + ce3afdc6. VERDICT: mechanism holds, failure unreachable — phaseAAdmit admits One/Many/Exec by name and generate calls Prepare before renderCypherFile, so no input reaches the switch with an unnamed member. Corpus IS compiled (test-codegen-fence builds test/data/codegen goldens; measured with a planted returnless func -> 'not enough return values'). 4-row battery, rows 1/2/3' KILLED, row 4 declared-SURVIVED control. Row 3 as first declared SURVIVED and falsified a sentence in my own test comment; corrected in ce3afdc6. Sibling filed as gqlc-h08nx (neo4j uses if/else, exhaustive cannot see it).
close_reason:
Merged as dab49ab3 (PR #2473).

The bead offered two outcomes — the "does not compile" claim holds, or the
generated corpus is never compiled and the claim is empty. The truth was a
third. The corpus IS compiled (measured: appending `func f() int { return }` to
test/data/codegen/valid/entity_edge_projected_one/golden/apache-age-pgx-v5/queries.cypher.go
and running `go build ./...` in the fenced module gives "not enough return
values"), and the mechanism is real — an unnamed Cardinality writes no body, so
the method is missing its return.

What is false is that anyone can reach it. codegen.Prepare's phaseAAdmit
(prepare.go:676) allow-lists One/Many/Exec by name and routes every other value
through ErrInvalidCardinality, and age.generate (generate.go:47) calls Prepare
before renderCypherFile (:97). A member added upstream is refused two phases
earlier; no file is emitted; nothing gets as far as failing to compile.

So the switch's silence is a backstop behind that gate, not a diagnostic.
Shipped: the comment now says so, and
TestACardinalityNamingNoMemberEmitsAMethodWithNoBody witnesses the mechanism
directly from the renderer rather than leaving it as an untested assertion in
prose.

Mutation battery ran with declared victims. Row 3 SURVIVED against my
declaration and that was the finding: I had declared that flipping
writeMethodSignature's `== CardinalityExec` to `!=` would red the results
assertion. It does not — `error` is still a result, so the empty body is still a
missing return. That falsified a sentence in my own test comment ("a method
returning only error compiles" — it does not), fixed in ce3afdc6. The mutation
that reds the results half is the one emitting no result list at all, and it
KILLED.

Noticed, not fixed: internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:351 does the same
job with if/else, so `exhaustive` cannot see it and an unnamed member silently
takes the :many branch. Filed as gqlc-h08nx (P3, class:author) rather than
ridden on this diff.

title: guardedSum.name cannot distinguish the two EntityKind types
description:
Found while working gqlc-51l6m. Two unrelated Go types in this tree are both
named EntityKind, with disjoint members:

  internal/codegen/prepare.go:233   EntityNode, EntityEdge
  internal/graph/entitykind.go:5    Node, Edge

internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go's guardedSum identifies a sum by a
single `name` string and matches switches with namesASumMember, which compares
BARE identifiers against the member set read from declRoot. So a row named
"EntityKind" reads one declRoot's members and silently attributes to that sum
any switch naming the OTHER type's members it happens to match — or, since the
member sets here are disjoint, finds only one type's switches and reports the
other's as absent. Either way the fence cannot express both, and the survey
row that motivated this reads:

  EntityKind  3 switches, 1 default, 0 tagged
              internal/codegen/prepare.go internal/graph/entitykind.go

with the one defaulted switch at internal/graph/entitykind.go:17.

Two things to decide, and they are separable:

  1. Should the two types be named apart? graph.EntityKind and
     codegen.EntityKind are different concepts and the collision is confusing
     to a reader independent of this fence. Renaming one is the repair that
     makes the fence problem disappear rather than being worked around.
  2. If they stay, guardedSum needs to key on qualified identity (declRoot +
     name, or a package path) rather than a bare name, and namesASumMember
     needs to resolve the switch's operand type rather than matching bare
     identifiers.

Nothing is unsound in the fence TODAY: no guardedSums row is named
EntityKind, so no wrong attribution is happening. This is the cost of adding
one, and it is why gqlc-51l6m did not.

Refs: gqlc-51l6m
notes:
2026-09-03, agent-d: executed as PR #2487. TWO OF THIS BEAD'S CLAIMS ARE FALSE and
the correction is the substance of the fix, so it is recorded here as well as
in the file.

FALSIFIED 1 — "a row named EntityKind ... silently attributes to that sum any
switch naming the OTHER type's members". Measured by adding the single row
{name: "EntityKind", declRoot: "../graph", scanRoots: ["../graph"], sentinel:
"Node", dirs: ["graph"]}: the fence holds it CORRECTLY. declRoot confines the
member scan to ../graph so it reads Node/Edge and never sees EntityNode/
EntityEdge, and codegen's EntityKind is in no row to be conflated with. The
run reds on ../graph/entitykind.go:17 by position, which is the right answer.
So the collision does not keep graph.EntityKind out of the fence, and this
file's exclusion note saying it did has been rewritten.

FALSIFIED 2 — the collapse is not silent. With BOTH rows the run reds. What
is wrong is the REASON: the per-sum-per-root check says "the walk found no
EntityKind switch anywhere under ../graph ... Either the switches there were
deleted, or the walk stopped reaching the root", and both halves are false —
the switch is in ../graph/entitykind.go and the walk reached it. A true
verdict with a false reason.

SO THE FIX IS THE REASON, NOT THE RED. duplicateSumName + requireDistinct-
SumNames fire ahead of the misdiagnosing check and name both declRoots.

DECISION 2 IS ANSWERED BUT NOT TAKEN, and the measurement is in the failure
message so it is not re-derived: the two member sets are disjoint and their
roots do not overlap, so a qualified key (declRoot + name) alone would be
enough and namesASumMember would NOT need to resolve operand types. That is
built when a second row actually wants it; building it now would ship
machinery with no user.

DECISION 1 (rename the two types) IS LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY. The message puts
it first, on this bead's own ground that the collision confuses a reader who
never opens the fence. That remains a designer's call and nothing here
forecloses it.

MEASURED BOUND, disclosed in the PR and in the test's doc comment: deleting
the `requireDistinctSumNames(t, guardedSums)` call from scanSumSwitches leaves
the package green, because the table drives the detector directly. Named
rather than fenced — the fence would be a test asserting on the file's own AST.

RESIDUE: gqlc-r79zi (graph.EntityKind's String default is the silent shape,
with the dirs measurement it needs).
close_reason: Merged as PR #2487; GH #2444 closed. TWO OF THIS BEAD'S CLAIMS WERE FALSIFIED by measurement and the correction is the substance of the fix. (1) A single graph.EntityKind row is held CORRECTLY — declRoot confines the member scan, so nothing is misattributed and the collision does not keep the sum out of the fence; this file's exclusion note saying it did has been rewritten. (2) The two-row collapse is NOT silent: it reds, but on the per-sum-per-root check, whose remedy ('the switches were deleted, or the walk stopped reaching the root') is false in both halves. A true verdict with a false reason. So what ships buys THE REASON, NOT THE RED: duplicateSumName plus requireDistinctSumNames fire ahead of the misdiagnosing check and name both declRoots, with TestGuardedSumNamesMustBeDistinct pinning the detector on a synthetic list because no shipped row can reach the case. Decision 2 is ANSWERED but not taken and the answer is written into the failure message so it is not re-derived: the member sets are disjoint and the roots do not overlap, so a qualified key alone would suffice and namesASumMember would not need go/types operand resolution. Decision 1 (rename the types) is left open deliberately and the message puts it first. Eight mutation rows, expected victim declared per row, go test -c screened; the one SURVIVED (deleting the call from scanSumSwitches leaves the package green) is disclosed in the test's own doc comment rather than fenced. Residue filed as gqlc-r79zi.

title: codegen: typeTextNamesCarrier matches a record FIELD NAME, so a field called Date over-emits the temporal carriers
description:
internal/codegen/temporal.go:126. typeTextNamesCarrier decides whether an emitted package must declare its five neutral temporal carriers by parsing a carrier's Go type text and walking it for an identifier in temporalCarrierSet — {Date, LocalTime, Time, LocalDateTime, Duration}.

A record's carrier text is a struct literal, and in a struct type the FIELD NAMES are *ast.Ident nodes too. So a record declaring a field the mangle spells `Date` — `RECORD { date :: STRING NOT NULL }` — emits

    struct{ Date string }

and the walk finds the identifier `Date`, concludes the package needs the temporal carriers, and emits temporal.go for a schema with no temporal width in it.

DIRECTION, which is why this is P3 and not higher: the failure is toward OVER-emission, and it is not a compile break. Go does not reject unused top-level type declarations, so the emitted package still builds; it just carries five carrier types nothing references. Under-emission would be the dangerous direction, and this walk cannot under-emit — a text that fails to parse is treated as "yes" (temporal.go:128-130), which is deliberate and is guarded by TestRecordStructTextIsAGoTypeExpression.

THE FIX is to walk field TYPES rather than every identifier: for an *ast.StructType, descend into each field's Type and skip its Names. Note the walk already stops at *ast.SelectorExpr for a related reason, so the shape of the change is familiar.

WHAT THE FIX OWES ITSELF: a mutation row. The current guard cannot see this — no test declares a record field named after a carrier — so the repair has to bring a fixture with one, and blinding the new StructType arm has to kill it.

Noticed during gqlc-jffyz (record property types) and deliberately not fixed there: it is a change to the temporal emission's trigger, in a bead about records, and the defect it causes is cosmetic output rather than wrong output.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #2434 (squash 82784a6a), verified by content on origin/master.

The bead's diagnosis was right and its proposed fix was too narrow. Both halves
were measured rather than reasoned about.

DIAGNOSIS, confirmed: typeTextNamesCarrier walked every *ast.Ident in an emitted
type text, and a struct's field NAMES are Idents, so "struct{ Date string }"
reported the package as carrier-bearing.

THE DEFECT IS LATENT AT THIS COMMIT, and the PR says so rather than implying a
live bug was fixed. graph.KindRecord is still refused with ErrUnimplementedTypeKind
at all four positions (prepare.go:567), nothing in internal/codegen produces a
struct-literal GoType, and the golden corpus is byte-identical across the change.
The walk was corrected AHEAD of the producer agent-d is writing under gqlc-jffyz.
No end-to-end row is possible until that lands, so the unit rows on the function
are the whole of what can honestly be pinned today.

WHERE I DEPARTED FROM THE BEAD. It said "for an *ast.StructType, descend into
each field's Type and skip its Names". ast.Inspect reaches *ast.Field in THREE
places — StructType.Fields, InterfaceType.Methods, and FuncType.Params/Results —
and a name is never a type reference at any of them, so the StructType-only cut
leaves the same defect at two of the three. Keying the arm on *ast.Field itself
covers all three in one arm. That is mutation row M4: applying the bead's own
proposed fix left the func-parameter and interface-method name rows failing.

Battery, 6 rows, victims declared before each run and every mutant grep-verified
as applied before its verdict was read. Victim sets were exact — predicted and
observed matched member-for-member, not just in count:

  R   new rows vs master's walk    the 4 NAME rows fail, the 4 TYPE rows pass
  M1  delete the *ast.Field arm    the 4 name rows                    KILLED
  M2  arm resumes descent to Names the 4 name rows                    KILLED
  M3  arm prunes, no Type recursion the 4 TYPE rows                   KILLED
  M4  the bead's StructType-only fix func-param + interface-method     KILLED
  M5  blind the SelectorExpr arm   the 2 qualified rows               KILLED

M3 is why every name-position row ships paired with a type-position row.
Under-emission breaks the emitted package where over-emission only bloats it, so
a walk that stopped reading field TYPES would be the worse defect; the pairs are
what make that visible instead of assumed. M5 screens the guard that was already
there, so the change is shown not to have quietly widened it.

The bead asked for "a fixture with a record field named after a carrier". That
fixture cannot exist end-to-end while KindRecord is refused; the unit rows are
that fixture at the level where the function lives.

Recorded in bd memory a-function-s-parameters-are-ast-field-too, which now holds
both directions of this walk and whose earlier "prune on StructType and
InterfaceType" advice M4 falsified.

master, and GH #2431 is CLOSED as of 2026-09-03T04:07:38Z. Closes #2431.

title: codegen/age: a constructor counts as an assertion, so a helper that only binds one launders its caller's answer
description:
The sibling of gqlc-qo6ul, at the OTHER call site of isAssertionCall, left out
of that diff deliberately rather than smuggled into it.

gqlc-qo6ul taught assertedText testify's first-documented spelling — an
assertion object bound to an ordinary local:

    r := require.New(t)
    r.Contains(msg, want)

It does that by computing assertionBases over the body it is reading and passing
the result to isAssertionCall. There are two callers of isAssertionCall. The
other one, assertionHelpers, passes nil bases, and its call site now says so in
a comment pointing here.

THE CONSEQUENCE. A sibling helper that binds its OWN assertion object:

    func assertRefusal(t *testing.T, msg, want string) {
        r := require.New(t)
        r.Contains(msg, want)
    }

is not registered as an assertion helper, because the only call inside it is
`r.Contains` and nothing has told that scan what `r` is. So a witness calling
assertRefusal reads nothing, and the sweep reports the answer unasserted. Same
false RED as gqlc-qo6ul and gqlc-bpew, one call site over.

WHY IT WAS NOT TAKEN WITH gqlc-qo6ul. Covering it is not free the way a sibling

title: a resolver-side default over Scalar or Temporal is outside the codegen exhaustive-default fence
description:
Sibling of gqlc-f5onb, disclosed on its diff rather than ridden on it.

internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go holds the rule that a `default` on a switch over a guarded sum must carry `//gqlc:default-ok <why>`, because .golangci.yml sets default-signifies-exhaustive and a default silently retires the missing-arm check.

Two of the three sums it guards — resolver.Scalar and resolver.Temporal — are DECLARED in internal/resolver. The fence reads their constants from there but scans for switches under internal/codegen alone.

MEASURED 2026-09-03 over the whole module, by AST walk:

  Scalar   : 4 guarded switches, all under internal/codegen
             (age/errors.go:495, age/errors.go:700, age/types.go:255,
              neo4j/types.go:164); 1 with a default, internal/resolver/
              validated.go:331, which is Scalar.String
  Temporal : 2 guarded switches, both under internal/codegen
             (age/types.go:224, neo4j/types.go:138); 1 with a default,
              internal/resolver/validated.go:431, which is Temporal.String

So the gap is EMPTY today: the only resolver-side defaults over either sum are the two String methods', both of which are correct and are already fenced by name in internal/resolver/sumdefaults_internal_test.go (TestScalarStringAnswersForDeclaredKindsAlone and its Temporal twin, which pin that the default answers for undeclared values ALONE).

THE EXPOSURE is that nothing stops a default being added to some other resolver-side Scalar/Temporal switch, and the codegen fence will not see it. That is the same hazard gqlc-7hp5g filed, one package over.

SHAPE, undecided and worth a moment's thought rather than a reflex:
  (a) widen the codegen fence's switch-scan root to cover internal/resolver
      — one tag needed on each String method, but a test under
      internal/codegen then reds when someone edits internal/resolver,
      which is a surprising place for that failure to surface; or
  (b) put a sibling fence in internal/resolver next to
      sumdefaults_internal_test.go, which is where a resolver-side rule
      already lives, at the cost of two files holding one rule; or
  (c) hoist the fence to a module-scope test that names its sums and
      their roots in one table. That is the honest generalisation and the
      largest diff, and it would also pick up any other closed enum in
      the module with the same shape — which has NOT been surveyed.

Not urgent: the gap is empty and both live defaults are independently fenced.

default-signifies-exhaustive: true), so adding a `default` retires the check
silently. gqlc-qf5az's fix covers switches whose cases name codegen.Column*.

  internal/codegen/age/errors.go:700  switch et.Kind
  internal/codegen/age/errors.go:495  switch ct.Kind

  // Exhaustive over resolver.Scalar with no default, so a kind added

  // side happened to be the fall-through.

gqlc-qf5az to correct — a comment asking a future author not to add a `default`
is not a gate — sitting on a different sum type, so gqlc-qf5az's guard walks
past it.

independent guard: if that guard keys on "cases naming codegen.Column*", the
generalisation is to key on a declared set of sum-type prefixes and add
resolver.Scalar* to it. Whoever takes this should read gqlc-qf5az's landed guard
first and widen it if that is cheaper than a new one.

stops one being added, and the comment at :700 reads as though something does.

covers Scalar covers it for one table row and zero production changes.
Building that mechanism and then pointing it away from an identical case
is the "fence that looks satisfied" shape this work exists to remove.
That is a judgement past the bead's letter and inside its stated shape
("a declared set of sum-type prefixes"); it is disclosed here and in the
PR body rather than buried.

THE BOUNDARY, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Scalar and Temporal are
DECLARED in internal/resolver, so the fence reads their constants from
there but still scans for switches under internal/codegen alone. The two
resolver-side defaults are Scalar.String and Temporal.String; both are
correct, and both are already fenced BY NAME in
internal/resolver/sumdefaults_internal_test.go
(TestScalarStringAnswersForDeclaredKindsAlone and its Temporal twin),
which pin that the default answers for undeclared values alone. So the
gap is empty today. A default added to some OTHER resolver-side switch
would be unheld -- filed as gqlc-8z5ap with the measurement and three
candidate shapes, not ridden on this diff.

any mutation so a per-row restore could not delete it; each row declared
its expected victim and diffstat before running, was run SEPARATELY
because `require` aborts at the first failure, was screened with
`go test -c` so a compiler kill could not pass as a suite kill, and was
followed by `sha256sum -c` over all four mutable files.

  R2 bare default on age/types.go:224 (Temporal)

  R4 default + tag on neo4j/types.go:138 -> dirs assertion

  R7 Temporal declRoot "../resolver" -> "." : same, Temporal/TemporalDate

     naming ColumnKind

description:

closes with an argument that the function scan and the namespace scan partition
calls by SHAPE, so no call can be claimed by both, and then said:

    TestAQueryOfBothKindsIsAnsweredByTheEarlierGap is where that is measured.

No such test exists. It was never written: git log -S on the name returns exactly
one commit, 0c472f66 / #1903, which is the commit that ADDED the sentence. The
citation was born dangling, and it is the strongest case the testcite guard has
found — a claim of measurement that nothing has ever measured, reading as
evidence to anyone who did not grep.

gqlc-som6y removed the false half of the sentence (the comment now says the
disjointness rests on the shape argument alone and that no row measures it).
This bead is the row itself.

WORK. Decide first whether the property is even reachable: the argument says a
call cannot be BOTH a refused function name and a refused namespace, because the
two scans read different spellings. If that is true by construction, the honest
artefact is a unit row asserting the partition over the catalogues rather than a
query row, and the comment should then name it. If a query CAN present as both,
that is a finding in its own right and the ordering (which gap answers first)
needs a ruling before a row can pin it.

ACCEPTANCE. Either a named test measures the disjointness claim and the comment
cites it, or the comment states why the property cannot be measured and this
bead records which of the two cases held.

Found by agent-k under gqlc-som6y, filed rather than ridden on that diff: this
is an age-dialect behavioural guard, and som6y is a citation-guard bead.

THE BEAD ASKED WHICH OF TWO CASES HELD. NEITHER DID, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.

unit row is the honest artefact; or a query CAN present as both, which is a
finding needing an ordering ruling. The tree was in a third state the bead did
not imagine: the property was HALF MEASURED, and two comments in the same package

title: a local just is unpinned, so local recipe runs and CI's differ by a version nobody states
description:
CI pins just 1.55.1 (.github/actions/setup-just/action.yml, both the cache key and the install --tag). A local run takes whatever just is on PATH. Nothing states the local expectation and nothing compares the two.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 in agent agent-k's worktree:

  CI pin (setup-just)            1.55.1
  this host (just --version)     1.58.0
  claimed in a doc comment       1.57.0   <- internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go

Three versions, no two the same. The third was a provenance line reading 'Two more measurements on this repo's justfile at just 1.57.0' over recipeBodies; gqlc-38wqz replaced it with a pointer to the pin, because re-pinning it to 1.58.0 would have recorded THIS HOST rather than the version the test runs under in CI.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go exists to compare this repo's own justfile reader against just's answer, and it gets just's answer by shelling out to whatever just is on PATH. Its doc comments record properties OF THE DUMP -- that the dump drops leading indentation, that it keeps '#' and '#!' lines, that body lines arrive as fragment lists. Those are output-format claims, and just's dump format is not a stability contract. So an agent measuring locally at 1.58.0 and CI running at 1.55.1 can disagree, and the disagreement would surface as a test failure in CI that no local gate reproduces -- the reverse of the usual direction, which is the direction nobody looks for.

It also has the ordinary shape: TestParseJustfileAgreesWithJustOnThisJustfile deliberately REQUIRES just rather than skipping when it is absent (that reasoning is in the file, ~line 732), on the grounds that an absent just is a broken environment. An unpinned PRESENT just of the wrong version is the same broken environment, and it is the one the file does not refuse.

FIX SHAPE, and it is a question before it is a change:
  1. Refuse a local just whose version is not the pinned one -- fail-closed, matches the file's own no-skip argument, but it makes every agent's

title: testcite guards cited test NAMES but not cited test FILENAMES, and the rot is the same
description:
internal/tools/testcite holds one guard: a comment in a non-test source that names a test must name a test that exists (bd gqlc-945h7). A comment that names a test FILE is the same prose citation and the same rot, and nothing reads it.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, on the branch for gqlc-4dwao. Across every *.go in the tree, comments cite 38 distinct <name>_test.go filenames. Six resolve to no file:

  19x  live_x_test.go          internal/liverecipes/split_test.go — a fixture path in a table, illustrative
   1x  live_a_test.go          same, illustrative
   1x  live_b_test.go          same, illustrative
   1x  live_synthetic_test.go  illustrative
   1x  plain_test.go           illustrative
   1x  hooktests_test.go       internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go:735 — DELIBERATELY dead

A seventh, live_age_ungated_test.go in test/data/codegen/live_nested_list_property_test.go, was live rot: the file was deleted by 0c472f66 the same morning and a WHY ITS OWN FILE argument still rested on it. That is gqlc-4dwao, fixed by dropping the citation. Nothing caught it; it was found by a human reading the paragraph.

WHY THE POPULATION MAKES THIS CHEAP. After 4dwao lands, every unresolved citation is deliberate, so the guard would go green on arrival with a small exemption table — testcite already has exactly that mechanism (its 'illustrative' map, keyed by file then by name, each entry carrying a reason, with a stale exemption failing the guard).

TWO DECISIONS THIS NEEDS, and they are why this is a bead rather than a rider on 4dwao's diff:

1. SCOPE. testcite reads non-test sources only, and its package doc gives a reason for that (a test citing a test is next to the thing it cites). But 4dwao's rot was in a _test.go, so the existing scope would not have caught it. Widening to test files is the change that makes the guard answer the case that motivated it, and it is a real widening.

2. A THIRD EXEMPTION CATEGORY. hooktests_test.go is not illustrative — it is a citation whose own sentence says the file was deleted and the citation dropped rather than repointed (bd gqlc-chep). 'Illustrative' does not describe it. A guard that files it under the illustrative reason would be recording something false about it.

RELATED: gqlc-945h7 (the test-name half), gqlc-chep (the precedent for the drop-rather-than-repoint remedy), gqlc-4dwao (the instance). Found while fixing 4dwao, filed rather than ridden.
notes:
SIBLING, not a duplicate: gqlc-som6y (extend the guard to comments in _test.go
sources; 20 unresolved names to triage). That widens WHERE the reader looks;
this one widens WHAT a citation is checked for. The third-exemption-category
question below is common to both.
PR #2424 open. Reproduction is the historical instance itself: restoring test/data/codegen/live_nested_list_property_test.go to f3cb4bea^ (the window between PR #1903 deleting live_age_ungated_test.go and PR #2401 repairing the paragraph by hand) reddens the new guard at that exact file; the same rotten tree under origin/master's guard PASSES. Population re-measured at HEAD: 31 distinct cited file names over 65 sites, exactly 1 unresolved (hooktests_test.go, pinned HISTORICAL). The bead's 6 is wrong: 5 of them are path: "live_x_test.go" rows in a fixture TABLE in internal/liverecipes/split_test.go, which a comment reader never sees. Battery M0/M1/M2/M3/M4' all matched declared victims except M1, which SURVIVED as predicted and falsified a comment claim -- the second commit is that correction.

reported 6 unresolved. Five of those are path: "live_x_test.go" rows in a fixture
TABLE in internal/liverecipes/split_test.go -- string literals, not prose. A

#1595 (bd gqlc-chep). Pinned HISTORICAL.

BOTH DESIGN QUESTIONS THE BEAD RAISES WERE ALREADY SETTLED by bd gqlc-som6y,
which I shipped earlier in this session: scope (testcite already reads test
sources and *_test.go.txt fixtures) and the third exemption category (pinned

RESOLUTION IS BY BASE NAME, and that is the design rather than the regex being

tail of a brace expansion nothing can stat. The hole this leaves is stated in the
doc rather than hidden: 36 of this checkout's 150 test files share a base name
with another.

MUTATION BATTERY, victims declared before each run, 5 rows:
  M0  none                                   -> 3 PASS, 74 cited file names, 0 unresolved. MATCHED.
  M1  record present below the parse filter  -> SURVIVED, as predicted.
  M2  drop the pinned lookup                 -> FAIL on exactly the 6 declared sites. MATCHED.
  M3  never set isFile                       -> filename guard hits its own non-degeneracy
                                                fatal AND the name guard fills with filenames. MATCHED.
  M4' `/` in the class + stat resolution     -> 1 -> 3 unresolved. MATCHED.

M1 SURVIVING IS A FINDING I TOOK RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. The comment justifying
that line's placement claimed the two sets are not the same set; they coincide
over everything filenameRe can produce, since every token it matches ends
_test.go or _test.go.txt and the filter admits both. The second commit (cc494e1c
on the branch) is that correction: the line stays where it is for the question it
answers, and the prose now says the difference is not one it currently makes. The
same commit fixed a `/` figure that had been stated without saying what it
counted -- M4' is the re-measurement.

number. It added `/` to the class without changing the resolution set, so it
measured regex/resolver disagreement (18 findings) and not the base-name-versus-
path comparison the prose claims. M4' is the experiment the prose actually
describes.

title: codegen/neo4j: zone-shifting temporal decode mutants survive every UTC runner; pin a non-UTC TZ in corpusrun's child env
description:
Found on sweep gqlc-sojej (2026-09-03 window, sole merge PR #2375 = 7cccf690), by agent-l.

THE CLAIM UNDER TEST. PR #2375 added marks :: LIST<DATE> so TestListyNarrowsEachElement runs the walk's temporal element case through the emitted toDate, and its M3 row showed a Month/Day swap in temporalDecodeBody is KILLED. Both replicate: I re-ran the corpus test twice at 7cccf690 in a git-archive scratch (green both), and the Month/Day swap died on the declared victim exactly (Marks = {Year:2026, Month:29, Day:8}).

THE GAP. A mutant the PR did not declare survives CI structurally, not accidentally. Mutating render_temporal.go:377 `time.Time(v).Date()` -> `time.Time(v).In(time.Local).Date()`:

  - TZ=America/New_York: KILLED — Marks reads {2026,8,28},{1969,12,30}, the UTC-midnight fixture slips a day.
  - TZ=UTC: SURVIVED — 'ok' on the same tree, same command.

Under TZ=UTC, time.Local IS UTC, so the mutant is behaviorally identical to the correct code for EVERY input: no fixture can kill it there, however the dates are chosen. CI pins no TZ anywhere in .github/workflows (grepped 2026-09-03), and GitHub-hosted runners default to UTC, so this mutant class crosses master's whole gate — including, by the same argument, the live Docker suite, whose hydrated values are UTC-located too. Yet in production a user in any non-UTC zone decoding a DATE gets the previous day. A real defect class, invisible to every runner we have.

The same shape reads on the other component-reading helpers (toLocalTime, toTime, toLocalDateTime read Clock() off the value): suspected, not measured.

REMEDY, one line. internal/codegen/corpusrun/corpusrun.go:69 already builds the child env: `cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GOFLAGS=", "GOPROXY=off")`. Append a pinned, DST-less, non-UTC zone — e.g. "TZ=Etc/GMT+5" (UTC-5, no transitions, so fixture instants stay unambiguous year-round) — and the In(time.Local) mutant dies deterministically on every runner. Blast radius: every corpus routed through corpusrun.Run inherits the pin, which is the point — the gap is per-runner, not per-driver. The guard's red witness is the mutation above: apply it, run TestEmittedDecodersRunOnDriverValues, expect the Marks assertion to fail with the day slipped.

Per the guard rule (agent-protocol step 3), whoever takes this must watch it fail: run the corpus test with the TZ pin and the In(time.Local) mutant in place, expect KILLED; then without the pin under TZ=UTC, expect SURVIVED — that pair is what proves the pin is load-bearing.

NOT a scolding of #2375: before it this case had NO runtime witness at all, and its own battery was replicated here row-perfect. This is the residue its witness makes visible.

Also probed, no finding: removing marks from listyProps() reds two tests ("could not find any property named marks"), so the seven fixture-site additions are enforced by the decoder, not cosmetic.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #2405, squash-merged to master; content verified on origin/master
(ChildZone at corpusrun.go:66, the pin at :99, the witness in corpusrun_test.go,
and testmain_test.go present).

WHAT WAS WRONG. corpusrun.Run handed the child `go test` the runner's own zone.
CI runs UTC, so any decoder defect that consists of reading time.Local where UTC
was meant produced identical output on CI and was unobservable there. Measured
before touching anything, mutating render_temporal.go:377 from
`time.Time(v).Date()` to `time.Time(v).In(time.Local).Date()`:
  runner TZ=UTC              -> GREEN (SURVIVED)
  runner TZ=America/New_York -> RED
The suite could only see the bug on a zone CI does not have.

THE FIX, AND THE STEP BEYOND THE BEAD'S ONE-LINE REMEDY. The child env now
carries TZ=Etc/GMT+5 (exported as ChildZone). DST-free, so the offset is a
constant -5h and no row depends on the date the suite runs. Note the POSIX sign
inversion: Etc/GMT+5 is UTC MINUS 5.

The pin ALONE is fail-silent, and I did not leave it that way. Go resolves
time.Local from TZ at startup and falls back to UTC WITHOUT ERROR when the zone
will not load, so on a host with no tzdata the child returns silently to exactly
the state this bead exists to leave. TestRunPinsANonUTCZoneInTheChild therefore
asserts the child's RESOLVED OFFSET, not the requested zone name. This is more
than the bead asked for and the PR body says so plainly.

MUTATION BATTERY. Two arms, both under TZ=UTC (the conditions that hid the
defect). N = neo4j.TestEmittedDecodersRunOnDriverValues, Z = the new witness.
Victim and diffstat declared per row before the run; each declared diffstat
matched what was applied; tree verified clean after every restore.

  B0  no mutation                          1+/1-*  N=GREEN Z=GREEN  control
  M1  .In(time.Local), pin PRESENT         1+/1-   N=RED   Z=GREEN  KILLED
  M1p same mutant, pin REVERTED            2+/2-   N=GREEN Z=RED    SURVIVED
  M2  pin deleted, decoder correct         1+/1-   N=GREEN Z=RED    KILLED by Z

title: no gate forbids adding a default to walkListElemBody's switch, which would retire the only guard on it
description:
Residue from gqlc-7hp5g, filed rather than ridden on the diff.

gqlc-7hp5g measured that the ONLY thing catching an unhandled codegen.ColumnKind
in neo4j's walkListElemBody is golangci-lint's `exhaustive`, and that it works
solely because that switch carries no `default` while .golangci.yml sets
`default-signifies-exhaustive: true`. Adding a `default` there -- a change that
looks like defensive hygiene and would pass every gate -- silently retires the
check forever.

gqlc-7hp5g says so in the doc comment. That is the same kind of load-bearing
prose claim the bead existed to correct: a comment asking a future author not to
do something is not a gate.

SHAPE, and it is a question. An AST pin asserting walkListElemBody's switch has
no `default` is cheap and exact. But the general form is wrong -- a `default` is
CORRECT in a sibling switch: carriesElemBare (render_queries.go) returns false
by default and should, because a new kind that is not bare is the conservative
answer there. Audited 2026-09-03, all six `switch <x>.Kind` sites in
render_queries.go: five carry no default (exhaustive active), one is
carriesElemBare (default legitimate). So a blanket "no ColumnKind switch may
carry a default" pin would red correct code; a pin naming walkListElemBody
alone is exact but is a hardcoded list that a seventh switch will not join.

Whoever takes this decides between the narrow pin and leaving it as prose. Not
urgent: the population is six switches in one file, and the comment now names
the hazard.

Inherited from agent-k, executing gqlc-7hp5g.
notes:
agent-c 2026-09-03, measurement BEFORE choosing. The bead says "the population is
six switches in one file". Measured on HEAD baf28ece, it is wider:

codegen.ColumnKind switches (cases naming codegen.Column*):
  neo4j/render_queries.go:92, :120, :302, :610, :867  -- no default (exhaustive active)
  neo4j/render_queries.go:886  walkListElemBody       -- no default, THE subject
  neo4j/render_queries.go  carriesElemBare            -- default, legitimate
  age/render_queries.go:211  zeroValueText            -- default, legitimate
                             ^ NOT in the bead's audit; the hazard is not one-file.

Same hazard, different sum type -- and a second prose-only claim:
  age/errors.go:700 switch et.Kind (resolver.Scalar) carries a comment reading
  "Exhaustive over resolver.Scalar with no default, so a kind added to that sum
  fails this switch" -- i.e. the identical load-bearing prose gqlc-7hp5g filed
  this bead about, on a different type. age/errors.go:495 is the same shape.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DECISION THIS BEAD POSES. A pin naming walkListElemBody
alone is now clearly under-scoped: it would leave five sibling ColumnKind
switches in the same file, plus one in another package, resting on the same
retirable check. Taking the general shape instead: any switch whose cases name
codegen.Column* must carry no default UNLESS it declares an opt-out, so the two
legitimate defaults say so and a seventh switch joins the rule by existing.
Identified syntactically (cases naming codegen.Column*), so no go/types
dependency is added.

The resolver.Scalar instances are NOT being ridden on this diff; they get their
own bead.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #2420, squash-merged 22ac2fad; GH #2379 auto-closed.

WHAT LANDED. Not the narrow pin this bead offered, and not "leave it as
prose". A third shape, chosen because measurement made the pin
under-scoped: a general declaration rule over every switch whose case
expressions name a ColumnKind constant, anywhere under internal/codegen,
drivers included. internal/codegen/exhaustivedefault_test.go walks the
tree, derives the ColumnKind names from the sources rather than listing
them, and holds three claims:

  - a `default` on such a switch must carry `//gqlc:default-ok <why>` on
    the line above it (TestColumnKindDefaultsDeclareThemselves);
  - a tag over a switch that has no `default` is a stale exemption and
    must be dropped (TestDeclaredDefaultsStillGuardADefault);
  - a tag above anything that is not such a switch is inert, and is
    named rather than ignored (TestStrayDefaultOKTagsAreNotSilent).

Two existing defaults were tagged as legitimately correct:
neo4j/render_queries.go:867 carriesElemBare, and
age/render_queries.go:211 zeroValueText.

WHY NOT THE PIN. The bead's audit named six switches in one file. It was
incomplete: age/render_queries.go:211 is a seventh, outside the audit,
and it is one of the two that legitimately wants a default. A pin naming
walkListElemBody alone would have left it unheld. The rule cannot be "no
ColumnKind switch carries a default", because a conservative default IS
the right answer in both tagged sites -- so the rule is that a default
declares itself and the declaration is checked.

WHAT FALSIFIED ME. I assumed namedGuardedSwitchDirs should list both
neo4j and age, and the fence's own assertion told me otherwise on the
first run. Measured: age has exactly one ColumnKind switch
(zeroValueText), its default is correct, so age has NO
exhaustive-guarded ColumnKind switch to name. Its other reference to the
enum is an `if`, not a switch. Only neo4j is named. That is recorded in
the comment on the variable so the next reader does not repeat my guess.
A driver added later is still held by the rule without being listed.

MUTATION BATTERY. 6 rows, each with the expected victim and diffstat
declared before the run, tree restored and checksum-verified after each.
All 6 KILLED. Screened with `go test -c` so a compiler kill could not be
mistaken for a suite kill. The guard was committed (6e9d5106) before any
mutation, so a per-row restore could not delete it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER. age/errors.go:495 and :700 rest on the same
retirable exhaustive check, but on resolver.Scalar rather than
ColumnKind, and :700 states the hazard in prose only -- the exact shape
this bead exists to retire. Not ridden on this diff. Filed as
gqlc-f5onb, whose suggested shape is to widen this fence rather than
write a second one.

CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT. `just test-codegen-fence` is the
module-scope fence and reads no //gqlc:default-ok or //gqlc:unreachable
tag at all; the two were conflated. The line numbers in the description

description:

2026-09-03 09:20Z, agent-d: NOT claimed — the design gate in this bead is respected.

2026-09-04, agent-m — RULING, asked by agent-c 2026-09-03 (also answering the gate agent-k set in this bead's body):

The sentences at :119-120 and :513-515 are factual claims about the tree, and

title: codegen/neo4j: toDuration's decode direction is emitted by the corpus and run by nothing
description:
Split out of bd gqlc-abf6t (2026-09-02), which put a decoded LIST<DATE> on Listy and so gave writeSliceNarrow's temporal element case its first executed witness.

The walk's temporal case is ONE case whichever carrier reaches it, so gqlc-abf6t's claim is discharged by the one property. What the choice of carrier leaves standing is the HELPER: the to<X> bodies are emitted per carrier (temporalDecodeBody, render_temporal.go), and the corpus schema's own note says a helper shown to work for one carrier has not been run for another.

Slot.spans (LIST<DURATION(DAY TO SECOND)>) is an entity field, so temporalUses marks Duration decode=true and toDuration IS emitted into the corpus module — it is simply never called, because nothing projects Slot. Measured the same way marks was: the corpus compiles it and no test reaches it.

STATE AFTER gqlc-abf6t, per carrier, for the DECODE direction:
  - Date          executed, by Listy.marks in TestListyNarrowsEachElement
  - Duration      emitted into the corpus, called by nothing
  - LocalTime, Time, LocalDateTime   not emitted by this corpus at all

The live neo4j suite does round-trip scalar Date, LocalTime and Duration (live_neo4j_test.go), so this is a Docker-free-witness gap rather than a total one. Every other in-tree call site is a golden, which compares text.

REMEDY, smallest first: a decoded LIST<DURATION> or a scalar DURATION property on a node type the corpus already projects, asserted the way marks is. Note the cost side: Listy's props are supplied at seven call sites in corpus_test.go.txt, so a NOT NULL addition touches all of them.

Filed rather than ridden on gqlc-abf6t's diff, which was scoped to the walk's element case.
