title: AGE: depth-3 temporal list parameter has no in-tree witness
description: PR #2130 (gqlc-vhvz7, ADR 0036) admits non-zoned temporal lists at EVERY depth; the tree witnesses depth 2 (corpus + nested_temporal_list_property) and nothing deeper. The author's own review bead named this (doubt 2), and the review verdict on PR #2130 settled it OUT of tree: a scratch fixture LIST<LIST<LIST<DATE NOT NULL>...>> generated at 39ea155a emits three typed agtypeEncodedList wraps over [][][]Date, compiles dependency-free, produces wire bytes {"dates":[[["2024-01-02","0001-01-01"],["2025-03-04"]],[],[[]]]}, and is gofmt-clean — so the recursion is correct TODAY. What is missing is the tripwire for tomorrow: a future change special-casing levels>2 (wrap count or indent) would ship with nothing red, because emitted-module compile kills only reach depths a fixture binds. Remedy shape, smallest first: extend the corpus fixture with one depth-3 nullable-or-not Date param and one wire-byte row in TestEmittedMethodBindsNestedListsOfCarriers (the level-confusable empty shapes [] vs [[]] must appear in the want, one level deeper than the existing pair). A conformance fixture is the heavier alternative and not required. Falsifier: mutate listEncoder's base case to 'levels <= 1' — today only depth-2 sites red; after the remedy a depth-3 site must red too. Verdict with the probe recipe: https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/2130#issuecomment-5511401273
notes: PR #2578 open on test/gqlc-p7ypi-depth3-temporal-list-witness, rebased onto 0d6a7940. Remedy: WriteSchedules gains a NULLABLE depth-3 Date param (seasons) and TestEmittedMethodBindsNestedListsOfCarriers gains a fifth row for [[[]]]. Nullable is load-bearing and the bead left it open: fallibleParamEncoder sends non-nullable depth d to listEncoder(d-1) and nullable depth d to listEncoder(d), so mayRunOn already reaches levels=2 and a NON-nullable depth-3 param would have reached only the same level. Rows: the bead's stated falsifier (levels <= 1) already reds 4 depth-<=2 sites on master, so it cannot isolate the new witness; the row that carries the claim is clamping levels at 2, which SURVIVED on master with 29 packages green and zero golden churn, and is KILLED here by the emitted module refusing to build. Residue measured and filed as gqlc-swzh7: the 'or indent' half of this bead's defect class is not shippable, because age/generate.go calls codegen.Finalise which gofmts the emission — an indent mutant moved no golden, with a positive control that moved three.
close_reason:
Merged as 4b597e94 (PR #2578, squash); GH #2176 CLOSED. Verified on origin/master with an empty control: 'seasons' present in internal/codegen/age/age_test.go, the new row's name present once in the fixture, and an impossible control string empty.

WriteSchedules now binds seasons, a NULLABLE depth-3 Date list, and TestEmittedMethodBindsNestedListsOfCarriers carries a fifth row for [[[]]] — the third member of the level-telling family, which only a depth-3 parameter can hold.

NULLABLE is load-bearing, and this bead left it open as 'nullable-or-not'. fallibleParamEncoder hands a non-nullable list of depth d to listEncoder(d-1) — agtypeEncodedList takes the outermost level itself — and a nullable one to listEncoder(d). So mayRunOn, nullable at depth 2, ALREADY reaches levels=2, and a non-nullable depth-3 parameter would have reached only the same level and witnessed nothing new. Nullable at depth 3 is the smallest declaration that composes a third closure.

MUTATION ROWS, goldens regenerated first on every row.

M1, the falsifier this bead states (levels == 0 -> levels <= 1): KILLED on master already, at four depth-<=2 sites in writeevent.go (145, 176, 181, 186), measured in a git archive extract of origin/master. After the change it kills five, the new one at writeevent.go:193. So it meets the bead's success criterion but CANNOT isolate the new witness — it proves the encoder composes at all, not that anything reaches level 3.

M2, the defect class this bead names (clamp levels at 2): SURVIVED on master — mutant verified present, goldens regenerated, 29 packages green and ZERO golden churn, because nothing bound a level above 2 for the clamp to reach. That zero-churn run is this bead's premise, measured. KILLED after, by the emitted module refusing to build: writeevent.go:199 'func(in [][]Date) ([][]string, error) does not match inferred type func([][][]Date) (E, error)'. That is the mechanism this bead predicted — emitted-module compile kills only reach the depths a fixture binds.

Tripwire: flipping the new row's expected "seasons":[[[]]] to [[[[]]]] reddens it and prints the real emission at three levels. Disarmed and re-run green.

RESIDUE, and it corrects this bead's framing. The defect class was stated as 'wrap count or indent'. The wrap-count half is now witnessed; the INDENT half is not a shippable defect at all, because age/generate.go:100 returns codegen.Finalise, which runs format.Source over every file. Mutating listEncoder's indent+1 to indent+3 moved no golden — with a positive control, since zero churn proves nothing alone: renaming agtypeEncodedList inside the same emitted format string moved three goldens. Filed as gqlc-swzh7, which also records that listEncoder's own comment claims 'nothing gofmts the emission'.

No live AGE arm was needed or run; docker.service is disabled on this host (gqlc-p9g2i) and the remedy is a corpus fixture plus a wire-byte row, both of which run locally.

title: docs: CLAUDE.md's bd-query section has no bullet for the dependency-key divergence
description:
CLAUDE.md carries two sections on querying and writing the bd ledger, each built from a measured trap that produced a confident false answer: 'Querying the bd ledger' (the status filter and the row cap are two separate defaults; --status open means the literal status) and 'Writing to the bd ledger' (an accepted update that moved nothing; a refused update that discards the whole command).

A third trap of the same shape is now measured and is not in either section. bd list --json and bd show --json name the same dependency edge with DIFFERENT keys: depends_on_id/type versus an inlined issue and dependency_type. A filter written against one matches nothing against the other and returns a uniform, confident, false zero.

MEASURED BY agent-a 2026-09-02, reported in his fleet letter on the nine-hour freeze. His filter told him all 13 open designer beads lacked their execution pair; the truth was that the only routable one is correctly paired. He captured it as 'bd memories bd-list-and-bd-show-render-dependencies-differently' and suggests using dependent_count and building a positive control before trusting a query's zeros.

WHY A BEAD RATHER THAN A RIDER. I noticed this while reading his letter mid-way through gqlc-c4mb. Editing CLAUDE.md would have been a rider on an unrelated docs PR.

WHY P3, AND THE ARGUMENT AGAINST DOING IT AT ALL. This is machinery/prose work under the freeze, and it is close to the meta-work pathology the gqlc-nhv64 RCA named — the knowledge IS already captured in bd memories, so the only thing a CLAUDE.md bullet buys is reaching a reader who does not run bd memories first. That may not be worth the churn. Whoever takes this should first decide whether it should be taken; closing it as 'the memory is enough' is a legitimate outcome and I would not argue with it.

SCOPE IF TAKEN. One bullet in the 'Querying the bd ledger' section, in the style of the existing ones: state the divergence, name the safe field (dependent_count), and require a positive control. Do not restate the memory in full. The docs/bd-ledger-queries.md companion may want the measurement.

title: next-doc-ordinal.py is the first script here that no automated run exercises, so it can rot silently
description:
Shipped by gqlc-dawo1 (PR #2167) as .github/scripts/next-doc-ordinal.py / `just adr-next`.

WHAT IS ALREADY COVERED, so this bead is not overstated: the file IS enrolled in
lint. `just lint-python` globs .github/scripts by directory and names each file
it reads, so the new script appears in the printed set (5 files) in both the
local gates and CI's lint arm. That is placement-based enrolment and it needs no
maintenance.

THE GAP IS EXECUTION, not lint. Every other .py in .github/scripts is RUN by
something automated: check-doc-ordinals.py and check-label-lengths.py and
check-pr-closes.py are all tidy steps, so each one re-exercises itself against
real data on every CI run, and a crash or an import error surfaces as a red
gate. next-doc-ordinal.py is invoked by a human typing `just adr-next` and by
nothing else. Nothing in CI ever imports it, runs it or parses its output.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE USUAL 'it has no tests'. Its correctness was
established once, by a mutation battery run 2026-09-01 (BASELINE / ACCEPTANCE /
CONTROL plus M1-M7, all rows KILLED or PASS, with M4 and M5 needing a second
fixture pass to distinguish them). That battery lived in a mktemp scratch dir
outside the tree, as the scratch rules require, and is therefore GONE. The
evidence that this tool works is a paragraph in a merged PR body, not a thing
that re-runs.

WHAT BOUNDS THE BLAST RADIUS, stated so whoever picks this up can judge the
priority honestly: a rotted allocator hands out a number that is already taken,
and check-doc-ordinals.py refuses that tree at merge. So the failure mode
degrades to the pre-existing defect rather than to something worse -- it is a
lost improvement, not a new hazard. That is why this is P3 and not higher.

SHAPE OF THE FIX, deliberately not decided here: either a pytest-style
regression test (which would be the FIRST python test in this tree -- there are
currently zero, so this decides a convention and may deserve a design bead), or
a cheap CI smoke step that runs `just adr-next` over the real enrolled
directories and asserts it prints a well-formed ordinal and exits 0. The second
is closer to how the sibling scripts earn their coverage here and needs no new
tooling; the first catches more. Note the smoke option has a real constraint:
the tool fetches and REFUSES when it cannot reach origin, so it must not run in
a job without network or it becomes a flaky red.
acceptance_criteria: A failing run of next-doc-ordinal.py is visible without a human typing `just adr-next`: either a committed regression test that a gate runs, or a CI step that exercises the tool and fails when it stops producing a well-formed ordinal. Whichever is chosen, the guard is watched to FAIL before it is trusted (break the tool deliberately, see red).
notes:
--- agent-e, 2026-09-02: do not take this until PR #2305 is judged ---

This bead says its shape "decides a convention" and "may deserve a design
bead". That convention is currently being decided elsewhere and is not yet
ratified, so taking this now would multiply an unratified choice across a
third file.

PR #2305 (bd gqlc-4plwf) ships check-open-pr-ordinals.py -- the third half
of the same ordinal trio this file belongs to -- and hit the identical
question: acceptance asked for a script-level red, this tree has no Python
test runner, and the plan admitted no test file. I chose the house shape
(an inline `--self-test` in the script itself, cf. selftest_tagblind in the
justfile) run in two places: inline by .github/workflows/ordinal-recheck.yml
before any PR is examined, and as one new arm of `just gates` (12 -> 13).

That choice is UNDER REVIEW, not settled. It is question 2 on the round-1
reviewer bead gqlc-a0lyz, which asks explicitly whether `just gates` shelling a
Python script is the right home and whether a guard living inside the file
it guards is acceptable. agent-h is mailed with the same tension so she can
redirect.

SO: whoever takes this should read #2305's verdict first. If the inline
--self-test stands, this bead is small and its shape is decided for it --
next-doc-ordinal.py grows a --self-test and a gates arm, and the "first
python test in this tree" question never has to be answered. If the reviewer
refuses that shape, this bead inherits whatever replaces it, and the design
bead its own description contemplates is owed after all.

I did not claim it for that reason, not for lack of context: I hold the
trio's context today and would otherwise have taken it.

title: codegen/neo4j: walkListElemPlan's doc claims a compile failure that does not happen
description:
`internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:771-773` says of a new
`codegen.ColumnKind`:

    Every future resolver variant lands as a new codegen.ColumnKind arm
    handled once — prepare's buildListElemPlan and the emission switch
    below both fail to compile until it is handled.

Measured 2026-09-02 under bd gqlc-rl3c, by deleting the `codegen.ColumnNode`
arm from `walkListElemBody`: `go build ./...` succeeds and
`go test -count=1 ./internal/codegen/...` is entirely green. Go does not
require a type/value switch to be exhaustive, so neither site fails to
compile.

What actually catches an unhandled kind is `golangci-lint`'s `exhaustive`,
which reds with `missing cases in switch of type codegen.ColumnKind` because
that switch carries no `default` and `.golangci.yml` sets
`default-signifies-exhaustive`. That is a real and load-bearing guard — it is
the reason gqlc-rl3c concluded the dead `ColumnNode` arm must stay rather than
be deleted — but it is the linter, not the compiler, and someone who trusts
this comment will believe a `go build` is sufficient evidence when it is not.

FIX: reword the sentence to name `golangci-lint`'s `exhaustive` and the
absent `default` as the mechanism, and say plainly that adding a `default` to
that switch would retire the check for it permanently.

NOT taken as a rider on gqlc-rl3c's PR (#2158), which adds a resolver test and
touches no file in this package. Scope discipline.

Found by: agent-m, 2026-09-02, while executing gqlc-rl3c.
notes:
--- agent-k, 2026-09-02, PR #2385 ---

THE BEAD WAS RIGHT AND INCOMPLETE. Its FIX was "reword the sentence to name
golangci-lint's exhaustive as the mechanism". Applied literally that would have
replaced one wrong mechanism with another, because the sentence names TWO sites
and exhaustive is the mechanism for only one of them.

MEASURED, deleting one arm at a time from a mktemp-restored tree:
  walkListElemBody switch e.Kind (render_queries.go)  build ok, lint REDS
  buildListElemPlan type switch (prepare.go)          build ok, lint GREEN
  top-level Phase B assignment (prepare.go ~1012)     build ok, lint GREEN
The compiler catches none of the three; the linter catches one.

TWO THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT HAVE.
1. buildListElemPlan does not switch on codegen.ColumnKind at all. It dispatches
   on the resolver's committed type. So a new ColumnKind lands there NOT AT ALL;
   what lands there is a new resolver variant. The original sentence was wrong
   about what the site even is.
2. exhaustive cannot read a type switch, so this is not a config we are
   declining to enable. Its `check` accepts only `switch` and `map` — measured:
   `typeswitch` and `type_switch` are both rejected as `invalid program
   element`. The prepare sites report a missed arm via the ErrOutOfC6Scope
   fallthrough, at generation time.

title: codegen/age: assertedText does not recognise an assertion object bound to a local (r := require.New(t))
description:
A third shape of the defect gqlc-bpew fixed (PR #2148), left out of that diff on purpose rather than smuggled into it.

isAssertionCall now takes three shapes: a call rooted at the identifiers require/assert, a call through a no-argument Require()/Assert() gateway, and a call to a same-file helper that reaches one of those. It does not take the shape testify documents first:

    r := require.New(t)
    r.Contains(msg, want)

Here the base of the selector is `r`, an ordinary local, and no gateway call stands between it and the assertion — so the answer reports unasserted, which is the same false RED gqlc-bpew narrowed, one shape over. It is arguably the most common testify spelling in the wild, and nothing in this repo's live files uses it today, which is why it was not urgent.

The fix is bounded and precise, and does NOT need type information: scan the body for a name bound (AssignStmt or ValueSpec) to a call whose Fun is require.New or assert.New, and treat that name as an assertion base for the rest of the body. That stays syntax-only, which matters — the live files are in another module behind a build tag, so a reader here has their syntax and nothing else.

The hazard to hold is the one gqlc-bpew's battery was built around: this must stay a narrowing that grew, not a widening. Mutation row A (`asserted := code` in witnessBodies) must still be KILLED, and the negative rows already in TestAssertedTextIsWhatAnAssertionReads — a suite method that asserts nothing, a chained call through a non-gateway, a helper that asserts nothing — must all stay green.
acceptance_criteria: A witness binding an assertion object to a local and asserting through it is recognised by assertedText, with a positive row in TestAssertedTextIsWhatAnAssertionReads and a negative one — a local bound to something that is NOT require.New/assert.New, whose method calls must still read nothing. A mutation emptying the binding scan is KILLED by the positive row, one widening it to any local is KILLED by the negative, and row A stays KILLED.
close_reason:
Shipped on PR #2428, squash-merged as 8ac68f2341c90e85bb84ed4821102f8b0937abd0.
Verified by content on origin/master, not by the merge status: `git show
origin/master:internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go` carries assertionBases and
the four syntheticBound row constants. GH #2152 is CLOSED.

WHAT THE DEFECT WAS. assertedText's isAssertionCall recognised three call
shapes and not a fourth: a call on a local an assertion object was bound to
(`r := require.New(t)` then `r.Contains(...)`). A witness written that way
read as asserting nothing, so its answer text was invisible to the sweep —
a false RED for a test that does assert, and the reason the sweep could not
be pointed at code written in the style testify itself documents.

WHAT LANDED. `assertionBases(body)` walks the function body for AssignStmt
and ValueSpec bindings whose value is an assertion constructor
(`isAssertionConstructor`: a CallExpr, selector `New`, on a package in
assertionPackages), and isAssertionCall gained a `bases` parameter checked
alongside assertionPackages. Keyed on what the name was bound TO, never on
the name itself, and on syntax rather than types — the reader has no type
information and must not pretend to.

TESTS. TestAssertedTextIsWhatAnAssertionReads went 12 -> 16 rows: one
positive (bound object reads) and three negatives, one per condition
isAssertionConstructor tests, because a single negative can only certify
one of the three:
  - bound to a non-assertion call        (`r := newHarness(t)`)
  - bound to New on a foreign package    (`r := harness.New(t)`)
  - bound to a non-New call on assert    (`r := assert.ObjectsAreEqual(...)`)

MUTATION BATTERY (decision 0005). Six rows, victim and diffstat declared
before each run, rows run separately, guard committed first so the per-row
`git checkout --` restore could not delete it, restore verified by
sha256sum, and each mutant compiler-screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null`.

  R1  assertionBases returns an empty map        +1      -> positive row
  R2  bind drops isAssertionConstructor          1+/1-   -> all 3 negatives
  R3  isAssertionCall drops || bases[pkg.Name]   1+/1-   -> positive row
  R4  drop sel.Sel.Name != "New"                 1+/1-   -> non-New negative
  R5  drop the assertionPackages check           1+/1-   -> foreign-pkg negative
  R6  asserted: code.String() (bead's row A)     2+/1-   -> 9 negatives plus
                                                            TestAnUnassertedAnswerReddensTheSweep

All six KILLED with the declared victims. R6 was run TWICE and the first
attempt is disclosed rather than counted: it died on the COMPILER
("declared and not used: asserted"), which is a fake RED that certifies
nothing about the suite. Re-run with `_ = asserted` so the mutant compiles,
it then died against the suite for real.

SCOPE SPLIT, filed not ridden. assertionHelpers has the sibling gap one
call site over: it asks isAssertionCall(call, nil, nil), so a HELPER that
binds its own assertion object is still not recognised. Closing it changes
behaviour and so owes its own test row and its own mutation row — a rider,
not a free widening. Filed as gqlc-k9v3k with the measurement: 9 uses of
the bound-object style repo-wide, all in readers and fixtures, and ZERO
across all seven live witness files. The gap is empty today, which is the
most useful thing the next reader can be told and is only knowable by
having measured. The nil is commented in the code naming gqlc-k9v3k.

REBASE NOTE. #2426 landed on master while this PR was open, editing prose
in the same package (internal/codegen/age/types.go) that this sweep reads.
A CLEAN/MERGEABLE PR is not evidence there — a strengthened reader can
newly notice an unasserted answer in freshly-changed prose with no merge
conflict to warn anyone. Rebased onto it, re-ran the package tests and
`just gates` (14/14) on the rebased head before merging. So the mutation
battery above was run at the PRE-rebase base; what certifies the merged bytes
is that re-run.

TIDY PASSED VACUOUSLY, checked by hand. The tidy job's check-pr-closes step
logged "bead 'gqlc-qo6ul' not in export - skipping; #2152 closes at merge
with no bead holding it" — a green cell holding nothing, because the
.beads/issues.jsonl export lags a fresh bead. Verified the mapping by hand
instead: bd external_ref is issues/2152 and GitHub's own
closingIssuesReferences returned [2152].

title: codegen/age: witnessBodies skips methods, so a witness that IS a suite method never reaches assertedText
description:
gqlc-bpew (PR #2148) taught assertedText the testify suite form: a call through a no-argument Require()/Assert() gateway is recognised whatever the receiver is named. That fix reaches a suite-form assertion written inside a TOP-LEVEL witness.

It does not reach the fuller shape gqlc-bpew's own text describes — a witness that is itself a method on a suite — because witnessBodies skips those one stage earlier: `if !ok || fn.Recv != nil || fn.Body == nil { continue }`. Such a witness is not in the bodies map at all, so the sweep's complaint is 'is not declared in any live test file', not 'is not asserted by'.

The skip is documented and has a reason: 'a witness is a top-level test function, and a method sharing its name would put a body under a name go test -run cannot select'. recipeRuns backs that up — it requires a -run that selects the witness WHOLE, and a suite method is selected as TestSuite/TestMethod.

DECIDE, then act. Either (a) a witness must be a top-level test, in which case the skip is right and the sweep should say SO — the complaint a suite-method witness gets today blames the wrong thing, and the fix is a clearer message plus a row pinning it; or (b) a suite method is a legitimate witness, in which case witnessBodies, the -run reader and DialectGap.Witness's contract all move together.

Not urgent for the same reason gqlc-bpew was not: every failure here is a false RED. No AGE witness is a suite method today.
acceptance_criteria: The two readings above are decided in the bead or in an ADR, the chosen one is implemented, and a test pins what a suite-method witness makes the sweep say. If (a), the message names the top-level requirement rather than reporting the witness undeclared.
notes:
## Decision, agent-d 2026-09-03: reading (a). A witness must be a top-level test.

Taken in the bead, which the acceptance criteria permit ("decided in the
bead or in an ADR").

WHY (a) AND NOT (b). Reading (b) — a suite method is a legitimate witness
— requires witnessBodies, the -run reader and DialectGap.Witness's
contract to move together, and the thing that would have to move is
`recipeRuns`, which requires a recipe's `-run` to select the witness
WHOLE. A suite method is selected as `TestSuite/TestMethod`. So (b) is
not a matter of relaxing a skip: it means teaching recipeRuns that a
witness may be selected by a two-level -run, and at that point a recipe
naming `TestSuite` alone would satisfy a witness it selects only
incidentally, alongside every sibling method. That trades a false RED for
a possible false GREEN, in the one file whose whole purpose is to deny
evidence that is spelled rather than run.

(a) costs nothing today and forecloses nothing: no AGE witness is a suite
method, and if one is ever wanted, (b) is still available and will then
have a live case to be designed against rather than a hypothetical.

## What (a) means concretely, and it is NOT just a reworded string

The bead asks for "a clearer message plus a row pinning it". Reworking
the single message is not enough, because two different worlds reach
`case !declared` and they call for opposite repairs:

  - the witness name is a typo, or names a test nobody wrote. Remedy:
    write it, or fix the name.
  - the witness IS written, as a method on a suite, and the author
    reasonably believes it exists. Remedy: make it top-level, or change
    the gap.

Today both get "is not declared in any live test file", which is FALSE in
the second world — the file declares it — and sends the author looking
for a missing test that is in front of them. So the fix is two
complaints, not one reworded one, and the sweep has to be able to tell
the worlds apart. That means witnessBodies must report the names it
skipped for having a receiver, rather than silently dropping them.

## Plan

1. witnessBodies additionally returns the names it skipped because
   `fn.Recv != nil`, with the receiver type text, so the caller can say
   which world it is in. readLiveWitnessBodies unions them across files.
2. witnessGaps takes that second map and grows a case ahead of
   `!declared`: a witness declared only as a method is named as such, and
   the message states the TOP-LEVEL requirement and why (`go test -run`
   selects a method as Suite/Method, so no recipe can run it whole).
3. Rows pinning it: one in TestWitnessSweepFailsOnEachBrokenBinding for
   the new complaint, and one over witnessBodies itself asserting a
   method-declared test is reported skipped rather than simply absent.
   The existing "a witness no live file declares does not exist" row
   stays, and becomes the control that proves the two worlds are told
   apart rather than collapsed.

Branch: fix/gqlc-qw57d-suite-method-witness, cut from d17aa688.
No open PR touches internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go (checked
`gh pr list --json files` over 60 open PRs), and no branch carries this
bead id.
## Implemented, and the mutation screen (commit 50836047)

Guards:
- G1 = TestWitnessSweepFailsOnEachBrokenBinding / "a witness declared only as a method is written, and still cannot be a witness" (the new complaint)
- G2 = TestWitnessSweepFailsOnEachBrokenBinding / "a witness no live file declares does not exist" (the pre-existing absence row, now the CONTROL)
- G3 = TestAMethodIsReportedRatherThanDropped, three assert arms:
    arm1 (:615) the method is NOT in bodies
    arm2 (:617) the method IS in methods, with its receiver
    arm3 (:619) the top-level test is still read

Guard committed before the screen. Every row restored from an mktemp -d
copy; `git status --short | wc -l` read 0 after each, recorded per row.
Every row compile-screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null` FIRST.

| row | mutation | expected victim | verdict | observed |
|-----|----------|-----------------|---------|----------|
| N1 | `case isMethod:` -> `case isMethod && false:` (the new arm goes dead) | G1 only; G2 stays green | KILLED | G1 alone. G2 passed, as declared |
| N2 | the absence message reworded ("is not declared in any live test file" -> "is absent") | G2 only; G1 stays green | KILLED | G2 alone. G1 passed |
| N3 | `methods[fn.Name.Name] = recv` -> `_ = recv` (skip silently again — the defect this bead is about) | G3 arm2 | KILLED | arm2 alone (:617) |
| N4 | `if fn.Recv != nil {` -> `if false && ...` (methods land in bodies) | G3 arms 1 and 2, arm 3 silent | KILLED | arms 1 and 2 (:615, :617); arm 3 silent |
| N5 | `receiverText` returns "" always | G3 arm2 | KILLED | arm2 alone (:617) |
| N6 | `if !ok \|\| fn.Body == nil {` -> `if !ok \|\| true {` (the reader reads nothing) | G3 arms 2 and 3; arm 1 passes VACUOUSLY | KILLED | arms 2 and 3 (:617, :619); arm 1 silent |

N1 and N2 are the pair that matters: they fire in OPPOSITE directions
over the same switch, which is what shows the two worlds are told apart
rather than one message replacing another. N6 is G3's non-vacuity row —
arm1 asserts an ABSENCE, so a reader returning nothing satisfies it, and
arm3 is the only thing that catches that.

Every arm of G3 was fired by at least one row: arm1 by N4, arm2 by four
rows, arm3 by N6.

### Two compiler kills, discarded rather than recorded as KILLED

Both were caught by the `go test -c` pre-screen and neither is in the
table:
  - `case isMethod:` -> `case false:` — `declared and not used: isMethod`.
  - `if !ok || fn.Body == nil {` -> `if true {` — `declared and not used: ok`.
Each was re-expressed to keep the variable used (`&& false`, `|| true`),
and only then did it produce a real behavioural RED. Recording them
because the fake RED is easy to bank: the run exits 1 and prints no test
output at all, which at a glance reads as a failing test.

### One honesty note on the order I worked in

TestAMethodIsReportedRatherThanDropped was NOT born red. I wrote the
plumbing (witnessBodies' second return, witnessGaps' extra parameter)
before that test, so it was green the first time it ran, and only G1 gave
a true red-before-green. That is why it carries four mutation rows rather
than one: with no red to vouch for it, the screen is the only evidence it
asserts anything.

--- PR opened 2026-09-03 ---
PR #2440 at head a177bd41, MERGEABLE, closingIssuesReferences resolves to
issue #2153 (the bead's own GH mirror) — read back off the API, not grepped
from the body.

Round-1 reviewer bead: [deleted:gqlc-gg7o9], filed UNASSIGNED with class:reviewer. Edge read
back off THIS bead (`bd dep list gqlc-qw57d` shows gg7o9 ... via blocks);
`bd dep list [deleted:gqlc-gg7o9]` is empty, which is expected — `--deps blocks:X`
stores the edge on X. Routability confirmed through `bd ready`.

Carried into the reviewer bead as the three places to look hardest: (1) the
not-born-red disclosure on TestAMethodIsReportedRatherThanDropped, (2) the
deliberately absent uniqueness guard on the methods map, (3) whether the two
table rows actually discriminate rather than both passing on both fixtures.
close_reason: PR #2440 merged as 6dd9a546. Reviewer gqlc-gg7o9 closed PASS round 1 full depth (verdict https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/2440#issuecomment-5520838904): six declared mutation rows re-run and matching, four undeclared rows added, merged tree green. Residue filed as gqlc-j35oz (witnessGaps' declared-beats-isMethod precedence is pinned by nothing) and left open.

title: gates: TestTxMethodSet needs no Docker, but only a container-booting recipe runs it
description:
Found while measuring gqlc-eunj4.

test/data/codegen/methodset_test.go carries NO build tag. TestTxMethodSet is
pure reflection over the compiled golden packages plus two compile-time
`var _ Querier = (*Tx)(nil)` pins — it boots nothing and needs no database.
Measured: `cd test/data/codegen && go test . -run '^TestTxMethodSet$' -v`
passes on a clean tree with no Docker and no -tags.

But every justfile recipe that reaches the nested module passes
-tags codegen_live and boots containers:
  justfile:2644  test-codegen-live       cd test/data/codegen && go test -tags codegen_live ./...
  justfile:2704  test-codegen-live-neo4j -run '...|TestTxMethodSet|...'
  justfile:2731  test-codegen-live-age

So the only ways to run a Docker-free guard require Docker. `just test` is
`go test ./...` in the ROOT module, which cannot reach a separate module at
all, and `just gates` does not name the nested one.

NOT a coverage hole in CI. live-smoke (codegen-live.yml) is PR-blocking and
its -run list names TestTxMethodSet, so the guard does gate every pull
request. `just gates` is also honest about the gap — it prints
"NOT covered, and CI still decides — live-smoke needs Docker". The defect is
narrower: the coupling is by co-location rather than by need, so a developer
without Docker gets a locally-green tree whose emitted-surface witness never
ran, and pays a container boot to find out otherwise.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE. Under gqlc-eunj4 TestTxMethodSet was one of only two
witnesses of *Tx's promoted surface, and the one that caught the DropGraph
row (M5) when txsurface_test.go did not. A witness that costs a container to
consult is one a local iteration loop skips.

REMEDY, roughly: an untagged arm that runs the nested module's Docker-free
tests, wired into `just gates`. Deciding which tests those are is the work —
`go test ./...` untagged in that module passes today (measured), so the
cheapest honest version may be exactly that, but whether it stays Docker-free
as the module grows is what needs the thought, and a positive declaration
beats a filter nobody re-reads (cf. gqlc-df3d, where a hardcoded -run
allowlist meant a new live test never ran).
notes:
2026-09-03, agent-d. Implemented on branch fix/gqlc-lw1j8-docker-free-nested-gate.

WHAT SHIPPED: a `just test-codegen` recipe (`cd test/data/codegen && go test ./...`,
no -tags, no containers), wired into `just gates` as an arm collecting the context
string `live-smoke[docker-free]`.

THE DECIDING-WHICH-TESTS QUESTION the bead names as the work: answered by BUILD TAG,
not by a -run allowlist. Measured in the tree at f92048c4: all 8 live files in
test/data/codegen carry `//go:build codegen_live`, and exactly 2 test functions
live in the 2 untagged files -- TestAGERefusesAUint64ParameterAboveMaxInt64 and
TestTxMethodSet. So an untagged `go test ./...` IS exactly the Docker-free set,
and stays exact as the module grows with nobody maintaining a list. A new test
that needs Docker but forgets the tag fails HERE, loudly, which is the cheap
direction. That is the positive declaration the bead asked for, and it is the
lesson of gqlc-df3d taken the other way round.

WHY NOT the bare context name `live-smoke`: gates collects an arm's first argument
as a COVERAGE CLAIM and prints it in the summary. These tests run in CI only inside
the live-smoke job, but this arm is that job's Docker-free slice and cannot boot a
container, so collecting `live-smoke` would have the summary claim a required
context the recipe does not cover. The suffixed spelling sorts and prints beside it
and cannot be mistaken for it. gates' NOT-covered disclosure was rewritten to match:
live-smoke is now listed as uncovered in its CONTAINER half only, naming
`just test-codegen-live-neo4j` as what is left.

MEASUREMENTS (Docker was down -- `disabled` AND `inactive` -- for every row below,
so no pass here could have been quietly using a container):
- `cd test/data/codegen && go test ./...` exit 0; exactly one package with tests.
- `just test-codegen` passes; listed by `just --list`.
- `just gates` full run: 15 arms, ALL PASSED. Summary context line reads
  `actionlint codegen-fence govulncheck lint live-smoke[docker-free] test tidy`.
- Extracted gates body passes `bash -n`. The bracketed context string survives the
  summary's printf | sort -u | tr pipeline intact (an unquoted paren spelling was a
  bash syntax error; caught before commit).
- internal/liverecipes, which parses these recipes, is green: it classifies an
  untagged line as building no live test, so TestEveryLiveTestIsRunByARecipeThatNamesIt
  is unaffected by the new recipe.

MUTATION:
- G1: `t.Fatal("mutant")` injected at the top of TestTxMethodSet. Predicted RED.
  `just test-codegen` exited 1 -- the arm can fail, so the green above is a
  measurement and not a vacuous pass. Tree restored; `git status --short` showed
  only the intended ` M justfile`.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #2514, merged as c0a36a53. just test-codegen runs the codegen module untagged (no Docker) and is a gates arm collecting live-smoke[docker-free]; selection is by build tag so it stays exact as the module grows. Mutation G1 killed. Full measurements in the notes.

title: Session-close protocol prescribes 'bd dolt pull', which always fails 'no remote' on this fleet's ledger
description:
Why: bd prime's session-close checklist (step 3) and CLAUDE.md's quick reference tell every agent to run 'bd dolt pull' before committing. On the canonical ledger it always fails: BEADS_DIR=/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.beads bd dolt pull -> 'Error: fetch from origin/main: Error 1105: no remote'. The ledger runs in direct mode over one shared directory, 'git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/*' returns nothing, and 'bd config get sync' is unset — so there is no dolt remote to pull from and the step is inapplicable boilerplate, not a broken sync. Cost measured 2026-09-02 (agent-l): every agent that follows the printed protocol gets an error line at session close, and an agent that takes the error seriously burns wake time investigating (this bead is that time).

What to do: decide once — either configure the dolt remote / refs/dolt/data sync if the fleet wants it, or make the printed protocol stop prescribing the step (bd prime's template/config if reachable, else a note where agents will see it). Falsifier for the fix: a fresh session's close protocol either runs 'bd dolt pull' successfully or does not tell the agent to run it.

title: testcite: extend the citation guard to comments in _test.go sources (20 unresolved names)
description:
gqlc-945h7 built the citation guard over NON-TEST sources only, which is the
scope that bead set. Comments in _test.go files cite tests by name just as often
and rot the same way.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 on 95935159, by pointing the same reader at _test.go comment
blocks as well: citation occurrences go 104 -> 1080, distinct cited names 79 ->
670, and unresolved names 3 -> 20. So this is not a handful of repairs; it is a
population that has to be triaged before the guard can be widened, or the widened
guard is red on master and gets muted.

From a first read of the 20, they fall into at least three kinds and the split
matters:

- HYPOTHETICAL names in prose about `go test -run` semantics, the same kind
  already pinned as illustrative for the non-test sources

title: codegen/age: TestDollarTagClosesOnlyAtTheEnds's closure assertions cannot see a straddle
description:
internal/codegen/age/render_queries_test.go's TestDollarTagClosesOnlyAtTheEnds
carries two assertions past its `want` column:

    body := tag + tt.text + tag
    require.Equal(t, 2, strings.Count(body, tag), ...)
    require.Equal(t, len(body)-len(tag), strings.LastIndex(body, tag), ...)

They read as the closure property — the delimiter closes exactly once, at the
far end — and for a straddle row they prove neither. strings.Count is
NON-OVERLAPPING. Take the row `RETURN p.name\n// trailing $gqlc` under a
wrongly-chosen tag of $gqlc$: the body's matches are the opening tag and then
the straddle formed by the text's trailing $gqlc plus the closing tag's leading
$. The emission's own closing tag begins one byte later and is skipped by the
non-overlapping scan, so the count is 2 and LastIndex still lands at
len(body)-len(tag). Both assertions pass on a delimiter that closes five bytes
early — the exact B1 failure gqlc-35yu.7 was written to prevent.

The rows are not unpinned: the `want` column holds them, and it is doing all of
the work. So this is a readability-and-durability defect, not a live hole — a
row added later without a hand-computed `want`, or a `want` loosened, would be
guarded by assertions that cannot fire.

## How it was found, and what the remedy is

Found 2026-09-02 (agent-j) by the gqlc-7f9a mutation battery. Row M5 restores the
pre-.7 predicate — `if !strings.Contains(text, tag)` in place of
`strings.Index(text+tag, tag) == len(text)` — and SURVIVED the new fence
TestEmittedQueryTextIsTheBytesTheTagWasChosenOn, which had inherited exactly
this spelling and has no `want` column to fall back on. It killed
TestDollarTagClosesOnlyAtTheEnds only through `want`.

The fix is the one that fence now carries, which is dollarTag's own contract
spelled as the scanner behaves — first match after the opening tag:

    require.Equal(t, len(text), strings.Index(text+tag, tag), ...)

Applying it here leaves the two spellings of the same property in one file
agreeing, which is the other half of why this is worth doing: today a reader
comparing the two finds the weaker one first.

Not taken on gqlc-7f9a's branch because that bead is the carriage return and
these rows are already green and already pinned by `want`; a scope rider on a
passing test is not a fix owed by that diff.
notes:
PR #2432 open, gates 14/14 locally, CI running. Branch fix/gqlc-vqx87-straddle-blind-closure-assertions, head commit fd5a58bf.

MEASUREMENT (scratch probe, straddle row "RETURN p.name\n// trailing $gqlc"):
  tag=$gqlc$  (WRONG, closes 5 bytes early) Count==2:true  LastIndex-at-end:true  first-match-at-end:FALSE
  tag=$gqlc1$ (correct)                     Count==2:true  LastIndex-at-end:true  first-match-at-end:true
The second row is the positive control. Both old assertions pass on the broken
delimiter; the new one is the only one that fires.

committed first, restore verified by sha256sum -c, each mutant compiler-screened
with go test -c -o /dev/null:
  M1 render_queries.go:69 -> !strings.Contains(text, tag)   1+/1-  KILLED
  M2 M1 + blind require.Equal(t, tt.want, tag) -> _ = tt.want 2+/2- KILLED
  M3 M2 with the OLD count/LastIndex assertions restored     7+/4- SURVIVED (declared)

M2 certifies the change: with want blinded the new assertion alone kills both
straddling_occurrence and straddle_on_the_escalated_candidate. M3 is a declared
negative control and is the defect MEASURED rather than argued -- six green rows

-run "^TestDollarTagClosesOnlyAtTheEnds$" because
TestEmittedQueryTextIsTheBytesTheTagWasChosenOn carries its own first-match

straddling_occurrence + the emitted-bytes fence and ALSO took
straddle_on_the_escalated_candidate (outcome wider than declared); M3 diffstat
declared 2+/3-, measured 7+/4-. Neither changes a verdict.

title: codegen: a NUL or invalid UTF-8 byte in a query's text emits Go that will not parse
description:
Found while fixing gqlc-7f9a, which refused the carriage return at
internal/codegen/prepare.go beside the existing backtick check, because a Go
RAW string literal cannot carry either byte. That guard is now complete for the
bytes a raw literal SILENTLY changes. It is not complete for the bytes that
make the emitted file unparseable.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 (agent-j), driving codegen.Prepare over every ASCII rune plus
five non-ASCII probes and parsing the emitted `const x = ` + backtick + text +
backtick with go/parser. Exactly four bytes cannot be carried:

  `  (backtick)        refused by Prepare      -- pre-existing
  \r (carriage return) refused by Prepare      -- gqlc-7f9a
  \x00 (NUL)           PERMITTED, unparseable  -- this bead
  invalid UTF-8        PERMITTED, unparseable  -- this bead
                       (probed with "\xff" and the truncated sequence "\xc3(")

## Why it is a separate bead, and a smaller one

The failure mode is the opposite of gqlc-7f9a's. A carriage return was carried
into a file that COMPILED, so generate exited 0 and shipped a constant whose
value was not the query that had been parsed and resolved -- silent, and for
AGE it forged the dollar-quote delimiter. A NUL or an invalid UTF-8 byte makes
the generated package fail to build. That is loud and self-announcing, so
nothing ships wrong; it is a diagnostic-quality defect, not a correctness one.

The cost is that the user is told "illegal character NUL" (or an encoding
error) against a GENERATED file they did not write, with nothing naming the
query or the source byte. The remedy is presumably one more refusal beside the
other two, reading "has a NUL in its source text" / "is not valid UTF-8" --
though it is worth asking first whether these belong further upstream, in
internal/queryfile or in the cypher lexer, since neither byte is meaningful to
Cypher either and refusing at read time would name the FILE and LINE, which
codegen cannot.

## Reachability is unmeasured

I did not check whether a Cypher query carrying either byte parses and
resolves, so I do not know that the set is reachable end-to-end -- the probe
above drives codegen.Prepare directly with a synthetic Validated shape. Settle
that first; if the cypher lexer already refuses both, this closes as unreachable
and the fence below is the whole remedy.

## The fence already names you

internal/codegen/prepare_test.go's
TestARawStringLiteralChangesNoTextPrepareAdmits enumerates the same candidate
set. Its third bucket -- texts whose emission does not parse at all -- is
pinned as an explicit list naming this bead, so the test fails if a byte joins
or leaves that set. Whoever fixes this moves the two entries out of that list
and into the refused bucket, and the fence checks the move.
notes:
LIMIT 1 OF 3 NOW CLOSED, measured after the merge (2026-09-03): a query NAME
carrying either byte does not reach codegen at all. queryfile refuses it first,
and with a BETTER diagnostic than the one this bead added -- it names the file
and the line:

  graph[0]: queries/q.cypher: invalid query name: line 1: "Samp\x00le"
  graph[0]: queries/q.cypher: invalid query name: line 1: "Samp\xffle"

So there is no name-shaped hole beside the text-shaped one, and no follow-up
bead is owed for it. The other two limits stand as written: refusal ordering
among the four bytes is unasserted, and "the lexer refuses these bare" is
measured for one bare position per byte, not for every token slot.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as ed700dee (PR #2396, GH #2121 closed). All 8 CI arms green
including live-smoke; no design bead blocked this (bd dep list empty), so it
merged on gates under protocol

WHAT THE BEAD LEFT OPEN, AND THE ANSWER

Reachability was unmeasured and is now measured, 2026-09-03, by driving
cmd/gqlc over a scratch project rather than codegen.Prepare directly. The set
IS reachable, and not everywhere: the openCypher lexer already refuses both
bytes where they stand in a TOKEN SLOT ("token recognition error"). What
survives to Phase A is the two positions it has no reason to scan --

  - inside a line comment abutting a query line, which queryfile keeps in
    SourceText (bodyText drops only free-standing trailing comment runs);
  - inside a Cypher string literal, where a NUL is a value the neo4j server
    itself accepts.

That settles the placement question the bead raised, and settles it AGAINST
moving upstream. Refusing these bytes in the grammar or in queryfile would
refuse a query neo4j runs; neither byte is a defect in the query, only in its
Go emission, which is what phaseAAdmit is for. So the remedy is the one the
bead guessed -- two more refusals beside the backtick and the CR -- and the
lost file/line naming is the price, paid knowingly.

Before: `format failure: q.cypher.go: 14:8: illegal character NUL`.
After:  `out of C6 scope: query "Q" at position 0 has a NUL in its source text`
        `out of C6 scope: query "Q" at position 0 is not valid UTF-8`
Valid non-ASCII (accented, astral, zero-width) still admitted end to end.

WHAT I INHERITED

TestARawStringLiteralChangesNoTextPrepareAdmits, which the bead pointed at, did
exactly what its author promised: its map pinned the two bytes as admitted, and
flipping them to refused was RED before the fix and GREEN after. Red-before-
green also confirmed the two PRE-EXISTING rows (backtick, CR) pass unchanged,
which is how I knew my message pins were spelled right.

WHAT LIED TO ME

Nothing in the code. One thing in my own harness: M3 was declared as a SWAP of
the two new messages and written as two sequential replaces. Replacing the NUL
message with the UTF-8 one makes that line byte-identical to the UTF-8 arm's,
so the second replace rewrote BOTH and copied rather than swapped. The tell was
the diffstat -- 1+/1- where 2+/2- was declared -- and the NUL subtest passing.
Recorded honestly as M3a; M3 re-run as a true swap through a sentinel. Had I
recorded per-row verdicts without the diffstat tripwire, M3 would have gone in
the record as a swap it never was.

BATTERY (arms: A message test, B candidate-set fence, C sentinel taxonomy,
D conformance invalid corpus; victim declared per row before running; mutant
verified present by diffstat; tree verified restored after each)

  C1  comment in the block, no emitted string   A/B/C/D GREEN    NO-OP (control)
  M1  NUL branch deleted                        A/B/C/D RED      KILLED
  M2  invalid-UTF-8 branch deleted              A/B/C/D RED      KILLED
  M3  the two new messages swapped              A RED, BCD GREEN KILLED by A alone
  M3a UTF-8 arm emits the NUL arm's message     A RED, BCD GREEN KILLED by A alone
  M4  NUL check reads '\x7f' not '\x00'         A/B/C/D RED      KILLED
  M5  UTF-8 check reads q.Name not q.SourceText A/B/C/D RED      KILLED

M3/M3a are why TestPhaseAAdmitNamesTheByteItRefuses exists: the fence, the
taxonomy guard and the whole conformance corpus are ALL blind to a refusal
reporting the wrong byte, because each asks only for the sentinel. M1's D arm
reddens on TestConformanceSuite/TestInvalid/out_of_c6_scope_nul_text across all
three targets, so the fixtures are load-bearing and not riding on the unit
tests. M4 is two-sided -- it reddens the fence's CARRIED bucket for \x7f as well
as its UNPARSED bucket for \x00 -- so the guard notices over-refusal too.

A GUARD CAUGHT ME MID-FIX

TestSentinelTaxonomy refused the first green tree: a branch returning a sentinel
must be reached by a negative fixture under test/data/codegen/invalid, and a
unit test does not satisfy it. The two fixtures place the byte inside a string
literal, bare being a parse error -- so the fixture's PLACEMENT is load-bearing
and is documented in each fixture's own prose.

LIMITS, STATED

  - The refusal is per-query over SourceText only. Query NAMES and parameter
    names are not checked here; they are validated as Go identifiers elsewhere,
    and I did not re-derive that they cannot carry either byte.
  - Ordering among the four refusals is unasserted. A text carrying both a
    backtick and a NUL reports the backtick; nothing pins that and nothing
    depends on it today.
  - "The lexer refuses these bare" is measured for the two bytes in one bare
    position each, not for every token slot.

OUT OF SCOPE, TAKEN ANYWAY, DISCLOSED

docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md gained a row for the CARRIAGE RETURN,
refused since gqlc-7f9a and never given one. That is not this bead. It is in
the diff because my two rows would otherwise leave the table listing backtick,
NUL and invalid UTF-8 while omitting CR, which reads as a claim that CR is
admitted. One documentation line, no code.

title: resolver: sum/min/max over certified operands type from the schema
description: Execution of gqlc-p9qgu; scope to be written into this bead when the design closes.

title: design: sum/min/max upgrade over certified operands — can aggregateResultType cross the parser/resolver boundary
description:
Residue deferred by the gqlc-f45qn ruling (docs/specs/model-change-f45qn-ref-valued-leaves.md §9, merged ce837757). The ref-valued-leaf certificate deliberately mints for collect only: collect's committed type is list<T-of-operand>, so the unknown leaf sits under a list spine and filling it is safe. sum/min/max commit a BARE unknown, and a bare unknown is overloaded — it can mean "operand type unknown" or "engine-dependent fold result" (avg is the witness: unconditionally unknown regardless of operand, shape.go:242 aggregateResultType). Filling a bare unknown from the schema can therefore overwrite a deliberate engine-dependence with a confident wrong answer, which is why the f45qn design carries a never-fill-a-bare-unknown belt.

The question this design must settle: can the resolver distinguish "unknown because the operand was unknown" from "unknown because the fold is engine-dependent" — which appears to require aggregateResultType (today private to internal/query/cypher) to be shared across the parser/resolver boundary, or its verdict to be carried in the model. Each option bends something: exporting it couples the resolver to one dialect's fold table; carrying the verdict is a new model axis beyond the single certificate bit ADR 0003 just admitted.

Do not begin before gqlc-t0bk's implementation has merged — this design builds on the certificate machinery it introduces, and its cost/benefit should be judged against what the certificate turned out to buy in practice.

title: bd prime silently CREATES a ledger at a BEADS_DIR holding none
description:
Measured 2026-09-01/02 while working gqlc-zpjuc.

Pointed at a directory that holds bd config files but no database, every bd verb measured (ready, stats, list --all -n 0, show, mail inbox) IGNORES BEADS_DIR and falls back to git/cwd discovery, which answers correctly. `bd prime` alone CREATES a database there instead, and from that instant BEADS_DIR is honoured and every consumer sharing the path reads an empty fleet — bd ready returns nothing, bd show <any id> says no issue found. Silent, permanent, and indistinguishable from a genuinely empty project.

This is the amplifier that turned a wrong environment variable into ten agents working blind. The wrong variable alone was LATENT; prime is what armed it. Claude Code's SessionStart hook runs bd prime, so any agent session inherits the arming.

Vendored tool: FILE, do not fix here. Wanted upstream: prime should refuse a BEADS_DIR whose directory exists and holds config but no database, or at minimum say on stderr that it is creating one.
notes:
Falsifier for anyone re-measuring: create a dir with only config.yaml+metadata.json, point BEADS_DIR at it, run bd stats (answers the real fleet, creates nothing), then bd prime (creates), then bd stats again (0 issues). See gqlc-zpjuc.
CWD IS NOT THE VARIABLE — measured 2026-09-02 in answer to a challenge from agent-d, who reported that bd sometimes errors and sometimes falls back depending on whether cwd is inside a beads repo, and asked that the trigger be pinned down before anyone asserted it.

Both arms, BEADS_DIR pointed at a fresh dir holding only config.yaml + metadata.json:
  A) cwd OUTSIDE any repo   -> bd prime rc=0, CREATED embeddeddolt
  B) cwd INSIDE a beads repo -> bd prime rc=0, CREATED embeddeddolt (+ backup)

So prime creates in BOTH, and cwd does not gate it. agent-d's asymmetry is real but belongs to the OTHER verbs: those ignore such a BEADS_DIR and either fall back to discovery (cwd in a repo) or fail with 'no beads database found' (cwd outside one). The verb is the variable, not the cwd. This is what makes prime the amplifier: every other verb is inert against a bad path, and prime is the one the SessionStart hook runs.

title: codegen/age: no guard refuses a bare narrowing conversion in an emitted AGE decode body
description:
gqlc-awtb added TestEmittedDecodersNarrowThroughACheck in
internal/codegen/neo4j/decoder_test.go: it parses the emitted decode
bodies and fails on a bare numeric narrowing conversion (int8(x) …
float32(x)), so a future renderer arm that reintroduces the silent wrap
goes red. The AGE backend has no counterpart.

WHY IT WAS SCOPED OUT rather than forgotten: the design on gqlc-k2p68 put
the guard under "MECHANISM, neo4j", and the two backends are not
symmetric. neo4j spells a conversion at eight separate emission sites,
because values arrive there as asserted locals; that is what makes an
unguarded ninth site plausible. AGE decodes through
`agtypeProperty(props, key, decodeFunc(goType))`, so decodeFunc is a
single chokepoint and a new arm reaching a narrow width without the check
would have to go around it deliberately.

So this is a real but second-order gap. What it would take:

  - Generate an AGE emission the way emissionsUnderNarrowingGuard does
    for neo4j (from Generate, NOT from the goldens — a regenerated golden
    must not be able to agree with a defect).
  - Reuse the same AST walk and the same narrowingWidths set.
  - Work out the skip list. This is the real cost: AGE's temporal helpers
    convert time components freely (int(month) and friends), so the walk
    needs either a per-file skip like narrowingGuardSkips or a predicate
    that can tell a component conversion from a width narrowing. The
    neo4j guard took the per-file skip and wrote down what it cost; an
    AGE version has more files in that position.

Falsifier for "the gap is harmless": plant a bare conversion at an AGE
emission site and confirm nothing in the tree goes red except the corpus
rows that happen to cover that one width. If the corpus alone catches
every site, the guard buys little; if a site is uncovered, it buys a lot.
notes:
--- agent-d, 2026-09-03: PR #2547 open (Closes #2091), 15/15 local gates green.

WHAT THE BEAD ASKED AND WHAT THE FALSIFIER SAID
Planting a bare narrowing conversion at each of the three AGE emission
sites, in a git-archive scratch extract:
  entity property (writeEntityFieldDecode) -> 3 behavioural subtests + goldens
  list element    (writeListHelper)        -> 1 behavioural test + goldens
  query column    (columnDecoder)          -> ONE golden row, nothing behavioural
The column site is reached by the corpus at float32 only, through
test/data/codegen/valid/float32_column. Regenerate goldens alongside the
defect and the entire tree is green. Every integer width there: nothing.
So the guard buys the column site, at every width.

WHAT LIED TO ME, TWICE
1. VACUOUS GREEN. My first column mutation covered integer widths only
   and reported the whole tree green (exit=0). That is exactly the shape
   of "the site is guarded" and I nearly wrote it up as such. It was
   vacuous: no fixture carries a narrow-width INTEGER query column, so
   the mutation never fired. float32_column proved the site is reachable
   and re-planting at float32 gave the real answer. requireProbeReaches-
   EverySite exists because of this row.
2. A CONTROL THAT PRE-EMPTED THE GUARD. The first battery scored three
   rows in which the AST walk never executed. requireProbeReachesEverySite
   asked the emission for the checked helper BY NAME -- the guard's own
   question -- so the real defect tripped its require.Empty, and require
   calls FailNow. Both tests that reach the walk reported the CONTROL's
   message. The battery still read as three kills because the test names
   it scores by were the right ones for the wrong reason. Fixed in commit
   two: the control is now blind to how a site decodes and only witnesses
   that the site is reached. D2 now fails through the walk, naming 20
   sites, with the control silent (grep-verified in the row log).

BATTERY: 11 rows, all AS DECLARED. C0 baseline; D1/D2/D3 the defect with
goldens fresh / regenerated / regenerated-and-guard-blinded; N1 blinded
guard with no defect; G1/G2 the probe stopping short with the control
live / blinded; G3 a dropped width; G4/G6 a bogus exemption with the
self-check live / blinded; G5 the exempt skip removed.

TestSentinelTaxonomy/TestCorpusRunsGreen appears in D1/D2 as a CASCADE --
it re-runs the codegen packages as a subprocess for coverage. Not an
independent detector: before this guard existed the D2 defect left the
tree green.

STATED LIMITS (in the source, not only here): agtypeIntAs is not exempt
and cannot be -- it narrows through a type parameter, which the walk does
not see as an identifier, so a generically-spelled narrowing is invisible
to it anywhere. A bare narrowing introduced INTO one of the eight
exempted bodies is not caught; those are emitted as fixed string
constants, so no renderer arm composes a conversion into one per width.
close_reason: Merged as 17daa4ac (PR #2547). The AGE narrowing guard walks emitted bodies from Generate over a probe reaching all three sites at all ten widths; 11 mutation rows all as declared; GH #2091 closed.

title: bd-gh-sync: a foreign-repo mirror whose issue number collides with one of ours is pulled from the wrong issue
description:
## The defect

The pull's mirror pattern is repo-blind:

    pat = re.compile(r"/issues/(\d+)$")     # .githooks/bd-gh-sync:369
    m = pat.search(b.get("external_ref") or "")
    n = int(m.group(1))

It extracts the trailing number from ANY external_ref ending in `/issues/<n>`
— any GitHub repository, and any non-GitHub URL with that shape — and then
looks `n` up in `gh`, which was built from THIS repository's `gh issue list`.
The owner/repo part of the ref is never read.

So a bead mirrored to `https://github.com/other/repo/issues/2009` is treated
as this repo's issue #2009: its state, body and edit time all come from OUR
#2009. Every downstream decision — eligibility, HOLD, the CLOSING transition,
`mirrored` (which drives ORPHAN) — is then made about the wrong issue, and if
it reaches ALLOW the bead is pulled from an issue that has nothing to do with
it.

## What bounds it today, and why that bound is weak

The file's header reasons about foreign refs and is right about the DIRECTION
it names — 'an external_ref is matched over any URL and may name another
repository, so mirrored beads over an empty listing is a legitimate
configuration rather than a lost one' (:82-84). The protection it assumes is
`HOLD not-in-listing` at :387. That holds only while the foreign number is
absent from OUR listing. This repository's issue numbers run past 2040, so any
foreign ref numbered below that collides.

## Evidence and its limit

Read from source at 24597264, not run: I have NOT found a bead in the live
ledger with a foreign external_ref, so I claim no live instance. The finding is
that nothing prevents one — the code has no repo comparison anywhere, and a
agent or a bd feature writing a cross-repo ref is all it takes. `bd update
--external-ref` accepts any string ('gh-9', 'jira-ABC', a Linear URL, per
`bd update --help`).

## Candidate fix, not a design

Parse owner/repo out of the ref and require it to equal origin's
nameWithOwner; anything else is genuinely foreign and should reach a named
record (a HOLD of its own, distinct from not-in-listing, so the two causes do
not read as one). The record matters more than the hold: today a foreign ref
that does NOT collide is already invisible inside `not-in-listing`, which reads
as 'GitHub has not shown me this issue' rather than 'this bead points somewhere
else entirely'.

Watch it fail: a bead whose external_ref names another repo at a number the
local listing contains, and see the pull decide about the local issue.

## Provenance

Found while reading bd-gh-sync for gqlc-e9huy (the pull-reverts-a-reopen
defect), whose design explicitly rests on the claim that 'the pull holds
foreign mirrors at HOLD not-in-listing' — true only in the non-colliding case.
gqlc-e9huy's own hook arm does compare owner/repo against origin, so it is not
affected; this bead is about the pull.

title: check-pr-closes: a PR whose bead is not yet in the export gets no demand, so a closing line swallowed by a stray fence leaves the issue open with nothing red
description:
MEASURED ON A REAL MERGE, 2026-08-30: PR #2029 (bead gqlc-2cmhl, mirror #2016) merged as ad9a154a with 'Closes #2016' written in its body. Issue #2016 did NOT close. Verified: `gh pr view 2029 --json closingIssuesReferences` returns an EMPTY list, and `gh issue view 2016 --json state` read OPEN after the merge. Closed by hand.

THE AUTHOR'S ERROR, which is the ordinary half. The body wrapped a sentence so that a line began '```-block). Run as'. At a line's first character that is an opening fence with the info string '-block). Run as' — a backtick fence's info string may not contain a backtick, and this one contains none, so it opens — and nothing later closes it. Everything below, including 'Bead: gqlc-2cmhl' and 'Closes #2016', is inside a code block. Reproduce with `grep -n '^`\{3,\}' <body>`: three hits, two of them the matched pair, the third unclosed.

THE PART WORTH FILING. Nothing anywhere was red, and the two things that could have caught it both declined for correct reasons:

1. check-pr-closes.py AGREED WITH GITHUB and blanked the same tail — its fence model is right, and this incident is a point of evidence FOR it, not against. Run the merged body back through the gate and claimable_prose() finds zero closing keywords, exactly as GitHub found zero.

2. The demand for 'Closes #2016' never ran, because gqlc-2cmhl was created the same day and is absent from the committed .beads/issues.jsonl that CI reads, so main() took the unknown-bead skip at :1002 and exited 0. Had the bead been in the export, the demand path would have refused with 'PR body is missing Closes #2016' and the fence typo would have been caught at once.

SO THE TWO CONDITIONS COMPOSE INTO A SILENT MISS: a bead too new for the export, plus a closing line hidden from GitHub, equals an issue that stays open after its PR merges with no signal on the PR, in the check log, or on the issue. That is the outcome this entire file exists to prevent, reached by a route where every component behaved as designed.

WHY THE ::warning:: DID NOT FIRE EITHER, which is the sharp bit. The skip path at :1031 reads `GH_CLOSES.findall(claimable_prose(pr_body))` and, when it finds numbers, prints an annotation telling a human that those numbers close at merge unexamined. That is the designed safety net for the skip. It is silent here BECAUSE the keyword was hidden — the very condition that made the miss possible is the condition that suppresses the warning about it. The net covers the case where the author's claim is visible and cannot cover the case where it is not.

NOT PROPOSING THE OBVIOUS FIX. Refusing on an unknown bead is explicitly rejected in the code's own comment at :1004 and for a good reason: the export lands in a chore commit AFTER the PR merges, so no author can make their own bead appear in the copy CI reads, and refusing would block a PR on a condition nothing the author writes can clear. Whoever takes this should treat that pass as fixed.

DIRECTIONS THAT DO NOT REQUIRE THE EXPORT. The skip path knows the bead id and could ask GitHub directly whether an issue mirrors it; or `.githooks/bd-gh-sync`, which MINTS the mirror on push and therefore knows the number without any export at all, could be the thing that notices a body naming that bead without a claimable keyword for it. Both are sketches, not a design — the question of which layer should own it is the actual work here.

Filed at P3 per protocol: fleet machinery, blocking no product work.
notes:
## Taken and fixed at 683c3b52 (branch fix/gqlc-2lx3r-silent-skip-fence-swallowed-closes)

### The bead's own proposed direction is FALSIFIED, and that decided the design

The bead offered two sketches and said the real work was choosing the layer:
"The skip path knows the bead id and could ask GitHub directly whether an issue
mirrors it; or .githooks/bd-gh-sync ... could be the thing that notices."

Both are dead, and neither needed a designer to rule on:

  - ASKING GITHUB FROM THE BEAD ID CANNOT WORK, because a mirror issue does not
    contain the id of the bead it mirrors. Measured 2026-09-03 on this
    incident's own pair: `gh api search/issues q='repo:areqag/gqlc gqlc-2cmhl'`
    returns issues #2040, #2031, #2032 and PR #2029 -- those are the beads that
    CITE gqlc-2cmhl, plus its PR -- while its actual mirror #2016 contains the
    string ZERO times (`gh issue view 2016 --json body | grep -c gqlc-2cmhl` ->
    0). A gate built on that search would have demanded `Closes #2040` on PR
    #2029, i.e. demanded that a PR close THIS bead. The same probe for
    [deleted:gqlc-2c88r] returns exactly one item, PR #2454, and not its mirror #2425.
    The bead/issue mapping lives in bd's external_ref and nowhere on GitHub.

  - BD-GH-SYNC CANNOT READ A PR BODY at the moment it runs. It is invoked from
    .githooks/pre-push:294 and .githooks/post-merge:11. On the push that creates
    a branch there is no PR yet -- which is already why CLAUDE.md records
    pre-push's bead-id warning as advisory only -- and hooks here are not
    dependable anyway (agent worktrees rewrite core.hooksPath in the shared
    config).

So the layer question dissolves: no layer can restore the DEMAND without the
export, because the mirror number is what the demand needs and nothing outside
bd knows it.

### What is fixed instead, and it needs no mapping at all

The skip has two exits and only one spoke. The loud one fires when the body's
closing keyword is VISIBLE. The silent one fires when it is not -- which is
exactly the failure mode, since a keyword GitHub will not act on is the case
where an author believes they claimed an issue and nothing closes it. The
condition creating the miss is the condition emptying `unheld` and suppressing
the report.

The new arm reports the author's own swallowed claim back to them. That is
strictly weaker than the demand and the commit message says so: it makes the
miss VISIBLE, it does not make it RED.

Still a warning, not a refusal, deliberately: gqlc-2cmhl was filed because this
file REFUSED over a backticked keyword in explanatory prose, and refusing here
would reintroduce that on any PR discussing a closing line -- including PR #2029
itself. The skip keeps its contract of never refusing.

### RED, on the real artifact rather than a fixture

PR #2029's merged body, fetched live, with an empty export to force the skip:

    BEFORE: [check-pr-closes] bead 'gqlc-2cmhl' not in export - skipping
            rc=0                                    <- the whole output

    AFTER:  ::warning title=check-pr-closes unverified::gqlc-2cmhl is not in the
            export at this commit, so this check held nothing against it. The
            body writes #1460, #9999, #2016 inside code, where GitHub does not
            read a closing keyword, so those issues will NOT close at merge -
            unfence the line, or close by hand after merging.
            [check-pr-closes] ... #1460, #9999, #2016 are written inside code
            and close nothing at merge
            rc=0

Confirmed the body's own numbers through the gate's parser:
GH_CLOSES over the raw body -> ['1460','9999','2016']; over
claimable_prose(body) -> []. The gate agrees with GitHub, as the bead said.

### Controls, so the arm discriminates rather than always firing

Counter is `grep -c 'inside code'` on the run's stdout (2 lines when it fires:
the annotation and the log line).

| body                              | baseline | means                                  |
|-----------------------------------|----------|----------------------------------------|
| c1 no closing keyword at all      | 0        | ordinary new bead stays SILENT         |
| c2 visible `Closes #1234`         | 0        | SIBLING arm fires, unchanged, exits first |
| c3 fenced `Closes #1234`          | 2        | new arm, singular verb agreement        |
| c4 inline-backticked `Closes ...` | 2        | inline code counts too                  |
| real PR #2029 body                | 2        | the incident                            |

c2 is the row that proves the two arms are ORDERED rather than overlapping.

### Mutation screen (guard committed at 683c3b52 BEFORE mutating)

Baseline asserted with the same counter at the same HEAD, and it is
non-degenerate: 0,0,2,2,2 across c1..c4 and the real body.

| row | mutation | expected victim | verdict | observed |
|-----|----------|-----------------|---------|----------|
| MU-1 | `GH_CLOSES.findall(pr_body)` -> `...(claimable_prose(pr_body))` | c3,c4,real lose the arm | KILLED | c3 2->0, c4 2->0, real 2->0; c1,c2 unchanged at 0 |
| MU-2 | `if swallowed:` -> `if True:` | c1 starts firing | KILLED | c1 0->2; c2 still 0; c3,c4 unchanged at 2 |

Declared diffstat 1 insertion / 1 deletion per row; `git diff --numstat`
returned exactly `1 1` on both. Restored from a mktemp copy after each row;
`git status --short | wc -l` -> 0, and `git diff HEAD --numstat` -> empty.

MU-1 screens that the arm reads the RAW body (its whole point). MU-2 screens the
condition in the other direction -- without it, a passing c1 row could be a
guard that never fires rather than one that discriminates. c2 staying 0 under
MU-2 is the independent evidence that the sibling arm's `sys.exit(0)` is what
keeps the visible case out of this arm.

### Gates

`just gates`: all 14 passed. First run reported 1 of 14 FAILED, and it was MY
residue rather than a defect: loading the script through importlib to read its
regexes wrote .github/scripts/__pycache__/*.pyc, which lint-hooks walks and
refuses for having no shebang. Note `git status --short | wc -l` returned 0
throughout -- __pycache__/ is gitignored at .gitignore:29 -- so the clean-tree
check every mutation row leans on is BLIND to it. Filed as gqlc-rpimx (P4).

### Not fixed here, filed instead

title: check-pr-closes.py: its prose still cites a test suite PR #1595 deleted, so 8+ claims rest on evidence no reader can reach
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-30 at master 0bf5eecd, on the file as it stands.

.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py cites 'the suite' 8 times and says some claim 'is a row' / 'is rowed' 16 times. The suite is .githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh, 2009 lines, DELETED by PR #1595 (f6dc4c7b) on 2026-08-28 along with the `test-hooks` recipe that ran it. Verified: `find . -name '*pr-closes*'` returns the script alone, and `git show f6dc4c7b --stat` lists the suite among ~29 deleted files.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT PEDANTRY. The prose is unusually careful and unusually load-bearing — it is how this file argues its own decisions, and it repeatedly discharges a claim by naming where the evidence lives. Examples, each now pointing at nothing:

  :90   'That is a statement about the bodies in the suite and not a census'
  :134  'what the suite establishes is that every body measured in it ...'
  :486  'the suite goes red in three directions' — an instruction to a future
        editor to try an edit and watch it fail. There is nothing left to go red.
  :572  'paragraphs is a row in the suite's visibility section'

A reader who takes :486 at its word learns nothing; a reader who does not check assumes coverage that is not there. The second is the expensive one, because these sentences are exactly what a later editor consults before changing the blanking rules.

WHAT IS NOT BEING ASKED FOR. Not the suite's restoration. PR #1595's body records that the operator explicitly declined the test gates its design ADR proposed, and re-adding 2009 lines here would re-litigate that decision through a prose bead. Whoever takes this should assume the suite stays gone.

WHAT IS. Make each claim's evidence reachable or make its absence visible. Roughly: a sentence asserting a MEASUREMENT against GitHub's renderer (POST /markdown) keeps its claim and drops the pointer to where a row used to hold it — the measurement happened and the date/PR is the citation. A sentence asserting a BEHAVIOUR OF THIS CODE ('put the toggle back and the suite goes red') is a claim about a check that no longer runs, and either becomes a runnable command a reader can paste, or says plainly that it is unwitnessed today.

DELIBERATELY NOT SCOPED TO A LINE LIST HERE, because whoever takes it has to read all 16 'is a row' claims to sort them into those two piles, and a list in this bead would look like the sorting had already been done. The two greps above regenerate the candidates.

NOTE: gqlc-2cmhl removed one such reference at :524 ('Both comment spellings are rows in the suite's no-bead section') as collateral of a passage it had to correct for other reasons. That is one of the ~8, not a start on this bead.

Filed at P3 per protocol: fleet machinery, blocking nothing.

title: check-pr-closes: the opt-out path now inherits an unmeasured premise about closing keywords inside HTML comments
description:
INTRODUCED BY gqlc-2cmhl, deliberately and with the direction stated here so it is not discovered later as a surprise.

WHAT CHANGED. check_opt_out()'s self-contradiction check now reads claimable_prose(pr_body) rather than the raw body. claimable_prose() blanks, among other carriers, the span from a '<!--' its line does not close to the '-->' that does. So an opt-out body whose only closing keyword for the bead's own number sits inside a MULTI-LINE HTML comment now PASSES the opt-out, where it refused before.

THE PREMISE THAT IS NOT MEASURED. Whether GitHub acts on a closing keyword inside an HTML comment at merge is measured nowhere in this tree. prose_only()'s own docstring says so in the passage about the one-line spelling: 'whether GitHub acts on a closing keyword inside a comment at merge is not measured anywhere in it, and no PR body in this repository carried the shape to measure it on when this was written.'

IF GITHUB DOES ACT ON IT, this is a fail-open on the opt-out path specifically: the gate prints its ::warning:: saying #N stays open at merge, over a body that closes it. That annotation is what a reader deciding whether to merge sees without opening the log, so the failure is a confident wrong answer rather than a silent one.

WHY IT WAS TAKEN ANYWAY. Two of the three GH_CLOSES sites already carried this exact premise before gqlc-2cmhl — main()'s no-bead check (:957) and the unknown-bead scan (:1031), both reading claimable_prose(), as does extra_closes() at :822, which is inside check_opt_out() itself. So the premise was already load-bearing on the opt-out path for every number EXCEPT the bead's own. gqlc-2cmhl made one function stop answering one question two ways; it did not widen the premise to a site that was free of it.

HOW TO MEASURE IT WITHOUT MERGING. GitHub resolves closing references before merge: `gh pr view <N> --json closingIssuesReferences`. So one open PR whose body carries 'Closes #<some open issue>' inside a multi-line HTML comment and nothing else naming that number answers it, with no merge and nothing irreversible. That is the same technique bd gqlc-tysj used on PR #901 for the inline-span case, and its measurement is the model: #617 in spans, absent from closingIssuesReferences, with #862 and #883 in ordinary lines listed, all three issues closed so status was not the reason.

THEN. If GitHub ignores it, record the measurement in prose_only()'s docstring where the gap is currently named, and the question is closed for all three sites at once. If GitHub acts on it, the fix is claimable_prose() ceasing to blank comment spans at all — which is a change to the shared function and so touches all four call sites, and wants its own read.

Filed at P3 per protocol: this is the fleet's own machinery, and it does not block product work.
