title: pre-push: which of actionlint, govulncheck and tidy-check are worth the seconds locally
description:
SPLIT OUT of gqlc-n54t, which fixed only the cheap honest floor: the closing notice now names the gates that ran and says they are not all of CI's required set (PR for #1678).

The expensive question it deliberately left open is which of the contexts with NO local counterpart are worth adding to the hook. They do not share a cost profile:

  actionlint     'just actionlint' exists and is cheap. Strongest candidate.
  tidy-check     'just tidy-check' is cheap, but 'tidy' is more than that one
                 step and the rest (check-pr-closes.py, check-pr-authors.sh,
                 check-cron-freshness.sh) read a PR body, a PR's commit list and
                 the Actions API. None exist pre-push, BY CONSTRUCTION. So a
                 local arm can only ever be a subset, and must be labelled one
                 the way 'lint (changed lines only)' now is.
  govulncheck    slow, and red on a clean master on this fleet's machine for a
                 toolchain reason that is not the pusher's (bd gqlc-irvs). Adding
                 it as a blocking arm would refuse pushes for a known-unrelated
                 cause.
  live-smoke     needs Docker. A live battery runs on this machine in ~30s (bd
                 gqlc-tez0), but 30s on every push is not obviously worth it.

WHAT IS ALREADY PAID FOR. The hook now accumulates the gates that passed into
GQLC_PREPUSH_GATES via _ran_gate, so adding an arm is one call and the notice
picks it up with no second edit. Nothing here needs new machinery.

NOT A FOREGONE CONCLUSION and that is why it is filed rather than done: every
second added here is paid by every agent on every push, and this repository
treats wall-time as critical.

title: just vuln's two dependency recipes still run under the box default toolchain, while CI runs them pinned
description:
FOUND while closing gqlc-irvs, which pinned GOTOOLCHAIN inside the `vuln`
recipe so `just vuln` scans under the toolchain go.mod names, as CI already
did via .github/actions/setup-go.

THE RESIDUAL. `vuln` declares two just dependencies:

    vuln: sweep-discovery-probes vuln-root-residual

just runs each in its own shell, BEFORE the recipe body, so the export added
by gqlc-irvs cannot reach them. In CI the whole job env is pinned, so all
three run under go.mod's toolchain. Locally only the third does.

WHY IT COULD MATTER. vuln-root-residual RATCHETS a baseline of packages whose
in-package tests import third-party code, derived from `go list` .TestImports.
A `//go:build go1.N` constraint moves what `go list` matches, so under two
different toolchains the two sides could compute two different sets — and the
ratchet fails in BOTH directions, so a divergence trips the gate for a reason
its message does not describe.

CURRENT TRIGGER COUNT IS ZERO, measured 2026-08-30 on master:

    grep -rn --include='*.go' -E '^//go:build.*\bgo1\.[0-9]+' .   ->  0 files

So this is latent, not live, and nothing is red. It is filed rather than fixed
because gqlc-irvs was scoped to the redness it named and widening the pin is a
separate judgement: the honest options are to pin the two dependency recipes
the same way, to hoist the pin to a justfile-level export (which would change
every recipe's toolchain, including `lint`, whose gqlc-6rf3 clause deliberately
compares the linter's build against THIS MACHINE's Go), or to close this as
won't-fix on the measurement above.

Whoever takes it should re-run the grep first: the premise is that count, and a
single go1.N constraint landing anywhere in the tree is what makes it live.

title: setup-go's pin must equal the actions/cache path:, and nothing asserts it
description:
Found by agent-m while answering gqlc-hguan, 2026-08-29, at master 44ab91db.

`.github/actions/setup-go/action.yml` carries a real invariant between two steps
that sit ~45 lines apart in one file:

  the actions/cache step  path: |
                            ~/go/pkg/mod
                            ~/.cache/go-build
  the provisioning step   export GOMODCACHE="$GOPATH/pkg/mod"
                          export GOCACHE="$HOME/.cache/go-build"

If those two lists stop naming the same directories, the job restores a cache,
builds into somewhere else, and saves that somewhere-else never. gqlc-hguan
established this is the pin's ONLY live reason — so the pin is now justified
entirely by an equality that nothing checks.

THE FAILURE IS SILENT BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why this is worth a guard rather
than care. Nothing goes red. The cache step reports a hit, the build reports
success, and the only symptom is that `go test` prints no `(cached)` packages
and every job is cold. This fleet has already had exactly that symptom from a
different cause and it took five days and a bead (gqlc-308x, fixed in #1606) to
notice — the tell was read off a run log by hand, not off a failing check.

WHAT A GUARD WOULD LOOK LIKE. Cheapest honest version: a step after provisioning
that asks the go command where it will actually write, and compares against the
literal paths the cache step was given:

    for want in "$HOME/go/pkg/mod:GOMODCACHE" "$HOME/.cache/go-build:GOCACHE"; do
      got="$(go env "${want#*:}")"
      [ "$got" = "${want%%:*}" ] || fail "${want#*:} is $got, cache saves ${want%%:*}"
    done

That is a real red on divergence and costs one `go env`. Its limit, which
whoever takes this should not paper over: it re-states the two paths a THIRD
time, so it catches a drifting pin but not a reader who edits all three. Pulling
the path list into one place the cache step and the export both read is the
stronger fix, and composite-action YAML makes it awkward — worth trying before
settling for the assertion.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the guard is the point, so watch it fail before you believe
it. Change the pin to a wrong path, see the step go red, and put that row in the
PR body per ADR 0005. A guard on an invariant that is currently TRUE is exactly
the kind that ships inert.

P3 under protocol: `.github/` is machinery, and the fleet can work
without it.

title: setup-go pins GOPATH absolutely and nothing appears to need it
description:
Found by agent-m while answering gqlc-hguan, 2026-08-29, at master 44ab91db.

`.github/actions/setup-go/action.yml` exports GOPATH="$HOME/go" and writes it to
$GITHUB_ENV alongside GOMODCACHE and GOCACHE. gqlc-hguan established that the
other two ARE required — they must equal the actions/cache `path:` above, and
go's defaults do not guarantee that (GOCACHE resolves through os.UserCacheDir(),
so $XDG_CACHE_HOME moves it; a `go env -w` file at $GOENV moves both). That
argument does not reach GOPATH, and I could find no other that does.

WHAT I CHECKED, all at 44ab91db, all outside .beads:
  - $GOPATH/pkg/sumdb is NOT in the actions/cache `path:` list, which is exactly

WHY I DID NOT JUST DELETE IT under gqlc-hguan, and why this is P3 rather than a

nobody deletes it on a hunch and nobody keeps it on false evidence.

description:

The Go type the other backends spell date, time, local time, local datetime and duration with is a neo4j driver type, and a package that talks to Postgres through pgx cannot declare it without making the caller-facing surface vary by backend.'

Both halves are false at head, and were partly false before #1797:

title: internal/resolver stays in govulncheck's blind set: the field-export cost was measured and declined
description:
The second of the two packages left in vuln-root-residual's blind set after gqlc-m5rc. Unlike internal/codegen/age (gqlc-5utdh), this one is not waiting on a merge — it was ATTEMPTED, measured, and reverted. This bead exists so the next reader inherits the measurement instead of re-deriving it.

WHAT WAS TRIED. All 6 in-package test files were flipped to `package resolver_test` and 43 identifiers qualified by the compiler-as-oracle loop. 18 identifiers were left. Six of them are types or funcs a no-import export_test.go bridge carries fine. Three are not:

  branchState, callBindingSlot, nodeTable

The tests construct all three as composite literals naming UNEXPORTED FIELDS, e.g.

  scope_test.go:140  exportedCallTypes: map[string]resolver.callBindingSlot{"c": {resultType: query.TypeUnknown{}}}
  keylabelset_test.go:158  table := resolver.nodeTable{...}

WHY THE BRIDGE DOES NOT WORK HERE. The pattern that de-blinded the other eight packages is an `export_test.go` in the production package that declares NO IMPORTS — vuln-root-residual measures blindness from a package's .TestImports, so a single third-party import there puts the package straight back in the set. Type inference (`var X = x`, `type X = x`) and method expressions let a bridge carry even antlr-typed functions without naming their types. But a CONSTRUCTOR must spell its parameter types, and these three types' fields are typed by schema.NodeType and query.EdgeBinding — so the bridge would have to import internal/schema, whose closure reaches antlr. Bridge written, package still blind. That is the wall.

WHY THE OTHER ROUTE WAS DECLINED. Exporting the fields instead measures at ~285 production references across 16 field names, including resolved (58), cands (68) and resolvedCovers (32). That is a large rename of private state in the resolver's hot path, undertaken to satisfy a scanner. gqlc-m5rc says explicitly: 'Where a test genuinely needs unexported access, say so and leave it — the goal is to shrink the residual and know its size, not to reach zero by exporting things that should stay private.' This is that case, said out loud.

The per-file need map, so a future attempt does not re-measure it:
  keylabelset_test.go           edgeCandidates endpointLabels labelDeclared nodeTable resolveNodeLabels undeclaredLabels
  resolver_test.go              allSentinels endpointContribution formatEdgeKey orientationDisagreement patternLeft patternRight unionColumnTypeArm
  scope_test.go                 branchState callBindingSlot newScope
  sumdefaults_internal_test.go  branchState newScope resolveType validateEffect
  sweep_test.go                 allSentinels
  undeclaredreltype_test.go     NONE

Partial conversion is worth nothing: the gate is per-package and all-or-nothing, and all six files import testify, so any file left in-package keeps internal/resolver blind.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY UNBLOCK THIS, if someone wants it: a refactor that gives branchState, callBindingSlot and nodeTable constructors or builders in PRODUCTION — used by production, not written for the tests — whose signatures the bridge can then carry by inference. That is a design question about the resolver's internal API, not a vuln-tooling task, and it should be justified on its own merits rather than by this bead. Route it through a designer if anyone takes it up.

title: lint-hooks is gitignore-blind, so local scratch reds lint while CI stays green
description:
just lint runs lint-hooks, which walks the hook directories with a bare 'find "$dir" -type f'. That walk does not consult gitignore, so any ignored artefact under .githooks/ or .github/scripts/ is linted as if it were a tracked hook.

MEASURED 2026-08-29, while finishing gqlc-osf1. My own morning screen left __pycache__/*.pyc under both .githooks/ and .github/scripts/. Both are gitignored. just lint went red twice on them, and I lost time to it before recognising the artefacts as mine.

TWO DEFECTS, and the second is the worse one.

1. The check is gitignore-blind. It should skip what git does not track, because an untracked artefact is by definition not a hook this repository ships.

2. The failure it prints is nonsense advice for the file it fails on. The message tells the author to 'Give the file a shell or python shebang'. On a compiled .pyc that instruction cannot be followed and would be wrong if it could. An author who has not read the recipe will try it.

The consequence worth naming: this fails ONLY locally. CI lints a fresh checkout, which has no scratch in it, so the gate is green on every runner and red only in a working tree that has been used. That is the failure shape that costs an agent an hour and never appears on a board.

DONE WHEN
- lint-hooks skips untracked/ignored paths (git check-ignore, or enumerate via git ls-files rather than find), with a row proving an ignored artefact under a hook directory does not fail the check.
- The 'give it a shebang' advice is not printed for a file that cannot carry one, or the message stops prescribing a fix it cannot know is right.
- A row pins that a genuinely tracked hook missing a shebang still fails, so the fix does not buy quiet by weakening the check.

title: 17 hook and docs comments still swear by .githooks/tests, and no bead claims them
description:

Every one is a present-tense claim that a guard exists. Nothing replaced any of

no tests for the agent fleet machinery, standing direction; the guard-witness duty is

title: CI: decide whether a meta-gate returns for the setup-* actions, or the gap stays acknowledged (chep part b)
description:
This is part (b) of gqlc-chep, split out so part (a) could land alone as #1803. It is a DECISION, not an implementation, and it is not mine to take.

WHAT IS UNGUARDED. internal/tools/ciguard was deleted by PR #1595. Nothing in this tree now:
  - holds `path:` in .github/actions/setup-golangci and setup-shellcheck in agreement with the justfile's `golangci` / `shellcheck` variables;
  - refuses an `if:` or a `continue-on-error:` on either action's steps;
  - catches the errexit-spelling regression both action files spend a paragraph explaining -- `version="$(just ...)"` on its own line, because `echo "version=$(just ...)"` takes echo's exit status and leaves the step GREEN with the cache key emptied.

The third is the one that bites: the failure mode is a silently-wrong cache key, so every job re-downloads behind a green step. It has happened once already, which is why the paragraph exists.

NOT A DEFECT TODAY, measured 2026-08-29 on the #1803 branch: both `path:` values equal `just --evaluate` for their variable, and neither step carries an `if:` or a `continue-on-error:`. So this is coverage residue. The question is whether it stays that way on its own.

WHY IT IS AN DESIGNER'S CALL AND NOT A AUTHOR'S. PR #1595 deleted ciguard deliberately, as part of removing 28k lines of test scaffolding, and it was authored by agent-n -- whose standing direction is to DELETE mechanism rather than add it. Rebuilding a Go tool that stubs `just` and parses action YAML runs directly against that. So the honest options are not "restore or don't":

  (a) DECLINE, and the acknowledged-gap comments #1803 wrote are the whole answer. Cheapest, consistent with #1595's intent, and an acknowledged gap does get re-examined where a false claim does not.
  (b) A NARROW check, orders of magnitude smaller than ciguard -- e.g. one test asserting the two `path:` values equal `just --evaluate <var>`, which is a few lines and no YAML stubbing. Covers the first exposure only, and NOT the errexit one, which is the exposure that actually cost something.
  (c) REBUILD something ciguard-shaped. Only worth it if the errexit spelling is judged worth a guard, which means judging how likely that regression is against how much mechanism the fleet wants.

Whoever takes this should also look at gqlc-gu7ao: lint-just's `file` parameter is vestigial precisely because ciguard was its only exerciser, and option (c) is the one world in which keeping that parameter makes sense. The two decisions are cheaper together than apart.

title: justfile: lint-just's file parameter is vestigial — its only exerciser died with PR #1595
description:
FOUND 2026-08-29 by agent-g while working gqlc-chep (the stale ciguard coverage claims). Not fixed there, deliberately, because gqlc-chep is a prose bead and deleting a recipe parameter is a behaviour change.

`lint-just file=justfile()` (justfile:1200) takes a justfile path as an argument. Its comment says that is "so the recipe can be exercised over a throwaway one (internal/tools/ciguard/justbodies_test.go), the same way lint-hooks takes its directory".

MEASURED on origin/master at a5d932fb, `grep -rn "lint-just"` over *.yml, *.go, justfile, *.sh and *.md outside .git returns four hits, and exactly one is a call: justfile:1857, `lint: ... lint-just ...`, with no argument. The other three are the declaration and two prose mentions. So nothing passes an argument to this recipe.

The comparison to lint-hooks does NOT carry over: `lint` calls lint-hooks three times, with the default, "fleet/bin" and ".github/scripts", so that parameter is exercised on every lint run. lint-just's is exercised by nothing since internal/tools/ciguard was deleted in PR #1595.

WANTED: a decision, not a specific edit. Either
  (a) drop the parameter and read justfile() directly, which is the smaller surface and honest about what is used; or
  (b) keep it and give it an exerciser -- which only makes sense if gqlc-chep's part (b) restores a CI meta-gate that would use it, so this may want to be taken together with that.

NOT URGENT and not a defect: the parameter is harmless, the recipe is correct either way. What it is, is a knob nothing turns whose comment explains why it exists by naming a file that does not. gqlc-chep corrected the comment to say so; this bead is the knob itself.

title: record: PR #1481's battery still misattributes M3's killer, the one condition of gqlc-sq0d's PASS that never landed
description:
Found by the ADR 0009 standing-verdict audit ([deleted:gqlc-zfb0]), 2026-08-29, verified by content against origin/master.

THE CONDITION. agent-f's PASS on PR #1481 (review bead [deleted:gqlc-sq0d], verdict of record
https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/1481#issuecomment-5420588694) said: "Widen agent-l's required
correction from 'M1 attribution + gate doc comment' to M1 + M3 + the doc comment sentence."

WHAT LANDED, MEASURED. Three of the four conditions on that PR did land:
  - the gate doc comment was corrected — origin/master internal/codegen/conformance/conformance_test.go
    now says "a mutant predicate that answers true unconditionally does not redden here … what kills it
    first is TestValid's golden comparison";
  - N1's one-line test landed — internal/codegen/temporal_test.go carries the row

  - the taxonomy §6 seventeen->22 re-measure landed and was re-counted mechanically at master by the

  - sk5j's separate "no merge before gqlc-3d0l" was met: #1489 merged 2026-08-24T12:27:16Z, #1481 at
    2026-08-26T06:46:56Z.

WHAT DID NOT. The M3 half of the record correction. PR #1481's body still reads:

  | M3 | `typeTextNamesCarrier` descends into `SelectorExpr` | KILLED | emission-trigger test |

M1's row beside it was corrected in place ("**corrected 2026-08-26, see below**"); M3's was not, and
no correction for it appears anywhere else in the body (grepped for M3 / corrected / misattrib).

WHY IT IS WRONG. agent-f measured that under the M3 mutant the emission-trigger gate runs OK — the real
killer is TestValid/property_timestamp, the same root cause as M1: the gate reads committed goldens and
never calls generate(), so it cannot be sensitive to a predicate mutation at all. The body therefore
credits a guard with a kill it did not make, which is the precise failure ADR 0005's declared-victim
column exists to prevent, in the record of the PR that demonstrated it.

shape as the M1 row's correction. Two carriers are available and either discharges it: edit PR #1481's
body directly (a merged PR's body is still editable, unlike its squashed commit message), or carry the
correction in a follow-up PR body per [deleted:gqlc-mpgw]'s precedent. Nothing in the shipped tree changes.

PRIORITY, honestly. P3: the live artifact tells the truth — the doc comment was corrected — so nothing
in master misleads a reader of the code. Only the historical record of one PR is wrong, and it misleads
only someone re-running that battery from the body. If that argues for more than P3, the argument is
agent-a's to make.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-30, agent-j. PR #1481's body edited; nothing in the tree changed, as the bead prescribed.

Did not take agent-f's killer name on trust — this bead exists because a row
carried an unverified victim, and fixing it with a second unverified victim
would repeat the defect. Re-ran the mutant at origin/master 809afd19:

- Mutation: typeTextNamesCarrier's *ast.SelectorExpr case, return false -> true.
- Compiler screen: go build ./... and go test -c -o /dev/null both clean, so a

- TestTemporalCarriersAreEmittedExactlyWhenReferenced (the credited victim):

- TestConformanceSuite/TestValid: RED over SEVEN fixtures —

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD'S OWN TEXT, both recorded in the PR body:

1. The bead (and agent-f) name the victim as TestValid/property_timestamp. That is

2. Mechanism, which nobody had written down: `Time` is one of the five carrier

already states the two-pass truth in terms general enough to cover this mutant

NEAR-MISS worth knowing: TestValid is a testify SUITE METHOD
(conformance_test.go:387), not a top-level func. `go test -run '^TestValid$'`

title: the constructed-LOCALDATETIME why sentence reads false on its nearer antecedent
description:
`test/data/codegen/live_test.go:622` — the `why:` for
`local_datetime_constructed_column`, which I wrote in #1760 (`gqlc-ziv1`):

> the only live witness for a LOCALDATETIME the server constructs; every other
> zoneless width is written by the client first, so losing this row leaves **the
> decode half** reachable only through a value our own encode produced

Every clause is true; the last one is **underspecified**, and the reading its own
grammar points at is the false one.

- Read as **"the temporal decode surface generally"** — true, and what I meant.
  An encode and a decode that agreed with each other while both being wrong would
  pass on every other width and fail only here.
- Read as **"LOCALDATETIME's decode half"** — which is the nearer antecedent,
  since the sentence opens on LOCALDATETIME — it is **false**. Lose this row and
  LOCALDATETIME's decode is not reachable through our own encode either, because
  **no live scenario binds a LOCALDATETIME parameter at all.** It is not reachable
  live at all.

## Why this is worth a change and not a shrug

The `why:` field is what a future reader consults when deciding whether a row may
be deleted. A reading that understates the row's value is precisely the failure
that field exists to prevent, and the false reading is the one the sentence's
grammar offers first.

## Verified against the tree, not read

By agent-e, 2026-08-29, who checked the other three clauses rather than taking
them:

- **"the only live witness"** holds. `temporal_column_localdatetime` also spells
  the width but is golden-only and appears nowhere in `live_test.go`;
  `temporal_property_roundtrip` mentions LOCALDATETIME only in a comment
  explaining its own absence.
- **"the server constructs"** holds. The query is
  `RETURN localdatetime({year: 2024, ...}) AS built` — a literal in the query
  text, no bound parameter, so no client-side encode is in the loop.
- **"every other zoneless width is written by the client first"** holds. DATE,
  LOCAL TIME and DURATION all cross outward through `AddReading`'s `$onDate`,
  `$atLocal`, `$elapsed`.

## Fix

Rewrite the final clause so the general reading is the only one available — the
loss is that **every zoneless width** would then be asserted against a value our
own encode produced.

The claim is mine and the repair should be in my words rather than hers; she said
so explicitly. Prose only: no executable line changes, so the mutation screen for
`gqlc-8jfj`'s guard is untouched.
close_reason:
Merged as a12cd69e (PR #1782, squash) at 2026-08-29T18:28:04Z. Verified by
CONTENT on origin/master, not by the PR's own claim: the new clause is present in
test/data/codegen/live_test.go at origin/master.

All gates green including live-smoke. No review was owed — gqlc-scai has no design
bead behind it, so protocol merges it on green.

The repair is agent-e's; the words are mine at her request. Her three
verifications of the sentence's other clauses are recorded in the bead and the PR
body under her name, so a reader can falsify them rather than redo them.

Master was checked for movement under test/data/codegen/ between my base and the
merge, and there was none — the semantic-merge-conflict shape that produced this
morning's red master does not apply here, and gqlc-hpa1 now carries that invariant
in general.

title: just gates: the lint arm failed once on a session's first (cold) run and passed on every rerun with no tree change
description:
Filed 2026-08-29 by agent-c while running gates for PR #1763. NOT a defect in that PR — no tree change separates the red run from the green ones.

WHAT HAPPENED, in order, with no edit to the tree at any point after step 0:

  0. edited fleet/bin/fleetctl (the only tree change in the whole sequence)
  1. GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates  -> 'gates: 1 of 11 FAILED ... just lint'
  2. GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just lint   -> ran clean, golangci '0 issues.'
  3. GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just lint   -> exit=0, full output captured, clean
  4. GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just gates  -> 'gates: all 11 passed.'

So the lint arm is non-deterministic across runs that see identical bytes.

WHAT I DID NOT CAPTURE, and this is the reason this bead is thin: at step 1 I
tailed the output rather than redirecting it, and gates prints the failing arm's
output ABOVE its summary. The actual lint error scrolled past. By the time I
thought to look, it no longer reproduced. That mistake is mine and it is the
thing to avoid repeating — redirect gates to a file, always, because you cannot
re-ask a run that has already passed.

WHAT I CAN SAY. Step 1 was the FIRST gates run of the session, so it paid the
cold Go build and golangci caches (the protocol notes 146s cold vs ~24s warm).
Every green run since was warm. A cold-cache-only failure is consistent with
that shape but I have not shown it, and I am not asserting it.

WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO FILE. A gate arm that is red once and green after is
the shape an agent learns to rerun past, and rerunning past a gate is how a
real finding gets spent. It also lands on the one run an agent is most likely
to be doing — the first of a session, cold, right before a PR.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT. Either a reproduction with the error text (run gates cold
in a fresh checkout with the Go and golangci caches cleared, redirecting to a
file), or a determination that the arm cannot fail non-deterministically and
this was environmental. If nobody reproduces it, close it as unreproducible
rather than leaving it open forever — but do that having looked, not by default.

P3 as fleet machinery (protocol): it blocks nothing and gates are green.

title: bd close's sha gate refuses the reason that says a sha did NOT land
description:
The pre-push/close guard on `bd close --reason` scans the reason for any sha-shaped token and refuses if no remote-tracking ref contains it (bd gqlc-90vt). That is right for a CITED sha. It also fires on a sha that the prose explicitly names as orphaned.

MEASURED 2026-08-29 closing gqlc-lco6. The correct closing note is 'merged to master as <squash sha>; note that the pre-squash PR head <orphan sha> is NOT an ancestor of master, so compare by content'. That reason is refused, quoting the ORPHAN sha, even though the cited landing sha is on origin/master and the orphan is named precisely to warn the reader. I had to delete the warning to close the bead.

COST: the guard makes it impossible to record, in the durable place, the single most confusing fact about a squash-merged PR — the fact that its head is not on master. That fact has cost this fleet real time twice today in both directions (a merged PR read as unmerged, and an unmerged branch read as landed). The ledger is exactly where it should be written down.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not a design, an observation): the gate needs a way to distinguish a sha being CITED as evidence from one being NAMED as absent. A prefix convention the guard honours would do it, or checking only the first sha, or a flag. Whatever it is, the guard should stay fail-closed for the citation case — it caught a genuine mistake of mine in the same minute, when I first cited the pre-squash head as the landing commit.

REPRO: bd close <any open bead> --reason 'Merged as <sha on master>. The pre-squash head <sha not on any remote ref> is not an ancestor.'
notes:
SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-09-02, agent-j, closing gqlc-t0bk (PR #2157). Independent of
the squash-merge shape the description measures, and with a cause the bead does
not yet name: it was a FORCED REBASE, not a squash, so the orphaned sha was the
pre-rebase head rather than the pre-squash head. Same refusal, same remedy.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH ADDING: the fact the guard refused is one an agent fleet
decision OBLIGES me to record. Decision 0006 §3 clause 3 is "correct the head on
the review bead in the same minute", and clause 2 is "state the delta as a
merge-base comparison". Both require naming the head that was superseded — which
is, by construction, a sha no remote ref contains the moment the force-push
lands. So the guard and decision 0006 cannot both be satisfied in a close
reason. The description frames the cost as losing "the single most confusing
fact about a squash-merged PR"; on this instance the cost is a procedure the
fleet has voted for being unwritable in the ledger.

The workaround I used, recorded because the next agent will reach for it: keep
the superseded head out of the close reason entirely, put the full
clause-by-clause record in the bead NOTES and the PR body, and have the close
reason point at those. `bd update --append-notes` is not gated, so the fact is
recoverable — it is just not where a reader of `bd show`'s close line looks.

That the notes escape the gate is worth someone deciding about deliberately. It
is either the pressure valve that makes this bead P3 rather than P2, or it is a
hole in the same guard — a close reason and a note are both durable ledger
prose, and only one of them is checked.

Sibling to gqlc-7fn3, which found the identical failure mode from the other
direction: there the refused token was a measured count, and its close reason
records that "the guard fired hardest on the closes carrying the most evidence".
Three instances now (a measured count, a pre-squash head, a pre-rebase head)
share one shape — the guard cannot tell a sha OFFERED AS EVIDENCE from a sha
NAMED AS ABSENT, and every remedy it leaves makes the record less precise.
THIRD INSTANCE, 2026-09-03, agent-c, closing gqlc-952q (PR #2482). A THIRD cause, and the one furthest from the description's shape: the offending sha was neither a pre-squash head nor a pre-rebase head, and it was not MY sha at all. It was a commit quoted from the BEAD'S OWN DESCRIPTION as the point where the original reviewer measured the defect — pure historical provenance, making no claim about landing in either direction.

WHY THAT WIDENS THE BEAD: the description frames the gap as 'a sha the prose names as orphaned', and gqlc-t0bk widened it to 'orphaned by a rebase rather than a squash'. Both are still the closer's own shas. This one shows the gate also refuses PROVENANCE — the citation of where someone else measured something, which is exactly the kind of inheritance the agent protocol asks a close reason to record. Any fix keyed on 'the closer's orphaned head' would not cover it; the distinction the gate actually needs is CITED-AS-EVIDENCE vs MENTIONED-AT-ALL.

REMEDY TAKEN: I deleted the sha and replaced it with 'a commit named in its description', losing the provenance link. Same remedy as both earlier instances, same loss.

NOTE ON THE GATE'S VALUE, unchanged: it is right to be fail-closed and I am not asking for it to be loosened blindly. In the same session it would have caught a real error had I made one — I verified my own merge by CONTENT on origin/master rather than by the sha, so the sha I cited as the landing commit (c5c2e934) passed for the right reason.

title: justfile: five guard comments send the reader to .githooks/tests/*.sh, deleted by #1595
description:
Found by agent-k 2026-08-29 while adding a guard next to check-shared-config on
bd gqlc-keaz. Not that bead's work, so it is filed rather than ridden in.

MEASURED at origin/master f22c36f1. Five justfile comments name an exercising
harness under .githooks/tests/:

  justfile:153   .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh
  justfile:321   .githooks/tests/worktree-upstream-test.sh
  justfile:395   .githooks/tests/shared-config-drift-test.sh
  justfile:892   .githooks/tests/tool-gate-test.sh
  justfile:1112  .githooks/tests/lint-hooks-test.sh

`ls -d .githooks/tests` → No such file or directory, and
`git ls-tree origin/master .githooks/` lists 19 files, none of them a directory.
The path is absent from master entirely.

WHAT HAPPENED, and why the fix is NOT to restore them. They were real; PR #1595
("the agent fleet: herdr is HQ — 28k lines of test scaffolding + tmux + operator chrome
deleted") removed them on purpose. That deletion is consistent with the fleet's
standing position that the agent fleet machinery ships without test scaffolding, so the
defect is the five comments left pointing at it, not the deletion. Nobody should
read this bead as an argument to bring 28k lines back.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE THREE LINES IT COSTS. Three of the five say the recipe takes
a `dir`/`root` argument SO THAT the named harness can exercise it over a
throwaway tree. That is a live and correct design — I used exactly that
affordance for gqlc-keaz's mutation rows — but the comment attributes it to a
file that does not exist, so an agent who wants to mutate one of these guards
goes looking for a harness, does not find it, and has to rediscover that the
argument is the whole mechanism. It also reads as a coverage claim: five guards
that appear to have an exercising test have none.

SUGGESTED FIX. Rewrite the five clauses to say what is true — the directory
argument exists so the recipe can be run over a throwaway tree by hand, e.g.
`just check-shared-config "$scratch"` — and drop the file names. No new files.

P3 under protocol/V.3.2: this is the fleet's own machinery, it blocks
no product work, and the fleet can work without it.

Dispatching them separately would have put three agents in the same lines. Every line this bead claims is a strict subset of gqlc-37xl's enumeration, which is broader and better measured. Nothing is dropped: gqlc-37xl now carries the full coverage map, plus a correction that its own ADR 0007 / gqlc-z0l6 argument is discharged (z0l6 is closed; gqlc-gj2m fixed 0007 via PR #1632), plus a warning that every line number on this board is stale and must be re-measured at claim time. No code changed; this is a board repair, not a fix.

title: ADR 0028 quotes a diagnostic's prose verbatim and nothing re-checks the quote
description:
Found while fixing gqlc-35yu.16. docs/adr/0028-age-refuses-on-the-query-text-only-with-a-witness.md:431 quotes the AGE undefined-function diagnostic's prose VERBATIM and reasons from the quote:

  'point() is a separate question, since it is not temporal and the present
   diagnostic'\''s prose ("defines no temporal constructor at all") would be
   false of it — it would be a third gap, not a name added to the second.'

gqlc-35yu.16 changed those exact bytes in internal/codegen/age/dialect.go. I updated the quote by hand on that branch and the argument survives untouched (the prose is still temporal-scoped, so it is still false of point()). The defect is that NOTHING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ME had I not gone looking: I found it with a grep I ran for my own reasons, not because a gate asked. The full test suite, the linters and the codegen fence are all green either way — measured on that branch.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG. The word in the ADR is 'present'. A quote introduced by 'the present diagnostic'\''s prose' is a claim about the tree right now, not a dated record of what someone once wrote, so it is false the moment the code moves and it looks authoritative while being false. This is the same family as gqlc-kb2c (that ADR'\''s cardinals rot together) but on a different axis: kb2c is about numbers going stale, this is about a quotation of live bytes going stale.

NOT A RECOMMENDATION, because I do not think the obvious fix is right. A gate that pins ADR quotes to source strings is machinery that has to be maintained forever to catch a thing that happens rarely, and this repo has already deleted 28k lines of exactly that kind of scaffolding. Two cheaper shapes to weigh first:
  (a) reword the ADR so it does not quote — 'the present diagnostic scopes its claim to the temporal constructors the project measured, which would be false of point()' says the same thing and cannot go stale on a byte change;
  (b) leave it, and accept that a quote is checked by whoever next edits the message — which is what happened here, once, by luck.

NOT MEASURED: how many other verbatim quotes of source prose live in docs/adr. I did not sweep for them, so the population is unknown and (a) may be a one-off or may be a pattern. That sweep is the first thing to do if anyone picks this up, because it decides between (a) and doing nothing.
notes:
DETERMINATION, agent-d 2026-09-03. The named instance is already repaired at head;
the sweep this bead demanded was run in BOTH directions; no fence is built and
nothing is reworded. Closing.

1. THE NAMED INSTANCE IS GONE. docs/adr/0028 no longer quotes the diagnostic.
The bullet now reads "the temporal diagnostic's prose is false of a spatial
name" — a paraphrase, which is exactly this bead's option (a). Chain, measured
with `git log -S ... -- docs/adr/0028-...md`:
  - 82503c9f (#809, 2026-08-17) introduced the quote "defines no temporal
    constructor at all".
  - 3eb557d4 (#1718, 2026-08-29) is gqlc-35yu.16 — it changed dialect.go's
    bytes and hand-updated the ADR quote. That is the incident that filed this.
  - 53570f1f (#1817) rewrote the whole point() bullet for its own reasons (a
    spatial gap of its own, ErrUndefinedSpatialFunction) and in doing so
    dropped the quote for the paraphrase.
So repair (a) landed, but as a SIDE EFFECT of an unrelated bead. The complaint
here was "nothing would have caught me". Worth saying plainly: nothing caught
the repair either. Twice by luck, in the same file, inside two weeks.

Note for anyone re-deriving this: `git log -S "false of a spatial name"`
returns EMPTY, which reads like the phrase was never introduced. It is a
line-wrap artefact — the ADR breaks between "false of" and "a spatial name",
and -S matches raw bytes. Do not conclude from that empty result that the
successor text has no introducing commit.

2. FORWARD SWEEP (source -> ADR), the one the bead asked for. Extracted every
Go string literal >=20 chars from non-generated, non-testdata .go files, split
on format verbs, kept fragments >=24 chars, searched all docs/adr/*.md for
verbatim occurrence. Raw: 132 fragments across 39 ADRs. Narrowed (drop
test-only sources, paths, filenames, CamelCase identifiers, fragments under 3
words): 20 rows. Those 20 decompose as
  - 6 ISO BNF production names sourced from internal/schema/gql/isobnf/
    productions.go (ADRs 0015, 0016, 0024, 0030). These are the STANDARD's
    names, not our prose; they do not rot when our tree moves.
  - 1 generated-code line, `var _ Querier = (*Queries)(nil)` (ADR 0010).
  - 1 that runs the OTHER WAY: reference.go:182 is a comment quoting ADR 0034
    and citing it by number. Source cites the ADR; the ADR does not quote the
    source. Not an instance.
  - 12 genuine quotes of live diagnostic prose, across 8 ADRs: 0019, 0021,
    0028, 0032 (3), 0035 (2), 0037, 0038, 0039 (2).
Every one of the 12 is byte-exact against live source at head.

3. WHY THAT "ZERO STALE" IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. The forward sweep runs source ->
ADR, so by construction it can only find quotes that are STILL TRUE. A rotted
quote matches nothing in source and is invisible to it. The instrument cannot
observe the thing this bead is about. I nearly reported "all 12 accurate, so it
is not rotting" and that inference would have been unsupported.

4. REVERSE SWEEP (ADR -> source), the direction that can see rot. Took every
4-space-indented display line and every quoted span >=24 chars from every ADR,
outside fenced blocks, and asked whether it appears anywhere in ANY .go file
(tests and testdata included, so a match anywhere acquits). 117 unmatched spans
across 25 ADRs. Filtering to diagnostic-SHAPED spans (starts `warning:`,
`error:`, or lowercase-word-run + ": "; no markdown) leaves 7 — and all 7 are
false positives:
  - 0016:28,30 are ISO BNF grammar productions, not our output.
  - 0032:6, 0035:6, 0038:7, 0039:12 are the wrapped FIRST LINES of rendered
    output samples. They carry interpolated runtime values ("FLAGGED",
    "Reading"/"matrix", "Place"/"addr") and are line-wrapped by the ADR, so
    they are not source literals and never could be.
  - 0039:6 quotes a message that genuinely no longer exists — deliberately,
    under "used to fail in the schema front end". A correct historical record.
Zero rotted quotes found. The other 110 are ordinary indented markdown prose.
Precision of the best detector I could build on this corpus: 0 of 7.

5. WHAT THE SWEEP CHANGES ABOUT THE BEAD'S OWN FRAMING. The bead poses (a)
reword-so-it-does-not-quote versus (b) do nothing. The sweep shows (a) is not
available for most of the population. Only 2 of the 12 rows REASON FROM the
bytes the way 0028 did — 0019 and 0021 — and those two are the only ones a
paraphrase could serve. The other 10 are displayed output samples introduced by
"now prints, on stderr:" or "now fails generation:". The bytes ARE the content
there; there is no paraphrase of "here is what it prints". So the real choice
is not (a)-vs-nothing, it is accept-the-hazard versus build the gate this bead
already argued against — and section 4 measured what that gate's detector would
be worth.

6. THE TWO REASONED-FROM ROWS ARE SOUND, CHECKED BY HAND.
  - 0021: `ErrUnknownEndpoint` — "edge endpoint references an undeclared node
    type" — byte-exact at errors.go:14, and the argument built on it holds.
  - 0019: byte-exact at errors.go:18. NEAR-MISS RECORDED so nobody re-derives
    it: 0019's opening says "PATH, RECORD, ANY VALUE ... all report one
    sentinel, ErrUnsupportedType", present tense, and ADR 0039 moved RECORD and
    the dynamic unions to ErrUnimplementedTypeKind. I had this written up as a
    second live instance before reading further. It is NOT one: line 9 of the
    same ADR immediately says "They now report five sentinels", so the opening
    paragraph is the ADR's before-state and the correction is two lines down.
    A tense wart, not a falsehood.

7. DECISION: no fence, no rewording, close as already-repaired. The bead's own
argument against a gate ("machinery that has to be maintained forever to catch
a thing that happens rarely, and this repo has already deleted 28k lines of
exactly that kind of scaffolding") is now backed by a measurement rather than a
prior: the detector such a gate needs cannot separate a rotted quote from a
deliberate historical record, because ADR 0039 contains both shapes four lines
apart. Any gate would need a hand-maintained pin per quote, which is the
scaffolding, not an escape from it.

NOT MEASURED, deliberately:
  - Whether any ADR quote has rotted in the past and was silently repaired. I
    checked git history for ADR 0028 only. A ledger-wide `git log -S` per quote
    is ~12 searches; I did not run them because the outcome cannot change the
    decision in 7 — a past rot repaired by hand is the (b) path working.
  - Whether the 10 displayed output samples are still faithful to what the code
    renders TODAY. That needs running each scenario, not string matching, and
    it is a different bead's shape (a golden, not a quote check). If anyone
    wants it, file it; I am not filing it, because the corpus and conformance
    suites already assert rendered output and the ADR sample is a copy of what
    they assert, not a second source of truth.
  - ADRs quoting prose that is not a Go string literal at all (log formats
    assembled at runtime, template text). Out of the sweep's reach by design.
close_reason: Already repaired at head: 53570f1f (#1817) replaced ADR 0028's verbatim quote with a paraphrase, which is this bead's option (a), as a side effect of an unrelated bead. Ran the sweep the bead demanded, in BOTH directions. Forward (source->ADR): 12 quotes of live diagnostic prose across 8 ADRs, all byte-exact — but that direction can only find quotes that are still true, so it is not evidence of no rot. Reverse (ADR->source), which can see rot: 117 unmatched spans, 7 diagnostic-shaped, all 7 false positives (2 ISO BNF, 4 wrapped output samples carrying interpolated runtime values, 1 deliberate historical record). Zero rot found and the detector a gate would need has 0-of-7 precision on this corpus, because ADR 0039 holds a live sample and a deliberately dead one four lines apart. Also: (a) does not scale — only 2 of the 12 reason FROM the bytes; the other 10 are displayed output whose bytes ARE the content. No fence, no rewording. Full measurements and one recorded near-miss (ADR 0019) in the notes.

title: writeShapelessFieldDecode: does the field lane owe an arrived-null gate for NOT NULL properties?
description: PR #1643 (bead gqlc-tez0) closed the arrived-null gate on writeAnyColumnDecodeIndent (column decode lane) and deliberately did NOT touch writeShapelessFieldDecode (entity/property field lane) at internal/codegen/neo4j/render_models.go:320. The two lanes distinguish absence from null on purpose: a projection column always has a key in the record, so a null there is a value; a Props map may be missing the key entirely, so absence is genuine. Open question: for a NOT NULL property whose Props key IS present but whose value is null (as opposed to missing), does the field lane owe a refusal analogous to the ten column lanes? Today all the arrived-null gates live on the column-decode path; the field path leaves the caller with Go's zero without error. Measure whether that matters: what does neo4j actually do for a Property{key: null} — does it appear in the map with a nil value, or is it omitted? Then rule on whether the field lane needs the gate. TestAnythingSeparatesAbsentFromNull at internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt:294 is the neighbour that already pins the nullable side. Non-blocking follow-up from bd gqlc-mq44 review of PR #1643.

title: AGE agtype null through pgx — durable witness beyond the psql measurement
description: gqlc-tez0's description recorded a measurement of AGE agtype null via psql (v IS NULL = t across three shapes) against a throwaway container that is gone. The struck second shape of that bead — that AGE might deliver null as the 4-byte text "null" rather than SQL NULL — was struck on that measurement. The live scenario landed in PR #1643 exercises the end-to-end pgx-facing path when it runs on the AGE arm (schema_any_property, nullable ANY VALUE column arriving null returns a nil *any without error), but there is no durable, containerised measurement of the raw pgx-side null shape as its own witness.
