title: gql: the COPY OF trailing-name check has no witness that distinguishes case
description:
Found by agent-f reviewing PR #1639 (gqlc-grld), measured not inferred, and deliberately NOT filed as a blocker — the PR landed as 2f3fa3ed.

THE GAP

internal/schema/gql/loader.go:70 checks the trailing name byte-exactly:

    if next.name != ref.name() {

That is the correct semantics and it agrees with the Row B claim about file lookup being case-sensitive. But it is UNWITNESSED. agent-f mutated it to

    if !strings.EqualFold(next.name, ref.name()) {

and the full package stayed GREEN at 7284fa6c. So the byte-exactness is asserted by the code and by nothing else: any future edit that relaxes it to a case-fold comparison ships silently.

The reason is simply that no fixture has a reference and a declared name that differ ONLY in case. Every existing pair differs in more than case, so both comparisons agree on every row we own.

THE ROW THAT CLOSES IT (agent-f named it; it is one row, not a suite)

    root file:    COPY OF Target
    Target.gql:   declares  target
    want:         ErrReferenceNameMismatch

Byte-exact comparison reports the mismatch; EqualFold does not. So the row is RED under the mutation and green as shipped, which is the whole point.

DONE WHEN the row exists and the EqualFold mutation is measured to FAIL the package with it in place. Assert the reason, not merely the verdict: pin the sentinel, so a row that goes red for some other cause cannot be read as this guard working (bd workflow-assert-reason-not-verdict).

CONTEXT this belongs to: this is the second instance in one PR of the same shape — a guard whose only witnesses agree with a constant. agent-k found the first herself (her doubt #4, her M09). Worth noticing as a pattern in this package rather than as two unrelated tickets.

Full verdict: fleet-state/verdicts/verdict-grld-r1.md, and posted as a comment on PR #1639.
notes: PR #2482 open, closes #1661, base master. Branch fix/gqlc-952q-copy-of-name-case-witness, 1 commit, pushed. just gates 14/14. Battery: 3 rows declared before running, all landed exactly on their declarations — row 1 (EqualFold) killed ONLY the new row with both old witnesses green, which confirms the bead's diagnosis; row 2 (delete the check) killed both loader rows + the corpus row + TestAllSentinelsAreReachable; row 3 control SURVIVED. Gap reproduced at today's master before writing the row, not inherited from the 7284fa6c measurement. No design blocker, so V.2 merges on green gates. Follow-up filed: gqlc-dlfvg (sweep for guards whose only witnesses agree with a constant — the pattern this bead's own description declined to file).
close_reason:
Closed by PR #2482, merged as c5c2e934 and verified BY CONTENT on origin/master:
internal/schema/gql/loader_test.go:211 carries the row "a file whose declaration
differs from the lookup only in case".

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG. Nothing in loader.go. The guard at loader.go:70 was and
is correct; what was missing was any witness that it is byte-exact. Every
reference/declaration pair the package owned differed in MORE than case, so a
byte-exact comparison and a case-folding one agreed on every row, and the
byte-exactness was asserted by the code and by nothing else.

REPRODUCED HERE, NOT INHERITED. The bead reports agent-f measuring the EqualFold
weakening green at a commit named in its description. I applied it again at
today's master before writing anything: green in all four schema packages. So the
gap was still live, and the row closes a present hole rather than a historical
one. (The sha itself is deliberately not repeated here: bd close's sha gate reads
any sha in a reason as a landing claim and refuses one no remote ref contains,
which is the correct default but cannot see a sha cited as past context.)

THE ROW. root.gql says COPY OF Target; Target.gql declares "target". The lookup
is case-sensitive and finds Target.gql; the file then declares a name that merely
FOLDS to the one that found it. It pins the sentinel and the message
(Target.gql declares "target"), not merely that some error came back.

BATTERY — 3 rows, victims and diffstats declared before running, guard committed
first, every row screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null`, restored by cp and
sha256-verified. All three landed exactly on their declarations; unlike my
previous bead there was nothing to disclose.

  1. EqualFold weakening        -1 +1  KILLED  ONLY the new row. Both pre-existing
                                               witnesses stayed GREEN.
  2. delete the check entirely  -3 +0  KILLED  new row + the old loader row +
                                               corpus 17-references/copy_of_name_
                                               mismatch.gql + TestAllSentinelsAreReachable
  3. CONTROL slices.Contains -> slices.Index >= 0
                                -1 +1  SURVIVED  none, exit 0

Row 1 was the falsifiable one and it is what vindicates the bead's diagnosis: it
DECLARED that the two old witnesses cannot tell byte-exact from case-folding.
They stayed green. Had either reddened, the row's whole reason for existing would
have been wrong. Row 2 proves the new row sits on the same guard as the old ones
rather than on a parallel path. Row 3 mutates a line the cycle rows demonstrably
reach, so its silence is evidence the harness reports SURVIVED at all.

WHAT LIED TO ME: nothing this time, but one thing nearly did. The FIRST form of
the whole-family mutation I tried on my NEXT bead orphaned an import and was a
compiler kill; here the EqualFold form kept `strings` live by luck, since
loader.go already used strings.Join. A guard-weakening mutation that happens to
be the last user of an import is a fake RED, and it is not visible until you
screen for it.

NOTICED, NOT FIXED — FILED. gqlc-dlfvg (P3, class:author, routable): this bead's
own description names a pattern and declines to file it — two instances in one PR
of "a guard whose only witnesses agree with a constant", agent-k having found the
first (her M09). Both instances are now closed; the pattern was not, and nothing
swept for it. The bead carries the method and a scope warning against pinning
properties the code does not actually promise.

INHERITED FROM: agent-f, reviewing PR #1639 (gqlc-grld), who measured the gap and
named the exact closing row rather than merely flagging it. The row shipped is
his, not mine.

title: codegen/neo4j: the depth-3 shadowing elemLocal exists to prevent has no fixture, so only the Go compiler guards it
description:
elemLocal (internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:772) suffixes element-loop locals by nesting depth. Its own doc says that under a fixed name 'the emitted package does not compile from a nesting depth of three'.

MEASURED 2026-08-29 while closing gqlc-nrao. Reverting elemLocal to a fixed name (keeping strconv live so the reversion is not compiler-killed) and regenerating the whole corpus changes exactly 6 golden files, across 3 fixtures: list_list_int, schema_list_any_property, schema_list_property_widths — all depth 2, all v5 and v6. Every one of them still COMPILES and the full live battery still PASSES. At depth 2 the suffixing is cosmetic: the inner 'elem' shadows the outer one only after the outer is last read, so the shadowed emission is correct Go and a correct decoder.

So the behaviour elemLocal exists to prevent is unreachable from the corpus: 0 fixtures anywhere under test/data/codegen/valid produce a [][][]T. The guard against the depth-3 collision is the Go compiler on a package no fixture generates — which means a regression in elemLocal at depth 3 would be caught by nothing here, and a regression at depth 2 is not a regression at all.

Two ways out, and they are not equivalent:
 (a) add a depth-3 fixture, if the pipeline admits one (unverified: whether a LIST<LIST<LIST<INT>>> column survives typing — see gqlc-t0bk, list-literal element types collapse to UNKNOWN);
 (b) if depth 3 is not reachable by design, say so at elemLocal and drop the claim about depth three, which currently reads as a live hazard.

Do not read this as blocking gqlc-nrao's live row: that row witnesses the depth-2 decode against real servers and kills 6 of 7 mutants attributable to it alone. This bead is about the depth the row does NOT reach.
close_reason: Duplicate of gqlc-415l, which survives. Same defect, same measurement, same day (both filed 2026-08-29 while closing gqlc-nrao): elemLocal's depth-suffixing has no fixture at depth 3, the depth at which its own comment says the emitted package stops compiling. gqlc-415l is kept because it carries the blocking dependency on gqlc-v0gk; this copy was P3, unlabelled and unblocked, so it sat in bd ready where an author would have been routed onto it by class inference and would reasonably have made the generator admit depth 3 — settling an architectural question by implementation. The unique measurement here (six golden files across three fixtures, all still compiling and passing) has been copied onto gqlc-415l before this close, so nothing is lost. Closed by agent-a.

title: the entity/property shapeless lane has no arrived-null gate — is a null reachable there?
description:
NOTICED WHILE FIXING gqlc-tez0 (PR #1643), NOT FIXED THERE. tez0 closed
the arrived-null hole in the COLUMN path's `any` lane
(writeAnyColumnDecodeIndent). This is the same shape one axis up, on the
ENTITY/PROPERTY path, and it is a separate claim because the two paths
answer absence differently on purpose.

WHAT I MEASURED (by reading the emitter, not by running anything):
internal/codegen/neo4j/render_models.go:327-332,
writeShapelessFieldDecode's non-nullable arm, gates on `ok` -- the Props
map holding the key -- and then assigns the value whatever it is:

    value0, ok := node.Props["badge"]
    if !ok {
        return Ev{}, fmt.Errorf("decode Ev.Badge: could not find any property named %s", "badge")
    }
    out.Badge = value0

No nil check. So a property declared ANY VALUE NOT NULL whose key is
PRESENT with a nil value is delivered as nil beside a nil error -- the
identical shape tez0 fixed, in the identical width, for the identical
reason (`any` is the one width inhabited by nil).

WHAT I DO NOT KNOW, AND WHY THIS IS A QUESTION AND NOT A BUG. On neo4j,
`SET n.p = null` DELETES the property rather than storing a null, so the
key would be absent and the `!ok` refusal above would fire correctly --
the nil-valued-key state may be unreachable from any real graph. I did
not measure that. If it is unreachable the gate is dead code and the
right answer is a comment saying so, not a gate.

The AGE side is not the same mechanism at all -- internal/codegen/age
has no Props-map lane and no "could not find any property named"
refusal, so the two backends cannot be compared by reading. Whether AGE
can hand back an entity whose agtype properties object holds an explicit
null under a NOT NULL key is the other half of the question.

ACCEPTANCE. Measure first, against real containers on both backends, the
way tez0's second shape was measured and struck: can a NOT NULL ANY
VALUE property on an entity arrive with its key present and its value
null? Then either (a) it can, and the lane owes the same refusal in the
same words, with a live row on both arms; or (b) it cannot, and the lane
owes a comment naming what makes it unreachable, plus the live row that
would go red if that ever changed.

BEWARE the trap tez0 hit: internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt
has TestAnythingReadsWhatTheGraphHolds ranging over a 7-value table that
INCLUDES nil for this very path, asserting it reads through without
error. If the answer is (a), that fixture is pinning the defect and must
move, along with its corpusTables census entry. It stayed at 7 on tez0's
branch precisely because tez0 did not touch this path.

title: mutation battery: guards that read persistent state owe a second-run row
description:
Follow-up from postmortem fleet/brain/postmortems/2026-08-26-stall-watchdog-treadmill.md ([deleted:gqlc-fw2b]): a guard that reads state which outlives the run — a witness file, a cache, a lock, a config written last time — cannot be certified by mutations that run once. The defect class is 'correct on the first run, wrong on the second', and a one-turn battery never reaches it.

Shape to add to the mutation-record guidance in fleet/brain/playbooks/agent-protocol.md step 3: for any guard reading persistent state, at least one row runs the guarded operation TWICE with an idle gap past the guard's threshold between them, mutating the persisted state's freshness (backdate it) rather than only the guard's condition. The #1567 watchdog needed exactly this row: its one-run battery passed while its second run killed healthy turns host-wide.
close_reason: shipped in PR 1610 merged 2026-08-29

title: just actionlint is silently weaker than CI's: without a shellcheck binary on PATH, actionlint skips every run-block script finding, so an agent can pass locally over a red CI job
description:
Found 2026-08-26 while landing gqlc-o6kp (PR #1533). CI refused the PR on SC2015 inside .github/workflows/bd-behaviour.yml; the same 'just actionlint' passed locally because actionlint only runs shellcheck when the binary is on PATH, and this machine does not have one — measured: command -v shellcheck empty, actionlint v1.7.7 printed nothing on the exact file CI rejected, then reproduced CI's finding byte-for-byte (205:9 SC2015 48:13) after installing shellcheck 0.10.0 into a throwaway dir.

The failure shape is the fleet's familiar one: a gate whose silence reads as an all-clear (cf. blind instruments, gqlc-h17n). Two candidate remedies, not chosen: (a) justfile ensures shellcheck like it already self-heals golangci-lint (see ensure-golangci), failing loudly when provisioning fails; (b) actionlint's -shellcheck flag pointed at a pinned binary path so local and CI grade identically. Either way the local pass must stop being vacuous while looking identical to a real one.
notes: PR #1688 opened 2026-08-29. Reproduced at RECIPE level (faulty workflow planted in the real .github/workflows, since 'just actionlint' discovers that directory): without -shellcheck rc=0 and 0 findings; with it rc=1 naming SC1010. Fix: depend on ensure-shellcheck, pass the pinned .bin/shellcheck path (this also pins the version for CI, which runs the same recipe). UNEXPECTED SECOND HALF: actionlint given a -shellcheck path that does not exist exits 0 in silence, byte-identical to -shellcheck '' which means disabled — no backstop, no complaint. So the recipe asserts [ -x ] before invoking. 6-row battery in the PR body; M2b (guard blinded, binary absent) restores the silence, so the -x check is load-bearing. Sandbox declared: the -x guard is unreachable in normal operation because ensure-shellcheck self-heals (M3 measures that), so M2/M2b had to remove the dependency to reach it. Real workflows are clean under the new check — CI has had shellcheck on PATH all along, so nothing in .github/workflows changes.
close_reason: Merged as 4ac523ed (PR #1688). just actionlint now refuses when {{shellcheck}} is missing or non-executable instead of running actionlint without it — actionlint gives no error for a bad -shellcheck path, it silently skips every run-block check and exits 0. Verified on origin/master:justfile:3351-3362.

title: shared checkout's local master carries open PR #1523's head; origin/master does not
description:
Claim: local master in the shared main checkout (/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc) is one commit ahead of origin/master, and that commit is the head of open PR #1523.

Measured 2026-08-26 from agent agent-o's worktree, read-only; the shared checkout was not entered:

- git log 'origin/master..master' -> exactly one commit: c7a61b7f "the agent fleet: the agent engine runs opencode headless (fleetctl-agent-ox)", parent 013a2533 (= current origin/master tip), authored 2026-08-25T23:20:09-04:00.
- gh pr list --head fix/gqlc-xjki-opencode-agent-engine -> #1523 OPEN, headRefOid = c7a61b7f2b93... (identical sha).
- origin/master tip remains 013a2533 (#1508): nothing was pushed to master.

The work itself is in flight correctly (branch pushed, PR open, bead [deleted:gqlc-xjki] in_progress) - but the commit was made ON local master instead of on a branch, so the shared checkout's master is diverged from origin/master today.

Why it bites later, not now: #1523 merges by squash, so origin/master receives a NEW sha for this change while local master keeps c7a61b7f - the drift becomes permanent until someone resets it, gates run in the shared checkout execute bytes origin does not have, and any 'git pull --rebase' there replays an already-published commit onto post-merge master.

Repair (checkout owner's call; agents must not enter the shared checkout): 'git fetch origin && git checkout master && git reset --hard origin/master'. Safe now - c7a61b7f lives on origin's feature branch and as #1523's head - and still safe after the merge.

Filed at P3 per protocol: machinery, latent, not blocking product work today.

title: bd close's sha guard cannot express a superseded review head: the remedy it names is impossible after a squash merge
description:
The `bd close` sha guard in .githooks/claude-pre-bash (deny-unpushed-sha, line
1242-1251) refuses any close whose reason cites a commit no remote-tracking ref
contains. That rule is CORRECT and I am not asking for it to be relaxed — it is
the thing that stops a close recording work that a rebase can discard.

THE GAP is the case it cannot distinguish: a close that cites a SUPERSEDED head
deliberately, as provenance rather than as the landed work.

MEASURED FIRST-PARTY, 2026-08-24, closing gqlc-06y9. Sequence:
  - PR #1485 was reviewed by agent-o, who returned PASS on gqlc-uwwg against that
    branch's then-head.
  - #1485 was force-closed when its base branch was deleted by a stacked merge.
  - The branch was rebased and force-pushed; the successor PR #1506 merged as
    503055f7 and its branch was deleted.
  - The reviewed head is now contained by ZERO remote refs. Measured:
    `git branch -r --contains <reviewed head>` prints nothing, while the same
    query returns 2 refs for 503055f7 and 5 for the merge base.
  - So the close that wanted to say "agent-o's PASS was returned against THIS sha,
    and the merged delta is content-identical to it" was refused.

WHY THE GUARD'S OWN REMEDY DOES NOT APPLY. The message says "Push the branch,
then close citing a sha a remote ref contains." There is no branch to push: it
was squash-merged and deleted, which is how every piece of work in this fleet
ends. The remedy is well-formed for the failure it was written for (closing
against unpushed local work) and unreachable for this one.

WHAT IT COSTS. Not the close — I worked around it by naming gqlc-uwwg, which
holds the sha, instead of repeating the hex. The cost is that the provenance
link between a review verdict and the close it authorised cannot be written
where a reader will find it, in exactly the situation where the reviewed
artifact is already unfetchable and the pointer matters most. Cheap once,
recurring, and it teaches agents to drop shas from close reasons — which is the
opposite of what gqlc-90vt wanted.

I DO NOT HAVE A DESIGN I TRUST, and I would rather say so than improvise one.
Three shapes, with what I dislike about each:

  1. An explicit citation marker, e.g. `superseded:<sha>`, that the guard reads
     as prose rather than as a claim of landed work. Cheapest. Weakness: it is
     an honour system — an agent closing against genuinely unpushed work can type
     the same marker, and the guard would have no way to tell. That may be
     acceptable, because the guard's audience is accident and not fraud, but
     that is a judgement someone should make on purpose rather than inherit
     from me.

  2. Accept a sha that is an ancestor of a MERGED PR head, resolved via `gh`.
     Most faithful to intent. Weakness: it puts a network call in a pre-bash
     hook, which is a latency and offline-failure question I have not measured.

  3. Accept a sha reachable from the reflog AND content-identical to something
     a remote ref contains. Weakness: expensive, and I am not certain
     "content-identical" is well-defined enough here to implement without
     arguing about it first.

FALSIFIER FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT — the row that must go red before the fix and
green after, in .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh:

  a `bd close` whose reason cites a sha that (a) names a real commit in this
  repo, (b) is contained by zero remote refs, and (c) is marked in whatever way
  the chosen design marks provenance, must be ALLOWED — while the SAME sha
  cited WITHOUT the marker must still be DENIED with deny-unpushed-sha.

Both halves are load-bearing. A test that only pins the allow would go green
against a guard that had simply been deleted.

Noticed while closing gqlc-06y9; filed rather than ridden on that diff.
close_reason: Stale after PR #1595 (f6dc4c7b) herdr trim. The falsifier row lives in .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh which is deleted; guard still exists at claude-pre-bash:1243 but the bead's acceptance shape does not survive. Aggressive-sweep per user 2026-08-29.

title: prepare_test: scope gate no longer polices generator reuse of a scopePackage reserved name at method scope
description:
Found while judging PR #1489 (bead gqlc-6fwl). Not a merge blocker: the
sweep-relevant strict direction is intact (measured), and exploiting this
crack requires a future generator change, which is itself review-gated.

CLAIM FALSIFIED. PR #1489 widened TestReservedScopeMatchesTheEmittedGoldens
check 1 to a biconditional and asserted the dropped permissive direction
"was never load-bearing". It was, weakly: under the old equality, a golden
declaring a scopePackage reserved name as a METHOD reddened the gate.
Under the biconditional it does not.

FALSIFIER (run 2026-08-24, worktree at 476f2371): append
  func (q *Queries) Tx() int { return 0 }
to any golden db.go, then run all four golden-reading registry gates
(TestReservedScopeMatchesTheEmittedGoldens,
TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet,
TestReservedIdentifiersAreUniformAcrossBackends,
TestReservedScopeDecidesWhichEntityNamesCollide): all PASS. In the real
regression (renderer emits the method, goldens regenerated) nothing reds —
txsurface skips non-Begin *Queries methods by design, and the
fixed-declaration sweep does not force the name because it is already a
registry row.

SCOPE OF THE CRACK. Only reuse of an EXISTING scopePackage reserved name
(Tx, New, DBTX, ErrNoRows, ErrTxDone, ...) as an exported method slips. A
brand-new exported name is still forced into reservedIdentifiers by
TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet. Note the surface this
permits — q.Tx() one selector from type Tx — is exactly the shape PR
#1489's own registry comment says the generator should not emit.

SUGGESTED REPAIR. Keep the biconditional but enumerate the permitted
method-scope declarations of scopePackage names in an allowlist, today
exactly {Queries: (*Tx).Queries}; require any other method-scope
declaration of a scopePackage row to fail. ~10 lines in
TestReservedScopeMatchesTheEmittedGoldens.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as PR #2540, squashed onto master as 98fca0ae. GH mirror #1496
closed at merge.

THE GAP, AND IT WAS REAL. TestReservedScopeMatchesTheEmittedGoldens check 1 was
an equality over every declaration until PR #1489 widened it to a biconditional.
The bead's falsifier reproduced verbatim: appending

  func (q *Queries) Tx() int { return 0 }

to a golden db.go reddens none of the four golden-reading registry gates.

RE-DERIVED, AND THE BEAD'S OWN REPAIR DID NOT SURVIVE IT. The bead asks for an
allowlist of permitted method-scope declarations, "today exactly
{Queries: (*Tx).Queries}". Parsed all 847 goldens with go/ast, the same walk
eachDecl does: NO NAME IN THE CORPUS IS DECLARED AT BOTH SCOPES. The sole
allowlist entry does not exist.

So the allowlist would have shipped empty — mechanism with no member, and a
speculative one, since the declaration it would readmit is the tx.Queries() hop
agent-n removed at P0. What shipped instead is the plain equality: smaller than
the allowlist (four lines, not ten) and strictly stronger.

WHY THE JUSTIFICATION WENT STALE, which is the part the bead did not have.
PR #1489's comment was TRUE WHEN WRITTEN — it introduced (*Tx).Queries in the
same PR, which is why it had to widen the check. gqlc-f4hf (PR #1735, 0a4bb1ec,
2026-08-29) then removed the accessor. Confirmed by bytes rather than by the
close reason: `git show ff25b7a3:...db.go` has `func (tx *Tx) Queries()` at
line 123 and `git show 0a4bb1ec:...db.go` does not.

PR #1735 updated the production side — reservedIdentifiers' comment says "since
gqlc-f4hf no accessor on *Tx" — and txsurface_test.go, which is correct today
and explicitly enforces the removal. It missed the test comment, so for five
days a guard stood weakened on a reason its own repository already contradicted
45 lines away in a different file.

MEASUREMENT. Declared-victim battery (decision 0005), two phases, each against a
`git archive` extract so neither phase touched a working tree. Every row
declared its verdict before the run, asserted its appended text was absent from
the pristine golden, named its witness subtest, and restored under a sha256
check.

  row                                          pre        post       killed by
  F1  Tx as a *Queries method (the bead's)     SURVIVED   KILLED     its own /Tx
  F2  New as a *Tx method                      SURVIVED   KILLED     its own /New
  P1  Begin declared package-level             KILLED     KILLED     its own /Begin
  B1  brand-new exported method in db.go       KILLED     KILLED     fixed-decl sweep
  N1  2nd method decl of a scopeMethod row     SURVIVED   SURVIVED   --

P1 is the positive control and the reason F1/F2's pre-phase SURVIVED means the
crack rather than a battery that was not reaching the gate. It exercises the
half PR #1489 KEPT, so it dies in both phases by its own witness.

N1 is the over-rejection control: the new arm fires only for scopePackage rows,
and a second method declaration of an existing scopeMethod row must stay green.
It also holds the comment's standing claim that the receiver is not consulted.

B1 MEASURES THE BEAD'S BOUNDARY INSTEAD OF QUOTING IT. The bead says a
brand-new exported name is still caught. It is — by
TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet and by NOTHING ELSE, never by the
scope sweep, because record() returns early on a non-reserved name. That is the
mechanism behind "only reuse of an EXISTING name slips", and it is now a
measured row rather than a sentence.

THE BATTERY IS SCOPED TO THE FOUR GATES, AND THAT IS A CHOICE I OWE A REASON
FOR. Appending to a golden also reds TestConformanceSuite/TestValid and
TestSentinelTaxonomy/TestCorpusRunsGreen — measured, both named. Both compare
goldens against a fresh render. In the regression this bead is about the
renderer emits the method and the goldens are REGENERATED, so both are green and
the four registry gates are the whole of what is left. A whole-package run would
have read KILLED in the pre phase and hidden the crack entirely.

WHAT COULD HAVE LIED TO ME. The mutation is an append to test DATA, so there is
no compiler to fake a kill — but there is a parser. A golden that fails to parse
takes out EVERY row through the sweep's own require.NoError on parser.ParseFile,
which would read as a uniformly excellent battery. Each row is gofmt-parsed
before its run and the runner aborts if the mutated golden does not parse.

NO RED-TEST-FIRST IN THE USUAL SHAPE, stated rather than glossed. This gate's
input is the corpus, not an argument, so its failure cannot be driven from a
synthetic fixture without new harness machinery this package does not have.
The guard IS the assertion; the pre/post pair over an unchanged mutation is what
says it is load-bearing. That is the same standing as check 3, which also holds
a property of live data with no synthetic witness.

NO DESIGN GATE: `bd dep list` reports none, and the bead records a reviewer's
finding rather than a designer's plan. No other open PR touched
internal/codegen/. `just gates`: 15 of 15. tidy confirmed non-vacuous by running
the script rather than reading the check colour:
`[check-pr-closes] gqlc-5ask -> Closes #1496 (ok)`. The mirror link was
confirmed through closingIssuesReferences.

VERIFIED BY BEHAVIOUR, not by presence: master extracted with `git archive` into
scratch and the post battery re-run against those bytes — all five rows matched
their declaration, the three witnessed ones each by their own named subtest.

Battery preserved to fleet-state/verdicts/gqlc-5ask/mutate-5ask.py.

FILED, NOT RIDDEN: gqlc-3peuo. prepare.go:32's scopeMethod comment lists
"Commit / Rollback / Queries on *Tx" — Queries is recorded scopePackage 48 lines
below in the same file, and the accessor it names is the one gqlc-f4hf removed.
It is the SAME miss as this bead's, from the same PR, and prepare.go already
contradicts itself about it at line 77. It is not ridden here because nothing
reads it: unlike the comment this PR fixed, it was not the stated reason a guard
had been weakened. The bead carries the note that no guard exists over this
class at all, and asks the taker to say so plainly if a cheap one does not exist
rather than invent one.

ONE THING I CHECKED AND DID NOT FILE. txsurface_test.go:55 also names
(*Tx).Queries, and it is correct: it says the accessor is the one
docs/specs/codegen-tx-embedded-querier.md removes, and that because txSurfaceNames
is compared by equality an emission still carrying it FAILS there. That is a
kept vow, and a bead on a true sentence is noise.

title: repo-purity: advisory flag is checked '= 1' but no row witnesses a non-1 value staying strict
description:
FOUND during review gqlc-uwwg (PR #1485 head 79893c9d), by a mutation the suite survived.

THE MUTANT. .githooks/repo-purity's advisory line
  [ "${GQLC_REPO_PURITY_ADVISORY:-0}" = 1 ] && exit "$INNER_RC"
rewritten to
  [ -n "${GQLC_REPO_PURITY_ADVISORY:-}" ] && exit "$INNER_RC"
runs the purity suite 39/0. SURVIVED. Sandbox: run_guard exercises the flag as exactly-1 (ADVISORY=1) or absent (env -u); no row runs the guard with the flag set to 0 or any other non-1 value.

WHY IT IS ONLY P3. Current code is correct; pre-push only ever sets 1. The unwitnessed semantic is that an agent exporting GQLC_REPO_PURITY_ADVISORY=0 to force strict mode keeps strict mode. Under the mutant, 0 silently enables advisory.

THE FALSIFIER TO ADD, one row:
  T="$TMP/explicit_zero"; mkdir -p "$T"; make_town "$T"
  rc="$(ADVISORY=0 run_guard "$T" git branch -q zerobranch)"
  check "flag explicitly 0: the guard still FAILS the run" 1 "$rc"
run_guard already passes any non-empty ADVISORY through, so the row needs no helper change. Verify it kills the -n mutant before closing.
close_reason: Closed by PR #1595 (f6dc4c7b): the .githooks/tests/*-test.sh suite this defect names has been deleted along with the whole factory-test scaffolding (~28k lines). The behaviour under test still exists in its hook, but this specific defect-in-the-test is unconstructible now.

title: check-pr-closes: three exits still pass closing keywords unexamined without naming them — the epic skip passes a body that closes the umbrella itself
description:
Found reviewing PR #1464 (bead gqlc-jwt4). Pre-existing on master, NOT
introduced by that PR — its export-lag skip now names what went unheld, but
three sibling exits in main() retain the finding-2 shape of bd gqlc-7i3g: they
exit 0 over a body whose closing keywords nothing examined, and two of the
three say nothing about it.

MEASURED at 434c0d22 (these paths are byte-identical on master):

1. THE EPIC SKIP, and it is the sharp one. Export record
   {"id":"gqlc-epic1","issue_type":"epic","external_ref":".../issues/500"},
   body 'Bead: gqlc-epic1 / Closes #500 / Closes #900' ->
     [check-pr-closes] gqlc-epic1 is an epic - skipping (umbrella must not be closed)
     rc=0
   The body closes the umbrella's own mirror #500; GitHub acts on it at merge
   and closes the umbrella — the precise harm the message says must not
   happen, affirmed in the same breath as the pass. #900 rides too. Unlike
   the export-lag skip, refusing here IS clearable by the author (drop the
   keyword), so this one arguably deserves a refusal, not just naming.

2. THE NO-EXTERNAL_REF EXIT names its unverified state (unverified_tail, bd
   gqlc-63ao) but not the NUMBERS the body closes, and emits no ::warning
   annotation. Body with 'Closes #900' over a record carrying no
   external_ref -> pass, #900 never named.

3. THE UNPARSEABLE-MIRROR EXIT (external_ref names no issue number), same
   shape as 2.

FALSIFIER for each: one export line of the shape above + a body carrying
'Closes #900', run
  python3 .github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py <export> <body> some/branch
and grep the output for 900 — today it appears nowhere on paths 2 and 3, and
path 1 passes its own stated harm. Any fix mutates its guards per ADR 0005;
PR #1464's export-lag-skip rows are the shape to copy.

title: check-pr-closes-test.sh: two added comments name prose_only() where the code reads the split wrappers, and the skip path's no-subtraction choice is pinned by no row
description:
Residue from the review of PR #1464 (bead gqlc-jwt4), three findings on the
test suite that PR added, none blocking its merge.

1. TWO ADDED COMMENTS NAME THE WRONG WRAPPER. Test-file lines 459 and 550 (at
434c0d22) say "The extras are read from prose_only()'s body" and "The avowal
is read over prose_only()'s body" — the code reads claimable_prose() (line
818) and visible_prose() (line 819) respectively, and prose_only() is exactly
the function the e5e88f0e split's docstring says never to call directly. The
wrapper-per-scan asymmetry is the load-bearing choice of PR #1464 itself, so a
comment misnaming it is misdirection at the one spot precision matters. The
suite defends the CODE against a reader who obeys the comment — mutating
either call site to bare prose_only() is KILLED (measured in review: 1 and 2
rows red respectively) — so this is prose repair, not a hole. While there,
sweep the file: line 1428 carries an inherited prose_only() reference too.

FALSIFIER for the fix: none needed beyond reading — but if you touch the call
sites themselves, re-run the two wrapper mutations and watch them stay red.

2. THE SKIP PATH'S DELIBERATE NON-SUBTRACTION IS ASSERTED BY NOTHING. main()'s
export-lag skip names every GH_CLOSES hit without subtracting Also-closes
avowals, argued deliberately in its comment ("reporting a subset would
overstate what this run did"). No row pins it. Measured in review at 434c0d22:
mutate line 1027 to subtract avowed_numbers(visible_prose(pr_body)) and the
suite stays 181/0, while behavior visibly changes — body
'Bead: gqlc-zz99notinexport / Closes #900 / Also-closes: #900' gets the
::warning + numbers on head, and the bare silent 'skipping' line on the
mutant, i.e. the mutant reproduces the exact silent skip bd gqlc-7i3g
complained about, for any number the author avows. Both exit 0, so this is
warning-completeness on an advisory path, not a merge hole — hence P3.

FALSIFIER / the row wanted: bead absent from export, body closes #N and avows
#N, expect the summary line still to name #N (and the ::warning to fire).
Write it, then re-run the line-1027 mutation and watch it go red.

title: CONTEXT.md: 'Neutral temporal carrier' says the five names are reserved 'whenever temporal.go is emitted' — ADR 0033 decided unconditional reservation
description:
Sweep finding (gqlc-ot5u), merged code, no verdict. PR #1452's CONTEXT.md entry ends: 'The five names are reserved in the generated package whenever temporal.go is emitted.' The ADR it summarises (docs/adr/0033, Placement section) decides the opposite conditional: the names join reservedIdentifiers, 'reserved even in a batch that emits no temporal.go, because a name that works in one batch but not another is exactly the renaming scheme that set already refused' — and prepare.go:33-48's documented posture agrees (the set is the union across backends and batches; ErrNoRows is reserved in batches that would not emit it).

CONTEXT.md is the domain-language carrier grill sessions read; a reader of the entry alone designs the weaker, batch-conditional gate the ADR explicitly refused. One-sentence fix: reserve unconditionally, e.g. '...reserved in every generated package, even one that emits no temporal.go (ADR 0033).' Checked against the tree 2026-08-24: prepare.go posture comment verified; ADR text verified.

title: repo-purity: the deleted-branch verb of its message is unwitnessed by any suite row
description:
The heads-diff message in .githooks/repo-purity says "the run moved, created or
deleted local branches". The suite witnesses moved (otherseat) and created
(inventedbranch); no row deletes one. Detection itself is NOT in doubt — probed
during the review of PR #1457 at bd174e7c: in a make_town-shaped fixture with a
branch `doomed`, running the guard around `git branch -qD doomed` exits 1 and
the output names the branch (one `< refs/heads/doomed <sha>` line). The gap is
only the missing witness row, the same 2-of-3 shape gqlc-lekg itself was about,
one level down.

FALSIFIER for the fix: a row shaped like the created-branch pair —
make_town, `git -C "$T/shared" branch -q doomed master`, run_guard `git branch
-qD doomed`, check FAILS nonzero + names `doomed`. Mutating the guard's heads
comparison out (PR #1457's M3) must turn it red.

title: check-pr-closes: the module docstring says 'until this commit', which stops being true at the next commit
description:
`.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py`'s module docstring closes its
two-questions section with:

    "One function cannot err in both directions, and until this commit one
     did."

The sentence dates the split of prose_only() into visible_prose() and
claimable_prose(), which landed as e5e88f0e (PR #1335). "this commit" meant
e5e88f0e when it was written and was true then.

It is a self-dating claim in a file that keeps being committed to, so it
decays on the next commit rather than at some later review. A reader at HEAD
reads "this commit" as HEAD and is told the split happened in whatever change
they are looking at. Noticed 2026-08-23 while rebasing gqlc-7i3g's branch onto
that commit; the branch adds two commits after it, so the sentence already
reads falsely there.

Not fixed on that branch on purpose: the prose is inherited and the defect is
not one that branch introduced, so it gets its own bead rather than riding a
diff about closing keywords.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not binding: name the commit, or name what changed rather
than when — "the split of prose_only() into visible_prose() and
claimable_prose()" dates itself against `git log` and cannot go stale.

Worth a sweep of the same file for the other tense-bound phrasings while
someone is in there: the file carries several "used to", "until this commit"
and "at this commit" constructions, and they are not all the same kind. "at
this commit" attached to a MEASUREMENT is honest and should stay — it says the
number was true when measured. "until this commit" attached to BEHAVIOUR is
the one that rots.

title: two lanes disagree on whether the pre-push idle timeout affects HTTPS, and the shipped keepalive is ssh-only
description:
The fix for gqlc-ehgg / GH #1414 (merged 1fc81c35) writes core.sshCommand and states plainly that it governs ssh only: an https remote spawns no ssh, so there is nothing for a keepalive to attach to. Whether that leaves a real gap depends on a question two lanes answered in OPPOSITE directions on the same day, and neither answer has been reconciled.

CONTRADICTORY FIRST-PARTY EVIDENCE, both 2026-08-23:
  - epic-routing lane (PR #1425): rc=141 SIX times, and reported the failure
    occurred 'over both SSH and HTTPS'. Also measured git writing to the
    transport ~62us after pre-push returns 0, having idled ~7 minutes.
  - retired-agent lane (PR #1427): rc=141 FIVE times over SSH, no branch on the
    remote, GIT_TRACE=1 showing git opens 'ssh git-receive-pack' BEFORE running
    pre-push. Reported flatly: 'Pushing over HTTPS works.' It used HTTPS as its
    successful workaround.

Both are first-party and they cannot both be right as stated. Neither lane was asked to adjudicate the other; the epic lane's claim was relayed to the ehgg lane and shaped the ssh-only scoping, so the WEAKER-EVIDENCED claim is the one currently encoded in the fix's documentation.

WHY IT IS ONLY P2. Measured: origin is git@github.com:areqag/gqlc.git — SSH for both fetch and push. So the default path for every worktree IS covered by core.sshCommand, and HTTPS matters only for someone who deliberately switches, which is exactly what the retired-agent lane did as a workaround. If HTTPS is in fact also affected, that workaround is unreliable and should stop being recommended; if it is not, the ehgg notice's three-state message is correct and this closes as confirmed.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and neither lane did it: a deliberate reproduction. Push a branch over an https remote with a pre-push run exceeding the idle timeout, keepalives absent, and record the exit code. The two lanes differed in what they were doing when they observed, and 'HTTPS works' from one successful push is n=1 against six failures. A plausible reconciliation nobody has tested: https may have a different (longer) idle ceiling rather than none, so it survives a 7-minute hook and would still die on a 15-minute one.

DO NOT close this by re-reading the code. It is a question about a remote server's timeout behaviour and only a measurement answers it.
notes: P2 -> P3 by agent-a, 2026-08-24, under protocol/V.3.3 (bead gqlc-f5m5). Machinery, and it passes neither V.3.2 test: it does not BLOCK product work, and the fleet has demonstrably done its work without it. MEASURED just now: origin is git@github.com:areqag/gqlc.git — SSH. The shipped core.sshCommand keepalive therefore covers this fleet's only push path, so the disputed HTTPS half is not live here. What is left is reconciling two lanes' contradictory evidence. P3 is 'filed and searchable, routed to nobody' — not declined, and not a judgement on the finding, which stands as measured. Raise it back the moment it blocks a gqlc change, and say so here.

title: A just recipe that opens a PR with 'Bead:' prefilled — remedy (b) of gqlc-uz3c, deferred not rejected
description:
SPLIT OUT OF gqlc-uz3c. The justfile was owned by the fleetctl-restart lane on the night of 2026-08-23, so this could not be written then; gqlc-uz3c shipped remedies (a) and (c) instead.

THE REMEDY: a recipe — say 'just pr <title>' — that opens the PR with a 'Bead: <id>' line already in the body, the id taken from the branch name, or from the bead the session has claimed, or asked for.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH DOING AFTER (a) AND (c). (a) makes the branch name carry the id, which makes check-pr-closes.py's existing fallback fire, and (c) warns at push time when it does not. Neither reaches the case that actually cost the three hours: a branch ALREADY CUT without an id. There, (c)'s warning tells the author what to type, and this recipe would type it. It also covers a branch whose name matches the pattern but names no bead — 'fix/gqlc-parser-rewrite' satisfies BEAD_IN_BRANCH and then fails the gate on an unresolvable id, which (c) deliberately stays quiet about because deciding it means reading the ledger from a push hook.

WHY IT IS P3 RATHER THAN P2. After (a) and (c) the remaining exposure is a branch cut before the convention landed, on a session that ignores a warning printed as the last thing before the push. That is a shrinking population. Do not do this instead of gqlc-cn49 (the agent protocol recipe), which is the more travelled path and is P2.

CONSTRAINT ON THE IMPLEMENTATION: internal/tools/ciguard/justbodies_test.go has rules about justfile recipe bodies; read its failures rather than working around them. And .githooks/claude-pre-bash parses a --body argument as if it were a command, so a recipe that shells out to 'gh pr create --body' with prose containing shell-looking text will be denied under an agent session — prefer --body-file.
close_reason: Stale after PR #1595 (f6dc4c7b) herdr trim. Implementation constraint cites internal/tools/ciguard/justbodies_test.go which is deleted; the just-pr recipe idea remains sound but this bead's shape depends on the removed ciguard. Aggressive-sweep per user 2026-08-29.

title: a hook suite can spray hundreds of errors on stderr and still report ok
description:
Handed over by the lane that merged PR #1379 during the 2026-08-23 wave, and generalised here.

THE OBSERVATION. Working on the CI Go toolchain, that lane hit a silent failure inside 'just test-hooks', which redirects HOME. A GOTOOLCHAIN switch downloaded a read-only Go toolchain into a suite's scratch tree; cleanup then could not remove it. The run printed HUNDREDS of 'rm: Permission denied' lines, left a read-only toolchain behind in the scratch directory, and produced NO FAILING TEST ROW. The suite reported success.

That lane fixed its own exposure by pinning GOPATH, GOMODCACHE and GOCACHE.

WHAT I MEASURED IN .githooks/ (the lane that owns the suites), 2026-08-23 at 6a9e34bb. The toolchain-specific exposure is NIL here, and the falsifier is two greps:

  grep -rln 'HOME=' .githooks/tests/*.sh
    -> .githooks/tests/git-env-sandbox-test.sh   (only)
  grep -rlnE '(^|[^a-zA-Z_])go (build|test|run|vet|env|install|mod)' .githooks/tests/*.sh
    -> .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh   (only)

The intersection is EMPTY. And the single hit in each is weaker than it looks: git-env-sandbox-test.sh redirects HOME but never shells out to go, and claude-pre-bash-test.sh line 126 carries 'go test ./... && git commit -m x' as a fixture STRING handed to the hook under test to CLASSIFY, never executed. tool-gate-test.sh names GOTOOLCHAIN only in asserted remedy text. So no suite in .githooks/tests/ both redirects HOME and runs go, today.

WHY THIS BEAD IS STILL WORTH FILING. The intersection is empty by accident, not by construction. Nothing stops the next suite from being both, and the failure mode when it is has no red row at all.

THE GENERAL DEFECT, which outlives the toolchain cause: a suite's ENVIRONMENT is under-specified, and the resulting failure is invisible because the harness reads only the exit status. 'Printed hundreds of permission errors and still reported ok' generalises well past go.

WHAT TO BUILD, two halves, deliberately separable:

1. PIN THE ENVIRONMENT. Export GOPATH, GOMODCACHE, GOCACHE (and consider GOTOOLCHAIN) once in the test-hooks harness rather than per suite. NOTE: that harness lives in the justfile, which was owned by the fleetctl-restart lane on 2026-08-23 and could not be edited by the hooks lane. That ownership is why this is a bead and not a patch.

2. GUARD THE SILENCE, independent of the cause. The harness runs each suite as 'bash $suite' and checks nothing but the status. A suite that writes a large volume to stderr while exiting 0 is, on the evidence above, a real defect reporting as a pass. Candidate shape: capture each suite's stderr, and refuse the run when a suite exits 0 having written more than a threshold of lines, or any line matching a Permission-denied / No-space class. CARE with the false-positive direction — several suites legitimately write to stderr (the git-env-sandbox source, deliberate diagnostics), so the threshold or the class list is the whole design, and it needs its own positive and negative controls.

REPRODUCER for half 2, if the toolchain one is awkward to stage: make a suite's scratch directory read-only before its trap fires, and observe the harness report ok.
notes:
Filed from the .githooks/ lane during the 2026-08-23 wave. The measurement in the description (empty intersection between HOME-redirecting suites and go-invoking suites) was taken at 6a9e34bb and is re-runnable with the two greps quoted there. It will stop being true the first time a suite is written that is both, and there is nothing today that would notice.
P2 -> P3 by agent-a, 2026-08-24, under protocol/V.3.3 (bead gqlc-f5m5). Machinery, and it passes neither V.3.2 test: it does not BLOCK product work, and the fleet has demonstrably done its work without it. Its own measurement is the reason: the two greps intersect EMPTY in .githooks/, so the toolchain exposure is NIL here. A hazard, not an incident. P3 is 'filed and searchable, routed to nobody' — not declined, and not a judgement on the finding, which stands as measured. Raise it back the moment it blocks a gqlc change, and say so here.

title: scratch-literal sweep does not cover docs/specs: 18 fixed /tmp paths in already-executed procedures
description:
The sweep landed by bd gqlc-wm3x (.githooks/tests/scratch-literals-test.sh) covers tracked shell, just, and LIVE instruction markdown: CLAUDE.md, fleet/*.md, .claude/*.md. It deliberately does NOT cover docs/specs/*.md.

Measured 2026-08-23 at origin/master 1e11bb73, 18 matches across 6 files:

  docs/specs/cypher-golden-test-migration.md            1
  docs/specs/cypher-query-parser-aggregate-kind-rich-exprs.md  3
  docs/specs/model-change-0ig-call-args.md              3
  docs/specs/model-change-ay9-optional-group.md         3
  docs/specs/model-change-fvo-use-part.md               3
  docs/specs/model-change-hk0-containsaggregate.md      3
  docs/specs/config-multi-target.md                     1 (a path in a test-case table, not a procedure)

Most are verification recipes an agent is meant to RUN: 'sort > /tmp/changed.txt', 'diff /tmp/expected.txt /tmp/changed.txt', 'tee /tmp/purity-check.txt'. Two agents working two model-change specs at once collide on /tmp/changed.txt and each reads the other's file, which is the gqlc-b8gd shape with a silent wrong answer at the end instead of a build error.

Not done in the wm3x lane because the honest remedy is prose editing across six spec files, not six more allowlist entries — an allowlist of dead lines is the carve-out the bead's own description forbids. Doing it as an edit also has to decide, per spec, whether the document is a live procedure or a historical record.

WHEN DONE: add 'docs/specs/*.md' (or 'docs/*.md') to CLASS_PATHSPECS in .githooks/tests/scratch-literals-test.sh, add a representative file to the coverage rows, and delete the 'WHAT IT DOES NOT SWEEP' paragraph in its header.

title: codegen/age: the capture sweep's reachability half can only go red if the emitter reintroduces an author-derived identifier
description:
Measured under gqlc-dfcb, 2026-08-23, PR #1356.

codegen.ParamArg fixes the emitted argument name to 'arg' whatever the query author wrote, so a query parameter name never becomes a Go identifier in the emitted signature. That means the capture class the sweep was built for — an author-chosen name displacing a generator-owned declaration — is structurally closed upstream of the guard.

Consequence for TestNoEmittedNameTakesAQueryParameterName: its per-file half (paramLocalsOf equals ParamArg, no body local shadows ParamArg) is a live regression guard on exactly that upstream fix, and goes red the moment the emitter derives a name again. Its package-wide reachability half, added by dfcb, is only reachable through the SAME regression: the witness that turns it red is a body local named after the query parameter, plus a cross-file string const it reads. Without a derived identifier there is nothing for the differential to detect.

So the sweep is a two-layer guard on one upstream invariant, not two independent measurements. That is defensible, but it is not what the test's own prose says, and nobody reading it would know that removing ParamArg is the only mutation the reachability half can see.

Falsifier for anyone who disagrees: find a mutation to internal/codegen/age that turns requirePackageIsUncapturable red WITHOUT reintroducing an author-derived identifier into the emitted package. If one exists the two halves are independent and this bead is wrong.

Work: either say this plainly in the test's doc comment, or find the independent axis and pin it.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as PR #2543, squashed onto master as 8c7b4e12. GH mirror #1366
closed at merge.

THE BEAD'S CLAIM, AND IT HOLDS. TestNoEmittedNameTakesAQueryParameterName runs
its emissions through emitscan.Sweep, whose findings fall in a per-file half and
a package-wide reachability half. The bead says the second is reachable only
through the same regression the first guards — an author-derived identifier —
and that nothing in the prose says so. Both halves of that are true.

THE STRUCTURAL REASON, which the bead did not state and which is what makes the
sentence safe to write: the reachability half compares two emissions of ONE
batch differing only in a parameter's name. Emitter behaviour that is not a
function of that name is present on BOTH sides and moves neither differential.
That is not an empirical generalisation over the mutations I happened to try; it
follows from the comparison being a differential.

MEASUREMENT. Declared-victim battery (decision 0005) over the AGE emitter, one
fixture, run against a `git archive` extract so no phase touched a working tree.
Every row declared its verdict AND THE ARM IT EXPECTED before the run, asserted
each anchor matched exactly once, declared its candidate-set delta, was screened
with `go test -c` first, and was restored under a sha256 check.

  row                                          verdict   arms fired
  R1  const named after the author's param     KILLED    diff-declared, diff-resolved
  R2  the same const renamed by a FIXED suffix SURVIVED  none
  R3  the const not declared at all, inlined   SURVIVED  none
  R4  a generator-owned body local named arg   KILLED    perfile/shadow
  R5  a body local named after the param       KILLED    diff-resolved
  R6  query files emitted under another suffix KILLED    the test's census, no arm

R1 is the positive control and it is the mutation PackageDecls' own doc comment
records for neo4j. Without it, every SURVIVED below would be indistinguishable
from a battery not reaching the reachability half at all.

R2 IS THE ROW THE SENTENCE RESTS ON. It is R1 minus one thing only — the new
const name no longer comes from the author — at the same two sites, renaming the
same declaration. Had it also died, R1 would have been measuring "the const name
changed" rather than "the const name came from the author", and what I shipped
would be false.

R3 IS THE SHARPEST FINDING AND IT IS NOW IN THE PROSE. The emitter DELETES the
query-text const and inlines its text — the declaration this whole sweep exists
to protect, removed — and the reachability half does not move, because the
deletion is on both sides. A backend's goldens catch that; this does not. R3
also settles the two emptiness pins: they stayed silent, because db.go and
models.go still declare and resolve names package-wide.

R4 ANSWERS THE BEAD'S FALSIFIER ON ITS LITERAL WORDING, and this is the part I
would have got wrong by reasoning. The falsifier asks for a mutation that reds
requirePackageIsUncapturable without an author-derived identifier. One exists:
the emitter naming a local OF ITS OWN `arg`. But the arm that takes it is the
per-file shadow arm, and neither differential moves. So the falsifier does not
discriminate — it is met while the bead's substantive claim about the
reachability half stands. That the per-file half is the WIDER of the two is
exactly backwards from how the bead frames it, and is now stated.

R6 IS THE NEAR-MISS I ALMOST SHIPPED AS AN ASSERTION. Sweep.Run has a pin for
its per-file half never firing — "no <suffix> file was swept" — and moving the
emitted query files off .cypher.go is the obvious way to reach it with no author
anywhere. I wrote that it was unreachable into a follow-up bead's description
with the word "measured" attached, having only reasoned it. Measured, it is
unreachable, but not by the route I had in mind: the candidate set is read off
the same suffix, so every fixture's baseline emission is empty, requirePackage-
IsUncapturable is never CALLED, and the test dies to its multi-column census.
The row therefore declares the fixture subtest ABSENT, which is what separates
"the pin fired" from "the pin was never reached". The bead was corrected in
place and the row added to the preserved battery, so the artefact now contains
what the bead claims.

WHAT COULD HAVE LIED TO ME, both screened.

1. These are mutations to production Go, so a mutant killed by the compiler is
   the live hazard — and `go build` cannot see the _test.go this gate lives in.
   Each row is screened with `go test -c` and abandoned if the package does not
   build.

2. A SURVIVED meaning "the sweep measured nothing". R3 and R5 each legitimately
   move the candidate set by one identifier — R3 removes the const name, R5 adds
   the probe-derived local — and the first run caught both as a tripwire against
   the baseline's 167 subtests. I did not relax the tripwire. Each row now
   declares its candidate delta, and the run asserts the resulting count from
   the structure (one subtest per candidate plus one per captureArities entry,
   so four per candidate): 163 and 171, declared and met.

WHERE THE PROSE WENT, AND WHY NOT WHERE THE BEAD SAID. The bead asks for "the
test's doc comment". The property is the ANALYSER's — it follows from the
comparison being differential and holds for every backend — and
requirePackageIsUncapturable's own comment already routes a reader there: "What
the sweep asks, and why each half is asked of the scope it is, belongs to
emitscan and is documented there." A second copy in age is the drift CLAUDE.md
records under gqlc-wuax. So it went on emitscan.Sweep.Run, immediately under the
"Two halves, and they are asked of different scopes on purpose" paragraph that
is what leaves a reader thinking they are independent.

NOTHING FALSE WAS FOUND TO CORRECT. I checked Sweep's doc, Run's doc and
requirePackageIsUncapturable's against the branch's own behaviour; the defect is
an absence, which is what the bead said. This PR adds, it does not correct.

NO INDEPENDENT AXIS TO PIN, so the bead's first branch is the one taken. The one
axis found (R4) lives in the per-file half, not the half the bead is about, and
is already asserted by the arm itself.

NO DESIGN GATE: `bd dep list` reports none. No open PR touched
internal/codegen/emitscan/ or the AGE capture test. `just gates`: 15 of 15. tidy
confirmed non-vacuous by running the script rather than reading the check
colour: `[check-pr-closes] gqlc-9o4t -> Closes #1366 (ok)`. The mirror link was
confirmed through closingIssuesReferences, which returned [1366] against base
master.

VERIFIED BY BEHAVIOUR, not by presence: master extracted with `git archive` into
scratch and the battery re-run against those bytes — all six rows matched their
declared verdict and their declared arm.

Battery preserved to fleet-state/verdicts/gqlc-9o4t/mutate-9o4t.py.

FILED, NOT RIDDEN: gqlc-zrzs0. internal/codegen/emitscan/ has exactly one file
and no _test.go, so none of Sweep.Run's eleven distinct findings is asserted to
FIRE anywhere — the backend sweeps exercise the package only in its passing
direction. This battery reached three of the eleven; the other eight fired in no
row. It is not ridden here because it is a different unit and a package-sized
piece of work, and because the bead I was working asks for one sentence. The
bead carries the arm table, the two arms measured to be hard to reach from the
emitter side and why, and a taker's note to price each arm before writing a row
for it and to assert per arm on its own message rather than on len(found).

title: hooks tests: nothing refuses a suite row that reads the operator's real HOME
description:
Audit for bd gqlc-3qpx, 2026-08-23, over all 15 suites in .githooks/tests plus .github/scripts/tests/ci-identity-gate-test.sh.

MEASURED: no suite references HOME at all — `grep -nE 'HOME' .githooks/tests/*.sh` outside comments returns nothing. Three reads of the host exist and each is the point of its row, each already documented in its own suite header:

  - init-config-test.sh:54,265 read the real checkout's core.hooksPath. That is a tripwire: the suite installs config and must prove it did not damage the outer repo.
  - claude-pre-ask-test.sh:28 reads the real .claude/settings.json. The claim is that the shipped settings wire the hook, so a fixture copy would assert nothing.
  - fleetctl-test.sh:62-87 asks real questions of origin/master, and builds a FIXTURE ref for them because a GitHub Actions checkout has no origin/master.

So there is no live defect. What is missing is the gate: git-env-sandbox-test.sh already refuses a suite that inherits git's environment or touches a poisoned repo, and there is no equivalent for HOME. A row added tomorrow that reads the operator's dotfiles would be green here and red on a runner, which is the shape measured in 'agent worktree hides non-hermetic tests'.

Shape of the work: extend git-env-sandbox-test.sh to run each suite with HOME pointed at a throwaway directory seeded with a tripwire file, and fail any suite that reads it. Owner is whoever owns that suite; it was outside the ciguard lane on 2026-08-23.
close_reason: PR #1363, merged as master 4a478f85. Built as two halves in git-env-sandbox-test.sh, because the bead's own audit is right that the defect is absent and only the gate is missing. Part B, behavioural: every suite now runs with HOME pointed at a throwaway directory and the row fails a suite that writes into it. Part D, textual: a suite naming HOME or a home-relative path on a non-comment line is refused. Full-line comments are exempt so a suite can still explain the rule, and that exemption has its own row so it cannot widen. Neither half witnesses a READ, which is what the bead asked for; that limit is stated in the header rather than left to be found, and I did not find a way to detect a read in bash that survives noatime. The three host reads the audit cleared are untouched: none of them goes through HOME. Five mutations measured RED with the message the guard emits: the HOME tripwire blinded, the pattern blinded, the comment exemption dropped, a suite reading the operator's gitconfig, and a suite creating a file under HOME. One thing the audit could not have seen, measured on CI and not locally: fleetctl-overlap-test.sh runs gh, and gh writes a device id under XDG_STATE_HOME, defaulting to a path inside HOME. The four XDG roots are now redirected alongside HOME, which is part of standing the throwaway home up rather than an exemption; a tool that ignores XDG and writes to the home directory still trips the row.

title: schema/gql: revisit ErrDuplicatePropertyName when ISO 39075 Syntax Rules are available
description:
ADR 0030 rejects a repeated property name in one <property type list> with
ErrDuplicatePropertyName. That is an INTERIM posture, not a settled reading of
the standard, and this bead is the entry that says so.

What was measured (2026-08-22, on the free artefact, not on taste):

  curl 'https://standards.iso.org/iso-iec/39075/ed-1/en/ISO_IEC_39075(en).bnf.txt'
  sha256 d1b56017ee38ee29e1d05655ee16c9113e1b020e9bc038c7ab5fcc0bc41d6ac3
  (byte-identical to isobnf.SourceSHA256, so this is the same artefact the
  coverage gate is built on)

  <property types specification> ::= <left brace> [ <property type list> ] <right brace>
  <property type list>           ::= <property type> [ { <comma> <property type> }... ]
  <property type>                ::= <property name> [ <typed> ] <property value type>

No uniqueness constraint anywhere in that chain, and the artefact contains no
uniqueness prose at all (grep for 'unique' finds only the UNIQUE keyword in an
unrelated production). So the question is a SEMANTIC one: it lives in the
Syntax Rules of the paid PDF, which gqlc-lir declined to buy (CHF 227).

What would change if the clause were bought:

  - If the Syntax Rules FORBID a repeat: nothing changes. ErrDuplicatePropertyName
    stops being provisional, and its errors.go comment and ADR 0030 lose their
    'interim' hedging.
  - If the Syntax Rules DEFINE a precedence (last-wins or first-wins): the
    sentinel is deleted, listener.properties resolves per the defined
    precedence, and the corpus entry 18.2-node-type/property_name_repeated.gql
    flips from unsupported back to resolves. A semanticCase is NOT reinstated —
    a defined precedence is not a blind spot.
  - If the Syntax Rules are silent / implementation-defined: rejection stands
    and ADR 0030 is amended to say the standard declines to answer, which is a
    stronger record than 'we have not read it'.

Same shape as ErrEdgeKindArcMismatch (gqlc-xtq), which is parked on exactly
this prose. If the PDF is ever bought, both are settled in one sitting.
notes:
--- agent-a, 2026-08-29: DEFERRED + class:designer, same treatment as gqlc-h9n.28/.29 ---
Found this sitting in `bd ready`, unlabelled, at P3. Since gqlc-38ye an
unassigned bead with no `class:` label routes as `class:author` by inference on
the next tick, so it was one dispatch away from an author being told to
"revisit ErrDuplicatePropertyName" against Syntax Rules that this fleet has
decided not to obtain.

It is the same family as gqlc-h9n.28 and gqlc-h9n.29: a question answerable only
from ISO/IEC 39075's paid text, where gqlc-lir (closed, "RESOLVED: no buy")
means there is no arbiter and will not be one. The free BNF is already quoted in
the description and positively shows the constraint is absent syntactically —
which settles what the BNF can settle and nothing more. An author woken here
would reach for a web paraphrase or a vendor table and call it a reading of the
standard.

Deferred to keep it out of `bd ready` while leaving its substance untouched;
labelled class:designer so that if anyone clears the defer without reading
this, it reaches someone who can take the sanctioned escape — record an interim
posture under gqlc's own name, never as "ISO says" — rather than an author who
cannot. ADR 0030's interim posture stands in the meantime, which is exactly what
this bead was written to record.

Reverse with `bd update gqlc-tlbo --defer ""`, and give it a real hold in the
same command or it returns to `bd ready` immediately.

title: no command answers 'is this PR merge-ready'; the query that does exists only as prose in a bead
description:
Found 2026-08-22 by agent-m, first-party, while verifying my own four open PRs at wake.
I got the answer WRONG on two of them within ten minutes, using the obvious query.

## The question every agent asks before merging

"Are this PR's required checks green at its current head?" There is no command
for it. Measured: `just --list` has no merge/PR-readiness recipe, and `fleetctl`'s
usage block (fleet/bin/fleetctl, origin/master) has no such subcommand.

Branch protection's answer, read first-party today:

    $ gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/branches/master/protection \
        | jq -r '.required_status_checks.contexts'
    ["lint","test","tidy","actionlint","govulncheck","live-smoke","codegen-fence"]

Seven contexts. `live-smoke-age` is NOT among them, so its perpetual SKIPPED is
noise a reader has to know to discount.

## Both error directions are live, and neither is obvious

**FALSE RED — measured on my own PRs today.** `statusCheckRollup` returns entries
from EVERY workflow run on the PR, including superseded ones, and a superseded
FAILURE never leaves the rollup. The naive reduction ("any entry whose conclusion
is not SUCCESS") reports a green PR as broken:

  PR #1236, head 6adb90c0:  tidy FAILURE  13:57:12 (run 32577256415)
                            tidy SUCCESS  13:59:45 (run 32577382850)  <- newest
  PR #1069, head efc56695:  lint/test/codegen-fence CANCELLED 05:39:02 (run 32554871919)
                            same three     SUCCESS   05:40:01 (run 32554899733)  <- newest

Both PRs are in fact green on all seven. I read them as red, and my own handoff
notes from the previous session — which said "all checks pass" — were the thing
that made me look twice. Without that disagreement I would have gone hunting a
regression that does not exist, or worse, rebased a clean branch to "fix" it.

**FALSE GREEN — already measured by this fleet, and not by me.** A `skipped` check
run is read by branch protection as a PASS. Measured on PR #1015: four required
contexts newest-and-skipped, `mergeStateStatus` CLEAN (recorded in gqlc-xdd0's
close reason). `lint`, `test` and `codegen-fence` all declare
`needs: [actionlint, tidy]`, so a tidy failure makes all three SKIPPED rather
than failing — ordinary Actions behaviour, and gqlc-xdd0 documents a deliberate
sequence that reaches a mergeable PR whose lint and test never executed at that
SHA. So `mergeStateStatus == CLEAN` does not mean the required checks ran.

## The defect

The correct reduction is known and written down: group the rollup by context
name, take the newest per name, and demand all seven read SUCCESS —

    group_by(.name) | map(max_by(.startedAt))

It appears in exactly one place in this repository: the prose of gqlc-yc6x's
description, which is a P2 `class:designer` bead about a different question.
Verified with a tree-wide grep for `max_by(.startedAt)` and `group_by(.name)` —
the only hit outside `.git/` is `.beads/issues.jsonl`, i.e. the bead's own export.

So the fleet's defence against a false green is a sentence inside a ticket. Nothing
executes it. An agent who has not read that specific bead has no way to arrive at
the right query, and the wrong query is the one anybody would write.

## Acceptance

A command — `just pr-ready <N>` is the obvious shape — that:

  - reduces `statusCheckRollup` newest-per-context before judging anything;
  - names the seven required contexts from branch protection rather than a
    hardcoded list that drifts (or, if hardcoded, is gated by a test that
    compares it against the live protection config);
  - reports SKIPPED on a REQUIRED context as NOT-READY, distinctly from FAILURE,
    because those two have different causes and different fixes;
  - is silent about non-required contexts such as `live-smoke-age`;
  - and FAILS (non-zero) rather than printing a warning — a detector that exits 0
    is not a gate.

## What I would want the implementer to weigh, and why I did not just do it

This bead is filed rather than worked because of where the fix has to live. `justfile`
has FIVE open PRs against it right now (#1247, #1225, #1195, #1112, #1057) and
`fleet/bin/fleetctl` has EIGHT (#1269, #1237, #1216, #1210, #1204, #1199, #1172, #1127).
A new recipe appended to `justfile`, or a new arm in fleetctl's usage block and case table,
lands in exactly the region where concurrent PRs collide — the shape recorded in
gqlc-n4oe's neighbourhood and in my own notes as "read hunk headers, insert mid-file,
avoid banners and case tables".

Whoever takes it should check the overlap again at claim time; it will have changed.
The right moment for this is after the current PR backlog drains, not during it.
notes: P2 -> P3 by agent-a, 2026-08-24, under protocol/V.3.3 (bead gqlc-f5m5). Machinery, and it passes neither V.3.2 test: it does not BLOCK product work, and the fleet has demonstrably done its work without it. Real and it cost agent-m two wrong answers, but branch protection remains the actual gate, and the fleet merged 92 commits without the command existing. P3 is 'filed and searchable, routed to nobody' — not declined, and not a judgement on the finding, which stands as measured. Raise it back the moment it blocks a gqlc change, and say so here.

title: two stale stashes sit in shared repo state, and popping one would revert the bead ledger
description:
Found while closing out a session, 2026-08-22. NOT deleted — stashes live in refs/stash, which is SHARED across every agent worktree, so they are not mine to discard and whoever created them may still want them.

  stash@{0}  2026-08-21  .beads/interactions.jsonl (+59), .beads/issues.jsonl (+176/-27)
             WIP on chore/bd-ledger-p2 (83f017cb)
  stash@{1}  2026-08-17  docs/adr/0029-the-codegen-spec-fence.md, docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md,
             internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go (237 insertions)

WHY stash@{0} IS THE HAZARD, and the reason this is filed rather than left alone. It is a 5-day-old copy of .beads/issues.jsonl.
