title: vuln: clear the three uncalled advisories the widened scan now surfaces
description:
Widening the scan in gqlc-rohp made the nested module test/data/codegen report three advisories that govulncheck classifies as not-called, so the gate exits 0 and does not block:

- GO-2026-5158 — go.opentelemetry.io/otel v1.41.0, baggage parsing no longer caps raw header length. Imported, not called. Fixed in v1.42.0.
- GO-2026-5841 — github.com/klauspost/compress v1.18.5, OOB read in .../s2. Required, not imported. Fixed in v1.18.7.
- GO-2026-5932 — golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp unmaintained and unsafe by design. Required, not imported. No fix available; nothing in this tree imports openpgp, so this one is permanent noise unless x/crypto drops the package.

Both fixable ones are indirect deps of testcontainers-go v0.43.0. Not bumped in gqlc-rohp because there is no reachable exposure and pinning indirect deps ahead of the module that requires them is churn that go mod tidy can undo. Bump them when testcontainers-go next moves, or pin deliberately if the classification changes to called.

Also worth reporting upstream: govulncheck v1.6.0 silently drops the imports of an in-package test variant, because it keys loaded packages by import path and `p [p.test]` collides with `p`. Reproduced minimally — identical module, identical deps, identical flags, only `package v` vs `package v_test` differing: the in-package form reported nothing, the external form reported the vulnerability with a call trace. gqlc-rohp works around it by keeping the live battery an external test package, held by test-codegen-fence.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver/codegen: rationale text from the edge-set work is incomplete or reaches across layers
description:
Three comment/citation sites left by gqlc-35yu.9. None change behaviour; each
is a place where the text a future reader is asked to trust says less than the
code guarantees, or justifies itself from the wrong layer.

1. internal/resolver/resolve.go, edgeProbes' doc comment, and
   docs/specs/resolver-stage-r3.md §4.4. Both name `src == tgt` as THE reason
   two probes can name one key. Under ADR 0022 plural endpoints there is a
   second: overlapping srcs/tgts give (A,B) twice with A != B. The
   postcondition (the result is a set) is unaffected — the enumeration dedupes
   on the whole EdgeKey, not on the self-loop condition — but the stated
   rationale is not exhaustive, so a reader checking the code against the
   reason would conclude the dedupe is dead on the plural path. See gqlc-kph4,
   which is the coverage side of the same observation.

2. internal/resolver/resolve_test.go, TestEdgeUnionKeysAreASet. Its comment
   justifies the assertion by what codegen does with a duplicate (emits the
   switch case twice, package fails to compile). AGENTS.md discourages
   cross-layer appeals: the resolver's own reason to return a set is R3 §4.6
   dispatching on the candidate count, which is true whether or not codegen
   exists. Restate it from the resolver's contract and let the codegen
   consequence be at most a closing aside.

3. internal/codegen/prepare.go, admitEdgeUnionCandidates. The first gate (fewer
   than two candidates) cites "R3 spec §4.4" for the invariant it is asserting.
   The third gate — two candidates sharing an edge label — likewise depends on
   the resolver having returned a set rather than a bag, since a bag would
   reach it as a false duplicate-label refusal. It carries no citation. Give it
   the same one.
notes:
MANAGER SEQUENCING NOTE (2026-08-01). Deliberately NOT staffed in parallel with
gqlc-kph4, which is in flight on feat/resolver-plural-undirected-coverage.

This bead's item 1 is the edgeProbes doc comment and R3 spec §4.4 — the exact
text kph4 will be rewriting, because kph4's whole subject is the plural-endpoint
path those two currently describe incompletely. Two agents editing the same
paragraphs concurrently produces a conflict whose resolution is a judgement
call neither of them is placed to make.

Items 2 and 3 (TestEdgeUnionKeysAreASet's cross-layer justification, and the
missing R3 §4.4 citation on admitEdgeUnionCandidates' third gate) are genuinely
independent of kph4 and could have gone now. Kept together with item 1 anyway:
splitting one small comment-accuracy bead into two branches and two PRs costs
more review attention than it saves wall-clock, and item 1 is the one with real
content.

Staff immediately once kph4 lands, and re-read item 1 first — kph4 may have
already made it true, in which case this bead shrinks to items 2 and 3.

title: docs: sentinel taxonomy tables in docs/specs drift from codegen.allSentinels, with no fence
description:
docs/specs/codegen-stage-c3.md, c4.md, c5.md and c6.md carry taxonomy tables mapping
constructs to error sentinels, plus a mirror of codegen.allSentinels annotated with the
stage that introduced each. Nothing checks those tables against the Go slice, so they
drift.

Known drift as of gqlc-35yu.9:
  - the LIST / ANY property refusal added for apache-age-pgx-v5 (round 2) routes
    through ErrUnrepresentableWidth and is not in the construct tables
  - ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion (round 3, shared Phase A gate) is in neither the
    construct tables nor the allSentinels mirror

Raised by Carmack during gqlc-35yu.9 and deliberately not fixed there: the branch's own
precedent left the tables alone, and a drive-by two-row edit on an AGE-owned branch is
the wrong unit of work for drift that is already several entries deep.

Do this as one sweep: reconcile every table against allSentinels, and decide whether
the stage specs are historical records of what stage Cn delivered (in which case a
sentinel added by a later epic does not belong in them, and the mirror needs a new home)
or a live index (in which case add a fence that fails when the two disagree, the way
TestSentinelReachability already forces fixture coverage).
notes:
Fence landed on chore/sentinel-taxonomy-fence. Forks resolved:

(1) Historical record vs live index — HISTORICAL, decided on evidence rather than
taste. C2/C3/C4/C5 taxonomy tables name ErrOutOfC2Scope..ErrOutOfC5Scope, sentinels
retired by the per-stage rename; a fence over them would demand falsifying what each
stage shipped. C6 §7 also declares itself the last stage, so a sentinel arriving after
it has no stage spec left to be recorded in — the mirror genuinely has nowhere to go
inside the series. So the stage specs freeze and the mirror gets a new home:
docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md, a live index the fence owns. One pointer line
added to C6 §7 saying the live index moved; C0–C5 untouched, since a reader following
the series arrives at C6 and the new doc explains the relationship.

(2) Fence shape — plain Go test, TestSentinelTaxonomy in internal/codegen/errors_test.go,
inside package codegen so it reads allSentinels directly. No new just recipe and no new
CI job: the required-context list on master is exact, and splitting a job silently
deletes a context. The existing `test` job runs it.

(3) Naming the slice members — the test parses errors.go with go/parser and binds
ident->value through the errors.New message literal, rather than a hand-written
name switch. conformance_test.go sentinelIdent is already such a switch and is a third
mirror of the same set; adding a fourth to fence the second would be the disease. The
fence asserts message uniqueness so the binding stays sound.

(4) Three directions, not two. index<->allSentinels; taxonomy rows<->index; and
declared-in-errors.go <-> documented (index union excluded). The third is the one the
first two cannot see: a sentinel declared and left out of allSentinels leaves both other
sets agreeing on a membership that never grew.

(5) Rejected: asserting document row order matches slice order. Buys tidy diffs, costs a
red suite on a legitimate reorder.

(6) Rejected: naming age.ErrUnsupportedQuery / ErrUnsupportedSchema in the doc. They are
outside allSentinels and have no exported set to fence, so naming them would add exactly
the kind of unfenced claim this bead exists to remove. The preamble says backend packages
carry their own sentinels without naming symbols.

Drift found, all of it fixed on the same branch so the fence lands green:
  - ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion is in allSentinels and has two invalid fixtures, and
    appears in zero files under docs/. C6 §7 says fifteen sentinels; the slice has sixteen.
  - ErrUnrepresentableWidth catchment is stale in kind, not just in rows. C3/C4/C5 tables
    enumerate "the eight unrepresentable widths" as a property of the language. Since the
    AGE backend it is the target TypeMap answer: AGE also refuses BYTES, the five
    temporals, LIST and ANY, and unrepresentable_width_list_schema /
    unrepresentable_width_any_schema pin widths no table names. The live doc states the
    backend-relative rule instead of enumerating.
  - The tables carry a stage-relative "Retires at" column that stopped meaning anything at
    C6. The live doc drops it and keeps an "Introduced" column that can hold a bead id.

Verified by mutation, not by assertion: six drift modes each fail with a message naming
the doc, the section and the edit — missing index row (the real drift), index naming a
retired sentinel, missing construct row, missing exclusion row, misspelt sentinel, and a
construct routed to a non-reachable sentinel. Gates: just test, just lint, just
actionlint, just test-codegen-fence all green.
REVIEW: VERDICT FAIL. Manager confirms two of the three blockers by direct test; the third by reading. Returned for a fix round.

The fence itself is sound. The reviewer broke it six ways and it named the document and the section every time; I had already broken it a seventh (an undeclared sentinel) with the same result. Every one of the author's five claims verified. The problem is not the fence — it is what the fence is fencing, and a hole in the one axis the fence was built for.

B1 (BLOCKING). docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md:81 states a phase at which the refusal cannot fire:

  | ErrUnrepresentableWidth | A projected column, or a query parameter, whose property width the target's type table has no carrier for. | Phase A |

Prepare runs phaseZAdmit before phaseAAdmit (prepare.go:238), and phaseZAdmit walks every property of every node and edge type, so any width the target refuses always loses at Phase Z. The code says so itself, in phaseAAdmit's own doc comment (prepare.go:544-547): "Phase Z already caught schema-side offenders so a column projecting an unrepresentable-width property is unreachable unless the query declares an unrepresentable width on a parameter."

I read that comment directly rather than take the report's word. Note it is the COLUMN half of the row that is unreachable; the parameter half is fine. So the row is half-wrong rather than wholly wrong, which is if anything worse — it reads as authoritative and a contributor cannot tell which half to trust. Corroborating: all five unrepresentable_width_* fixtures are *_schema, and §4 step 3 tells a contributor to add a fixture per construct, which for the column half is impossible.

The reviewer flags the same defect at :90 (ErrAliasRequired at Phase B, where prepare.go:717 calls rowFieldName(col.Name) on a column prepare.go:579 already called it on in Phase A — identical predicate, identical input, byte-identical error strings). I have not verified that second instance myself; the implementer should, and should say which way it went.

This is precisely the failure the fence cannot see. A fence holds a document against the code for CONSISTENCY. Nothing holds its prose against the code for CORRECTNESS, so the prose has to be right at commit time. Shipping a wrong phase inside a document whose header calls itself "the live index", in a bead whose entire premise is that documentation drifted from code, is not acceptable.

B2 (BLOCKING). errors_test.go:176-177 has a silent `continue` on the axis the AST parse exists for:

  if !ok || len(value.Names) != 1 || len(value.Values) != 1 { continue }

I reproduced this myself. Adding to errors.go's own var block:

  ErrMultiA, ErrMultiB = errors.New("multi a"), errors.New("multi b")

— two sentinels, one ValueSpec, absent from allSentinels, documented nowhere — leaves `go test -run TestSentinelTaxonomy ./internal/codegen/` GREEN. Direction (c) is bypassed by a comma.

What makes this blocking rather than a gap: twelve lines below, at :184, the author writes a LOUD Require for the adjacent failure mode (declared as something other than errors.New), and it fires correctly. The same author, in the same function, treated one neighbour as a hard error and the other as a skip. That asymmetry is not a scoping decision, and it is one line.

Second bypass of the same axis: errors_test.go:165 parses the single file "errors.go", so a sentinel declared in any other file of package codegen is invisible to (c). parser.ParseDir over the package closes it. Nothing in the repo pins sentinels to errors.go.

B3 (BLOCKING, accepted on the reviewer's evidence). §2 omits the list-leaf construct for ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion. admitEdgeUnionCandidates has two call sites (prepare.go:597 column, prepare.go:1013 list-element chain), and invalid/unrepresentable_edge_union_shared_label_list has its own committed fixture for the second. §2's preamble asserts a sentinel carries EVERY construct in its catchment, and §2 does carry list-leaf rows for ErrUnrepresentableWidth and ErrOutOfC6Scope. So the document breaks its own stated contract, on the exact sentinel whose absence from the docs motivated this bead.

NON-BLOCKING, and I am ruling on each rather than leaving them to the implementer:

N1 — §3 is an unaudited silencing valve. The reviewer dropped ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion from allSentinels, moved its row to §3 with the text "Silenced by fiat.", deleted both fixtures, and the whole codegen tree stayed green while prepare.go:671 still returns that sentinel. That is real, but it is NOT a regression — the pre-commit state was no better, and the escape needs three coordinated edits. The repo already has the counter-measure in another package (internal/schema/gql/sentinel_coverage_test.go, TestAllSentinelsAreReachable, which reads errors off the wire for exactly this reason). FILE AS A FOLLOW-UP, do not fix here. The bead is about drift between doc and code; reachability is a different axis and deserves its own bead rather than being smuggled into this one.

N2 — three rows present defensive branches (prepare.go:589, :650-655, whose own comments say a synthetic seam is required to reach them) as ordinary user-refusable constructs. FIX HERE. It is the same class as B1 — a contributor will try to write an impossible fixture — and the document already has a section for the distinction.

N3 — ":13 says three renames ago; the chain C2->C3->C4->C5->C6 is four." FIX HERE. It is one word, and the sentence is load-bearing for the design fork the author used to justify the whole approach.

N4 — ":29-30 says allSentinels is the closed set Generate may return on user input", falsified by age.ErrUnsupportedQuery, which is not in allSentinels. FIX HERE, as the reviewer suggests: "the shared front end may return", not "Generate".

N5, N6, N7 — leave. N5 and N6 are diagnosable in seconds, N7 is inherited wording from the repo's own sweepIdentifiers comment and changing it here widens the diff for no gain.
Review FAIL addressed on the same branch.

B1b, the ErrAliasRequired-at-Phase-B question the manager left open: the flag is
CORRECT, the branch is unreachable. Structurally, prepare.go:579 (Phase A) and :717
(Phase B) both call rowFieldName(col.Name) over the same q.Validated.Columns of the
same q, rowFieldName is a pure function of its argument, and Prepare runs phaseAAdmit
to completion before phaseBDerive, first-offender-wins. So Phase A always returns
first, with a byte-identical message.

Rather than argue it, I instrumented all eighteen sentinel fail-sites in prepare.go
with a file-sink counter and ran the whole suite. Only five are reached:
EU_shared_label (x5), A_alias (x4), A_nonproperty_param (x2), L_width (x1),
L_unknown_type (x1). The Phase B alias site is not among them, nor is the Phase A
width-column site. First attempt at this measurement used println and read as
"nothing is reachable" — go test hides passing packages stderr. Worth remembering.

The same sweep corrected two rows the review did not flag, in both directions:
  - the list-leaf width row (L_width) and the list-leaf no-arm row (L_unknown_type)
    ARE reached, so they stay in the reachable table. I had been about to demote the
    first on the same shadowed-by-Phase-Z reasoning as the column row; the data says
    no.
  - A_backtick and A_width_param are reachable in principle but reached by no
    fixture. Not a doc defect, a corpus gap; not fixed here.

Document restructured rather than patched: §2 now carries reachable constructs only,
new §3 "Branches no input reaches" carries the six shadowed/defensive branches with
the reason named per row (shadowed = an earlier phase applied the same predicate to
the same input; defensive = an upstream invariant would have to break). §4 is the
old §3, §5 the old §4. This is what B1 and N2 have in common, and splitting the table
is what makes §5 step 3 ("a fixture per construct") true instead of impossible.

B2: declaredSentinels now walks every non-test .go file in the package rather than
errors.go alone, and a multi-name var spec is handled by pairing names with values
positionally, with a hard Require when the two do not pair one to one. The managers
own repro (ErrMultiA, ErrMultiB = ...) now fails, as does a sentinel declared in a
second file, as does `ErrPairA, ErrPairB error`.

B3: added the list-element-chain row for ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion, which
invalid/unrepresentable_edge_union_shared_label_list covers.

N3 fixed (four renames, C2->C3->C4->C5->C6, not three). N4 fixed (§1 now says the
shared front end, and says a Generate call can fail outside the set). N1 left alone
per ruling.

Fence gained a fourth assertion, TestUnreachedBranchesNameRealSentinels: a §3 row
must name a sentinel allSentinels still holds. Six drift modes re-verified against
the renumbered document, including renaming a heading out from under the parser.
Gates: just test, just lint, just actionlint, just test-codegen-fence all green.
HANDOFF 2026-08-01. Refix committed at 097cc79 on chore/sentinel-taxonomy-fence, tree clean. Adversarial review of the refix was dispatched and DIED ON SESSION QUOTA before a verdict — NO VERDICT EXISTS, do not merge. Re-dispatch against 097cc79.

A coverage gap filed as documented intent is worse than the original bug; (b) does ANYTHING fail when a section 3 branch becomes reachable again, or does the new fourth assertion only check that the names are real sentinels? title: codegen/age: a multi-label node or edge type refuses the whole schema
description:
age.rejectMultiLabelSchema fails generation when the schema declares a node or
edge type keyed on more than one label. Verified against apache/age 1.7.0:
`CREATE (x:A:B {n: 1})` is a syntax error — AGE stamps exactly one label on a
vertex or an edge and its parser has no syntax for a second — so a graph
matching such a type cannot be written through this backend and no value
matching it can arrive to be decoded.

The gate is on the schema's whole entity table rather than on the columns a
batch projects, because Phase Z names an entity for every type in the schema
and the emitted Go surface is backend-invariant: a struct no query could fill
is still a struct the package would have to declare, with a label check
nothing could satisfy.

The cost is the same shape as gqlc-35yu.13's: a schema carrying one multi-label
type refuses AGE generation for the whole batch, including queries that never
touch it. test/data/codegen/valid/entity_multi_label_named is the fixture; it
is enrolled for neo4j-go-v5 only.
acceptance_criteria:
Either:
- a per-entity admission lands in the shared prepare phase, so a backend can
  refuse one entity without refusing the schema, and the AGE gate narrows to
  the queries that actually project the refused type; or
- the bead closes recording that whole-schema refusal is the right posture,
  with the reason stated where an author hitting it will find it.
notes:
SEQUENCING (2026-08-03): held behind gqlc-35yu.13 rather than parallelised, on a genuine collision — not on conflict risk as a blanket excuse.

Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one.

Territory: .15's answer lands in internal/codegen/age/prepare.go's gate and, if the per-entity route is taken, in the shared internal/codegen/prepare.go admission phase. .13 is in flight in exactly that gate — it is the LIST/ANY-width arm of the same unservedColumn machinery. Two agents editing one gate is a merge conflict for no gain.

Design: .15's two acceptance branches are not independent of .13's outcome. Both beads describe the SAME cost shape verbatim — 'a schema carrying one refused type refuses AGE generation for the whole batch, including queries that never touch it'. If .13 builds a per-entity admission mechanism, .15 consumes it and becomes a one-line enrolment. If .13 keeps whole-schema refusal, then .15 is no longer a per-bead choice at all: it is the same posture decision for both, and deciding it twice in two branches is how the two arms end up disagreeing.

So .15 starts after .13 merges, and its first act is to read what .13 actually did rather than re-deriving the posture blind. If .13 lands per-entity admission, .15 should be small. If it does not, .15 owns the posture decision for both arms and should say so in its own acceptance.

OUTCOME (2026-08-03, branch feat/age-multi-label-posture): second branch taken — whole-schema refusal recorded as the posture, in docs/adr/0027-age-refuses-a-multi-label-schema-whole.md. Not on principle; both alternatives were built and measured.

Shape (a), omit the struct on AGE: enrolled valid/entity_multi_label_named in both targets, dropped the entity on AGE, regenerated goldens. TestBackendInvariantSurface RED — "entity_multi_label_named declares a different Go surface under neo4j-go-v5 than under apache-age-pgx-v5", the AGE surface holding 3 declarations to neo4j's 4.

Shape (b/c), emit the struct and narrow the refusal to projecting queries: TestBackendInvariantSurface stays GREEN, because the comparison is over declarations and decodePersonEmployee is an unexported receiver-less func it skips. It emits, at exit 0, a decoder reading `if label != "Employee&Person"` — gqlc's own LabelSetKey join spelling, which no AGE vertex carries and no AGE statement can stamp. That is the disposition ADR 0025 rejected for temporal kinds.

The ADR 0025 channel shape does not transfer: the temporal enum splits, so its answer has to vary per member. Label-set arity does not — one label or unrepresentable, permanently, because the constraint is in AGE's grammar. A refusal channel whose answer can never vary reads as a capability.

The diagnostic is rewritten to carry the reasoning: names each refused type and its labels, gives `CREATE (x:A:B)` as the witness that does not parse, counts the queries the schema refusal takes with it, names both exits.

NO invalid/ FIXTURE, and none is possible today: manifest sentinels resolve through sentinelByName's three lanes (codegen., queryfile., cypher.) and conformance imports no single backend, so age.ErrUnsupportedSchema is unnameable there. Filed as gqlc-rv0h. The corpus is instead pinned from the AGE side — TestRejectsMultiLabelSchema asserts both that the manifest omits apache-age-pgx-v5 and that this backend refuses the schema.

INCIDENTAL FINDING: the GQL grammar admits no `&` in an edge's key label set — `-[:WORKED_FOR&FOR]->` fails with "no viable alternative at input ':WORKED_FOR&FOR'". So the EntityEdge arm of the multi-label check is unreachable from real input. Kept, because codegen.Entity can carry one and a grammar change would reach it silently.

title: codegen/age: fence that every AGE target emits an identical SessionInit
description:
All 12 apache-age-pgx-v5 golden targets carry their own copy of SessionInit.
Nothing asserts directly that the copies agree.

Today they agree by construction -- SessionInit is emitted from one template
with no per-target variation -- and the codegen fence proves each golden
matches what the emitter produces. So the property holds transitively. What
is unpinned is the template gaining a per-target conditional: the fence would
stay green while the copies diverged.

This matters because live_age_session_test.go binds ONE package's SessionInit
to pools that hand out handles generated into others. That binding is only
sound while the copies issue the same statements. The live arm checks the two
packages it mixes (rightly -- that is its own precondition), but the general
claim is a pure-text property of the emitted tree and does not belong behind a
testcontainer.

Assert it offline: read SessionInit's body out of every
test/data/codegen/valid/*/golden/apache-age-pgx-v5/graph.go and require all 12
byte-identical. No container, runs in the default build, fails the moment the
template grows a per-target branch.

Found by Linus as NB2 on gqlc-35yu.8, where the finding was ruled a naming
defect in that bead's own test and the exhaustive claim was split out to here.
notes:
--- agent-d, 2026-09-03 — shipped as PR #2553 ---

STALE COUNT IN THE BEAD. It says "all 12 apache-age-pgx-v5 golden targets".
Measured at HEAD: 63. The property still holds across all 63 — every
SessionInit body hashes identically — so this lands as a fence, not a fix.

I distrusted that uniform hash before building on it. A per-file hash of an
extraction that silently returned nothing would also come back 63-identical,
which is the shape that certifies a lie. Printed one extraction: 27 lines,
the search_path set_config call plus the AGE operator canary. Real.

THE FENCE. TestEveryTargetEmitsTheSameSessionInit, internal/codegen/age/
session_init_test.go. AST-locates SessionInit in every golden graph.go, slices
its RAW SOURCE from the func keyword through the closing brace, requires all
copies byte-identical. Raw bytes rather than the AST so the statements'
explanatory comments are held too — those say why the search_path call and the
canary are shaped as they are, and a per-target branch would plausibly arrive
there first. Row P2 is that claim's evidence, not an assumption.

THREE VACUOUS PASSES REFUSED. A narrowing glob (floor >10, not NotEmpty: an
all-identical answer over a singleton asserts nothing); a golden declaring no
SessionInit ("nothing to compare" in a sweep whose subject is that every
target carries one); a SessionInit arriving as a method. Each has its own row.

BATTERY, 8 rows, all AS DECLARED. git-archive extract, sha256 restore
tripwire. Every divergence row declared the STRING the failure must contain
before the run, so a row cannot pass by being red for an unrelated reason, and
every row was checked to have actually RUN the test rather than been skipped
by an unanchored -run.
  P0 none                                                 green / green
  P1 one target's session statement respelled               red / red
  P2 one target's comment drifts, statements untouched      red / red
  P3 one target loses SessionInit outright                  red / red
  P4 one target's SessionInit arrives as a method           red / red
  P5 glob narrows to one fixture, nothing else wrong        red / red
  N1 P1's drift planted, agreement assertion blinded      green / green

N1 and N2 each blind exactly the one assertion their paired row depends on, so

  .../one_col_many/.../graph.go emits a SessionInit that differs from

P4 is refused by the same message as P3 ("declares no top-level SessionInit").
That is accurate rather than a collision: a method is not a top-level func,
and the sweep's subject is the exported function the live arm binds to.

title: spec: the :many empty-result contract (empty slice, not nil) is emitted but unspecified
description:
Generated `:many` methods emit `out := make([]RowT, 0, len(records))`, so an empty result set returns a non-nil zero-length slice rather than nil. That is a deliberate emitter choice, but `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md` never states it — the only nearby line is §'Columns is a non-empty slice', which is about something else.

gqlc-35yu.4 strengthened the live battery from `require.Empty` (which accepts nil) to `require.NotNil`, so the behaviour is now pinned by a test while remaining absent from the spec. Test and spec disagree about what is normative.

Worth settling before gqlc-35yu.8 brings the AGE arm into the same battery: if AGE's emitter reaches for `var out []RowT` the arm fails, and whether that failure is a bug in AGE or an over-tight test is currently unanswerable from the documents. The uniform-generated-interface promise argues for making it normative rather than relaxing the test.
acceptance_criteria: codegen-stage-c1.md states the :many empty-result contract explicitly and distinguishes it from :one's ErrNoRows; the live battery's assertion cites it.

title: TCK conformance ledger: execute the openCypher TCK against neo4j + AGE and track per-backend coverage
description:
Owner idea, 2026-07-31. Not yet scoped — this bead exists to hold the idea and the design tension, not to authorise a harness.

Proposal: run the whole vendored openCypher TCK generically against BOTH backends (neo4j and Apache AGE), analyse coverage, and incrementally drive it up.

CURRENT STATE
- The TCK is vendored at test/data/query/cypher/tck (tag 2024.3, via `just fetch-tck`).
- It is consumed PARSE-ONLY, by internal/query/cypher/acceptance_test.go, over a SUBSET of feature dirs (match, return, match-where, return-skip-limit, union, with, with-where, return-orderby, with-orderBy, with-skip-limit). Nothing executes TCK scenarios against a live backend.
- gqlc-35yu.4/.8 build a shared live scenario battery with per-backend adapters against live containers. That harness is the natural substrate for this work, which is why this bead depends on the epic.

THE DESIGN TENSION — RESOLVE BEFORE BUILDING
gqlc is a code generator, not a query engine. The TCK tests ENGINE semantics. So "TCK coverage" is ambiguous across three quite different levels, with very different cost and value:
  L1 PARSE      — does gqlc parse the scenario's query? (partially covered today)
  L2 GENERATE   — can gqlc emit code for it? Most TCK scenarios carry no schema and no typed params, so this needs a synthesised schema per scenario.
  L3 EXECUTE    — does the GENERATED code, run against backend X, produce the TCK's expected result table? This is the real prize and by far the most expensive: each scenario ships its own graph fixture as Cypher plus an expected-results table, so the harness must set up, generate, compile, run, and compare.

"100% coverage" is probably the WRONG TARGET. A large fraction of the TCK is out of scope for gqlc BY DESIGN — dynamic queries, and everything gqlc deliberately rejects (C6 scope limits, alias-required expressions, and similar). Chasing 100% would mean either weakening those rejections or permanently carrying a pile of unexplained failures.

The more valuable and actually achievable goal: a CLASSIFIED COVERAGE LEDGER in which every TCK scenario is either passing on a given backend or carries a recorded, reviewed reason for not being — out-of-scope-by-design, backend dialect gap, or genuine gqlc gap. Then the number to drive to zero is "genuine gqlc gaps", not "non-passing scenarios", and the ledger doubles as a per-backend dialect-gap map (which is adjacent to gqlc-35yu.12).

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Which level (L1/L2/L3) is the target? L3 per-backend is what "validate against both implementations" implies, but it is a large harness.
- Is the ledger a committed artefact (reviewable diff when coverage shifts) or a generated report?
- Where does it run? L3 against two live containers is nightly-job shaped, not PR-CI shaped.
acceptance_criteria: Framing agreed with the owner (which of the three coverage levels this targets, and how deliberately-out-of-scope scenarios are classified) before any harness work starts.
notes:
=== FRAMING RESOLVED 2026-08-01 — acceptance criterion met, harness work authorised ===
Decided under standing delegated authority (owner directive 2026-08-01: decide, record,
report). Reversible: nothing is built yet.

1. LEVEL — staged L1 -> L2 -> L3, one ledger spanning all three.
   The three levels are not alternatives; they are columns. A scenario that does not
   parse cannot generate, and one that does not generate cannot execute, so the ledger
   carries a per-level status and the levels gate each other naturally.
   L1 (parse) is backend-INDEPENDENT — it tests gqlc's Cypher front end, not a backend.
   It needs no container and no part of the 35yu epic, so it is separable and starts
   first. Split out as its own bead (see below); gqlc-modl retains L2/L3.
   L3 is the real prize and stays gated on 35yu.4/.8's live harness.

2. "100% COVERAGE" IS THE WRONG TARGET — this reverses the shape of the owner's original
   ask deliberately. A large fraction of the TCK exercises dynamic queries and constructs
   gqlc rejects BY DESIGN (C6 scope limits, alias-required expressions). Driving
   non-passing to zero would mean weakening those rejections. The number driven to zero
   is GENUINE GQLC GAPS.

3. CLASSIFICATION IS A CLOSED ENUM, and unclassified is a hard failure:
     pass | out-of-scope-by-design (must cite the ADR or spec clause) |
